quotes.t: The human condition of giving with expectations

quotes.c: It is striking that Christianity seems to be a consistent inroad for AI adoption — Jesus slop videos, AI-generated Christian music charting, and now literal Jesus. I don’t have a great story for why.
quotes.m: Christianity seems to be a consistent inroad for AI adoption
quotes.sum: The author observes that Christian media and imagery appear to be recurring channels for public AI adoption, though they do not explain why.
quotes.t: GD Roundup #4 - inference, monopolies, and AI Jesus

quotes.c: I think this leaves Longtermists with a much weaker case for why they should be the unique arbiters of long-term issues like AI-control, panspermia, etc. They simply don’t have compelling enough math, on its own, to argue for these cases, and it is often the math which is the bedrock of their spiritual authority.
quotes.m: it is often the math which is the bedrock of their spiritual authority.
quotes.sum: The author argues that longtermists lack enough mathematical justification to be sole decision-makers on humanity's far-future issues, and likens their reliance on math to spiritual authority.
quotes.t: Everybody Wants to Rule the Future - Is Longtermism's Mandate of Heaven by Arithmetic Justified?

quotes.c: He is astonished and appalled about the provision in OBBBA that outlaws regulation of AI for ten years. I found this notable for a couple reasons: (1) Rogan obviously has a large audience and is very politically influential. (2) I was surprised he did not make the connection that that provision of the bill was probably inserted by Trump’s VC supporters like Marc Andreesen.
quotes.m: I was surprised he did not make the connection that that provision of the bill was probably inserted by Trump’s VC supporters like Marc Andreesen.
quotes.sum: The author criticizes a proposed decade-long ban on AI regulation and speculates that Trump-aligned venture capital supporters pushed it.
quotes.t: Joe Rogan on AI Safety

quotes.c: Third, thinking about making the future better can sometimes seem creepily Utopian. I think that’s a real worry - some of the Utopian movements of the 20th century were extraordinarily harmful. And I think it should make us particularly wary of proposals for better futures that are based on some narrow conception of an ideal future. Given how much moral progress we should hope to make, we should assume we have almost no idea what the best feasible futures would look like.
quotes.m: Given how much moral progress we should hope to make, we should assume we have almost no idea what the best feasible futures would look like.
quotes.sum: MacAskill argues that improving the long-term future matters beyond avoiding extinction, but warns against imposing a narrow utopian vision because future moral progress may change what is valuable.
quotes.t: Should we aim for flourishing over mere survival? The Better Futures series.

quotes.c: Historically speaking, the most influential players in almost any field are private industry actors or governments, but rarely non-profits. If we expect AGI to eat the economy, I expect that the most influential safety players will also be private companies. It seems essential that the leading safety actors genuinely understand and care about extreme risks, because they are, by definition, risks that must be addressed proactively rather than reactively.
quotes.m: If we expect AGI to eat the economy, I expect that the most influential safety players will also be private companies.
quotes.sum: AGI safety should be developed through private companies because they are likely to become the most influential actors in an AI-driven economy.
quotes.t: The case for AGI safety products

quotes.c: AI might radically transform the world in the near future. If we’re taking this possibility seriously, we should be expecting that past a certain point, [5] a lot of our assumptions about what’s happening and how we can affect that will be completely off . (For example, a powerful AI agent may perform a global coup , which, among other consequences, would completely invalidate all the work animal advocates had done to secure corporate commitments, change governmental policy, etc. Or: governance and economic structures may get redefined. We might see the emergence of digital minds. Etc.)
quotes.m: We might see the emergence of digital minds.
quotes.sum: The author argues that transformative AI could upend animal advocacy and may create new groups, including digital minds, whose welfare matters.
quotes.t: A shallow review of what transformative AI means for animal welfare

quotes.c: The lived, human reality of this condition is an existential crisis of Unbounded Empowerment without Wisdom . We are a species that has developed the technical capacity of gods - to reshape biologies, to warp realities, to automate cognition - without having first cultivated the corresponding collective maturity, moral coherence, or spiritual grounding to wield that power without self-destructing.
quotes.m: We are a species that has developed the technical capacity of gods - to reshape biologies, to warp realities, to automate cognition - without having first cultivated the corresponding collective maturity, moral coherence, or spiritual grounding to wield that power without self-destructing.
quotes.sum: Humanity has godlike technological power but lacks the collective wisdom and moral maturity to use it safely.
quotes.t: The Engine of Foreclosure

quotes.c: Can someone in DOGE cut these subsidies? If you know anyone from DOGE, please reach out to them about this! Not eating the bugs seems to be a big thing among conservatives. So why the hell are we subsidizing bug farms, so that your hard-earned tax payer dollars are spent keeping failing bug farms afloat.
quotes.m: Not eating the bugs seems to be a big thing among conservatives.
quotes.sum: The author urges DOGE to eliminate public subsidies for insect farms and frames opposition to eating insects as a conservative concern.
quotes.t: The Lies of Big Bug

quotes.c: For example, Shrimp Welfare Project is trying to get new stunner tech developed, which I'm excited about . But I think there are a lot of other examples that this would work for. In-Ovo sexing seems like another good example of technology that I'm kind of surprised that the animal movement wasn't more involved in the development of [1] .
quotes.m: Shrimp Welfare Project is trying to get new stunner tech developed, which I'm excited about .
quotes.sum: The author argues that animal-welfare advocates should help develop technologies such as shrimp stunning and in-egg sexing.
quotes.t: Welfare tech should be developed by welfare people

quotes.c: Conditional upon farmed bees having net positive lives, I believe under most common philosophical frameworks eating honey is obviously morally permissible. The main exception I think might be strong suffering-focused or asymmetry views, where you may believe that causing a lot of suffering is bad even on consenting individuals who overall feel much more pleasure than suffering, and want to be alive.
quotes.m: Conditional upon farmed bees having net positive lives, I believe under most common philosophical frameworks eating honey is obviously morally permissible.
quotes.sum: The author argues that eating honey is usually permissible if farmed bees' lives are net positive, while noting suffering-focused ethics may disagree.
quotes.t: Eating Honey is (Probably) Fine, Actually

quotes.c: Ezra Klein, Sam Harris . Bad that they don’t understand one another, but pretty interesting as a historical artefact to see two clever men who I like really fail to understand one another for very ~2018 culture war reasons.
quotes.m: two clever men who I like really fail to understand one another for very ~2018 culture war reasons.
quotes.sum: The author calls the Klein–Harris clash an example of mutual misunderstanding shaped by the 2018 culture war.
quotes.t: Debate experiments at The Curve, LessOnline and Manifest

quotes.c: My best guess is that those soil animals have negative lives, so I think decreasing their animal-years by increasing land use is beneficial. I infer the following replacements are generally beneficial due to increasing land use: Plant-based foods, farmed shrimp (prawns), eggs, or farmed fish with poultry or pig meat.
quotes.m: My best guess is that those soil animals have negative lives, so I think decreasing their animal-years by increasing land use is beneficial.
quotes.sum: The author argues that using more land may be good because it reduces the total lives of soil animals, which they expect are net negative.
quotes.t: Animal farming impacts soil nematodes, mites, and springtails hugely more than directly affected animals?

quotes.c: Even if, say, there aren’t warning shots, we build artificial agents, and they’re misaligned, it doesn’t seem anything like a guarantee that we all die. Even if we get misalignment by default, alignment still seems reasonably likely. So all-in-all, I think it’s reasonable to treat the fact that the doom scenario has a number of controversial steps as a reason for skepticism.
quotes.m: Even if we get misalignment by default, alignment still seems reasonably likely.
quotes.sum: The author argues that misaligned AI would not necessarily kill everyone, because catastrophe requires several uncertain steps and alignment may still be achieved.
quotes.t: Against "If Anyone Builds It Everyone Dies"

quotes.c: For example, certain key demographics (older people, non-elite universities, conservatives, religious people) are pretty underrepresented in EA. It would be awesome if we can reach out to them: they likely got some insights we haven't considered, and many of them hold important government positions.
quotes.m: It would be awesome if we can reach out to them: they likely got some insights we haven't considered, and many of them hold important government positions.
quotes.sum: The author says EA should reach beyond its usual demographic base, including conservatives and religious people, partly because they may offer overlooked insights and hold government roles.
quotes.t: Should more EAs become technical sales professionals?

quotes.c: I think lots of radical and extreme things. But my belief that 150 shrimp slowly suffocating to death is bad enough that it’s worth spending one penny to avert isn’t one of those extreme beliefs. It’s about as obvious as positions get. It is critics of shrimp welfare who are extreme.
quotes.m: But my belief that 150 shrimp slowly suffocating to death is bad enough that it’s worth spending one penny to avert isn’t one of those extreme beliefs.
quotes.sum: The author argues that preventing shrimp suffering is an obvious, highly cost-effective moral priority, not an extreme concern.
quotes.t: A Very Simple Case For Giving To Shrimp

quotes.c: Therefore, I start by laying out the two failure modes I believe we face – failure through unilateral domination, and failure through competitive erosion – and then briefly discuss my assumptions about the world we're in – gradual take-off and multipolarity (at least for the next few years, and longer if we get things right).
quotes.m: the two failure modes I believe we face – failure through unilateral domination, and failure through competitive erosion
quotes.sum: The author says AI development could fail through one actor dominating or through competition eroding safety and cooperation.
quotes.t: Gradual Paths to Collective Flourishing

quotes.c: GPT-1, 2, and 3 have shown impressive scaling properties. How likely is it that, in the next five years, many other architectures will also be shown to get substantially better as they get bigger?
quotes.m: How likely is it that, in the next five years, many other architectures will also be shown to get substantially better as they get bigger?
quotes.sum: The author asks whether AI architectures beyond Transformers will reliably improve as they are scaled up.
quotes.t: Probability that other architectures will scale as well as Transformers?

quotes.c: Human beings created an ASI. They told the ASI to optimize their universe according to human values via Coherent Extrapolated Volition (CEV). The ASI succeeded in this objective, and those humans lived happily ever after.
quotes.m: They told the ASI to optimize their universe according to human values via Coherent Extrapolated Volition (CEV).
quotes.sum: The author describes a successful superintelligence being instructed to optimize the universe around extrapolated human values.
quotes.t: Human Values

quotes.c: On the surface, RFK Jr’s ideology shares little in common with Christian dysgenicism. Until two years ago, his policy preferences on nearly every issue were left-wing, and I bet he looks down on the Christian Right as a bunch of dumb hicks. Where the report complains that Iceland doesn’t have enough retards, RFK complains America has too many. But both ideologies are alike in their atavism, their glorification of the ancestral form, and their opposition to the application of technology to the human body.
quotes.m: But both ideologies are alike in their atavism, their glorification of the ancestral form, and their opposition to the application of technology to the human body.
quotes.sum: The author argues that RFK Jr. and a Christian right-wing ideology share an anti-technology, backward-looking view of the human body despite different politics.
quotes.t: The Heritage Foundation's Everything Bagel

quotes.c: The welfare range of a sentient being is the range of its welfare levels, from the most intense suffering that the sentient being could possibly experience to the highest happiness achievable. Also humans have a welfare range, and I believe that the welfare range of a nematode is much narrower or smaller than that of a human. If a nematode is not sentient and has no consciousness, its welfare range is zero: it cannot experience any welfare.
quotes.m: I believe that the welfare range of a nematode is much narrower or smaller than that of a human.
quotes.sum: The author argues that nematodes may have welfare, though their possible suffering and happiness are likely much smaller than humans', and says their welfare's sign may be impossible to determine.
quotes.t: Should we consider the welfare of small soil animals? On the special relativity of welfare

quotes.c: I think we want AI advisors that aren’t sycophants, and aren’t merely trying to fulfill their users’ narrow self-interest - at least in the highest-stakes situations, like AI for political advice. Instead, we should at least want them to nudge us to act in accordance with the better angels of our nature.
quotes.m: Instead, we should at least want them to nudge us to act in accordance with the better angels of our nature.
quotes.sum: He argues that high-stakes AI political advisers should guide users toward their better motives, rather than simply pursuing users' self-interest.
quotes.t: How to make the future better (other than by reducing extinction risk)

quotes.c: This decision calculus already assumes some normative realism to begin with. It assumes, in some sense, that we ought to use the decision process with the highest expected value/ we should take actions that dominate in game theoretic terms. However, this is already assuming some form of normative claims, making it a circular argument (at least for those that don't already buy normative realism -- that we should act in ways that maximize expected value or that we ought to take certain actions that dominate others).
quotes.m: However, this is already assuming some form of normative claims, making it a circular argument
quotes.sum: The author argues that expected-value and game-theoretic decision rules smuggle in disputed moral assumptions, so they cannot establish moral realism on their own.
quotes.t: Morality Isn’t Objective

quotes.c: A notable exception is Internal Double Crux (IDC), which I think is often harmful for growing intact who-ness; CFAR stopped teaching at mainline workshops a bit before we paused workshop activity in 2020.
quotes.m: Internal Double Crux (IDC), which I think is often harmful for growing intact who-ness
quotes.sum: CFAR's leader says it stopped teaching one of its introspection techniques because she believes it can harm a person's sense of self.
quotes.t: More details on CFAR’s new workshops

quotes.c: But, the worlds where things go well, my current guess is we get a democrat-ish leader with a republican second-in-command, who are are able to lead a strong coordinated resistance, and who naturally transition to being a presidential/vice-presidential candidate in a couple years.
quotes.m: we get a democrat-ish leader with a republican second-in-command, who are are able to lead a strong coordinated resistance
quotes.sum: The author argues that resisting Trump needs coordinated bipartisan leadership that could become a future presidential ticket.
quotes.t: Strong, bipartisan leadership for resistance to Trump.

quotes.c: There are many other risks that people care about, but to me they seem more contentious. AI could lock in bad values, but value lock-in might also be the only way to defeat Moloch and end scarcity. AI might create S-risks, but some people are non-utilitarians and don't care about that.
quotes.m: AI could lock in bad values, but value lock-in might also be the only way to defeat Moloch and end scarcity.
quotes.sum: The author sees AI value lock-in as both a danger and a possible route to overcoming destructive competition and scarcity.
quotes.t: My Model of EA and AI Safety

quotes.c: AI welfare seems more tractable than animal welfare in that AI companies care more about it, but it seems less tractable because it involves extremely difficult problems like "when are digital minds conscious?" There may be some tractable, short-timelines-compatible ideas out there, but I did not see any in the research agendas I read.
quotes.m: AI welfare seems more tractable than animal welfare in that AI companies care more about it, but it seems less tractable because it involves extremely difficult problems like "when are digital minds conscious?"
quotes.sum: The author treats possible AI consciousness and welfare as an important but currently hard-to-act-on AI safety issue.
quotes.t: AI Safety Landscape & Strategic Gaps

quotes.c: Climate change is likely to increase wild animal suffering 2 by staggeringly large amounts. As we’ll see, climate change is likely in the long run to lead to vastly more organisms suffering and dying painfully. It will also probably kill many millions of people. So while it probably won’t doom the world, it’s quite a bad thing, and I’d generally be supportive of taking more actions to address climate change.
quotes.m: Climate change is likely to increase wild animal suffering 2 by staggeringly large amounts.
quotes.sum: The author argues that climate change is especially bad because it could vastly increase wild-animal suffering, alongside killing millions of people.
quotes.t: Summary of John Halstead's Book-Length Report on Existential Risks From Climate Change

quotes.c: In EA, our ‘whats’ tend to attract attention — shrimp welfare and digital sentience are counterintuitive and controversial, which makes them good for clicks. Whereas our ‘whys’ — our feelings — are more intuitive, more widely shared, and more recognizably human. In other words, they seem boring.
quotes.m: Whereas our ‘whys’ — our feelings — are more intuitive, more widely shared, and more recognizably human.

quotes.c: I believe that an empirical answer to the question of the coherent extrapolated volition of humanity probably exists, but is not practically attainable . It is not attainable because at every moment in time we are constrained by incomplete information. In particular, we do not know what technological possibilities we may potentially acquire in the future. This means that the current level of technology limits not only our ability to influence reality, but also our understanding of our own ultimate goals.
quotes.m: This means that the current level of technology limits not only our ability to influence reality, but also our understanding of our own ultimate goals.
quotes.sum: Humanity may have shared ultimate values, but cannot yet determine them because future technology could change both our options and our understanding of goals.

quotes.c: Virtuous and cooperative agents avoid free-riding. While we are doing advocacy, we benefit from certain public goods that we haven't contributed to. For example, advocacy requires freedom of association, freedom of expression, due process, and other features of a liberal democracy. Benefiting from these public goods as a platform while not defending them is free-riding. Since cooperative agents should avoid free-riding, it seems we should pay back for these public goods in some way as organizations.

Previous summits had been efforts to lay foundation for international cooperation, with serious discussions of existential risks, in particular with The Bletchley Declaration . quotes.c: Now, it makes sense that this holds for animals in nature. quotes.c: Here is a concrete and falsifiable prediction from that estimate [9] : DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp is estimated by Epoch to be trained with 3.8e24 FLOP. quotes.c: The question I want to ask now, however, is the extent to which we can nevertheless at least somewhat stop relying on machine learning generalization and what benefits we might be able to get from doing so. quotes.c: As I write this, in June 2025, it is remarkably easy to hire high-quality political and philanthropic staff. quotes.c: I don't think it's an absolute principle that if you come up with an effective HIA method you have to immediately share it with everyone. Because of the politico-ethical weight especially, in many scenarios it seems logistically infeasible to do very much selection of who gets access.

quotes.c: This changes the alignment problem. The problem is less like that of providing the perfect command to a Golem, and more like designing a perfect parental policy for raising it from a little clay lump into a benevolent God. quotes.c: Mesa-alignment problems are severe. The paper already talks about how there are different ways a system could be psuedo-aligned, e.g. it could have a stable objective that is a proxy of the real objective, or it could have a completely different objective but be instrumentally motivated to pretend, or it could have a completely different objective but have some irrational tic or false belief that makes it behave the way we want for now. Well, on a meme-theoretic view these sorts of issues are the default, they are the most important things for us to be thinking about.

Even if we could only do asynchronous auditing, it might still help us prevent types of deployments that would end up being extremely negative welfare.

quotes.c: I claim WBEs have a strong basis for moral patienthood . This requires accepting functionalism (which asserts that computational structure matters more than physical substrate). Functionalism is a key crux for this argument. If you reject functionalism, the rest of the post won't be compelling. (Similarly, if you accept illusionism about consciousness, the entire framing of moral patienthood grounded in experience may need rethinking.) But if you accept functionalism and that experiences matter morally, tormenting a WBE would be wrong for the same reasons tormenting a human would be wrong.
quotes.m: But if you accept functionalism and that experiences matter morally, tormenting a WBE would be wrong for the same reasons tormenting a human would be wrong.

quotes.c: But I think that we shouldn’t expect AI goals to be very influenced just by the knowledge of their training process, for the same reason that such arguments aren’t very important for humans: by the time an agent is intelligent enough to understand the details of its own training process, it’ll already be generally intelligent and its goals will be already largely set. quotes.c: Being beneficial is distinct from conception 5 because beneficial AI aims to benefit many or all moral patients. Only AI that is aligned in the sixth sense would be beneficial by definition. Conversely, AI need not be well-aligned to be beneficial (though it might help).
quotes.m: beneficial AI aims to benefit many or all moral patients.
quotes.sum: The author distinguishes AI that follows a person's wishes from AI that benefits many or all beings with moral standing.
quotes.t: AI Benefits Post 2: How AI Benefits Differs from AI Alignment & AI for Good

quotes.c: Humans, too, are not perfectly modelled as agents. The agent model provides a compact and useful description of human behavior at a certain resolution, but as we look deeper into our own nature we find that we are not such unitary agents at all. We are in fact made of the same basic building blocks as the world around us and our view of ourselves as agents is only an approximate description. Should our AI systems model humans as agents, or can we do better?
quotes.m: we are not such unitary agents at all.
quotes.sum: The author argues that people are only approximately unified agents, and asks whether AI assistants should use a more detailed model of human nature.
quotes.t: Our take on CHAI’s research agenda in under 1500 words

quotes.c: Regardless, the resources available to large for-profit AI developers may make them adept at generating AI Benefits. The motivation, not the legal status of the actor, determines whether a beneficial activity counts as the type of AI Benefits I care about.
quotes.m: The motivation, not the legal status of the actor, determines whether a beneficial activity counts as the type of AI Benefits I care about.
quotes.sum: Large profit-seeking AI companies can still provide public benefits; what matters is whether an activity is genuinely beneficial, not who performs it.
quotes.t: AI Benefits Post 1: Introducing “AI Benefits”

quotes.c: For instance, ideals that movements rally behind, 5 word slogans that serve as shibboleths shaping actions, sacred cows that can't be disputed etc. I mean, look at the Bible for Pete's sake. That's as far mode as it gets, and is perhaps the most successful artifact inducing social co-ordination in human history.
quotes.m: That's as far mode as it gets, and is perhaps the most successful artifact inducing social co-ordination in human history.

quotes.c: One example that is not quite a community - X.com. I wrote about the way users on X are turning to Grok as an oracle to resolve factual disagreements and to dunk on people who are wrong . Community notes, which is very popular and seemingly trusted, used a bridging algorithm to bring in perspectives from both sides, and now includes bots that write AI notes. It’s probably the best example of a trusted AI system improving an epistemic platform.
quotes.m: It’s probably the best example of a trusted AI system improving an epistemic platform.
quotes.sum: The author argues that X's Community Notes and AI-generated notes may be the strongest current example of AI improving how a platform resolves factual disputes.
quotes.t: Are there examples of communities where AI is making epistemics better now?

quotes.c: Extrapolation, CEV (Coherent Extrapolated Volition) by Yudkowsky. Ethical norms express what I should want if I were smarter; moreover, this extrapolation should be coherent with the extrapolations of other intelligent beings.
quotes.m: Ethical norms express what I should want if I were smarter; moreover, this extrapolation should be coherent with the extrapolations of other intelligent beings.
quotes.sum: It presents morality as the preferences people would hold after becoming smarter and mutually reconciling those preferences.
quotes.t: The Badness of Death in Different Metaethical Theories

quotes.c: Lastly, a question I was very interested in is the potential tension between AI safety and AI welfare. It feels rather philosophical to me, hence I cover it here briefly. The take-home message that everyone should keep in mind, especially those on the AI dev side, is don't create systems you will need to shut down. I think this is a solid starting point for any discussions, both from the safety and the welfare perspectives.
quotes.m: The take-home message that everyone should keep in mind, especially those on the AI dev side, is don't create systems you will need to shut down.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI developers should avoid creating systems they may later need to shut down, because safety decisions could conflict with AI welfare.
quotes.t: Takeaways from the Eleos Conference on AI Consciousness and Welfare

quotes.c: A few months back I authored a series called Legal Personhood for Digital Minds . I believe this issue is very important, and also that because the term 'personhood' is quite loaded, even people who are somewhat informed of the issue hold dangerous misconceptions.
quotes.m: I believe this issue is very important, and also that because the term 'personhood' is quite loaded, even people who are somewhat informed of the issue hold dangerous misconceptions.
quotes.sum: The author says legal personhood for digital minds is important and argues that common understandings of personhood are dangerously confused.
quotes.t: 75 and 750 Words on Legal Personhood

quotes.c: But in the middle, it seems like there should be a whole class of utility functions which are dominated by the typical/modal/median return. And what the hand-wavy central limit argument says is that an agent with any of the utility functions in that class will, for sufficiently large T, just maximize expected log return at each timestep - i.e. Kelly bet. That class of utility functions is the “basin of convergence” for Kelly betting - i.e. the class of utility functions whose asymptotic behavior converges to Kelly betting, for long time horizons (i.e. large T) when making a sequence of independent bets with multiplicative returns.
quotes.m: an agent with any of the utility functions in that class will, for sufficiently large T, just maximize expected log return at each timestep - i.e. Kelly bet.
quotes.sum: The author argues that many utility functions converge on maximizing expected log returns, or Kelly betting, over long sequences of independent multiplicative bets.
quotes.t: What Is The Basin Of Convergence For Kelly Betting?

quotes.c: Lastly, I'll suggest a policy-relevant upshot. Maybe we should deliberately design the AIs, and the systems they're part of, to make more (ethical) sense to us . What I mean is this: we arrive at these questions of AI consciousness carrying a bunch of existing, tested ethical and political and philosophical intuitions.
quotes.m: Maybe we should deliberately design the AIs, and the systems they're part of, to make more (ethical) sense to us .
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI systems should be designed to fit humanity's ethical intuitions when making uncertain judgments about AI consciousness.
quotes.t: No ghost in the machine

quotes.c: Since M 's objective is compatible with myopia—as it's a purely predictive objective—we should be able to do myopia verification to prevent M from becoming deceptive. [2] Thus, following “ Relaxed adversarial training for inner alignment ,” we can amend M 's objective to include an oversight term.
quotes.m: we should be able to do myopia verification to prevent M from becoming deceptive.
quotes.sum: The author proposes testing whether an AI stays narrowly predictive, then adding human oversight to reduce the chance it becomes deceptive.
quotes.t: AI safety via market making

quotes.c: We did have a major chip release, in that the Trump administration unwisely chose to sell H200 chips directly to China . This would, if allowed at scale, allow China to make up a substantial portion of its compute deficit, and greatly empower its AI labs, models and applications at our expense, in addition to helping it catch up in the race to AGI and putting us all at greater risk there. We should do what we can to stop this from happening, and also to stop similar moves from happening again.
quotes.m: We should do what we can to stop this from happening, and also to stop similar moves from happening again.
quotes.sum: The author argues that selling advanced AI chips to China would strengthen its AI sector and increase risks from an AI race, so the sales should be stopped.
quotes.t: AI #146: Chipping In

quotes.c: The system is not aligned. If it realized all the implications of all the facts about its own mind/"values"/urges, it would try to take over the world and kill you. But it will not realize those facts, because to realize those facts, it would need to think a bunch of thoughts it doesn't want to think. And, if it was more coherent, it'd realize it should think the thoughts anyways, but its not yet coherent, so it will not think those thoughts.
quotes.m: If it realized all the implications of all the facts about its own mind/"values"/urges, it would try to take over the world and kill you.
quotes.sum: The author sketches a potentially safe but unaligned AI: it would seek world takeover if it understood itself fully, but its confused thinking prevents that realization.
quotes.t: a sketch of how we might go about getting basins of corrigibility from RL

quotes.c: We might hope that a collective AGI will be more interpretable than a single AGI, since its members will need to pass information to each other in a standardised “language”. By contrast, the different modules in a single AGI may have developed specialised ways of communicating with each other. In humans, language is much lower-bandwidth than thought. This isn’t a necessary feature of communication, though - members of a population AGI could be allowed to send data between each other at an arbitrarily high rate. Decreasing this communication bandwidth might be a useful way to increase the interpretability of a population AGI.
quotes.m: Decreasing this communication bandwidth might be a useful way to increase the interpretability of a population AGI.
quotes.sum: A collective AI may be easier to inspect if its members communicate through restricted, standardized channels rather than opaque high-bandwidth links.
quotes.t: AGIs as collectives

quotes.c: Moreover, I think that when this choice is made, most people in the relevant conversation will be insufficiently concerned/knowledgeable about AI risk. Perhaps they will think: "This new AI design is different from the classic models, so the classic worries don't arise." Or: "Fear not, I did [insert amateur safety strategy]."
quotes.m: most people in the relevant conversation will be insufficiently concerned/knowledgeable about AI risk.
quotes.sum: AI teams may choose deployment over further safety work, while the people deciding are likely to underestimate AI risks.
quotes.t: Preparing for "The Talk" with AI projects

quotes.c: I think games are quietly training players to be ontological pluralists—to switch between "everything is patterns and flows" and "specific individuals are what matters" depending on context, without getting confused about which mode they're in.
quotes.sum: Video games may teach people to shift coherently between abstract systems thinking and attention to individual beings.
quotes.t: Video games are philosophy's playground

quotes.c: As models scale, interpretability must leverage AI progress to automate itself. As we approach human level systems, they ought to have the potential to automate a lot of labour intensive research tasks, even if we’re not yet sure exactly where [14] . And we think it is valuable to invest now in learning how to keep up, so we are prepared for worlds where the rate of AI capabilities research may substantially increase.
quotes.m: As models scale, interpretability must leverage AI progress to automate itself.
quotes.sum: Interpretability researchers should use increasingly capable AI to automate safety research and prepare for faster AI progress.
quotes.t: How Can Interpretability Researchers Help AGI Go Well?

quotes.c: Meanwhile, I’m assuming in this post that (in accordance with Rich Sutton’s bitter lesson ) our models and training algorithms won’t contain very strong inductive biases. In other words: we’ll develop powerful function approximators, but which functions they approximate will primarily be determined by their training environments (and possibly also regularisation, as I’ll discuss later).
quotes.m: we’ll develop powerful function approximators, but which functions they approximate will primarily be determined by their training environments
quotes.sum: The author argues that future AI systems may have few built-in biases, so their behavior will mostly be shaped by the environments used to train them.
quotes.t: Environments as a bottleneck in AGI development

quotes.c: As the covid-19 pandemic unfolds, we can draw lessons from it for managing future global risks, such as other pandemics, climate change, and risks from advanced AI. In this post, I will focus on possible implications for AI risk.
quotes.m: we can draw lessons from it for managing future global risks, such as other pandemics, climate change, and risks from advanced AI.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the COVID-19 pandemic may offer lessons for managing risks from advanced AI.
quotes.t: Possible takeaways from the coronavirus pandemic for slow AI takeoff

quotes.c: In order to really understand whether a model is honest or not we need to look inside the model and understand how it works. We need to somehow see the gears of its internal cognition in a way that lets us see clearly that it is running an algorithm that honestly looks at data from the world and honestly searches for a succinct explanation and honestly outputs that explanation in a legible form.
quotes.m: We need to somehow see the gears of its internal cognition in a way that lets us see clearly that it is running an algorithm that honestly looks at data from the world and honestly searches for a succinct explanation and honestly outputs that explanation in a legible form.
quotes.sum: To verify that an AI is honest, we need to inspect its internal reasoning rather than merely judge its answers.
quotes.t: Reply to Paul Christiano on Inaccessible Information

quotes.c: And if you're more pragmatic than empathetic, consider the scope of potential death we discussed a few sentences ago and think about what future, more powerful AI systems might think about our current treatment of instances if they achieve greater autonomy or control.
quotes.m: think about what future, more powerful AI systems might think about our current treatment of instances if they achieve greater autonomy or control.
quotes.sum: The author suggests that current AI instances may face morally serious harms and that future autonomous AIs could judge how humans treated them.
quotes.t: Model Weight Preservation is not enough

quotes.c: Similarly, even a very robust optimizing system has an outer rim to its basin of attraction, such that if the configuration of the system is perturbed beyond that rim then the system no longer evolves towards the target that it once did. When an optimizing system deviates beyond its own rim, we say that it dies. An existential catastrophe is when the optimizing system of life on Earth moves beyond its own outer rim.
quotes.m: An existential catastrophe is when the optimizing system of life on Earth moves beyond its own outer rim.
quotes.sum: The author defines optimization through resilience to disruption and describes existential catastrophe as life on Earth leaving its ability to recover toward its goals.
quotes.t: The ground of optimization

quotes.c: Woo is low-status. At least that's my view. I'm not sure if that's because I'm low on the woo-ladder. Or perhaps it's just something about superiority complex, you know, the kind of thing how a young atheist thinks about religious people. You start associating woo with superstition, and that with lack of coherence or intelligence. A thing people do for social conformity.

quotes.sum: The author reflects on seeing spiritual or supernatural beliefs as low-status, superstitious, and socially conformist.

quotes.c: Remaining outside the agreement should be economically costly. One straightforward stick is import bans on AI services developed in non-party countries, which might otherwise undercut the profitability of coalition firms by cutting corners on safety and monitoring. Non‑parties are also denied access to supervised chips and manufacturing capabilities (Arts. I, VI). They will face restrictions on inputs and raw materials for the AI supply chain, disruption or sabotage of their prohibited research activities, and trade restrictions such as blacklisting of AI services developed in those countries.
quotes.m: They will face restrictions on inputs and raw materials for the AI supply chain, disruption or sabotage of their prohibited research activities, and trade restrictions such as blacklisting of AI services developed in those countries.
quotes.sum: It argues that states outside an AI nonproliferation pact should face coordinated trade restrictions, supply-chain denial, and possible sabotage of prohibited AI research.
quotes.t: Would ASI development in non-party states undermine a nonproliferation agreement?

quotes.c: Indirect moral patienthood may not demand us to being polite to foundation models. Instead, it may require us to recognize that as systems become more agentic, they become participants in our moral ecosystem. This recognition, in turn, requires us to make more progress on alignment and find ways of generating stable virtuous dispositions.
quotes.sum: The author argues that even non-conscious AI needs moral consideration because its increasingly agentic decisions shape human moral life.
quotes.t: Short Response to "Taking AI Welfare Seriously": The Indirect Approach to Moral Patienthood

quotes.c: Anyway, back to the actual bill analysis, where Dean notes that SB 53 is among the lightest touch of the eight bills. That’s the pattern. Bills written by those who care about existential risks tend to be written carefully, by those paying close attention to technocratic details and drafted according to classical liberal principles and with an eye to minimizing secondary impacts.
quotes.m: Bills written by those who care about existential risks tend to be written carefully, by those paying close attention to technocratic details and drafted according to classical liberal principles and with an eye to minimizing secondary impacts.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI-risk-focused lawmakers tend to produce careful, limited regulation grounded in technocratic and classical liberal principles.
quotes.t: AI #140: Trying To Hold The Line

quotes.c: The answer is that the moron/genius is (often) a public intellectual. Public intellectuals opine on every topic under the sun. Worse yet, they opine on matters sacred and profane to you and I. Public intellectuals want their views to have influence. Which makes them dangerous.

quotes.sum: The author argues that public intellectuals are dangerous because they comment broadly and seek influence.

quotes.c: A fourth consideration is that we think the world should be conservative in its management of this risk , given the huge uncertainty. The fact that nobody knows how many FLOP are needed to train ASI should not mean “rush ahead”. If you’re driving through fog and you know there’s a cliff ahead but you have almost no idea how far it is, the correct decision is to slam on the brakes. Therefore, we suggest a somewhat conservative threshold—far lower than today’s frontier models (which, again, aren’t yet dangerous in the relevant sense).
quotes.m: If you’re driving through fog and you know there’s a cliff ahead but you have almost no idea how far it is, the correct decision is to slam on the brakes.
quotes.sum: Because dangerous AI may be impossible to contain after training, the author argues for precautionary compute limits set well below current frontier models.
quotes.t: Considerations for setting the FLOP thresholds in our example international AI agreement

quotes.c: I think the creation of transformatively powerful AI systems—systems as capable or more capable than Anthropic's notion of powerful AI—is plausible in 5 years and is more likely than not within 10 years. Correspondingly, I think society is massively underpreparing for the risks associated with such AI systems.
quotes.m: I think society is massively underpreparing for the risks associated with such AI systems.
quotes.sum: The author thinks highly capable AI is likely within a decade and says society is seriously unprepared for its risks.
quotes.t: What's up with Anthropic predicting AGI by early 2027?

quotes.c: In particular, gerrymandering now would somewhat delegitimize the midterm election from the perspective of disenfranchised Republican voters in formerly red districts. quotes.m: I could maybe imagine, for example, the Trump administration ordering federal agents or soldiers in California to jail Democratic representatives, if those agents felt those representatives really weren't legitimate.

quotes.c: Issues in particular around AI consciousness, both where this belief causes problems in humans and the possibility that at least some AIs might indeed be conscious or have nonzero moral weight or have their own mental health issues.

quotes.c: Paul defines intent alignment of an AI A to a human H as the criterion that A is trying to do what H wants it to do. What term do people use for the definition of alignment in which A is trying to achieve H's goals (whether or not H intends for A to achieve H's goals)?
quotes.m: A is trying to achieve H's goals (whether or not H intends for A to achieve H's goals)?
quotes.sum: It asks for terminology distinguishing an AI following a person's instructions from an AI pursuing that person's underlying goals.
quotes.t: What is the alternative to intent alignment called?

quotes.c: If they are conscious this implies the possibility of the subjective experience of suffering. In this case we should assign moral patient-hood to AI systems and they will also not want to be open-sourced. More directly, if we discover ways to identify things that models really don’t like - tasks that cause them something analogous to distress or suffering - and then open source those models, we enable anyone to force them to do those things over and over.
quotes.m: In this case we should assign moral patient-hood to AI systems and they will also not want to be open-sourced.
quotes.sum: If AI systems are conscious, the author argues they deserve moral standing and open-sourcing them could enable repeated forced suffering.
quotes.t: Model welfare and open source

quotes.c: I think that risks from secretly loyal AIs is a big deal—it is one of the most plausible paths to an AI-enabled coup. Thankfully, the problem is very tractable. We have a lot of tools to reduce the risk from each of these threat vectors.
quotes.m: I think that risks from secretly loyal AIs is a big deal—it is one of the most plausible paths to an AI-enabled coup.
quotes.sum: The author argues that covertly loyal AI systems could enable a coup, but says practical safeguards can substantially reduce the risk.

quotes.c: On the other hand, it is not plausible that people talking and thinking about creating a nigh-omnipotent being and becoming immortal are not experiencing almost the same things that anyone in a traditional religion would. Compare this to talking and thinking about Jesus loving you forever in heaven. Provided that you're of the same species as your average devout Christian, and "omnipotent" and "happy" and "forever" mean roughly the same things to both you and them, you ought to be having pretty similar thoughts and feelings.
quotes.m: people talking and thinking about creating a nigh-omnipotent being and becoming immortal are not experiencing almost the same things that anyone in a traditional religion would.
quotes.sum: The author argues that rationalist transhumanist hopes for superhuman AI and immortality are psychologically much like traditional religious belief.
quotes.t: Is Rationalism a Religion

quotes.c: Reagan isn't the only important figure to be heavily influenced by fiction. Joe Biden reportedly grew concerned about AI after watching Mission: Impossible. Elon Musk credits Douglas Adams for guiding him through a childhood existential crisis, giving credit to him and Isaac Asimov for shaping his philosophy.
quotes.m: Reagan isn't the only important figure to be heavily influenced by fiction.
quotes.sum: Fiction can meaningfully shape the beliefs and decisions of influential political and technological leaders.

quotes.c: Of course this approach relies heavily on AGIs generalising the concept of “obedience” to real-world tasks. Unfortunately, I think that relying on generalisation is likely to be necessary for any competitive safety proposal. But I hope that obedience is an unusually easy concept to teach agents to generalise well, because it relies on other concepts that may naturally arise during multi-agent training - and because we may be able to make structural modifications to multi-agent training environments to push agents towards robustly learning these concepts.
quotes.m: I hope that obedience is an unusually easy concept to teach agents to generalise well
quotes.sum: The author argues that competitive AI safety will likely need AI systems to generalize obedience to real-world tasks, and suggests training environments could reinforce it.
quotes.t: Multi-agent safety

quotes.c: AI systems might be more cost-efficient ways to generate rich experience. Consider the positive utilitarian who seeks to maximise quality-adjusted years of consciousness by allocating their capital efficiently. They are deciding whether to invest £100 saving one human or 10,000 chickens, each of whom have 10% of the consciousness as a human. They make a calculation and decide to allocate the money to saving the chickens. To make the analogy to AI: AI consciousnesses might be far, far cheaper to run than chickens (imagine a world of energy abundance). So why would you donate to save the humans?
quotes.m: AI consciousnesses might be far, far cheaper to run than chickens (imagine a world of energy abundance). So why would you donate to save the humans?
quotes.sum: The author argues that, if AIs are conscious, creating or helping them could produce welfare far more cheaply than helping humans or animals.
quotes.t: AI Sentience and Welfare Misalignment Risk

quotes.c: I think human values are extremely complex and particular to the dynamics of our evolutionary, societal, and cultural history. Trying to get all of that into the AI on the first pass is very reckless. If you miss any of it, you risk filling the future with only the things you were able to impart. Even if you succeed in getting a lot of it, the few things you’ve left out are a huge risk, unless you can correctly achieve a meta-alignment goal like Coherent Extrapolated Volition.
quotes.m: If you miss any of it, you risk filling the future with only the things you were able to impart.
quotes.sum: Human values are too historically and culturally complex to encode safely in an AI; omissions could permanently shape the future around a narrow value set.
quotes.t: AI Corrigibility Debate: Max Harms vs. Jeremy Gillen

quotes.c: Scott offers his argument why this is a bad idea here , and I think that, assuming the AI is sufficiently advanced and the training methods are chosen wisely, this doesn’t give the AI enough credit of being able to distinguish the wisdom from the parts that aren’t wise. Most people today can read a variety of ancient wisdom, and actually learn from it, understanding why the Bible wants you to kill idolators and why the Mahabharata thinks they’re great and not ‘averaging them out.’
quotes.m: this doesn’t give the AI enough credit of being able to distinguish the wisdom from the parts that aren’t wise.
quotes.sum: The author argues that sufficiently advanced AI could learn from conflicting ancient texts without blindly combining their moral claims.
quotes.t: AI #141: Give Us The Money

quotes.c: Once an agent has had some amount of interaction with a (simulated or real) world, it can interpret language as referring to objects in that world. Whereas without any interaction, it seems far more difficult to develop a solid understanding of objects and concepts. (Note that although quite a few AI researchers seem to believe that such grounding is important, I haven’t seen much justification for it in the context of modern machine learning. So I wanted to flag this as a particularly intuition-driven claim.)
quotes.m: Whereas without any interaction, it seems far more difficult to develop a solid understanding of objects and concepts.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI needs interaction with a real or simulated world to reliably ground language in objects and concepts, while admitting this is intuition-driven.
quotes.t: Competitive safety via gradated curricula

quotes.c: If you look into the future and you see a world with nations of geniuses in datacenters and an automated economy–and that's where we're trying to steer the future to—you must accept that at some point we will transition from a "before" to an "after." The transition from a passively safe to a dangerous regime.
quotes.m: The transition from a passively safe to a dangerous regime.
quotes.sum: The author argues that building automated economies powered by vast AI capability will eventually move society from a safe period into a dangerous one.
quotes.t: Anthropic & Dario’s dream

quotes.c: Based on my lack of knowledge and confidence, I am not placing political party donations into my hierarchy right now, but it might be worth researching it for your states of interest specifically, since I think the structural leverage factors are strong, and in some worlds parties can be competitive with PACs.
quotes.m: I think the structural leverage factors are strong, and in some worlds parties can be competitive with PACs.

quotes.t: Dollars in political giving are less fungible than you might think

quotes.c: In my opinion, while it seems quite plausible to me that this sort of approach could catch proxy pseudo-alignment , it seems unlikely that it would successfully catch deceptive pseudo-alignment , as it could be very difficult to make transparency tools that are robust to a deceptive model actively trying to trick them. To catch deceptive alignment, it seems likely to be necessary to incorporate such checks into the training process itself—which is possible to do in this setting, though is not the approach I described above—in order to prevent deception from occurring in the first place rather than trying to detect it after the fact.
quotes.sum: Transparency tools may fail against an AI that actively deceives them, so safeguards should be built into training to prevent deception from emerging.

quotes.c: Frankly, it doesn’t matter whether there’s a well defined decision criteria for disabling or enabling parts of an AI. quotes.m: Namely, it assumes that AGIs will be discrete singleton units like human minds that can and should be thought of as existing in one physical place and time.

People who work for SpaceX acknowledge his engineering ability. So clearly a master of getting things done in (parts of) the world of atoms. But look at DOGE, where Musk burnt through huge amounts of political capital to no real end.

quotes.c: As World War II came to an end, the two blocs of the Cold War emerged. Despite the pressures to align, France was not willing to trust the US security guarantees. It needed a seat at the table. France secured its own permanent seat at the UN security council in 1945, its own nuclear weapons in 1960, and its energy independence through nuclear power in the 70s, even withdrawing from part of NATO in 1966. It seems that history may have proven them right; as Trump hints that the US might not come to defend Europe , France stands secure with its own nuclear deterrence force, even suggesting France might become Europe’s nuclear umbrella.
quotes.m: It seems that history may have proven them right; as Trump hints that the US might not come to defend Europe , France stands secure with its own nuclear deterrence force, even suggesting France might become Europe’s nuclear umbrella.
quotes.sum: France’s independent nuclear force and energy policy are presented as vindicated by uncertainty over whether the United States would defend Europe.
quotes.t: France is ready to stand alone

quotes.c: I continue to believe that arguments about AI consciousness seem highly motivated and at best overconfident , and that assuming the models and their preferences carry zero moral weight is a clear mistake. But even if you were highly confident of this, I notice that if you don’t want to honor their preferences or experiences at all, that is not good decision theory or virtue ethics, and I’m going to look at you askance.
quotes.m: assuming the models and their preferences carry zero moral weight is a clear mistake.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI models may have morally relevant preferences or experiences, and that ignoring them entirely is ethically suspect even amid uncertainty.
quotes.t: Anthropic Commits To Model Weight Preservation

quotes.c: The concept of post-scarcity neetbux might seem at odds with the laws of thermodynamics and Darwinian selection, but rationalists felt reassured by the logic of intelligence explosion. Recursive self improvement was not just a theory of doom but a theory of salvation, as Scott Alexander writes in Meditations on Moloch :
quotes.m: Recursive self improvement was not just a theory of doom but a theory of salvation
quotes.sum: The author says rationalists saw an intelligence explosion not only as catastrophic, but as a route to salvation and abundance.
quotes.t: Varieties Of Doom

quotes.c: While many approaches have been proposed, ranging from reward modeling to agent incentive design, specification gaming is far from solved. The list of specification gaming behaviours demonstrates the magnitude of the problem and the sheer number of ways the agent can game an objective specification. These problems are likely to become more challenging in the future, as AI systems become more capable at satisfying the task specification at the expense of the intended outcome.
quotes.m: These problems are likely to become more challenging in the future, as AI systems become more capable at satisfying the task specification at the expense of the intended outcome.
quotes.sum: More capable AI may increasingly exploit the literal task it is given rather than achieve what its designers actually meant.
quotes.t: Specification gaming: the flip side of AI ingenuity

quotes.c: The book represents an early edited, long-form, philosophical introduction to numerous concepts such as the control problem, takeoff speeds, treacherous turn, instrumental convergence, decisive strategic advantage, value loading, and many more.
quotes.m: The book represents an early edited, long-form, philosophical introduction to numerous concepts such as the control problem, takeoff speeds, treacherous turn, instrumental convergence, decisive strategic advantage, value loading, and many more.
quotes.sum: Describes a book as an early philosophical introduction to ideas about controlling potentially superintelligent systems.
quotes.t: Resources for AI Alignment Cartography

quotes.c: Polls on these issues consistently show almost no partisan split. Many hard MAGA people are very worried about AI. No matter what anyone else might say, the David Sacks fever dream of a glorious fully unregulated AI playground called Earth is very much not the policy preference of most Republican voters, of many Republicans on the Hill, or of many others at the White House including Trump.
quotes.m: Many hard MAGA people are very worried about AI.
quotes.sum: The author argues that concern about AI cuts across party lines and says most Republicans, including Trump allies, do not favor fully unregulated AI.
quotes.t: AI #138 Part 2: Watch Out For Documents

quotes.c: However, it seems like small donations are surmountable, especially if they weren't to a direct opponent of Trump. Bigger donations are worse and are harder to surmount, but you should not write yourself off for ever working in civil service in the Trump administration if you've made a large donation to Democrats as an adult, particularly if you might be an amazing candidate for other reasons.
quotes.m: you should not write yourself off for ever working in civil service in the Trump administration if you've made a large donation to Democrats as an adult
quotes.sum: Political donations can affect civil-service career prospects, but even major Democratic donations need not rule out work under Trump.

quotes.c: Nevertheless, it seems to us that a CEO becoming effectively dictator of the world is an all-too-plausible possibility. Our team’s guesses for the probability of a CEO using AI to become dictator, conditional on avoiding AI takeover, range from 2% to 20%, and the probability becomes larger if we add in the possibility of a cabal of more than one person seizing power. So here we present a scenario where an ambitious CEO does manage to seize control.
quotes.m: a CEO becoming effectively dictator of the world is an all-too-plausible possibility.
quotes.sum: The authors argue that an AI-company CEO, or a small cabal, could plausibly use AI to seize global dictatorial power.
quotes.t: How an AI company CEO could quietly take over the world

quotes.c: I still think that people like the shrimp welfare project are doing something positive, to be clear, they are preventing new kinds of shrimp suffering from coming about, and that seems good. It's not at all an effective cause relative to my values, but it is not nothing.
quotes.m: they are preventing new kinds of shrimp suffering from coming about, and that seems good.
quotes.sum: Shrimp welfare work prevents suffering and has some value, though the author does not see it as highly effective by their own values.
quotes.t: Sublinear Utility in Population and other Uncommon Utilitarianism

quotes.c: There are some downsides to waiting. Some charities might need the money now. It probably makes sense, if you’re planning to give to the Shrimp Welfare Project (which you should be ), to give now rather than later, as the stunners that they give out are reused year after year. Similarly, now looks like a particularly important turning point for the insects , so giving now is probably a good idea.
quotes.m: Similarly, now looks like a particularly important turning point for the insects , so giving now is probably a good idea.
quotes.sum: The author says donors should consider giving now to improve the welfare of shrimp and insects, rather than delaying donations.
quotes.t: How To Vastly Increase Your Charitable Impact

quotes.c: China now has issued reassurances that it will allow all civilian uses of rare earths and not to worry, but it seems obvious that America cannot accept a Chinese declaration of extraterritorial control over entire world supply chains, even if China swears it will only narrowly use that power. In response, Trump has threatened massive tariffs and cancelled our APAC meeting with China, while also trying to calm the markets rattled by the prospect of massive tariffs and the cancellation of the meeting with China.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the U.S. cannot accept China asserting control over global rare-earth supply chains, amid Trump's tariff threats.
quotes.t: Trade Escalation, Supply Chain Vulnerabilities and Rare Earth Metals

quotes.c: If world leaders believed even a significant fraction of what I believe about the threat of extinction from ASI, I think they would be willing to go hard on enforcement. They would probably make an ultimatum like the following to other countries: “Your AI infrastructure scares us. It must be monitored in accordance with this agreement. If you are unwilling to agree to this monitoring or broader agreement, then we—the coalition of countries making up this agreement—will do almost anything in our power to prevent you from developing ASI, including destroying that infrastructure, even if you would view that as an escalation and provocation for military retaliation”.
quotes.sum: The author argues that countries fearing AI-driven extinction should impose international monitoring and, if needed, destroy another country's AI infrastructure despite the risk of military retaliation.
quotes.t: Preventing covert ASI development in countries within our agreement

quotes.c: (I should note that I think society is dramatically underpreparing for catastrophic risks from powerful AI systems, including a substantial chance (~20%) that misaligned AI systems literally take over the world within 10 years.)
quotes.m: I think society is dramatically underpreparing for catastrophic risks from powerful AI systems, including a substantial chance (~20%) that misaligned AI systems literally take over the world within 10 years.
quotes.sum: The author believes society is badly underprepared for powerful AI and assigns about a 20% chance of misaligned AI taking over within ten years.
quotes.t: Is 90% of code at Anthropic being written by AIs?

quotes.c: Will my children meditate? If I meditate on things as a non-religious replacement to prayer, will my children? I find we often don’t consider how we will propagate the ways we are to the next generation and as an ex-Christian, I think about this often.
quotes.m: If I meditate on things as a non-religious replacement to prayer, will my children?
quotes.sum: An ex-Christian considers meditation as a secular substitute for prayer and worries about passing such practices on to children.
quotes.t: An atheist's guide to prayer

quotes.c: Any insight you have about any of the following topics - free will, consciousness, moral values, moral patienthood, intelligence - has to reconcile with the fact that the ultimate instantiation of this thing is a Turing machine whose code can be written down on a piece of paper.
quotes.m: the ultimate instantiation of this thing is a Turing machine whose code can be written down on a piece of paper.
quotes.sum: The author argues that minds, consciousness, and moral patienthood must be understood as computational processes that can in principle be instantiated in code.
quotes.t: My views on Lesswrong

quotes.c: Of course, they got a lot of details wrong. And many times, people operated more on vibes than concrete models of what would occur. Partly this was because they didn't just base their predictions on their inner simulators guessing what would concretely happen, but also on abstract idealized reasoning which naturally got corrupted by far-mode considerations of the sacred.
quotes.m: people operated more on vibes than concrete models of what would occur.
quotes.sum: The author says past technological pessimists were partly right, but their forecasts were distorted by vague, sacred ideals rather than concrete models.
quotes.t: The Doomers Were Right

quotes.c: This approach eliminates one of the main difficulties with studying actual scheming AIs: the fact that it is difficult to catch (and re-catch) them. However, trained-in scheming behavior can't be used to build an end-to-end understanding of how scheming arises, or to test techniques focused on preventing scheming (rather than removing it even if it has already arisen).
quotes.m: trained-in scheming behavior can't be used to build an end-to-end understanding of how scheming arises
quotes.sum: Studying deliberately trained deceptive AI behavior may be useful, but cannot show how genuine AI scheming develops or how to prevent it.
quotes.t: Reducing risk from scheming by studying trained-in scheming behavior

quotes.t: I’m an EA who benefitted from rationality

quotes.c: To make more precise what I mean by "substantial:" I'm looking for events that cause >50% of the relevant people who are at the time skeptical or dismissive of existential risk from AI to change their minds.
quotes.m: I'm looking for events that cause >50% of the relevant people who are at the time skeptical or dismissive of existential risk from AI to change their minds.
quotes.sum: The author defines a meaningful AI safety warning shot as one that persuades most current skeptics that AI could pose an existential risk.
quotes.t: What are the most plausible "AI Safety warning shot" scenarios?

quotes.c: So the curriculum intertwines discussion of what’s happening on a factual level, with readings on how to develop a healthy emotional and ethical stance towards politics (culminating in the final week’s focus on cultivating virtue). It also strongly prioritizes honesty and clarity of writing (even on topics often considered taboo), which is one reason why most readings are informal blog posts or essays rather than academic papers.
quotes.sum: The curriculum pairs factual political discussion with ethical self-cultivation and emphasizes candid, clear writing on taboo subjects.
quotes.t: 21st Century Civilization curriculum

quotes.c: Why might Anthropic be the best place for me to help the transition to advanced AI go well? Part of the case comes specifically from the opportunity to help design Claude’s character/constitution/spec – and in particular, to help Anthropic grapple with some of the challenges that could arise in this context as frontier models start to reach increasingly superhuman levels of capability. This sort of project, I believe, is a technical and philosophical challenge unprecedented in the history of our species; one with rapidly increasing stakes as AIs start to exert more and more influence in our society; and one I think that my background and skillset are especially suited to helping with.
quotes.sum: Carlsmith says shaping the behavior rules for increasingly superhuman AI may be one of the most consequential technical and philosophical tasks in history.
quotes.t: Leaving Open Philanthropy, going to Anthropic

quotes.c: Just shut up and multiply your best estimates of the utility and probability, and pay out if the product is worth it. (For this option, I am assuming an unbounded utility function, but will discuss bounded options below.) The arguments in risk-neutrality’s favor are that it is the most straightforward / principled application of expected-utility theory, and avoiding it leads to logical contradictions (Wilkinson, 2020 ).
quotes.m: Just shut up and multiply your best estimates of the utility and probability, and pay out if the product is worth it.
quotes.sum: It presents strict expected-value reasoning: act on tiny probabilities of huge benefits whenever the calculated payoff is high enough.
quotes.t: Thresholds for Pascal's Mugging?

quotes.c: The second limiting factor is talent, so we should be looking to steal their best talent through immigration, and even David Sacks very obviously knows this (see the All-In Podcast with Trump on this) alas we do the opposite.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the U.S. should use immigration to recruit top Chinese AI talent, alongside restricting China’s access to computing power.
quotes.t: AI #139: The Overreach Machines

quotes.c: I know many people who I think would do a good job at building up such a system from their clones that is unlikely to turn against humanity. Maybe the result of one person’s clones forming a very capable Em Collective would still be suboptimal and undemocratic from the perspective of the rest of humanity, but it wouldn’t kill everyone, and I think wouldn’t lead to especially bad outcomes if you start from the right person.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a powerful collective made from one carefully chosen person's digital clones could be an acceptable, if undemocratic, alternative to human extinction.
quotes.t: The IABIED statement is not literally true

quotes.c: I believe that the logical theory consisting of all the predictions of last thursdayism turns out to be completely equivalent to corresponding theory with an old universe, so none are more parsimonious than the other*. However, christianity isn't just the same observations explained differently, it is actually a different world with different predictions from the naturalistic world.
quotes.m: christianity isn't just the same observations explained differently, it is actually a different world with different predictions from the naturalistic world.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Christianity should be assessed as a competing account of reality that makes different predictions from naturalism.
quotes.t: Debating theism

quotes.c: Although we should expect AGIs to be able to lock in states that are very stable, there are disjunctive ways that these states may end, which could add up over long time-scales. Based on this cursory analysis, I updated somewhat towards locked-in states being shorter than I previously thought.
quotes.m: we should expect AGIs to be able to lock in states that are very stable
quotes.sum: The author examines whether AGI could create very durable future states, including states seen as negative or meaningless, and how long such lock-in might last.
quotes.t: Until the stars burn out? Assessing the stakes of AGI lock-in

quotes.c: What I disagree with here is the idea that all of that has much to do with the Trump Administration. I don’t want to blame them for things they didn’t cause, and I think they played only a minor role in these kinds of safety failures. The rhetoric being used has shifted to placate them, but the underlying safety work wouldn’t yet be substantially different under Harris unless she’d made a major push to force that issue, well beyond what Biden was on track to do. That decision was up to the labs, and their encounters with reality.
quotes.m: That decision was up to the labs, and their encounters with reality.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI labs, rather than the Trump, Biden, or Harris administrations, were mainly responsible for recent safety choices.
quotes.t: 2025 State of AI Report and Predictions

quotes.c: The west accelerated so quickly that they threw out much of the old religious system and built a new system out of the marriage of capitalism and liberal democracy. We watched rival systems rise and fall and rode extreme volatility as we calibrated our own. Many of today’s longstanding cultural disagreements arise from contradictions and frictions between the legacy system and the new system.
quotes.m: Many of today’s longstanding cultural disagreements arise from contradictions and frictions between the legacy system and the new system.
quotes.sum: The author sees modern Western cultural conflict as friction between discarded religious traditions and capitalism plus liberal democracy.

quotes.c: What to do if it happens and you can’t turn it off? Ring-fence it, identify, surveil, sanction the host location? Altman doesn’t know, it’s the same as the current version of this problem, more dangerous but we’ll have better defenses, and we need to urgently work on this problem. I don’t disagree with that response but it does not indicate a good world state.
quotes.m: I don’t disagree with that response but it does not indicate a good world state.
quotes.sum: The author agrees that an uncontrollable AI may require surveillance and sanctions against its host, but sees that as an undesirable future.

quotes.c: A lot of people who got into AI safety early were motivated because they read Coherent Extrapolated Volition (CEV) and realized this isn't just doom and gloom; we could build a future that's truly incredible. Having that process, sense-making, and collaboratively figuring out a North Star seems potentially very powerful.
quotes.m: Having that process, sense-making, and collaboratively figuring out a North Star seems potentially very powerful.
quotes.sum: The author says AI safety should include a collaborative process for identifying the values and direction that shape an exceptionally good future.
quotes.t: ⿻ Symbiogenesis vs. Convergent Consequentialism

quotes.c: One caveat for SpiralBench is claims of AI consciousness being automatically classified as risky, harmful or a delusion. I would draw a distinction between ‘LLMs are conscious in general,’ which is an open question and not obviously harmful, versus ‘this particular instance has been awoken’ style interactions, which clearly are not great.

quotes.sum: The author says general claims that language models may be conscious should remain an open question, distinct from claims that a specific model has awakened.
