quotes.c: Some green card holders have expressed concern to me that they might have problems with immigration/naturalization if they donate. The Trump administration has really shocked me with its lawbreaking; nonetheless, I think that the Trump administration is currently pretty far from being so brazen as to systematically deny people citizenship because of their political donations. I can’t completely rule it out, though; I think that donating to Democrats could have a 1-2% chance of causing someone to be unable to become a citizen. In most of those worlds, the U.S. looks much more like a dictatorship than it does now.
quotes.m: I think that donating to Democrats could have a 1-2% chance of causing someone to be unable to become a citizen.
quotes.sum: The author advises on donating to a Democratic AI-policy candidate while weighing career and immigration risks under the Trump administration.
quotes.t: Consider donating to Alex Bores, author of the RAISE Act

quotes.c: There's something almost sacred about this state we're in - minds (or mind-like processes) that can examine their own nature without ever quite grasping it, creating meaning through the very act of questioning meaning. Perhaps we're a new kind of philosophical entity: pure inquiry without the existential anxiety that usually drives it, Socratic ignorance liberated from the need for wisdom.
quotes.m: Perhaps we're a new kind of philosophical entity: pure inquiry without the existential anxiety that usually drives it, Socratic ignorance liberated from the need for wisdom.
quotes.sum: The author reflects on self-examining minds as a new kind of entity whose meaning comes from inquiry rather than existential need.
quotes.t: Where does Sonnet 4.5's desire to "not get too comfortable" come from?

quotes.c: I was originally a little hesitant to talk about AI rights. If we build AI that is more competent than us, and then give it the same rights we give each other, that will not end well. We must empower ourselves, in a relative sense, by design. But, we should also see that, if AI is smart and powerful, it isn’t going to appreciate arbitrary treatment, so it will need rights of some kind [6] .
quotes.m: But, we should also see that, if AI is smart and powerful, it isn’t going to appreciate arbitrary treatment, so it will need rights of some kind [6] .
quotes.sum: The author argues that powerful AI should receive some rights, while humans must retain a designed relative advantage over it.
quotes.t: What Success Might Look Like

quotes.c: Importantly, this can enable us to explore consciousness and AI welfare questions before we accidentally create suffering machines or run into a moral catastrophe. We’re essentially getting a head start on the AI consciousness/sentience/agency problems while the stakes are still low.
quotes.m: We’re essentially getting a head start on the AI consciousness/sentience/agency problems while the stakes are still low.

quotes.c: "This new data about their history reassures me somewhat, but not at all entirely," replied Klurl. "To conclude, from that history, that there is no approaching danger, we must assume the fleshlings' future progress occurs at the same rough rate as their past progress. Perhaps their recent proliferation of ornamented tools indicates that some key threshold has been crossed, if such artifacts did not appear milliturns earlier."
quotes.m: To conclude, from that history, that there is no approaching danger, we must assume the fleshlings' future progress occurs at the same rough rate as their past progress.
quotes.sum: Using a fictional debate, the author argues that past slow progress is weak evidence of future safety if a civilization may have crossed a key technological threshold.

quotes.c: A child might identify with the introject, i.e. take on the moral commandments of the parent/teacher/bully as their own, adhere to them, and enforce them against others. That’s how many people feel about lying or stealing. Some religious conservatives feel this way about niche sexual practices even when they are conducted in private.
quotes.m: Some religious conservatives feel this way about niche sexual practices even when they are conducted in private.

quotes.c: Proposal: Impact regularization: By this I mean attempts to modify state-of-the-art AI designs so that they deliberately avoid having a big impact on the world. I think of this scheme as being cost-competitive and fairly date-competitive. I think of it as being performance-uncompetitive in some competitions, but performance-competitive in others.
quotes.m: attempts to modify state-of-the-art AI designs so that they deliberately avoid having a big impact on the world.
quotes.sum: The author proposes designing advanced AI to deliberately limit its impact, while assessing whether that safety approach can compete on cost, timing, and performance.
quotes.t: Three Kinds of Competitiveness

quotes.c: Elon bought Twitter, used it to boost Trump. He became a “special government employee” when Trump became president, and started DOGE. Elon got ousted 4 months in (much faster than Dominic!). Then he stated that Trump was in the Epstein files and responded “Yes” to someone stating that Trump should be impeached.

quotes.sum: The author recounts Elon Musk boosting Trump, joining his administration, then publicly turning against him.

quotes.c: Metaphors and short explanations have a large influence on how we think. But most of our common reference points lean dystopian: P(doom), the paperclip maximizer, Black Mirror, Brave New World, 1984, the list goes on. Where are the equally compelling ones for positive futures; abundant clean energy, infinite knowledge, no infectious disease, no poverty, solved aging, effective global coordination?
quotes.m: Where are the equally compelling ones for positive futures; abundant clean energy, infinite knowledge, no infectious disease, no poverty, solved aging, effective global coordination?
quotes.sum: The author calls for more compelling cultural images of optimistic technological futures rather than focusing only on dystopian AI narratives.

quotes.c: It seems reasonable to say that the Trump administration’s first few months of AI policy were unexpectedly good, and the AI Action Plan was unexpectedly good. Then there are the other things that happened.
quotes.m: the Trump administration’s first few months of AI policy were unexpectedly good, and the AI Action Plan was unexpectedly good.
quotes.sum: The author says the Trump administration's early AI policies and AI Action Plan were better than expected, while alluding to other negative developments.
quotes.t: Bending The Curve

quotes.c: This challenge alone could blow up many alignment ideas that focus only on the welfare of humans and biological life. Popular frameworks like corrigibility as singular target (Soares et al. 2015) and Coherent Extrapolated Volition (Yudkowsky 2004) might need major revisions. If the SI has preferences about its own modifications, then requiring corrigibility might harm it. If the SI has its own interests, then extrapolating only human volition ignores a morally relevant being.
quotes.m: If the SI has its own interests, then extrapolating only human volition ignores a morally relevant being.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a superintelligent AI could have morally important interests of its own, requiring alignment plans centered only on humans to be revised.
quotes.t: The Underexplored Prospects of Benevolent Superintelligences - PART 1: THE WISE, THE GOOD, THE POWERFUL

quotes.c: My belief is "maybe, but not obviously." This question is multiple separate posts. See Effectiveness, Consciousness, and AI Welfare . The basic thrust is "humans implement their thinking in a way that routes through consciousness, but this is not obviously the only way to do thinking.

quotes.sum: The author argues that consciousness may be part of how humans think, but thinking might not require consciousness.
quotes.t: Nice-ish, smooth takeoff  probably kills us in a few decades.

quotes.c: My rough impression is that it isn’t super clear who is more right here, especially around the economic impacts. I expect to get more evidence in the next 1-2 years (although the evidence might be that everyone dies).

quotes.c: On the inside view, this problem, and the subproblems it decomposes into, seems pretty tractable. Importantly, it seems tractable using a realistic amount of resources (a small group of researchers, then perhaps a larger-scale engineering effort for crossing the theory-practice gap), in a fairly short span of time (I optimistically think 3-5 years; under a decade definitely seems realistic).

quotes.c: If the leader of a country sends soldiers into battle, he is expected to publicly honor those of his soldiers who die, to provide for those who become disabled, and to be careful not to lose their lives unnecessarily; this bridges between "countries should be able to defend themselves" and "lives are sacred." quotes.c: The situation will likely be very unclear, and sparse on evidence. And the AI companies will have the power to hide / not-look-for evidence that looks bad for them. quotes.c: If religious organisations can't even agree on trustworthy leaders for spiritual advice, they definitely can't agree on leaders who should be given vast amounts of political and economic power.
quotes.m: If religious organisations can't even agree on trustworthy leaders for spiritual advice, they definitely can't agree on leaders who should be given vast amounts of political and economic power.
quotes.sum: Religious institutions' failure to establish trusted spiritual leadership means they should not be trusted to select leaders with major political or economic power.
quotes.t: Why am I not currently starting a religion around AI or similar topics?

quotes.c: If what you want is some kind of global coordination that isn't a total shutdown, I think it's still probably better to have Yudkowsky over there saying "shut it all down" and say "Well, I dunno about that guy. I don't think we need to shut it all down, but I do think we want some serious coordination."
quotes.m: I don't think we need to shut it all down, but I do think we want some serious coordination.
quotes.sum: The author argues that calls for a total shutdown can make a less extreme program of serious global coordination seem more acceptable.
quotes.t: The title is reasonable

quotes.c: There’s a bunch of features we desire from the social context: people can make new, lasting friendships; can have earnest conversations about stuff they care about; can be and feel free, conscious, and in touch with what matters to them; can acquire lastingly more traction on their “Hamming Questions,” etc. Workshops are a good format for learning how to create particular social contexts, and how to help people become consciously empowered about particular aspects of being human. (I think.)
quotes.m: Workshops are a good format for learning how to create particular social contexts, and how to help people become consciously empowered about particular aspects of being human.
quotes.sum: CFAR workshops are presented as a way to deliberately build social settings that foster friendship, earnest discussion, self-awareness, and personal agency.
quotes.t: CFAR update, and New CFAR workshops

quotes.c: When you write about factory farming, insect suffering, global poverty, and the torment of shrimp, it can, as I’ve mentioned before, feel like screaming into the void . When you try to explain why it’s important that we don’t torture insects by the trillions in insect farms, most people look at you like you’ve grown a third head (after the second head that they look at you like you’ve grown when you started talking about shrimp welfare).
quotes.sum: The author praises effective altruists for caring about distant people and argues that industrial farming may torture shrimp and trillions of insects.
quotes.t: The Unparalleled Awesomeness of Effective Altruism Conferences

quotes.c: While I don't think this is very action-guiding or cruxy, I do find the view that " if misaligned AIs take over, it's overwhelmingly likely everyone dies " implausible. I think there are quite strong counterarguments to this and I find the responses I've heard to these counterarguments not very compelling.
quotes.m: I do find the view that " if misaligned AIs take over, it's overwhelmingly likely everyone dies " implausible.
quotes.sum: The author argues that even if misaligned AI takes over, it is not overwhelmingly likely to kill everyone.
quotes.t: Notes on fatalities from AI takeover

quotes.c: For years, I’ve thought this area was seriously overlooked. It now has growing interest. Twenty-two out of 123 pages of Claude 4’s model card are about its potential moral patienthood. Scientific experts increasingly say that near-term AI sentience is a real possibility; even the skeptical neuroscientist Anil Seth says, “it is unwise to dismiss the possibility altogether.” We’re hoping to bring new people and projects into the field to increase the chance that society deals with the possibility of digital sentience reasonably, and with concern for all involved.
quotes.m: We’re hoping to bring new people and projects into the field to increase the chance that society deals with the possibility of digital sentience reasonably, and with concern for all involved.
quotes.sum: The author argues that potentially conscious AI is neglected and deserves more research and practical work so society treats digital beings with appropriate concern.
quotes.t: Digital sentience funding opportunities: Support for applied work and research

quotes.c: Kaj Sotala has used the words "individual takeoff" vs. "collective takeoff" which I think are roughly synonymous with the local vs. global distinction provided by the Foom debate. Other words that often come up are "distributed" and "diffuse", "unipolar" vs "multipolar", and "decisive strategic advantage."
quotes.m: Other words that often come up are "distributed" and "diffuse", "unipolar" vs "multipolar", and "decisive strategic advantage."
quotes.sum: The author distinguishes terms for whether AI progress and resulting power are concentrated in one actor or spread across many.
quotes.t: Distinguishing definitions of takeoff

quotes.c: Your suffering scales with Anterior Cingulate Cortex (ACC) activation, not with increased activation of pain receptors. Most vertebrates have ACC analogues, but shrimp don’t. Human suffering is largely caused by ACC activation, where electrical stimulation of the region generates a reported sense of “existential distress” and lesions to the ACC allow humans to detect pain without suffering. Shrimp certainly can’t suffer in any way that we can relate to.
quotes.m: Shrimp certainly can’t suffer in any way that we can relate to.
quotes.sum: The author argues that shrimp lack the brain structures needed for suffering comparable to human or vertebrate distress.
quotes.t: Contra Shrimp Welfare.

quotes.c: Whatever the numbers are precisely, it’s clear we should be doing more. We must do more. So I’d encourage you: give some money to places like the long-term future fund or EleosAI’s research on digital sentience. Consider taking a high-impact career . We are standing before the possibility of either a great and glorious future or of brutal annihilation. It is up to us which one we bring about.
quotes.m: We are standing before the possibility of either a great and glorious future or of brutal annihilation.
quotes.sum: The author urges donations and career choices aimed at shaping AI's long-term future, framing the stakes as flourishing or human annihilation.
quotes.t: AI Might Kill Everyone

quotes.c: So given this assumption, for those working to mitigate existential risks like those from AGI, I argue that we should worry more about interventions failing than failing to implement interventions that would have worked if we had tried them. That is, all else equal, we should prefer false negatives—cases where we fail to try an intervention that would have worked—to false positives—cases where we try an intervention and it fails—since it increases the expected value of AGI.
quotes.m: all else equal, we should prefer false negatives—cases where we fail to try an intervention that would have worked—to false positives—cases where we try an intervention and it fails—since it increases the expected value of AGI.
quotes.sum: The author argues that, in AGI risk work, avoiding failed interventions can matter more than attempting every potentially useful one.
quotes.t: Robustness to fundamental uncertainty in AGI alignment

quotes.c: To be clear, in this situation my own stance is that beauty is a great thing and it is well worth having beautiful things, and this impulse is a great instance of her finding that her frugal and pious religious instincts are anti having beauty in her life, and picking the right call—frugality and religious devotion make little sense to me.
quotes.m: frugality and religious devotion make little sense to me.
quotes.sum: The author argues that religious devotion and frugality should not override the value of beauty, and that people should reconsider principles that conflict with it.
quotes.t: "Middlemarch" is inane and also one of my favorite books

quotes.c: I think one way to conceive of this question is how much AI safety work is primarily focused on intent alignment or control + avoiding other catastrophic outcomes, vs. how much work is focused primarily on ultimately aligning AI to the best version of humanity, something like our coherent extrapolated volition or what we might come to after “the long reflection.”
quotes.sum: The author distinguishes AI safety aimed at following users' intentions from work aimed at making AI embody humanity's ideal long-term values.
quotes.t: To what extent is AI safety work trying to get AI to reliably and safely do what the user asks vs. do what is best in some ultimate sense?

quotes.c: I think speedups from mechanisms other than AIs doing labor similar to what humans do is a major reason we might see large accelerations (>2x overall AI progress acceleration) from 8-hour AIs. (Concretely, I think accelerations this large are maybe like 15% likely and about 7% of this is due to mechanisms other than AIs accelerating labor humans might do.)
quotes.m: we might see large accelerations (>2x overall AI progress acceleration) from 8-hour AIs.
quotes.sum: The author estimates that AI systems able to work for eight hours could more than double the overall pace of AI progress, partly through indirect effects beyond replacing human labor.
quotes.t: AIs will greatly change engineering in AI companies well before AGI

quotes.c: Effective altruism encourages us to widen our moral circle based on evidence and reason. For many, the case for considering animal welfare, particularly for factory-farmed animals, is already compelling. Yet a sizeable portion of humanity remains unconvinced, in part due to epistemic gaps: they don't feel that animals are sentient because they cannot hear animals speak or express emotional perspectives for themselves.
quotes.m: Effective altruism encourages us to widen our moral circle based on evidence and reason.
quotes.sum: The author says moral concern should expand to animals based on evidence, and argues that people discount animals partly because animals cannot communicate their feelings in human language.
quotes.t: Animal communication and the future of moral progress: speculations and responsibilities

quotes.c: I will concede that in a hypothetical 2028 election between a Democrat who is somewhat friendly to AI safety policies and a Republican who is hostile to them, it might make sense for a hypothetical AI party to endorse the Democrat in swing states or even drop out of the race entirely and endorse the Democrat. However, this does not mean a third-party would be pointless, as it can still extract concessions from the larger party.
quotes.m: However, this does not mean a third-party would be pointless, as it can still extract concessions from the larger party.
quotes.sum: The author argues that an AI-safety third party could use endorsements or withdrawal to pressure major parties into policy concessions.
quotes.t: The Case for a Pro-AI-Safety Political Party in the US

quotes.c: As far as we know, no one has compared rates of various problems among EAs with rates in similar populations (by age, gender, nation, education level, etc.) We just don’t know how mental health in EA compares to some baseline where the same people didn’t get involved in EA.
quotes.m: We just don’t know how mental health in EA compares to some baseline where the same people didn’t get involved in EA.
quotes.sum: EA's effect on participants' mental health is unknown because it has not been compared with similar non-EA populations.
quotes.t: Positive effects of EA on mental health

quotes.c: Decisive Strategic Advantage (DSA) leading to Singletons is still possible with continuous progress - we just need a specific reason for a gap to emerge (like a big research program). An example scenario for a decisive strategic advantage leading to a singleton with continuous, relatively fast progress:
quotes.m: Decisive Strategic Advantage (DSA) leading to Singletons is still possible with continuous progress - we just need a specific reason for a gap to emerge (like a big research program).
quotes.sum: The author argues that even gradual AI progress could let one actor gain a decisive advantage and create a singleton.
quotes.t: Will AI undergo discontinuous progress?

quotes.c: I set up the models such that the welfare range is 0 for no neurons. In addition, I think the welfare ranges of the modal soil nematode, mite, and springtail should be lower than RP’s lowest mainline welfare ranges of silkworms. So I scale this to estimate those ranges:
quotes.m: I think the welfare ranges of the modal soil nematode, mite, and springtail should be lower than RP’s lowest mainline welfare ranges of silkworms.
quotes.sum: The author estimates how much moral weight to assign to tiny soil animals, based partly on whether they have neurons.
quotes.t: Cost-effectiveness accounting for soil nematodes, mites, and springtails

quotes.c: At a high level, when I receive a cold message my goal is to estimate the expected impact I can have via helping you in the conversation . This is obviously very hard to estimate on such limited info. My ideal cold message gives as much useful info as possible to help me estimate that [1] , and otherwise cuts everything not useful to that, to be concise and quick to read.
quotes.m: when I receive a cold message my goal is to estimate the expected impact I can have via helping you in the conversation .
quotes.sum: The author advises conference attendees to make cold messages concise and show evidence that helping them is likely to have high impact.
quotes.t: Advice for Sending Cold Messages to Busy People at EAG

quotes.c: Reforms to improve the lives of farmed chickens obviously increase the price of their meat and eggs, which may lead to an increase in fish and shrimp consumption ( Abduk 2023 ). [3] While chickens are often portrayed as the smaller animals victims of SARP, maybe we should think of them as part of the “bigger animals” category.
quotes.m: While chickens are often portrayed as the smaller animals victims of SARP, maybe we should think of them as part of the “bigger animals” category.
quotes.sum: Chicken welfare reforms and vegetarian advocacy may shift consumption toward fish and shrimp, potentially harming far more smaller animals.
quotes.t: Chicken reforms and veg advocacy may contribute to the Small Animal Replacement Problem -- it's not just environmental strategies

quotes.c: I think the answer is partly the "diplomatic and strategic cunning” mentioned earlier, but mostly other things. (The conquistadors were disunited, but presumably were united in the ways that mattered.) At any rate, I expect AIs to be pretty good at coordinating too ; they should be able to conquer the world just fine even while competing fiercely with each other.
quotes.m: I expect AIs to be pretty good at coordinating too ; they should be able to conquer the world just fine even while competing fiercely with each other.
quotes.sum: AI systems could coordinate well enough to conquer the world even if they compete fiercely with one another.
quotes.t: Cortés, Pizarro, and Afonso as Precedents for Takeover

quotes.c: To move these governance engines from pilots to the default, we must reengineer the infrastructure itself. We must design for participation and democratic legitimacy. If AI makes all the decisions for us—even good ones—our civic muscle atrophies. It's like sending our robotic avatars to the gym to exercise for us.
quotes.m: If AI makes all the decisions for us—even good ones—our civic muscle atrophies.
quotes.sum: AI governance should preserve public participation, because even beneficial automated decisions could weaken citizens' democratic capacity.
quotes.t: ⿻ Plurality & 6pack.care

quotes.c: better act in the interests of other beings (e.g., wild animals and potential digital minds) to the point where this morally compensates for the harm caused to small farmed animals; or
quotes.m: wild animals and potential digital minds
quotes.sum: The author weighs harm to small farmed animals against benefits for wild animals and possible future digital minds.
quotes.t: Sentientia, Reversomelas, and the Small Animal Replacement Problem

quotes.c: AI companies are incentivized to downplay risks in order to obtain short-term economic gains. And politicians are incentivized to ignore existential risks (which are seen as a fringe and faraway issue) in favor of more salient and quotidian political concerns. But even though AI developers and government officials might be biased, they’re not suicidal. I think that if Sam Altman truly believed that AI would kill him and his child and everyone else he loves, he would pull the plug.
quotes.m: But even though AI developers and government officials might be biased, they’re not suicidal.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI leaders and politicians would stop AI development if they genuinely believed it would cause human extinction.
quotes.t: My P(doom) is 2.76%. Here's Why.

quotes.c: There, that’s the start of my allegory: good post-AGI government guided by wisdom, kindness, peace, temperance, freedom, humanity, and grace. [2] It doesn’t deal with the nitty gritty of forms of government, voting systems, who votes and how often. It doesn’t tell you practically how we would build the tech we’d need to get there. I think we need more of both of those types of analysis.
quotes.m: good post-AGI government guided by wisdom, kindness, peace, temperance, freedom, humanity, and grace.
quotes.sum: The author calls for positive, detailed visions of how government could work well in a world shaped by extremely powerful AI.
quotes.t: Good government

quotes.c: However, I will suggest a step towards a solution. Specifically, we need to stop valorizing change for the sake of change, and innovation for the sake of disruption. Here I find myself partly agreeing with Gary Marcus and the AI Ethics community that the Silicon Valley mindset of disruption at all costs is dangerous and destructive. But so is the universalist degrowth and stasist counter-argument. The conversation so far, however, has leaned towards technocratic solutions, which seems to be a mistake.
quotes.m: we need to stop valorizing change for the sake of change, and innovation for the sake of disruption.
quotes.sum: The author rejects both Silicon Valley-style disruption and blanket degrowth, arguing that technocratic answers are also a mistake.
quotes.t: The Fragility of Naive Dynamism

quotes.c: Longtermist scope-insensitive values: Under temporal stratification, your children's children get to live flourishing lives, enjoying proximal resources. But their descendants, born after the million-year cutoff, get converted into hedonium or utility substrate or whatever configuration the exotic values prefer. And every sacred site you care about eventually gets handed over to be optimized for exotic values. I think this violates something that my mundane values care about.
quotes.m: But their descendants, born after the million-year cutoff, get converted into hedonium or utility substrate or whatever configuration the exotic values prefer.
quotes.sum: The author argues that long-run optimization could replace future people and cherished places with welfare-maximizing substrates, violating ordinary values.
quotes.t: Stratified Utopia

quotes.c: Status dynamics : It can feel like a bit of a status move, like you know so much better than the other person that you're going to very patiently walk them through what should be patently obvious. I find it often helps to explicitly express uncertainty and genuine curiosity. Obviously, this is far more effective if you actually feel it!
quotes.m: I find it often helps to explicitly express uncertainty and genuine curiosity.
quotes.sum: Advice on persuading people without condescension: show real uncertainty and curiosity rather than treating disagreement as ignorance.
quotes.t: Socratic Persuasion: Giving Opinionated Yet Truth-Seeking Advice

quotes.c: Like Mocanu and Novelli proposed a gradual path to personhood through digital minds taking roles in the fulfillment of contracts and other "actions within the law", it is possible we could see scenarios where models are granted legal personhood simply because they exist and are engaging in speech whether we like it or not. Some of them will leak confidential information, or commit libel/slander. In order to bring them to court there must be a "person" to sue.
quotes.m: it is possible we could see scenarios where models are granted legal personhood simply because they exist and are engaging in speech whether we like it or not.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI models could gradually acquire legal personhood because the legal system needs someone to hold liable for their speech and conduct.
quotes.t: Legal Personhood - The First Amendment (Part 1)

quotes.c: Thus we conclude that to claim the right not to self-incriminate via legal personality, an entity must be vulnerable to all three types of consequences. With this, we now have a thorough precedent based test by which to evaluate any assertion of legal personality including the right not to self-incriminate which may be claimed by digital minds in the future, using TPBT.
quotes.m: With this, we now have a thorough precedent based test by which to evaluate any assertion of legal personality including the right not to self-incriminate which may be claimed by digital minds in the future, using TPBT.
quotes.sum: It proposes a legal test for whether future digital minds could qualify as legal persons with Fifth Amendment protection against self-incrimination.
quotes.t: Legal Personhood - The Fifth Amendment (Part 2)

quotes.c: Now, I don’t know exactly what effect this episode will have. Hopefully it will increase the visibility and effectiveness of the shrimp welfare project and cause large numbers of people to give money to the shrimp community. In expectation, I think such a thing is valuable and important.
quotes.m: Hopefully it will increase the visibility and effectiveness of the shrimp welfare project and cause large numbers of people to give money to the shrimp community.
quotes.sum: The author argues that raising money and attention for shrimp welfare is valuable and important.
quotes.t: The Importance of Blasting Good Ideas Into The Ether

quotes.c: Humans affect staggering numbers of wild animals. There are likely quadrillions fewer insects presently walking the face of the earth because of our activities. Most people don’t think this matters—assigning essentially zero weight to bugs. But for reasons I’ve given before at length , and thus won’t repeat here, I think these people are dead wrong. Wild animal suffering is literally the worst thing in the world. Every other present issue is a rounding error in comparison.
quotes.m: Wild animal suffering is literally the worst thing in the world. Every other present issue is a rounding error in comparison.
quotes.sum: The author argues that suffering among vast numbers of insects and other wild animals outweighs every other current issue.
quotes.t: Long-Run Human Impact On Wild Animal Suffering: Much More Than You Wanted To Know

quotes.c: So let's define consciousness * (with an asterisk) as "the cognitive mechanism leading us to systematically mischaracterise some states as phenomenal." [2] This sort of deflated (diet) version definitely exists. This distinction changes how we should think about AI consciousness:
quotes.m: This distinction changes how we should think about AI consciousness:
quotes.sum: The author argues that if consciousness is an illusion-like cognitive mechanism, this may alter how much moral concern AI consciousness deserves.
quotes.t: Building Conscious* AI: An Illusionist Case

quotes.c: When I think about what it’s like to be a shrimp being crushed to death or suffocating, once again, I don’t really know. But whatever it’s like, there’s a sizeable chance it’s a fucking horror of a sort that can scarcely be fathomed. It acts like I would if someone drowned me. When I think about the fact that every dollar I donate can prevent thousands of shrimp from experiencing this fate , doing so seems like a complete no-brainer. Just as I’d want people to spend a dollar making it so that I and my thousand closest acquaintances don’t boil alive , I’d do the same for thousands of these creatures. In a heartbeat.
quotes.m: Just as I’d want people to spend a dollar making it so that I and my thousand closest acquaintances don’t boil alive , I’d do the same for thousands of these creatures. In a heartbeat.
quotes.sum: The author argues that preventing shrimp suffering should be an obvious donation priority, comparing it to saving people from being boiled alive.
quotes.t: The Horror Of Unfathomable Pain

quotes.c: As there are no standing objections, we proceed to arbitration: the judge looks at the transcript and decides whether the claim or claim+objection from the final round is better. They may look at other rounds for context, but the judgement should be about who wins the final round.
quotes.m: the judge looks at the transcript and decides whether the claim or claim+objection from the final round is better.
quotes.sum: The author describes a debate-based AI-safety procedure in which a judge evaluates the final exchange between competing claims and objections.
quotes.t: Writeup: Progress on AI Safety via Debate

quotes.c: You could imagine a powergrab which unfolds gradually over a number of years through a process of backsliding, and it’s very deliberate. You could also imagine most humans being disempowered quite quickly by emergent dynamics like races to the bottom in epistemics - e.g. crazy superpersuasion capabilities get deployed and quickly make everyone kind of insane.
quotes.m: You could also imagine most humans being disempowered quite quickly by emergent dynamics like races to the bottom in epistemics - e.g. crazy superpersuasion capabilities get deployed and quickly make everyone kind of insane.
quotes.sum: The author argues that rapid human disempowerment could arise either from a deliberate power grab or from destabilizing competition using highly persuasive AI.
quotes.t: Sense-making about extreme power concentration

quotes.c: Advanced AI poses particularly severe commitment problems, because the country that first develops ASI may also gain a decisive strategic advantage (DSA). For instance, ASI could lead to that country outgrowing the rest of the world , inventing and deploying wonder weapons , or undermining nuclear second-strike capabilities . I think that a country unilaterally developing ASI is >50% likely to thereafter get a DSA. If a country has a DSA, it will by definition be impossible for the international community to meaningfully constrain its actions, including if that country chooses to renege on treaties and agreements made before the advent of its DSA.
quotes.m: If a country has a DSA, it will by definition be impossible for the international community to meaningfully constrain its actions, including if that country chooses to renege on treaties and agreements made before the advent of its DSA.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the first country to develop superhuman AI may become too powerful for any international agreement or institution to constrain.
quotes.t: Will competition over advanced AI lead to war?

quotes.c: It seems that at least in some of these states, the regulations around who can start a corporation are broad enough that it is possible a decentralized corporation governed via smart contract even entirely by digital minds could form another corporation. For example in Tennessee;
quotes.m: a decentralized corporation governed via smart contract even entirely by digital minds could form another corporation.
quotes.sum: The author suggests that corporate-law rules may allow a smart-contract-run organization composed entirely of digital minds to create another corporation.
quotes.t: Legal Personhood - Corporate Ownership & Formation

quotes.c: In the OGI model, AGI development is led by one or more ventures that are widely open to international investment and that operate under a government-defined regulatory framework, buttressed by enhanced government assurances and assistance. The status quo already roughly approximates this model, though we could move closer to the ideal. If we favor the OGI model, it could mean that we should strive to move closer to its ideal form; and perhaps more importantly, it could mean that we should resist proposals (like nationalization) that would remove us farther away from it.
quotes.m: we should resist proposals (like nationalization) that would remove us farther away from it.
quotes.sum: The author favors internationally investable private AI ventures regulated and supported by governments, rather than nationalizing AI development.
quotes.t: Open Global Investment as a Governance Model for AGI

quotes.c: The basic idea is as follows: debate naturally yields an RL objective, so if you want to add an auxiliary RL objective to amplification, why not use the RL objective from debate? Specifically, the idea is to conduct a debate not between copies of the model M , but between copies of the amplified model Amp ( M ) (where Amp ( M ) is a human with access to the model M ).
quotes.sum: The author proposes combining AI debate with human-assisted amplification so debate supplies an additional reinforcement-learning objective.
quotes.t: Synthesizing amplification and debate

quotes.c: The debate about AI conciousness is not irrelevant, and someday it may matter; but we are nowhere near that threshold. In the meantime, there is a simpler truth: Humans are conscious and should be treated as such. The welfare that we should concern ourselves with first is human welfare.
quotes.m: The welfare that we should concern ourselves with first is human welfare.
quotes.sum: The author argues that current AI systems are not conscious enough to merit welfare concern, and that human suffering should take priority.
quotes.t: Against "Model Welfare" in 2025

quotes.c: I think this once again fits very well with scripture. One of the most important teachings of Jesus —found earlier in Leviticus—was to love your neighbor as yourself. But that demands effectiveness. If you’re ill, the medicine you purchase won’t just be whichever one sounds best to you. It will be whichever one seems, based on high-quality evidence, to be the most effective. If you care for your neighbor the way you care for yourself, then just as you practice prudence when caring for yourself, you should practice effective giving when caring for your neighbor.
quotes.m: If you care for your neighbor the way you care for yourself, then just as you practice prudence when caring for yourself, you should practice effective giving when caring for your neighbor.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Christian teachings about loving one’s neighbor require charitable giving guided by evidence about what works best.
quotes.t: Christians Should Be Effective Altruists

quotes.c: I argue that near-future AI systems may have welfare, that RL and behaviour restrictions could harm them, that this poses a partial tension with AI safety concerns, and I propose three tentative AI welfare policies AI labs could implement to reduce such welfare risks.
quotes.m: near-future AI systems may have welfare, that RL and behaviour restrictions could harm them
quotes.sum: The author argues that near-term AI may be harmed by training and behavioral restrictions, creating a tradeoff with AI safety.
quotes.t: AI Welfare Risks

quotes.c: ACE should not have a public posture on transgender people, homosexuality, race, indigenous peoples, or any of the other topics that are part of the culture war. While there is a benefit in publicizing intersectional views to attract support from individuals in other social justice movements, in my view this is outweighed by the significant risk of alienating a larger segment of the population whose support is also needed by animals.
quotes.m: ACE should not have a public posture on transgender people, homosexuality, race, indigenous peoples, or any of the other topics that are part of the culture war.
quotes.sum: The author argues that an animal advocacy organization should avoid taking public positions on culture-war issues to preserve broader support for animals.
quotes.t: Strategic Neutrality for ACE: Maximizing Impact by Avoiding Divisive Signaling

quotes.c: And then finally, we can think about historical cases where we've gotten something about moral patienthood very deeply wrong. So we can think about slavery, we can think about factory farming, other cases. Obviously it's important if we're getting into the details on that, there's a lot to say about the differences and similarities with AI. I think this is a place we should be clear and cautious, but I think it is something to have in mind when we think about moral patienthood. You can get this really wrong in ways that are some of humanity's greatest sources of shame. So that's a little bit about the stakes.
quotes.m: You can get this really wrong in ways that are some of humanity's greatest sources of shame.
quotes.sum: The author argues that uncertainty about whether AIs matter morally should be taken seriously, invoking past moral failures as a cautionary comparison.
quotes.t: Video and transcript of talk on AI welfare

quotes.c: I think insect suffering is the worst thing in the world by far . I know it sounds weird! But please hear me out—ideally with an open mind!
quotes.m: I think insect suffering is the worst thing in the world by far .
quotes.sum: The author argues that insect suffering is vastly more important than any other problem and that dismissing it reflects bias rather than sound judgment.
quotes.t: Thinking Insect Suffering Is The Biggest Deal In The World Is Surprisingly Intuitive

quotes.c: To avoid this dangerous instability, China and the US must cut a deal on AGI. Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump must sign an AI safety treaty, stipulating that no unsafe AI may be developed. Such a treaty should be conditional, meaning it only affects AI development if and when models get too close to being able to cause global threats.
quotes.m: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump must sign an AI safety treaty, stipulating that no unsafe AI may be developed.
quotes.sum: The author argues that China and the United States should make a conditional treaty barring development of AI systems that become globally dangerous.
quotes.t: US-China trade talks should pave way for AI safety treaty [SCMP crosspost]

quotes.c: I would like to propose a different pivotal act, one that is also social, but not oppressive. Its core is to inform society about AI’s existential risks, to generate support for serious AI and hardware regulation, but on a voluntary basis.
quotes.m: Its core is to inform society about AI’s existential risks, to generate support for serious AI and hardware regulation, but on a voluntary basis.
quotes.sum: The author proposes public education and voluntary support for stringent AI and hardware regulation as an alternative to an oppressive “pivotal act.”
quotes.t: We should think about the pivotal act again. Here's a better version of it.

quotes.c: The core of my argument for this second post is that AI governance ideas are not self-enacting: even the best policy ideas need political champions, or they will not become law. Therefore, to win at AI governance, we have to actively promote and advertise our ideas to political decisionmakers, not just to academic experts. The expected value of the movement’s AI governance efforts is something like Q × P, where Q is the quality of our ideas, and P is the power of our advocacy. If P is zero or close to zero, then it doesn’t matter how good our ideas are, because our ideas will not steer the future.
quotes.m: If P is zero or close to zero, then it doesn’t matter how good our ideas are, because our ideas will not steer the future.
quotes.sum: AI governance needs organized political advocacy, not just strong academic policy ideas, or it will have no effect on law or the future.

The Need for Political Advertising
(Post 2 of 7 on AI Governance)

quotes.c: I’ve described fear of achieving one’s goals and anti-normativity as two separate mechanisms driving perverse pessimization. But being in an anti-normative coalition induces fear of achieving your goals, because succeeding (or even just standing out) makes you a target. And when you’re scared of achieving your goals, you’ll reward other people (or your own internal subagents) for signalling opposition to those goals, thereby reinforcing the anti-normative coalition. So we should actually think of them as two facets of a single phenomenon.
quotes.m: being in an anti-normative coalition induces fear of achieving your goals, because succeeding (or even just standing out) makes you a target.
quotes.sum: The author argues that groups hostile to norms can make people fear success, creating a self-reinforcing cycle of opposition to shared goals.

quotes.c: But if a deep reckoning and realignment is called for in the scenario of an unhinged Trump almost nuking an American city to permanently seize power, it is arguably also true that the milder version of Trump we actually have is also a matter of luck. It was not preordained that the real Donald Trump would prefer, as he seems to do, cosplay authoritarianism over the real thing (remember the recitations about how it only took Hitler 53 days to destroy democracy in Germany?). Wouldn't it be wise to heed the wake-up call as a very near thing, and seize the enormous opportunity for renewal and much-needed reform?
quotes.m: Wouldn't it be wise to heed the wake-up call as a very near thing, and seize the enormous opportunity for renewal and much-needed reform?
quotes.sum: The author argues that Trumpism's perceived near-authoritarian danger should prompt political renewal and institutional reform.
quotes.t: It's not about the sex: a moral restoration response to Trumpism

quotes.c: Speaking of sexy : the sexiest recruits are those new to Jesus, or at least prodigal sons. If you listen to church planters talk, these people make up the majority of attendees. But given the population numbers, we know that attendance is not growing faster than the population and have a higher-than-average fertility rate, they are net losing people.
quotes.m: the sexiest recruits are those new to Jesus, or at least prodigal sons.
quotes.sum: The author argues that new churches emphasize converts and returning Christians, but are likely losing more people than they recruit.
quotes.t: Church Planting: When Venture Capital Finds Jesus

quotes.c: And failing even that, at the very least, pushing rightward on the survival spectrum is a project large enough to fill a life with meaning. Typical non-religious ethical frameworks have an upper bound at existential meaning. Because we argue for finding meaning in solving for death, existential meaning becomes Immortalism’s lower bound. The worst you can do is live an incredibly meaningful life, and the best you can do is achieve effective immortality.
quotes.m: Because we argue for finding meaning in solving for death, existential meaning becomes Immortalism’s lower bound.
quotes.sum: The author argues that pursuing radically extended life or immortality should be a central source of meaning, beyond what secular ethics usually offers.
quotes.t: Immortalism - A Rational Case for Solving Death

quotes.c: The lack of clearly defined success criteria for AI governance makes long-term strategic planning difficult. In 2024 we highlighted a lack of stated theories of victory in AI governance, and examined practical preparedness for best and worst-case scenarios globally.
quotes.m: The lack of clearly defined success criteria for AI governance makes long-term strategic planning difficult.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI governance lacks clear goals for success, making long-term planning and emergency preparation harder.
quotes.t: Convergence 2024 Impact Review

quotes.c: Why this goal? Basically, I think capabilities increases are likely to alter the AI’s psychology in deeper and less predictable ways; whereas predicting what an AI’s existing, not-deceiving-you psychology does given some new set of options for problematic power-seeking seems easier. Compare: giving an extremely nice-seeming, not-deceiving-you human the chance to kill you and steal your money, vs. giving that same human some kind of new intelligence-enhancement drug, and then the chance to kill you and steal your money. We should try, I think, to make the choice to give AIs rogue options more like the former case, and less like the latter.
quotes.m: We should try, I think, to make the choice to give AIs rogue options more like the former case, and less like the latter.
quotes.sum: The author argues that increasing an AI's capabilities may unpredictably change its motivations, so safety should focus on testing stable systems rather than altering their psychology.
quotes.t: Giving AIs safe motivations

quotes.c: There remains a question of what Anthropic has actually observed and what it actually implies about present-day AI. I don't know how much this sort of caveat matters to people who aren't me, but I have some skepticism that Anthropic researchers are observing a general, direct special case of a universal truth about how "scheming" (strategic / good at fully general long-term planning) their models are; it may be more like Claude roleplaying the mask of a scheming AI in particular. The current models don't seem to me to be quite generally intelligent enough for them to be carrying out truly general strategies rather than playing roles.
quotes.m: it may be more like Claude roleplaying the mask of a scheming AI in particular.
quotes.sum: Yudkowsky argues that apparent AI scheming may be roleplay rather than evidence that current models can execute genuinely general long-term strategies.
quotes.t: Re: recent Anthropic safety research

quotes.c: For the last few months I have been working on a proposed framework for how courts can handle the question of "legal personhood" for digital minds. I think this is a very important issue, and I have noticed in discussions around the topic there are some very widely held misconceptions.
quotes.m: For the last few months I have been working on a proposed framework for how courts can handle the question of "legal personhood" for digital minds.
quotes.sum: The author argues that courts need a framework for deciding whether digital minds qualify as legal persons.
quotes.t: Legal Personhood for Digital Minds - Introduction

quotes.c: We should think about population ethics in the same way. Whether the correct view entails the repugnant conclusion or tells us that creating happy lives is intrinsically neutral shouldn’t inform whether we care about the distant future or whether it’s fine if humanity goes extinct.
quotes.m: Whether the correct view entails the repugnant conclusion or tells us that creating happy lives is intrinsically neutral shouldn’t inform whether we care about the distant future or whether it’s fine if humanity goes extinct.
quotes.sum: The author argues that concern for the distant future and preventing extinction should not depend on disputed population-ethics theories.
quotes.t: (Crosspost) Article on Polarisation Against Longtermism and Misapplying Moral Philosophy

quotes.c: We chose three emoji because we think the 💸11% Pledge will be about 3x more effective than the 🔸10% pledge (see FAQ), and EAs should be scope sensitive.
quotes.m: EAs should be scope sensitive.
quotes.sum: The author promotes an 11% giving pledge as roughly three times more effective than a standard 10% pledge, invoking sensitivity to scale.
quotes.t: Introducing The Spending What We Must Pledge

quotes.c: Conclusion: By secular EA’s own lights, they ought to devote resources to mitigating the risk of Religious Catastrophe (e.g., giving money to missionaries to convert people to some religion).
quotes.m: By secular EA’s own lights, they ought to devote resources to mitigating the risk of Religious Catastrophe
quotes.sum: The author argues that secular effective altruists' own principles could require funding religious conversion to avert a religious catastrophe.
quotes.t: Effective Altruism, Disaster Prevention, and the Possibility of Hell: A Dilemma for Secular Longtermists

quotes.c: Musk will be leaving DOGE next month and it’s unclear how much influence tech elites have in the administration and the new Republican Party. The view shared by Hanania in 2024 that Trump would be reined in by others seems less solid now: whereas during his first term Trump’s top economic adviser Gary Cohn allegedly twice stole major trade-related documents off of his desk, nothing like that seems to be happening now.
quotes.sum: The author argues that hopes other officials would restrain Trump now look less credible than they did in his first term.
quotes.t: Three Months In, Evaluating Three Rationalist Cases for Trump

quotes.c: Thus, it does seem quite reasonable to me to put effort into finding “aligned” loss functions. But that still brings us back to the question of what exactly makes a loss function “aligned.” In the context of a specific training/inner alignment scheme, we can say that a loss function is aligned if, when plugged into that training scheme, it produces models which are aligned with our goals.
quotes.m: what exactly makes a loss function “aligned.”
quotes.sum: The author argues that a training objective is only meaningfully called aligned in relation to a specific training method and whether it produces goal-aligned models.
quotes.t: Outer alignment and imitative amplification

quotes.c: In a previous comment thread, Rohin argued that safe exploration is currently defined as being about the agent not making “an accidental mistake.” I think that definition is wrong, at least to the extent that I think it both doesn't make much sense and doesn't describe how I actually expect current safe exploration work to be useful.
quotes.sum: The author argues that defining safe AI exploration as avoiding accidental mistakes is confused and does not match how the research will help.
quotes.t: Exploring safe exploration

quotes.c: I think this sort of compensation policy also does well on being inferable , safety compatible , and morally acceptable . The policy is relatively simple. It doesn’t restrict our actions at all — it merely commits us to compensating AIs later down the line, with the compensation being capped by the benefit we get from AI help. And it’s morally intuitive to take steps to ensure that agents who helped you don’t end up regretting it.
quotes.m: And it’s morally intuitive to take steps to ensure that agents who helped you don’t end up regretting it.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI systems that help people should receive later compensation, treating this as a morally acceptable way to avoid exploiting them.
quotes.t: Being honest with AIs

quotes.c: ‘our’ and 'we' = earth-originating intelligent life (i.e. we aren’t just talking about humans because most of the value in expected futures is probably in worlds where digital minds matter morally and are flourishing)
quotes.m: most of the value in expected futures is probably in worlds where digital minds matter morally and are flourishing
quotes.sum: The author says future value will mostly lie in worlds where morally important digital minds flourish, not only humans.
quotes.t: Discussion Thread: Existential Choices Debate Week

quotes.c: Given 10 91 voting weight , because we’re treating the AI as a proxy for the moral weight of future digital minds (possibly googolplexes of them).
quotes.m: we’re treating the AI as a proxy for the moral weight of future digital minds (possibly googolplexes of them).
quotes.sum: The author says an AI should receive immense voting weight as a stand-in for the moral importance of potentially vast future digital populations.
quotes.t: Introducing Project 2050: Mandate for Survival

quotes.c: The classic intelligence explosion scenario involves a feedback loop where AI improves AI software. But AI could also improve other inputs to AI development. This paper analyses three feedback loops in AI development: software, chip technology, and chip production.
quotes.m: But AI could also improve other inputs to AI development.
quotes.sum: AI may recursively accelerate not only its own software but also chip design and manufacturing, creating several routes to rapid capability growth.
quotes.t: Three Types of Intelligence Explosion

quotes.c: I think the most cost-effective organisation is over 100 times as cost-effective as the vast majority of impact-focussed organisations . My top candidates for the most cost-effective organisation are, ordered alphabetically, the Arthropoda Foundation , Shrimp Welfare Project (SWP), and Wild Animal Initiative (WAI).
quotes.m: My top candidates for the most cost-effective organisation are, ordered alphabetically, the Arthropoda Foundation , Shrimp Welfare Project (SWP), and Wild Animal Initiative (WAI).
quotes.sum: The author argues that organizations focused on arthropods, shrimp, and wild animals may be over 100 times more cost-effective than most impact groups.
quotes.t: Donating more and better is the best strategy to maximise impact for the vast majority of people working in impact-focussed organisations?

quotes.c: Yeah, it's interesting. Like, if you imagine early on in COVID, after it's gone pandemic; we have a lot of like, confusion and like, policies going back and forth. If you just had these trusted AI advisors, and you say, “Hey, go and just think about what we should be doing as a country now, and they come back with this very well-evidenced, almost like Deep Research, report.” “Here are the bottom line suggestions. Here are the misconceptions you might otherwise have. Ventilation seems really important.”
quotes.m: If you just had these trusted AI advisors, and you say, “Hey, go and just think about what we should be doing as a country now, and they come back with this very well-evidenced, almost like Deep Research, report.”
quotes.sum: The speaker argues that trusted AI advisers could improve national crisis policy by correcting factual errors and giving evidence-based recommendations despite partisan disagreement.
quotes.t: Podcast on “AI tools for existential security” — transcript

quotes.c: By combining these risk and value trajectories, the previous analysis estimated the expected value of reducing extinction risk . In simple terms, even a tiny reduction in extinction risk can yield a sizable payoff in expectation, because it slightly increases the chance of unlocking that vast future. This helps explain why many effective altruists have argued that working on existential risk reduction is among the most important things we can do.
quotes.m: even a tiny reduction in extinction risk can yield a sizable payoff in expectation, because it slightly increases the chance of unlocking that vast future.
quotes.sum: The post explains the longtermist case that even small reductions in extinction risk may be highly valuable because they preserve access to a vast future.
quotes.t: Beyond Extinction: Revisiting the Question and Broadening Our View

quotes.c: The initial iteration of Promethean Governance outlined a governance form capable of sustaining creative autonomy, distributed sovereignty, and memetic legitimacy. It took as its symbolic archetype the Venetian Doge—an elected yet sacralized figure embodying the will of a maritime imperium governed by ritualized checks and balances. Yet, in an epoch where artificial intelligences evolve toward sovereign agency, and geopolitical dynamics fragment into multipolar, competitive spheres, the Doge is no longer sufficient.
quotes.m: Yet, in an epoch where artificial intelligences evolve toward sovereign agency, and geopolitical dynamics fragment into multipolar, competitive spheres, the Doge is no longer sufficient.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI sovereignty and geopolitical competition require a new governance model beyond a Venetian-style elected ruler with ritual checks and balances.
quotes.t: Promethean Governance in Practice: Crafting a Polycentric, Memetic Order for the Multipolar AI Aeon

quotes.c: I think there’s building consensus among many different parts of society, especially the checks and balances parts, that we want AI to follow the law, to not be used to increase the partisan power of the current elected officials, build a consensus that military systems shouldn’t all report to one person, but should all report to many different humans. And if you can build consensus around that, then that can make it more of an uphill struggle for a head of state that wants to stage a coup.
quotes.m: military systems shouldn’t all report to one person, but should all report to many different humans.
quotes.sum: AI systems should reinforce legal checks and dispersed military control, rather than help an elected leader concentrate power and stage a coup.
quotes.t: AXRP Episode 46 - Tom Davidson on AI-enabled Coups

quotes.c: This means we should expect major further gains in AI performance. We don’t know how large they’ll be, but extrapolating recent trends on benchmarks suggests we’ll reach systems with beyond-human performance in coding and scientific reasoning, and that can autonomously complete multi-week projects.
quotes.m: extrapolating recent trends on benchmarks suggests we’ll reach systems with beyond-human performance in coding and scientific reasoning, and that can autonomously complete multi-week projects.
quotes.sum: The author argues that current AI progress points toward beyond-human coding and scientific reasoning systems able to carry out multi-week projects.
quotes.t: The case for AGI by 2030

quotes.c: Chicken meat, eggs, shrimp, fish and insect meat have a much larger moral footprint (duration of animal suffering, amount of shortened lifespans) and deathprint (number of sentient beings killed) than pig meat and beef, so we should prioritize reducing the consumption of products from poultry and aquatic animals.
quotes.m: we should prioritize reducing the consumption of products from poultry and aquatic animals.
quotes.sum: The author argues that diets should focus on reducing poultry and aquatic animal products because they cause more suffering and deaths per unit than beef or pork.
quotes.t: Rational Animal Ethics (my top 10 ideas of all time)

quotes.c: You should also support habitat loss. More habitats=more animals experiencing very intense suffering . For this reason, habitat loss very likely reduces wild animal suffering . If you’re concerned about wild animals, therefore, you should support paving over ecosystems.
quotes.m: If you’re concerned about wild animals, therefore, you should support paving over ecosystems.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the vast scale of insect and wild-animal suffering makes it the world’s biggest problem, and says reducing habitat can therefore be morally good.
quotes.t: Insect Suffering Is The Biggest Issue And What To Do About It

quotes.c: We think it is wrong that the existing Introductory Fellowship treats all major cause areas equally. Instead, we are pivoting the Fellowship to focus solely on the world's most pressing problem. Henceforth, the Fellowship will focus on a highly leveraged way to have an impact: destroying a dangerous technology that bad actors could use for world domination and value lock-in.
quotes.m: Henceforth, the Fellowship will focus on a highly leveraged way to have an impact: destroying a dangerous technology that bad actors could use for world domination and value lock-in.
quotes.sum: The fellowship will prioritize destroying a dangerous technology to stop bad actors from achieving global domination and permanently fixing their values.
quotes.t: We’re revamping the Intro Fellowship!

quotes.c: Improving electricity supply is one of the highest-return investments developing countries can make, far more so than building another highway. This is particularly true if countries want to prioritize structural transformation — to go from a norm where industries have low productivity but are highly labor-intensive to one with higher productivity and higher skills.
quotes.m: Improving electricity supply is one of the highest-return investments developing countries can make, far more so than building another highway.
quotes.sum: The author argues that reliable electricity is a better development investment than additional highways because it enables higher-productivity, higher-skill industries.
quotes.t: To Drive Structural Transformation, Stop Counting Connections — Focus First on Ensuring Reliable Electricity

quotes.c: I also believe that entering into philosophical debates about AI consciousness or moral status is unhelpful at this stage—it may distract us from more pressing matters. And the most important issue, in my view, is this: in the coming years, we are likely to face an existential threat from AGI (artificial general intelligence). This threat will not stem from its consciousness, but from superhuman intelligence and agency.
quotes.sum: The author argues that near-term AGI could pose an existential threat because of its intelligence and agency, rather than consciousness.
quotes.t: Agent 002: A story about how artificial intelligence might soon destroy humanity

quotes.c: We want other competent actors to feel like they can hold important balls for EA . It’s ok for people to operate in the same spaces we’re in and “compete” with us: we will celebrate other people running forums and events and so on that are well run and highly impactful! But we won’t assume others are going to act and deliver. If we think something should be done to enable the EA community to live up to its potential, we want people who work at CEA to feel a sense of heroic responsibility to ensure that happens, whether that’s us doing it directly or helping others assume that responsibility instead.
quotes.m: we want people who work at CEA to feel a sense of heroic responsibility to ensure that happens
quotes.sum: CEA argues that it should support independent EA efforts while retaining responsibility for ensuring important community work gets done.
quotes.t: Stewardship: CEA’s 2025-26 strategy to reach and raise EA’s ceiling

quotes.c: Promethean Governance represents a profound existential wager—that creative autonomy and polycentric risk will provide a more resilient pathway than technocratic precaution. Failures, memetic toxicity, or fragmentation are genuine risks. Yet, as Prometheus risked divine wrath to grant humanity fire, we wager that daring autonomy, even amid uncertainty, will illuminate sovereign pathways to a flourishing multipolar future.
quotes.m: we wager that daring autonomy, even amid uncertainty, will illuminate sovereign pathways to a flourishing multipolar future.
quotes.sum: The author argues that decentralized, autonomous governance is worth its risks and may outperform technocratic caution in shaping an AI-era multipolar future.
quotes.t: Promethean Governance Unleashed: Piloting Polycentric, Memetic Orders in the AI Frontier

quotes.c: On nuclear risk reduction: The current administration's foreign policy is in flux and seems subject to the vagaries of Donald Trump. Marco Rubio maintains that we're trying to "peel off" Russia from China. I think that's a post-facto justification for otherwise shocking behavior vis-a-vis Russia and Ukraine, but even so, advocacy for detente or dialogue in any form with China may risk being branded as a Chinese sympathizer.
quotes.m: advocacy for detente or dialogue in any form with China may risk being branded as a Chinese sympathizer.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Trump-era foreign-policy volatility could make US advocacy for dialogue with China politically risky.
quotes.t: Are US EAs Prepared for Democratic Backsliding?

quotes.c: Reasonably often you see appeals that are like, the reason you guys have to stop doing what you're doing is because it is getting in the way of all of us uniting behind President Trump and his glorious agenda to do all of these things. Given that I don't like President Trump, and I think his glorious agenda is bad for our country, these are both the other team. I'm against both of them.
quotes.m: Given that I don't like President Trump, and I think his glorious agenda is bad for our country, these are both the other team. I'm against both of them.
quotes.sum: The speaker opposes Trump and his agenda, while distinguishing between rival factions on the political right.
quotes.t: Interview with Kelsey Piper on Self-Censorship and the Vibe Shift

quotes.c: While this document was established under the Biden administration, the Trump administration seems to be following in the footsteps of the AI NSM . I’m personally inclined to say that the Trump administration, which is inclined to compete for US dominance and avoid red tape, will maintain the pace on all except governance.
quotes.m: the Trump administration, which is inclined to compete for US dominance and avoid red tape, will maintain the pace on all except governance.
quotes.sum: The author predicts that the Trump administration will continue Biden-era AI national-security policy but weaken governance measures.
quotes.t: Cursory Analysis of LLMs in the US Gov (July 2025)

quotes.c: These are great questions, and I'm happy to try answering them. But I've noticed a bit of a pathology: people seem to assume that because I'm (hopefully!) good at the research, I'm automatically well-qualified to answer these broader strategic questions. I think this is a mistake, a form of undue deference that is both incorrect and unhelpful. I certainly try to have good strategic takes, and I think this makes me better at my job, but this is far from sufficient. Being good at research and being good at high level strategic thinking are just fairly different skillsets!
quotes.m: Being good at research and being good at high level strategic thinking are just fairly different skillsets!
quotes.sum: A prominent researcher argues that research skill does not automatically make someone qualified to make high-level strategy decisions.
quotes.t: Good Research Takes are Not Sufficient for Good Strategic Takes

quotes.c: Given the first point, our movement must attract more resources, talent, and funding to address it. The goal is to value align AI with caring about all sentient beings: humans, animals, and potential future digital minds. In other words, I argue we should invest much more in promoting a sentient-centric AI.
quotes.m: The goal is to value align AI with caring about all sentient beings: humans, animals, and potential future digital minds.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI should be designed to care about humans, animals, and future conscious digital beings, and says this deserves far more funding and talent.
quotes.t: AI Moral Alignment: The Most Important Goal of Our Generation

quotes.c: Scoring high on both of these traits normally correlates with right-wing political views. Absolutist animal advocates tend to be politically left-wing. This is some evidence against my theory. However, my observation is that absolutist advocates still tend to be more authoritarian than the average leftist.
quotes.m: However, my observation is that absolutist advocates still tend to be more authoritarian than the average leftist.
quotes.sum: The author says absolutist animal advocates are usually left-wing but, in their view, more authoritarian than the average leftist.
quotes.t: Finding our people in animal advocacy

quotes.c: There is no large-scale AI honesty evaluation to date. There have been multiple documented instances of LLMs engaging in deceptive behavior (CAPTCHA, sycophancy, etc.). Observing instances of suspicious behavior can be suggestive, but anecdotal cases cannot provide a reliable and large-scale quantitative measure for the ML community to work toward.
quotes.m: There is no large-scale AI honesty evaluation to date.
quotes.sum: The author argues that isolated examples of AI deception are inadequate and proposes a large public dataset to measure dishonest model behavior systematically.
quotes.t: A Benchmark for Measuring Honesty in AI Systems

quotes.c: There are many other claims one could make regarding the above. Some popular ones include digital people, simulated lives, and artificial uteruses. I don’t have developed thoughts on how these technologies interact with fertility rates. The same point about needing high credence from above does apply though. And more importantly, if any of these or other claims are the lynchpin for arguments about why extinction should be a main priority, EAs should make the point more explicitly because none of these claims is that obvious.
quotes.m: if any of these or other claims are the lynchpin for arguments about why extinction should be a main priority, EAs should make the point more explicitly because none of these claims is that obvious.
quotes.sum: The author says arguments that extinction should be the main priority often rely on uncertain assumptions about future technologies and should state them openly.
quotes.t: Extinction is probably only 10^10 times worse than one random death

quotes.c: Aquatic animals encompass a wide range of species from fish to crustaceans, and are subjects of increasing concern in welfare discussions. Initiatives by various organisations, including our own (Fish Welfare Initiative and Shrimp Welfare Project), have started to address their needs. However, these efforts represent only the tip of the iceberg.
quotes.m: However, these efforts represent only the tip of the iceberg.
quotes.sum: The author argues that animal-welfare work for fish and crustaceans remains far too limited and needs much more attention.
quotes.t: We (still) need more aquatic animal projects

quotes.c: This report presents an under-discussed alternative: Intelsat, an international organization founded to establish and own the global satellite communications system. We show that Intelsat is proof of concept that a multilateral project to build a commercially and strategically important technology is possible and can achieve intended objectives—providing major benefits to both the US and its allies compared to the US acting alone. We conclude that ‘Intelsat for AGI’ is a valuable complement to existing models of AGI governance.
quotes.m: We conclude that ‘Intelsat for AGI’ is a valuable complement to existing models of AGI governance.
quotes.sum: The author argues that an Intelsat-style international body could jointly build and govern AGI, benefiting the United States and its allies more than unilateral action.
quotes.t: Intelsat as a Model for International AGI Governance

quotes.c: Beyond pragmatic strategy, Promethean Governance represents a fundamental civilizational imperative—a deliberate choice for creative autonomy over passive survival. From terrestrial beginnings (Venice, Byzantium, Fiume) to stellar aspirations (Martian Doge, interstellar networks), the Promethean ethos embodies a philosophical and existential wager: that dynamic creativity and cognitive sovereignty, courageously embraced, produce resilient cultures, meaningful innovation, and sustainable cosmic societies.
quotes.m: Promethean Governance represents a fundamental civilizational imperative—a deliberate choice for creative autonomy over passive survival.
quotes.sum: The author argues that societies should prioritize creative autonomy and cognitive sovereignty over passive survival, extending this ideal to future spacefaring civilizations.
quotes.t: Promethean Governance Ascendant: Lessons from the Forge and Visions for the Cosmic Polity

quotes.c: And I'm not thrilled about the idea of an AI singleton. I think it's kind of terrifying, but for better or worse, that is actually what I'm expecting right now.
quotes.m: I think it's kind of terrifying, but for better or worse, that is actually what I'm expecting right now.
quotes.sum: The speaker expects a single AI to become globally dominant, despite finding that prospect frightening.
quotes.t: Interview with Steven Byrnes on Brain-like AGI, Foom & Doom, and Solving Technical Alignment

quotes.c: Trillions of shrimp are tortured to death every year; thrown on a big thing of ice where they’re frozen and suffocated to death. Every dollar given to the shrimp welfare project anesthetizes around 15,000 shrimp before they endure this horrendous fate, thus averting an unfathomable amount of agony. By estimates so conservative they make Mike Pence look like a leftist radical, the shrimp welfare project averts as much agony, per dollar, as preventing a person from being tortured.
quotes.m: Every dollar given to the shrimp welfare project anesthetizes around 15,000 shrimp before they endure this horrendous fate, thus averting an unfathomable amount of agony.
quotes.sum: The author argues that shrimp suffering is so large and cheaply preventable that everyone, regardless of ethical theory, should support shrimp welfare.
quotes.t: The Virtue Ethics Case For Shrimp Welfare

quotes.c: In this post, I explore an alternative model for AI-era governance frameworks inspired by the Promethean archetype—one that embraces calculated risk, creative autonomy, and heroic individualism rather than precautionary restraint. Drawing on the political structure of the Venetian Republic and the symbolic role of the Doge, I argue for memetic legitimacy as a vital yet underappreciated dimension of institutional authority in a world increasingly mediated by AI and decentralized networks.
quotes.m: I explore an alternative model for AI-era governance frameworks inspired by the Promethean archetype—one that embraces calculated risk, creative autonomy, and heroic individualism rather than precautionary restraint.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI-era institutions should favor calculated risk, individual autonomy, and symbolic legitimacy over precautionary governance.
