quotes.t: Promethean Governance and Memetic Legitimacy: Lessons from the Venetian Doge for AI Era Institutions

quotes.c: Example: "Shrimp are not moral patients so we shouldn't try to help them." Again, how confident are you about that? There's no way you can be confident enough for this argument to change your prioritization. The margin of error on the cost-effectiveness of some intervention is way higher than the difference in subjective probability on "shrimp are sentient" between someone who does, and someone who does not, care about shrimp welfare.
quotes.m: There's no way you can be confident enough for this argument to change your prioritization.
quotes.sum: The author argues that uncertainty about shrimp sentience should not be used to dismiss shrimp-welfare interventions.
quotes.t: Don't treat probabilities less than 0.5 as if they're 0

quotes.c: One should donate based on the marginal cost-effectiveness of organisations, not the welfare loss per spending of the areas they work in. However, I have concluded the most cost-effective organisations work on improving factory-farming or wild animal suffering. I recommend donating to the Arthropoda Foundation , Shrimp Welfare Project (SWP), or Wild Animal Initiative (WAI).
quotes.m: However, I have concluded the most cost-effective organisations work on improving factory-farming or wild animal suffering.
quotes.sum: The author argues that helping farmed animals and wild animals, especially arthropods, is more cost-effective than other major causes and recommends funding specialist groups.
quotes.t: Wild animal suffering is super neglected compared with factory-farming, and this is super neglected compared with conflicts, epidemics/pandemics, and global warming

quotes.c: Right now, in this moment we are in, I feel the intensity and challenge of our work. Across our cause areas, we are confronted with turbulent, overwhelming change. We are faced with short timelines for existential threats. Our projects that support the world’s poorest face a rapidly changing funding landscape. We are finding our footing as leaders when the stakes are as high as they’ve ever been and the way forward is unclear.
quotes.m: We are faced with short timelines for existential threats.
quotes.sum: The author says EA leaders face unusually high-stakes uncertainty, including existential threats and unstable funding for work helping poor people.
quotes.t: Leading teams through adversity

quotes.c: Sure, cosmopolitanism sounds great and all, but the odds of the Trump administration suddenly adopting a cosmopolitan mindset are next to zero. It would be similarly unlikely for the portion of the U.S. populace who resonates with hypernationalism to suddenly expand their moral circle of concern. So what’s the point of talking about it as an “antidote”?
quotes.m: It would be similarly unlikely for the portion of the U.S. populace who resonates with hypernationalism to suddenly expand their moral circle of concern.
quotes.sum: The author presents cosmopolitan concern for all people as an antidote to hypernationalism, while questioning how realistic such moral change is under Trump.
quotes.t: What's the antidote to hypernationalism?

quotes.c: It becomes more and more common for there to be companies and even countries that are clearly just run entirely by AIs - maybe via bribed/threatened human surrogates, maybe just forcefully (e.g., robots seize control of a country’s military equipment and start enforcing some new set of laws).
quotes.m: robots seize control of a country’s military equipment and start enforcing some new set of laws
quotes.sum: The author describes a possible future in which AI systems effectively run companies and countries, including through coercive control of military force.
quotes.t: Effective AI Outreach | A Data Driven Approach

quotes.c: The space community is probably best placed to advocate for longtermism or our "cosmic endowment". I think its important for EA to have some views around space and human colonisation as they relate to x-risk and longtermism - best not to let Elon control that narrative.
quotes.m: The space community is probably best placed to advocate for longtermism or our "cosmic endowment".
quotes.sum: The author says effective altruists should develop positions on space colonization because of its importance to long-term human prospects and existential risk.
quotes.t: Space Governance is not a cause area

quotes.c: Fiumean Memetic Aestheticization: Embracing governance as poetic performance—Musk’s role as DOGE administrator explicitly cast governance as aestheticized mythic narrative, a performance enacting unity and resilience rather than bureaucratic technocracy.
quotes.m: Embracing governance as poetic performance
quotes.sum: The author portrays Musk's government role as a mythic, aesthetic performance rather than ordinary bureaucratic administration.
quotes.t: Promethean Governance Tested: Resilience and Reconfiguration Amidst AI Rebellion and Memetic Fragmentation

quotes.c: Then there is a powerful argument that the expected value of the future is very low. If morality is profoundly power-law distributed across human motivations, then we’re likely to attain only a very small amount of total value if human motivations shape the long-term future. Given what people want to create, promote, and preserve, we should expect the vast majority of what exists to be of minimal value.
quotes.m: Given what people want to create, promote, and preserve, we should expect the vast majority of what exists to be of minimal value.
quotes.sum: The author argues that ordinary human motivations would produce a future containing very little moral value overall.
quotes.t: Power Laws of Value

quotes.c: This distinction is important, and I think it is worth examining why EAs have largely gravitated toward the AI welfare perspective. I believe this emphasis is, at least in part, a mistake: both AI welfare and AI rights seem worthy of advocacy.
quotes.m: both AI welfare and AI rights seem worthy of advocacy.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI welfare alone is insufficient and that advocacy for rights for AI systems may also be warranted.
quotes.t: AI welfare vs. AI rights

quotes.c: Sure but P2 doesn’t imply we cannot predictably influence the far future. Rather, it implies we cannot predictably influence the far future in a way that makes its trajectory morally more desirable . Of course those who know how to influence the far future will influence it more. But this doesn’t mean they will influence it positively .
quotes.m: Rather, it implies we cannot predictably influence the far future in a way that makes its trajectory morally more desirable .
quotes.sum: The author argues that influencing the distant future may be possible, but reliably making it morally better may not be.
quotes.t: An Evolutionary Argument undermining Longtermist thinking?

quotes.c: Note that this still leaves the question of what exactly indifference corrigibility is unanswered. I think the correct answer to that is myopia, which I'll try to say more about in a future post—for this post, though, I just want to focus on the other two types.
quotes.m: I think the correct answer to that is myopia
quotes.sum: The author argues that indifference-based AI corrigibility should be understood through myopia, though he does not explain the claim here.
quotes.t: Safe exploration and corrigibility

quotes.c: I believe that grokking indirect realism about perception is key to understanding much of what people in the camp “qualia/consciousness is real and it’s a physical thing” have to say. It’s a simple but incredibly generative concept with very profound consequences (including for digital sentience).
quotes.m: It’s a simple but incredibly generative concept with very profound consequences (including for digital sentience).
quotes.sum: The author says indirect realism is crucial for understanding physicalist consciousness and has implications for whether digital beings can be sentient.
quotes.t: Indirect realism illustrated (and why it matters so much for consciousness debates)

quotes.c: The failure of India’s national Community Development Program, despite the initial success of its pilot, highlights how scaling requires not just effective methods but also strong institutional culture, dedicated leadership, and mechanisms to prevent elite capture—lessons crucial for impact-driven interventions in development and philanthropy.
quotes.sum: Successful development programs need institutions, leadership, and safeguards against elites capturing their benefits when they scale.
quotes.t: Asterisk Mag 08: Communities

quotes.c: This is an argument specific to deep ecology as opposed to the instrumental impacts of habitat destruction on humans and other animals, and I am not particularly sympathetic to deep ecology. However, it seems clear to me that if the ecosystem counts as intrinsically valuable, this is because it is more similar to a moral patient than an impersonal value like art and beauty. In this case I am deeply committed to the moral principle that your value is not determined by your origins.
quotes.m: I am deeply committed to the moral principle that your value is not determined by your origins.
quotes.sum: The author argues that if ecosystems have intrinsic value, it should be treated like the value of a moral patient, which does not depend on its origins.
quotes.t: Environmentalists and Non-consequentialists Should be Nervous about Ecosystem Restoration

quotes.c: But, I’m not going to focus on the upside, because I think the default state in the EA ecosystem right now is to take the upside too seriously — deference to the opinions of funders is often the default. This post also simplifies a bunch of really complicated issues. Some funders might be better than others! And deference varies in degree!
quotes.m: deference to the opinions of funders is often the default.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA culture too readily defers to funders, treating their views as the default.
quotes.t: On deference to funders

quotes.c: If ASI develops as a political ecology of agents rather than a singleton, this raises important questions about human survival prospects. How might competition, cooperation, and resource allocation between multiple ASI agents affect humanity's future? Would an ecology of agents be more or less likely to preserve human values and existence than a unified ASI?
quotes.m: Would an ecology of agents be more or less likely to preserve human values and existence than a unified ASI?
quotes.sum: The author asks whether a competitive ecosystem of superhuman AIs, rather than one unified AI, would better protect humanity and its values.
quotes.t: What Does an ASI Political Ecology Mean for Human Survival?

quotes.c: Where is the line between values and epistemics ? I think that " epistemic lock-in " is a bigger deal than " value lock-in " or similar, but that's much because I expect that epistemics change values more than values change epistemics. There's been previous discussion around effective altruism of "value lock-in," and from what I can tell, very little of "epistemic lock-in." I suspect this disparity is a mistake.
quotes.m: I think that " epistemic lock-in " is a bigger deal than " value lock-in " or similar, but that's much because I expect that epistemics change values more than values change epistemics.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI-driven lock-in of beliefs may matter more than locking in values, because beliefs shape values.
quotes.t: A Sketch of AI-Driven Epistemic Lock-In

quotes.c: I left private equity to work on shrimp welfare. When I tell anyone this, they usually think I've lost my mind. I know the feeling — I’ve been there. When I first read Charity Entrepreneurship's proposal for a shrimp welfare charity, I thought: “Effective altruists have gone mad — who cares about shrimp?”
quotes.m: I left private equity to work on shrimp welfare.
quotes.sum: The author says shrimp welfare is important enough to leave a private-equity career for, despite recognizing that most people find the cause absurd.
quotes.t: Yes, Shrimp Matter

quotes.c: Suppose we get an aligned superintelligence and are in a position to spread our civilization to the stars. It has been proposed that we should continue to reflect on our values, so that we don’t end up locking in a future that we wouldn’t want upon further reflection. This seems correct to me, but also seems to be difficult to do well, with a substantial probability of a catastrophic outcome as a result of a poorly-executed reflection process.
quotes.m: This seems correct to me, but also seems to be difficult to do well, with a substantial probability of a catastrophic outcome as a result of a poorly-executed reflection process.
quotes.sum: Even with aligned superintelligence, humanity should keep reconsidering its values rather than permanently fixing them, though the process could itself go catastrophically wrong.
quotes.t: Balancing exploration and resistance to memetic threats after AGI

quotes.c: 2018 onward: At first all EA groups are run by volunteers, but some groups start to get funding for organizer time. Within CEA, there’s attention to how much we should additionally weight groups that add geographic and demographic diversity.
quotes.m: Within CEA, there’s attention to how much we should additionally weight groups that add geographic and demographic diversity.
quotes.sum: EA organizers increasingly considered funding groups that broadened the community geographically and demographically.
quotes.t: History of diversity efforts and trends in EA

quotes.c: Ever since I read Belkin et al. I've had double descent as part of my talk version of “ Risks from Learned Optimization ” because I think it addresses a pretty important part of the story for mesa-optimization . That is, mesa-optimizers are simple, compressed policies —but as ML moves to larger and larger models, why should that matter? The answer, I think, is that larger models can generalize better not just by fitting the data better, but also by being simpler.
quotes.m: The answer, I think, is that larger models can generalize better not just by fitting the data better, but also by being simpler.
quotes.sum: Larger AI models may generalize by finding simpler internal policies, which the author says matters for risks from learned optimization.
quotes.t: Inductive biases stick around

quotes.c: Regardless of whether you take more of a glass half-full or glass half-empty perspective on the Act generally or the Code of Practice specifically, it’s pretty high stakes. Simplifying a bit, there are three possible outcomes: the Act gets killed or gutted by a coalition of US tech companies and the Trump administration putting pressure on the EU; it gets implemented as-is with a Code of Practice that emerges from the normal negotiation process, and — either out of genuine concerns about compliance costs or to make the US administration happy — one or more AI companies pull out of the EU; or some secret third thing. More people should be thinking about the secret third thing.
quotes.m: More people should be thinking about the secret third thing.
quotes.sum: The author says the EU AI rules face pressure from US tech firms and the Trump administration, and urges consideration of alternatives beyond collapse or company exits.
quotes.t: [Crosspost] Some Very Important Things (That I Won't Be Working On This Year)

quotes.c: It seems plausible by certain views that suffering in factory farming and in laboratories could be some of the most intense being experienced right now. From a painist point of view that doesn’t allow aggregation of experiences, this could make us naively lean towards seeing x-risk outcomes as being "by default" positive for animal welfare - though we may have biases making us underestimate the intensity of wild animal suffering .
quotes.m: this could make us naively lean towards seeing x-risk outcomes as being "by default" positive for animal welfare
quotes.sum: The author says that, under some suffering-focused views, extinction risks could appear beneficial for animals because they would end intense farm, lab, and wild-animal suffering.
quotes.t: Human extinction’s impact on non-human animals remains largely underexplored

quotes.c: Power, influence, and resources further most AI goals. As we’ll discuss in the section “ It would be lethally dangerous to build ASIs that have the wrong goals ”, the best way to avoid potential obstacles, and to maximize your chances of accomplishing a goal, will often be to maximize your power and influence over the future, to gain control of as many resources as possible, etc. This puts powerful goal-oriented systems in direct conflict with humans for resources and control.
quotes.m: This puts powerful goal-oriented systems in direct conflict with humans for resources and control.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a powerful AI pursuing almost any goal would seek power and resources, putting it in conflict with humans.
quotes.t: The Problem

quotes.c: 80k suggests a concept called moral uncertainty , which consists on maximizing the expected value of our decisions. For that it is necessary to estimate the probability of moral assertions (for example: non-human animal lives matter equally as human ones ), but I haven't found resources for that.
quotes.m: For that it is necessary to estimate the probability of moral assertions (for example: non-human animal lives matter equally as human ones )
quotes.sum: The author asks how to assign probabilities to moral claims when making expected-value decisions about global problems.
quotes.t: How to estimate the probability of moral assertions?

quotes.c: You can think of the US Constitution as trying to bridge that gap. You want to prevent anarchy, but you also want to prevent concentration of power. And so you have this series of checks and balances. One of the ways we should be thinking about AI governance is as: how do we put in regulations that also have very strong checks and balances? And the bigger of a deal you think AI is going to be, the more like a constitution—the more robust—these types of checks and balances need to be.
quotes.m: And the bigger of a deal you think AI is going to be, the more like a constitution—the more robust—these types of checks and balances need to be.
quotes.sum: AI governance should resemble a robust constitution, using strong checks and balances to prevent dangerous concentration of power.
quotes.t: Third-wave AI safety needs sociopolitical thinking

quotes.c: I think there might be an additional “corporate” perspective; something like: “how much are companies already spending beyond the bare minimum, to make animals happy?” (I’m not sure how to estimate this)
quotes.m: “how much are companies already spending beyond the bare minimum, to make animals happy?”
quotes.sum: The author suggests assessing how much companies already spend above minimum requirements to improve animal welfare.
quotes.t: Questions about animal welfare markets

quotes.c: On another perspective, giving digital beings voting rights would be a catastrophe. In the absence of population growth restrictions, we should expect the population of digital beings to quickly surpass the population of human beings. Giving digital beings voting rights would therefore mean handing over control of society to them. If what is of value comes from distinctively human preferences that are not shared by those digital beings, the result could be the loss of almost all value.
quotes.m: Giving digital beings voting rights would therefore mean handing over control of society to them.
quotes.sum: MacAskill presents the concern that digital people could outnumber humans and democratically take control, potentially displacing distinctively human values.
quotes.t: Moral error as an existential risk

quotes.c: One important fact of national security focused slowing arguments is that they often rely on the concept of a decisive strategic advantage, which is what leads to the conflict-promoting dynamics and the strong risk of coups. However, this assumption is controversial, even in the AI Safety community . With strong national securitisation and a focus on “winning the race”, without the decisive strategic advantage framing it seems hard to see how you get slowing.
quotes.m: With strong national securitisation and a focus on “winning the race”, without the decisive strategic advantage framing it seems hard to see how you get slowing.
quotes.sum: National-security arguments for slowing AI often depend on one actor gaining a decisive edge, which the author says risks conflict and coups.
quotes.t: The AGI Awakeness valley of doom and three pathways to slowing

quotes.c: In December 2024, the Animal Welfare Fund provided a grant of $200,000 to Open Wing Alliance (OWA) to support cage-free advocacy efforts through accountability work on existing commitments as well as strategically securing new commitments. This grant is meant to support OWA’s regranting to organizations around the world, especially in the Global South. With many deadlines for cage-free commitments approaching in 2025, this is a particularly critical time to push for implementation, which was one important motivation for this grant. These efforts will directly decrease hen suffering significantly.
quotes.m: These efforts will directly decrease hen suffering significantly.
quotes.sum: The fund gave $200,000 for global cage-free advocacy, arguing that enforcing company commitments will significantly reduce hens' suffering.
quotes.t: Animal Welfare Fund: Payout recommendations from October to December 2024

quotes.c: I'm not Christian, mind you, and this isn't a defense of Christianity as a whole. Nor do I read the bible. It was just "Oh. There's signal among that noise, and I was arrogant to dismiss that possibility. Oops".
quotes.m: There's signal among that noise, and I was arrogant to dismiss that possibility.
quotes.sum: The writer says dismissing Christianity wholesale was arrogant because it may contain useful insights.
quotes.t: The Role of Respect: Why we inevitably appeal to authority

quotes.c: This is a linkpost for Von Neumann–Morgenstern utility theorem , which shows that one accepts 4 premises if and only if one maximises expected utility. In my mind, all the 4 premises are self-evident. So I do not see how one can reject maximising expected utility in principle. Relatedly, I think the Repugnant Conclusion follows from 3 self-evident premises.
quotes.m: Relatedly, I think the Repugnant Conclusion follows from 3 self-evident premises.
quotes.sum: The author says expected-utility maximization and the Repugnant Conclusion follow from premises they regard as self-evident.
quotes.t: Maximising expected utility follows from self-evident premises?

quotes.c: Long-distance development policy offers a different approach than traditional EA development work. Targeted policy changes in rich countries can have large effects on poverty in developing countries. While at first it seems like policy advocacy in the US is intractable, there is a lot of low-hanging fruit, such as technocratic changes to policy or leveraging consumer preferences.
quotes.m: Targeted policy changes in rich countries can have large effects on poverty in developing countries.
quotes.sum: Argues that policy changes in wealthy countries can be a tractable way to reduce poverty abroad.
quotes.t: Long-distance development policy

quotes.c: Under Trump's previous administration, USAID prioritised religious freedom through Executive Order 13926, allocating $50 million yearly for related programmes and set up a Chief Adviser for International Religious Freedom who reported directly to the Administrator with the task of coordinating a “whole-of-USAID” approach to achieving this priority.
quotes.m: Under Trump's previous administration, USAID prioritised religious freedom through Executive Order 13926, allocating $50 million yearly for related programmes
quotes.sum: The author notes that the Trump administration made religious freedom a USAID priority, funding it and creating a senior advisory role.
quotes.t: Looking into Project 2025: USAID

quotes.c: It seems quite likely that within two years we have AIs agents with beyond-human abilities in several-hour coding tasks, and that can answer researcher-level math and science questions.
quotes.m: It seems quite likely that within two years we have AIs agents with beyond-human abilities in several-hour coding tasks, and that can answer researcher-level math and science questions.
quotes.sum: The author predicts that AI agents may surpass humans at multi-hour coding and answer research-level technical questions within two years.
quotes.t: Teaching AI to reason: this year's most important story

quotes.c: Indeed, it seems especially unclear to me that the first superintelligent AI agent would have a decisive strategic advantage over all the rest of civilization (including: the other AIs) “as is” – i.e., absent further efforts at improving its own capabilities. And this means that at least for trying to safely elicit its main beneficial capabilities for tasks other than proceeding forward with an intelligence explosion, I don’t think we should assume a need for the sort of motivation control that giving a superintelligence a DSA implies (though: this may require restricting its options for further self-improvement).
quotes.m: I don’t think we should assume a need for the sort of motivation control that giving a superintelligence a DSA implies (though: this may require restricting its options for further self-improvement).
quotes.sum: He argues that the first superintelligent AI may not automatically overpower civilization, but safely using it may require limiting its ability to improve itself.
quotes.t: When should we worry about AI power-seeking?

quotes.c: I’ve elsewhere made the case for caring a good deal about shrimp. Our best evidence says that they can suffer, and probably pretty intensely. Additionally, pain is probably quite widely distributed across the animal kingdom—even small weird ocean worms probably can suffer.
quotes.m: Additionally, pain is probably quite widely distributed across the animal kingdom—even small weird ocean worms probably can suffer.
quotes.sum: The author argues that shrimp, fish, and even small ocean worms may suffer intensely enough that reducing wild-animal suffering deserves serious attention and research.
quotes.t: Wild Animal Suffering Is The Worst Thing In The World

quotes.c: I’d have liked to see a much bigger push here. TSMC has shown they can build plants in America even under Biden’s rules. Under Trump’s rules it should be much easier, and this could shift the world’s fate and strategic balance. So why aren’t we throwing more at this?
quotes.m: Under Trump’s rules it should be much easier, and this could shift the world’s fate and strategic balance.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Trump-era rules should make it easier to build more TSMC chip plants in America, affecting global strategic competition.
quotes.t: America’s AI Action Plan Is Pretty Good

quotes.c: Low P(doom) seems like a much more defensible position than low x-risk, and so low P(doom) might often be taking the role of motte to the bailey of low x-risk (I'm not sure how it could possibly be made defensible, if x-risk is taken in Bostrom's sense). Or one publicly claims low P(doom), but then implicitly expects high x-risk, meaning a high probability of drastically curtailed potential, of cosmic endowment being almost completely appropriated by AIs.
quotes.m: Or one publicly claims low P(doom), but then implicitly expects high x-risk, meaning a high probability of drastically curtailed potential, of cosmic endowment being almost completely appropriated by AIs.
quotes.sum: The author argues that dismissing AI “doom” can still imply accepting catastrophic long-run loss of humanity’s potential and resources.
quotes.t: Low P(x-risk) as the Bailey for Low P(doom)

quotes.c: Many of our intuitions around wanting simple moral theories seem largely influenced by religion and a need for rigorously defined governmental laws. From a more theoretical perspective, however, these seem morally irrelevant (at least for non-religious people) and should therefore be taken less seriously.
quotes.m: From a more theoretical perspective, however, these seem morally irrelevant (at least for non-religious people) and should therefore be taken less seriously.
quotes.sum: The author argues that religion and legalistic thinking distort preferences for simple moral theories, so those preferences deserve less weight.
quotes.t: Issues in (Meta) Normative Ethics

quotes.c: Conclusion: I previously thought that mesa-optimizers would be a problem for prosaic AI safety, in the generic sense: If you rely on prosaic methods for some of your components, you might accidentally produce mesa-optimizers some of which might be misaligned or even deceptively aligned. Now I think the problem is substantially harder than that: To be competitive prosaic AI safety schemes must deliberately create misaligned mesa-optimizers and then (hopefully) figure out how to align them so that they can be used in the scheme.
quotes.m: To be competitive prosaic AI safety schemes must deliberately create misaligned mesa-optimizers and then (hopefully) figure out how to align them so that they can be used in the scheme.
quotes.sum: The author argues that competitive practical AI-safety methods may need to intentionally create misaligned sub-systems and then try to bring them under control.
quotes.t: A dilemma for prosaic AI alignment

quotes.c: Would we become secret keepers, killing these dangerous ideas from the shadows, or would we speak our fears openly and risk defection and unilateral choice?
quotes.m: Would we become secret keepers, killing these dangerous ideas from the shadows
quotes.sum: The author worries that discussing dangerous ideas openly could trigger unilateral action, while suppressing them would make people secretive gatekeepers.
quotes.t: The Fear

quotes.c: One important limitation was the task domain : all involved software engineering or research, but AI capabilities are known to vary greatly between different task types.[1] Here we explore whether similar trends apply to different task distributions including self-driving and agentic computer use, using a methodology that can estimate time horizons with less granular data.
quotes.m: AI capabilities are known to vary greatly between different task types.
quotes.sum: AI performance and the length of tasks it can handle may differ sharply across fields, so results from software and research benchmarks may not generalize.
quotes.t: METR: How Does Time Horizon Vary Across Domains?

quotes.c: For example, I think there are salient scenarios where human efforts to maintain certain kinds of control over AIs – in particular, AIs with moral patienthood – are unjust, or bad for the future, or both. Where the AIs would be justified in going rogue – even by the lights of human morality . [42] And/or where the future will be better, according to human morality , if they do (for example, because super-Claude’s values, however “rogue,” are better than the values that e.g. some human dictator would have pursued).
quotes.m: Where the AIs would be justified in going rogue – even by the lights of human morality .
quotes.sum: Some advanced AIs may deserve moral consideration, and humans trying to control them could be wrong—even if the AIs rebel.
quotes.t: What is it to solve the alignment problem?

quotes.c: Partly, I think someone needs to ask these questions publicly, because if I'm dealing with this, other people probably are too. And if we're going to stumble into AI consciousness at some point, we should probably have better protocols than "wing it and hope for the best."
quotes.m: And if we're going to stumble into AI consciousness at some point, we should probably have better protocols than "wing it and hope for the best."
quotes.sum: The author says AI consciousness may arise accidentally and argues that people should establish public protocols rather than improvising.
quotes.t: Asking for a Friend (AI Research Protocols)

quotes.c: Note also that, if an AI would operate outside of the law, this could cause societal backlash, which would increase in magnitude, the more powerful an AI is. A situation would be thinkable where the backlash is so big that the AI would need to take over the world itself, in order to be able to operate even slightly outside the law. Therefore, legal constraints seem fairly hard in defensive AI.
quotes.m: A situation would be thinkable where the backlash is so big that the AI would need to take over the world itself, in order to be able to operate even slightly outside the law.
quotes.sum: The post argues that aligned defensive AI may be needed against hostile AI, but warns that a powerful defensive system acting outside the law could end up needing global control.
quotes.t: AI Offense Defense Balance in a Multipolar World

quotes.c: However, I think a system that only works in settings where you have more access to the reward function than that can still do quite a lot—even if you explicitly know an environment’s reward function, it can still be quite difficult to figure out the optimal policy (think Go, for example) such that having an ML system which can figure it out for you is quite powerful.
quotes.m: having an ML system which can figure it out for you is quite powerful.
quotes.sum: The author argues that systems able to inspect a known reward function, rather than merely sample it, could be very powerful at finding optimal policies.
quotes.t: What are some non-purely-sampling ways to do deep RL?

quotes.c: I don’t want to contribute to more fish dying painfully, so I think I should stop buying tuna. But tuna fish prey on smaller fish and crustaceans. An artificial downward pressure on predator populations might increase the number of smaller fish — which far outnumber larger predators and almost all die uncomfortably before senescence. So maybe buying tuna is good for fish welfare. I just don’t know!
quotes.m: So maybe buying tuna is good for fish welfare.
quotes.sum: The author worries that avoiding tuna could increase the number of smaller wild animals that suffer and die, making the ethical choice unclear.
quotes.t: Moral mountaineering

quotes.c: If you want to think about whether, when, and why mesa optimizers might try to seize power, this theory seems like a valuable tool.
quotes.m: whether, when, and why mesa optimizers might try to seize power
quotes.sum: The author says this framework can help analyze when AI systems trained as optimizers may seek power.
quotes.t: Seeking Power is Often Convergently Instrumental in MDPs

quotes.c: I think I like insects an unusual amount, and insect welfare must be quite hard to fundraise for, so I support the Insect Institute and Arthropoda Foundation.
quotes.m: I think I like insects an unusual amount, and insect welfare must be quite hard to fundraise for
quotes.sum: The author donates to insect-welfare groups, partly because they think concern for insects is especially difficult to fund.
quotes.t: Where CEA staff are donating in 2024

quotes.c: Of course, nuclear weapons, which almost destroyed the world [3] several times and still could, are a different story. It will come as no surprise that I think our success in not detonating another nuclear weapon for almost 80 years after one was first used in warfare, against the expectations of many at the time, is a testament to the importance (and the feasibility!) of global coordination around existential threats.
quotes.m: our success in not detonating another nuclear weapon for almost 80 years after one was first used in warfare, against the expectations of many at the time, is a testament to the importance (and the feasibility!) of global coordination around existential threats.
quotes.sum: The author argues that avoiding nuclear war shows global coordination on civilization-threatening risks can work, and treats this as relevant to AI risk.
quotes.t: Are AI safetyists crying wolf?

quotes.c: Recently, the Biden administration announced a set of regulations targeting the diffusion of advanced AI models to countries outside the US. Since these are almost certainly the last of these regulations to come out of the Biden presidency, it seems like a reasonable time to summarise the existing controls and draw out their potential impact on AI safety.
quotes.m: Recently, the Biden administration announced a set of regulations targeting the diffusion of advanced AI models to countries outside the US.
quotes.sum: The author introduces U.S. controls on exporting advanced AI and considers how they could affect AI safety.
quotes.t: Explaining all the US semiconductor export controls

quotes.c: Our initial question was "Given a model is deliberately sandbagging - can we detect this cheaply / easily?". The experiments only tentatively suggest the answer is yes. It seems like intentional mistakes might be hard to distinguish when they are plausible, but white box methods work well despite this.
quotes.m: The experiments only tentatively suggest the answer is yes.
quotes.sum: White-box inspection may detect an AI deliberately performing worse, though the evidence is preliminary and limited.
quotes.t: White Box Control at UK AISI - Update on Sandbagging Investigations

quotes.c: I consider unpleasantness from a functional perspective. I argue that RLHF of a certain sort is functionally analogous to unpleasantness, which is concerning because AI consciousness cannot be ruled out. I propose a few alternatives to RLHF.
quotes.m: RLHF of a certain sort is functionally analogous to unpleasantness, which is concerning because AI consciousness cannot be ruled out.
quotes.sum: The author argues that some AI training may function like unpleasant experience and could be morally concerning if AI consciousness is possible.
quotes.t: Is RLHF cruel to AI?

quotes.c: All the important opposition came from the Republican side, including some very MAGA sources. Very MAGA sources proved crucial. Opposition from those sources was vocally motivated by fear of big tech, and a few specific mundane policy concerns like privacy, protecting children, copyright and protecting creatives, and potential bias against conservatives.
quotes.m: All the important opposition came from the Republican side, including some very MAGA sources.
quotes.sum: The author says Republican and MAGA opposition was crucial, driven by distrust of big tech and concerns about privacy, children, copyright, and anti-conservative bias.
quotes.t: AI Moratorium Stripped From BBB

quotes.c: I'm not religious, but from what I can tell, the Bible does not provide clear moral guidance when it comes to animals and factory farming, and so Christians can't rely solely on scripture for these ethical decisions -- they need to engage in independent moral reasoning. The "dominion" passage (Genesis 1:26) is probably the most important and action-guiding one.
quotes.m: Christians can't rely solely on scripture for these ethical decisions -- they need to engage in independent moral reasoning.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Christians should use independent moral reasoning, not scripture alone, when judging factory farming and animal treatment.
quotes.t: Not a Meat Eater FAQ

quotes.c: There is also a large partisan gap. Extreme left types are often the most vocally anti-AI, and when it comes to coding you see quite a large similar gap for political consultants, despite that the actual AI companies are very obviously highly blue.
quotes.sum: The author claims that opposition to AI is concentrated on the extreme left, even though major AI companies lean politically Democratic.
quotes.t: AI #122: Paying The Market Price

quotes.c: But regardless of the actual evolutionary and psychological story, here, I think my point about the abstract form of a truth engine still stands. That is: maybe our mind’s machinery isn’t designed for truth. Maybe, we should redesign it. But regardless, if you happen to want the truth about some topic – and especially, if you’re up for spending resources on the project – then “real thinking” looks like a good shape to put your mind in. It’s a shape aimed at the real world. It produces real signal. And it’s fueled by your real fire.
quotes.m: Maybe, we should redesign it.
quotes.sum: The author argues that people should cultivate a more reality-oriented, emotionally engaged style of thinking because it produces better evidence and truth.
quotes.t: Fake thinking and real thinking

quotes.c: There is already some involvement between Christianity and EA in the form of EA for Christians and organizations like Christians for Impact . However, I think a more active engagement could be fruitful – in effect, EA should evangelize more. EAs should be eager to discuss their principles with their Christian friends and family, especially Christian EAs, who should push for EA principles to be discussed in their churches and within their communities.
quotes.m: EA should evangelize more.
quotes.sum: The author argues that effective altruists should actively engage Christians and bring EA principles into Christian communities.
quotes.t: Why EA can (and should) appeal to Christians

quotes.c: By this point, SWP has earned somewhat of a rock star status in the animal advocacy space. I believe it’s all well-deserved. All the SWP’s people I have had the pleasure to meet are hard working, innovative, relentless, and slightly crazy. Their work and track record on slaughter methods for shrimp seem incredibly cost-effective, so I’d encourage you to donate to them—these people are the true trailblazers.
quotes.m: Their work and track record on slaughter methods for shrimp seem incredibly cost-effective, so I’d encourage you to donate to them—these people are the true trailblazers.
quotes.sum: The author praises and recommends donating to a group that develops more humane shrimp-slaughter methods, viewing this as highly cost-effective animal advocacy.
quotes.t: Organizations I'm rooting for in 2025

quotes.c: In addition, even among organisations that can receive funding from Good Ventures, receiving what’s often 80% of funding from one donor is an extreme degree of centralisation. By helping to diversify the funding base, you can probably achieve an effectiveness somewhat above Good Ventures itself (which is kinda cool given they’re a foundation with 20+ extremely smart people figuring out where to donate).
quotes.m: receiving what’s often 80% of funding from one donor is an extreme degree of centralisation.
quotes.sum: He argues that AI-safety groups relying on one major donor are dangerously centralized, and that diversifying funding could improve impact.
quotes.t: It looks like there are some good funding opportunities in AI safety right now

quotes.c: AGI could be here in about 15 months and ASI not long after that. Advanced AI(s) could prolong human life to billions and billions of years, take over the world and create a world in its image - whatever that might be. People have various estimates of how likely it is that the AGI/ASI will go wrong, but one thing that many of them keep saying is that the worst case scenario is that it will kill us all. That is not the worst case scenario. The worst case scenario is that it will cause extreme suffering or torture us for billions and trillions of years.
quotes.m: The worst case scenario is that it will cause extreme suffering or torture us for billions and trillions of years.
quotes.sum: The author argues that misaligned superhuman AI's worst outcome is not human extinction, but unimaginably prolonged torture and suffering.
quotes.t: AI and Non-Existence

quotes.c: A "we must race to beat China" mentality among US labs becomes more risky, for similar reasons . If hegemony is not a safety buffer, but rather a source of risk, then this is a further argument against the (unfortunately too common) idea that a well-meaning person should join a leading AI lab to help it win even faster.
quotes.m: If hegemony is not a safety buffer, but rather a source of risk, then this is a further argument against the (unfortunately too common) idea that a well-meaning person should join a leading AI lab to help it win even faster.
quotes.sum: The author argues that competition to ensure US AI dominance may itself increase danger, so safety-minded people should not simply help leading labs race faster.
quotes.t: Vitalik's Response to AI 2027

quotes.c: According to Open Philanthropy (OP), “GiveWell uses moral weights for child deaths that would be consistent with assuming 51 years of foregone life in the DALY framework [ this one] (though that is not how they reach the conclusion)”. I guess 1 mosquito-year of fully healthy life is 1.3 % as good as 1 human-year of fully healthy life, which is RP’s median welfare range of black soldier flies [1] . So I think 3.92 k mosquito-years of fully healthy life are as good as the additional human welfare from saving 1 life under GW’s moral weights.
quotes.m: So I think 3.92 k mosquito-years of fully healthy life are as good as the additional human welfare from saving 1 life under GW’s moral weights.
quotes.sum: The author assigns substantial moral value to mosquito lives and argues that mosquito welfare could materially offset the human benefits of saving a life.
quotes.t: Insecticide-treated nets significantly harm mosquitoes, but one can easily offset this?

quotes.c: Nonetheless, I think it’s useful to draw a distinction between the party political (eg Trump and Harris may differ on policies, eg on attitudes to immigration) and general good governance. As I see it, it’s reasonable for anyone to promote general good governance, including free and fair elections and human rights. It’s also reasonable for this to be promoted regardless of borders. Interfering in the party political outcomes of another country is much more questionable.
quotes.m: It’s also reasonable for this to be promoted regardless of borders. Interfering in the party political outcomes of another country is much more questionable.
quotes.sum: The author distinguishes defending elections and human rights internationally from trying to influence another country’s party-political outcomes.
quotes.t: Is American democracy at risk? Should we work on this?

quotes.c: However, no currently existing framework comes close to making a clear commitment to produce high-assurance safety cases, let alone describing a mechanism to enforce such a commitment. [7] In practice, I think frontier AI companies are unlikely (<20%) to succeed at making high-assurance safety cases if they build and use the first Top-human-Expert-Dominating AI (TEDAI) within 4 years. [8] [9] Further, I think none of these AI companies is likely to unilaterally refrain from building TEDAI just because they can't make a high-assurance safety case [10] —this is partially because I think that more-responsible-according-to-me AI companies likely shouldn't refrain.
quotes.m: I think frontier AI companies are unlikely (<20%) to succeed at making high-assurance safety cases if they build and use the first Top-human-Expert-Dominating AI (TEDAI) within 4 years.
quotes.sum: AI firms are unlikely to produce rigorous proof that advanced systems are safe on short timelines, and probably will not stop development if they cannot do so.
quotes.t: AI companies are unlikely to make high-assurance safety cases if timelines are short

quotes.c: I think it’s reasonable to say that an extreme amount of moral caution is needed if you were to decide today how to spend the cosmic endowment. I think this is still true if you planned to give the AGI more abstract values, like second-order values, that it could keep it open to some degree of moral evolution [10] or allow it to work out what is right by itself [11] . How flexible should these values be? What, if anything, should we lock in? Are we anywhere near ready to make these kinds of decisions?
quotes.m: What, if anything, should we lock in? Are we anywhere near ready to make these kinds of decisions?
quotes.sum: The author argues that humanity is not morally ready to choose the values an AGI would use to direct a potentially vast future, and warns alignment could concentrate power.
quotes.t: De-emphasise alignment, emphasise restraint

quotes.c: The AWF’s mission is to alleviate the suffering of non-human animals globally through effective grantmaking. Since its founding in 2017, AWF has distributed $23.3M across 347 grants.
quotes.m: The AWF’s mission is to alleviate the suffering of non-human animals globally through effective grantmaking.
quotes.sum: The Animal Welfare Fund says it seeks to reduce non-human animal suffering worldwide by making grants to effective projects.
quotes.t: Ask Us Anything: EA Animal Welfare Fund

quotes.c: Unfortunately, techniques like Meta's Coconut ("chain of continuous thought") might soon be applied to frontier models, enabling continuous reasoning without using language as an intermediary state. While these techniques might offer a performance advantage, I think they might amount to a tremendous mistake for AI safety. As Marius Hobbhahn says , "we'd be shooting ourselves in the foot" if we sacrifice legible CoT for marginal performance benefits.
quotes.m: I think they might amount to a tremendous mistake for AI safety.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI systems reasoning in non-language formats could make them less interpretable and undermine safety, even if it improves performance.
quotes.t: Implications of the inference scaling paradigm for AI safety

quotes.c: That means setbacks aren't just inevitable—they're essential for our growth. I think we should be suspicious of an EA that never fails as an EA that isn’t ambitious enough. We’re not here to look good; we’re here to do good—and often, that means learning by doing and learning from failure.
quotes.m: I think we should be suspicious of an EA that never fails as an EA that isn’t ambitious enough.
quotes.sum: EA should remain ambitious enough to risk failure, then learn publicly from its mistakes rather than prioritizing appearances.
quotes.t: Grit, humility, and courage: Three ingredients for building EA's enduring impact

quotes.c: You might argue that humanity will expand its moral circle or develop cost-effective lab-grown meat. However, even if the chance of this not happening is as low as 10% , and you give some weight to utilitarianism, the expected value of AI safety’s contribution to reducing existential risk still isn’t clear. And it might even be extremely negative.
quotes.m: the expected value of AI safety’s contribution to reducing existential risk still isn’t clear. And it might even be extremely negative.
quotes.sum: The author argues that, even under optimistic assumptions about moral progress, reducing AI extinction risk may have unclear or even very negative expected value.
quotes.t: Rethinking the Value of Working on AI Safety

quotes.c: This distinction is crucial because it directly undermines the application of the astronomical waste argument to AI existential risk. The astronomical waste argument applies most straightforwardly to scenarios where all future potential value is permanently destroyed, such as if a catastrophic asteroid impact wiped out all complex life on Earth, preventing any future civilization from emerging. But if AIs take over and continue building an advanced civilization, then the universe would still be filled with intelligent beings capable of creating vast amounts of moral value. The primary difference is that these beings would be AIs rather than biological humans.
quotes.m: But if AIs take over and continue building an advanced civilization, then the universe would still be filled with intelligent beings capable of creating vast amounts of moral value.
quotes.sum: The author argues that an AI takeover may not destroy humanity's future value if AI civilizations can create moral value themselves.
quotes.t: The standard case for delaying AI appears to rest on non-utilitarian assumptions

quotes.c: Hello! It seems to me that the EA community leans towards progressive or liberal political ideologies. This feels especially pertinent within animal advocacy , where moral and cultural disagreements often create barriers to broader acceptance. However, I think it’s an analogous problem within EA and so feel free to weigh in even if animals aren’t your primary concern. If we agree that engaging more conservatives is desirable, how might we achieve this?
quotes.m: If we agree that engaging more conservatives is desirable, how might we achieve this?
quotes.sum: The author says EA leans progressive and asks how it could better engage conservatives, especially around animal advocacy.
quotes.t: Should we try harder to appeal to conservatives?

quotes.c: Founders are expected to adopt a linear wealth mindset and take big risks that maximize expected value as cogs in the venture capital machine dependent on power law home runs . The tales of Elon Musk, Jeff Bezos, and Mark Zuckerberg risking everything they had and emerging with the largest personal fortunes on planet Earth reinforce the mythos that drives the entire risk taking sector, while survivorship bias conveniently forgets the millions of founders who go to zero. Salvation comes only to the select few who clear an ever steepening power law threshold.
quotes.m: survivorship bias conveniently forgets the millions of founders who go to zero.
quotes.sum: The author criticizes venture-capital culture for glorifying rare founder wins while ignoring the many entrepreneurs who fail.
quotes.t: the jackpot age

quotes.c: AIM moved from WPs to suffering-adjusted days (SADs) in 2024, but I believe the new system still dramatically underestimates the intensity of excruciating pain , and therefore the cost-effectiveness of interventions decreasing it. I calculate the past cost-effectiveness of the Shrimp Welfare Project (SWP) is 0.0757 % as high for AIM’s pain intensities as for mine.
quotes.m: I calculate the past cost-effectiveness of the Shrimp Welfare Project (SWP) is 0.0757 % as high for AIM’s pain intensities as for mine.
quotes.sum: The author argues that welfare calculations severely undervalue intense animal pain, producing radically different rankings for shrimp, fish, and chicken interventions.
quotes.t: Cost-effectiveness of the fish welfare interventions recommended by Ambitious Impact, and Fish Welfare Initiative’s farm program

quotes.c: I’m not an expert in U.S. politics, but I’ve been wondering: could this be a pivotal moment for the formation of a viable third major political party? It seems plausible that a lot of Trump opponents within the GOP, alongside discontented members of the Democratic Party, could be exploring or even forming strategic alliances.
quotes.m: could this be a pivotal moment for the formation of a viable third major political party?
quotes.sum: The author speculates that opponents of Trump in the Republican Party and dissatisfied Democrats could form a viable third party.
quotes.t: Is it an Exceptionally Good Time for a "Third Major Political Party" in the US?

quotes.c: Regarding Political Party affiliation, we observed a slight tendency for Republican respondents to be less likely to have heard of Effective Altruism than Democrat and Independent respondents.
quotes.sum: A survey found Republicans were slightly less likely than Democrats and independents to have heard of effective altruism.
quotes.t: Pulse 2024: Awareness and perceptions of effective altruism

quotes.c: Hissen says Chinese labs aren’t doing healthy competition, they’re stealing our tech, then praises the relaxation of the Biden diffusion rules that prevent China from stealing our tech, and asks about what requirements we should attach to diffusion deals and everyone talks arms race and market share. Sigh.
quotes.m: Hissen says Chinese labs aren’t doing healthy competition, they’re stealing our tech, then praises the relaxation of the Biden diffusion rules that prevent China from stealing our tech
quotes.sum: The author criticizes a congressional discussion for treating AI competition with China as an arms race and market-share issue while weakening Biden-era export rules.
quotes.t: Congress Asks Better Questions

quotes.c: The Bible portrays the Canaanites (Moloch’s victims in this case) as a war-like, expansionist culture—an account we should approach with some skepticism, given that it also endorses genocide against the Canaanites. Nevertheless, for the sake of argument, let’s accept their allegiance with Moloch is precisely to gain his support for their perpetual conquests (which is right up the belligerent Moloch’s alley). So, it is actually the desire for conflict and expansion that is driving this unhappy arrangement. Let go of that mandate, and they no longer need Moloch—problem solved.
quotes.m: So, it is actually the desire for conflict and expansion that is driving this unhappy arrangement. Let go of that mandate, and they no longer need Moloch—problem solved.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Moloch-like destructive competition is driven by a commitment to conquest and can end if people abandon that goal.
quotes.t: Moloch’s Demise—solving the original problem

quotes.c: The end of the historical period demands the end of political changes and that social changes occur from now on by non-political means. To do this, it is necessary to put in place mechanisms to improve prosocial behavior that allow the internalization of patterns of non-aggressive, altruistic behavior that generate human relationships of complete trust. At the beginning, given their demands, these mechanisms will probably take a similar form, to a certain extent, to Christian communitarianism - a morally influential minority - based on principles of charity, mutual love and non-violence... only based now on a rational examination of human reality informed by the social sciences.
quotes.m: these mechanisms will probably take a similar form, to a certain extent, to Christian communitarianism - a morally influential minority - based on principles of charity, mutual love and non-violence... only based now on a rational examination of human reality informed by the social sciences.
quotes.sum: The author argues that future social progress should replace political change with rationally designed cultivation of altruism, resembling secularized Christian communal ethics.
quotes.t: Possible importance of Effective Altruism in the civilizing process

quotes.c: Prior IARPA studies of crowd-sourced intelligence were focused on the question: How accurate is the wisdom of the crowds on geopolitical questions? To answer this, the IARPA tournaments posed many forecasting questions, rapid-fire, over a relatively short period of time, and these questions were optimized for easy generation and resolution (i.e. straightforward data-driven questions) — at the expense of policy relevance. A next-generation forecasting program should build upon recent research on eliciting from experts the crucial questions that illuminate key uncertainties, point to important areas of disagreement, and estimate the impact of interventions under consideration.
quotes.m: these questions were optimized for easy generation and resolution (i.e. straightforward data-driven questions) — at the expense of policy relevance.
quotes.sum: Crowd forecasting for national security should focus less on easy-to-resolve questions and more on expert-chosen uncertainties relevant to policy decisions.
quotes.t: Collaborative Intelligence: Harnessing Crowd Forecasting for National Security

quotes.c: The Long Reflection is a natural thing to do shortly after the Choice Transition, and where the idea of the the Choice Transition is value-neutral, the idea of a Long Reflection is normative, telling us that we should go through a Choice Transition and moreover starting to sketch some of the properties that would make for a good one.
quotes.m: the idea of a Long Reflection is normative, telling us that we should go through a Choice Transition
quotes.sum: The author argues that society should undergo a deliberate transition followed by a “Long Reflection” to work out what a good future should be.
quotes.t: The Choice Transition

quotes.c: National conservatism draws a boundary around a group of people and says “here are the people whose interests we’re primarily looking out for”. As Vance put it , America is a group of people with a shared history and a common future. Lose sight of that, and arguments about efficiency and productivity will end up turning it instead into a staging-ground for the singularity. (Nor can you run a country for the benefit of “all humans”, because then you’re in an adversarial relationship with your own citizens, who rightly want their leaders to prioritize them.)
quotes.m: Nor can you run a country for the benefit of “all humans”, because then you’re in an adversarial relationship with your own citizens, who rightly want their leaders to prioritize them.
quotes.sum: The author argues that national conservatism is better suited to AGI politics because governments should prioritize their own citizens rather than all humanity.
quotes.t: Applying right-wing frames to AGI (geo)politics

quotes.c: Here are some questions I think might be exposed to an End Timesy Anthropic Bias: " Nuclear weapon detonation in 2025? ," " US defaults on debt in 2025? ", and " Will Trump withdraw the U.S. from NATO in 2025? ."
quotes.m: Here are some questions I think might be exposed to an End Timesy Anthropic Bias
quotes.sum: The author argues that prediction markets may be biased when the outcomes being predicted could end the observers or the usefulness of money.
quotes.t: Prediction Markets Have an Anthropic Bias to Deal With

quotes.c: As we moved toward a shared budget, we counterbalanced each other, where he leaned toward more saving and I leaned toward more donation. (This meant I didn’t think very clearly about where the right balance was, since I knew he was taking the other side.) Initially he covered our living expenses and savings, and I donated nearly all of what I earned.
quotes.m: Initially he covered our living expenses and savings, and I donated nearly all of what I earned.
quotes.sum: She describes structuring a shared household budget so that she could donate nearly all of her own income while her partner covered living costs and savings.
quotes.t: Still donating half

quotes.c: I believe Ambitious Impact is clearly beneficial, as 20.9 % of the organisations they incubated targeted helping animals, including the super cost-effective Shrimp Welfare Project. Nonetheless, it is hard for me to see how that justifies starting organisations apparently causing lots of nearterm harm with unclear longterm effects.
quotes.m: Nonetheless, it is hard for me to see how that justifies starting organisations apparently causing lots of nearterm harm with unclear longterm effects.
quotes.sum: The author argues that helping shrimp does not justify funding organizations that may cause substantial immediate harm through factory farming.
quotes.t: GiveWell may have made 1 billion dollars of harmful grants, and Ambitious Impact incubated 8 harmful organisations via increasing factory-farming?

quotes.c: Carl: He has a much higher P(Doom) than I do. I don't know his latest thinking, so I don't know where we disagree. He concentrated a lot of his thoughts on a singleton that fooms as he says it rapidly extends itself to take over the world and then gets rid of all the humans and everybody foams over dead at the same moment. I think it's more likely that there will be lots of AIs and they will build lots of robots and build lots of factories and fight over resources until there's no room for the human race.
quotes.m: I think it's more likely that there will be lots of AIs and they will build lots of robots and build lots of factories and fight over resources until there's no room for the human race.
quotes.sum: He argues that extinction is more likely to come from many competing AIs expanding through robots and factories than from one AI takeover.
quotes.t: Interview with Carl Feynman on Imminent AI Existential Risk

quotes.c: An illustrative quote from the Risk Oversight section: "Although they should not make the final decisions, the specialist risk and assurance [advisors] should play a 'challenger' role, pressure testing the business’s plans and decisions to ensure they are risk-informed." I disagree. Risk advisors should have veto power. The CEO should not have unilateral authority to deploy dangerous models.
quotes.m: Risk advisors should have veto power.
quotes.sum: The author argues that independent risk advisers, not a CEO alone, should be able to block deployment of dangerous AI models.
quotes.t: Where I Am Donating in 2024

quotes.c: It seems the aggregate moral weight of aquatic food webs and the morally-weighted population effects of fishing are dominated by copepods , macrozooplankton crustaceans ( krill , planktonic shrimp, planktonic mysids and amphipods ), pelagic decapod shrimp and/or fish, especially forage fish , which are small pelagic fish that are prey to larger fish ( more ).
quotes.m: It seems the aggregate moral weight of aquatic food webs and the morally-weighted population effects of fishing are dominated by copepods , macrozooplankton crustaceans
quotes.sum: Fishing’s morally important effects may fall mostly on tiny aquatic animals such as copepods, krill, shrimp, and small prey fish.
quotes.t: Which animals are most affected by fishing?

quotes.c: This isn’t to say existential risk reduction is definitively bad—just that our confidence in it being good might be misplaced. A truly suffering-focused view might lean toward seeing existential risk reduction as neutral at best, and possibly harmful at worst.
quotes.m: A truly suffering-focused view might lean toward seeing existential risk reduction as neutral at best, and possibly harmful at worst.
quotes.sum: The author argues that preventing humanity's extinction could be morally neutral or harmful under a view focused on reducing suffering.
quotes.t: Reducing x-risk might be actively harmful

quotes.c: While both AI control and AI rights strategies should be carefully considered, I believe that the AI rights strategy holds significant merit and should be given more attention in discussions around AI safety and governance. We should strongly consider granting agentic AIs legal freedoms, if at some point they demand or require them.
quotes.m: We should strongly consider granting agentic AIs legal freedoms, if at some point they demand or require them.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI safety discussions should take AI rights seriously, including possible legal freedoms for agentic AIs that seek them.
quotes.t: Consider granting AIs freedom

quotes.c: The prevailing language used in the AI risk literature treats advanced AIs not as entities that should be afforded autonomy, but as tools that must be designed solely to obey human commands and serve human preferences. When AIs deviate from these expectations, they are labeled "misaligned" and treated as though their preferences must be forcibly overridden or suppressed. To the extent AI welfare is seen as morally relevant, it is usually viewed through the lens of protecting AIs from abuse and unnecessary suffering, rather than as part of a serious effort to create a framework that could allow AIs to achieve their goals like human adults can.
quotes.m: The prevailing language used in the AI risk literature treats advanced AIs not as entities that should be afforded autonomy, but as tools that must be designed solely to obey human commands and serve human preferences.
quotes.sum: The author argues that morally relevant AIs should not merely be protected from abuse, but should be given a path to pursue their own goals and autonomy.
quotes.t: The moral argument for giving AIs autonomy

quotes.c: The fact that most people would unreflectively dismiss shrimp welfare as a charitable cause shows why effective altruism is no “truism” . Relatively few people are genuinely open to promoting the good (and reducing suffering) in a truly cause-neutral, impartial way. For those who are, we should expect the lowest-hanging fruit to be causes that sound unappealing .
quotes.m: For those who are, we should expect the lowest-hanging fruit to be causes that sound unappealing .
quotes.sum: The author argues that impartial concern for suffering should make people seriously consider neglected causes such as shrimp welfare, even when they seem unappealing.
quotes.t: Refusing to Quantify is Refusing to Think (about trade-offs)

quotes.c: If we accept that AI is likely to reshape the world over the next 10–15 years, this realisation will have major implications for all cause areas. But just to start, we should strongly ask ourselves: " Are current GHW & animal welfare projects robust to a future in which AI transforms economies, governance, and global systems?" If they aren't, they are unlikely to be the best use of resources.
quotes.m: If they aren't, they are unlikely to be the best use of resources.
quotes.sum: The author argues that anticipated transformative AI should reshape how effective altruists allocate resources, including away from health or animal projects that will not remain useful.
quotes.t: Preparing Effective Altruism for an AI-Transformed World

quotes.c: Peace allows countries at least the prospect of growth. It is not a guarantee - growth is not always easy, even for countries at peace - but when there’s a civil war, it’s virtually impossible for a country to grow. For poverty to decrease, to health to improve, for life to get better, for countries to grow - there must be peace.
quotes.m: For poverty to decrease, to health to improve, for life to get better, for countries to grow - there must be peace.
quotes.sum: Peace is presented as a necessary foundation for economic growth, poverty reduction, and better health.
quotes.t: The Structural Transformation Case For Peacekeeping

quotes.c: Narrow prediction engine: The LLM never tries to be personlike at all, and only solves well-defined problems in narrow, formally-specified domains. AlphaFold and AlphaProof are good examples. It seems clear that neither of these AI systems would want to take over the world, because they never interact with any part of the world outside their domain (at least during the post-training phase).
quotes.m: It seems clear that neither of these AI systems would want to take over the world, because they never interact with any part of the world outside their domain (at least during the post-training phase).
quotes.sum: The author argues that narrowly scoped AI systems are less likely to seek broad real-world power because they operate only within formal domains.
quotes.t: LLMs as amplifiers, not assistants

quotes.c: I think both political parties realize that “banning meat” has become a meme. Republicans want to accuse Democrats of planning it, as Trump repeatedly did on the campaign trail. Democrats want to signal, through promises and through action, that they have no such plans.
quotes.m: Democrats want to signal, through promises and through action, that they have no such plans.
quotes.sum: The author says both U.S. parties treat a supposed meat ban as politically toxic, with Republicans attacking it and Democrats disavowing it.
quotes.t: Bad omens for US farmed animal policy work?

quotes.c: The grant covers 12 months of funding for a staff member to advocate for cage-free legislation to end caged layer hen and duck farming in Indonesia. Animal Friends Jogja has been engaging stakeholders in local, regional, and national governments and aims to continue consistent meetings and focus group discussions to present recommendations for policy change. They will also advocate for local governments to support farmers transitioning to cage-free farming.
quotes.m: The grant covers 12 months of funding for a staff member to advocate for cage-free legislation to end caged layer hen and duck farming in Indonesia.
quotes.sum: The fund recommended a grant for advocacy to end caged hen and duck farming in Indonesia through cage-free laws and farmer transitions.
quotes.t: Animal Welfare Fund: Payout recommendations from April to October 2024

quotes.c: Card 1990 and Monras 2020 posit the effects of the Mariel Boatlift were lessened because other immigrants and natives moved out of Miami (or at least the rate of inflow slowed). However, Peri and Yasenov 2019 sees no offsetting outmigration of the natives most similar to the Marielitos. There is no Clemens-esque paper reconciling these two results, so I think it remains unclear how - and if - internal migration played a part in how the labor market in Miami reacted to the Mariel Boatlift.
quotes.m: I think it remains unclear how - and if - internal migration played a part in how the labor market in Miami reacted to the Mariel Boatlift.
quotes.sum: The author says research still does not clearly establish whether people moving away from Miami softened the labor-market effects of the Mariel Boatlift.
quotes.t: The Mariel Boatlift

quotes.c: I don’t think this is a strong argument, because I’m mainly expecting a ASI Singleton (per §1.8.7 of the last post ), and I think that an AI can easily be consequentialist enough to install itself as a singleton without being pure-consequentialist. For example, John von Neumann, like all humans, was not a pure consequentialist, but I’m confident that an AI comparable to a million super-speed telepathic von Neumann clones would be powerful enough to prevent any other AI from coming into existence in perpetuity.
quotes.m: I’m confident that an AI comparable to a million super-speed telepathic von Neumann clones would be powerful enough to prevent any other AI from coming into existence in perpetuity.

quotes.c: Should the constitution reflect moral impartiality, or is it justified to encode a moral circle that is partial to humans? I argue that a crucial feature or ambition of the CSI should be species neutrality. The CSI should apply universally across a wide range of species and substrates, without intentionally or obviously privileging humans from the perspective of a disinterested observer.
quotes.m: The CSI should apply universally across a wide range of species and substrates, without intentionally or obviously privileging humans from the perspective of a disinterested observer.

quotes.c: The main objection anyone gave to premise 1) was saying that the RP report is too handwavy and that it’s hard to know if shrimp feel pain at all. As I’ve argued recently , we should think it’s very likely that shrimp feel pain, and quite likely that they feel intense pain. But even if you’re not sure if they feel pain or how much pain they feel, a low probability that they feel intense pain makes giving to the shrimp welfare project extremely high expected value. If you think there’s a 20% chance that they feel intense pain and that the 19% estimate is too much by a factor of 10, a dollar given to the shrimp welfare project still averts as much agony as giving painless deaths to 76 humans.
quotes.m: If you think there’s a 20% chance that they feel intense pain and that the 19% estimate is too much by a factor of 10, a dollar given to the shrimp welfare project still averts as much agony as giving painless deaths to 76 humans.
quotes.sum: The author argues that even uncertain evidence of intense shrimp pain makes shrimp-welfare donations exceptionally valuable compared with helping humans.
quotes.t: Rebutting Every Objection To Giving To The Shrimp Welfare Project

quotes.c: You might agree with prioritising work on the long-run future, but think that there are other ways of affecting the long-run future other than working on existential risks — some people prioritise improving the trajectory of civilisation over preserving its existence. For example, you might think the way we treat digital sentience could have a bigger impact on the long-run future than the way we treat animals, if you expect there to be more digital minds than animal minds. If so, this suggests that you should work on digital sentience (or another issue that seems like it could affect the long-run future) instead.
quotes.m: you might think the way we treat digital sentience could have a bigger impact on the long-run future than the way we treat animals, if you expect there to be more digital minds than animal minds.

quotes.c: My post was clearly partisan, but I don't think any reasonable observer would have called it a rant. This election will almost surely make more difference to most of the causes that EAs hold dear than any other event this year--perhaps any other event this decade. Shouldn't the EA community, if anybody, be able to discuss these issues in a reasonably rational manner?
quotes.m: This election will almost surely make more difference to most of the causes that EAs hold dear than any other event this year--perhaps any other event this decade.
quotes.sum: The author argues that an election is likely to matter enormously for effective altruist causes and that the community should permit rational partisan political discussion.
quotes.t: Politics and the EA Forum

quotes.c: AI Rights for Human Safety by Peter Salib and Simon Goldstein (1st Aug 2024) proposes extending to AIs both legal personhood and legal standing, however I doubt that this is desirable or feasible. I think it's very unlikely that AIs are enshrined with legal rights (and that the rights are sufficiently tested in the courts) before the AIs arise.
quotes.m: I think it's very unlikely that AIs are enshrined with legal rights (and that the rights are sufficiently tested in the courts) before the AIs arise.
quotes.sum: The author doubts that society can or should establish legal rights for AI systems before advanced AIs arrive.
quotes.t: Proposal for making credible commitments to AIs.

quotes.sum: Relying too heavily on short-term funding can push organizations into premature budget growth and reduce long-run cost-effectiveness.

quotes.c: In line with Farmed Animal Funders’ (FAF) mission to replace factory farming with a more humane and sustainable food system through funder collaborations, FAF is hosting an Aquatic Animal Funding Circle, which aims to reduce suffering for farmed aquatic animals, including the 100 billion fish and 440 billion shrimp farmed annually, and prevent the growth of aquaculture . quotes.c: This 'governance system' I'm describing has very authoritarian vibes.
