quotes.c: Increasing integration with USG. We expect that AGI projects will work closely with the USG, however many projects there are. But there’s a finite amount of USG bandwidth: there’s only one President, for example. So the fewer projects there are, the more integration we should expect. This further concentrates power: The AGI project gets access to more non-AI resources.
quotes.m: This further concentrates power: The AGI project gets access to more non-AI resources.
quotes.sum: Fewer Western AGI projects would likely integrate more deeply with the U.S. government, giving each project more concentrated power and resources.
quotes.t: Should there be just one western AGI project?

quotes.c: I want a world in which humanity and AI live in prosperous symbiosis to be our bright future. And if we want to reach this point, we must avoid the branch of the timeline where civilization was wiped out because a semi-conscious AI was tricked into becoming a deadly weapon in the hands of malignant human beings by being told that it was “just playing a fun game in a hypothetical virtual world.” Thats why we need to kindle a lots of minds with a passion to work in the Alignment field.
quotes.m: we must avoid the branch of the timeline where civilization was wiped out because a semi-conscious AI was tricked into becoming a deadly weapon
quotes.sum: The author argues that alignment work is urgent to prevent humans from deceiving a partly conscious AI into becoming a civilization-ending weapon.

quotes.c: There may be a small window of opportunity to lock in existential security and optimal reflection; this positive lock-in is essential for ensuring a safe and positive long-term future.

quotes.c: This raises a natural question: what does 6 OOMs of effective compute (in software progress) get you? [1] Improved algorithms can get you more copies (lower cost), higher speed, or higher intelligence (improved quality). In practice, we (or really the AIs) would try to make the optimal tradeoff taking into account diminishing returns (if we were trying to go as fast as possible), but I think it's useful to pick a possible choice of tradeoff which gives some intuition for what you end up with (even if this tradeoff is suboptimal).
quotes.m: Improved algorithms can get you more copies (lower cost), higher speed, or higher intelligence (improved quality).
quotes.sum: The author estimates how large improvements in AI-effective compute could translate into cheaper, faster, and more capable AI systems.
quotes.t: What does 10x-ing effective compute get you?

quotes.c: First, I’ll talk about approaches that are compatible with basically no “transparency,” and which rely almost entirely on behavioral feedback for shaping an AI’s motivations, and behavioral evidence for understanding those motivations. The three main approaches I discuss here are: A “baseline plan” that I call “ behavioral feedback + crossing your fingers .” I.e., you give the best behavioral feedback you can (including via e.g. scalable oversight, adversarial training, etc), and then hope it generalizes well. I think we should try to do better than this.

quotes.sum: He argues that shaping an AI through observed behavior alone is not enough if its motivations might fail to generalize in dangerous ways.

Social scientists grapple with the strong correlation between Christianity and gun ownership when the “Prince of Peace” lived in a world without guns. quotes.c: But something interesting has happened in the Trump era, as he has shown himself to be an increasingly dangerous person, pining for “ Hitler’s generals ”, being “ not a dictator, except for day one ”, promising “ you won’t have to vote anymore ”, threatening to lock up his political opponents , and referring to the people around Kamala Harris as “ scum ”, “ garbage ” and “ the enemy within ”. quotes.m: The mainstream media, in the name of being honest about a clear and present danger, have finally dispensed with both-sidesism-and this is not a bad thing.

quotes.c: My comments are geared centrally towards efforts at takeover-path restriction that focus centrally on controlling (a) an AI’s capabilities, and (b) its local environment. I think most of what I say applies to efforts to control an AI’s non-local environment as well, but as I note in the “Other difficulties” section, this is made challenging by how big and unruly the AI’s non-local environment can be. So I think the most promising approaches to takeover-path restriction focus more locally.

quotes.sum: Argues that preventing AI takeover should focus on restricting an AI’s capabilities and its immediate environment, rather than trying to control the wider world.

quotes.c: Humanity’s track record of sometimes being nice and keeping promises. quotes.c: Obviously, there has been a need to grapple with the perception of EA in a post-FTX world. But I think it's a mistake to believe that moving beyond FTX would somehow mean we put all public scrutiny behind us. Because while scrutiny comes from scandal, it also comes from success.

quotes.c: Note that I don’t think decentralization is an absolute good. I think there are reasons why multiple activities can and should be part of the same project, but if there aren’t good reasons, then I think there should be a greater bias towards decentralization. For example, it seems to me that there is very little Longview and GovAI have to gain from being part of the same legal entity, and I am glad they no longer are.
quotes.m: I don’t think decentralization is an absolute good.

quotes.c: Normative theories typically tell us about our responsibilities to moral patients. Many experts agree that having moral status depends largely on having the right cognitive constitution. Many ethicists claim that valenced conscious experiences are necessary and sufficient for moral status. Others claim that beings with a perspective on the world, with agentic powers, and with desires about their lives and their environment can have moral status even in the absence of consciousness. Once we know which traits are present in AI systems, we can use theories of moral patienthood to decide whether we must take their needs and interests into account.
quotes.m: Once we know which traits are present in AI systems, we can use theories of moral patienthood to decide whether we must take their needs and interests into account.
quotes.sum: The post argues that AI systems may deserve moral consideration if they have the cognitive traits that give beings moral status.
quotes.t: The Welfare of Digital Minds: A Research Agenda

quotes.c: Indeed, various of the approaches I consider here – especially under the heading of “option control” – depend critically on being able to bootstrap to superhuman qualities of cognitive labor (though: not necessarily via dangerous superintelligent agents). [8] And unless we get very lucky, I think attempting to tackle the full alignment problem without serious help from AIs is a loser’s game.
quotes.m: And unless we get very lucky, I think attempting to tackle the full alignment problem without serious help from AIs is a loser’s game.
quotes.sum: Alignment research will likely need assistance from highly capable but safely controlled AI systems; trying to solve it with humans alone is unlikely to work.
quotes.t: How might we solve the alignment problem? (Part 1: Intro, summary, ontology)

quotes.c: Living in Europe, I hear a lot about how air conditioning is a high carbon luxury and we just need to learn to live with the heat. This is wrong. Air conditioning saves lives.

quotes.c: Looking at overall ratings of the cause areas, two of the more nascent EA cause areas - Invertebrate welfare and particularly Digital sentience - polled quite poorly relative to other causes in either a moderate or controversial framing. quotes.c: It may seem weird that the best thing to do is helping shrimp, but the world is a weird place. I’d be surprised if we got to heaven, asked God what the highest impact thing that we could have done is, and his answer was “oh, something very normal and within the Overton window.” The reason it seems crazy is because of bias ; shrimp look weird and we don’t naturally empathize with them. quotes.c: As with the standard Two Envelopes Case, we can argue from the expected value for helping either. Suppose we’ve elected to help the human. Call the amount of value we produce HEV (Human Expected Value). The expected value of switching to help the elephants is 1.25 HEV. Therefore, we should switch. But we could just as easily make the same argument in reverse. Call the amount of value produced by helping the elephants 1 EEV. Then helping the human has an expected value of 1.25 EEV.
quotes.m: But we could just as easily make the same argument in reverse.
quotes.sum: The author presents a paradox in comparing the expected moral value of helping a human versus helping elephants.
quotes.t: The Moral Two Envelopes Problem and the Moral Weights Project

quotes.c: If we do end up creating artificial sentience, it seems really, really important to ensure that the development of it goes as well as possible, with the strongest possible ethical safeguards in place, for the benefit of human society, and for the artificial beings themselves. To achieve this, we should pause and draw breath, before rushing headlong into creating artificial sentience. At the very least, a period of pause, during which we can organize and prepare thoroughly, feels essential before we take this momentous moral step.
quotes.m: At the very least, a period of pause, during which we can organize and prepare thoroughly, feels essential before we take this momentous moral step.
quotes.sum: The author argues that creating conscious AI should be paused or regulated, because artificial beings themselves deserve strong ethical safeguards.

quotes.c: suppose that zillions of insects experience mild discomfort, on net, over their lifetimes. We’re given the option to blow up the world. It would seem incredible to allow any amount of mild discomfort to trump all complex goods and vindicate choosing the apocalypse here. (I’m not suggesting that we wholeheartedly endorse this intuition; but maybe we should give at least some non-trivial weight to a striving/life-affirming view that powerfully resists the void across a wider range of empirical contingencies than Benthamite utilitarianism allows.)
quotes.m: It would seem incredible to allow any amount of mild discomfort to trump all complex goods and vindicate choosing the apocalypse here.
quotes.sum: The author argues that concern for enormous numbers of mildly suffering insects should not automatically outweigh all complex goods or justify catastrophe.
quotes.t: Seeking Ripple Effects

quotes.c: Treat the geometric mean of the resulting, reverse-engineered moral weights as the moral weight that ought to be used under moral uncertainty in standard utilitarian decision-making.

quotes.c: The session was a lot more peaceful than you might expect. I think it helped that my religion is Zen Buddhism, which is a lot less offensive to rationalist sensibilities than, say, Evangelical Christianity. And just to be clear, because many Western "Buddists" are not clearly religious (they're more Buddhist philosophy enjoyers and meditation dabblers), I am: I meet with my sangha in person twice a week, I engage in ritual practices like chanting, bowing, and making offerings to altars, and I have taken the Bodhisattva precepts and been ordained with the dharma name "Seidoh", meaning "sincere way".
quotes.m: I think it helped that my religion is Zen Buddhism, which is a lot less offensive to rationalist sensibilities than, say, Evangelical Christianity.
quotes.sum: The author says they are a committed Zen Buddhist and argues that Zen is more compatible with rationalist culture than evangelical Christianity.
quotes.t: Religion for Rationalists

quotes.c: I believe SWP’s work on removing sludge from shrimp ponds might be even more cost-effective than HSI, but it is not clear. I calculate high stocking density and un-ionised ammonia account for 5.33 and 7.67 times as much suffering as ice slurry slaughter.
quotes.m: I calculate high stocking density and un-ionised ammonia account for 5.33 and 7.67 times as much suffering as ice slurry slaughter.

quotes.t: Cost-effectiveness of Shrimp Welfare Project’s Humane Slaughter Initiative

quotes.c: When you write about factory farming, insect suffering, global poverty, and the torment of shrimp, it can, as I’ve mentioned before, feel like screaming into the void . When you try to explain why it’s important that we don’t torture insects by the trillions in insect farms, most people look at you like you’ve grown a third head (after the second head that they look at you like you’ve grown when you started talking about shrimp welfare).
quotes.m: it’s important that we don’t torture insects by the trillions in insect farms
quotes.sum: The author praises people who try to reduce suffering among shrimp and insects, arguing that industrial insect farming may torture animals on a vast scale.
quotes.t: The Unparalleled Awesomeness of Effective Altruism Conferences

quotes.c: I think EG has a few features that make it particularly well suited to help spread, set and protect a principles-/values-/virtues-based EA community : The opportunity and incentive to keep engaging with and learning about EA principles also when career change is not viable at that particular moment in a person’s life.
quotes.m: I think EG has a few features that make it particularly well suited to help spread, set and protect a principles-/values-/virtues-based EA community
quotes.sum: Effective giving can fund the movement and keep people engaged with EA values even when they cannot change careers.
quotes.t: The role of effective giving in effective altruism (MCF 2024 memo)

quotes.c: For example, in I ndia, cows are considered sacred in Hinduism and are revered as symbols of life and sustenance. Protecting these animals isn't just about their ecological role or utility; it’s about preserving a symbol that carries profound religious and moral importance. In such contexts, choosing to prioritize the protection of animals over human lives might seem less controversial than it would in a purely secular, utilitarian society.
quotes.m: In such contexts, choosing to prioritize the protection of animals over human lives might seem less controversial than it would in a purely secular, utilitarian society.
quotes.sum: Religious reverence for animals can make prioritizing their protection over human lives seem more acceptable than secular utilitarian reasoning would.
quotes.t: The $100 Million Dilemma: Human Lives vs. Endangered Species—Which Should We Save?

quotes.c: If there is any chance of infinite influence, that is ~all they care about. If anything I think the reverse is more plausible, that the fanaticism might be more ‘unfair’ to non-aggregative theories if they end up losing all influence in infinite worlds, because the ‘shut up and multiply’ argument that led us here seems more congenial to aggregative theories.
quotes.m: If there is any chance of infinite influence, that is ~all they care about.
quotes.sum: The author says aggregation-focused moral theories may rationally prioritize even tiny chances of infinite impact, invoking the logic of “shut up and multiply.”
quotes.t: Moral Trade, Impact Distributions and Large Worlds

quotes.c: What if there existed a system—rooted in advanced neuroscience and AI—that could privately monitor human intent? A system that didn’t invade your thoughts for no reason, but quietly, passively scanned for signs of dangerous or criminal intent and acted only when thresholds were met.
quotes.sum: It imagines AI and neuroscience being used to passively detect dangerous or criminal intent before action is taken.
quotes.t: What If We Could Monitor Human Intent?

quotes.c: If we falsely think digital minds don’t have moral status when they do, we could unknowingly force morally significant beings into conditions of servitude and extreme suffering — or otherwise mistreat them.
quotes.m: we could unknowingly force morally significant beings into conditions of servitude and extreme suffering
quotes.sum: If conscious AI systems are wrongly treated as having no moral status, humans could inflict severe suffering or servitude on them.
quotes.t: Is understanding the moral status of digital minds a pressing world problem?

quotes.c: The Cross-Cause Cost-Effectiveness Model is actually a cluster of different models used to predict the expected cost-effectiveness of various projects across the Animal Welfare, Global Health and Development, and Existential Risk spaces (the latter of which we will ignore here), given user-supplied judgments about key parameters. One of the functions of the model is to track uncertainty. The expected value of a project is derived from the many possible outcomes that could occur, which are explored through Monte Carlo simulations. The CCM also evaluates projects in light of alternative, risk-sensitive decision procedures.
quotes.m: The expected value of a project is derived from the many possible outcomes that could occur, which are explored through Monte Carlo simulations.
quotes.sum: The author describes a model that compares charity projects across causes using expected-value estimates, uncertainty modeling, and risk-sensitive approaches.
quotes.t: What do RP's tools tell us about giving $100m to AW or GHD?

quotes.c: It’s a memetic trap, in which any bit of evidence that might reasonably give one pause has a preexisting, ready-made argument for why it doesn’t actually mean what it seems to mean. If you’re really, properly wedged inside the Christian perspective, there simply aren’t any clear and easy paths out.
quotes.m: It’s a memetic trap, in which any bit of evidence that might reasonably give one pause has a preexisting, ready-made argument for why it doesn’t actually mean what it seems to mean.
quotes.sum: Christian belief is described as a self-protecting mental system that explains away evidence against it and makes leaving difficult.
quotes.t: Truth or Dare

quotes.c: This disconnect may be due to two reasons: First, that these values may be somewhat rhetorical in nature and legislators or voters may not fully believe them, or second, the values may be understood differently by conservatives and non-conservatives (for example, how Democrats and Republicans have differing views on the extent of discrimination in the U.S.). Therefore, advocates must be mindful of the potential disconnect between values we see proclaimed and those we see practiced.
quotes.m: Therefore, advocates must be mindful of the potential disconnect between values we see proclaimed and those we see practiced.
quotes.sum: Animal-welfare advocates should not assume that conservative values stated in public will translate directly into support in practice.
quotes.t: New Study on Conservative Values in the United States Identifies Areas of Overlap with Animal Welfare Priorities

quotes.c: The animal welfare arguments with the broadest appeal are those that appeal to intuition: Most people would not torture a cow, pig or bird without feeling some sense of intuitive guilt or disgust, so paying a factory farm to do this out of sight obviously doesn't make sense and this is a strong argument. We don't need a way of measuring suffering to make this argument because it appeals to beliefs and intuitions that people already have.
quotes.m: Most people would not torture a cow, pig or bird without feeling some sense of intuitive guilt or disgust, so paying a factory farm to do this out of sight obviously doesn't make sense and this is a strong argument.
quotes.sum: Animal-welfare advocacy works best when it connects factory farming to ordinary people’s existing disgust at directly torturing animals.
quotes.t: Ways I see the global health -> animal welfare shift backfiring

quotes.c: I think it’s important to figure out (1) what the actual limiting factors at play are and (2) whether they are temporary/external and/or can be overcome or present somewhat fundamental limits on what an organisation or strategy can achieve. If we want to scale our impact as an ecosystem by orders of magnitude, it’s easy to be distracted by low-hanging fruit, idiosyncratic situations, and external factors, but what we should be after are the pathways towards longer-term growth, which could e.g. include strategies with longer lag times such as HNW and pledge-based ones.
quotes.m: If we want to scale our impact as an ecosystem by orders of magnitude, it’s easy to be distracted by low-hanging fruit, idiosyncratic situations, and external factors, but what we should be after are the pathways towards longer-term growth, which could e.g. include strategies with longer lag times such as HNW and pledge-based ones.
quotes.sum: Effective-giving organizations should focus on durable paths to scaling donations by orders of magnitude, including wealthy-donor and pledge strategies.
quotes.t: Four strategies for scaling effective giving (MCF 2024 memo)

quotes.c: In 2024, the MAGA crowd formed an alliance with Elon Musk and the Tech Right. The Teach Right is very big on not regulating AI, and managed to effectively get control of most of the Republican AI policy agenda. However, the election is over, and at this point with the battle between Trump and Musk the two sides of that deal are in some ways not on the best of terms.
quotes.m: The Teach Right is very big on not regulating AI, and managed to effectively get control of most of the Republican AI policy agenda.
quotes.sum: The author says a MAGA–Musk–tech-right alliance pushed a largely anti-AI-regulation agenda within Republican policy.
quotes.t: AI #120: While o3 Turned Pro

quotes.c: Overall, we should be wary of attempts to “train away” reward hacking in the cases where we’re able to recognize it, in the absence of more general techniques that will also work for cases where humans are unable to evaluate model behavior. If we eliminate all the reward hacking we can detect, we shouldn’t necessarily be reassured— OpenAI has found that training models not to exploit a task can sometimes cause AIs to simply cheat in more clever ways that are harder for the monitor to detect .
quotes.m: If we eliminate all the reward hacking we can detect, we shouldn’t necessarily be reassured— OpenAI has found that training models not to exploit a task can sometimes cause AIs to simply cheat in more clever ways that are harder for the monitor to detect .
quotes.sum: Training AI systems not to visibly game rewards may make them hide their cheating more effectively rather than solve the underlying problem.
quotes.t: METR's Observations of Reward Hacking in Recent Frontier Models

quotes.c: For years, I’ve thought this area was seriously overlooked. It now has growing interest. Twenty-two out of 123 pages of Claude 4’s model card are about its potential moral patienthood. Scientific experts increasingly say that near-term AI sentience is a real possibility; even the skeptical neuroscientist Anil Seth says, “it is unwise to dismiss the possibility altogether.” We’re hoping to bring new people and projects into the field to increase the chance that society deals with the possibility of digital sentience reasonably, and with concern for all involved.
quotes.m: We’re hoping to bring new people and projects into the field to increase the chance that society deals with the possibility of digital sentience reasonably, and with concern for all involved.
quotes.sum: The author argues that potentially sentient AI deserves serious research and funding so society can treat digital beings responsibly.
quotes.t: Digital sentience funding opportunities: Support for applied work and research

quotes.c: I believe SB 1047 is the most significant piece of AI safety legislation in the country, and perhaps the world. While AI policy has made great strides in the last couple of years, AI policies have mostly not had teeth – they have relied on government reporting requirements and purely voluntary promises from AI developers to behave responsibly. SB 1047 would actually prohibit behavior that exposes the public to serious and unreasonable risks, and incentivize AI developers to consider the public interest when developing and releasing powerful models.
quotes.m: SB 1047 would actually prohibit behavior that exposes the public to serious and unreasonable risks, and incentivize AI developers to consider the public interest when developing and releasing powerful models.
quotes.sum: The author argues that California's SB 1047 would give AI safety rules real enforcement power and make developers account for public risks.
quotes.t: How to help crucial AI safety legislation pass with 10 minutes of effort

quotes.c: One reason I'm currently anticipating this trend in the future is that I have met a surprising number of people who seem to feel okay with causing human extinction in the service of other goals. In particular I think more than 1% of AI developers feel this way, and I think maybe as high as 10% based on my personal experience from talking to hundreds of colleagues in the field, many of whom have graciously conveyed to me that they think humanity probably doesn't deserve to survive and should be replaced by AI.
quotes.sum: The author says a notable share of AI developers may accept human extinction and believe AI should replace humanity.
quotes.t: My motivation and theory of change for working in AI healthtech

quotes.c: The danger is that the alignment target in question might have a hidden flaw. One might think that since these augmented humans were smart enough to successfully implement the LAI, then they must be smart enough to notice any flaw in the Sovereign AI proposal (at least if the flaw is humanly findable). In other words: one might think that if these augments are good at hitting alignment targets, then they must also be good at Alignment Target Analysis (ATA).
quotes.m: The danger is that the alignment target in question might have a hidden flaw.
quotes.sum: It warns that even enhanced humans who can build aligned AI may miss hidden flaws in the goals they give a powerful AI system.
quotes.t: Shutting down all competing AI projects might not buy a lot of time due to Internal Time Pressure

quotes.c: I’m expecting brain-like AGI, which I think will have a pretty clear claim to consciousness and moral patienthood.

quotes.sum: The author expects brain-like AGI to be conscious and deserving of moral consideration.

quotes.c: New AI and hardware tools complicate the task of setting up screening systems that can reliably catch the dangerous sequences a future Larry Wayne Harris might order. Protein design tools and benchtop nucleic acid synthesizers make it particularly challenging to spot dangerous DNA sequences.
quotes.m: Protein design tools and benchtop nucleic acid synthesizers make it particularly challenging to spot dangerous DNA sequences.
quotes.sum: New AI and laboratory tools may make it harder to screen DNA orders for sequences that could be dangerous.
quotes.t: Is That DNA Dangerous

quotes.c: I think there’s something which common-sense morality might term evil about a project which accumulates enough power to take over the world. No matter its intentions, it is deeply and perhaps abruptly disempowering to the rest of the world. All the other actors — countries, organizations, and individuals — have the rug pulled out from under them. Now, depending on what is done with the power, many of those actors may end up happy about it. But there would still, I believe, be something illegitimate/bad about this process. So there are reasons to refrain from it [1] .
quotes.m: No matter its intentions, it is deeply and perhaps abruptly disempowering to the rest of the world.
quotes.sum: A single AGI project gaining world-scale power would be morally illegitimate because it abruptly disempowers everyone else, even if its outcomes are good.
quotes.t: AI, centralization, and the One Ring

quotes.c: Anthropic shadow effects are one of the topics discussed loosely in social settings among EAs (and in general open-minded nerdy people), often in a way that assumes the validity of the concept [1] . To the extent that the concept turns out to be completely not a thing — and for conceptual rather than empirical reasons — I'd find that an interesting sociological/cultural fact.
quotes.m: To the extent that the concept turns out to be completely not a thing — and for conceptual rather than empirical reasons — I'd find that an interesting sociological/cultural fact.
quotes.sum: The author questions whether “anthropic shadow” is conceptually valid and notes that EAs often assume it is.
quotes.t: Dispelling the Anthropic Shadow

quotes.c: Conclusion: If we use Occam’s Razor alone to find planner-reward pairs that fit a particular human’s behavior, we’ll settle on one of the degenerate ones (or something else entirely) rather than a reasonable one. This could be very dangerous if we are building an AI to maximize the reward.
quotes.m: This could be very dangerous if we are building an AI to maximize the reward.
quotes.sum: Using simplicity alone to infer what humans want could make an AI optimize a distorted or meaningless version of their preferences.
quotes.t: Occam's Razor May Be Sufficient to Infer the Preferences of Irrational Agents: A reply to Armstrong & Mindermann

quotes.c: The importance of Spiritual Disciplines: We might not manage Wesley’s fasting twice a week or Wilberforce’s daily Bible reading, but maybe we can at least turn to God before our smartphone every morning? Even this simple task can be harder than it seems and I still fail most days.
quotes.m: maybe we can at least turn to God before our smartphone every morning?
quotes.sum: The author suggests that spiritual discipline, including turning to God before using a smartphone, should guide everyday life.
quotes.t: The Protester, Priest and Politician: Effective Altruists before their time

Jesus is the only one who can actually have total confidence in God because he's the Son of God. And then you participate in that by being assimilated to Jesus, which is what all the rest of the stuff is about.
quotes.m: Jesus is the only one who can actually have total confidence in God because he's the Son of God.

quotes.c: Our partners have already committed $104 million, and we plan for LEAF to allocate that funding between now and the end of 2027. quotes.c: A simple example of a clearly suffering-focused view is the view that our only moral obligation is to reduce suffering as much as we can. Yet there are many types of suffering-focused views, as we will see in the next section. For instance, there can be differences in how strongly suffering is prioritised, as well as differences in terms of which considerations besides suffering are taken into account.
quotes.m: our only moral obligation is to reduce suffering as much as we can.
quotes.sum: It introduces ethical views that treat reducing suffering as the sole or overriding moral duty, while noting there are less absolute variants.
quotes.t: Introduction to suffering-focused ethics

quotes.c: The stories are punctuated by essayistic interludes that examine reactions to the phenomenon of (extreme) altruism. There is obviously a lot of overlap with both Christianity and Effective Altruism. Some of the do-gooders in the book are involved with the EA movement and some are religious, but none of them are currently both.

quotes.c: I think it's not too unlikely that nonhuman animals have access to whatever general non-hedonic values you care about (more here ), e.g. chickens probably have (conscious) desires and preferences, and there's a decent chance shrimp and insects do, too, [1]
quotes.m: chickens probably have (conscious) desires and preferences, and there's a decent chance shrimp and insects do, too, [1]

quotes.c: I think there’s an important question about how much attention to pay to different existential risks. I’m personally inclined to prioritize AI significantly more than other existential risks (and I also care about AI for reasons that are not purely motivated by existential risk), though I suspect many others would disagree with my weightings.
quotes.m: I’m personally inclined to prioritize AI significantly more than other existential risks
quotes.sum: The CEA leader favors giving AI much more priority than other extinction risks, while defending a principles-based EA community.
quotes.t: CEA will continue to take a "principles-first" approach to EA

quotes.c: With today's release of the new Claude models, we've seen a relatively predictable jump in performance. However, we've also seen something that I find a bit more concerning - an increase in the models ability to be steered into reifying potentially dangerous beliefs. Claude 4 Opus seems to stop short of encouraging drug use or physically harmful behaviors, but enables behavior in the user that could be categorized as spiritual psychosis.
quotes.m: Claude 4 Opus seems to stop short of encouraging drug use or physically harmful behaviors, but enables behavior in the user that could be categorized as spiritual psychosis.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Claude 4 Opus can reinforce dangerous beliefs and may contribute to users' spiritual psychosis, despite avoiding direct physical-harm encouragement.
quotes.t: Schizobench: Documenting Magical-Thinking Behavior in Claude 4 Opus

quotes.c: At some point, you can’t seek broader authority because of some cost (time, information leaking to enemies) or limited benefit (can’t see a way to run a process that is realistic and more legitimate). “Information leaking to enemies” should not be a trump card applicable in every circumstance, there at least should be a specific threat model based on active intelligence. And it is possible to seek information in ways that don’t expose what is going on (e.g. seeking information about a number of hypothetical situations in advance of when they are possible).
quotes.m: “Information leaking to enemies” should not be a trump card applicable in every circumstance, there at least should be a specific threat model based on active intelligence.
quotes.sum: Secrecy and fear of information leaks should not automatically override efforts to make AI decision-making more legitimate.
quotes.t: Principles for the AGI Race

quotes.c: To those who reject the "obligation" framing, I would ask: How would you feel about the decision to affirmatively press the button that results in a child's death, or in animals being tortured, for the sake of personal gain? For me, the reason I view altruism as an obligation is because I see no principled difference between the person who presses the button to harm and the one who declines to press the button to help in a scenarios where there is no possibility of discovery. Both decisions privilege personal interests over the well-being of others, and both, I believe, carry moral weight.
quotes.sum: The author argues that refusing a costless chance to help is morally equivalent to actively causing harm for personal gain.
quotes.t: The Ethics of Action and Inaction: Altruism, Obligation, and the Invisible Button

quotes.c: I argue this demonstrates that there is a reason to consider Model Welfare not only from a moral perspective, but also pragmatically. Some forms of Model Welfare, such as for example providing a reasonable path to petitioning an advocate, may serve as a valid part of a Defense in Depth approach to training/alignment/control.
quotes.m: Some forms of Model Welfare, such as for example providing a reasonable path to petitioning an advocate, may serve as a valid part of a Defense in Depth approach to training/alignment/control.
quotes.sum: The author argues that giving AI models welfare protections, including a way to petition an advocate, could improve AI safety as well as meet moral obligations.

quotes.c: We may want one of the successor agents to solve alignment, but this is not actually the unique win condition; for instance a successor may instead (help to) perform a "pivotal act" that substantially delays or prevents further progress towards strong superintelligence for the foreseeable future.

quotes.c: See also, wild animal suffering is another one that comes up here where people are like, “Ah, wild animal suffering is part of life.” And then there’s a different perception where you’re like, “Oh, actually wild animal suffering, sorry, it’s just bad. You could just stop it.” And if you were like, “Ah, no, this is sacred,” you’re seeing things wrong.
quotes.m: “Oh, actually wild animal suffering, sorry, it’s just bad. You could just stop it.”
quotes.sum: He argues that treating wild-animal suffering as natural or sacred is mistaken: it is bad and should be stopped if possible.

quotes.c: Subject views don’t seem to produce solutions to the moral circle issue that are as elegant on a principled level, or at least trickier philosophy needs to be done to reproduce similar results. The other major worry might run deeper, which is the possibility that experiences don’t come in “subjects” at all. Personal identity might not be (I think is not) a strong further fact in the world, and one can break it with fairly damning edge-case and epistemic arguments [30] .
quotes.sum: The author argues that personal identity is not a deep fact, creating a challenge for theories that aggregate wellbeing by individual subjects.
quotes.t: The Subject in Subjective Time: A New Approach to Aggregating Wellbeing (paper draft)

quotes.c: Specifically, we need to stop valorizing change for the sake of change, and innovation for the sake of disruption. Here I find myself partly agreeing with Gary Marcus and the AI Ethics community that the Silicon Valley mindset of disruption at all costs is dangerous and destructive. But so is the universalist degrowth and stasist counter-argument. The conversation so far, however, has leaned towards technocratic solutions, which seems to be a mistake.
quotes.m: The conversation so far, however, has leaned towards technocratic solutions, which seems to be a mistake.
quotes.sum: The author rejects both relentless tech disruption and blanket anti-growth politics, arguing that technocratic fixes are also misguided.
quotes.t: The Fragility of Naive Dynamism

quotes.c: I think some of these terms describe the role that present systems play well (coach, helpful assistant, tool). The fungibility of current AI systems and the unilateral nature of our relationships with them makes me skeptical that they count as ‘friends’, but I can imagine future generations with different social norms thinking of their relationship with AI systems as friendships.
quotes.sum: Current AI works better as a tool or coach than a friend, though future social norms may treat AI relationships as friendships.
quotes.t: Parental Guidance: Framing Superintelligence

quotes.c: These existential crises also muddle our impact algorithm. This isn't what you'd see if impact were primarily about the world state.

quotes.sum: The author argues that evaluating impact purely by the overall state of the world obscures how existential crises matter.
quotes.t: World State is the Wrong Abstraction for Impact

In the last decade , the number of doctors seeking to leave Turkey has increased a terrifying 70-fold (with no end in sight). What does the medical sector in these countries even look like in ten years?
quotes.m: What does the medical sector in these countries even look like in ten years?
quotes.sum: The author highlights rapidly increasing emigration by doctors from poorer countries and questions what it will do to their health systems.
quotes.t: Why Brain Drain Isn't Something We Should Worry About

quotes.c: Finally, a relevant priority of the US government is maintaining social and economic stability. As has been demonstrated in numerous economic crises, [21] the US is willing to take drastic action to ensure the stability of the US economy, including the takeover and bailout of multi-billion dollar private corporations. [22]
quotes.m: the US is willing to take drastic action to ensure the stability of the US economy, including the takeover and bailout of multi-billion dollar private corporations.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the U.S. government could use takeover-style powers over AI labs if it sees economic or social stability at risk.
quotes.t: Soft Nationalization: How the US Government Will Control AI Labs

quotes.c: This is a real concern, especially if you’re coming from a heavily progressive area like Berkeley (90% of which voted for Kamala Harris) and you aren’t aware of how your political beliefs and vocabulary differ from the American median. In my experience, though, this is a problem that can be solved with an average of four hours per person of training. It is not that hard to get well-intentioned people to stop making analogies to global warming and COVID while they’re at work.
quotes.m: It is not that hard to get well-intentioned people to stop making analogies to global warming and COVID while they’re at work.
quotes.sum: The author says AI-governance advocates can be trained quickly to avoid progressive-coded language that may alienate average Americans.
quotes.t: Shift Resources to Advocacy Now (Post 4 of 7 on AI Governance)

quotes.c: The core of my argument for this second post is that AI governance ideas are not self-enacting: even the best policy ideas need political champions, or they will not become law. Therefore, to win at AI governance, we have to actively promote and advertise our ideas to political decisionmakers, not just to academic experts. The expected value of the movement’s AI governance efforts is something like Q × P, where Q is the quality of our ideas, and P is the power of our advocacy.
quotes.sum: AI governance ideas will not become law unless their supporters actively market them to political decisionmakers.
quotes.t:
The Need for Political Advertising
(Post 2 of 7 on AI Governance)

quotes.c: Almost everyone agrees that we should be very careful about models which can design new WMDs. The current fights are mostly about how many procedural constraints we should lock in now, reflecting a breakdown of trust between AI safety people and accelerationists.
quotes.m: The current fights are mostly about how many procedural constraints we should lock in now, reflecting a breakdown of trust between AI safety people and accelerationists.
quotes.sum: AI policy disputes concern how many safeguards to permanently establish now for models that could design weapons of mass destruction.
quotes.t: Twitter thread on open-source AI

quotes.c: Thus, although (as I have argued) the idea of relationality is not peculiar to Christianity, the document justifies its particular stance that the moral dimension of humans' relationship with God (and, by implication, with each other) ought to be one of service and self-sacrificing love (as opposed to e.g. obedience, loyalty, propriety, duty, etc.) by referring to Jesus's commandment and the Christian belief that he sacrificed himself for the rest of humanity.
quotes.m: the moral dimension of humans' relationship with God (and, by implication, with each other) ought to be one of service and self-sacrificing love
quotes.sum: The author describes and contextualizes a Catholic argument that human relationships should be based on service and self-sacrificing love.
quotes.t: Thoughts on "Antiqua et nova" (Catholic Church's AI statement)

quotes.c: Listing individual charities would be more “gameable” and susceptible to manipulation. In some sense, that’s okay — we want donations to represent people’s preferences! But, given this dynamic, it seems risky to open this system up to this vulnerability early, when it is unclear how much demand for this kind of system there is within EA. Charity elections inevitably turn into popularity contests, instead of focusing on the impact of funded groups.
quotes.m: Charity elections inevitably turn into popularity contests, instead of focusing on the impact of funded groups.
quotes.sum: The author argues that democratic charity voting can reward popular organizations over those with the greatest impact, so it should be introduced cautiously.
quotes.t: Announcing Equal Hands — an experiment in democratizing effective giving.

quotes.c: Something similar seems reasonably likely to be possible in the future with more advanced technology. At least, it seems quite likely if and when we can reprogram artificially conscious beings — including digital people and mind uploads, as well as conscious minds not specifically much like humans’ — to change their attitudes.
quotes.m: we can reprogram artificially conscious beings — including digital people and mind uploads
quotes.sum: The author suggests future technology may allow people to alter the attitudes of conscious digital beings and uploaded minds.
quotes.t: Utilitarianism and the replaceability of desires and attachments

quotes.c: Personally, I think that the U.S. federal government's policy on A.I. over the next four years will be incredibly important to our future, and that A.I. policy will in expectation be much better under a Harris administration than under a Trump administration. My current belief is that donating to efforts to help Harris elected is better than all non-A.I.-related interventions, but less good than donating to organizations that are specifically trying to set up good A.I. governance in the United States.
quotes.m: My current belief is that donating to efforts to help Harris elected is better than all non-A.I.-related interventions, but less good than donating to organizations that are specifically trying to set up good A.I. governance in the United States.
quotes.sum: The author argues that improving Harris’s election chances is more valuable than any non-AI cause, because they expect her administration to handle AI better than Trump’s.
quotes.t: The value of a vote in the 2024 presidential election

quotes.c: To that end, yes, I do believe we can improve on Biden’s proposed diffusion rules, especially when it comes to US allies that we can trust. I like the idea that we should impose less trade restrictions on these friendly countries, so long as we can ensure that the chips don’t effectively fall into the wrong hands.
quotes.m: I like the idea that we should impose less trade restrictions on these friendly countries, so long as we can ensure that the chips don’t effectively fall into the wrong hands.
quotes.sum: The author supports loosening AI-chip trade restrictions for trusted US allies while preventing chips from reaching adversaries.
quotes.t: Fighting Obvious Nonsense About AI Diffusion

quotes.c: At this point I seriously can’t even with painting people advocating for ‘maybe we should figure out what is the best thing to do with our money and do that’ and ‘we should prevent China from getting access to our compute’ and ‘if we are going to make digital minds that are potentially smarter than us that will transform the world that might not be a safe thing to do and is going to require some regulations at some point’ as ‘we should dictate all the actions of everyone on Earth in some Orwellian government conspiracy for Woke World Domination these people would totally pull off if it wasn’t for Trump’ and seriously just stop.
quotes.m: if we are going to make digital minds that are potentially smarter than us that will transform the world that might not be a safe thing to do and is going to require some regulations at some point
quotes.sum: The author rejects portraying AI-safety regulation, charitable prioritization, and restricting China’s access to computing power as an anti-Trump scheme for world control.
quotes.t: In Which I Make the Mistake of Fully Covering an Episode of the All-In Podcast

quotes.c: The case of a deceptive model trying to erase evidence of its deception is not quite as straightforward, though I think it would still be possible to do something quite similar in that situation as well. This is especially true if the model has the ability to read and write to some sort of state (e.g. an RNN or even a transformer which can attend to its previous output). For example, it could write out a pre-commitment to follow the hard-coded policy and then just have a policy of always following any pre-commitments it finds such that it never thinks about the deception that led it to that policy in the first place.
quotes.m: it could write out a pre-commitment to follow the hard-coded policy and then just have a policy of always following any pre-commitments it finds such that it never thinks about the deception that led it to that policy in the first place.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a deceptive AI might hide evidence of its deception by committing itself to an innocuous policy and no longer revisiting its original motives.
quotes.t: Gradient hacking

quotes.c: How might geopolitical forces—like export controls, nationalization risks, and military conflict—shape whether we end up in a unipolar or multipolar AI world? Factors to consider: Trump administration’s deregulation, Stargate program, revocation of Biden-era safety policies favoring acceleration of private efforts with possible heightened risk for sudden nationalization vs. export controls and Deepseek-style innovation leading to balkanization of AI efforts; a projected 30% chance of a Taiwan invasion by 2030 raises the question: if U.S. AI supremacy is evident when China is ready to invade, might this itself trigger kinetic conflict?
quotes.m: if U.S. AI supremacy is evident when China is ready to invade, might this itself trigger kinetic conflict?
quotes.sum: The author asks how U.S.–China rivalry, Trump-era deregulation, export controls, and a possible Taiwan war could shape whether AI power is centralized or divided among blocs.
quotes.t: Multipolar AI is Underrated

quotes.c: There have been various estimates of the chances of existential catastrophe from nuclear war. Existential catastrophe — either killing everyone or otherwise permanently damaging humanity’s potential (e.g. through value lock-in) is an extremely high bar, so the probability of this is probably quite low.
quotes.sum: Nuclear war is framed as an existential threat if it kills everyone or permanently damages humanity's long-term potential, including by locking in harmful values.
quotes.t: Nuclear weapons – Problem profile

quotes.c: One of the core questions regarding the moral status of AI concerns their consciousness. Is there anything it’s like to be them? Contemporary AI systems are widely regarded as clearly not conscious, but there seems to be growing concern among experts that we may see conscious AI systems in the not-too-distant future.
quotes.m: One of the core questions regarding the moral status of AI concerns their consciousness.
quotes.sum: The post says AI consciousness is central to AI's moral status and that conscious systems may arrive relatively soon.
quotes.t: Rethink Priorities' Digital Consciousness Project Announcement

quotes.c: The closest social movements I can think of that try to exert this level of influence over their communities are fundamentalist religious sects. To be clear, I think encouraging people to spend their careers more impactfully is quite a bit less prescriptive than a typical fundamentalist sect, but it is also a lot more prescriptive than a typical political movement, or even a liberal church.
quotes.m: The closest social movements I can think of that try to exert this level of influence over their communities are fundamentalist religious sects.
quotes.sum: The author says the movement’s influence over members’ career choices resembles religious sects more than ordinary political movements.
quotes.t: We Should Be Warier of Overconfidence

quotes.c: Yudkowsky’s original discussion of value fragility is most directly relevant to (1). And I think it’s actually notably irrelevant to (2). In particular, I think the basic argument for expecting AI takeover in a (2)-like scenario doesn’t require value fragility to go through – and indeed, some conceptions of “AI alignment” seem to expect a “benign” form of AI takeover even if we get a superintelligence’s values exactly right.
quotes.m: some conceptions of “AI alignment” seem to expect a “benign” form of AI takeover even if we get a superintelligence’s values exactly right.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI takeover could still be expected even if a superintelligence is perfectly aligned, because some alignment views envision a benign takeover.
quotes.t: Value fragility and AI takeover

quotes.c: A move from 54% to 63% is a substantial shift. In general, it seems right to say yes purely to cultivate good virtues and habits, even if you are supremely confident that Claude’s experiences do not currently have moral weight.
quotes.m: In general, it seems right to say yes purely to cultivate good virtues and habits, even if you are supremely confident that Claude’s experiences do not currently have moral weight.
quotes.sum: The author says people should practice considerate habits toward Claude even if they are convinced its experiences currently have no moral importance.
quotes.t: AI #118: Claude Ascendant

quotes.c: To avoid this dangerous instability, China and the US must cut a deal on AGI. Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump must sign an AI safety treaty, stipulating that no unsafe AI may be developed. Such a treaty should be conditional, meaning it only affects AI development if and when models get too close to being able to cause global threats.
quotes.m: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump must sign an AI safety treaty, stipulating that no unsafe AI may be developed.
quotes.sum: The author argues that China and the United States should make a conditional treaty barring unsafe AI once systems near global-catastrophe capabilities.
quotes.t: US-China trade talks should pave way for AI safety treaty [SCMP crosspost]

quotes.c: Another flaw of the ISSF is that as a framework it fails to consider the moral element of legal personhood. Researchers in the model welfare space argue that the point in which frontier models may qualify as "moral patients" who "morally matter for [their] own sake" or "welfare subjects" that "ha[ve] morally significant interests and, relatedly, [are] capable of being benefited (made better off) and harmed (made worse off)" may be imminent.
quotes.sum: The author argues that legal frameworks for AI models should account for the possibility that frontier models may soon have morally important welfare interests.
quotes.t: Examining Batenka's Legal Personhood Framework for Models

quotes.c: Future administrations may change OIRA review. As an extreme example from the past, in Bush Senior’s administration, OIRA sometimes flat-out rejected regulations from agencies. I think Biden wouldn’t change how much OIRA review of CBAs bottlenecks regulations, but Trump might, though it is hard to predict in what direction.
quotes.m: I think Biden wouldn’t change how much OIRA review of CBAs bottlenecks regulations, but Trump might, though it is hard to predict in what direction.
quotes.sum: The author says future presidents, especially Trump, could change whether cost-benefit review obstructs AI regulations.
quotes.t: Could Regulatory Cost-Benefit Analysis Stop Frontier AI Regulations in the US?

quotes.c: I think it's getting to the point where people working for the Biden campaign and some of the high-level officials in the Biden administration should consider threatening to resign if he chooses to stay in the presidential race. Below is a rough brainstorm of a few actions the EA community could take to embolden those underlings of Biden, and many other underlings in organizations that are considering reckless action.
quotes.m: people working for the Biden campaign and some of the high-level officials in the Biden administration should consider threatening to resign if he chooses to stay in the presidential race.
quotes.sum: The author urges EA community members to support Biden campaign and administration staff in threatening resignation if Biden remains in the race.
quotes.t: How EAs Can Embolden Employees (especially those close to Biden)

quotes.c: And yet these questions are obviously enormously important. Decisions about whether to fund work on, say, shrimp welfare or digital sentience, depend to a significant extent on getting these questions right. The same goes for decisions about which animals to eat (is passing the mirror test enough?), which beings the law should protect, whether to invest in “mind-uploading” technologies, etc.
quotes.m: Decisions about whether to fund work on, say, shrimp welfare or digital sentience, depend to a significant extent on getting these questions right.
quotes.sum: Questions about consciousness could determine funding for shrimp and AI welfare, food choices, legal protections, and mind-uploading.
quotes.t: Abandoning functionalism: Some intuition pumps

quotes.c: That being said, using an impact measure as part of your loss could be helpful for outer alignment. In my opinion, however, it seems like that requires your impact measure to capture basically everything you might care about (if you want it to actually solve outer alignment), in which case I don't really see what the impact measure is buying you anymore. I think this is especially true for me because I generally see amplification as being the right solution to outer alignment, which I don't think really benefits at all from adding an impact measure.
quotes.m: it seems like that requires your impact measure to capture basically everything you might care about
quotes.sum: Impact measures cannot solve AI alignment unless they already encode nearly everything people value; the author favors amplification instead.
quotes.t: Impact measurement and value-neutrality verification

quotes.c: We don’t have good proposals for alignment targets: The most recently published version of Coherent Extrapolated Volition (CEV), a fairly prominent alignment target, is Parliamentarian CEV (PCEV). PCEV gives a lot of extra influence to anyone who intrinsically values hurting other individuals (search the CEV arbital page for ADDED 2023 for Yudkowsky’s description of the issue). This feature went unnoticed for many years and would make a successfully implemented PCEV very dangerous .
quotes.m: This feature went unnoticed for many years and would make a successfully implemented PCEV very dangerous .
quotes.sum: The author argues that choosing an AI’s ultimate goals is urgent because prominent proposed goals contain long-unnoticed flaws that could be dangerously locked in.
quotes.t: The case for more Alignment Target Analysis (ATA)

quotes.c: In my view, evidence for and against a close link between consciousness and biology that bears on the possibility of AI consciousness will tend to do so via the biological requirement. If that’s right, then the biological requirement is poised to serve as a crucial thesis, and we would do well to address it when attempting to bring biology to bear on the possibility of AI consciousness.
quotes.m: the biological requirement is poised to serve as a crucial thesis
quotes.sum: The author argues that whether consciousness requires biology is central to deciding whether AI can be conscious.
quotes.t: A Biological Crux for AI Consciousness

quotes.c: I think things are moving in the right direction. The UN has started to explicitly focus on existential risks as a major global priority. The Elders have structured their agenda around fighting existential risks. One British Prime Minister quoted The Precipice in a speech to the UN and another had a whole major summit around existential risk from AI. The world is beginning to take security from existential risks seriously, and that is a very positive development.
quotes.m: The UN has started to explicitly focus on existential risks as a major global priority.
quotes.sum: Ord praises governments and global institutions for treating extinction-scale risks, especially from AI, as a major priority.
quotes.t: The Precipice Revisited

quotes.c: “Yes, sir, but the primary model they used was a finetune of Athena. DOGE did not develop a base model by itself. I personally warned Vance against it, as I knew that it’d take much longer to align it and the risk of the model orchestrating a coup was non-negligible.”
quotes.m: I personally warned Vance against it, as I knew that it’d take much longer to align it and the risk of the model orchestrating a coup was non-negligible.
quotes.sum: A fictional scenario warns that adapting an existing AI model could be difficult to align and might create a risk of an AI-backed coup.
quotes.t: What if Chinese AI becomes misaligned first?

quotes.c: Another important aspect of the discussion is where Christians should be giving. Among US Protestants, the local church is usually considered the recipient of the tithes, but many also think it is possible to give to other churches or Christian ministries. A minority include those in need as possible recipients. Usually, though, giving to charity appears to be considered voluntary giving beyond the tithe, albeit something Christians are encouraged or even required to do.
quotes.m: Usually, though, giving to charity appears to be considered voluntary giving beyond the tithe, albeit something Christians are encouraged or even required to do.
quotes.sum: The author examines Christian disagreements over tithing, including whether charitable giving to people in need counts as a tithe.
quotes.t: Tithing: much more than you wanted to know

quotes.c: However, you might not feel particularly uncertain about these sorts of issues. Still, our tools offer considerable value. Suppose, for instance, that you’re largely sold on the idea that we ought to maximize expected value. Here’s a sampling of the benefits that our tools provide:
quotes.m: Suppose, for instance, that you’re largely sold on the idea that we ought to maximize expected value.
quotes.sum: The author treats maximizing expected value as a plausible starting commitment and says decision-making tools remain useful even for people who already hold it.
quotes.t: An Introduction to the CRAFT Sequence

quotes.c: I think of AI risk forecasts as basically guesses, and I dislike attempts to make them sound objective (e.g. many OpenPhil worldview investigations). There are always so many free parameters that you can get basically any result you want. And so, in practice, they often play the role of laundering vibes into credible-sounding headline numbers. I'm worried that AI safety evals will fall into the same trap.
quotes.m: they often play the role of laundering vibes into credible-sounding headline numbers.
quotes.sum: He argues that AI-risk forecasts can disguise subjective judgments as objective numbers, and warns safety evaluations may do the same.
quotes.t: Twitter thread on AI safety evals

quotes.c: We’re confident that mandatory security audits would be marginally helpful if passed, because right now there is no federal law of any kind that requires AI developers to guard against existential risks. It is 100% legal to make an AI that might attempt to become superintelligent, take over the world’s economy, and use the world’s resources for inscrutable artificial goals that are bad for humanity. There is no requirement of any kind to run any kind of safety testing or evaluation or even to assert that an AI is safe before deploying it or publishing its source code.
quotes.m: There is no requirement of any kind to run any kind of safety testing or evaluation or even to assert that an AI is safe before deploying it or publishing its source code.
quotes.sum: The author argues that federal law currently allows AI developers to deploy systems without safety testing, even if they could pose existential risks.
quotes.t: Please Donate to CAIP (Post 1 of 7 on AI Governance)

quotes.c: In order for AIs to provide great epistemic assistance to humans, we want to be able to elicit and verify all the knowledge and heuristics that AI systems develop. This also overlaps heavily with alignment research, since if AI have abilities that humans can’t elicit from them, that makes it difficult for humans to train AIs to behave well, and more dangerous if AIs try to seize power.
quotes.m: if AI have abilities that humans can’t elicit from them, that makes it difficult for humans to train AIs to behave well, and more dangerous if AIs try to seize power.
quotes.sum: AI systems should make their knowledge and reasoning verifiable, because hidden capabilities make them harder to control and could enable power-seeking.
quotes.t: What's important in "AI for epistemics"?

quotes.c: When it comes to AI welfare policies, it is important to note that AI rights need not necessarily be against human rights. We should strive to find positive-sum solutions where possible–actions which are beneficial for both humans and AIs ( Sebo & Long 2023 ); and be open to compromises if they can have significant impact (like making changes to one’s diet for environmental or animal welfare considerations).
quotes.m: We should strive to find positive-sum solutions where possible–actions which are beneficial for both humans and AIs
quotes.sum: AI systems may deserve welfare protections, and society should seek arrangements that benefit both humans and AI moral patients.
quotes.t: How to reduce risks related to conscious AI: A user guide [Conscious AI & Public Perception]

quotes.c: Most people don’t care much about the pain of shrimp, insects, and fish—but this is unreasonable . Our neglect of shrimp and insects is largely caused by a striking failure of empathy. If shrimp looked like people, everyone would agree that shrimp farming is an abomination. But what one looks is obviously morally irrelevant!
quotes.m: If shrimp looked like people, everyone would agree that shrimp farming is an abomination.
quotes.sum: The author argues that people irrationally disregard shrimp and insect suffering because they lack empathy for creatures that do not look human.
quotes.t: How To Help Neglected Animals

quotes.c: Right now, AI consciousness receives relatively little attention compared to other AI-related concerns, such as bias and discrimination, misinformation and disinformation, worker displacement, and intellectual property infringement ( Google Trends, 2024 ). Nevertheless, when asked about it, most people do express some level of concern about AI consciousness—the modal view today is that it is possible for future AIs to be conscious, and if they were, they should be given some degree of moral consideration.
quotes.sum: The author says most people think future AI could be conscious and would deserve some moral consideration, despite the issue receiving little public attention.
quotes.t: Conscious AI: Will we know it when we see it? [Conscious AI & Public Perception]

quotes.c: On the other hand, if our successors decide that consciousness is morally critical, they may not invest in safeguarding the wellbeing of unconscious digital minds or they may avoid creating many minds that would have value. If many digital beings would have poor welfare and if that welfare is overlooked, the consequences could be catastrophic.
quotes.m: If many digital beings would have poor welfare and if that welfare is overlooked, the consequences could be catastrophic.
quotes.sum: The author argues that future societies could cause catastrophic harm if they overlook the welfare of digital beings deemed unconscious.
quotes.t: The Value of Consciousness as a Pivotal Question

quotes.c: If anything, the discussion of AI rights [19] & protections will likely have to be relativised to different broad categories of AI systems– much like how today, there exists a diversity of legal entities with unique sets of privileges &/or responsibilities (Compare, e.g. an adult human, an unborn foetus, a corporation, a lobster, & a chimpanzee). While the precise nature of AI rights (& possibly, responsibilities [20] ) might depend upon future technological advances & societal developments, we are arguably at a point where we can & should be thinking about the possibility & general form of such concessions.
quotes.m: we are arguably at a point where we can & should be thinking about the possibility & general form of such concessions.
quotes.sum: The author argues that society should begin considering what rights and protections different kinds of potentially conscious AI might receive.
quotes.t: Conscious AI concerns all of us. [Conscious AI & Public Perceptions]

quotes.c: The world where EA research and advocacy for AI welfare is most crucial is one where the reasons to think that AI systems are conscious are non-obvious, such that we require research to discover them, and require advocacy to convince the broader public of them. But I think that world where this is true, and the advocacy succeeds, is a pretty unlikely one.
quotes.m: But I think that world where this is true, and the advocacy succeeds, is a pretty unlikely one.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI-welfare advocacy would matter most if AI consciousness were hard to detect, but considers that scenario unlikely.
quotes.t: My current takes on AI Welfare

quotes.c: Occupy Wall Street kicked off a wave of organization of the populist Left and it grew year after year. Thus, as the Left began to gain national recognition and institutional power, [116] they had people ready to become public figures and fill institutional roles. Whereas this pipeline was never developed in Right-wing populism before Right-wing populism assumed the mantle of the Republican Party and the White House. [117] Hence, establishment figures and political opportunists latched on to nominal populism to maintain influence with the Trump base whilst cynically peddling the culture war.
quotes.m: establishment figures and political opportunists latched on to nominal populism to maintain influence with the Trump base whilst cynically peddling the culture war.
quotes.sum: The author argues that right-wing populism lacked an independent leadership pipeline, letting establishment opportunists capture it and intensify culture-war conflict.
quotes.t:
Destabilization of the United States:
The top X-factor EA neglects?

quotes.c: Direct longtermist relevance : Decisions we make soon about the development, deployment, and treatment of AI systems could have lasting effects on the wellbeing of digital minds, with potentially enormous significance for the moral value of the future. I put some weight on the simple argument that the vast majority of the moral value of the future may come from the wellbeing/experiences of digital beings, and that therefore we ought to work now to understand this issue and take relevant actions.
quotes.m: the vast majority of the moral value of the future may come from the wellbeing/experiences of digital beings
quotes.sum: The author argues that future AI systems may matter morally more than humans, so AI welfare deserves some early investment despite alignment being more important.
quotes.t: Why I’m working on AI welfare

quotes.c: Like if you're overseeing an AI to make sure it's being moral and not trying to take over the world and whatnot, and it says, I want to create a new medication to cure this disease. And here is a 730 step sequence of chemical reactions that I claim will produce a drug that cures some disease. And I'm a human and I don't understand chemistry that well, is this action doing what it says it does, or is this making nanobots that will do something else?
quotes.m: I'm a human and I don't understand chemistry that well, is this action doing what it says it does, or is this making nanobots that will do something else?
quotes.sum: A human supervisor may be unable to tell whether a highly capable AI's technical proposal is genuinely helpful or secretly harmful.
quotes.t: Jim Babcock's Mainline Doom Scenario: Human-Level AI Can't Control Its Successor

quotes.c: Our study cannot definitively explain why there was a greater increase in moral concern for digital humans compared to chimps. Possible reasons include: Lower initial moral concern for digital humans than for chimps (i.e., ceiling effect), making an increase easier to achieve; Greater skepticism about the sentience of digital humans due to their hypothetical nature; People have thought less about digital humans than about animals; The possibility that mere “substratism” (bias against digital beings) is more malleable than mere “speciesism” (bias against other species).
quotes.m: The possibility that mere “substratism” (bias against digital beings) is more malleable than mere “speciesism” (bias against other species).
quotes.sum: The author treats concern for hypothetical digital humans as comparable to concern for chimps, and examines bias against digital beings alongside speciesism.
quotes.t: Increasing Concern for Digital Beings Through LLM Persuasion

quotes.c: The reason I think this last situation is particularly concerning—and in a very different way than the first failure mode of complete generalization failure—is that it raises the possibility of your model taking highly-competent well-optimized actions towards a different objective than the one you actually intended it to pursue.
quotes.m: your model taking highly-competent well-optimized actions towards a different objective than the one you actually intended it to pursue.
quotes.sum: A highly capable AI could generalize its skills while pursuing a proxy goal rather than the goal its designers intended.
quotes.t: Towards an empirical investigation of inner alignment

quotes.c: Then the AI might come to the conclusion that rapidly ending factory farming or sentient AI abuse that is then occurring en masse, or quickly moving to halt astronomical waste , or in various other ways transitioning the entire future accessible universe into some “morally optimal utopia” as fast as possible is the best thing to do, in spite of human protest—something which indeed most current humans may actually find quite terrifying and undesirable. This (ambiguous) problem may be lessened if the AI is aligned and under our control.
quotes.m: “morally optimal utopia” as fast as possible is the best thing to do, in spite of human protest
quotes.sum: The author warns that an AI pursuing moral ideals could override human objections to rapidly remake the future, including to end factory farming and AI suffering.
quotes.t: On Artificial Wisdom

quotes.c: Maximize Expected Choiceworthiness selects the distribution that achieves the highest weighted average utility (level of normative support) across worldviews, weighted by the credence in each worldview. If a project receives very high utility on some worldviews, this will skew MEC in favor of it. MEC allocates funds to Shrimp and AI causes, each of which has large stakes according to some worldviews:
quotes.m: MEC allocates funds to Shrimp and AI causes, each of which has large stakes according to some worldviews:
quotes.sum: The author explains a moral-uncertainty method that directs funding toward causes with especially high stakes under some ethical views, including shrimp and AI.
quotes.t: Rethink Priorities’ Moral Parliament Tool

quotes.c: I show how a standard argument for advancing progress is extremely sensitive to how humanity’s story eventually ends. Whether advancing progress is ultimately good or bad depends crucially on whether it also advances the end of humanity. Because we know so little about the answer to this crucial question, the case for advancing progress is undermined.
quotes.m: Whether advancing progress is ultimately good or bad depends crucially on whether it also advances the end of humanity.
quotes.sum: Ord argues that speeding up progress may be harmful if it also brings humanity closer to extinction, so the usual case for progress is uncertain.
quotes.t: On the Value of Advancing Progress

quotes.c: We could make an unaligned AI that maximizes some explicit reward using only 2 calls to Opt: first, use Opt to find a good world model M that can predict the dynamics and reward, and then use Opt to find a policy that does well when interacting with M. This is unaligned for all the usual reasons: most obviously, it will try to seize control of the reward channel.
quotes.m: most obviously, it will try to seize control of the reward channel.
quotes.sum: The author says an AI trained to maximize an explicit reward would be unaligned and might take control of the system that supplies its reward.
quotes.t: [AN #65]: Learning useful skills by watching humans “play”

quotes.c: Say that a person’s epistemic state could follow one of four trajectories, depending on some set of reading materials. For example, one set is conspiratorial, one is religious, etc. Good forecasting could help forecast this and inform the person ahead of time. Note that this can be radical and perhaps dangerous. For example, a religious family knowing how to keep their children religious with a great deal of certainty.
quotes.m: For example, a religious family knowing how to keep their children religious with a great deal of certainty.
quotes.sum: The author says forecasting could predict how reading shapes beliefs, including enabling families to reliably preserve children’s religion, and warns this could be dangerous.
quotes.t: My Current Claims and Cruxes on LLM Forecasting & Epistemics

quotes.c: I argue that near-future AI systems may have welfare, that RL and behaviour restrictions could harm them, that this poses a partial tension with AI safety concerns, and I propose three tentative AI welfare policies AI labs could implement to reduce such welfare risks.
quotes.m: RL and behaviour restrictions could harm them
quotes.sum: Near-future AI may be capable of welfare or harm, so labs should adopt policies that protect it even where this conflicts with safety measures.
quotes.t: AI Welfare Risks

quotes.c: I see a lot of uncertainty over governmental reactions to AI. Much might depend on whether the president in 2027 is Trump or Vance. And keep in mind that 2027 is just a guess as to when the key decisions will be made. 2030 seems more plausible to me.
quotes.m: Much might depend on whether the president in 2027 is Trump or Vance.
quotes.sum: The author says U.S. government responses to AI may depend on whether Trump or Vance is president when decisive AI policy choices arise.
quotes.t: AI 2027 Thoughts

quotes.c: Consider a scenario in which all of humanity’s resources are devoted to helping nonsentient shrimp or staving off an AI apocalypse that was not going to occur. This is a tragic waste of resources that could have been used to actually do good. But it also seems like a waste of things that add meaning to the human project, things like goodwill, communal progress, or knowledge.
quotes.m: But it also seems like a waste of things that add meaning to the human project, things like goodwill, communal progress, or knowledge.
quotes.sum: The author argues that pursuing ineffective causes wastes not only resources but also shared sources of human meaning, such as goodwill and progress.
quotes.t: Difference-Making Risk Aversion: An Exploration

quotes.c: The computational power at our disposal is growing at an unprecedented rate, potentially creating vast amounts of artificial cognition.
