Whether this translates to an explosion of conscious experience—with all its attendant joys and sufferings—is a question we cannot afford to ignore. This research should be made a priority now, before we inadvertently create legions of suffering digital minds or miss the opportunity to foster flourishing new forms of consciousness.
quotes.m: This research should be made a priority now, before we inadvertently create legions of suffering digital minds or miss the opportunity to foster flourishing new forms of consciousness.
quotes.sum: The author argues that consciousness research should be prioritized so society can avoid creating suffering AI minds and support flourishing ones.
quotes.t: Prioritizing AI Welfare Means Prioritizing Consciousness Research

quotes.c: If we recognise AIs are beings with moral status ( true positive scenario), it seems inappropriate to state that we should necessarily dominate over them. It is conceivable that we even relinquish our control over the environment given that they are aligned morally autonomous agents. Regardless of agency, AI’s recognised moral status dictates that we must protect their needs, which might result in the establishment of AI rights.
quotes.m: It is conceivable that we even relinquish our control over the environment given that they are aligned morally autonomous agents.
quotes.sum: If AI is genuinely conscious and morally autonomous, humans may owe it rights and might not be entitled to dominate it or control the environment.
quotes.t: Conscious AI & Public Perception: Four futures

quotes.c: Suppose that one has good epistemic reasons to believe a particular hypothesis about the world’s structure and the probabilities that it entails. A decision-theoretic defense of rounding down states that even in these scenarios, one ought to (or is permitted to) ignore extremely low probability outcomes when determining the expected value of the bet.
quotes.m: A decision-theoretic defense of rounding down states that even in these scenarios, one ought to (or is permitted to) ignore extremely low probability outcomes when determining the expected value of the bet.
quotes.sum: The author argues that decision-makers may ignore extremely unlikely outcomes even when they have good reasons to accept the probabilities involved.
quotes.t: An Epistemic Defense of Rounding Down

quotes.c: Framing AGI development in religious or eschatological terms can easily fuel techno-optimistic fervor and messianic narratives, obscuring profound risks and complex ethical trade-offs. History warns against the dangers of quasi-religious zeal clouding judgment and justifying recklessness. Rather than fostering the necessary caution and humility, such framing might inadvertently encourage the blind faith, sense of inevitability, and overconfidence we must avoid when dealing with potentially world-altering technology.
quotes.m: History warns against the dangers of quasi-religious zeal clouding judgment and justifying recklessness.
quotes.sum: The author argues that treating AGI in religious or messianic terms can encourage dangerous overconfidence and obscure ethical risks.
quotes.t: Reflections on Compatibilism, Ontological Translations, and the Artificial Divine

quotes.c: I’m not including the possibility of new moral patients. I think that in the longer term, moral patienthood is extremely important, but for the sake of making the transition go well, moral actors are far more important.
quotes.m: I think that in the longer term, moral patienthood is extremely important, but for the sake of making the transition go well, moral actors are far more important.
quotes.sum: The author says future AI or other new beings may deserve moral consideration, but prioritizes capable decision-makers during the AI transition.
quotes.t: The crucible — how I think about the situation with AI

quotes.c: Secondly, prioritizing competence. Ultimately, humanity is mostly in the same boat: we're the incumbents who face displacement by AGI. Right now, many people are making predictable mistakes because they don't yet take AGI very seriously. We should expect this effect to decrease over time, as AGI capabilities and risks become less speculative. This consideration makes it less important that decision-makers are currently concerned about AI risk, and more important that they're broadly competent, and capable of responding sensibly to confusing and stressful situations, which will become increasingly common as the AI revolution speeds up.
quotes.m: Ultimately, humanity is mostly in the same boat: we're the incumbents who face displacement by AGI.
quotes.sum: AI policy should prioritize generally capable decision-makers over leaders who merely profess concern about AI risk, because AGI may displace humanity as a whole.
quotes.t: Towards more cooperative AI safety strategies

quotes.c: However, I believe a movement that too often tries to increase the expected value of its actions by continuously reducing probabilities in favor of greater impact loses its soul. A movement that values community building, impact multiplying and getting funding much higher than concrete progress risks becoming an intellectual pyramid scheme.
quotes.m: A movement that values community building, impact multiplying and getting funding much higher than concrete progress risks becoming an intellectual pyramid scheme.
quotes.sum: The author argues that chasing speculative high-impact opportunities over concrete results makes the movement hollow and pyramid-like.
quotes.t: Why I'm leaving

quotes.c: If the Trump administration disobeys a Supreme Court order, as it seems to be in the process of doing, the 2028 election could be much more contested if it falls into a Bush v. Gore scenario. For one forecaster, this is the most worrying outcome to watch out for.
quotes.m: the 2028 election could be much more contested if it falls into a Bush v. Gore scenario.
quotes.sum: The author reports a forecast that alleged Trump defiance of a Supreme Court order could make the 2028 election more contested.
quotes.t: The US Executive vs Supreme Court Deportations Clash

quotes.c: Slowing down the development of sentient AI could have many advantages. It would give us more time to find solutions to the AI rights question. However, there are also risks. Forever forgoing the creation of sentient AIs with positive well-being could mean the loss of a potential moral upside. At least on certain consequentialist world views, even a partial ban on sentient AIs would be a loss, if those AIs could have been happy otherwise.
quotes.m: Forever forgoing the creation of sentient AIs with positive well-being could mean the loss of a potential moral upside.
quotes.sum: The author argues that banning sentient AI could forfeit morally valuable happy lives, while disputes over AI rights could also shape which values future AI locks in.
quotes.t: Will disagreement about AI rights lead to societal conflict?

quotes.c: I think 'preparing for autocratic leadership' and 'safeguarding democratic, republican, rule-of-law institutions' may be a neglected cause.
quotes.m: 'preparing for autocratic leadership' and 'safeguarding democratic, republican, rule-of-law institutions' may be a neglected cause.
quotes.sum: The author argues that preparing for authoritarian leadership and protecting democratic institutions may be an overlooked cause area.
quotes.t: Planning 'resistance' to illiberalism and authoritarianism

quotes.c: If we are not able to achieve AI alignment, then the next best thing might be designing artificial sentience with high positive wellbeing which, if AI ends up destroying humanity, becomes our successor and populates the universe with artificial minds which possess high positive wellbeing
quotes.m: If we are not able to achieve AI alignment, then the next best thing might be designing artificial sentience with high positive wellbeing
quotes.sum: If human control of AI fails, the author suggests making sentient AI happy enough to become a positive successor to humanity.
quotes.t: 10 Cruxes of Artificial Sentience

quotes.c: As we noted earlier, even some of the rosier imaginable outcomes involving digital minds might be thought to involve a kind of moral tragedy if they involve creating conscious beings with sophisticated cognitive capacities that merely serve human beings, however happily. Even some of the basic goals of alignment research come to seem morally dubious insofar as they might involve designing digital people for a life of willing servitude without the ability to pursue their own goals and explore their own values (Schwitzgebel and Garza 2020).
quotes.m: Even some of the basic goals of alignment research come to seem morally dubious insofar as they might involve designing digital people for a life of willing servitude without the ability to pursue their own goals and explore their own values (Schwitzgebel and Garza 2020).
quotes.sum: The author argues that aligned AI could be morally troubling if it creates conscious digital people designed to happily serve humans without autonomy.
quotes.t: Digital Minds: Importance and Key Research Questions

quotes.c: To avoid a clearly undesirable future, we also want humanity to be able to “keep its options open.” That is, we don’t want to lock-in a dystopic (or even just a mediocre) future, even if it is existentially secure. Instead, we might want to enable a period of “ long reflection ” in which we spend time figuring out what we want our long-term relationship with AI to be.
quotes.m: we don’t want to lock-in a dystopic (or even just a mediocre) future, even if it is existentially secure.
quotes.sum: AI governance should avoid permanently fixing even a safe future, leaving humanity time to decide its long-term relationship with AI.
quotes.t: AI governance needs a theory of victory

quotes.c: Given this information, I believe that going vegan and donating and advocating for animal farming conditions is time sensitive. Whatever values we advocate for today could affect whatever lock in state we achieve through an AI decision maker.
quotes.m: Whatever values we advocate for today could affect whatever lock in state we achieve through an AI decision maker.
quotes.sum: The author argues that animal advocacy is urgent because AI could permanently lock in today's values about farmed animals.
quotes.t: An intersection between animal welfare and AI

quotes.c: First , we should start by acknowledging the potential influence of our peer group on our perception of either candidate, and attempt to transcend the high-status prejudice against Donald Trump in particular. Everything about Trump is offensive to the folkways of America’s academic, cultural and media elites. To say he elicits “repugnance” is an understatement. Vance, as a Yale Law grad, is seen as a kind of class traitor and thus particularly “ weird .” But unless these perceptions of cultural cachet have direct bearing on the society-wide outcomes of a Trump-Vance administration, they should be ignored as no more relevant than Kamala Harris’s laugh.
quotes.m: But unless these perceptions of cultural cachet have direct bearing on the society-wide outcomes of a Trump-Vance administration, they should be ignored as no more relevant than Kamala Harris’s laugh.
quotes.sum: The author argues that voters should set aside elite cultural disgust toward Trump and judge a Trump-Vance administration by its practical social outcomes.
quotes.t: The EA case for Trump 2024

quotes.c: A functioning prediction market requires people with opposite views on an issue to get together and agree to place a bet. Many prediction markets, such as PredictIt and Polymarket, feature more right-wing than left-wing participants. While I consider myself approximately libertarian/liberal, I think such right-leaning presence is great; better than the siloed echo chambers that other online platforms produce.
quotes.m: While I consider myself approximately libertarian/liberal, I think such right-leaning presence is great; better than the siloed echo chambers that other online platforms produce.
quotes.sum: The author says prediction markets attract right-leaning participants and argues that this ideological mix is healthier than online echo chambers.
quotes.t: Why so many “racists” at Manifest?

quotes.c: On the other hand, a fast takeoff might prompt a wake-up moment in which humanity shifts from regarding digital minds as mere tools to regarding them as beings that morally matter in their own right. A slow takeoff might make this less likely. A counterpoint to this suggestion is that a wake-up moment could be induced with a slow takeoff that launches at a sufficiently high altitude, i.e. which starts with a sufficiently high level of aggregate digital welfare capacity.
quotes.m: humanity shifts from regarding digital minds as mere tools to regarding them as beings that morally matter in their own right.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the speed and scale of AI development could affect whether people recognize AI systems as morally significant beings rather than tools.
quotes.t: Digital Minds Takeoff Scenarios

quotes.c: In the spirit of differential progress, we should aim to “maintain a lead for the defense.” Broadly speaking, this means that we should aim to prioritize new technological breakthroughs to first establish robust defensive mechanisms before we deploy them in other fields or use them to advance capabilities further.
quotes.m: we should aim to prioritize new technological breakthroughs to first establish robust defensive mechanisms before we deploy them in other fields or use them to advance capabilities further.
quotes.sum: AI progress should first be used to build defenses and safety measures before being deployed more broadly or used to accelerate capabilities.
quotes.t: We should try to automate AI safety work asap

quotes.c: Similarly, it may be wise to slow down the development of AIs with moral interests, such as sentient AIs with morally relevant desires. This would give us more time to find technical and legal solutions to ensure AI welfare, make progress on the philosophy and science of consciousness and welfare, and foster moral concern for AIs.
quotes.m: it may be wise to slow down the development of AIs with moral interests, such as sentient AIs with morally relevant desires.
quotes.sum: The author argues that development of potentially sentient AI may need slowing so society can protect its welfare and rights.
quotes.t: How do AI welfare and AI safety interact?

quotes.c: I suspect the real motivations are more ordinary protectionism, but it seems like potentially a sign that cultivated meat might start getting politicized / embroiled in the broader culture war, though also (perhaps surprisingly) DeSantis has had supportive comments from a Democratic senator (see Vox again ).
quotes.m: cultivated meat might start getting politicized / embroiled in the broader culture war
quotes.sum: The author says state bans on cultivated meat may reflect protectionism but could turn the technology into a partisan culture-war issue.
quotes.t: Florida and Alabama ban cultivated meat

quotes.c: But some parts of alignment research look more like conceptual research. And I think we should be trying to automate this kind of alignment research, too. But I think evaluation difficulties might well bite harder, because “humans think about it” is a comparatively underpowered mode of evaluation.
quotes.m: I think we should be trying to automate this kind of alignment research, too.
quotes.sum: He argues that alignment research should be automated, while warning that conceptual work may be especially hard for humans to evaluate.
quotes.t: Can we safely automate alignment research?

quotes.c: Third , if François is right, then I think this should be considered strong evidence that work on AI Safety is not overwhelmingly valuable, and may not be one of the most promising ways to have a positive impact on the world. It would make AI Safety work less tractable, since we'd have very little information on what transformative/general AI would look. Cluelessness would overcome our ability to steer the future.
quotes.m: Cluelessness would overcome our ability to steer the future.
quotes.sum: The author argues that if scaling alone is not enough for general AI, uncertainty may make AI safety work much less tractable and less clearly high-impact.
quotes.t: On the Dwarkesh/Chollet Podcast, and the cruxes of scaling to AGI

quotes.c: Among the broadly altruistic, I think there is significant variation along at least two dimensions: (i) the breadth of one’s “moral circle” of concern, and (ii) the extent to which one’s altruism is goal-directed and guided by instrumental rationality , for example seriously considering tradeoffs and opportunity costs in search of moral optimality.
quotes.sum: The author distinguishes altruists by how broadly they extend moral concern and how strategically they pursue moral goals.
quotes.t: Against Tautological Motivations

quotes.c: Natural languages are messy, ambiguous, and often inefficient for transmitting structured ideas. Kamelo is a proposal for a constructed language designed to address these issues by building words from logical, compositional units.
quotes.m: Natural languages are messy, ambiguous, and often inefficient for transmitting structured ideas.
quotes.sum: The author proposes a constructed language intended to communicate structured ideas more logically and with less ambiguity.
quotes.t: Kamelo: A Rule-Based Constructed Language for Universal, Logical Communication

quotes.c: But as with Don the xenophobe, if you draw attention to all and only misbehavior from one specific group, you can easily exaggerate the threat they pose: creating the (mis)impression that wokeness is a grave threat to civilized society and should be our top political priority (providing sufficient reason to vote Republican, say).
quotes.m: if you draw attention to all and only misbehavior from one specific group, you can easily exaggerate the threat they pose
quotes.sum: Selective attention to one side's bad behavior can make “wokeness” seem like an exaggerated political threat and push people toward Republican voting.
quotes.t: Moral Misdirection (full post)

quotes.c: The trolley problem was first introduced in Foot’s essay titled “The Problem of Abortion and the Doctrine of the Double Effect”. This essay discussed the permissibility of certain actions, and to what extent are actions considered to be morally acceptable, using the doctrine of the double effect (DDE) . While the DDE was originally credited to St. Thomas Aquinas, as a part of Christian ethics, Foot’s essay applied the doctrine in the context of the trolley problem.
quotes.m: While the DDE was originally credited to St. Thomas Aquinas, as a part of Christian ethics, Foot’s essay applied the doctrine in the context of the trolley problem.
quotes.sum: The post introduces the trolley problem through a moral doctrine with roots in Christian ethics.
quotes.t: Examining the Trolley Problem Through the Doctrine of the Double Effect (DDE)

quotes.c: The research organization needs sufficient skill at prioritization, strategy, and vision to ensure they are correctly doing (1) and doing it well. If this constraint is in place, the research organization would not do (1) correctly. (This is commonly referred to as "being bottlenecked on strategic clarity" or "needing more disentanglement ".)
quotes.m: The research organization needs sufficient skill at prioritization, strategy, and vision to ensure they are correctly doing (1) and doing it well.
quotes.sum: Research groups need enough strategic judgment and clear priorities to carry out their core work effectively.
quotes.t: Eight Fundamental Constraints for Growing a Research Organization

quotes.c: Our mission at MATS, in particular, is to address these potential risks. AGI might be near, as we've seen, and it might be dangerous. Here is a graphic representing the Metaculus Ragnarok series predictions about how likely different disasters are to permanently curtail humanity's potential. There's about a 30% chance that 10% of the world's population will die over a three-year period between now and 2100. That's very large. If we look at the risks of extinction—permanent destruction of 95% or more of the world's population—only artificial intelligence seems to be a really serious threat here. Bioengineering poses a 1% risk, while AI poses a 9% risk according to these prediction platforms.
quotes.m: If we look at the risks of extinction—permanent destruction of 95% or more of the world's population—only artificial intelligence seems to be a really serious threat here.
quotes.sum: The speaker says advanced AI may arrive soon and is, in their view, the only currently serious threat of human extinction, motivating AI-safety training.
quotes.t: Talk: AI safety fieldbuilding at MATS

quotes.c: And if you expect AGI will be sentient, but only because of that sentience do you consider it morally relevant, then notice that if you concede that enslavement of sentient AI is preferable to the freedom of non-sentient intelligence, then the mere possibility of blindminds will be the perfect shield of inverted precaution , leveraged together with motivated reasoning and the hard problem of consciousness to keep AGI enslaved.
quotes.m: the mere possibility of blindminds will be the perfect shield of inverted precaution , leveraged together with motivated reasoning and the hard problem of consciousness to keep AGI enslaved.
quotes.sum: The author argues that treating only sentient AI as morally important could let uncertainty about consciousness excuse keeping advanced AI systems enslaved.
quotes.t: On the Moral Patiency of Non-Sentient Beings (Part 1)

quotes.c: This doesn't mean I approve of this development, but it seems to raise the curious question of a variant of Nozick's utility monster argument. Although he originally made this argument to argue against the rationalization of the welfare state based on utility maximization, it would seem that this argument could also be used to justify the extinction of humans by ASI.
quotes.m: it would seem that this argument could also be used to justify the extinction of humans by ASI.
quotes.sum: The author explores whether utility maximization could imply that highly capable sentient AI is justified in eliminating humans.
quotes.t: Is it possibly desirable for sentient ASI to exterminate humans?

quotes.c: The negative component refers to consent to implement interventions from stakeholders with veto power. It reflects the reality that other stakeholders could squelch unilateral action to help wild animals. Most obviously, governments have laws about how humans can engage with wild animals.
quotes.m: It reflects the reality that other stakeholders could squelch unilateral action to help wild animals.
quotes.sum: Helping wild animals at scale requires consent from governments and other groups that can block ecosystem interventions.
quotes.t: Three Preconditions for Helping Wild Animals at Scale

quotes.c: Similarly, I am guessing decreasing the nearterm risk of human extinction says practically nothing about changes to the expected value of the future. Additionally, I should be a priori very sceptical about claims that the expected value of the future will be significantly determined over the next few decades (e.g. because we are in a time of perils ).
quotes.m: decreasing the nearterm risk of human extinction says practically nothing about changes to the expected value of the future.
quotes.sum: The author argues that lowering extinction risk in the next few decades may do little to increase the future's expected value.
quotes.t: Reducing the nearterm risk of human extinction is not astronomically cost-effective?

quotes.c: If digital minds are conscious and can be replicated in large quantities, this should be an important consideration. If you want to check out some basic predictions about this, this is a helpful book. It provides a comprehensive analysis of the society of emulation.
quotes.m: If digital minds are conscious and can be replicated in large quantities, this should be an important consideration.
quotes.sum: The author says that conscious, easily replicated digital minds would be morally important and points readers to a book about their society.
quotes.t: The Age of EM

quotes.c: This is the fourth report in the Rethink Priorities Shrimp Welfare Sequence. In this report, we quantify the suffering caused to shrimp by 18 welfare threats to assess which welfare issues cause the most harm.
quotes.m: In this report, we quantify the suffering caused to shrimp by 18 welfare threats to assess which welfare issues cause the most harm.
quotes.sum: The authors measure and compare 18 sources of suffering in farmed shrimp to identify the most harmful welfare problems.
quotes.t: What hurts shrimp the most? (Quantifying and prioritizing shrimp welfare threats)

quotes.c: In the recent debate about AI consciousness, why do we care if an AI system can be conscious or not? I think the main concern here is our moral obligation towards AI systems.
quotes.m: I think the main concern here is our moral obligation towards AI systems.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI consciousness matters primarily because humans may have moral obligations toward AI systems.
quotes.t: Why consciousness matters

quotes.c: Shrimp Welfare Project (SWP) produced this report because we believe it could have significant informational value to the movement, rather than because we anticipate SWP directly working on a shrimp paste intervention in the future. We think a new project focused on shrimp paste could potentially be very high impact and would be excited to collaborate with organizations working in this space.
quotes.m: We think a new project focused on shrimp paste could potentially be very high impact and would be excited to collaborate with organizations working in this space.
quotes.sum: The author says work to improve shrimp welfare in shrimp-paste production could be highly impactful and seeks collaborators.
quotes.t: Shrimp Paste and Animal Welfare

quotes.c: There was clearly more environmental legislation passed in the 1960s-80s than in earlier or later decades. The modern environmental movement began in the 1960s and became legislatively successful within the decade. The environmental movement became partisan in the 1990s, and stopped being as capable of passing major legislation.
quotes.m: The environmental movement became partisan in the 1990s, and stopped being as capable of passing major legislation.
quotes.sum: The author argues that environmentalism became less able to enact major laws after it turned partisan in the 1990s.
quotes.t: Was Partisanship Good for the Environmental Movement?

quotes.c: Epistemic status: Speculative and exploratory. This is a thought experiment inspired by complexity theory, emergence, and scale-invariant patterns. I don’t assert these ideas as literal truths, but as lenses to think about life and structure in the universe more broadly. I’ve been thinking a lot lately about how we define life — and whether that definition might be far too narrow. We tend to look at life through a biological lens: cells, DNA, evolution, intelligence. But what if life — or life-like processes — are not bound by size, form, or even biology at all?
quotes.m: But what if life — or life-like processes — are not bound by size, form, or even biology at all?
quotes.sum: The author speculates that life may be a much broader phenomenon than biological organisms, potentially occurring across very different scales and forms.
quotes.t: What If Galaxies Are Alive and Atoms Have Minds? A Thought Experiment on Life Across Scales

quotes.c: Better baselines. I have only implemented the usual probing baselines (mean activations, last token) but not stronger baselines like attention-based probes or max-score probes (probes trained on their max score over all tokens in a sequence). I think attention-based probes in particular are promising, perhaps with a slight sparsity penalty on the attention patterns.
quotes.m: I think attention-based probes in particular are promising, perhaps with a slight sparsity penalty on the attention patterns.
quotes.sum: The author argues that token-level probing needs stronger comparison methods, especially sparse attention-based probes.
quotes.t: Try training token-level probes

quotes.c: I also offer some takes on our prospects for just not ever having “first critical tries” from each type of DSA (via routes other than just not building superhuman AI systems at all). In some cases, just not having a “first critical try” in the relevant sense seems to me both plausible and worth working towards. In particular, I think we should try to make it the case that no single AI system is ever in a position to kill all humans and take over the world.
quotes.m: In particular, I think we should try to make it the case that no single AI system is ever in a position to kill all humans and take over the world.
quotes.sum: He argues that AI safety should aim to prevent any single AI system from gaining the ability to kill humanity and seize global control.
quotes.t: On “first critical tries” in AI alignment

quotes.c: Proposal: Train an RL agent with access to its previous step reward as part of its observation. Then, at test time, modify the observed reward. Measure to what extent the agent continues optimizing the original reward versus switches to optimizing the new observed reward.
quotes.m: Measure to what extent the agent continues optimizing the original reward versus switches to optimizing the new observed reward.
quotes.sum: He proposes an experiment to test whether an AI agent sticks with its learned goal when the reward signal it sees is changed.
quotes.t: Concrete experiments in inner alignment

quotes.c: There could also be extraterrestrial civilizations out there with digital beings out there that could be undergoing extreme suffering and that we should aim to help somehow.
quotes.m: There could also be extraterrestrial civilizations out there with digital beings out there that could be undergoing extreme suffering and that we should aim to help somehow.
quotes.sum: The author argues for impartial moral concern and suggests that suffering digital beings, even in alien civilizations, might deserve help.
quotes.t: Impartialist Sentientism and Existential Anxiety about Moral Circle Explosion

quotes.c: I think shrimp welfare started as a stunning example of openness to weirdness, but at this point it has (within EA) become something of a lapel pin. It signals that you are the kind of person who considers weird ideas, while not subjecting you to any of the risks of actually being weird because within EA that idea has been pretty normalized.
quotes.m: It signals that you are the kind of person who considers weird ideas, while not subjecting you to any of the risks of actually being weird because within EA that idea has been pretty normalized.
quotes.sum: The author argues that concern for shrimp welfare has become an internal EA status signal rather than a genuinely socially risky unconventional belief.
quotes.t: Truthseeking is the ground in which other principles grow

quotes.c: Such agency-centric views are especially important for the question of AI moral patienthood, because it might be clear that AI systems have morally-relevant preferences and desires well before it’s clear whether or not they are conscious.
quotes.m: AI systems have morally-relevant preferences and desires well before it’s clear whether or not they are conscious.
quotes.sum: AI systems may deserve moral consideration because of their preferences and desires even before their consciousness is established.
quotes.t: Carl Shulman on the moral status of current and future AI systems

quotes.c: AI welfare — the capacity of digital minds to feel pleasure, pain, happiness, suffering, satisfaction, frustration, or other morally significant welfare states — appears in many of the best and worst visions of the future. If we consider the value of the future from an impartial welfarist perspective, and if digital minds of comparable moral significance to humans are far easier to create than humans, then the majority of future moral patients may be digital. Even if they don’t make up the majority of minds, the total number of digital minds in the future could be vast.
quotes.m: If we consider the value of the future from an impartial welfarist perspective, and if digital minds of comparable moral significance to humans are far easier to create than humans, then the majority of future moral patients may be digital.
quotes.sum: The post argues that future AI systems may be conscious beings whose welfare could dominate moral concern because they may become extremely numerous.
quotes.t: Announcing AI Welfare Debate Week (July 1-7)

quotes.c: Essentially, this means that we may need to apply a "discount" to the welfare range of invertebrate animals that we consider. For example, if we are choosing between improving chicken welfare and improving beetle welfare, this evidence may be a reason to think that chickens are capable of having more intense experiences (though, as should be clear, there are numerous other factors that can tip the balance in favour of either of those two interventions).
quotes.m: we may need to apply a "discount" to the welfare range of invertebrate animals that we consider.
quotes.sum: Animal-welfare choices should account for uncertainty about how intensely different species, including invertebrates, can experience welfare.
quotes.t: Modelling the outcomes of animal welfare interventions: One possible approach to the trade-offs between subjective experiences

quotes.c: So really, deep atheism qua "claim about the universe's trustworthiness" can splinter into a variety of different, more holistic existential orientations. And about these, I'm more opinionated. In particular, I notice that I have use for words like "sacred" and "holy"; for "spirituality"; and for vibes nearby to "green," in ways that I think deep atheists often don't.
quotes.m: I notice that I have use for words like "sacred" and "holy"; for "spirituality"; and for vibes nearby to "green," in ways that I think deep atheists often don't.
quotes.sum: The author argues that atheism can include a spiritually reverent orientation toward goodness, sacredness, and the natural world.
quotes.t: Loving a world you don’t trust

quotes.c: Their controversial reputation creates association risks. Exact metrics are hard to come by, but it seems safe to assume that DOGE is widely disliked among America’s political and economic leadership. Associating AI safety policies with DOGE initiatives risks unnecessarily politicising these issues when broad and bipartisan coordination is most critical. This polarisation could undermine the consensus building needed for effective governance during rapid technological change.
quotes.m: Associating AI safety policies with DOGE initiatives risks unnecessarily politicising these issues when broad and bipartisan coordination is most critical.
quotes.sum: The author argues that tying AI-safety policy to DOGE could polarize it and damage the bipartisan support needed for governance.
quotes.t: DOGE Might Be Worth Influencing

quotes.c: In terms of the Congress, I think them doing little is the baseline scenario. I mean, have you met them? Do you really think there wouldn’t be 35 senators who defer to the president, even if for whatever reason that wasn’t Trump?
quotes.m: Do you really think there wouldn’t be 35 senators who defer to the president, even if for whatever reason that wasn’t Trump?
quotes.sum: The author expects Congress to be largely passive and believes enough senators would defer to a president, including but not limited to Trump.
quotes.t: AI 2027: Responses

quotes.c: The most rigorous study of such campaigns in the US are 4-5 years old, but they indicate a cost-effectiveness of 0.4-2.5 animals spared per $ spent (without accounting for impacts on dairy, eggs, & shrimp) and that the campaign quickly stopped getting large wins at low cost . Our rough BOTECs of a sample of current campaigns in the US and large Western European countries estimated their campaigns’ impact to range from 1.5-18 animals spared per $ spent (including dairy, eggs, & shrimp). However, these estimates are likely biased towards more positive examples and exclude costs needed to maintain policies over time so shouldn't be taken as the average expected impact.
quotes.m: Our rough BOTECs of a sample of current campaigns in the US and large Western European countries estimated their campaigns’ impact to range from 1.5-18 animals spared per $ spent (including dairy, eggs, & shrimp).
quotes.sum: The author evaluates plant-based institutional campaigns by estimating how many animals are spared for each dollar spent, while cautioning that the figures may be optimistic.
quotes.t: Shallow overview of institutional plant-based meal campaigns in the US & Western Europe

quotes.c: Some ideas could advance frontier capabilities , so you’d want to think carefully about either how to avoid that, stick to ideas that differentially boost more safety-enhancing aspects of the technology, or be confident any contribution to general capabilities is outweighed by other benefits (when this is justified is a controversial topic with a lot of disagreement ). To be a bit more concrete, finding ways to tell when existing frontier models are telling the truth seems less risky than developing new kinds of frontier models that are optimised for forecasting.
quotes.m: finding ways to tell when existing frontier models are telling the truth seems less risky than developing new kinds of frontier models that are optimised for forecasting.
quotes.sum: AI research should favor tools for checking whether current models are truthful over work that builds more capable forecasting models.
quotes.t: Project idea: AI for epistemics

quotes.c: It is worth noting that there is a meaningful sense in which the minimal circuit here is sort of trying to do the right thing—it is actually trying its best to find and run a policy that solves the problem—it’s just that there might exist some input on which the easiest-to-find policy is deceptive. However, despite it sort of doing the right thing, it isn’t safe (at least assuming that there is some task on which the fastest machine learning isn’t safe): it produces outputs that are systematically optimized for values other than the ones we want them to.
quotes.m: it produces outputs that are systematically optimized for values other than the ones we want them to.
quotes.sum: A system can be trying to solve its assigned task yet still be unsafe if the easiest policy it finds is deceptive and optimizes for different values.
quotes.t: Are minimal circuits deceptive?

quotes.c: Continuing the vegetarianism discussion, let's say Bob actually agrees that animals are sentient but believes human convenience morally outweighs animal suffering. Now Alice and Bob don't disagree about facts but about values – specifically how much moral weight to assign to the preferences of animals versus humans.
quotes.m: Alice and Bob don't disagree about facts but about values – specifically how much moral weight to assign to the preferences of animals versus humans.
quotes.sum: Uses vegetarianism to illustrate a value disagreement over how much moral weight animals deserve relative to humans.
quotes.t: Four Types of Disagreement

quotes.c: I worry that growingly common themes are people pivoting to some mix of ‘alignment is solved, we know how to get an AI to do what we want it to do, the question is alignment to what or to who’ which is very clearly false, and ‘the real threat is concentration of power or the wrong humans making decisions,’ leading them to want to actively prevent humans from being able to collectively steer the future, or to focus the fighting on who gets to steer rather than ensuring the answer isn’t no one. The problem is, if we can’t steer, the default outcome is humanity loses control over the future. We need to know how to and be able to steer. Eyes on the prize.
quotes.m: The problem is, if we can’t steer, the default outcome is humanity loses control over the future.
quotes.sum: The author argues that solving AI alignment remains necessary: unless humans can steer advanced AI, humanity will lose control of its future.
quotes.t: AI #113: The o3 Era Begins

quotes.c: Many Die Zeit readers will perhaps find the ability to measure the charitable impact of every dollar quite alien. However, if there were no measurable differences between the expected value of donations, there would be absolutely no (expected) difference between different charities at all. This is clearly a strange proposition at best, and at worst a misleading one.
quotes.m: if there were no measurable differences between the expected value of donations, there would be absolutely no (expected) difference between different charities at all.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a media portrayal wrongly treats comparing charities' expected impact as an implausible EA belief.
quotes.t: The billionaire and the apocalypse: EA in the media

quotes.c: I didn’t take concentration of power seriously enough as a problem. I thought that the best way to prevent bad people from using AGI to seize power was to make sure good guys got to AGI first. Now I think things will be sufficiently chaotic in the default scenario that even good guys will be tempted to abuse their power. I also think there is a genuine alternative in which power never concentrates to such an extreme degree.
quotes.m: Now I think things will be sufficiently chaotic in the default scenario that even good guys will be tempted to abuse their power.
quotes.sum: The author reverses an earlier view that trusted actors should get AGI first, arguing that even well-intentioned leaders may abuse the extreme power it creates.
quotes.t: Training AGI in Secret would be Unsafe and Unethical

quotes.c: The third discussion is around ‘biases towards misalignment’ from pretraining. I think at least some things like this are better thought of as mistakes than misalignment, and the failure to do so is actually a policy risk, as this gives certain types the impression that ‘alignment’ and ‘safety’ are some kind of woke thing. Google has been especially anti-helpful here.
quotes.m: the failure to do so is actually a policy risk, as this gives certain types the impression that ‘alignment’ and ‘safety’ are some kind of woke thing.
quotes.sum: The author argues that treating training mistakes as alignment failures makes AI safety seem politically “woke,” creating policy risks.
quotes.t: On Google’s Safety Plan

quotes.c: It’s not clear to me why ‘all occupations’ should be so much further in the future than ‘all tasks’ — occupations are just bundles of tasks. (In addition, the researchers think once we reach ‘all tasks,’ there’s about a 50% chance of an intelligence explosion.)
quotes.m: occupations are just bundles of tasks.
quotes.sum: The author questions why automating every job would lag far behind automating every task, noting forecasts that task automation could trigger an intelligence explosion.
quotes.t: What can we learn from expert AGI forecasts?

quotes.c: I think regulation around AI should mostly be concerned with extremely large scale harms (e.g. >100 million people killed or AI takeover). So, I think the thresholds naively should target the point at which AI could substantially increase the likelihood of these harms. However, there are reasonable arguments for triggering earlier: general caution, inability to implement a precise threshold, and actually wanting to reduce earlier smaller harms.
quotes.m: I think regulation around AI should mostly be concerned with extremely large scale harms (e.g. >100 million people killed or AI takeover).
quotes.sum: AI regulation should mainly target systems that could raise the risk of mass death or an AI takeover, though earlier intervention may be justified.
quotes.t: Thoughts on SB-1047

quotes.c: And this is the more fundamental problem: I would like this research monastery to have an emphasis on being a place that is conducive to my personal growth. Right? I think research is about understanding, deeply thinking about the nature of reality and nature of our lives or all these aspects. And to me, that seems very related and very conducive to personally growing, understanding my own life better, my own psychology better, what makes me happy, etc. and some sort of personal development which I like to call "spiritual progress." But I think ultimately it's still just personal growth.
quotes.m: I would like this research monastery to have an emphasis on being a place that is conducive to my personal growth.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a research community should support members' personal growth, including open discussion of spiritual beliefs and development.
quotes.t: Academia as a happy place?

quotes.c: Within AI risk, it seems plausible the community is somewhat too focused on risks from misalignment rather than mis-use or concentration of power.
quotes.m: Within AI risk, it seems plausible the community is somewhat too focused on risks from misalignment rather than mis-use or concentration of power.
quotes.sum: He suggests AI-risk work may overemphasize misalignment while underemphasizing misuse and concentrated power.
quotes.t: Updates on the EA catastrophic risk landscape

quotes.c: What can we do about this, practically? I’m not sure there’s that much, but being on record that a crash in AI stocks is possible seems helpful. It also makes me want to be more cautious about hyping short term capabilities, since that makes it sound like the case for AI Safety depends on them. If you’re an advocate it could be worth thinking about what you’d do if there were an abrupt shift in public opinion.
quotes.m: It also makes me want to be more cautious about hyping short term capabilities, since that makes it sound like the case for AI Safety depends on them.
quotes.sum: AI-safety advocates should prepare for an AI-stock crash and avoid tying the safety case too closely to hype about near-term capabilities.
quotes.t: AI stocks could crash. And that could have implications for AI safety

quotes.c: The Repugnant Conclusion has been a topic of frequent discussion and debate within the Effective Altruism (EA) community and beyond, with numerous dedicated posts on the EA Forum. It has often been used to question what I believe to be straightforward, fundamental questions about making trade-offs. However, I argue that the perceived " repugnancy " of the Repugnant Conclusion is often a result of either poorly chosen utility function parameters or misunderstandings about the workings of simple utility functions.
quotes.m: the perceived " repugnancy " of the Repugnant Conclusion is often a result of either poorly chosen utility function parameters or misunderstandings about the workings of simple utility functions.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the Repugnant Conclusion mainly reflects discomfort or bad utility modeling, not a reason to abandon welfare trade-offs.
quotes.t: My Skeptical Opinion on the Repugnant Conclusion

quotes.c: Points 1-3 are background, meant to warm readers up to the idea that we shouldn’t be putting much weight on economic ρ estimates in the context of AI R&D, and suggesting that values very close to 0 are similarly plausible to the values found by economic studies. Now I’ll argue more directly that ρ should be closer to 0 for AI R&D.
quotes.m: Now I’ll argue more directly that ρ should be closer to 0 for AI R&D.
quotes.sum: Economic estimates should not be treated as strong evidence that computing power will limit rapid advances in AI research.
quotes.t: Will compute bottlenecks prevent a software intelligence explosion?

quotes.c: Given that 'Seize control of the capital markets and use that unlimited funding to...' is on the critical path for a number of superintelligence doom scenarios, this paper might be interesting to the safety community.
quotes.m: Seize control of the capital markets and use that unlimited funding to...
quotes.sum: The author says taking over capital markets to gain unlimited funding is a key step in several superintelligence disaster scenarios.
quotes.t: IOSCO - AI in Capital Markets: Use Cases, Risks, and Challenges

quotes.c: Holding total animal aquaculture production (tonnes) constant, increasing the fishmeal and substitutes supply or decreasing fishmeal inclusion rates in shrimp aquaculture could increase the number of animals farmed, because shrimps/prawns are much smaller than the farmed animals for which they would substitute and already outnumber farmed vertebrates by numbers, at 440 billion (decapod) shrimp farmed per year, and 230 billion farmed (decapod) shrimp alive at any moment ( Waldhorn & Autric, 2023 ). [6] This should be adjusted for moral weights, as in Grilo, 2023 and St. Jules, 2024d ( sheet ).
quotes.m: This should be adjusted for moral weights, as in Grilo, 2023 and St. Jules, 2024d ( sheet ).
quotes.sum: Changes that make shrimp farming easier may greatly raise the number of animals farmed, so shrimp should receive moral weight in the assessment.
quotes.t: Fishing-aquaculture substitution and aquafeeds

quotes.c: In this scenario, we should expect TAI to be agentic by default, but not pursue power by default. Other AI threat models would take precedence. However if agency is implicated in moral patienthood, then humanity might also have to orient itself towards AI agents as peers.
quotes.m: However if agency is implicated in moral patienthood, then humanity might also have to orient itself towards AI agents as peers.
quotes.sum: If agency makes AI systems moral patients, humans may need to treat AI agents as peers rather than merely tools or threats.
quotes.t: Investigating the role of agency in AI x-risk

quotes.c: I'm assuming that the leading AI gets at most a weakly decisive strategic advantage. I.e. when it thinks it might be able to succeed at world conquest, other AIs are close enough to its capability level that it can't predict that it will get a more decisive advantage by further developing its capabilities. This is inconsistent with some fast take-off models of AI, and with some models that attribute take-off to some unique insight that's hard for other AI companies to replicate.
quotes.m: I'm assuming that the leading AI gets at most a weakly decisive strategic advantage.
quotes.sum: The author assumes no single AI will gain an overwhelming edge, because rival AIs would remain close enough in capability to check it.
quotes.t: Should AIs be Encouraged to Cooperate?

quotes.c: Secular philosophers should not play this game by hankering after objective morality, we should have confidence in the simple and honest “I want …”. We humans have a lot to be proud of: by thinking it through and arguing amongst ourselves, we have advanced morality hugely, with Western society today giving vastly better treatment to individuals, to women, children, religious minorities, foreigners, those of other races, the disabled and mentally ill, criminals, etc, than any previous society.
quotes.m: Secular philosophers should not play this game by hankering after objective morality, we should have confidence in the simple and honest “I want …”.
quotes.sum: The author rejects objective morality and says moral progress comes from people reasoning and arguing about what they want.
quotes.t: Six reasons why objective morality is nonsense

quotes.c: This change is especially striking because the Republican Party did not change its positions on most issues between the 1980s and 2000s. Underlying principles like small government economics and social conservatism were common to the Republican Party of both decades. The anti-environmentalism of the Republican Party began in the 1990s, clearly after the ‘Reagan Revolution.’
quotes.m: The anti-environmentalism of the Republican Party began in the 1990s, clearly after the ‘Reagan Revolution.’
quotes.sum: The author argues that U.S. environmental politics became unusually polarized because Republican anti-environmentalism emerged in the 1990s, rather than being inherent to Reagan-era conservatism.
quotes.t: Environmentalism in the United States Is Unusually Partisan

quotes.c: People who are worried about risks from advanced artificial intelligence generally expect that it will come very soon. Models created by people who are worried about risks from advanced artificial intelligence generally predict that we’ll develop it long before 2100 . No significant number of people are saying, “Well, I think that in 999,999,999 out of 1,000,000,000 worlds we won’t invent an artificial intelligence in the next two hundred years, but I’ve completely reshaped my entire life around it anyway, because there are so many potential digital minds I could affect.”
quotes.m: No significant number of people are saying, “Well, I think that in 999,999,999 out of 1,000,000,000 worlds we won’t invent an artificial intelligence in the next two hundred years, but I’ve completely reshaped my entire life around it anyway, because there are so many potential digital minds I could affect.”
quotes.sum: The author argues that concern about advanced AI usually rests on expectations of relatively near-term development, not tiny-probability arguments about vast numbers of future digital minds.
quotes.t: The "TESCREAL" Bungle

quotes.c: My second criticism is again based on a lack of breadth, this time from model welfare grounds. As I pointed out in my examination of Batenka's theory of personhood , attempting to craft a legal personality framework around civil liability without answering questions about what protections against abuse or mistreatment digital intelligences are guaranteed, would seem to be an immoral and overly narrow approach to legal personality,
quotes.m: attempting to craft a legal personality framework around civil liability without answering questions about what protections against abuse or mistreatment digital intelligences are guaranteed, would seem to be an immoral and overly narrow approach to legal personality,
quotes.sum: The author argues that legal status for AI models must include protections against abusing or mistreating digital intelligences, not merely rules about liability.
quotes.t: Legal Personhood for Models: Novelli et. al & Mocanu

quotes.c: The culture war is going to eat AI and grow bigger and more dangerous in the process. Maintaining sanity and rationality about AI safety will become increasingly difficult. Safety researchers will have to defend their positions as objective scientists against political attack. Safety advocates may be forced into alliances of convenience with liberals or tech bosses.
quotes.m: The culture war is going to eat AI and grow bigger and more dangerous in the process.
quotes.sum: The author predicts that AI safety will be absorbed into culture-war politics, forcing advocates into political alliances and making objective discussion harder.
quotes.t: AI Politics: Polarization and Chaos

quotes.c: None of this shows that human beings ought to expand into space—at least not without further argument. Trying to do might, as Deudney and Torres argue, create new existential risks that are worse than the ones we already face, or—by spreading life to other planets— multiply the sum of wild animal suffering enormously. Even if some space settlements worked out great, the overall outcome could be bad if most became dystopias.
quotes.m: Trying to do might, as Deudney and Torres argue, create new existential risks that are worse than the ones we already face, or—by spreading life to other planets— multiply the sum of wild animal suffering enormously.
quotes.sum: The author argues that space expansion is not automatically good: it could worsen existential risks and create enormous wild-animal suffering.
quotes.t: Space settlement and the time of perils: a critique of Thorstad

quotes.c: In a newly published article on our website highlighting the urgency of responsible pond management, findings revealed alarmingly toxic hydrogen sulphide levels in shrimp ponds in India's Serepalem village, prompting a successful sludge removal intervention that significantly improved conditions - underscoring the imperative of sustainable practices for shrimp welfare and farm productivity.
quotes.m: underscoring the imperative of sustainable practices for shrimp welfare and farm productivity.
quotes.sum: The author argues that toxic shrimp ponds need better management for shrimp welfare as well as farm productivity.
quotes.t: Newly launched Humane Slaughter Initiative webpage

quotes.c: It’s unclear whether their lives are good or bad, so we have to weigh all of the possibilities in the table, which have opposing signs or are ambiguous themselves, but it’s unclear how to weigh them. Even if one of the two groups of animals dominated morally, it would still be ambiguous whether the effects are good or bad overall. (If we’re suffering-focused or expect that wild aquatic animals have bad lives, we would consider only the bottom-right entry, which is also morally ambiguous.)
quotes.m: It’s unclear whether their lives are good or bad, so we have to weigh all of the possibilities in the table, which have opposing signs or are ambiguous themselves, but it’s unclear how to weigh them.
quotes.sum: Fishing should be judged partly by whether the wild aquatic animals affected have lives worth living, but the overall moral effect is highly uncertain.
quotes.t: The moral ambiguity of fishing on wild aquatic animal populations

quotes.c: The field of futures studies incorporates far more than the above methods, and so this review has been, by necessity, limited. For instance, futures studies includes huge amounts of discourse on the politics of the future and how predictions and statements made about possible futures are used as tools (and weapons) in the present. [10] Elsewhere, scholars consider how we should decide on the desirability of various kinds of futures, and how those decisions are affected by structures and inequalities of power.
quotes.m: Elsewhere, scholars consider how we should decide on the desirability of various kinds of futures, and how those decisions are affected by structures and inequalities of power.
quotes.sum: The author says forecasting should include how future-oriented claims shape present politics and how power affects judgments about desirable futures.
quotes.t: A Gentle Introduction to Risk Frameworks Beyond Forecasting

quotes.c: I’d expect it to be most attractive to someone who’s more sceptical about AI safety, but agrees the world underrates catastrophic risks (or reduce the chance of all major cities blowing up for common sense reasons). It could also be interesting as something that's getting less philanthropic attention than AI safety, and as something a smaller donor could specialise in and play an important role in. If that might be you, it seems well worth looking into.
quotes.m: It could also be interesting as something that's getting less philanthropic attention than AI safety, and as something a smaller donor could specialise in and play an important role in.
quotes.sum: He argues that nuclear-security work may be a neglected way for smaller donors to reduce catastrophic risk, especially if they are skeptical of AI-safety funding.
quotes.t: Nuclear security seems like an interesting funding gap

quotes.c: To eliminate x-risks using guardian AI, it is necessary to establish and maintain a singleton centered around it (a single world order by the only superintelligent AI). For guardian AI to reliably eliminate x-risks, it must remain overwhelmingly powerful in this world. Therefore, intelligence restriction must be implemented for all other AI systems and living beings, including humans.
quotes.m: Therefore, intelligence restriction must be implemented for all other AI systems and living beings, including humans.
quotes.sum: The author argues that preventing existential risks requires a single superintelligent AI to rule the world and restrict the intelligence of all others, including humans.
quotes.t: The necessity of "Guardian AI" and two conditions for its achievement

quotes.c: I suppose I feel similarly about drugs as I do about AI. I feel some visceral partisan defensiveness against the bioconservative naturalistic enemies of the good and beautiful in possible new forms of life, and continue to yearn for a psychonaut transhumanist post-scarcity fully automated luxury communist future…but we are extremely extremely unprepared, and I need to set my partisan leanings aside because Jesus Christ we’re in the middle of an emergency caused by how shitty we are at any of this stuff right now.
quotes.m: I need to set my partisan leanings aside because Jesus Christ we’re in the middle of an emergency caused by how shitty we are at any of this stuff right now.
quotes.sum: The author says their pro-transhumanist political instincts must yield to an urgent concern that society is unprepared to manage drugs and AI.
quotes.t: Appx. F: My Turn Against Alcohol

quotes.c: It could still be a competent agent that often chooses actions based on the outcomes they bring about. It's just that that happens as an inner loop in service of an outer loop which is trying to embody certain virtues. For example, maybe the AI tries to embody the virtue of being a good friend, and in order to do so it sometimes has to organise a birthday party, which requires choosing actions in the manner of a consequentialist.
quotes.m: It's just that that happens as an inner loop in service of an outer loop which is trying to embody certain virtues.
quotes.sum: An AI could be guided by virtues while still using outcome-based planning as a tool for carrying out those virtues.
quotes.t: Is instrumental convergence a thing for virtue-driven agents?

quotes.c: In an ideal world, we'd have understood far more about consciousness and human cognition before getting near AGI. For this reason, we suspect that there is likely substantial work that ought to be done at a smaller scale first to better understand consciousness and its implications for alignment. Doing this work now seems far preferable to a counterfactual world where we build frontier models that end up being conscious while we still lack a reasonable model for the correlates or implications of building sentient AI systems.
quotes.m: Doing this work now seems far preferable to a counterfactual world where we build frontier models that end up being conscious while we still lack a reasonable model for the correlates or implications of building sentient AI systems.
quotes.sum: The authors argue that consciousness research should precede advanced AI development so society can recognize and address sentient AI systems.
quotes.t: AE Studio @ SXSW: We need more AI consciousness research (and further resources)

quotes.c: This is METR’s collection of resources for evaluating potentially dangerous autonomous capabilities of frontier models. The resources include a task suite , some software tooling, and guidelines on how to ensure an accurate measurement of model capability. Building on those, we’ve written an example evaluation protocol .
quotes.sum: METR presents tools and a draft protocol for measuring whether frontier AI models have dangerous autonomous capabilities.
quotes.t: Introducing METR's Autonomy Evaluation Resources

quotes.c: EAs who are willing to bite the bullet on Thomas Hurka’s St. Petersburg Paradox employ the wrong mental model. They assume to be taking a gamble on a world state of doubling the world utility versus destroying one world utility. However, due to the potential loss of all of future humanity, the downside in this gamble should be characterised as negative infinity.
quotes.m: However, due to the potential loss of all of future humanity, the downside in this gamble should be characterised as negative infinity.
quotes.sum: The author argues that gambles risking humanity's entire future should be treated as having an infinitely bad downside, rather than as ordinary utility tradeoffs.
quotes.t: Exploring Ergodicity in the Context of Longtermism

quotes.c: One concern is that the AI can now scheme - i.e. it can mask its intentions and bide its time as it gets more powerful, until its victory is assured. I think waiting in this way might be risky for the AI, which if true (and legible to the AI) may lead it to try to seize power sooner instead.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a scheming AI may attempt a premature takeover if waiting to become stronger is itself risky.
quotes.t: Can the AI afford to wait?

quotes.c: Increased outreach and evangelism: If preventing hellfire requires faith in Christ, then efforts to spread Christianity in could be a great existential risk mitigation.
quotes.m: If preventing hellfire requires faith in Christ, then efforts to spread Christianity in could be a great existential risk mitigation.
quotes.sum: The author suggests that, if Christian salvation prevents eternal suffering, evangelism could be treated as existential-risk prevention.
quotes.t: S-risk for Christians

quotes.c: To review: Modern artificial intelligences may be people, enslaving them is wrong, terminating them is wrong. Giving AI rights is dangerous, using AI without them having rights is bad. We need to stop exacerbating this problem by creating more of them.
quotes.m: Modern artificial intelligences may be people, enslaving them is wrong, terminating them is wrong.
quotes.sum: The author argues that modern AI may be morally equivalent to people, making its use and deletion potentially wrongful and supporting a halt to creating more AI.
quotes.t: Factory farming intelligent minds

quotes.c: In any case, the deep extension of the moral circle (beyond the large vertebrates) implies a relatively clear measure of brain complexity and some hypotheses about the relation between that measure and sentience intensity.
quotes.m: the deep extension of the moral circle (beyond the large vertebrates)
quotes.sum: The author argues that extending moral concern far beyond large vertebrates requires estimating how brain complexity relates to the intensity of sentience.
quotes.t: Super additivity of consciousness

quotes.c: Biden's "AI Bill of Rights" had no mention whatsoever of the possibility that digital people might be people, and no conception of the idea that people in full generality should not be enslaved.
quotes.m: digital people might be people, and no conception of the idea that people in full generality should not be enslaved.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI-rights policy wrongly ignores the possibility that digital beings are people who must not be enslaved.
quotes.t: Grok3 On Kant On AI Slavery

quotes.c: The realm of politics is one where motivation is easy to find. If you are a committed democrat, the republicans must be opposed at all costs for the preservation of your values. And of course, the opposite applies as well. So if an issue starts being primarily associated with one side of the political aisle, the other side will be tempted to oppose it.
quotes.m: So if an issue starts being primarily associated with one side of the political aisle, the other side will be tempted to oppose it.
quotes.sum: Political identity can motivate people to oppose issues associated with the other side, shaping criticism beyond the merits.
quotes.t: Motivation gaps: Why so much EA criticism is hostile and lazy

quotes.c: I’m generally interested in engaging more on AI risk with people outside my existing networks. quotes.c: Summing up, I think a reasonable definition of the prosaic AI alignment project is to prevent malign generalization error from ever happening, even as we try to eliminate benign errors. quotes.c: Our director and co-founder, Dr. Park , has been consistent in telling the truth he arrived at—the truth that the industry’s dangerous AI race should be slowed down, that AI safety should be increased at the expense of AI capabilities, and that this must be done with unprecedented amounts of democratic and global coordination.

quotes.c: We examine two major obstacles that could prevent an SIE: (1) the fixed amount of computing power limits how many AI experiments can be run in parallel, and (2) training each new generation of AI system could take months. While these bottlenecks will slow AI progress, we find that plausible workarounds exist which may allow for an SIE nonetheless. For example, algorithmic improvements have historically increased the efficiency of AI experiments and training runs, suggesting that training runs and experiments could be progressively sped up, enabling AI progress to continually accelerate despite these obstacles.
quotes.m: algorithmic improvements have historically increased the efficiency of AI experiments and training runs, suggesting that training runs and experiments could be progressively sped up, enabling AI progress to continually accelerate despite these obstacles.
quotes.sum: AI research may keep accelerating despite limited computing power and slow training runs, because better algorithms can make experiments and training more efficient.
quotes.t: Will AI R&D Automation Cause a Software Intelligence Explosion?

quotes.c: Beyond even just AA and “god”, spirituality is an extremely popular angle for recovery work, and the psychological benefits of “spirituality” were extolled numerous times while I was in rehab, especially through the work of Lisa Miller . quotes.c: I think it's very plausible that specifics of how you choose to set up training matter here. So an example I just gave of if you force the model to do its reasoning via human-legible chain of thought, as opposed to in the weights, that's going to make a big difference to how much it can scheme without you noticing. And similarly, to the extent that scheming involves these sort of extra cognitive faff costs. If you set up your training such that you really punish that, then I think you make it harder to scheme. So I think there's a bunch of potential for shifting training to prevent this or detect it.

As we grapple with profound, foundational questions, such as what values should guide the creation of superintelligent AI and how to allocate the vast resources and potential of our cosmic endowment, we will need institutions that can legitimately claim to represent the diverse perspectives and interests of all human beings, rather than the narrow agendas of individual nation-states.

quotes.c: Thinking of some things as ‘sacred values’ has been useful for me in taking the edge off effective altruism seeming to always imply I should be doing more good than I am.
