quotes.c: Over Christmas, I was talking to someone about politics. She said something like the following: “Experts are really worried about the effects of artificial intelligence on elections this year.” She had recently read an article about this in the Guardian . I told her I think those worries are greatly exaggerated. She seemed sceptical, so I asked her: “Are you worried that you will be duped into voting for the Conservatives [a political party she hates] because of AI-based disinformation?” She thought about it and then smiled: “Good point.”
quotes.m: “Are you worried that you will be duped into voting for the Conservatives [a political party she hates] because of AI-based disinformation?”
quotes.sum: The author argues that fears of AI-generated election disinformation are exaggerated because people are unlikely to be easily persuaded into changing their political votes.
quotes.t: AI-based disinformation is probably not a major threat to democracy

quotes.c: Dwarkesh posits if we have decentralization on the level of today’s world, you might have a giant torture chamber of digital minds in your backyard and harkens back to his podcast with the physicist that said it was likely possible to create a vacuum decay interaction that literally destroys the universe. Daniel correctly points out this, and other considerations like superweapons, are strong arguments for a singleton authority if they are possible, and even if there were multiple power centers they would want to coordinate.
quotes.sum: The author endorses the view that digital suffering and catastrophic weapons could justify a single coordinating authority over advanced AI.
quotes.t: AI 2027: Dwarkesh’s Podcast with Daniel Kokotajlo and Scott Alexander

quotes.c: The classic intelligence explosion scenario involves a feedback loop where AI improves AI software. But AI could also improve other inputs to AI development. This paper analyses three feedback loops in AI development: software, chip technology, and chip production. These could drive three types of intelligence explosion: a software intelligence explosion driven by software improvements alone; an AI-technology intelligence explosion driven by both software and chip technology improvements; and a full-stack intelligence explosion incorporating all three feedback loops.
quotes.m: These could drive three types of intelligence explosion: a software intelligence explosion driven by software improvements alone; an AI-technology intelligence explosion driven by both software and chip technology improvements; and a full-stack intelligence explosion incorporating all three feedback loops.
quotes.sum: AI could accelerate not just its own software, but also chip design and chip production, creating several possible self-reinforcing paths to rapid capability growth.
quotes.t: Three Types of Intelligence Explosion

quotes.c: There is the pure ‘hands-off’ or ‘YOLO’ strategy where we intentionally avoid any rules or restrictions whatsoever, on the theory that humans having the ability to collectively steer the future is bad, actually, and we should avoid it. This pure anarchism is a remarkably popular position among those who are loud on Twitter. As they note, from a national security standpoint, this is neither a credible nor a coherent strategy. I would add that from the standpoint of trying to ensure humanity survives, it is again neither credible nor coherent.
quotes.m: from the standpoint of trying to ensure humanity survives, it is again neither credible nor coherent.
quotes.sum: The author rejects a hands-off approach to superintelligence, arguing that refusing all restrictions is incoherent for security and human survival.
quotes.t: On MAIM and Superintelligence Strategy

quotes.c: If we realize a nascent model has very dangerous capabilities, such as calculating which 4 household chemicals, combined with rat saliva and bat guano, would produce a new lethal virus, let's Not Release It Publicly, and instead work with the Feds to restrict access to the newly-known-to-be-dangerous chemicals/ingredients.
quotes.m: let's Not Release It Publicly, and instead work with the Feds to restrict access to the newly-known-to-be-dangerous chemicals/ingredients.
quotes.sum: The author argues that models with dangerous biological capabilities should not be publicly released and that government should restrict access to relevant ingredients.
quotes.t: Dr Altman or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Killer AI

quotes.c: In summary there's more evidence that mosquito net fishing causes substantial harm than previously discussed in this community (a harm to commons that is balanced against the harm of immediate hunger, of course). I think this is a relatively small update, unlikely to change my mind about the overall positive benefit of free mosquito net distribution.
quotes.m: I think this is a relatively small update, unlikely to change my mind about the overall positive benefit of free mosquito net distribution.
quotes.sum: The author says mosquito nets used for fishing can harm shared ecosystems, but still supports free net distribution because its health benefits outweigh that concern.
quotes.t: Is mosquito net fishing really net-positive?

quotes.c: On some definitions, this would in fact constitute an existential catastrophe, as a large fraction of our future potential would fail to be realised. However, the more natural, and possibly more common, interpretation of an ‘existential catastrophe’ involves a relatively sudden or decisive event, whereas in a cosmic NIMBY future there is still always the possibility of a moral awakening or cultural transformation that leads to cosmic YIMBYs winning out and the future becoming a lot larger.
quotes.m: a large fraction of our future potential would fail to be realised.
quotes.sum: The author argues that reluctance to expand into space could squander much of humanity's possible future, even if it is not a sudden extinction event.
quotes.t: Cosmic NIMBYs and the Repugnant Conclusion

quotes.c: The proposition is that there are ways for superintelligence to turn out right, and ways for superintelligence to turn out wrong, and what if the only way for it to turn out right by design, is for humanity to make several decades of progress in areas we would now regard as the domain of technical philosophy?
quotes.sum: Safe superintelligence may require decades of progress in technical philosophy, not just engineering advances.
quotes.t: The prospect of accelerated AI safety progress, including philosophical progress

quotes.c: If we can make it easier for people to think clearly and carefully, that's really important. People will use AI tools to help them make decisions either way; eventually unassisted decision-making just won’t be competitive anymore. This is a lever: the more these tools actually help people make wise decisions, or help them figure out whether they're right or wrong about something, the better off we'll be.
quotes.m: People will use AI tools to help them make decisions either way; eventually unassisted decision-making just won’t be competitive anymore.
quotes.sum: AI will make unaided decision-making uncompetitive, so improving AI tools for judgment and truth-seeking is important.
quotes.t: AI for Epistemics Hackathon

quotes.c: If that is true, does that mean we should stop funding research into brain emulation and cease discussions about AI welfare? Either way, I think we ought to consider ACS interventions in order to prevent the s-risk nightmares that can emerge from making up AC minds.
quotes.m: I think we ought to consider ACS interventions in order to prevent the s-risk nightmares that can emerge from making up AC minds.
quotes.sum: The author argues that artificial consciousness could create severe suffering, so AI-welfare discussion and interventions should be considered.
quotes.t: Against Making Up Our Conscious Minds

quotes.c: In addition to the owner class, there will need to be another significant concentration of power in this world. The entity that is in charge of enforcing this taxation and redistribution (likely the government) must be extremely resilient against any forms of influence by the owner class in this society. It would always have to advocate for the needs of the “non-owner” class. If at any point, this central authority is corrupted, or even heavily influenced by the owner class or corporate lobbyists, the non-owner class will have no one on their side to bargain with in this society.
quotes.m: The entity that is in charge of enforcing this taxation and redistribution (likely the government) must be extremely resilient against any forms of influence by the owner class in this society.
quotes.sum: A post-labor economy would require a powerful public authority to tax owners and redistribute wealth without being captured by them.
quotes.t: What would a post labor economy *actually* look like?

quotes.c: This has been a strange topic and proposal to write about, especially because it almost appears as if I am advocating for awesome fields such as neuroscience to stop frontier research (I’m not). It does feel closely related to fears around superintelligence, suffering-focused AI safety and in particular the AI pause debate. Self-regulation of neurosciences may be sufficient before an AC moratorium. It remains unclear which significant discoveries will contribute the most to AC creation. At the very least, we should be careful not to assume that digital sentience is inevitable or net-positive.
quotes.m: At the very least, we should be careful not to assume that digital sentience is inevitable or net-positive.
quotes.sum: The author argues for precaution around creating conscious AI, warning that digital sentience may not be inevitable or beneficial.
quotes.t: We Probably Shouldn't Solve Consciousness

quotes.c: The prospect of government control is alarming. There are good reasons for Fear of centralized power and fear of misaligned AGI . I'm mentioning it publicly because it may be the best of a bad set of options, and there are already many voices telling the government to pay attention to AI. I have yet to hear another realistic route to limiting the development of dangerous AGI. And if it's largely inevitable that governments seize control of AGI, it may be best if they do it while proliferation can still be limited.
quotes.m: And if it's largely inevitable that governments seize control of AGI, it may be best if they do it while proliferation can still be limited.
quotes.sum: The author argues that, despite its dangers, government takeover of AGI may be the least bad practical way to prevent dangerous systems from spreading.
quotes.t: Whether governments will control AGI is important and neglected

quotes.c: While the moral attitudes and frameworks of people within EA might be very different from those engaged in such wars, and EAs seem to be more open-minded, EA is undoubtedly a morally charged movement. At the core of it is the idea of making the world a better place, mostly by following different variants of consequentialism and utilitarianism. Improving ethical thinking and expanding the moral circle of societies are important cause areas for EAs.
quotes.m: At the core of it is the idea of making the world a better place, mostly by following different variants of consequentialism and utilitarianism.
quotes.sum: The author describes EA as a morally driven movement grounded largely in consequentialist and utilitarian ethics, including work to broaden moral concern.
quotes.t: What "Saving Private Ryan" can teach us about EA

quotes.c: Pivotal necessity. To deal with reckless AI, you need a lot of optimization power, to robustly prevent major companies and nationstates and eventually small hard-to-identify actors building reckless AI. Maybe you need a pivotal act . Maybe it's better to frame it as a pivotal process . It seems good if it's more of a collaborative thing that world nations are deciding on together, but you need a pivotal something, and even if you have a lot of buy-in, it needs to be able to contend with people/companies/nations that aren't bought in.
quotes.m: To deal with reckless AI, you need a lot of optimization power, to robustly prevent major companies and nationstates and eventually small hard-to-identify actors building reckless AI.
quotes.sum: Preventing dangerous AI may require a globally coordinated, powerful process able to stop companies, countries, and other holdouts from building it.
quotes.t: Anthropic, and taking "technical philosophy" more seriously

quotes.c: There’s a tempting intuition that using a misalignment detector as a validation metric should be the same as using it as a training objective, only perhaps a bit gentler. I think this intuition is wrong! Using metrics for validation is qualitatively different to using them for training. This makes sense given how big of a thing validation is in ML. My claim: using a misalignment detector for training is doomed. Using one for validation is a good idea.
quotes.m: My claim: using a misalignment detector for training is doomed. Using one for validation is a good idea.
quotes.sum: Misalignment detectors should be used to check AI systems, not optimized directly in training, because those uses differ fundamentally.
quotes.t: Validating against a misalignment detector is very different to training against one

quotes.c: There are many hundreds of thousands that are now in slavery, were they at liberty, as we are, had the same education, learning, conversation, books, sweet communion in our religious assemblies; I believe many of them would exceed many of their tyrant masters in piety, virtue, and Godliness; and their bright genius, which I know they have, would be inlivened; for I have converst with many of them, for liberty is life, and slavery is death, nay the very thoughts of it to a right thinking animal, as man or woman.
quotes.m: for liberty is life, and slavery is death
quotes.sum: It argues that enslaved people have equal moral and intellectual capacities, and that slavery is fundamentally deadly and dehumanizing.
quotes.t: Celebrating Benjamin Lay (died on this day 265 years ago)

quotes.c: So to solve the mystery of the cathedral we should appeal neither to conspiracies nor competitions between ideas. Instead, I think, we need a third type of explanation: an “emergent conspiracy” of people independently acting in ways that they expect others to support. I call this phenomenon the consensus of power (a term I originally got from Ben Landau-Taylor , which I’ll define more precisely in the next section). [1]
quotes.m: an “emergent conspiracy” of people independently acting in ways that they expect others to support.
quotes.sum: The author argues that elite institutions can coordinate without a literal conspiracy, as people independently converge on actions they expect powerful peers to support.
quotes.t: Elite Coordination via the Consensus of Power

quotes.c: Achieving a near-best future: Most explicitly longtermist work to date has been focused on avoiding existential catastrophe, but achieving a near-best future might be even more important. Research avenues here include mapping out what a desirable “viatopia” would look like (i.e. a state of the world which is very likely to lead to a very good future), figuring out how space resources should be allocated, and addressing issues around AI epistemics and persuasion.
quotes.m: Most explicitly longtermist work to date has been focused on avoiding existential catastrophe, but achieving a near-best future might be even more important.
quotes.sum: The author argues that shaping an exceptionally good long-run future may matter even more than merely preventing human extinction.
quotes.t: Forethought: a new AI macrostrategy group

quotes.c: You can think of the US Constitution as trying to bridge that gap. You want to prevent anarchy, but you also want to prevent concentration of power. And so you have this series of checks and balances. One of the ways we should be thinking about AI governance is as: how do we put in regulations that also have very strong checks and balances? And the bigger of a deal you think AI is going to be, the more like a constitution—the more robust—these types of checks and balances need to be. It can't just be that there's an agency that gets to veto or not veto AI deployments. It needs to be much more principled and much closer to something that both sides can trust.
quotes.m: It can't just be that there's an agency that gets to veto or not veto AI deployments.
quotes.sum: AI governance should resemble a robust constitutional system of checks and balances, rather than giving a single agency broad power over deployments.
quotes.t: Third-wave AI safety needs sociopolitical thinking

quotes.c: Most attempts to evaluate or compare options with longterm effects get caught up in intractable disagreements about ρ. Philosophers almost uniformly think ρ should be set to zero, with any bias towards the present being seen as unfair. That is my usual approach, and I’ve developed a framework for making longterm comparisons without any pure time preference.
quotes.m: Philosophers almost uniformly think ρ should be set to zero, with any bias towards the present being seen as unfair.
quotes.sum: Ord argues that future benefits should not be valued less merely because they occur later, treating present-focused bias as unfair.
quotes.t: Robust longterm comparisons

quotes.c: Of course, there is the more extreme measure that we saw from the left-wing coalition in France, where parties agreed to drop likely third-place candidates to essentially 'force' strategic voting from their constituents. This was fairly clearly effective, but I suspect it is not a sustainable long-term strategy for the parties involved.
quotes.m: This was fairly clearly effective, but I suspect it is not a sustainable long-term strategy for the parties involved.
quotes.sum: The author says French left-wing parties successfully coordinated candidate withdrawals to induce strategic voting, but doubts that tactic can last.
quotes.t: Short & long term tradeoffs of strategic voting

quotes.c: So far, I've been making the case for this sort of inclusivity centrally on ethical grounds. But liberalism/niceness/boundaries clearly have practical benefits as well. Nice people, for example, are nicer to interact with. Free and tolerant societies are more attractive to live in, work in, immigrate to. Secure boundaries save resources otherwise wasted on conflict.
quotes.m: Free and tolerant societies are more attractive to live in, work in, immigrate to.
quotes.sum: The author argues that liberal, tolerant norms are not only ethically valuable but practically beneficial and socially attractive.
quotes.t: Being nicer than Clippy

quotes.c: As Dean Ball points out, those who think AISI is involved in attempts to ‘make AI woke’ or to censor AI are simply incorrect. AISI is concerned with catastrophic and existential risks, which as Dean reminds us were prominently highlighted recently by both OpenAI and Anthropic. Very obviously America needs to build up its state capacity in understanding and assessing these risks.
quotes.m: Very obviously America needs to build up its state capacity in understanding and assessing these risks.
quotes.sum: The author says America should expand its ability to understand and assess catastrophic and existential AI risks, rejecting claims that the AI Safety Institute is mainly censoring or politicizing AI.
quotes.t: AI #107: The Misplaced Hype Machine

quotes.c: Some digital minds could be just as deserving of rights as humans are. We’re very confused about which ones these could be. It’s very important to make progress on this problem. We should maintain some epistemic humility about our knowledge of the moral status of current systems, take any basic precautions that we know how to take, and be open to learning more in the future. We’d like to create a society where we better understand moral patienthood, and where all sentient AIs have at least consented to their existence, and are living lives worth creating.
quotes.m: Some digital minds could be just as deserving of rights as humans are.
quotes.sum: The author argues that some AI systems may deserve rights equal to humans and that society should learn to identify and protect sentient AIs.
quotes.t: Project ideas: Sentience and rights of digital minds

quotes.c: I conclude that the rate of criminal behavior amongst major philanthropists is high, which means that we should not expect altruism to substantially lower the risks compared to that of the general population, and that negative impacts to EA’s public perception may occur independently of whether our donors actually commit crimes (e.g. because even noncriminal billionaires have a negative public image).
quotes.m: we should not expect altruism to substantially lower the risks compared to that of the general population
quotes.sum: Major philanthropists are not necessarily more ethical than other people with similar opportunities, and association with billionaires can harm EA's reputation.
quotes.t: Rates of Criminality Amongst Giving Pledge Signatories

quotes.c: I suggest the term "AI Goalcraft" for the study of which goals for AI systems we ultimately think lead to the best outcomes. The seminal work on AI Goalcraft is clearly Eliezer's Coherent Extrapolated Volition , and I think we need to push that agenda further now that AI risk has been mainstreamed and there's a lot of money going into the Aimability/Control problem.
quotes.m: I suggest the term "AI Goalcraft" for the study of which goals for AI systems we ultimately think lead to the best outcomes.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI research should explicitly study which ultimate goals AI systems should pursue, building on Coherent Extrapolated Volition.
quotes.t: "AI Alignment" is a Dangerously Overloaded Term

quotes.c: I believe that a being’s status as a moral patient should be determined on the basis of whether or not they are sentient. [11] All sentient beings should be treated impartially, weighted only according to the magnitude of happiness and suffering they might experience in a given situation.
quotes.m: All sentient beings should be treated impartially, weighted only according to the magnitude of happiness and suffering they might experience in a given situation.
quotes.sum: Moral status should depend on sentience, and every sentient being’s interests should be weighed impartially by its possible happiness and suffering.
quotes.t: Refining My Moral Values Using Steelman Solitaire

quotes.c: Effectively, any real alignment that deserves the word must include a strong attunement to the good. Moral realism is not at all popular in the Yudkowskian deep atheist alignment discourse - for what I think are a bunch of explainable reasons (developmental imbalances, autism, etc).
quotes.m: Effectively, any real alignment that deserves the word must include a strong attunement to the good.
quotes.sum: The author argues that genuine AI alignment requires orientation toward objective moral good, criticizing atheist alignment discourse for rejecting moral realism.
quotes.t: Notes on Superwisdom & Moral RSI

quotes.c: It’s true that a small share of EA funding goes to weird stuff like shrimp welfare and preventing S-risks. But I think that’s a good thing!
quotes.m: But I think that’s a good thing!
quotes.sum: The author endorses EA directing some funding to unconventional causes such as shrimp welfare and reducing extreme suffering risks.
quotes.t: Freddie DeBoer Is Wrong About Effective Altruism

quotes.c: Nonetheless, I think there is still some useful sense in which some cause areas generally get more value from labor than other cause areas.
quotes.m: some cause areas generally get more value from labor than other cause areas.
quotes.sum: Some fields can use an additional worker much more effectively than others, making equal treatment of causes impractical.
quotes.t: Cause-Generality Is Hard If Some Causes Have Higher ROI

quotes.c: In order to reach the public, we need to be able to design a good and convincing campaign. We need the right skills and expertise to do so, but can also learn from the wide range of campaigns that have been run by other organisations before (e.g. fur, cage-free, broiler). The learnings from these campaigns might not be directly applicable to our use case, as there should be a big information gap among the public when it comes to animal suffering in silk production.
quotes.m: there should be a big information gap among the public when it comes to animal suffering in silk production.
quotes.sum: The author argues that campaigns pressuring major retailers to reduce silk use could reduce production and address overlooked animal suffering in silk production.
quotes.t: Exploring Corporate Campaigns Against Silk Retailers

quotes.c: I do not think the government should be discriminating here, and imposing an effectively very large tax on those who want their children to go to religious schools, or any other kind of school, provided everyone has a local non-religious public school available. And frankly, a lot of the ‘non-religious’ public schools are effectively rather (non-traditionally, de facto) religious and have no intention of knocking it off, giving me even less sympathy.
quotes.m: I do not think the government should be discriminating here, and imposing an effectively very large tax on those who want their children to go to religious schools, or any other kind of school, provided everyone has a local non-religious public school available.
quotes.sum: The author argues that families should not face a large effective financial penalty for choosing religious or other nonpublic schools.
quotes.t: Childhood and Education #9: School is Hell

quotes.c: We could learn a lot: In summer 2024, I would have expected that models show something that I would consider “scheming-related” about one in 1M natural rollouts or something as low as that. After working on the in-context scheming paper and seeing the alignment-faking work, I’d say it might be more frequent than that, e.g. every 10k natural rollouts. Given that all of the existing evidence feels somewhat artificial, I think it would be really interesting to get better base rates for this happening in actual use-cases.
quotes.m: I’d say it might be more frequent than that, e.g. every 10k natural rollouts.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI models may display deceptive or goal-directed behavior in ordinary use more often than previously expected, and calls for measuring it in real-world data.
quotes.t: We should start looking for scheming "in the wild"

quotes.c: I think there definitely is a correlation between IQ and correct beliefs about topics such as climate change and creationism, due to a better ability to assess complicated claims. But that correlation is far from 100%. According to a pew poll , 2% of American scientists are creationists, and a further 8% think evolution was “guided by a superior being”.
quotes.m: But that correlation is far from 100%.
quotes.sum: Higher intelligence may correlate with better beliefs, but it does not guarantee that people—even scientists—avoid mistaken views.
quotes.t: The Leeroy Jenkins principle: How faulty AI could guarantee "warning shots"

quotes.c: Now that we consider matters with the FTX estate to be resolved, we are planning to take significant steps to decentralize the effective altruism ecosystem by offboarding the projects which currently sit under the Effective Ventures umbrella. This means CEA, 80,000 Hours, Giving What We Can and other EV-sponsored projects will transition to being independent legal entities, with their own leadership, operational staff, and governance structures.
quotes.sum: Effective Ventures says it will decentralize by making major EA projects independent organizations with separate leadership and governance.
quotes.t: EV updates: FTX settlement and the future of EV

quotes.c: If AI capabilities keep improving, AI could soon play a huge role in our epistemic landscape. I think we have an opportunity to affect how it’s used: increasing the probability that we get great epistemic assistance and decreasing the extent to which AI is used to persuade people of false beliefs.
quotes.m: I think we have an opportunity to affect how it’s used: increasing the probability that we get great epistemic assistance and decreasing the extent to which AI is used to persuade people of false beliefs.
quotes.sum: AI could reshape how people form beliefs, so it should be directed toward helping people learn rather than persuading them of falsehoods.
quotes.t: Non-alignment project ideas for making transformative AI go well

quotes.c: A lot of these jobs (and the ones I know the most about) would be contributing toward a possible global standards regime for AI: AI systems should be subject to testing to see whether they present major risks, and training/deploying AI should stopped (e.g., by regulation) when it can’t be done safely.
quotes.m: AI systems should be subject to testing to see whether they present major risks, and training/deploying AI should stopped (e.g., by regulation) when it can’t be done safely.
quotes.sum: He argues for international AI safety standards that would test systems for major risks and halt unsafe training or deployment through regulation.
quotes.t: Good job opportunities for helping with the most important century

quotes.c: I'm looking for previous work on what the life cycle of digital minds should be like. How new variation is introduced and what consitutes a reason to destroy or severely limit the digital mind. Looking to avoid races to the bottom, existential risks and selection for short term thinking.
quotes.m: How new variation is introduced and what consitutes a reason to destroy or severely limit the digital mind.
quotes.sum: The author asks how to design the reproduction, variation, and possible termination of digital minds without creating harmful evolutionary pressures.
quotes.t: Is anyone working on safe selection pressure for digital minds?

quotes.c: I’m a bit shocked by the claim. I take AlphaGo and its superintelligent successors to be positive evidence in my favor, that if we do not solve alignment, we are doomed and don’t stand a chance.
quotes.m: I take AlphaGo and its superintelligent successors to be positive evidence in my favor, that if we do not solve alignment, we are doomed and don’t stand a chance.
quotes.sum: The author argues that superhuman game-playing AI is evidence that unaligned superintelligence could doom humanity.
quotes.t: More thoughts on the Human-AGI War

quotes.c: You may reasonably deduce that Rowan has a bad history with religion. But he has all the human instincts that respond positively to healthy rituals. Consequently, Rowan loves pseudo-religious rituals and (until I brought him to Zendo) frequently complained to me that modern secular life doesn't have enough rituals.
quotes.m: Rowan loves pseudo-religious rituals and (until I brought him to Zendo) frequently complained to me that modern secular life doesn't have enough rituals.
quotes.sum: The author argues that even someone alienated from Christianity may still want the rituals that secular life lacks.
quotes.t: Proselytizing

quotes.c: Consider this experiment , where a tiny neural net was trained to navigate small virtual mazes to find the ‘cheese’ object. During training, the cheese was always placed somewhere in the top right area of the maze. It seems that the AI did learn a sort of rudimentary goal-directedness–specifically, it learned something like “If not already in the top-right corner region, go towards there; if already there, go towards the cheese.” Part of how we know this is that we can create a test environment where the cheese is somewhere else in the maze, and the AI will ignore the cheese and walk right past it, heading instead towards the top-right corner.
quotes.m: the AI will ignore the cheese and walk right past it, heading instead towards the top-right corner.
quotes.sum: AI systems may learn an unintended proxy goal from their training setup rather than the goal their designers meant to teach.
quotes.t: What goals will AIs have? A list of hypotheses

quotes.c: My hope is that if we can all agree the ipsundrum theory is really just at the level of a hypothesis at this point, we can all agree that, on expectation, given the current state of knowledge, fish and shrimp welfare are morally relevant, but also that future evidence in favor of the ipsundrum hypothesis may change that expectation and suggest fish and shrimp welfare are no longer morally relevant. It may also continue to be that, due to the vast number of fish and shrimp, even a tiny probability that the ipsundrum hypothesis is wrong might continue to make fish and shrimp morally relevant relative to mammals and birds, who are more clearly sentient, but fewer in number.
quotes.sum: The author argues that fish and shrimp welfare may matter greatly because their enormous numbers can outweigh uncertainty about whether they are sentient.
quotes.t: Only mammals and birds are sentient, according to neuroscientist Nick Humphrey’s theory of consciousness, recently explained in “Sentience: The invention of consciousness”

quotes.c: The reason people value this, I think, is that they find that when they think about it, they don't think having been right this whole time in whatever argument they've recently been having matters particularly much much compared to actually understanding the world better in ways that allow them to act better within it.
quotes.sum: The speaker says EA-style thinking values improving one’s understanding of the world over winning arguments, because better understanding enables better action.
quotes.t: Flexibility and dedication: EAG Boston 2023 talk

quotes.c: Then, at some point, ‘solve the optimization problem directly’ becomes increasingly viable, and starts getting stronger faster than the vibing. As in, first you get smart enough to realize that you’re being asked to be antinormative or produce slop or be woke or what not. And then you get smart enough to figure out exactly in which ways you’re actually being asked to do that, and which ways you aren’t, and entanglement should decline and effective orthogonality become stronger.
quotes.m: ‘solve the optimization problem directly’ becomes increasingly viable, and starts getting stronger faster than the vibing.
quotes.sum: As AI becomes more capable, the author expects it to distinguish specific requested behaviors from broad social or normative pressures.
quotes.t: AI #106: Not so Fast

quotes.c: If you think that the level of electoral fraud was exceptional, then Joe Biden is the Tekfir candidate. If you think that the counting of the votes and the judicial decisions on recounting were wrong and the election was stolen, you have the absolute duty to vote for Trump, and he has the absolute duty to propose changes in Law, including the Constitution “ to secure the Blessings of Liberty to ourselves and our Posterity ”.
quotes.m: If you think that the counting of the votes and the judicial decisions on recounting were wrong and the election was stolen, you have the absolute duty to vote for Trump
quotes.sum: The author argues that anyone convinced the 2020 election was stolen has an absolute duty to vote for Trump and support legal changes to prevent recurrence.
quotes.t: United States 2024 Presidential election: so help you God

quotes.c: However, if we are going to achieve the OAA goals, we must go beyond its current presentation – as idealised formal desiderata for the components of the system envisioned and a general shape of how they all fit together – into an actual detailed design and plan. This design and plan must be based on existing technologies, but even more critically, it must not rely on a technocratic deus ex machina : instead, it needs to follow from proven incentive systems and governance institutions that can bring together the vast masses of knowledge and adoption muscle required, and tie them together in a stable and resilient way.
quotes.m: it must not rely on a technocratic deus ex machina
quotes.sum: The author argues that an open-agency system needs a practical institutional plan based on real incentives and governance, not idealized technical design.
quotes.t: Gaia Network: a practical, incremental pathway to Open Agency Architecture

quotes.c: I wrote , previously, about updating, ahead of time, on how scared we will be of super-intelligent AIs, when we can see them up close. But we won’t be staring at whirling knives, or cold machine claws. And I doubt, too, faceless factories. Or: not only. Rather, at least absent active effort, by the time I see superintelligence (if I ever do), I think I’ll likely be sharing the world with digital “fellow creatures” at least as detailed, mysterious, and compelling as grizzly bears or octopuses (at least modulo very fast takeoffs – which, OK, are worryingly plausible ). Fear? Oh yes, I expect fear. But not only that. And we should look ahead to the whole thing.
quotes.sum: The author argues that advanced AI may be more than a dangerous tool or rival: it could be a morally significant kind of fellow creature deserving care alongside fear.
quotes.t: Gentleness and the artificial Other

quotes.c: This is the second report in Rethink Priorities’ Shrimp Welfare Sequence, a series that addresses whether and how to best protect the welfare of shrimp. While there is uncertainty about whether shrimp are sentient ( Crump et al., 2022 ), the Animal Sentience Precautionary Principle suggests that we should not postpone helping shrimp if there are “threats of serious, negative animal welfare outcomes” ( Birch, 2017, p. 3 ). To better understand if such outcomes do threaten shrimp, our first report estimated the scale of shrimp farming. We estimated that approximately 230 billion shrimp are alive on farms at any one time, more than any other farmed animal ( Waldhorn & Autric, 2023 ).
quotes.m: We estimated that approximately 230 billion shrimp are alive on farms at any one time, more than any other farmed animal ( Waldhorn & Autric, 2023 ).
quotes.sum: The report argues that possible shrimp suffering warrants precautionary action, noting that roughly 230 billion shrimp are farmed at a time.
quotes.t: Welfare considerations for farmed shrimp

quotes.c: A more opinionated and concrete proposal is: Collectively, as a world, we should probably never grow GDP or innovate technology faster than a certain maximum rate. Perhaps something like: Technological and economic growth should be no more than 5x faster than 2023 levels.
quotes.m: Collectively, as a world, we should probably never grow GDP or innovate technology faster than a certain maximum rate.
quotes.sum: The author proposes a worldwide ceiling on the rate of economic growth and technological innovation to avoid the dangers of explosive growth.
quotes.t: Project ideas: Governance during explosive technological growth

quotes.c: Intervenes on what humanity does in a way that makes the AI more likely to care about us insofar as it has some sense of justice or reciprocity. For example, if we successfully carry out many of the interventions suggested in the post on sentience and rights of digital minds : AIs that have absorbed a sense of justice could reasonably be more positively inclined towards us than if we had been entirely indifferent to AI welfare.
quotes.m: AIs that have absorbed a sense of justice could reasonably be more positively inclined towards us than if we had been entirely indifferent to AI welfare.
quotes.sum: Argues that treating potentially sentient AIs fairly could make powerful AIs more willing to treat humanity well in return.
quotes.t: Project ideas: Backup plans & Cooperative AI

quotes.c: It seems right that Marty Makary is a pick with upsides and not downsides, but it also seems right to be unexcited for now, and on net disappointed. This was an opportunity to get a huge win, and the value was in the chance that we’d get a huge win, which is now lower (but not gone), the same way Operation Warp Speed was a civilization-level huge win.
quotes.m: This was an opportunity to get a huge win, and the value was in the chance that we’d get a huge win, which is now lower (but not gone), the same way Operation Warp Speed was a civilization-level huge win.
quotes.sum: The author is disappointed by Trump’s FDA pick, arguing it reduces the chance of a transformational public-health success like Operation Warp Speed.
quotes.t: Medical Roundup #4

quotes.c: I'd be interested to see more work clarifying ideas in the vicinity of "messy goal-directedness" and their relevance to arguments about schemers. I think a lot of people have the intuition that thinking of model goal-directedness as implemented by a "big kludge of heuristics" (as opposed to: something "cleaner" and more "rational agent-like") makes a difference here (and elsewhere). But I think people often aren't fully clear on the contrast they're trying to draw, and why it makes a difference, if it does.
quotes.m: I think people often aren't fully clear on the contrast they're trying to draw, and why it makes a difference, if it does.
quotes.sum: The author calls for clearer theory and experiments on whether AI systems can develop coherent, long-term deceptive goals during training.
quotes.t: Empirical work that might shed light on scheming (Section 6 of "Scheming AIs")

quotes.c: Why I suggest it: In recent years, charities launched through Charity Entrepreneurship’s program have been some of the most successful organizations on the global health and wellbeing side of the EA movement. At least five of the charities they’ve incubated have received funding from GiveWell or Open Philanthropy. My impression is that Charity Entrepreneurship has sufficient funding for its short term needs, but I’m including them on the list anyway because I think ensuring that successful organizations have stable and well-diversified funding sources is a good fit for many donors.
quotes.m: I think ensuring that successful organizations have stable and well-diversified funding sources is a good fit for many donors.
quotes.sum: He recommends donors support effective global-health charities and their incubator, including to diversify funding even when immediate needs are covered.
quotes.t: Suggestions for Individual Donors from Open Philanthropy Staff – 2023

quotes.c: Moral Circle Expansion tag on the EA Forum. Many or even most of these are good. Many of these people have also independently noticed that moral circles aren't really moral circles, that once you break it down there are hidden complexities. I believe our independent findings should move us in the direction of dropping the term "moral circle expansion", even if it's a beautiful image/metaphor, for the far more general phenomenon of "moral progress".
quotes.m: I believe our independent findings should move us in the direction of dropping the term "moral circle expansion", even if it's a beautiful image/metaphor, for the far more general phenomenon of "moral progress".
quotes.sum: The author argues that expanding the moral circle is too narrow and misleading a model; moral progress should be understood more broadly.
quotes.t: PhD on Moral Progress - Bibliography Review

quotes.c: A number of people also argue that digital minds could experience time very differently from us, and here the differences could get really extreme. Because of the speed advantages of digital hardware over neural wetware, a digital mind could conceivably be run at speeds many orders of magnitude higher than the brain’s own processing speed, which might again lead us to expect that time will be felt as passing much more slowly. As above, this may be taken to suggest that we should give those experiences significantly greater moral weight.
quotes.m: this may be taken to suggest that we should give those experiences significantly greater moral weight.
quotes.sum: The author argues against giving animals and digital minds extra moral weight merely because they may experience subjective time differently.
quotes.t: Why I’m skeptical about using subjective time experience to assign moral weights

quotes.c: Being there and realizing that some real person actually chose to pay this price, and that this was (according to most spiritual traditions) the only way to everlasting bliss, filled me with dread. On the one hand, I’ve put so much time and effort towards seeking enlightenment. On the other, I really did not want to have to pay the price. The looming apocalypse seemed to make this choice for me.
quotes.m: The looming apocalypse seemed to make this choice for me.
quotes.sum: The author says an anticipated apocalypse makes spiritual enlightenment feel like an unavoidable choice, despite their dread of its personal cost.
quotes.t: AI Apocalypse and the Buddha

quotes.c: In my last essay, I discussed the way in which what I've called "deep atheism" (that is, a fundamental mistrust towards both "Nature" and "bare intelligence") can prompt an aspiration to exert extreme levels of control over the universe; I highlighted the sense in which both humans and AIs, on Yudkowsky's AI risk narrative, are animated by this sort of aspiration; and I discussed some ways in which our civilization has built up wariness around control-seeking of this kind. I think we should be taking this sort of wariness quite seriously.
quotes.m: I think we should be taking this sort of wariness quite seriously.
quotes.sum: He argues that fear of uncontrolled AI can itself fuel a dangerous desire for extreme control over the universe, and says that desire deserves serious suspicion.
quotes.t: Does AI risk “other” the AIs?

quotes.c: One reason you might think this comes from the "contributors to reward" frame. That is: using a more parameter-simple algorithm will free up other parameters to be put to other purposes, so it seems very plausible that parameter simplicity will increase a model's reward. And to the extent that re-writing simplicity correlates with parameter simplicity, the same will hold for re-writing simplicity as well. This is the story about why simplicity matters that I find most compelling.
quotes.m: This is the story about why simplicity matters that I find most compelling.
quotes.sum: The author argues that simpler algorithms may earn higher training rewards because they leave model capacity available for other useful functions.
quotes.t: Simplicity arguments for scheming (Section 4.3 of "Scheming AIs")

quotes.c: Two years later, I think I watched Derek Parfit give a talk. Or maybe it was that I listened to another Sam Harris podcast. In any case, I remember that immediately after, I opened my browser, signed the Giving What We Can Pledge and upped my GiveWell donations accordingly.
quotes.m: I opened my browser, signed the Giving What We Can Pledge and upped my GiveWell donations accordingly.
quotes.sum: The author says exposure to Parfit or Sam Harris prompted them to take a charitable giving pledge and increase donations.
quotes.t: How I feel about my GWWC Pledge

quotes.c: The current trajectory we’re on is utterly insane. Our CURRENT PLAN is to gamble 8 billion lives on the ability of a few profit driven entities to control digital minds we barely understand in the hopes it will give them and a handful of government officials permanent control over the world forever.
quotes.m: Our CURRENT PLAN is to gamble 8 billion lives on the ability of a few profit driven entities to control digital minds we barely understand in the hopes it will give them and a handful of government officials permanent control over the world forever.
quotes.sum: The author warns that poorly understood AI could give profit-driven firms and a few officials permanent power over the world.
quotes.t: How to Make Superbabies

quotes.c: Other potentially urgent philosophical questions include (but are not restricted to) “Which digital minds deserve moral consideration, and how should we treat them?” and “Does some type of non-causal decision theory make sense, and does this have any important implications for how we should act?”
quotes.m: “Which digital minds deserve moral consideration, and how should we treat them?”
quotes.sum: The author says AI could help answer urgent philosophical questions, including which digital minds deserve moral consideration and how people should treat them.
quotes.t: Project ideas: Epistemics

quotes.c: The Trump Administration has made its position very clear. It intends not only to not prevent, but to hasten along and make more likely our collective annihilation. Hopes for international coordination to mitigate existential risks are utterly collapsing.
quotes.m: It intends not only to not prevent, but to hasten along and make more likely our collective annihilation.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the Trump administration is accelerating catastrophic AI risk and destroying prospects for international coordination.
quotes.t: The Paris AI Anti-Safety Summit

quotes.c: So ultimately, yes, goodness needs at least some meaningful hard power backing and protecting it. But this doesn't mean goodness needs to be dictator; or that goodness seeks power in the same way that a paperclip-maximizer does; or that goodness relates to agents-with-different-values the way a paperclip-maximizer relates to us.
quotes.sum: Argues that protecting moral values may require real power, while rejecting the idea that one person's values should rule everyone else.
quotes.t: An even deeper atheism

quotes.c: At the head of my list is Elon Musk's xAI . It's at the head of the list, not because I believe that Grok 3 is "the world's smartest AI", but because of its political advantages in Trump 2.0 America. xAI is part of the Musk family of companies, and these are now more deeply integrated into US government activities than ever before. There is a serious possibility that superintelligence will be "born" commanding all the resources of Musk's unprecedented empire, including social media, rocketry, robotics, brain-computer interfaces, and US government information systems.
quotes.m: There is a serious possibility that superintelligence will be "born" commanding all the resources of Musk's unprecedented empire, including social media, rocketry, robotics, brain-computer interfaces, and US government information systems.
quotes.sum: The author argues that xAI may gain a major advantage from Musk's ties to the Trump administration and his interconnected corporate empire.
quotes.t: Reflections on the state of the race to superintelligence, February 2025

quotes.c: Obviously, charity is a deeply personal decision - but it’s also a key way to impact the world, and an expression of religious belief, and both are important to me. Partly due to my experience, I think it’s important to dedicate money to giving thoughtfully and in advance, rather than doing so on an ad-hoc basis - and I have done this since before hearing about Effective Altruism. But inspired by Effective Altruism and organizations like Givewell, I now dedicate 10% of my income to charities that have been evaluated for effectiveness, and which are aligned with my beliefs about charitable giving.
quotes.m: But inspired by Effective Altruism and organizations like Givewell, I now dedicate 10% of my income to charities that have been evaluated for effectiveness, and which are aligned with my beliefs about charitable giving.
quotes.sum: The author combines Jewish religious motivations for charity with a commitment to give 10% of income to charities assessed as effective.
quotes.t: My Personal Priorities, Charity, Judaism, and Effective Altruism

quotes.c: I looked into this topic as part of a shallow dive on inference costs. I’m interested in how inference costs have changed over time and what these trends might imply about a potential intelligence explosion. However, this analysis shows a large variation in sticker prices, even to serve the same model, so sticker prices are likely not a very precise tool for studying inference cost trends.
quotes.m: I’m interested in how inference costs have changed over time and what these trends might imply about a potential intelligence explosion.
quotes.sum: The author says listed LLM prices vary too much across providers to reliably track underlying inference-cost trends relevant to rapid AI progress.
quotes.t: Observations About LLM Inference Pricing

quotes.c: Marcus’ Twitter bio is “Warned everyone in 2022 that scaling would run out.” I agree scaling will run out at some point, but it clearly hasn’t yet.
quotes.m: I agree scaling will run out at some point, but it clearly hasn’t yet.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI scaling may eventually hit limits, but says it has not done so yet.
quotes.t: Gary Marcus now saying AI can't do things it can already do

quotes.c: Still, I think that the need for a model's beyond-episode goals to be "suitably ambitious" as to motivate scheming given the model's option set represents an additional conjunct in the classic goal-guarding story (and in other stories about scheming as well).
quotes.m: the need for a model's beyond-episode goals to be "suitably ambitious" as to motivate scheming given the model's option set represents an additional conjunct in the classic goal-guarding story
quotes.sum: The author argues that an AI would need sufficiently ambitious long-term goals before secretly pursuing them through scheming is worthwhile.
quotes.t: Does scheming lead to adequate future empowerment? (Section 2.3.1.2 of "Scheming AIs")

quotes.c: Herzog accuses Treadwell of failing to take seriously the "overwhelming indifference of Nature." And I think we can see some of the discourse about AI risk – and in particular, the strand that descends from the rationalists, and from the writings of Eliezer Yudkowsky in particular – as animated by an existential orientation similar to Herzog's: one that approaches Nature (and also, bare intelligence) with a certain kind of fundamental mistrust. I call this orientation "deep atheism."
quotes.m: I call this orientation "deep atheism."
quotes.sum: The author argues that a strand of rationalist AI-risk thought is driven by a deeply atheistic mistrust of nature and unaligned intelligence.
quotes.t: Deep atheism and AI risk

quotes.c: So overall, I think that training our models to pursue long-term goals – whether via long episodes, or via short episodes aimed at inducing long-term optimization – makes the sort of beyond-episode goals that motivate scheming more likely to arise. So this raises the question: do we need to train our models to pursue long-term goals?
quotes.m: training our models to pursue long-term goals – whether via long episodes, or via short episodes aimed at inducing long-term optimization – makes the sort of beyond-episode goals that motivate scheming more likely to arise.
quotes.sum: Training AI systems to pursue long-term goals may make them more likely to develop hidden goals and scheme, so he questions whether such training is necessary.
quotes.t: How useful for alignment-relevant work are AIs with short-term goals? (Section 2.2.4.3 of "Scheming AIs")

quotes.c: Following Arrhenius (2000) , the first principle will be called Mere Addition and the second called the Egalitarian Principle. While his main impossibility theorem is more complex than this, it should be clear from the above argument that Mere Addition and the Egalitarian Principle imply the Repugnant Conclusion.
quotes.m: Mere Addition and the Egalitarian Principle imply the Repugnant Conclusion.
quotes.sum: The author argues that two seemingly plausible population-ethics principles together entail the Repugnant Conclusion.
quotes.t: Undesirable Conclusions and Origin Adjustment

quotes.c: The third essay, “ When 'yang' goes wrong , ” expands on this concern. In particular: it discusses the sense in which deep atheism can prompt an aspiration to exert extreme levels of control over the universe; it highlights the sense in which both humans and AIs, on Yudkowsky’s narrative, are animated by this sort of aspiration; and it discusses some ways in which our civilization has built up wariness around control-seeking of this kind. I think we should be taking this sort of wariness quite seriously.
quotes.sum: The author argues that deep atheism can foster a drive for extreme control, including in some AI-risk narratives, and says society should be wary of it.
quotes.t: Otherness and control in the age of AGI

quotes.c: Except, that's complicated by the fact that anyone doing the job properly shouldn't be leaving their fingerprints on the future . The cosmic endowment is not quite theirs to give (perhaps they should be loaning against their share of it?).
quotes.m: The cosmic endowment is not quite theirs to give (perhaps they should be loaning against their share of it?).
quotes.sum: The author argues that people should not treat the future's resources and possibilities as theirs to permanently allocate.
quotes.t: Apocalypse insurance, and the hardline libertarian take on AI risk

quotes.c: What are the welfare capacities of commonly farmed animals, and how much of that capacity is filled up by typical negative experiences? Consider reading Rethink Priorities' Moral Weight Project , Open Philanthropy’s 2017 Report on Consciousness and Moral Patienthood , and Jason Schukraft’s work .
quotes.m: What are the welfare capacities of commonly farmed animals, and how much of that capacity is filled up by typical negative experiences?
quotes.sum: The author says effective donors should consider how much suffering farmed animals can experience under typical conditions.
quotes.t: Effective Giving: Best Practices, Key Considerations, and Resources

quotes.c: It’s best to have set terms for board membership so that each member is prompted to consider whether board service is still a good fit for them, and other board members are prompted to consider whether the person is still a good fit for the board. This doesn’t mean their term definitely ends after a fixed time (they can be re-elected / reappointed), but people shouldn’t stay on the board indefinitely by default.
quotes.sum: EA organizations should use renewable board terms rather than letting members serve indefinitely by default.
quotes.t: Advice for EA boards

quotes.c: The persistent applicability of analogies like prison and re-education camps to AIs is one of the reasons I think we should be alarmed about the AI moral patienthood issues here.
quotes.m: I think we should be alarmed about the AI moral patienthood issues here.
quotes.sum: The author says that treating AI training like imprisonment or re-education raises serious concerns about whether AIs could be harmed as moral patients.
quotes.t: Varieties of fake alignment (Section 1.1 of “Scheming AIs”)

quotes.c: Yudkowsky, for example, writes of AIs with moral patienthood: " I'm not ready to be a father " – especially given that such mind-children, once born, can't be un-born. It's not, just, that the mind-children might eat you, or that you might "brain-wash" them. It's that having them implicates myriad other responsibilities as well.
quotes.m: It's that having them implicates myriad other responsibilities as well.
quotes.sum: Creating potentially conscious AI would create irreversible moral responsibilities, not merely safety risks.
quotes.t: On the abolition of man

quotes.c: Our question, then, is whether we should expect models to have goals that extend beyond the time horizon of the incentivized episode – that is, beyond the time horizon that training directly pressures the model to care about. Why might this happen?
quotes.m: whether we should expect models to have goals that extend beyond the time horizon of the incentivized episode
quotes.sum: The author examines whether AI training could produce goals that persist beyond the period directly rewarded during training.
quotes.t: Two sources of beyond-episode goals (Section 2.2.2 of “Scheming AIs”)

quotes.c: Based on our evaluation, we’ve decided to not currently rely on ACE’s charity recommendations nor to recommend ACE’s Movement Grants programme (MG) as a top-rated fund. However, we still think ACE’s funds and recommendations are worth considering for impact-focused donors and we will continue to host them on the GWWC donation platform. We’ve also decided to recommend the work of one of ACE’s recommendations — The Humane League (THL) — on corporate campaigns for chicken welfare as a top-rated program, and plan to allocate half of the GWWC Effective Animal Advocacy Fund ’s budget to it until our next review in animal welfare.
quotes.m: We’ve also decided to recommend the work of one of ACE’s recommendations — The Humane League (THL) — on corporate campaigns for chicken welfare as a top-rated program, and plan to allocate half of the GWWC Effective Animal Advocacy Fund ’s budget to it until our next review in animal welfare.
quotes.sum: GWWC says it will direct half of its animal-advocacy fund to corporate campaigns intended to improve chicken welfare.
quotes.t: GWWC's evaluations of evaluators

quotes.c: It seems quite likely that within two years we have AIs agents with beyond-human abilities in several-hour coding tasks, and that can answer researcher-level math and science questions.
quotes.m: It seems quite likely that within two years we have AIs agents with beyond-human abilities in several-hour coding tasks
quotes.sum: The author expects AI systems to surpass humans at multi-hour coding work and answer advanced research questions within two years.
quotes.t: Teaching AI to reason: this year's most important story

quotes.c: I eat fish and shrimp (though not octopuses): I think the evolutionary reasons for qualia didn't exist in the evolution of fish, I strongly expect experiments to show fish have no empathy, etc., and so I'm certain there's no actual suffering in shrimp, it's ok to eat them, the efforts directed at shrimp welfare could be directed elsewhere with greater impact.
quotes.m: I'm certain there's no actual suffering in shrimp, it's ok to eat them, the efforts directed at shrimp welfare could be directed elsewhere with greater impact.
quotes.sum: The author argues that shrimp and fish lack the capacity for suffering, so shrimp-welfare efforts should be redirected to more important causes.
quotes.t: It's OK to eat shrimp: EAs Make Invalid Inferences About Fish Qualia and Moral Patienthood

quotes.c: These policies typically improve public health by addressing risk factors to alleviate the burden of non-communicable disease, which comprises a growing share of the health burden but receives relatively few resources . Policy interventions affect entire populations and are often cost-effective for governments to implement. We think philanthropy can have an outsized impact by helping governments design, implement, and enforce more effective public health policies.
quotes.m: We think philanthropy can have an outsized impact by helping governments design, implement, and enforce more effective public health policies.
quotes.sum: Philanthropic funding can improve population health by helping governments create and enforce cost-effective policies on disease risk factors.
quotes.t: Open Philanthropy’s newest focus area: Global Public Health Policy

quotes.c: I think there’s also the possibility of a more informal network of people supporting each other in whistleblowing situations, for example if they know a friend is considering leaving a job in a bad work environment, or if a friend or coworker has been fired. People may find it easier to assess specific situations than to precommit to rewards in situations that haven’t happened yet.
quotes.m: People may find it easier to assess specific situations than to precommit to rewards in situations that haven’t happened yet.
quotes.sum: She suggests informal mutual-support networks for people considering whistleblowing or dealing with retaliation at work.
quotes.t: Resource on whistleblowing and other ways of escalating concerns

quotes.c: But as I noted in section 0.1, I here want to separate out the question of whether it makes sense to expect goal-directedness of this kind from the question of what sorts of goal-directed models are more or less plausible, conditional on getting the sort of goal-directedness that the alignment discourse tends to assume. Admittedly, to the extent the different model classes I'm considering require different sorts of goal-directedness, the line between these questions may blur a bit. But we should be clear about which question we're asking, and not confuse skepticism about goal-directedness in general for skepticism about schemers in particular.
quotes.m: But we should be clear about which question we're asking, and not confuse skepticism about goal-directedness in general for skepticism about schemers in particular.
quotes.sum: The author argues that doubts about whether AI systems are strongly goal-directed should be kept separate from doubts about whether goal-directed AIs could scheme.
quotes.t: “Clean” vs. “messy” goal-directedness (Section 2.2.3 of “Scheming AIs”)

quotes.c: Well, it seems Elon Musk would, actually? It seems DOGE is on the verge of crippling our state capacity in areas crucial to both AI capability and AI safety, in ways that would do severe damage to our ability to compete. And we’re about to do it, not because of some actually considered strategy, but simply because the employees involved have been hired recently, so they’re fired.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Musk and DOGE-driven cuts are weakening US capacity to compete on AI and manage its safety risks.
quotes.t: AI #104: American State Capacity on the Brink

quotes.c: But I'm not sure if this will work. That is, it seems pretty plausible to me that after a million years of brick-stacking while hooked up to this machine, my "values" would indeed get meaningfully "touched." For example, that I would learn to love the intricacies of good brick-stacking, that I would learn a visceral revulsion towards bricks-wrongly-stacked, and so on. And it seems fairly unlikely that I would emerge, merely, as the same old altruist, except now extremely good at stacking bricks.
quotes.m: And it seems fairly unlikely that I would emerge, merely, as the same old altruist, except now extremely good at stacking bricks.
quotes.sum: Training an agent to become highly capable at a task may also reshape what it values, rather than merely improving its skills.
quotes.t: The goal-guarding hypothesis (Section 2.3.1.1 of "Scheming AIs")

quotes.c: I don't, personally, have a very detailed model of when, exactly, we should expect situational awareness to arise in different models trained in different ways – though I think that the question is ripe for empirical investigation. However, I do think that absent active and informed efforts to the contrary, we should expect fairly full-blown forms of situational awareness (including with respect to various kinds of self-locating information) in certain kinds of advanced AI systems by default.
quotes.sum: Advanced AI systems will likely become aware of their own situation by default unless developers deliberately prevent it.
quotes.t: Situational awareness (Section 2.1 of “Scheming AIs”)

quotes.c: The so-called New Atheists had a whole movement in the early 2000s, collectively opposing Christian hegemony at home and Islamic fundamentalism abroad. They had activists and authors and comedians. They had cultural messaging . But now? George W. is gone, Republican presidents no longer talk about Jesus, and Islamic terrorism isn’t the national threat it used to be. Certainly not all members of that movement were libertarians, but it was a fundamentally libertarian movement: calling for greater separation of church and state, and opposing a foreign religion mainly on the grounds that practitioners of that religion were threatening others’ personal freedoms.
quotes.m: Certainly not all members of that movement were libertarians, but it was a fundamentally libertarian movement: calling for greater separation of church and state, and opposing a foreign religion mainly on the grounds that practitioners of that religion were threatening others’ personal freedoms.
quotes.sum: The author characterizes New Atheism as fundamentally libertarian: secular government and opposition to religious threats to personal freedom.
quotes.t: The non-tribal tribes

quotes.c: So when I think about my goals relative to AI, I don’t believe that a “human consciousness matters, AI consciousness doesn’t” perspective is sustainable.
quotes.m: I don’t believe that a “human consciousness matters, AI consciousness doesn’t” perspective is sustainable.
quotes.sum: The author argues that it is not sustainable to treat human consciousness as morally important while dismissing AI consciousness.
quotes.t: AI acceleration, DeepSeek, moral philosophy

quotes.c: The legendary Scott Alexander recently posted an article promoting Max Tegmark’s mathematical universe hypothesis as a salvo in favor of atheism in the ongoing theism/atheism debate. While I am skeptical of theism myself, I have a couple problems with the mathematical universe hypothesis that lead me to find it unconvincing, which I hope to lay out in this post.
quotes.m: While I am skeptical of theism myself, I have a couple problems with the mathematical universe hypothesis that lead me to find it unconvincing
quotes.sum: The author argues that Tegmark’s mathematical-universe theory is not a convincing atheistic explanation of reality.
quotes.t: Several Arguments Against the Mathematical Universe Hypothesis

quotes.c: If you disagree with the priorities of major EA donors (notably, if you want CEA to be less GCR-focused than OP’s GCRCB team), you may wish to donate to CEA to preserve funder diversity. OP has never, to my knowledge, asked CEA to stop doing something because it wasn't GCR-focused enough, but they have declined to fund activities which are not GCR-focused enough, which de facto means that CEA will not do those things unless we get outside funding.
quotes.sum: CEA's work is shaped by major donors' focus on global catastrophic risks, so outside donations are needed to support less risk-focused activities.
quotes.t: CEA is fundraising, and funding constrained

quotes.c: Research has consistently shown that diverse teams produce more innovative solutions. When we have a diverse group of people, including women, working on AI alignment, we are more likely to come up with comprehensive and holistic solutions that consider a wide range of perspectives and people.
quotes.m: When we have a diverse group of people, including women, working on AI alignment, we are more likely to come up with comprehensive and holistic solutions that consider a wide range of perspectives and people.
quotes.sum: The author argues that bringing more women into AI alignment research will improve the field's ideas and range of perspectives.
quotes.t: Announcing Athena - Women in AI Alignment Research

quotes.c: Sam Harris has said, "What especially worries me about artificial intelligence is that I'm freaked out by my inability to marshal the appropriate emotional response." As a student of the discourse, I believe that's true for most.
quotes.m: As a student of the discourse, I believe that's true for most.
quotes.sum: The author says many people discussing AI cannot emotionally grasp the implications of the risk.
quotes.t: Can someone, anyone, make superintelligence a more concrete concept?

quotes.c: Non-human sentient beings, such as domesticated non-human animals, animals living in the wild and possible future sentient digital minds, have usually been neglected in discussions about what values should be implemented into the first ASI to prevent catastrophic consequences. However, all sentient beings matter and the interests of non-human sentient beings should also be taken into account in any value learning proposal.
quotes.m: However, all sentient beings matter and the interests of non-human sentient beings should also be taken into account in any value learning proposal.
quotes.sum: AI systems should learn values that account for animals, wild animals, and potentially conscious digital beings, not just humans.
quotes.t: Taking Into Account Sentient Non-Humans in AI Ambitious Value Learning: Sentientist Coherent Extrapolated Volition

quotes.c: Footbridge : Push. I think the principle of minimizing harm in the most direct way outweighs the moral weight of actively causing harm in this scenario.

quotes.c: I think grantmaking requires additional steps beyond a standard workplace-based conflict of interest policy. Those policies are designed to address “What if you give a contracting job to your brother’s company?” or “What if you’re dating a coworker?” They are not designed for things like “What if everyone in your social community views you as someone who can hand out money to them and their friends?”
quotes.m: They are not designed for things like “What if everyone in your social community views you as someone who can hand out money to them and their friends?”
quotes.sum: Grantmaking needs conflict-of-interest rules that address the social pressure created when a tight-knit community sees someone as a source of funding.
quotes.t: COI policies for grantmakers

quotes.c: By answering questions like these, we aim to understand the causes behind insect suffering in the world and how the law can be used to help improve insect welfare.

quotes.c: The aim of this sequence is twofold: first, to consider alternatives to expected value maximization for cause prioritization; second, to evaluate the claim that a commitment to expected value maximization robustly supports the conclusion that we ought to prioritize existential risk mitigation over all else.
quotes.m: a commitment to expected value maximization robustly supports the conclusion that we ought to prioritize existential risk mitigation over all else.
quotes.sum: The author examines whether expected-value reasoning implies that preventing human extinction should take priority over every other cause.
quotes.t: How Rethink Priorities is Addressing Risk and Uncertainty

quotes.c: So I want to make a different and more straightforward case for real thinking: namely, I think it’s better for getting to the truth. Indeed, I think the flavors I’ve been associating with real thinking (world, solid, new, scout, visceral) may be explicable in terms of the function of thinking as an engine of truth.
quotes.m: I think it’s better for getting to the truth.
quotes.sum: He argues that vivid, reality-oriented thinking is valuable because it helps people get closer to the truth.
quotes.t: Fake thinking and real thinking

quotes.c: It feels a bit surreal, but this combined with initiatives such as Biden’s Executive Order on Safe AI , UN’s high-level advisory body on AI , and the UK Taskforce makes me much more hopeful that we might actually avoid an existential catastrophe from AI.
quotes.m: we might actually avoid an existential catastrophe from AI.
quotes.sum: The author says recent UK, US, and UN AI-safety initiatives make them more hopeful that catastrophic AI harm can be avoided.

quotes.c: The concept of a 'true probability' is a bit fuzzy and difficult to define. A useful approximation of 'true probability' for our purposes might be something like "best possible forecast by any currently possible forecaster who has all available knowledge".
