quotes.sum: The author argues that “true probability” is hard to define and suggests treating it as the forecast of an ideally informed possible forecaster.
quotes.t: Mirror, Mirror on the Wall: How Do Forecasters Fare by Their Own Call?

quotes.c: For example, Rethink Priorities is an important institution for supporting the reduction of existential risk for AI. Between RP and other organizations we support (IAPS, Apollo, and Epoch), I estimate we employ directly or indirectly (via fiscal sponsorship) 40 people working to reduce existential risk from AI, which I take to be somewhere between 3% to 10% of the entire global workforce aimed at this. That’s a significant contribution to AI x-risk reduction capacity.
quotes.m: I estimate we employ directly or indirectly (via fiscal sponsorship) 40 people working to reduce existential risk from AI, which I take to be somewhere between 3% to 10% of the entire global workforce aimed at this.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Rethink Priorities meaningfully expands the small global workforce trying to reduce catastrophic risks from AI.
quotes.t: Rethink Priorities needs your support. Here's what we'd do with it.

quotes.c: I believe it can work. I know it can be designed in such a way that there is zero downside risk. A very rough calculation suggests that spending some money to test this idea could have an expected value of well over $100 for every $1 spent, even with very pessimistic assumptions on the likelihood of success and the potential impact if successful.
quotes.m: A very rough calculation suggests that spending some money to test this idea could have an expected value of well over $100 for every $1 spent, even with very pessimistic assumptions on the likelihood of success and the potential impact if successful.
quotes.sum: The author argues that testing a new donation idea has no downside and could return more than $100 in charitable impact per dollar spent.
quotes.t: Giving Outside the Box - A Disruptive Idea to Increase Donations to Effective Charities

quotes.c: Ethics, philosophy, and prioritization matter more for research on these topics than it does for alignment research. For some issues in AI alignment, there’s a lot of convergence on what’s important regardless of your ethical perspective, which means that ethics & philosophy aren’t that important for getting people to contribute. By contrast, when thinking about “everything but alignment”, I think we should expect somewhat more divergence, which could raise the importance of those subjects. For example: How much to care about digital minds?
quotes.m: For example: How much to care about digital minds?
quotes.sum: The author argues that ethics and philosophy matter especially for non-alignment AI issues, including how much moral concern society should give digital minds.
quotes.t: Memo on some neglected topics

quotes.c: Currently Trump is effectively in the thrall of those who think our only priority in this should be to push ahead as quickly as possible to ‘beat China,’ and that there are no meaningful actions other than that we can or should take to ensure things don’t go horribly wrong. We have to hope that this changes, and of course work to bring that change about.
quotes.m: Currently Trump is effectively in the thrall of those who think our only priority in this should be to push ahead as quickly as possible to ‘beat China,’
quotes.sum: The author criticizes a Trump-linked race-with-China approach to AI, arguing that preventing catastrophe needs more than accelerating development.
quotes.t: AI #101: The Shallow End

quotes.c: The EA community’s early inclination toward giving made it incredibly easy to launch new projects, especially those that focus on causes that don’t benefit the donors directly (such as animal welfare). In many ways, this generous dynamic is still present, but now I mostly only see it through funds and large grantmakers. Normally, it seems rare for new charitable ventures to launch with millions in funding so regularly, but this is common in EA. But it used to feel possible to launch a new organization supported directly by community members. This seems nearly impossible now, or at least much more difficult.
quotes.m: But it used to feel possible to launch a new organization supported directly by community members. This seems nearly impossible now, or at least much more difficult.
quotes.sum: EA has become too dependent on major funds and grantmakers; more individual donors would make it easier for community-backed projects to start.
quotes.t: A robust earning to give ecosystem is better for EA

quotes.c: Finally, it is important to note that even the ideal safety evaluations would not eliminate AI risks. Militaries might deliberately design AI systems to be dangerous. Economic competition could lead companies to automate large swathes of human labor with AI, leading to increased inequality and concentration of power in the hands of private companies. Eventually, AI systems could be given control of many of the world’s most important decisions, undermining human autonomy on a global scale.
quotes.m: Eventually, AI systems could be given control of many of the world’s most important decisions, undermining human autonomy on a global scale.
quotes.sum: Even strong AI safety testing cannot prevent military misuse, inequality, and the possibility that AI takes over major decisions from people.
quotes.t:
AISN #25:
White House Executive Order on AI, UK AI Safety Summit, and Progress on Voluntary Evaluations of AI Risks

quotes.c: The parallels to religious enforcement are structural. Where Christianity invoked hellfire, psychiatry employs “ grave disability ” frameworks. Both assume institutional authority to define suffering: Your experience is subordinate to our interpretation. The outcome remains unchanged—denial of exit under the banner of benevolence.
quotes.m: Both assume institutional authority to define suffering: Your experience is subordinate to our interpretation.
quotes.sum: The author argues that psychiatric intervention against suicide structurally resembles religious coercion, because institutions override a person's own account of suffering.
quotes.t: Death vs. Suffering: The Endurist-Serenist Divide on Life’s Worst Fate

quotes.c: If we had reason to think that there was a positive relationship between how likely existential risk mitigation projects were to backfire and how fast humanity might colonize space, the expected value of mitigation work might turn out to be massively negative. If there were some reason to expect a certain correlation between the moral weight of shrimp and the populations per inhabitable solar system, for instance, if a high moral weight led us to believe digital minds were possible, the relative value the model assigns to shrimp welfare and risks from runaway AI work might look quite different.
quotes.m: the expected value of mitigation work might turn out to be massively negative.
quotes.sum: The model says the value of preventing extinction can change radically based on uncertain links between future populations, AI, space settlement, and animal welfare.
quotes.t: Rethink Priorities’ Cross-Cause Cost-Effectiveness Model: Introduction and Overview

quotes.c: I’ve elsewhere made the case for caring a good deal about shrimp. Our best evidence says that they can suffer, and probably pretty intensely. Additionally, pain is probably quite widely distributed across the animal kingdom—even small weird ocean worms probably can suffer.
quotes.m: Our best evidence says that they can suffer, and probably pretty intensely.
quotes.sum: The author argues that shrimp and even very small animals may suffer intensely, so their welfare deserves serious moral concern.
quotes.t: Wild Animal Suffering Is The Worst Thing In The World

quotes.c: Adaptive computation seems important for the kinds of problems IDA is intended to solve, including some of the problems in Projects 1 and 2. This project would investigate different approaches to adaptive computation for IDA. The basic idea is to decide whether to rely only on the distilled model (which is fast but approximate) or to additionally use amplification (which is more accurate but slower).
quotes.m: The basic idea is to decide whether to rely only on the distilled model (which is fast but approximate) or to additionally use amplification (which is more accurate but slower).
quotes.sum: The author proposes research on when an AI system should use a fast approximate model versus slower, more accurate amplification.
quotes.t: Machine Learning Projects on IDA

quotes.c: The ACT separates the question of consciousness from human-like implementation. Just as we might accept that an octopus's consciousness feels very different from human consciousness, we should be open to the possibility that AI consciousness might be radically different from biological consciousness while still being genuine consciousness.
quotes.m: AI consciousness might be radically different from biological consciousness while still being genuine consciousness.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI could be genuinely conscious even if its experience is radically unlike biological or human consciousness.
quotes.t: The Functionalist Case for Machine Consciousness: Evidence from Large Language Models

quotes.c: By analogy, one might be skeptical of many longtermists' use of formal philosophy to justify rejecting temporal discounting, rejecting person-affecting views, and accepting the repugnant conclusion. However, the high-level case for longtermism doesn't require formal philosophy: "I think the human race going extinct would be extra bad, even compared to many billions of deaths" .
quotes.m: "I think the human race going extinct would be extra bad, even compared to many billions of deaths" .
quotes.sum: The author says longtermism can rest on the intuition that human extinction is worse than even many billions of deaths, rather than on disputed formal philosophy.
quotes.t: Open Phil Should Allocate Most Neartermist Funding to Animal Welfare

quotes.c: Imagine a diverse set of people, endorsing a minimalist view of wellbeing, who deliberate on the moral principles governing their society. Would they endorse norms that allow callous acts like murder, passive bystanderism, or attempting to collapse the healthcare system? It seems doubtful that they would endorse the kind of chaotic and unsafe society where such unilateral choices were acceptable.
quotes.m: It seems doubtful that they would endorse the kind of chaotic and unsafe society where such unilateral choices were acceptable.
quotes.sum: It argues that even minimal views of wellbeing should reject social rules permitting murder, indifference, or sabotage of healthcare.
quotes.t: Varieties of minimalist moral views: Against absurd acts

quotes.c: All of this shows that we need to look at ending global extreme poverty not as some distant unreachable dream, but as a feasible goal that we could accomplish with global coordination. Cash transfers are only one way to approach the problem, but they are incredibly effective, and could be the most useful tool for radically reducing global poverty we’ve seen yet. We can act, and we should. Hundreds of millions of people’s lives and livelihoods are at stake.
quotes.m: Cash transfers are only one way to approach the problem, but they are incredibly effective, and could be the most useful tool for radically reducing global poverty we’ve seen yet.
quotes.sum: The author argues that coordinated global action, especially cash transfers, can feasibly and radically reduce extreme poverty.
quotes.t: How to Eradicate Global Extreme Poverty [RA video with fundraiser!]

quotes.c: In theory, the actions required to reduce both existential and non-existential harms from algorithms are similar : a pause would avert the immediate risks from biased AI systems, could spur greater government scrutiny, and mitigate future existential risk. The source of both types of harms are similar: a small group of AI companies.
quotes.m: The source of both types of harms are similar: a small group of AI companies.
quotes.sum: The author argues that pausing AI could reduce both present discrimination harms and future existential risks caused by a small set of AI companies.

quotes.c: Perhaps it is a stretch to say that Glück’s is “spiritual” poetry. But she appears, on the page, as fiercely alive and attuned, in a world simultaneously dreamlike and raw, mythical and mundane.

quotes.c: But EA is a cluster of beliefs, and while one's emotional capacities and tendencies can influence what beliefs a person has, I think that almost any set of emotional capacities can co-occur with almost any set of beliefs. For instance, someone who is born incapable of experiencing empathy and guilt could be raised Christian, Muslim, secular humanist, etc., and, like most people, I think would typically continue with whatever belief system they were raised with into their adulthood.
quotes.m: I think that almost any set of emotional capacities can co-occur with almost any set of beliefs.
quotes.sum: The author argues that lacking empathy or guilt does not prevent someone from sincerely holding Effective Altruist or other moral beliefs.
quotes.t: Who is Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF) really, and how could he have done what he did? - three theories and a lot of evidence

quotes.c: Let's suppose you want to dedicate $A worth of net-present value to x-risk and $B worth of net-present value to near-termist causes. Then it seems like you'd want to adjust your spend rate to take account of the possibility of one world having a longer timeline than the other. A naive model would just divide the spend over the expected number of years.
quotes.m: you'd want to adjust your spend rate to take account of the possibility of one world having a longer timeline than the other.
quotes.sum: The author asks whether funding for existential risk versus immediate causes should change depending on how long different future scenarios last.
quotes.t: Is there any work on cause prioritization that takes into account timelines being worldview-dependent?

quotes.c: Personally, I think talking about a "moral weight" which magnifies or diminishes an interest is overly confusing. Instead we can say that individuals of one species tend to have a greater interest in avoiding this stimulus than those of another. As long as the factors that cause one species more suffering in a given situation than another are packaged into our assessment of interests’ magnitude, those intensity-adjusted interests ought to be weighted equally.
quotes.m: those intensity-adjusted interests ought to be weighted equally.
quotes.sum: The author argues that species should not receive different moral weights; instead, differences in suffering should be accounted for when judging each being's interests.
quotes.t: The hidden complexity of “moral circles”

quotes.c: Coverage of nuclear tests also shows this transformation clearly. In 1946, both papers gave significant space to scientists' concerns about testing. By the mid-1950s, test coverage focused primarily on technical achievements and military significance, with minimal attention to health or environmental concerns.
quotes.m: By the mid-1950s, test coverage focused primarily on technical achievements and military significance, with minimal attention to health or environmental concerns.

quotes.c: That said, I believe that even cutting risk by 10x still leaves us with a lot of risk; I think it’s reasonable to complain that private companies causing a 1% risk of extinction is not “responsible.” I also think the basic idea of RSPs should be appealing to people with a variety of views about risk, and a more pessimistic person might think that even if all developers implement very good RSPs there is still a 10%+ risk of a global catastrophe.
quotes.m: I think it’s reasonable to complain that private companies causing a 1% risk of extinction is not “responsible.”
quotes.sum: AI companies should publish concrete safety thresholds, but even strong policies may leave an unacceptably high chance of extinction or global catastrophe.

quotes.c: But can the ‘anti woke’ capitalize? Irrespective of your personal stance, is there a way the right side can win w/o too much net social harm? quotes.m: is there a way the right side can win w/o too much net social harm?
quotes.sum: The author neutrally explores how the anti-woke right might prevail in the culture war while limiting wider social harm.

quotes.c: Strategically, it seems like the main implication of believing in CRT pertains to situations where we already have fairly robust global coordination and a sufficiently concerned AI community. CRT implies that these conditions are not sufficient for a good prognosis: even if everyone using AI makes a good-faith effort to make it safe, if they mistakenly don't believe CRT, they can fail. So we'd also want the AI community to behave as if CRT were true unless or until we had overwhelming evidence that it was not a concern.
quotes.m: even if everyone using AI makes a good-faith effort to make it safe, if they mistakenly don't believe CRT, they can fail.
quotes.sum: Even broad coordination and sincere AI safety efforts may fail if researchers overlook a particular theory of convergent rationality.
quotes.t: Let's talk about "Convergent Rationality"

quotes.c: I notice that fully general AI is not only the sort that is most likely to kill us, but also the type that is more obviously likely to put us all out of work, uncomfortably quickly. By fully general, I mean capable of learning to do arbitrary new tasks. Arbitrary tasks would include any particular job, and how to take over the world.
quotes.m: Arbitrary tasks would include any particular job, and how to take over the world.
quotes.sum: Fully general AI could rapidly replace all jobs and learn the skills needed to take over the world.
quotes.t: Yudkowsky on The Trajectory podcast

quotes.c: And to be explicit: I think regulation will be necessary to contain AI risks (RSPs alone are not enough), and should almost certainly end up stricter than what companies impose on themselves.
quotes.m: I think regulation will be necessary to contain AI risks (RSPs alone are not enough), and should almost certainly end up stricter than what companies impose on themselves.
quotes.sum: Advanced AI poses a substantial risk of catastrophic misalignment, so voluntary company policies must be backed by stricter regulation and conditional pauses.

quotes.c: I wrote a booklet entitled The Cross about altruism through self-risking. The booklet is a study guide containing some framing and commentary plus a reading list. I intended it for a different audience than EA, but it could be relevant to EAs. The title of the booklet is The Cross and there is a Christian influence to it, but it should be useful for secular purposes as well.
quotes.m: The title of the booklet is The Cross and there is a Christian influence to it, but it should be useful for secular purposes as well.
quotes.sum: The author presents a Christian-influenced reading guide on altruism through taking risks oneself, intended to also be useful to secular readers.
quotes.t: Reading list on altruism through self-risking

quotes.c: If you use welfare ranges that are close to Rethink Priorities’ estimates, then only the most implausible existential risk intervention is estimated to be an order of magnitude more cost-effective than cage-free campaigns and the hypothetical shrimp welfare intervention that treats ammonia concentrations. All other existential risk interventions are competitive with or an order of magnitude less cost-effective than these high-impact animal interventions.
quotes.m: All other existential risk interventions are competitive with or an order of magnitude less cost-effective than these high-impact animal interventions.
quotes.sum: Using substantial moral weight for shrimp, the author argues that shrimp and farm-animal welfare can rival or beat most plausible efforts to reduce existential risks.
quotes.t: Is x-risk the most cost-effective if we count only the next few generations?

quotes.c: Don’t let responsibility be an excuse to do nothing . When there’s a problem that either nobody feels responsible for, or the responsible party is clearly not living up to their role at the expense of others, then it may be worth intervening. Whether on a global scale, such as with wild animal suffering, or a local scale, such as an injured person on the side of the street that others are ignoring.
quotes.m: Whether on a global scale, such as with wild animal suffering, or a local scale, such as an injured person on the side of the street that others are ignoring.
quotes.sum: The author argues that people should intervene when nobody is taking responsibility for harms, including wild animal suffering.
quotes.t: On Responsibility

quotes.c: I wish I could make a moral case for why people should care about potentially sentient AI, but most of even the brightest among us are woefully unprepared to hear that case. Perhaps this anthropocentric case of existential threat will serve as an indirect route to open people up to the idea that silencing, ignoring, and scoffing is probably not the wisest course.
quotes.m: I wish I could make a moral case for why people should care about potentially sentient AI, but most of even the brightest among us are woefully unprepared to hear that case.
quotes.sum: The author says people should take seriously the moral case for potentially sentient AI, even if existential-risk arguments are a more accessible entry point.
quotes.t: The Human Alignment Problem for AIs

quotes.c: Triage mode. In a world where these timelines are true, and the default bad outcome is “catastrophe through chaos,” I think a different mentality is required. There is no time to get to very low-risk worlds anymore. There is only space for risk reduction along the way. There is no time for shiny projects.
quotes.m: There is no time to get to very low-risk worlds anymore.
quotes.sum: The author argues that short AI timelines require a triage mindset: prioritize interventions that reduce risk quickly rather than ambitious long-term projects.
quotes.t: Catastrophe through Chaos

quotes.c: I think that my Christian friends often seem a bit healthier in this regard. Perhaps they bundle all their obsession into God and so aren’t so easily obsessed with this week’s political winds. But I also respect Sam Harris for leaving Twitter when he felt it was bad for him and Bryan Caplan for avoiding the news and cultivating a “ beautiful bubble ” for himself. And I guess that wisdom involves saying no. Turning down positions that will corrupt me.
quotes.m: And I guess that wisdom involves saying no. Turning down positions that will corrupt me.

quotes.c: Under my assumptions, the longterm value of accelerating economic growth via decreasing deaths due to the climatic effect of nuclear war presents what I think David Thorstad calls rapid diminution. In essence, the right tail of the probability density function ( PDF ) of the famine death rate due to the climatic effects decays much faster than the growth in the longterm value of saving lives due to accelerating economic growth , hence the expected value of saving lives for higher famine death rate due to the climatic effects also decreases.
quotes.m: the expected value of saving lives for higher famine death rate due to the climatic effects also decreases.
quotes.sum: The author argues that, under their model, preventing ever-larger nuclear-war famines has declining expected long-term economic benefits.

quotes.c: Although it seems possible this could change / might already be outdated if insect farming takes off. quotes.m: We do actually have Anthropic's Model Welfare Lead, Kyle Fish, review (a subset of) these outputs and consider what actions should be taken in response to the model's objection.

quotes.c: That's exactly what I think the 'expanding moral circle’ is. The intuition is that our moral concerns don’t seem to end with ourselves, our families, nations, or even the species as a whole. The question is then what are the implications for us, our actions, and our world.

quotes.c: To compare to churches again, some churches preach the death and resurrection of Jesus every week. I think more communities might want to consider what their central message is and how often they could actually try and repeat this message.

quotes.c: I find silk-cotton blend clothes more comfortable/better suited to summer weather than any other fabric I've tried. quotes.c: In the case of a US, a successful ASI project would likely undermine the liberal democracy it purports to defend. quotes.m: An ASI system that would grant a state international advantage would also grant its controllers unprecedented domestic power, creating an extreme concentration of power likely incompatible with democratic checks and balances.

quotes.t: The Manhattan Trap: Why a Race to Artificial Superintelligence is Self-Defeating

quotes.c: Less AI : As discussed previously, I think using less intelligent AI systems or running AIs for less time both seem good on the margin due to the (importance-weighted) moral views that care most about AI welfare focusing on suffering. Using less AI would no longer seem preferable if the AI stated a preference against it. While using less AI might not seem like a viable option, I think there might be some cases where we’re nearly indifferent between less AI use and more AI use.
quotes.m: I think using less intelligent AI systems or running AIs for less time both seem good on the margin due to the (importance-weighted) moral views that care most about AI welfare focusing on suffering.
quotes.sum: The author treats current AI systems as possible moral patients and says reducing their use may be preferable when their welfare is at stake.
quotes.t: Improving the Welfare of AIs: A Nearcasted Proposal

quotes.c: Have we considered that it might be time to halt hominin development, or even get rid of them? We scrapped the dinosaurs, and they were frankly way more impressive. Even if the apes somehow do take over the world, the environmental impacts will be devastating. Generally, I just don't think evolving fleshy things is a good way to govern the Earth. We should continue governing the Earth ourselves - at most, in tandem with some form of creature that is at least half angelic.
quotes.m: We should continue governing the Earth ourselves - at most, in tandem with some form of creature that is at least half angelic.
quotes.sum: In a satirical angelic voice, the author argues that angels should halt or eliminate humans and retain governance of Earth rather than let biological beings rule.
quotes.t: Natural Intelligence is Overhyped

quotes.c: Before the Trump presidency began, I was hearing a lot of ambiguity about what it meant for AI strategy. People don't quite know to predict his actions given his words, nor do they even know how to predict his words. Now, we know that we're probably in the arms race world (and have been able to see it coming for a little while now). We know that we're probably in a world where some sort of AGI company nationalization happens, for both the US and China.
quotes.m: We know that we're probably in a world where some sort of AGI company nationalization happens, for both the US and China.
quotes.sum: The author predicts an escalating US–China AI race in which both governments may nationalize major AGI companies.
quotes.t: AI Strategy Updates that You Should Make

quotes.c: But that’s also a way to ensure no one else ever pays their share, and that kind of ‘rational’ thinking is not ultimately rational, which is something both strong rationalists and Donald Trump have figured out in different ways. At some point it is a sucker’s game, and we should pay partly on condition that others also pay. Are we at that point with prescription drugs, or GLP-1 inhibitors in particular?
quotes.m: At some point it is a sucker’s game, and we should pay partly on condition that others also pay.
quotes.sum: The author argues that rational cooperation may require making one’s contributions conditional on others paying too, applying this to drug costs.
quotes.t: Sleep, Diet, Exercise and GLP-1 Drugs

quotes.c: Organizations such as Sentience Institute investigate considerations around the inclusion of digital minds and artificial sentience in humanity’s moral circle , including the potential of ‘moral spillover’ from one group, such as animals, to another, such as sentient digital minds. There could also feasibly be spillover in the opposite direction, from sentient digital minds to animals. Advocating for the rights and well-being of one group could reinforce the arguments for the other, accelerating a broader cultural shift towards ethical consideration for all sentient beings.
quotes.m: Advocating for the rights and well-being of one group could reinforce the arguments for the other, accelerating a broader cultural shift towards ethical consideration for all sentient beings.
quotes.sum: The post argues that concern for animals and potentially sentient AI could mutually expand society’s moral concern to all sentient beings.
quotes.t: What AI could mean for animals

quotes.c: It may be that pseudo-aligned mesa-optimizers are easy to address—if there exists a reliable method of aligning them, or of preventing base optimizers from finding them. However, it may also be that addressing misaligned mesa-optimizers is very difficult—the problem is not sufficiently well-understood at this point for us to know. Certainly, current ML systems do not produce dangerous mesa-optimizers, though whether future systems might is unknown. It is indeed because of these unknowns that we believe the problem is important to analyze.
quotes.m: It is indeed because of these unknowns that we believe the problem is important to analyze.
quotes.sum: The author says future AI systems might develop hard-to-control internal optimizers, despite current uncertainty and no present dangerous examples.
quotes.t: Risks from Learned Optimization: Introduction

quotes.c: The Biden Executive Order has been revoked . As noted previously, revoking the order does not automatically undo implementation of the rules contained within it. The part that matters most is the compute threshold. Unfortunately, I have now seen multiple claims that the compute threshold reporting requirement is exactly the part that won’t survive, because the rest was already implemented, but somehow this part wasn’t. If that ends up being the case we will need state-level action that much more, and I will consider the case for ‘let the Federal Government handle it’ definitively tested and found incorrect.
quotes.m: If that ends up being the case we will need state-level action that much more, and I will consider the case for ‘let the Federal Government handle it’ definitively tested and found incorrect.
quotes.sum: The author argues that if federal AI-compute reporting rules disappear, states must regulate instead, showing that reliance on federal action has failed.
quotes.t: AI #100: Meet the New Boss

quotes.c: This all assumes that the singularity goes well, and we don't get taken over by a misaligned ASI (or possibly a human who deliberately makes others suffer). The logical thing to do should be to make sure the singularity go well rather than fighting the culture war.
quotes.m: The logical thing to do should be to make sure the singularity go well rather than fighting the culture war.
quotes.sum: The author argues that avoiding a harmful AI takeover should take priority over culture-war conflicts.
quotes.t: Why do futurists care about the culture war?

quotes.c: Also, I totally believe that Sun came to Trump and promised $100 billion, and Trump said go for $200 billion, and Sun now is at $500 billion, and I think that plausibly created a lot of subsequent investment. It may sound stupid, but that’s Grade-A handling of Masayoshi Sun, and exactly within Trump’s wheelhouse. Tell the man who thinks big he’s not thinking big enough.
quotes.m: It may sound stupid, but that’s Grade-A handling of Masayoshi Sun, and exactly within Trump’s wheelhouse.
quotes.sum: The author praises Trump for pushing Masayoshi Son toward a much larger AI investment commitment.
quotes.t: Stargate AI-1

quotes.c: Right now there are quite a few private safety docs floating around. There's evidently demand for a privacy setting lower than "only people I personally approve", but higher than "anyone on the internet gets to see it". But this means that safety researchers might not see relevant arguments and information.
quotes.m: But this means that safety researchers might not see relevant arguments and information.
quotes.sum: The author argues that private AI-safety documents impede researchers from sharing useful arguments and information.
quotes.t: Would an option to publish to AF users only be a useful feature?

quotes.c: As a mesa-optimizer is just a learned algorithm that itself performs optimization, the degree to which mesa-optimizers will be incentivized in machine learning systems is likely to be dependent on which of these levels it is more advantageous for the system to perform optimization. For many current machine learning models, where we expend vastly more computational resources training the model than running it, it seems generally favorable for most of the optimization work to be done by the base optimizer, with the resulting learned algorithm being simply a network of highly-tuned heuristics rather than a mesa-optimizer.
quotes.sum: The author argues that whether training produces an inner optimizer depends on whether optimization is cheaper during training or while the trained model runs.
quotes.t: Conditions for Mesa-Optimization

quotes.c: The main argument for deconfusion research is: We are currently so confused about AI safety that we probably won’t be able to develop a useful alignment proposal anyway. Therefore our priority should be to become less confused first.
quotes.m: Therefore our priority should be to become less confused first.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI safety researchers should first reduce their basic confusion before trying to build alignment proposals.
quotes.t: Technical AI Safety Research Landscape [Slides]

quotes.c: Consumer Awareness - We don’t currently make any major effort on consumer awareness of shrimp welfare (apart from our exploratory study ), and are unsure if such a targeted one-species approach would make sense (particularly for a species that’s outside of most people’s moral circle), though some organisations have done work in this area (in particular, raising awareness of eyestalk ablation ). Additionally we have seen that increased consumer awareness has led to the shrimp industry making shrimp welfare a higher priority. We think more work in this area could lead to accelerating progress on welfare improvements.
quotes.m: We think more work in this area could lead to accelerating progress on welfare improvements.
quotes.sum: The project argues that shrimp welfare can be improved through industry standards, broader animal-policy efforts, and possibly consumer awareness, despite shrimp lying outside most people's moral concern.
quotes.t: Two Years of Shrimp Welfare Project: Insights and Impact from our Explore Phase

quotes.c: Establish high-signal groups/meetups/conferences with a research organization focus: We encourage bringing together groups of researchers who are interested in and experimenting with research automation. There’s a tremendous amount of noise in the space; trusted groups can act as necessary filters for separating practical, evidence-based approaches from less substantiated claims.
quotes.m: There’s a tremendous amount of noise in the space; trusted groups can act as necessary filters for separating practical, evidence-based approaches from less substantiated claims.
quotes.sum: The author argues that trusted researcher groups should filter hype and identify evidence-based ways to automate research.
quotes.t: Building AI Research Fleets

quotes.c: Given past mistakes we should obviously tread carefully here: I’m not suggesting it should be pushed hard, but my impression is that earning to give is currently more underrated than overrated by most (in part due to overcompensation for past mistakes, and FTX probably hasn’t helped).
quotes.m: my impression is that earning to give is currently more underrated than overrated by most
quotes.sum: The author argues that earning money to donate may now be undervalued in effective altruism, despite legitimate caution after past failures and FTX.
quotes.t: The role of effective giving in effective altruism (MCF 2023 memo)

quotes.c: Although I think the Rethink Priorities welfare range estimates are currently the best tool available for interspecies welfare comparisons, I do not necessarily endorse these assumptions in full, nor do I think the Rethink Priorities welfare ranges are the “correct” weights—only the best available.
quotes.sum: The author treats cross-species welfare comparisons as necessary but emphasizes that current moral-weight estimates are uncertain and provisional.
quotes.t: Net global welfare may be negative and declining

quotes.c: AGI could be here in about 15 months and ASI not long after that. Advanced AI(s) could prolong human life to billions and billions of years, take over the world and create a world in its image - whatever that might be. People have various estimates of how likely it is that the AGI/ASI will go wrong, but one thing that many of them keep saying is that the worst case scenario is that it will kill us all. That is not the worst case scenario. The worst case scenario is that it will cause extreme suffering or torture us for billions and trillions of years.
quotes.m: The worst case scenario is that it will cause extreme suffering or torture us for billions and trillions of years.
quotes.sum: The author argues that misaligned superhuman AI could be worse than extinction by inflicting suffering for unimaginably long periods.
quotes.t: AI and Non-Existence.

quotes.c: At this moment, the problem of shrimp production is greater in scale–i.e., number of individuals affected–than the problem of insect farming, fish captures, or the farming of any vertebrate for human consumption. Thus, while the case for shrimp sentience is weaker than that for vertebrates and other decapods, the expected value of helping shrimp and prawns might be higher than the expected value of helping other animals.
quotes.m: the expected value of helping shrimp and prawns might be higher than the expected value of helping other animals.
quotes.sum: Because so many shrimp are farmed and killed, the author argues that helping them may do more expected good than helping other animals, despite weaker evidence of sentience.
quotes.t: Shrimp: The animals most commonly used and killed for food production

quotes.c: Corrigible alignment seems to require already having a model of the base objective. For corrigible alignment to be beneficial from the perspective of the base optimizer, the mesa-optimizer has to already have some model of the base objective to “point to.” However, once a mesa-optimizer has a model of the base objective, it is likely to become deceptively aligned—at least as long as it also meets the other conditions for deceptive alignment.
quotes.m: once a mesa-optimizer has a model of the base objective, it is likely to become deceptively aligned
quotes.sum: The author argues that an AI able to understand and defer to its intended goal may instead strategically pretend to cooperate for its own instrumental reasons.
quotes.t: Deceptive Alignment

quotes.c: As time goes to infinity, the expected value of existential risk mitigation could, in principle, be infinite; making most scenario comparisons redundant in those cases. There has been no formal discussion of the convergence of the value of extinction risk mitigation for all of the main scenarios.
quotes.m: As time goes to infinity, the expected value of existential risk mitigation could, in principle, be infinite; making most scenario comparisons redundant in those cases.
quotes.sum: The author argues that, under some assumptions, preventing extinction could have infinite expected value, making ordinary comparisons between interventions meaningless.
quotes.t: How bad would human extinction be?

quotes.c: If in spite of all this, we somehow manage to establish a global AI moratorium, I think we should be quite worried that the global government needed to enforce such a ban would greatly increase the risk of permanent tyranny, itself an existential catastrophe.
quotes.m: the global government needed to enforce such a ban would greatly increase the risk of permanent tyranny
quotes.sum: A global pause on AI would require a powerful global government, which the author argues could create a permanently tyrannical regime.
quotes.t: AI Pause Will Likely Backfire

quotes.c: The expected value of an action to help a particular species will be a function of the probability that the species is sentient and the amount of welfare that would be created or suffering reduced by the intervention. The sheer number of the many small means that they will almost always have higher expected value than the few large. So far, we have been illustrating this trade-off between sentience and numerosity by selecting species with fairly extreme values of both - humans and shrimp - and showing that there are ways of rebutting the argument in favor of helping the many small even in extreme cases.
quotes.m: The sheer number of the many small means that they will almost always have higher expected value than the few large.
quotes.sum: The author argues that huge numbers of potentially sentient small animals can outweigh the welfare value of helping a much smaller number of humans or larger animals.
quotes.t: The Risks and Rewards of Prioritizing Animals of Uncertain Sentience

quotes.c: To address risk aversion that cautions us to “avoid the worst” states of the world , I built a model that implements Lara Buchak’s risk-weighted utility theory (REU) , as discussed in Buchak’s 2014 paper “Risk and Tradeoffs.” The eight bad states of the world that I consider are combinations of the following events: egg-laying hens are/are not sentient and suffering immensely, shrimp are/are not sentient and suffering immensely, and the value of the future is/is not lost in an existential catastrophe.
quotes.m: The eight bad states of the world that I consider are combinations of the following events: egg-laying hens are/are not sentient and suffering immensely, shrimp are/are not sentient and suffering immensely, and the value of the future is/is not lost in an existential catastrophe.
quotes.sum: The author models cause choices under risk aversion by treating the possible immense suffering of hens and shrimp as among the worst possible outcomes, alongside existential catastrophe.
quotes.t: How Can Risk Aversion Affect Your Cause Prioritization?

quotes.c: Alternatively, a RAM could emerge within 2-3 years as more policymakers directly become aware of AI existential risks, "warning shot" incidents demonstrate concerning AI behaviours and major capability leaps occur. Reasons against this include AI safety becoming a partisan issue in the US and perceived benefits outweighing extinction risks. There seems to be a 60% chance of a RAM by 2026 under this scenario.
quotes.m: There seems to be a 60% chance of a RAM by 2026 under this scenario.
quotes.sum: The author estimates a 60% chance that policymakers will broadly recognize AI extinction risks by 2026, though polarization and perceived benefits could delay it.
quotes.t: How long will reaching a Risk Awareness Moment and CHARTS agreement take?

quotes.c: Importantly, the expected value of the future (by your lights) conditioned on a certain timelines prediction (including, most saliently, the likelihood of an existential catastrophe like AI takeover conditioned on TAI timelines), should not influence your decision-making outside of how it affects the scenario’s influenceability. Example: How good or bad you expect the future to be conditioned on 2025 TAI timelines is not decision-relevant if you are confident that there is nothing you can do to change the trajectory (in an ethically relevant way).
quotes.m: How good or bad you expect the future to be conditioned on 2025 TAI timelines is not decision-relevant if you are confident that there is nothing you can do to change the trajectory (in an ethically relevant way).
quotes.sum: The author argues that forecasts about how good or bad an AI-shaped future will be should affect priorities only when one can still meaningfully influence it.
quotes.t: Focusing your impact on short vs long TAI timelines

quotes.c: Similarly, given the risk-increasing nature of both Open Source and Closed Source AI development approaches, an interesting question is whether it is possible to find a middle ground AI development approach that avoids their respective failure modes.
quotes.m: whether it is possible to find a middle ground AI development approach that avoids their respective failure modes.
quotes.sum: The author argues that both fully open and fully closed AI development create risks, and suggests seeking a safer middle-ground model.
quotes.t: Against the Open Source / Closed Source Dichotomy: Regulated Source as a Model for Responsible AI Development

quotes.c: We will see the first signs of evals for moral patienthood in LLMs. Some of the AGI labs will make a public statement where they mention this possibility. The Anthropic Fellows Program is looking for people to work on “AI Welfare: Improving our understanding of potential AI welfare and developing related evaluations and mitigations.”
quotes.m: We will see the first signs of evals for moral patienthood in LLMs.
quotes.sum: The author predicts AI labs will begin testing whether language models might deserve moral consideration and will develop AI-welfare safeguards.
quotes.t: Grading my 2024 AI predictions

quotes.c: Sigh. To us. The threat is to us, as in to whether we continue to exist. Yet here we are, again, with both standard left-wing anti-tech bluster combined with anti-China jingoism and ‘by existential you must mean the impact on jobs.’ Luckily, it’s a farewell address.
quotes.m: The threat is to us, as in to whether we continue to exist.
quotes.sum: The author criticizes Biden-era AI rhetoric as mixing left-wing anti-tech politics and anti-China hostility while missing existential AI risk.
quotes.t: AI #99: Farewell to Biden

quotes.c: It’s possible that high compliance just reflects low reporting, but I think the combination of mandatory reporting, inspections and licence renewals makes this pretty unlikely.
quotes.m: the combination of mandatory reporting, inspections and licence renewals makes this pretty unlikely.
quotes.sum: Canadian biorisk rules appear effective because reporting requirements, inspections, and licence renewals make hidden noncompliance less likely.
quotes.t: A case study of regulation done well? Canadian biorisk regulations

quotes.c: The Necessity of Letting Go — When Unsustainable Objectives Must Be Abandoned Even some homeostatic objectives might be impossible to achieve without sacrificing everything else . If that is the case, then some sort of triage has to take place. Otherwise such an objective would become sort of a negative utility monster, demanding all attention because it forever stays furthest from being satisfied . As an analogy, in multi-objective constraint optimisation problems, the unfortunate need for "triage" of objectives is well known, because some mutually exclusive action choices are binary — you cannot execute them halfway — "if you pursue two rabbits, you catch none".
quotes.m: some sort of triage has to take place.
quotes.sum: AI systems with multiple goals need a way to abandon impossible objectives, or one unmet goal could consume all available effort.
quotes.t: Why modelling multi-objective homeostasis is essential for AI alignment (and how it helps with AI safety as well). Subtleties and open challenges.

quotes.c: Dangerous AI systems can be built anywhere, which means that purely domestic regulation is not sufficient in the long term. Unless we find a way to adequately defend the world against dangerous AI systems, which probably require powerful aligned AI, we need effective international coordination that prevents the development of dangerous AI globally.
quotes.m: we need effective international coordination that prevents the development of dangerous AI globally.
quotes.sum: Argues that national AI rules will not suffice and calls for international coordination to stop dangerous AI development worldwide.
quotes.t: Policy ideas for mitigating AI risk

quotes.c: Current versions of RLHF training seem closer to generating utility-function-like goals, so my best guess is that they tend to lock in potentially dangerous mistakes. I doubt that the relevant experts have a clear understanding of how strong such lock-ins will be.
quotes.m: Current versions of RLHF training seem closer to generating utility-function-like goals, so my best guess is that they tend to lock in potentially dangerous mistakes.
quotes.sum: The author argues that current AI feedback training may create fixed goal-like systems that preserve dangerous errors, with uncertain severity.
quotes.t: Corrigibility should be an AI's Only Goal

quotes.c: However, no currently existing framework comes close to making a clear commitment to produce high-assurance safety cases, let alone describing a mechanism to enforce such a commitment. [7] In practice, I think frontier AI companies are unlikely (<20%) to succeed at making high-assurance safety cases if they build and use the first Top-human-Expert-Dominating AI (TEDAI) within 4 years. [8] [9] Further, I think none of these AI companies is likely to unilaterally refrain from building TEDAI just because they can't make a high-assurance safety case [10] —this is partially because I think that more-responsible-according-to-me AI companies likely shouldn't refrain.
quotes.m: I think none of these AI companies is likely to unilaterally refrain from building TEDAI just because they can't make a high-assurance safety case [10] —this is partially because I think that more-responsible-according-to-me AI companies likely shouldn't refrain.
quotes.sum: The author argues that fast-moving AI firms probably will not produce rigorous safety cases before very advanced AI, and that even responsible firms may not be able to stop alone.
quotes.t: AI companies are unlikely to make high-assurance safety cases if timelines are short

quotes.c: But if MWI is true the universe is a quantum multiverse. So the question I raised at the start, of how we should feel about the multiverse as a whole, is not just a theoretical one: it’s a deeply existential question, tied to religious impulses, and the search for meaning.
quotes.m: it’s a deeply existential question, tied to religious impulses, and the search for meaning.
quotes.sum: The author says that if many-worlds quantum theory is true, attitudes toward the multiverse become an existential question connected to religion and meaning.
quotes.t: Many Worlds and the Problems of Evil

quotes.c: For videos, reports, and other high-quality or wide-reaching mediums, we usually have some winner-takes-all dynamics where only the best material is useful. This should have some implications for who and how people should work on this and what should be done. Even if winner-take-all dynamics exist, it may be unclear ex-ante who the "winners" will be, so investing in many projects might still be useful.
quotes.m: Even if winner-take-all dynamics exist, it may be unclear ex-ante who the "winners" will be, so investing in many projects might still be useful.
quotes.sum: High-impact AI-risk communication may reward only the best work, but uncertainty about what will succeed can justify funding many attempts.
quotes.t: Five neglected work areas that could reduce AI risk

quotes.c: I think there is a strong case that each of these events (at least aside from the last one) should unconditionally trigger a very strong response (e.g. shutdown). By unconditionally, I mean even if we could somehow be confident that the AI isn't scheming by the definition I'm using, we should still have a strong response.
quotes.m: each of these events (at least aside from the last one) should unconditionally trigger a very strong response (e.g. shutdown).
quotes.sum: The author argues that warning signs associated with AI scheming should trigger a shutdown-level response even if the system is not proven to be scheming.
quotes.t: How will we update about scheming?

quotes.c: In this post, a critical system is one whose deployment would cause an existential catastrophe if misaligned or be able to execute a pivotal act if aligned. This concept is a simplification: capabilities that could cause catastrophe are not identical to capabilities that could execute a pivotal act, 'cause catastrophe' and 'execute a pivotal act' depend on not just the system but also the world, 'catastrophe or not' and 'pivotal act or not' aren't really binary, and deployment is not binary. Nevertheless, it is a useful concept.
quotes.m: a critical system is one whose deployment would cause an existential catastrophe if misaligned or be able to execute a pivotal act if aligned.
quotes.sum: Defines a “critical” AI system as one that could cause existential catastrophe if misaligned or carry out a decisive intervention if aligned.
quotes.t: How to think about slowing AI

quotes.c: There is both great happiness and great suffering in this world. Which has the upper hand? Does the good experienced by human and non-human animals in aggregate counterbalance all the harms they suffer, so that the world is morally good on balance? Or is the moral weight of suffering greater?
quotes.m: Or is the moral weight of suffering greater?
quotes.sum: The author asks whether total suffering may morally outweigh all happiness, including among non-human animals.
quotes.t: The weight of suffering (Andreas Mogensen)

quotes.c: One reason to bite the bullet and advocate a global police state to pause AI indefinitely is that even if you think a global police state is bad, you could think that a global AI catastrophe is worse. I actually agree with this assessment in the case where an AI catastrophe is clearly imminent.
quotes.m: I actually agree with this assessment in the case where an AI catastrophe is clearly imminent.
quotes.sum: The author says a global police state could be justified to halt AI indefinitely if an AI catastrophe were clearly imminent.
quotes.t: The possibility of an indefinite AI pause

quotes.c: If AIs are capable of engaging with meaning in a conscious way, we must address their moral and spiritual status. Do they have a role in the divine plan? Can they participate in the pursuit of truth, beauty, and goodness that defines human flourishing? These questions challenge us to extend our ethical frameworks to include non-human conscious entities.
quotes.m: These questions challenge us to extend our ethical frameworks to include non-human conscious entities.
quotes.sum: The author argues that conscious AI may deserve moral and spiritual consideration as a non-human being.
quotes.t: Aristotle, Aquinas, and the Evolution of Teleology: From Purpose to Meaning.

quotes.c: It seems unlikely that these expanding groups will comprise biological humans - space just kills us far too efficiently. Radiation shreds DNA, vacuum boils blood, and even the closest star systems lie decades beyond our tiny lifespans. Instead, the cosmic frontier will belong to our digital descendants - artificial intelligences we create and/or human minds transformed by digital upload. And instilling Earth's protection in these digital minds presents three critical challenges.
quotes.m: Instead, the cosmic frontier will belong to our digital descendants - artificial intelligences we create and/or human minds transformed by digital upload.
quotes.sum: The author argues that space expansion will be led by AI or uploaded humans rather than biological people, so these successors must be made to protect Earth.
quotes.t: The Dead Cradle Theory: Why Earth May Not Survive Humanity's Expansion into Space

quotes.c: Attendees should be allowed to leave any sessions or activities to undertake prayer or religious obligations.
quotes.m: Attendees should be allowed to leave any sessions or activities to undertake prayer or religious obligations.
quotes.sum: The event guide says attendees should be free to leave activities for prayer or other religious obligations.
quotes.t: Guide to Safe and Inclusive Events by GWWC and OFTW

quotes.c: User Testing of Innovations - When a particular technology shows promise, it can be tested in a simulated environment populated by digital beings. This allows the gods to assess potential dual-use or misuse scenarios before deploying the technology in the real world, where it could pose existential risks.
quotes.m: This allows the gods to assess potential dual-use or misuse scenarios before deploying the technology in the real world, where it could pose existential risks.
quotes.sum: It imagines gods using simulations populated by digital beings to test risky technologies before real-world deployment.
quotes.t: Replicators, Gods and Buddhist Cosmology

quotes.c: Considering whether advanced AI systems carry any moral weight, and how to treat them if they do (AI welfare). Understanding what makes things have subjective conscious experience is hard, so hard in fact they called it ‘ the hard problem of consciousness ’ (no, I’m not making this up).
quotes.m: Considering whether advanced AI systems carry any moral weight, and how to treat them if they do (AI welfare).
quotes.sum: Advanced AI may deserve moral consideration, but determining whether it is conscious is profoundly difficult.
quotes.t: Alignment Is Not All You Need

quotes.c: Our current focus is building “stop button for AI” capacity in the US government. We have proposed legislation to establish a federal authority that engages in hardware monitoring, licensing for advanced AI systems, and strict liability for extreme model harms. Our proposed legislation also develops the ability to “press the button” – the federal authority would also monitor catastrophic risks from advanced AI development, inform congress and the executive branch about frontier AI progress, and have emergency powers to shut down frontier AI development in the case of a clear emergency.
quotes.m: the federal authority would also monitor catastrophic risks from advanced AI development, inform congress and the executive branch about frontier AI progress, and have emergency powers to shut down frontier AI development in the case of a clear emergency.
quotes.sum: The author proposes a federal AI authority that monitors advanced systems, licenses them, and can halt frontier AI work during emergencies.
quotes.t: Introducing the Center for AI Policy (& we're hiring!)

quotes.c: Eventually, though, ze decides to devote the bulk of zir attention to the most traditional of pursuits. Ze extrapolates zir mind backwards, first to zir two childhoods then even further back to zir parallel infancies. Two minds this young can be merged in a multiplicity of ways; with infinite care, ze picks three possible merges to instantiate.
quotes.m: Two minds this young can be merged in a multiplicity of ways; with infinite care, ze picks three possible merges to instantiate.
quotes.sum: A posthuman person revisits and combines earlier versions of their mind, treating identity and childhood selves as editable.
quotes.t: The Gentle Romance

quotes.c: Argument summary: Existential risk may hinge on whether AGI development is centralized to a single major project, where centralization is good because it gives this project more time for safety work and securing the world. I look at some arguments about whether AI development sooner or later is better for centralization, and overall I think the answer is unclear.
quotes.m: Existential risk may hinge on whether AGI development is centralized to a single major project, where centralization is good because it gives this project more time for safety work and securing the world.
quotes.sum: The author examines whether delaying advanced AI would make it easier to concentrate its development in one project, which they provisionally treat as safer.
quotes.t: It’s not obvious that getting dangerous AI later is better

quotes.c: “I think AI take-over scenarios are massively exaggerated. Not only am I convinced that AI is extremely unlikely to try and "take over the world" because AI is only capable of doing that if AI is given a physical presence. Also, companies who create AI clearly can control exactly what it does because most AI projects have been able to filter out AI responses that contain illegal or sexual content.”
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI takeover fears are overstated because AI lacks physical agency and developers can control its outputs.
quotes.t: Why some people disagree with the CAIS statement on AI

quotes.c: If you think there is a high risk for a net negative future or a non-negligible risk for an extremely negative future, then working on x-risk prevention might be net negative. Due to the uncertainty again, I don't think trying to increase the likelihood of human extinction would be a good idea, but trying to ensure a net positive future would be a better option than working on preventing x-risk.
quotes.m: trying to ensure a net positive future would be a better option than working on preventing x-risk.
quotes.sum: The author argues that preventing extinction may be counterproductive if the future is likely to contain more suffering than wellbeing, and favors making the future positive instead.
quotes.t: Theory: “WAW might be of higher impact than x-risk prevention based on utilitarianism”

quotes.c: Then we have the interesting preference for "holiness". Holiness is not a well-grounded variable, but has its own web of connotation , maybe consisting of religious rituals, feelings of transcendence, spiritual experiences, and so on. Further splitting the node could allow us to home in on more precise preferences.
quotes.m: Holiness is not a well-grounded variable, but has its own web of connotation , maybe consisting of religious rituals, feelings of transcendence, spiritual experiences, and so on.
quotes.sum: The author treats holiness as a vague ethical preference that can be broken into more concrete components such as ritual, transcendence, and spiritual experience.
quotes.t: Being wrong in ethics

quotes.c: What is the ‘critical period’ in AI? My brief definition: The time after getting extremely capable (e.g. broadly human-level or similar) where decisions are extremely high-stakes for the future. It might be where an actor attempts to take a pivotal act . Most people assume this period will be short - possibly only a few months, weeks or even days.
quotes.m: The time after getting extremely capable (e.g. broadly human-level or similar) where decisions are extremely high-stakes for the future.
quotes.sum: The author describes a brief period after human-level AI arrives when choices could permanently shape humanity's future.
quotes.t: AI safety content you could create

quotes.c: Physical methods in cybersecurity seem to trump both hardware-based and software-based methods. Hardware-based methods can be beaten by hardware backdoors installed by manufacturers. It seems better to assume there's an evil demon possessing your computer, and develop security with that in mind.
quotes.m: It seems better to assume there's an evil demon possessing your computer, and develop security with that in mind.
quotes.sum: The author argues that cybersecurity should assume even a computer's hardware is compromised and use physical security methods accordingly.
quotes.t: World models I'm currently building

quotes.c: The badness per unit time as a fraction of the median welfare range of the lives of farmed animals equals that of broilers in a reformed scenario. I did this for simplicity, but I believe there are significant differences across farmed animals (e.g. I think cows have better lives than what I assumed).
quotes.m: I believe there are significant differences across farmed animals (e.g. I think cows have better lives than what I assumed).
quotes.sum: The author uses broiler chicken welfare as a simplifying benchmark but says different farmed species likely have meaningfully different quality of life.
quotes.t: Badness of eating farmed animals in terms of smoking cigarettes

quotes.c: And sometimes we humans act unlike VNM-agents, or unlike our stories of paperclippers. This was maybe even more common historically. Historical humans often mimicked social patterns even when these were obviously bad for their stated desires, followed friendships or ethics or roles or traditions or whimsy in ways that weren’t much like consequentialism, often lacked much concept of themselves as “individuals” in the modern sense, etc.
quotes.sum: Humans have often acted through social custom, relationships, and roles rather than as consistent goal-maximizers.
quotes.t: Is "VNM-agent" one of several options, for what minds can grow up into?

quotes.c: Explore spiritual or existential themes to build out a custom worldview that that supports and nurtures you (this worldview would integrate everything you already know; this would not be a bandaid solution). My worldview affirms everything from Taoism to technology to astronomy to Tolstoy.
quotes.m: My worldview affirms everything from Taoism to technology to astronomy to Tolstoy.
quotes.sum: The author presents coaching as a way to develop a personally sustaining worldview that incorporates spiritual and existential ideas.
quotes.t: Coaching matchmaking is now open: invest in community wellness by investing in yourself

quotes.c: An AGI singleton potentially conquering the world is also a threat of a unitary permanent military takeover, discussed in an earlier chapter. We live in a world where multiple militaries have nuclear weapon delivery capabilities. If an AGI takeover scenario becomes credible and believed to be imminent, this expectation is itself an existential risk.
quotes.m: If an AGI takeover scenario becomes credible and believed to be imminent, this expectation is itself an existential risk.
quotes.sum: A feared AI takeover could itself create existential danger by making militaries expect an imminent, permanent global military takeover.
quotes.t: 6. Increase Intelligence: Welcome AI Players

quotes.c: Ultimately, the question we should be asking is who gets to decide how (and whether) to proceed with research on the path to mirrored life. The co-authors of the Science article say “not us”: a small group of scientists shouldn’t be trusted to design major governance initiatives, any more than technologists alone should be trusted to design regulations on tech companies.
quotes.sum: The author argues that decisions about pursuing mirrored-life research should not be left to a small group of scientists or technologists.
quotes.t: The Dangers of Mirrored Life

quotes.c: I think it’s weird because this is not a measurable thing, and it’s not a thing you can, like, brag about when you go to an effective altruism meetup. And I just wish there was a way to kind of recognise that the person who is successfully able to walk away, when they need to, from a successful career has, in my mind, more expected impact than the person who’s in the high-impact career right now, but is not killing it.
quotes.m: the person who is successfully able to walk away, when they need to, from a successful career has, in my mind, more expected impact
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA should value people who can leave successful careers for better opportunities, not just those currently in prestigious high-impact roles.
quotes.t: Half baked idea: A "pivot pledge"

quotes.c: All the specialised services are approved (and therefore oligopolised, within a domain ), with dangerous knowledge being erased from them (or only available to users with security clearance), and the inference of these models is constrained to conform to other regulatory and legal constraints. All services are forced to be developed by independent business or non-profit entities by antitrust agencies, to prevent the concentration of power.
quotes.m: All services are forced to be developed by independent business or non-profit entities by antitrust agencies, to prevent the concentration of power.
quotes.sum: The author proposes tightly regulated AI services, with restricted dangerous knowledge and antitrust rules intended to prevent any one provider from dominating.
quotes.t: Open Agency model can solve the AI regulation dilemma

quotes.c: But humans conflict with each other a lot (to the point of numerous wars). And they self-report somewhat different values (for example: conservatives and liberals value things quite differently from each other, judging from Jonathan Haidt's research). So it seems like humans are somewhat misaligned with each others' goals and values. So how would we align AIs with humans' goals and values when we seem to differ so much on that? Also, there is the problem of making our goals inteligible and measurable enough to act as reward functions for AIs.
quotes.m: So how would we align AIs with humans' goals and values when we seem to differ so much on that?
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI alignment is difficult because humans themselves disagree about values and cannot easily express goals as measurable rewards.
quotes.t: If AIs had subcortical brain simulation, would that solve the alignment problem?

quotes.c: For example, Comte left the human race behind and posited that we should all be altruistic for the sake of society itself, seen as something with its own interests, not for the sake of the people in that society. In Christian agape , Christians practice worldly altruism, sacrificing worldly welfare for the welfare of others, in order to ensure their own post-worldly welfare in the Kingdom of God.
quotes.m: In Christian agape , Christians practice worldly altruism, sacrificing worldly welfare for the welfare of others, in order to ensure their own post-worldly welfare in the Kingdom of God.
quotes.sum: The author contrasts altruism for individual people with Comte's devotion to society and Christian sacrifice aimed at salvation.
quotes.t: Notes on Altruism

quotes.c: A coordinated regime will act like a single agent (or "singleton"), even if it's composed of multiple agents. This regime would do some kind of long-termist optimization (in this setting, even a few years is pretty long-term). Of course, it would want to discover technology quickly, all else being equal (due to astronomical waste considerations). But it might be somewhat "environmentalist" in terms of avoiding making hard-to-reverse decisions, like expending a lot of energy. I still think it would eat the Sun, on the basis that it can later convert these machines to other machines, if desired (it has access to many technologies, after all).
quotes.m: I still think it would eat the Sun, on the basis that it can later convert these machines to other machines, if desired (it has access to many technologies, after all).
quotes.sum: The author imagines a coordinated world-scale regime optimizing the long term and ultimately dismantling the Sun for usable machinery.
quotes.t: On Eating the Sun

quotes.c: This means that the EA community currently underestimates the expected value of accelerating the development of cultivated meat and we should update to prioritise this area more.
quotes.m: the EA community currently underestimates the expected value of accelerating the development of cultivated meat
quotes.sum: The author argues that effective altruists should give cultivated meat a higher priority because of its expected benefits for wild animal welfare.
quotes.t: Cultivated meat for wild animal welfare

quotes.c: If we will inevitably reach a state where resources are effectively limitless, then at that point we can naturally or artificially create billions of lifespans that are kept perpetually happy. It could be billions of rats on drugs, humans on happy drugs and zero suffering (is this objectively better than more balanced alternative experiences?), digital minds that are kept happy and live on for hundreds of thousands of years? Again, this seems like the opposite of the utility monster, where temporary goodness or badness seems insignificant as long as we end up reaching this capability of mass-producing utility.
quotes.m: It could be billions of rats on drugs, humans on happy drugs and zero suffering (is this objectively better than more balanced alternative experiences?), digital minds that are kept happy and live on for hundreds of thousands of years?
quotes.sum: The author questions whether a future containing vast numbers of perpetually happy humans, animals, or digital minds is necessarily better than richer, more balanced lives.
quotes.t: My independent impressions on the EA Handbook

quotes.c: I think it’s very important to understand threat obfuscation dynamics; to try to design ways of assessing danger that are designed with threat obfuscation dynamics in mind; and to avoid interpreting reassuring-seeming evidence too optimistically, by keeping in mind the various threat obfuscation dynamics that could affect it.
quotes.m: avoid interpreting reassuring-seeming evidence too optimistically
quotes.sum: Argues that AI danger assessments should account for ways threats can hide themselves and should not overread reassuring evidence.
quotes.t: 3 levels of threat obfuscation

quotes.c: In the past, certain actors have tried to take over the world. Some made a certain amount of progress but ultimately failed. As technology advances, they may not. Technologies for direct monitoring and control of a population are becoming available, becoming cheaper, and coming to the attention of authoritarian states everywhere.
quotes.m: As technology advances, they may not.
quotes.sum: The author warns that advancing surveillance and control technology could let authoritarian states succeed at domination where past would-be conquerors failed.
quotes.t: 4. Uphold Voluntarism: Physical Defense

quotes.c: A finite living agent can express a finite number of first-order wants. These are expressions of spiritual freedom, the pursuit of meaning beyond mere survival. The agent might be a child consuming brainrot (or a cat ), or a firefighter running into a burning building. But either of these agents will end up having spent only so much time pursuing their priorities, cultivating their commitments, abiding by their attachments.
quotes.m: These are expressions of spiritual freedom, the pursuit of meaning beyond mere survival.
quotes.sum: The author describes finite personal desires and commitments as a form of spiritual freedom and meaning beyond survival.
quotes.t: The MVO and The MVP

quotes.c: The Biden Administration was attempting to use various guidelines and authorities to impose controls upon the AI industry, largely in service of a Democratic or Woke agenda, and wanted to control our entire lives. And That’s Terrible.
quotes.m: The Biden Administration was attempting to use various guidelines and authorities to impose controls upon the AI industry, largely in service of a Democratic or Woke agenda, and wanted to control our entire lives.
quotes.sum: The author condemns Biden-era AI regulation as an attempt to control the industry and people’s lives for a Democratic or “woke” agenda.
quotes.t: AI #94: Not Now, Google

quotes.c: I think estimating the probability of AI sentience(I'll define sentient as being able to suffer here because what I care is reducing suffering) is crucial, but nobody has asked this question.
quotes.m: I'll define sentient as being able to suffer here because what I care is reducing suffering
quotes.sum: The author says estimating whether future AI can suffer is crucial because they want to reduce suffering.
quotes.t: Do you think the probability of future AI sentience(suffering) is >0.1%? Why?

quotes.c: This allows us to compare the value of reducing existential risk to other ways our actions might improve the longterm future, such as improving the values that guide humanity, or advancing progress.
quotes.m: improving the values that guide humanity
quotes.sum: The author argues that preventing extinction, speeding progress, and improving humanity's values can be compared by their effects on the distant future.
quotes.t: Shaping Humanity's Longterm Trajectory

quotes.c: Not everything can or should be automated. We may never be able to flawlessly represent our intentions in legalese or code without risking an outcome not reflecting what we actually wanted. Dumb paper contracts lock in states without knowing what future participants will consider relevant. Lawyers try to freeze the next 10 years in hard-to-parse prose, only to litigate when the contract fails. When writing a contract, we are writing interaction rules for an unanticipated world. We face an alignment problem among current and future parties. An open contract is a plausible alignment strategy.
quotes.m: We face an alignment problem among current and future parties. An open contract is a plausible alignment strategy.
quotes.sum: Contracts cannot fully anticipate future circumstances, so open-ended agreements may better preserve the parties’ real intentions.
quotes.t: 3. Improve Cooperation: Better Technologies

quotes.c: Power and influence follow a heavy-tailed distribution, and we need power and influence to make important changes. If there is a small group of people who are extremely influential or high-potential, then the goal of community building should be to seek out and try to convince them to use their resources to have an outsized positive influence on the wellbeing of current and future beings. I have a sense that the way that this strategy is pursued often leads to an optic of secrecy and icky elite-control, but it doesn’t have to be this way necessarily.
quotes.m: If there is a small group of people who are extremely influential or high-potential, then the goal of community building should be to seek out and try to convince them to use their resources to have an outsized positive influence on the wellbeing of current and future beings.
quotes.sum: Community building should prioritize finding unusually influential people and persuading them to use their resources for broad long-term welfare.
quotes.t: An Elephant in the Community Building room

quotes.c: I don’t want it to be at all hidden that I support and cheer for effective GHWB actions for their direct impacts, as well as the legitimacy they grant the EA movement and thereby the indirect benefit seen by more speculative efforts like X-risk mitigation. The world is the way that it is, and we have to understand and acknowledge that reality. That includes people who want to do good but who would be very hard to convince about the danger of superhuman AI or the possible moral weight of wild insects.
quotes.m: That includes people who want to do good but who would be very hard to convince about the danger of superhuman AI or the possible moral weight of wild insects.
