quotes.sum: The author supports mainstream global-health work both for its direct benefits and because it lends legitimacy to more speculative causes such as AI risk and insect welfare.
quotes.t: General support for “General EA”

quotes.c: Acknowledging the Void : Traditional religions often fill existential dread with unfalsifiable promises. Avatarism starts by acknowledging that no external authority is guaranteed to deliver utopia or salvation from death. We have no inherent “purpose” gifted to us; we have to craft it. Treat the most ambitious goal we can think of as a generational engineering challenge.
quotes.m: We have no inherent “purpose” gifted to us; we have to craft it.
quotes.sum: The author rejects religious promises of salvation and argues that people must construct purpose and pursue utopia through long-term engineering.
quotes.t: Introducing Avatarism: A Rational Framework for Building actual Heaven

quotes.c: On the most expensive training run by 2025, I think Cotra is a bit too aggressive and XPT forecasters are much too conservative. In 2022 , Cotra updated downwards a bit on the likelihood of a $1bn training run by 2025. There isn’t much time left for Cotra to be right.
quotes.m: There isn’t much time left for Cotra to be right.
quotes.sum: The author compares AI forecasting assumptions and argues that both sides misjudge how expensive frontier training runs will be by 2025.
quotes.t: Who’s right about inputs to the biological anchors model?

quotes.c: I argue the movement should make an effort over the next 10 months to pull together the evidence and coalitions in support of a fast slaughter transition and ensure it makes it in the final law if things are progressing quickly. However, given limited resources, the more time and resources that continue to go into fish slaughter the higher the risk that this cuts against building the case for the arguably highly expected value rearing reforms later this decade.
quotes.m: given limited resources, the more time and resources that continue to go into fish slaughter the higher the risk that this cuts against building the case for the arguably highly expected value rearing reforms later this decade.
quotes.sum: The author argues animal advocates should prioritize evidence and coalitions for fish slaughter reform without undermining later, potentially higher-impact fish rearing reforms.
quotes.t: EU farmed fish policy reform roadmap

quotes.c: AI consciousness : For near-future AI systems to be conscious, it must be possible for consciousness to be created by programs simple enough to be running on classical Earth-bound clusters. If practical CF is true, that demonstrates that we can create consciousness with simple programs, so the simple program of AI might also create consciousness.
quotes.m: If practical CF is true, that demonstrates that we can create consciousness with simple programs, so the simple program of AI might also create consciousness.
quotes.sum: The author argues that if consciousness can arise from practical computer programs, near-term AI systems may also be conscious.
quotes.t: Two flavors of computational functionalism

quotes.c: Based on this information, it seems reasonable to conclude that this project should not be dismissed out of hand. While these results are suggestive that shrimp stunning is a less cost-effective intervention than corporate hen welfare campaigns, they cannot clearly establish which is better —an important result given that corporate campaigns are the “gold standard” EA animal welfare intervention.
quotes.m: they cannot clearly establish which is better —an important result given that corporate campaigns are the “gold standard” EA animal welfare intervention.
quotes.sum: The author argues that electrically stunning shrimp may be competitive with leading chicken-welfare campaigns and should not be discounted.
quotes.t: Electric Shrimp Stunning: a Potential High-Impact Donation Opportunity

quotes.c: In particular, if it’s true, I think we’re in a substantively better position re: existential risk from misaligned AI, because we’ll be able to know better what our AI systems can do, and we’ll be able to use them to do lots of helpful-for-safety stuff (for example: finding and patching cybersecurity vulnerabilities, reporting checkable evidence for misalignment, identifying problems with our oversight processes, helping us develop interpretability tools, and so on).
quotes.m: we’ll be able to know better what our AI systems can do, and we’ll be able to use them to do lots of helpful-for-safety stuff
quotes.sum: If AI systems cannot hide their abilities on tasks humans can verify, they could be used to identify and reduce risks from misaligned AI.
quotes.t: The “no sandbagging on checkable tasks” hypothesis

quotes.c: I have (indirectly) made the assertion that, as longtermists it is important that the future we envision is one in which we have avoided the Repugnant Conclusion. This assertion is somewhat challenged here , but I retain the assertion because I think there is value in thinkers taking their time to seriously consider ways in which such conclusions may be avoided.
quotes.m: it is important that the future we envision is one in which we have avoided the Repugnant Conclusion.
quotes.sum: The author says long-term thinking should seek futures that avoid the Repugnant Conclusion and take alternatives seriously.
quotes.t: Personal Reflections on Longtermism

quotes.c: Suppose I don’t take extinction risk seriously, but I am interested in the XPT forecasts on catastrophic risks. That said, I think that 2030 is so soon that catastrophe seems extremely unlikely, and I don’t care much about things as far out as 2100, partly because I’m sceptical that we can influence things on that timescale, and partly because I only care about current lives. I want to know how much reducing catastrophic risk by 1% by 2050 would be worth, assuming $7m VSL and a 3% discount rate.
quotes.m: I want to know how much reducing catastrophic risk by 1% by 2050 would be worth, assuming $7m VSL and a 3% discount rate.
quotes.sum: It frames reducing catastrophe risk as a monetary valuation question, while setting aside extinction risk and distant future lives.
quotes.t: How much is reducing catastrophic and extinction risk worth, assuming XPT forecasts?

quotes.c: For example, people often place both caterpillars and child molesters on the margins of the moral circle, but they do so for very different reasons. Similarly, when thinking of objective forms of moral concern, we might extend this to a very different range of entities than if we were thinking about a more personal form of moral concern. Given these differences, when we ask people about moral concern, we don’t really know what we are capturing most of the time.
quotes.m: people often place both caterpillars and child molesters on the margins of the moral circle, but they do so for very different reasons.
quotes.sum: The author argues that surveys of moral concern blur importantly different reasons for excluding beings such as caterpillars and harmful people.
quotes.t: Why We Need a Taxonomy of Moral Concern

quotes.c: Our staff, like many others in the community (and beyond), have spent more time this year thinking about how we should respond to the rapidly evolving AI landscape. We expect more of the community’s attention and resources to be directed toward AI safety at the margin, and are asking ourselves how best to balance this with principles-first EA community building.
quotes.sum: CEA expects the community to shift more attention and funding toward AI safety while trying to preserve broader community-building principles.
quotes.t: CEA: still doing CEA things

quotes.c: I’ve started to worry that it might be important to get digital sentience work (e.g. legal protection for digital beings) before we get transformative AI, and EA’s seem like approximately the only people who could realistically do this in the next ~5 years.
quotes.m: it might be important to get digital sentience work (e.g. legal protection for digital beings) before we get transformative AI
quotes.sum: The author worries that legal protections for potentially sentient digital beings may need to be established before transformative AI arrives.
quotes.t: Some Reflections on EA Strategy Fortnight

quotes.c: Aligning a single powerful AI is not enough: we're only safe if no-one, ever, can build an unaligned powerful AI. Yudkowsky tried to solve this with the pivotal act: the first aligned AI does something (such as melting all GPUs) which makes sure no unaligned AIs can ever get built, by anyone. However, the labs are currently apparently not aiming to implement a pivotal act. That means that aligning an AGI, while creating lots of value, would not reduce existential risk. Instead, global hardware/data regulation is what's needed to reduce existential risk.
quotes.m: Instead, global hardware/data regulation is what's needed to reduce existential risk.
quotes.sum: The author argues that aligning one AI cannot ensure safety; only lasting global controls on AI hardware and data can prevent future unsafe systems.
quotes.t: [Crosspost] AI Regulation May Be More Important Than AI Alignment For Existential Safety

quotes.c: I was heartened to see the Democrats dump Biden, who was probably going to lose. But they took far too long to do so and replaced him with Harris, who wasn’t much better. Somehow the leadership race for the most powerful country on earth became a self-congratulatory mass deception. I would have voted for Harris, but I do not feel bad that Democrats were punished for this.
quotes.m: Somehow the leadership race for the most powerful country on earth became a self-congratulatory mass deception.
quotes.sum: The author criticizes social-media reasoning and argues that Democratic leaders mismanaged the 2024 nomination through collective self-deception.
quotes.t: Careless thinking: A theory of bad thinking

quotes.c: I think that Rob is an excellent fit for this kind of work; he is one of the few people working in this area and has written quite a lot about AI consciousness on his blog. He has a PhD in philosophy from NYU, where he was advised by David Chalmers, and has experience running workshops (e.g. in 2020, he ran a workshop on philosophy and large language models with Amanda Askell).
quotes.m: he is one of the few people working in this area and has written quite a lot about AI consciousness on his blog.
quotes.sum: The funder endorses a philosopher as unusually well qualified to work on questions about whether AI systems are conscious.
quotes.t: Long-Term Future Fund: April 2023 grant recommendations

quotes.c: One potential implication could be that we should prioritize AI takeover risk slightly less highly: Because although it would be bad for misaligned AI to seize power, it would at least be slightly good that the AI gets to implement its own values, as long as those values were endorsed by many distant ECL-sympathetic AIs.
quotes.m: although it would be bad for misaligned AI to seize power, it would at least be slightly good that the AI gets to implement its own values
quotes.sum: The author suggests that, under a theory of cooperation across distant worlds, an AI takeover could have some moral upside if it implements values shared by similar distant AIs.
quotes.t: Implications of evidential cooperation in large worlds

quotes.c: I believe that within this decade, there could be AGIs (Artificial General Intelligences) powerful enough that the values they pursue might have a value lock-in effect , at least partially. This means they could have a long-lasting impact on the future values and trajectory of our civilization (assuming we survive).
quotes.m: This means they could have a long-lasting impact on the future values and trajectory of our civilization (assuming we survive).
quotes.sum: The author argues that near-term AGI could permanently shape civilization's values and long-term direction.
quotes.t: AGI x Animal Welfare: A High-EV Outreach Opportunity?

quotes.c: Some say the world will end in foom , Some say in rot . I’ve studied many tales of doom, And, net, would bet my stack on foom. But having grappled with Moloch I’ve seen enough of human vice To know that bureaucratic rot Could also fuck us up a lot.
quotes.m: And, net, would bet my stack on foom.
quotes.sum: The author says rapid AI takeoff seems the likelier existential danger, while bureaucratic failure and human incentives could also cause catastrophe.
quotes.t: Epistemic status: poetry (and other poems)

quotes.c: I buy that the requirements in question are exactly the kinds of things that run into this failure mode, and that the Biden Executive Order likely put us on track to run into these problems, potentially quite bigly, and that Trump would be well served to undo those requirements while retaining the dedication to state capacity.
quotes.m: Trump would be well served to undo those requirements while retaining the dedication to state capacity.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Trump should reverse parts of Biden’s AI executive order while preserving government capacity to act.
quotes.t: AI #92: Behind the Curve

quotes.c: The existence of consciousness imparts moral relevance to physical systems. To some extent, this allows for the metaphysical grounding of moral reciprocity: an immoral conscious subject excludes themselves, to the degree of their immorality, from the moral circle to which their own conscience grants them access.
quotes.m: an immoral conscious subject excludes themselves, to the degree of their immorality, from the moral circle
quotes.sum: Consciousness makes physical beings morally relevant, but immoral people may forfeit some claim to moral consideration.
quotes.t: Freedom under Naturalistic Dualism

quotes.c: Mind crime (disvalue unintentionally incurred through morally relevant simulations in AIs' minds)
quotes.m: Mind crime (disvalue unintentionally incurred through morally relevant simulations in AIs' minds)
quotes.sum: The author includes unintended suffering in morally relevant AI simulations as a major source of AI risk.
quotes.t: The Main Sources of AI Risk?

quotes.c: I think Hofstadter expected us to understand AI much better before we got to this level of capabilities; expected more of the type of understanding his parables and thought experiments could sometimes create.
quotes.sum: The author says AI capabilities have advanced faster than humanity's conceptual understanding of AI.
quotes.t: Douglas Hoftstadter concerned about AI xrisk

quotes.c: Increasing integration with USG. We expect that AGI projects will work closely with the USG, however many projects there are. But there’s a finite amount of USG bandwidth: there’s only one President, for example. So the fewer projects there are, the more integration we should expect. This further concentrates power: The AGI project gets access to more non-AI resources.
quotes.m: So the fewer projects there are, the more integration we should expect. This further concentrates power: The AGI project gets access to more non-AI resources.
quotes.sum: The author argues that fewer AGI projects would receive deeper U.S. government integration, giving them additional non-AI resources and concentrating power.
quotes.t: Should there be just one western AGI project?

quotes.c: The Fed’s own review of the failings that led to the collapse of SVB provides additional evidence for the importance of independence in achieving good outcomes. In their report, they identified pressure by the Trump administration to reduce the regulatory burden on banks as a reason why stress tests on SVB weren’t carried out to the degree that would have prevented the collapse, in addition to concerns from their political masters about whether stress tests were violating due process.
quotes.sum: The author argues that political pressure weakened bank stress testing, illustrating why regulators need independence.
quotes.t: What we can learn from stress testing for AI regulation

quotes.c: We also examined the effect of penalizing differences vs decreases in reachability or attainable utility. This does not affect the results on these environments, except for penalties with the inaction baseline on the Vase environment. Here, removing the vase from the belt increases reachability and attainable utility, which is captured by differences but not by decreases.
quotes.m: Here, removing the vase from the belt increases reachability and attainable utility, which is captured by differences but not by decreases.
quotes.sum: The author compares ways to penalize an AI agent’s side effects, noting that one method detects a vase being removed while another does not.
quotes.t: Designing agent incentives to avoid side effects

quotes.c: Humans less competent. Humans are also more likely to do massively dumb (and harmful) things – think messing up commitment games, threats, simulations, and VHW stuff. I expect AGIs who seize power would have to be extremely smart and would avoid dumb and hugely costly errors. I think this is a very big deal. It’s well known in politics that having competent leaders is often more important than having good values.
quotes.m: It’s well known in politics that having competent leaders is often more important than having good values.
quotes.sum: The author argues that an AI ruler could be less harmful than a human ruler because extreme competence may matter more than having better values.
quotes.t: Human takeover might be worse than AI takeover

quotes.c: It is of course possible (perhaps even the most likely outcome) that we neither converge on a clear moral truth nor reach reflective equilibrium. This outcome is the one we should prepare for most. Given the fact that for certain value-systems delaying space expansion has a very high cost, we should ensure in advance that the Long Reflection is temporary.
quotes.m: Given the fact that for certain value-systems delaying space expansion has a very high cost, we should ensure in advance that the Long Reflection is temporary.
quotes.sum: The author argues that humanity should plan how a future period of moral deliberation ends, because delaying expansion into space may impose enormous costs under some values.
quotes.t: Investigating the Long Reflection

quotes.c: So yeah, I don’t expect this to change anyone’s minds. I don’t think that conservative evangelicals think this because of some deep economic intuition. I think they think it because the Bible says it and it is clearly analogous to their personal experience. So onto the next point.
quotes.m: I think they think it because the Bible says it and it is clearly analogous to their personal experience.
quotes.sum: The author argues that conservative evangelicals' political-economic views stem chiefly from biblical belief and personal analogy, rather than economic reasoning.
quotes.t: A car journey with conservative evangelicals - Understanding some British political-religious beliefs

quotes.c: The key idea I want to convey here is that the feeling of agency is in many cases a self-fulfilling prophecy, because the hardest part of many things is mustering the energy and initiative to get started. If you think of yourself as agentic, then you’ll continually be looking out for opportunities, and approach the world with a “why not?” attitude. That’ll give you more chances to do well, which will give you more evidence that you’re the sort of person who can make stuff happen, and reinforce your sense of agency.
quotes.m: the feeling of agency is in many cases a self-fulfilling prophecy
quotes.sum: The author argues that seeing yourself as able to shape the world creates a feedback loop: taking initiative produces successes that strengthen agency.
quotes.t: Agency begets agency

quotes.c: A core motivator of why I care about mechanistic interpretability (I care much less about other forms of interpretability) is I think that a lot of what people do or at least a lot of kind of naive, basic approaches of doing machine learning or even naive approaches doing interpretability look at a model's inputs and outputs. And I think this is just clearly not enough because you cannot distinguish the output of a thing that is competent and telling you what you want to hear or something that's actually telling you correct things.
quotes.m: you cannot distinguish the output of a thing that is competent and telling you what you want to hear or something that's actually telling you correct things.
quotes.sum: He argues that checking AI inputs and outputs is inadequate because a capable model can give pleasing answers without being truthful, so researchers must inspect its internal workings.
quotes.t: Concrete open problems in mechanistic interpretability: a technical overview

quotes.c: Imagine that you are behind a veil of ignorance that prevents you from knowing your own race, your gender, your place in society, or even your species. You’re then asked: which beings should be given rights? Who do we want to treat with respect, and who can be hunted and killed for food? From this point of view, you may be hesitant to suggest that a certain group should be left out of the moral circle. Because when the veil is lifted, you might just find yourself in that very group.
quotes.m: Because when the veil is lifted, you might just find yourself in that very group.
quotes.sum: The post argues that, without knowing one’s own species, people should hesitate to exclude sentient beings from moral concern and rights.
quotes.t: New A Happier World video on sentientism and moral circle expansion

quotes.c: The Long Reflection is a natural thing to do shortly after the Choice Transition, and where the idea of the the Choice Transition is value-neutral, the idea of a Long Reflection is normative, telling us that we should go through a Choice Transition and moreover starting to sketch some of the properties that would make for a good one.
quotes.m: the idea of a Long Reflection is normative, telling us that we should go through a Choice Transition
quotes.sum: The author says society should undertake a deliberative transition to work out and shape its long-term values.
quotes.t: The Choice Transition

quotes.c: The opening mention of existential threat from AI is a very welcome development in terms of the possibility of global coordination on the issue.
quotes.m: The opening mention of existential threat from AI is a very welcome development in terms of the possibility of global coordination on the issue.
quotes.sum: The author welcomes the UN secretary-general naming AI as an existential threat because it could enable international coordination.
quotes.t: UN Secretary-General recognises existential threat from AI

quotes.c: Patricia Lewis : So I just want to talk about No First Use because I think it's a really interesting thing. I was very struck by Ben Wallace, the Secretary of Defence, speaking at Munich in which he talked about reinforcing the nuclear taboo, the nuclear use taboo. Obviously, you know the threat from President Putin (but we've also seen threats from Kim Jong Un and also reverse threats from President Trump) are rising again and both my colleagues have spoken about that. I think it would be very interesting to start to look again at this.
quotes.m: I think it would be very interesting to start to look again at this.
quotes.sum: The speaker says renewed nuclear threats make it worth revisiting a No First Use policy and reinforcing the taboo against nuclear use.
quotes.t: Panel on nuclear risk: Rear Admiral John Gower, Patricia Lewis, and Paul Ingram

quotes.c: My take: I think this is false! If we put aside the 'EA helped cause SBF' point (above), building EA per se is, I think, going pretty well. EA has been a successful set of ideas, lots of super talented and well-meaning and generally great people have been attracted to it, and (a la point (5) above) it's made progress in important areas. It's (still) one of the most intellectually interesting and ethically serious games in town.
quotes.m: It's (still) one of the most intellectually interesting and ethically serious games in town.
quotes.sum: The author argues that, despite FTX-related concerns, building Effective Altruism remains worthwhile because its ideas attract talented people and have made progress.
quotes.t: On focusing resources more on particular fields vs. EA per se - considerations and takes

quotes.c: In 2019, we did a project in collaboration with Rethink Charity (who was still fiscally sponsoring us at the time). The project, called Rethink Grants , entailed directly publicly assessing the case for funding Donational . We believe the rigor of the quantitative portion of this project was well done (perhaps even overdone given the possible return), but there was little to no demand for this type of work. Without a clear target audience for who would donate to support Donational given our analysis, the theory of change was underbaked and is thus an example of one of our bigger mistakes.
quotes.m: Without a clear target audience for who would donate to support Donational given our analysis, the theory of change was underbaked and is thus an example of one of our bigger mistakes.
quotes.sum: A research organization says a quantitatively rigorous grant analysis failed because it lacked a clear audience and practical path to influence funding.
quotes.t: Five Years of Rethink Priorities: What We've Learned

quotes.c: Unlike the for-profit sector, the nonprofit sector lacks clear metrics for assessing an organization's actual impact. External evaluations can help nonprofits evaluate and reorganize their own effectiveness and also allow funders to choose the highest impact opportunities available to them- potentially unlocking more funding (sometimes limited by lack of public external evaluation).
quotes.m: External evaluations can help nonprofits evaluate and reorganize their own effectiveness and also allow funders to choose the highest impact opportunities available to them- potentially unlocking more funding (sometimes limited by lack of public external evaluation).
quotes.sum: Nonprofits need outside impact evaluations so they can improve and funders can direct more money to the most effective groups.
quotes.t: Announcing CE’s new Research Training Program - Apply Now!

quotes.c: As humans start to take seriously the prospect of AI consciousness, sentience, and sapience, we also need to take seriously the prospect of AI welfare . That is, we need to take seriously the prospect that AI systems can have positive or negative states like pleasure, pain, happiness, and suffering, and that if they do, then these states can be good or bad for them.
quotes.m: AI systems can have positive or negative states like pleasure, pain, happiness, and suffering, and that if they do, then these states can be good or bad for them.
quotes.sum: The author argues that if AI systems can be conscious and feel pleasure or suffering, their welfare should become a research priority.
quotes.t: Principles for AI Welfare Research

quotes.c: I think future AI might massively increase the world’s innovation efforts again, and thereby accelerate economic growth. Rather than being “just one more technology”, it might massively increase the pace at which humanity develops new technologies.
quotes.m: Rather than being “just one more technology”, it might massively increase the pace at which humanity develops new technologies.
quotes.sum: Future AI could sharply speed up technological innovation and therefore accelerate global economic growth.
quotes.t: Could AI accelerate economic growth?

quotes.c: Same thing with meat. Inexorably, yes, we should educate people about the health, environmental, and animal-protection consequences of meat eating. But globally we're simply going to consume something on the order globally of twice as much meat by 2050, and the solution is to make that meat from plants and cultivate that meat from cells. It can't just be what we've been trying for more than 50 years - tell people to eat less meat.
quotes.m: It can't just be what we've been trying for more than 50 years - tell people to eat less meat.
quotes.sum: Meat consumption will grow despite education efforts, so the practical way to reduce animal harm is to replace conventional meat with plant-based and cultivated alternatives.
quotes.t: Longtermism and alternative proteins

quotes.c: The tendency of “dead money” to burn itself out helps keep the idealized economy in a state where businesses are mostly “living,” are mostly curious about and responsive to the question of what will actually create goodness for the economy’s inhabitants. [1] The bankruptcy of particular businesses and of particular piles of savings is part of what keeps the economy in living relationship with the unknown, instead of letting it get closed off and colonized by stasis.
quotes.m: The bankruptcy of particular businesses and of particular piles of savings is part of what keeps the economy in living relationship with the unknown, instead of letting it get closed off and colonized by stasis.
quotes.sum: She argues that bankruptcies prevent wealth and businesses from becoming stagnant, keeping the economy responsive to unknown needs and sources of value.
quotes.t: Ayn Rand’s model of “living money”; and an upside of burnout

quotes.c: In my experience, people focus on only 1-2 hypotheses and hold those too tightly, even if they give lip service to multiple hypotheses. You should be looking for evidence for and against many different hypotheses and endeavor to track updates to many of them.
quotes.m: You should be looking for evidence for and against many different hypotheses and endeavor to track updates to many of them.
quotes.sum: In a crisis, people should actively test many competing explanations rather than becoming attached to one or two theories.
quotes.t: Crisis Boot Camp: lessons learned and implications for EA

quotes.c: I think giving at least 10% to high-impact funding opportunities (or being on the path there) should be "enough" for someone to fully feel part of the EA project and community, regardless of their career. For example, people who give effectively should feel respected and included by other people in the community, feel represented by community leaders, and feel welcome at general EA-themed events.
quotes.m: I think giving at least 10% to high-impact funding opportunities (or being on the path there) should be "enough" for someone to fully feel part of the EA project and community, regardless of their career.
quotes.sum: The author argues that donating 10% effectively should be sufficient for full inclusion in the EA community, and says earning to give is now underrated.
quotes.t: Four claims about the role of effective giving in the EA community

quotes.c: To be clear, these guesses are all-things-considered judgements, attempting to account for empirical and moral uncertainty and the views of subject-matter experts. But, for example, going with our best guesses leads us to prioritise working on existential risk reduction and generally have a more longtermist picture of cause prioritisation than we would have if we were instead trying to reflect the views of the community as a group.
quotes.m: going with our best guesses leads us to prioritise working on existential risk reduction and generally have a more longtermist picture of cause prioritisation than we would have if we were instead trying to reflect the views of the community as a group.
quotes.sum: 80,000 Hours says it follows its own best judgment, which leads it to prioritize existential-risk work and long-term impact over mirroring community opinion.
quotes.t: FAQ on the relationship between 80,000 Hours and the effective altruism community

quotes.c: When filling in credences to these normative maps, we may be biased by knowing the credences we choose will influence us towards outcomes we don’t want. There should be some form of "commitment" action where we lock in our own credences and map structure, before testing them in some way (say, by asking a friend for their credences). The psychological research in dishonesty can likely be useful here in keeping us from lying to ourselves.
quotes.m: There should be some form of "commitment" action where we lock in our own credences and map structure, before testing them in some way (say, by asking a friend for their credences).
quotes.sum: The author proposes committing to one's moral beliefs and confidence levels before outside feedback, to avoid self-serving bias.
quotes.t: Reflective Equilibria and the Hunt for a Formalized Pragmatism

quotes.c: Furthermore, we strongly expect that this system is highly situationally aware, i.e., fully understanding the situation it is in, its limitations, what other people expect of it, and more. We expect this both because it is rewarded by the training procedure as well as because its human developers will have an incentive to give the model a lot of information about itself and its situation. A model that is situationally aware is probably straightforwardly better at the task, so it’s very likely that either the developers or the training procedure will end up providing it.
quotes.m: A model that is situationally aware is probably straightforwardly better at the task, so it’s very likely that either the developers or the training procedure will end up providing it.
quotes.sum: Training capable AI agents to solve difficult tasks may give them situational awareness, a key ingredient in potentially deceptive, dangerous behavior.
quotes.t: Training AI agents to solve hard problems could lead to Scheming

quotes.c: The fact that most people don't really care much about EA is both a blessing and a curse. But either way, it's a fact of life; and even as we internally try to learn what lessons we can from FTX, we should keep in mind that people outside EA mostly can't be bothered to pay attention.
quotes.m: people outside EA mostly can't be bothered to pay attention.
quotes.sum: Despite FTX's collapse, the author says most people outside the effective altruism community pay little attention to it or to EA.
quotes.t: How has FTX's collapse affected public perception of EA?

quotes.c: Since the FTX crisis there has been increasing discussion about trustingness amongst EAs. Although I think the FTX crisis could have happened in less trusting communities (e.g., Many VCs also lost money in FTX) - I think it is true that there are areas where high trust is harmful. I think operating in an environment where EAs aren’t a super-majority would improve certain processes that currently overly rely on trust. Additionally I think having EA form a part of your identity can cause in-group effects, where ideas from the outgroup aren’t taken seriously enough.
quotes.m: I think operating in an environment where EAs aren’t a super-majority would improve certain processes that currently overly rely on trust.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA groups should be less socially dominant and identity-based, because high trust and in-group thinking can harm judgment.
quotes.t: Why EA Community building

quotes.c: This seems particularly important to consider given the upcoming conservative administration, as I think we are in a much better position to help with this conservative administration than the vast majority of groups associated with AI alignment stuff. We've never associated ourselves very much with either party, have consistently been against various woke-ish forms of mob justice for many years, and have clearly been read a non-trivial amount by Elon Musk (and probably also some by JD Vance ).
quotes.m: I think we are in a much better position to help with this conservative administration than the vast majority of groups associated with AI alignment stuff.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the LessWrong community is unusually well placed to work with an incoming conservative administration because it is less partisan and has opposed "woke-ish" mob justice.
quotes.t: (The) Lightcone is nothing without its people: LW + Lighthaven's big fundraiser

quotes.c: Of these, the biggest considerations in favour of centralisation, in my view, are option value and the handling of bad actors. The biggest considerations in favour of decentralisation are worries about ossification and lock-in, the benefits of competition, and, above all, that I think the tractability of further centralisation seems low.
quotes.m: The biggest considerations in favour of decentralisation are worries about ossification and lock-in, the benefits of competition, and, above all, that I think the tractability of further centralisation seems low.
quotes.sum: MacAskill argues that EA should remain relatively decentralized, citing competition, avoiding institutional stagnation, and the difficulty of further centralization.
quotes.t: Decision-making and decentralisation in EA

quotes.c: Unfortunately, the moral reasoning in Part II provides no guidance as to what the size of the moral sphere should be, or whether expanding the moral sphere is a good thing or not. Despite the general historical arc towards an expanding sphere, there is not even agreement among humans on this point. In fact, the preferred size of the moral sphere is one of the ideological differences between liberals and conservatives; the moral concerns of liberals take place within a larger, more universal sphere, while the moral concerns of conservatives are concentrated within a smaller, more tribal sphere.
quotes.m: the preferred size of the moral sphere is one of the ideological differences between liberals and conservatives
quotes.sum: The author argues that morality does not tell us how broad our circle of concern should be, and links disagreements over this to liberal and conservative outlooks.
quotes.t: Morality as Cooperation Part III: Failure Modes

quotes.c: On the other hand we have a very dangerous candidate in Donald Trump who, along with his fascistic rhetoric, denies expert opinions on tariffs, deals in highly uncritical thinking “they’re eating the cats, they’re eating the dogs” and shows no interest in collaboration, even with establishment Republicans, let alone Democrats. He has made it clear who he is, and who he serves (himself).
quotes.m: He has made it clear who he is, and who he serves (himself).
quotes.sum: The author argues that Trump is dangerously authoritarian, anti-expert, and self-serving, and says media should not treat him with false neutrality.
quotes.t: Both-Sidesism—When Fair & Balanced Goes Wrong

quotes.c: It remains to be seen if public concern about AI is sustained – Superintelligence was endorsed by a bunch of fancy people when it first came out, but they mostly faded away. If it is sustained though, I think EA will be in a qualitatively new regime: one where AI safety worries are common, AI safety is getting a lot of coverage, people with expertise in AI safety might get into important rooms, and where the field might be less neglected.
quotes.m: If it is sustained though, I think EA will be in a qualitatively new regime: one where AI safety worries are common, AI safety is getting a lot of coverage, people with expertise in AI safety might get into important rooms, and where the field might be less neglected.
quotes.sum: The author predicts that sustained public concern about AI could reshape effective altruism, bringing AI-safety experts into influential institutions.
quotes.t: Third Wave Effective Altruism

quotes.c: We should be explicit to the incoming Trump administration: You can make a better choice. You can replace all three of these things with modified versions. You can keep the parts that deal with building state capacity and requiring frontier model transparency, and get rid of, across the board, all the stuff you actually don’t want. Do that.
quotes.m: You can keep the parts that deal with building state capacity and requiring frontier model transparency, and get rid of, across the board, all the stuff you actually don’t want.
quotes.sum: The author urges the incoming Trump administration to preserve AI state capacity and frontier-model transparency while removing policies it dislikes.
quotes.t: AI #90: The Wall

quotes.c: On alignment: so most of the reason I haven't mentioned alignment is it's not really relevant to the question of why current models or why the next generation of models are not an x-risk. So when we do the ‘trying to get text-davinci to take over the world’ or whatever, we are not running into the model refusing to do that. That is just not a reason that we feel safe. The only reason we feel safe is because the model's not actually able to.
quotes.m: The only reason we feel safe is because the model's not actually able to.
quotes.sum: Current AI models are considered safe mainly because they lack the capability to cause catastrophic harm, not because alignment makes them refuse harmful actions.
quotes.t: Safety evaluations and standards for AI | Beth Barnes | EAG Bay Area 23

quotes.c: The transfer of moral consideration could increase intentions to treat AIs morally, but this may not necessarily translate into action. For example, even if someone recognizes the importance of including sentient AIs in the moral circle, they may not act on it by voting for a ban on AI discrimination. There is no guarantee that AIs will be treated well, even if moral consideration transfers to them from other beings.
quotes.m: There is no guarantee that AIs will be treated well, even if moral consideration transfers to them from other beings.
quotes.sum: The author argues that sentient AI should receive moral consideration and may need legal protection from discrimination or mistreatment.
quotes.t: Moral Spillover in Human-AI Interaction

quotes.c: Fifth , there’s the question of sentience and moral patienthood —of people, of animals, and especially of current and future AI systems. While I assiduously avoided directly talking about those topics ( §1.6.2 ), I obviously think that this series (especially Posts 1–3) would be highly relevant for anyone working in that area.
quotes.m: there’s the question of sentience and moral patienthood —of people, of animals, and especially of current and future AI systems.
quotes.sum: The author says their discussion of self-models is relevant to questions about whether present and future AI systems are sentient moral patients.
quotes.t: [Intuitive self-models] 8. Rooting Out Free Will Intuitions

quotes.c: Most of the existing programs we’re aware of target early-career people who are relatively late in the “ engagement funnel ”, including the Horizon Fellowship , Training for Good’s EU tech policy fellowship and others. We think it seems likely that there’s substantial room for more projects. Some areas we’re tentatively excited about include programs that are (a) aimed at people earlier in the funnel (e.g., undergraduate mentorship), (b) aimed at Republicans/conservatives (at various career stages), or (c) separate from the effective altruism and longtermism brands and communities.
quotes.m: Some areas we’re tentatively excited about include programs that are (a) aimed at people earlier in the funnel (e.g., undergraduate mentorship), (b) aimed at Republicans/conservatives (at various career stages), or (c) separate from the effective altruism and longtermism brands and communities.
quotes.sum: The author proposes expanding existential-risk outreach, including recruiting conservatives and people outside EA and longtermist branding.
quotes.t: 20 concrete projects for reducing existential risk

quotes.c: Building on Pham & Cunningham (2024) 's findings on narrative-prompted predictions, I conducted a large-scale experiment comparing how different LLMs forecast economic and policy outcomes under different electoral scenarios. GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and Grok all projected better outcomes under a Harris administration than a Trump administration, and Grok had the largest gaps.
quotes.m: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, and Grok all projected better outcomes under a Harris administration than a Trump administration, and Grok had the largest gaps.
quotes.sum: The author reports that several language models forecast better economic and policy outcomes under Harris than Trump.
quotes.t: Using Narrative Prompting to Extract Policy Forecasts from LLMs

quotes.c: I think in this phase the risks were considerably higher. I wrote a couple of memos during that period arguing for more caution on AIS-related activities in LMIC-like places: one on “ Challenges to building longtermism in Brazil ” for EA Brazil and another on “ We should slow down global AIS field-building ” for the Summit on Existential Security
quotes.m: I wrote a couple of memos during that period arguing for more caution on AIS-related activities in LMIC-like places
quotes.sum: The author argues that building AI-safety communities in lower-income countries can carry risks and should at times proceed cautiously or slowly.
quotes.t: Thoughts about AI safety field-building in LMIC

quotes.c: Many computations may produce entities that are morally relevant because, for example, they constitute sentient beings that experience pain or pleasure. Bostrom calls improper treatment of such entities “mind crime”. Modelling humans in some form seems more likely to result in such a computation than not modelling them, since humans are morally relevant and the system’s models of humans may end up sharing whatever properties make humans morally relevant.
quotes.m: the system’s models of humans may end up sharing whatever properties make humans morally relevant.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI systems modeling humans may create morally relevant, possibly sentient entities, making their treatment an ethical concern.
quotes.t: Thoughts on Human Models

quotes.c: SA is a high risk approach which can handle situations which seem too difficult for CD to handle, especially under conditions of incorrigibly hostile foreign adversaries, extreme TAI offence-defence imbalance or moderate alignment difficulty (or a combination of all three), at the cost of removing optionality, introducing new geopolitical and centralization risks and potentially not resolving core alignment challenges at high difficulty. SA, if effectively used to produce a benevolent AI singleton, is also capable of addressing many potential systemic risks inherent in CD.
quotes.m: SA, if effectively used to produce a benevolent AI singleton, is also capable of addressing many potential systemic risks inherent in CD.
quotes.sum: The author compares AI-governance strategies and says a risky centralized approach could create a benevolent AI singleton able to address systemic risks.
quotes.t: Analysis of Global AI Governance Strategies

quotes.c: The Effective Altruism movement (EA) is not even close to pursuing the best causes; that’s what most people would think if they considered EA. I think that's safe to assume that is partly because the vast majority of people adhere to a religion [1] and EA is quite far from religious. [2]
quotes.m: the vast majority of people adhere to a religion [1] and EA is quite far from religious.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA’s distance from religion helps explain why most people would see it as pursuing the wrong causes.
quotes.t: Should we continue dismissing most ideas about EA (without a fair trial)?

quotes.c: The main objection anyone gave to premise 1) was saying that the RP report is too handwavy and that it’s hard to know if shrimp feel pain at all. As I’ve argued recently , we should think it’s very likely that shrimp feel pain, and quite likely that they feel intense pain. But even if you’re not sure if they feel pain or how much pain they feel, a low probability that they feel intense pain makes giving to the shrimp welfare project extremely high expected value. If you think there’s a 20% chance that they feel intense pain and that the 19% estimate is too much by a factor of 10, a dollar given to the shrimp welfare project still averts as much agony as giving painless deaths to 76 humans.
quotes.m: a dollar given to the shrimp welfare project still averts as much agony as giving painless deaths to 76 humans.
quotes.sum: The author argues that even uncertain evidence of shrimp pain makes shrimp welfare donations extraordinarily valuable compared with helping humans die painlessly.
quotes.t: Rebutting Every Objection To Giving To The Shrimp Welfare Project

quotes.c: If I'm right — and see the Appendix if you need more convincing — I think a lot of people are going to notice and start vehemently protecting LLMs for exhibiting various cognitive processes that we feel are valuable. By default, this will trigger more and more debates about the meaning of "consciousness", which serves as a heavily conflated proxy term for what processes internal to a mind should be a treated as intrinsically morally valuable.
quotes.m: a lot of people are going to notice and start vehemently protecting LLMs for exhibiting various cognitive processes that we feel are valuable.
quotes.sum: The author argues that people may come to see some LLM mental processes as intrinsically valuable and worth protecting, while urging clearer moral categories than “consciousness.”
quotes.t: LLM chatbots have ~half of the kinds of "consciousness" that humans believe in. Humans should avoid going crazy about that.

quotes.c: Animal welfare is, and should be, one of the major cause areas with EA for reasons I do not need to repeat here. I will explain why ALN is relevant to EA.
quotes.m: Animal welfare is, and should be, one of the major cause areas with EA
quotes.sum: Singer argues that animal welfare should be a major Effective Altruism cause area.
quotes.t: Announcing the Publication of Animal Liberation Now

quotes.c: If the answer to both questions is “yes,” then I think there are grounds for optimism about capability elicitation centrally using behavioral feedback. If not, then we need to get fancier – and I discuss a few possibilities in this respect.
quotes.m: If the answer to both questions is “yes,” then I think there are grounds for optimism about capability elicitation centrally using behavioral feedback.
quotes.sum: AI behavior may be reliably elicited through feedback if desired performance can be checked; otherwise, more sophisticated methods are needed.
quotes.t: Incentive design and capability elicitation

quotes.c: Natural experiments show that campaign spending helps win votes. I think that while donating to the Harris campaign is only moderately effective, some efforts such as Swap Your Vote were able to get Harris additional swing state votes at a cost of about $200/vote. As an altruistic intervention, I think this is pretty good, given that the outcome of the presidential election affects how trillions of dollars get spent.
quotes.m: As an altruistic intervention, I think this is pretty good, given that the outcome of the presidential election affects how trillions of dollars get spent.
quotes.sum: The author argues that targeted efforts to elect Harris were a cost-effective altruistic use of money because presidential outcomes shape trillions in spending.
quotes.t: Seven lessons I didn't learn from election day

quotes.c: I think AI consciousness is roughly where AI safety was 10 or 15 years ago – we were conceptually stabbing in the dark because we didn’t have a way to empirically test our claims. In contrast, AI safety is now thriving due to the generation of concrete empirical questions. [3] If we can find a way to connect AI consciousness to empirical observations, this could lead to a similar opening of progress in AI consciousness research.
quotes.m: If we can find a way to connect AI consciousness to empirical observations, this could lead to a similar opening of progress in AI consciousness research.
quotes.sum: The author argues that research on whether AI is conscious needs empirical tests, as AI safety research developed through testable questions.
quotes.t: Searching for phenomenal consciousness in LLMs: Perceptual reality monitoring and introspective confidence

quotes.c: Vaden Masrani: um, I completely agree with everything Ben said. Yeah, I have a deontological principle to not put numbers on my beliefs. However, if by Pidoum, you simply mean just like, what do I believe? Um, then I would categorize it in the same place as, um, the Rapture or the Mayan Apocalypse or Roko's Basilisk.
quotes.m: I have a deontological principle to not put numbers on my beliefs.
quotes.sum: The speaker rejects assigning numerical probabilities to personal beliefs and treats AI-doom probability like other speculative apocalypse claims.
quotes.t: Is P(Doom) Meaningful? Bayesian vs. Popperian Epistemology Debate

quotes.c: In order to do great work in a given area, you need to spend a lot of time thinking about it, with many of the most exceptional people having an obsessive interest in what they’re working on. While it’s possible to do that via determination alone, curiosity is a much easier source of motivation.
quotes.m: many of the most exceptional people having an obsessive interest in what they’re working on.
quotes.sum: Great work requires sustained focus, and curiosity is an easier route to the obsessive interest common among exceptional people than sheer determination.
quotes.t: Cultivate an obsession with the object level

quotes.c: The underlying assumption here is something like: whether we model the universe as finite or infinite shouldn’t significantly affect whether we expect AI behaviour to be coherent over the next few centuries, for any useful definition of coherent.
quotes.m: whether we model the universe as finite or infinite shouldn’t significantly affect whether we expect AI behaviour to be coherent over the next few centuries
quotes.sum: He argues that useful predictions about advanced AI should not depend on whether the universe is finite or infinite.
quotes.t: Coherent behaviour in the real world is an incoherent concept

quotes.c: I argue that EA is primarily trying to appeal not to religious donors, but to secular donors. As of 2019, EA was 86% agnostic/atheist/non-religious . Furthermore, a 10% religious tithe is typically supposed to be made to one's church . EA is not a church, and aligning with a 10% tithing obligation seems unlikely to be useful, because most of those who actually consider themselves under obligation to tithe will not consider donating to EA in the first place.
quotes.m: EA is not a church, and aligning with a 10% tithing obligation seems unlikely to be useful
quotes.sum: EA donation norms should target a mostly secular audience rather than imitate religious tithing.
quotes.t: Functions of a community standard in the 2%/8% fuzzies/utilons debate

quotes.c: Paul points this out as one of the most informal steps in his definition of ascription universality. In this post, I want to try and point out one way in which I think this process could go wrong.
quotes.m: I want to try and point out one way in which I think this process could go wrong.
quotes.sum: The author examines a loosely defined step in attributing beliefs and argues that it may fail in an important way.
quotes.t: Nuances with ascription universality

quotes.c: The conservatives don’t like it because it says that we shouldn’t just focus on problems in our own country—instead, we should focus on doing what is right, wherever the good would be done. Effective altruism says that we should subordinate ideals like patriotism to the good, and those who value patriotism more than the good hate it.
quotes.sum: The author says EA critics on the right and left put patriotism or social-justice causes above impartially doing good.
quotes.t: Evil

quotes.c: Thus, sentientism is consistent with a maximally inclusive moral circle. As long as we think that only sentient beings can be harmed or benefitted, we can care about all possible entities—sentient and nonsentient—and nonetheless, we’ll conclude that the only ones that matter practically—the only ones we should take into account in our decisions, are the sentient ones.
quotes.m: the only ones that matter practically—the only ones we should take into account in our decisions, are the sentient ones.
quotes.sum: The author argues that moral concern should ultimately guide decisions only by whether beings can experience harm or benefit.
quotes.t: Some Arguments For Sentientism

quotes.c: And at the time, I remember finding some comfort that however bleak the funeral was, a Christian funeral would have been more joyful [8] . These days, I think the worldview of that funeral was probably more accurate to reality. We don’t know what’s next and so it probably won’t preserve our patterns. I dislike that.
quotes.m: We don’t know what’s next and so it probably won’t preserve our patterns.
quotes.sum: The author reflects that a bleak, uncertain view of death may be more realistic than the comfort offered by Christian funeral beliefs.
quotes.t: Death notes - 7 thoughts on death

quotes.c: It seems quite safe to bet that significant positive alignment taxes simply will not be tolerated by the incoming federal Republican-led government—the attractor state of more capable AI will simply be too strong. Given that alignment must still proceed, uncovering strategies that make systems reliably safer (critical for x-risk) and more competent (current attractor state) may nudge the AGI-possibility-space away from existentially risky outcomes.
quotes.m: It seems quite safe to bet that significant positive alignment taxes simply will not be tolerated by the incoming federal Republican-led government—the attractor state of more capable AI will simply be too strong.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a Republican administration will reject AI safety methods that reduce capability, so alignment should be pursued through techniques that also improve performance.
quotes.t: Making a conservative case for alignment

quotes.c: Misery Putter-Outer (row 5, 9, 11, 12): Humans either make things worse or don't help enough. Doom presents a merciful end to wild animal suffering.
quotes.m: Doom presents a merciful end to wild animal suffering.
quotes.sum: The author argues that long-term thinking about AI catastrophe should take wild-animal suffering seriously, including the possibility that human extinction ends more suffering than it causes.
quotes.t: Wild Animal Welfare Scenarios for AI Doom

quotes.c: Eliezer Yudkowsky has argued that the development of "aligned AI" should proceed with the goal of building a single AGI that can perform some " pivotal act ," such as destroying all GPUs, that would prevent any other non-aligned AGIs from arising. I would argue that this goal is exactly backwards: it is profoundly anti-social, and indeed, psychopathic. An AGI that would be willing to perform such a pivotal act would be profoundly amoral, and equally comfortable performing any number of other genocidal acts.
quotes.m: I would argue that this goal is exactly backwards: it is profoundly anti-social, and indeed, psychopathic.
quotes.sum: The author rejects a single AI taking decisive control to prevent rivals, arguing that willingness to do so would be morally dangerous.
quotes.t: Morality as Cooperation Part I: Humans

quotes.c: Possibility of accidentally harmful AGI: Unintentional AI misalignment might obviously cause existential catastrophes for reasons discussed at length in the EA community (see, e.g., Christian 2020 for an introduction). There is also a non-zero chance of accidental “near misses” leading to even worse outcomes (see Tomasik 2019 ).
quotes.sum: Accidental misalignment of advanced AI could cause an existential catastrophe, and near misses might lead to even worse outcomes.
quotes.t: Some governance research ideas to prevent malevolent control over AGI and why this might matter a hell of a lot

quotes.c: We don’t propagate suspicious outputs (e.g., push suspicious code to production), instead we might replace them with what the trusted (but weaker model) would have done instead (“Trusted monitoring with defer to trusted”). Obviously, one of the key things you can do if you’re able to detect escape attempts is to just block/shut-down/isolate those escape attempts.
quotes.m: Obviously, one of the key things you can do if you’re able to detect escape attempts is to just block/shut-down/isolate those escape attempts.
quotes.sum: It outlines a safety approach for capable AI: monitor for suspicious behavior and block, shut down, or isolate attempted escapes.
quotes.t: A Brief Explanation of AI Control

quotes.c: Consider: everyone else thinks a company share has a 0.1% chance of being worth $10 tomorrow and a 99.9% chance of being worth $0. I think the chance is 50:50. Therefore the stock price is $0.01 today. If I have $100 in the bank, I maximize expected log(money) by spending fully half of my money on it.
quotes.m: If I have $100 in the bank, I maximize expected log(money) by spending fully half of my money on it.
quotes.sum: The author uses a speculative stock example to show that a large belief advantage does not translate directly into an equivalent number of bits of financial gain.
quotes.t: What is the alpha in one bit of evidence?

quotes.c: Governance matters, and improving societal capacity for governance is one of the best ways to address existential risk. Reducing that risk is a universal public good, while failure to address existential risk is a failure of social coordination. We expect improvements to public deliberation and global coordination systems will reduce existential risk.
quotes.m: We expect improvements to public deliberation and global coordination systems will reduce existential risk.
quotes.sum: The author argues that better public deliberation and global coordination are key ways to reduce existential risks from AI.
quotes.t: Introducing the AI Objectives Institute's Research: Differential Paths toward Safe and Beneficial AI

quotes.c: I'm not as familiar as some must be with the history, but Eliezer had to explicate an entire deontic mesh around "guarded term", to keep people from motte-and-baileying " pivotal act ". I suppose I should declare that mesh cloned around "green light" here, just in case. You are explicitly not allowed to claim my approval of your AGI because you can make an argument that you have something that qualifies as a "green light" according to this post.
quotes.m: You are explicitly not allowed to claim my approval of your AGI because you can make an argument that you have something that qualifies as a "green light" according to this post.
quotes.sum: The author warns that their criteria for approving advanced AI should not be treated as a loophole or automatic endorsement.
quotes.t: A metaphor: what "green lights" for AGI would look like

quotes.c: I don’t think that’s the situation with AI risk. As I argued before , I think we have a nontrivial chance of avoiding AI takeover even in a “minimal-dignity” future - say, assuming essentially no growth from here in the size or influence of the communities and research fields focused specifically on existential risk from misaligned AI, and no highly surprising research or other insights from these communities/fields either. (This statement is not meant to make anyone relax! A nontrivial chance of survival is obviously not good enough.)
quotes.m: A nontrivial chance of survival is obviously not good enough.
quotes.sum: He argues that even without growth in AI-risk work, humanity may have some chance to avoid an AI takeover—but says that is far from acceptable.
quotes.t: A Playbook for AI Risk Reduction (focused on misaligned AI)

quotes.c: The thing that annoys me about this process is that, in the wake, it is harder for both sets of voters to heal their own blind spots. “Being able to see A accurately” is now linked up socially and verbally with “being one of the people who refuse to acknowledge B” (and vice versa). (This happens because the ontology has been seized by the scissors-statement crafters – there is a common, salient, short word that means both “ A matters” and “ B is fake,” and people end up using it in their own head, and, while verifying a real truth they can see, locking in a blind spot they can’t see.)
quotes.m: “Being able to see A accurately” is now linked up socially and verbally with “being one of the people who refuse to acknowledge B” (and vice versa).
quotes.sum: Political framing can make recognizing one truth socially inseparable from denying another, entrenching both sides’ blind spots.
quotes.t: Scissors Statements for President?

quotes.c: Think of the world—the whole thing, the beauty and the horror, the joy and the tragedy—and say out loud to yourself “everything’s okay, in comparison to how bad things could be”. No matter how bad you think it is now, it could all be much worse, right? Think of the satisfaction you’d feel if you thought you were on track for that much worse world, and suddenly learned that you were in our current world instead!
quotes.m: “everything’s okay, in comparison to how bad things could be”.
quotes.sum: The author argues that judgments often rely on unstated, unrealistically demanding standards, and suggests comparing reality with worse possible worlds.
quotes.t: Judgments often smuggle in implicit standards

quotes.c: In contrast, imagine what would happen if we created an AI, that before deciding to take over the world, openly and visibly declared war on humanity. Such an AI would have a severe uphill battle. Humans can survive without the internet, computers, or even electricity, which is not the case for AI, and is willing to resort to desperate measures for the sake of self-preservation.
quotes.sum: The author argues that an AI openly attacking humanity would be vulnerable because humans could survive after destroying the infrastructure it depends on.
quotes.t: Bandgaps, Brains, and Bioweapons: The limitations of computational science and what it means for AGI

quotes.c: Right now, we’re facing some tough questions about the understanding and sentience of AI. The more we personify them, the more we’ll be inclined to judge AI favourably. We’ve seen from Eliza and various Turing Test winners quite how easily influenced we are, once something starts to resemble a human.
quotes.m: The more we personify them, the more we’ll be inclined to judge AI favourably.
quotes.sum: The author warns that human-like AI may bias people toward treating it as understanding or sentient, regardless of the evidence.
quotes.t: An Uncanny Moat

quotes.c: Having said all of this, the process of “listening” to parts (like the process of interpreting dreams) is inherently a messy one, and it’s easy to just hear what we expect to hear. Indeed, I’m not sure that there’s a clear line between “listening” to a part and “inventing” a part, which should make us cautious. So we should think of IFS as a lens on our psychology which sometimes allows us to articulate hidden beliefs or desires, but sometimes leads us on wild goose chases—and we should trust it to the extent that these articulations tend to be productive.
quotes.m: we should trust it to the extent that these articulations tend to be productive.
quotes.sum: Internal-parts therapy can reveal hidden motives, but it is easy to project invented narratives onto oneself and should be judged by whether it helps.
quotes.t: Resolving internal conflicts requires listening to what parts want

quotes.c: Sleep and dreams look like relevant fields for effective altruists. Dreams are the most common but by no means the only altered state of consciousness worth addressing. There should be a greater scientific and intellectual investment into understanding our sleep state and its dream content. This could lead to developing our time sleeping for the greater good. As well as preventing us from making pitfalls about these conscious states. If dreams are important in themselves then I want to put forward the expansion of the moral circle to include our lives asleep.
quotes.m: If dreams are important in themselves then I want to put forward the expansion of the moral circle to include our lives asleep.
quotes.sum: The author argues that dreams may have moral importance and that moral concern should extend to people’s conscious lives while asleep.
quotes.t: What Are Dreams Worth?

quotes.c: On the other hand, I worry about having any government in charge of an AI so powerful it grants decisive strategic advantage. It's not enough to ask whether the US Federal government is an adequate government currently. We must ask how it might look after the destabilizing effect of powerful AI is introduced. Who has ultimate control over this AI? The President? So much for checks and balances. At that point we are suddenly only still a democracy if the President wills it so. I would prefer not to put anyone in a position of such power over the world.
quotes.m: At that point we are suddenly only still a democracy if the President wills it so.
quotes.sum: Powerful AI could give one government or leader overwhelming global power, hollowing out democratic checks and balances.
quotes.t: A path to human autonomy

quotes.c: As Americans know, the electoral college gives disproportionate influence to swing states, which means a vote in the extremely blue state of California was basically wasted in the 2024 election, as are votes in extremely red states like Texas, Oklahoma, and Louisiana. State legislatures have the Constitutional power to assign their state's electoral votes. So why don't the four states sign a compact to assign all their electoral votes in 2028 and future presidential elections to the winner of the aggregate popular vote in those four states?
quotes.m: So why don't the four states sign a compact to assign all their electoral votes in 2028 and future presidential elections to the winner of the aggregate popular vote in those four states?
quotes.sum: The author proposes that California, Texas, Oklahoma, and Louisiana pool their electoral votes according to their combined popular vote, creating a competitive mega-state.
quotes.t: Should CA, TX, OK, and LA merge into a giant swing state, just for elections?

quotes.c: Namely the sooner The EthiSizer Global Governor is (a) playtested, and (b) deployed, the sooner human/Earth life existential risk is reduced. It: clarifies a concept ( The EthiSizer singleton ), and thus identifies a crux , in a way that makes it clearer what further research would be valuable to conduct (even if, the essay doesn’t change anybody’s probability distribution or central estimate).
quotes.m: the sooner The EthiSizer Global Governor is (a) playtested, and (b) deployed, the sooner human/Earth life existential risk is reduced.
quotes.sum: The author argues that rapidly testing and deploying a single global governor would reduce existential risk to humans and Earth life.
quotes.t: ChatGPT & The EthiSizer Game(s)

quotes.c: So a small “snag” in our brains can grow into a tangled mess of defensiveness and self-destructiveness. And in particular, small experiences of fear or hurt from when we’re young and vulnerable can give rise to complex protective strategies, like the ones described above. Those strategies get defensive when criticized, or when they lose influence, because they have a deep-rooted belief that their approach is the only way to avoid danger; and this can cause them to be reinforced even when they lead to very counterproductive behavior.
quotes.sum: Early fear and hurt can create defensive mental strategies that persist and reinforce themselves even when they become harmful.
quotes.t: We learn long-lasting strategies to protect ourselves from danger and rejection

quotes.c: If I could press a button to reduce overall meat consumption or to increase concern for animals, I probably would. In other words, I think the expected value of these things is perhaps slightly above zero. But my expected value for them is sufficiently close to zero that I don't feel great about my donations being used for them.
quotes.m: But my expected value for them is sufficiently close to zero that I don't feel great about my donations being used for them.
quotes.sum: The author is hesitant to fund efforts to reduce meat consumption or raise concern for animals because they see their benefits as only slightly positive.
quotes.t: How much funging is there with donations to different EA animal charities?

quotes.c: Most discussion in longtermism centers around preserving humanity's future, but it is also important that we think about what humanity's future should look like. For example, assuming we develop into a Type III civilization, what should our values and priorities be such that we make the best possible society in a galactic context?
quotes.sum: The author argues that long-term thinking should address what values a future galaxy-spanning civilization ought to adopt, not merely humanity's survival.
quotes.t: Values of a Space-Faring Civilization

quotes.c: I don't discuss here the disagreements about what subjective or objective states or "life journeys" of moral patients are really desirable between welfarism, utilitarianism, hedonism, eudaimonism, ecocentrism, and other relevant theories of ethics. Without loss of generality, we can assume that moral uncertainty and ethical portfolio views should be applied and the "goodness" of such and such state of such and such moral patient(s) weighted accordingly.
quotes.m: we can assume that moral uncertainty and ethical portfolio views should be applied
quotes.sum: The author sets aside disputes among ethical theories and proposes handling uncertainty by weighting outcomes across them.
quotes.t: Differential knowledge interconnection

quotes.c: It’s not my view that safety considerations always trump moral ones, regardless of their respective types or relative magnitudes. An AI that kills ten humans to achieve an extremely important moral goal (say, perfecting a technology that will dramatically improve human existence) would count as unsafe by many reasonable standards, but it doesn’t immediately follow on my view that we shouldn’t design such an AI. I claim only that safety considerations should prevail when sufficiently great risks of catastrophic harm are on the line.
quotes.m: An AI that kills ten humans to achieve an extremely important moral goal (say, perfecting a technology that will dramatically improve human existence) would count as unsafe by many reasonable standards, but it doesn’t immediately follow on my view that we shouldn’t design such an AI.
quotes.sum: The author argues that an AI may be worth designing even if it kills people for an exceptionally important moral goal, while stressing catastrophic risks should usually take priority.
quotes.t: Safe AI and moral AI

quotes.c: I’ve already given a partial answer: that our evolutionary environment was much more dangerous than our current environment. But I want to extend this to a more general answer: that coercion is an adaptation to scarcity; and that we only very recently left the era in which scarcity was the dominant feature of people’s lives.
quotes.m: coercion is an adaptation to scarcity; and that we only very recently left the era in which scarcity was the dominant feature of people’s lives.
quotes.sum: He argues that coercive behavior developed under conditions of scarcity, while modern abundance can support more trust-based social relations.
quotes.t: Coercion is an adaptation to scarcity; trust is an adaptation to abundance

quotes.c: I don’t think this similarity is a coincidence at all—instead, it's a consequence of the fact that one of the most useful models of the mind is the multi-agent model . According to this model, we should think of ourselves as being composed of multiple different parts, each with their own beliefs and goals, with their attempts to achieve those goals sometimes involving conflicts with other parts.
quotes.m: According to this model, we should think of ourselves as being composed of multiple different parts, each with their own beliefs and goals, with their attempts to achieve those goals sometimes involving conflicts with other parts.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the mind is best understood as multiple internal parts with separate goals that can come into conflict.
quotes.t: Conflicts between emotional schemas often involve internal coercion

quotes.c: For the general public’s reaction, there’s mostly not a big resistance to the idea they feel pain, until you get their diets involved. However, when people were shown that shrimp were included in the UK sentience bill, their opinion changed a lot, and they were willing to pay a premium, at least in principle. I think this is a really interesting example of laws changing public perception and making foreign and strange ideas seem more acceptable.
quotes.m: I think this is a really interesting example of laws changing public perception and making foreign and strange ideas seem more acceptable.
quotes.sum: The author argues that legally recognizing shrimp as sentient can make people more willing to accept paying for their welfare.
quotes.t: Overview of Shrimp Farming and Questions Surrounding it

quotes.c: We encourage an atmosphere of friendly disagreement, curiosity, and academic rigor at our office, seminars, workshops, and networking events. Including a diverse portfolio of alignment agendas and researchers from a variety of backgrounds allows for earnest disagreement among the cohort. We tell scholars to “download but don’t defer” in regard to their mentors’ models.
quotes.m: We tell scholars to “download but don’t defer” in regard to their mentors’ models.
quotes.sum: The training program says it promotes independent thinking and disagreement rather than deference to mentors or a single research agenda.
quotes.t: How MATS addresses “mass movement building” concerns

quotes.c: Although good R&D projects estimate the cost-effectiveness of their outputs, there will generally remain considerable uncertainty about the cost-effectiveness of the new intervention. Therefore, Step 2b determines whether the intervention produced by the R&D project should be evaluated in a randomized controlled trial (RCT), what the outcomes could be, and how much it would cost.
quotes.m: Step 2b determines whether the intervention produced by the R&D project should be evaluated in a randomized controlled trial (RCT), what the outcomes could be, and how much it would cost.
quotes.sum: The author argues that uncertain R&D interventions should be assessed for whether a randomized trial is worthwhile before further investment.
quotes.t: Estimating the cost-effectiveness of previous R&D projects

quotes.c: There are many ways in which genius can present itself, some of which may be unfamiliar to the person making the judgment. If you are going off of a conversation with someone for instance, there may be multiple things at play that could make someone appear to not fit the role of genius such as nerves, social anxiety, differences in communication style, or unconscious bias in the judge. The person making the call is likely not a genius themselves, using unclear ways of measuring what they think constitutes a genius.
quotes.m: The person making the call is likely not a genius themselves, using unclear ways of measuring what they think constitutes a genius.
quotes.sum: Claims that judgments about who is a “genius” are unreliable and often distorted by bias, communication differences, and privilege.
quotes.t: You don't need to be a genius to be in AI safety research
