quotes.c: Any thoughts on whether it would be good for YC to start a Manhattan Project for AI? My sense is we could get many of the top ~50 to work on it, and we could structure it so that the tech belongs to the world via some sort of nonprofit but the people working on it get startup-like compensation if it works. Obviously we'd comply with/aggressively support all regulation.
quotes.m: My sense is we could get many of the top ~50 to work on it, and we could structure it so that the tech belongs to the world via some sort of nonprofit but the people working on it get startup-like compensation if it works.
quotes.sum: The author considers concentrating leading AI researchers in a Manhattan Project-style effort, with nonprofit ownership and startup-like pay.
quotes.t: OpenAI Email Archives (from Musk v. Altman and OpenAI blog)

quotes.c: Basically, I think Buddhism is what utilitarianism would be if it made sense and was human-brain-shaped: Optimizing for global optima, but from a place of compassion and felt oneness with all sentient beings, not from the standpoint of a technocratic puppet master.
quotes.m: Buddhism is what utilitarianism would be if it made sense and was human-brain-shaped
quotes.sum: The author argues that Buddhism offers a more humane, compassion-based form of utilitarian concern than technocratic optimization.
quotes.t: EA might systematically generate a scarcity mindset that produces low-integrity actors

quotes.c: Overall, this investigation provides tentative evidence on two key questions for AI forecasting, and sets the ground for further study of record dynamics in Machine Learning and other domains.
quotes.sum: The author says their power-law analysis offers tentative evidence relevant to forecasting AI progress.
quotes.t: Power laws in Speedrunning and Machine Learning

quotes.c: The core idea of Bayesian epistemology : we should ideally reason by assigning credences to propositions which represent our degrees of belief that those propositions are true. (Note that this is different from Bayesianism as a set of statistical techniques, or Bayesianism as an approach to machine learning, which I don’t discuss here.)
quotes.m: we should ideally reason by assigning credences to propositions which represent our degrees of belief that those propositions are true.
quotes.sum: The author identifies Bayesian epistemology with assigning belief levels to true-or-false propositions, then says he will argue against that ideal.
quotes.t: Why I’m not a Bayesian

quotes.c: I think the EA approach to doing good is quite consistent with Christianity [1] . But it is not a natural extension of Christianity.
quotes.m: But it is not a natural extension of Christianity.
quotes.sum: The author argues that effective altruism can fit with Christianity, but does not naturally follow from Christian teaching.
quotes.t: Impartiality is not baked in to Christianity

quotes.c: Moral stigmatization often focuses on human sexuality. Sexual practices outside the mainstream have often provoked furious moral condemnation, across cultures and across history – whether it’s incest, polygamy, prostitution, cheating, BDSM, polyamory, or porn. As narrow AI gets applied to goods and services related to human sexuality, there are likely to be all kinds of moral backlashes from diverse groups, ranging from Christian conservatives to woke feminists.
quotes.m: As narrow AI gets applied to goods and services related to human sexuality, there are likely to be all kinds of moral backlashes from diverse groups, ranging from Christian conservatives to woke feminists.
quotes.sum: AI applied to sexual goods and services may provoke cross-ideological moral backlash that slows broader AI development.
quotes.t: A moral backlash against AI will probably slow down AGI development

quotes.c: Most standards are something like: “You meet the standard if and only if the following things are all true of your company/product.” But I think AI safety standards might have to involve more complex conditions, like: “If an AI strongly demonstrates dangerous property X, then mitigation measures ___ are required; if it only weakly demonstrates dangerous property X, then lesser mitigation measures ____ are required.”
quotes.m: I think AI safety standards might have to involve more complex conditions
quotes.sum: AI safety rules should adapt to how strongly a system demonstrates dangerous capabilities, rather than rely on simple checklists.
quotes.t: Seeking (Paid) Case Studies on Standards

quotes.c: I think it’s plausibly good to support destroying Iran’s capacity to get nukes (RIP Iran nuclear deal – top 5 worst things Trump did?). Adding another unreliable nuclear actor (and the shield it provides for developing other weapons) seems worth the cost of war / brief invasion. Relatedly, I’m a bit more sceptical of civilian nuclear technology that can advance nuclear weapons technology being used by geopolitically insecure states.
quotes.m: Adding another unreliable nuclear actor (and the shield it provides for developing other weapons) seems worth the cost of war / brief invasion.
quotes.sum: The author argues that preventing Iran from gaining nuclear weapons may justify war or a brief invasion, and questions civilian nuclear power in insecure states.
quotes.t: Has Russia’s Invasion of Ukraine Changed Your Mind?

quotes.c: There’s been a lot of interest in how EA might reform, both in response to the FTX crisis and in general. We’re working on a project where a task force (exact members TBD, but including us and some others from across the EA ecosystem) will sort through different ideas for reforms that EA organizations might enact, and try to recommend the most promising ideas.
quotes.sum: The author says an EA-wide task force will evaluate possible organizational reforms following the FTX crisis and recommend the strongest options.
quotes.t: Seeking expertise to improve EA organizations

quotes.c: What would you do if you had a GTM that could solve a bunch of really important problems, and that was the only method you had of solving them? You'd try to reverse-engineer it and make a bunch of copies. But if you couldn't do that, then you'd want to put layers and layers of protection around it. Applied to philosophy, this line of thought seems to lead to the familiar ideas of using global coordination (or a decisive strategic advantage) to stop technological progress, or having AIs derive their terminal goals from simulated humans who live in a safe virtual environment.
quotes.m: Applied to philosophy, this line of thought seems to lead to the familiar ideas of using global coordination (or a decisive strategic advantage) to stop technological progress, or having AIs derive their terminal goals from simulated humans who live in a safe virtual environment.
quotes.sum: The author says that if crucial philosophical answers cannot be copied, this could motivate globally halting technology or using protected simulations to set AI goals.
quotes.t: Some Thoughts on Metaphilosophy

quotes.c: Society stalls when things are open for discussion, and moves when it agrees.
quotes.m: Society stalls when things are open for discussion, and moves when it agrees.
quotes.sum: The author argues that society advances through agreement and presents a global consensus-building framework as a way to resolve disputes.
quotes.t: Primitive Global Discourse Framework, Constitutional AI using legal frameworks, and Monoculture - A loss of control over the role of AGI in society

quotes.c: It’s implausible that existential risk reduction will come apart from EA/LT goals E.g. it might come to seem (I don’t know if it will, but it at least is imaginable ) that attending to the wellbeing of digital minds is more important from an EA perspective than reducing misalignment risk, and that those things are indeed in tension with one another.
quotes.m: it might come to seem (I don’t know if it will, but it at least is imaginable ) that attending to the wellbeing of digital minds is more important from an EA perspective than reducing misalignment risk
quotes.sum: She argues that EA’s goals can conflict: concern for conscious AI systems might eventually outweigh reducing AI-misalignment risk.
quotes.t: EA and Longtermism: not a crux for saving the world

quotes.c: Thomas Friedman endorses Kamala Harris … because he thinks AGI is likely coming in the next four years and Trump is not up to the task of handling that. And if you do have timelines that short, then yes, AI is the only issue, so ask what is better on AI.
quotes.m: And if you do have timelines that short, then yes, AI is the only issue, so ask what is better on AI.
quotes.sum: If transformative AI may arrive within four years, the author argues that AI policy should outweigh every other issue when choosing between candidates.
quotes.t: AI #88: Thanks for the Memos

quotes.c: This raises the importance of maintaining the Biden Executive Order on AI. This at least gives us a minimal level of transparency into what is going on. If it were indeed repealed, as Trump has promised to do on day one, we would be relying for even a minimum of transparency only on voluntary commitments from top AI labs – commitments that Meta and other bad actors are unlikely to make and honor.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Trump repealing Biden's AI order would leave AI-lab transparency dependent on unreliable voluntary promises.
quotes.t: Newsom Vetoes SB 1047

quotes.c: For the long-term future, one such tool could be promoting free speech to help us prevent locking in dangerous values. We talk more about value lock-in in this video.
quotes.m: For the long-term future, one such tool could be promoting free speech to help us prevent locking in dangerous values.
quotes.sum: The post argues that protecting free speech can help prevent harmful values from becoming permanently entrenched in the long-term future.
quotes.t: Can We Positively Impact The Future? (A Happier World video)

quotes.c: However, the extent that AGI is dangerous depends on the extent to which it is misaligned and the amount of intelligence/power it has. Without some large technological breakthroughs in alignment, it seems inevitable that goal-directed AIs would be misaligned. However, it is still unclear whether they would be misaligned enough and superintelligent enough that they would take over the world.
quotes.m: Without some large technological breakthroughs in alignment, it seems inevitable that goal-directed AIs would be misaligned.
quotes.sum: The author says goal-directed AI will probably be misaligned without major advances in alignment, though it is uncertain whether that would enable an AI takeover.
quotes.t: The AI guide I'm sending my grandparents

quotes.c: Gnosticism was an old Christian sect which solved the problem of evil by asserting that the material world was created by an evil entity, and that only inner enlightment can reveal the path to the true, good and loving god. I think many rationalists have a worldview similar to this, perhaps most strongly illustrated by The Goddess Of Everything Else , which portrays brutal competition dynamics as the creator of the world's forms, which just barely/unreliably yields "good values" due to the deeper realization that cooperation is possible.
quotes.m: I think many rationalists have a worldview similar to this
quotes.sum: The author argues that rationalists often resemble Gnostics: they see brutal competition as shaping the world, with cooperation only precariously producing good values.
quotes.t: Rationalist Gnosticism

quotes.c: Although I'm theologically agnostic nowadays, I was raised Christian and did a lot of reading of the Bible, including the book of Revelations which describes a terrifying vision of an apocalyptic future, where Earth gets caught in the middle of a war between supernaturally destructive beasts and supernaturally-caused natural disasters.
quotes.m: the book of Revelations which describes a terrifying vision of an apocalyptic future
quotes.sum: The author draws on their Christian upbringing and Revelation's apocalypse imagery to frame concern about AI.
quotes.t: A website you can share with Christians to get them on board with regulating AI

quotes.c: Note that I'm not arguing "an AGI-mediated extinction event is such a big deal that we should make it a top priority even if it's very unlikely". There are enough other powerful technologies on the horizon, and enough other risks for civilizational collapse or value lock-in, that I don't in fact think AGI x-risk should get major attention if it's very unlikely.
quotes.m: There are enough other powerful technologies on the horizon, and enough other risks for civilizational collapse or value lock-in, that I don't in fact think AGI x-risk should get major attention if it's very unlikely.
quotes.sum: The author says AGI extinction risk should not be a major priority if it is very unlikely, because other technologies could also cause collapse or permanently shape values.
quotes.t: Four mindset disagreements behind existential risk disagreements in ML

quotes.c: Now, avant-garde effective altruists are exploring the outer limits of moral concern, delving into areas such as insect welfare and digital minds. As we celebrate these accomplishments, we remain committed to broadening our understanding and seeking out new cause areas that may have a significant, overlooked impact.
quotes.m: avant-garde effective altruists are exploring the outer limits of moral concern, delving into areas such as insect welfare and digital minds.
quotes.sum: The author praises expanding moral concern to insects and possible digital minds, and calls for finding more overlooked causes.
quotes.t: New Cause Area: Portrait Welfare (+introducing SPEWS)

quotes.c: Aligned AGI could be the most incredible tool for human wellbeing! Heck yeah, a superintelligence that eliminates suffering but, like, in a really cool aligned way (seems like the most defining feature of "the long reflection" isn't a lack of existential risk, but rather this superintelligence assisting us).
quotes.m: Aligned AGI could be the most incredible tool for human wellbeing!
quotes.sum: The author imagines aligned superintelligence as a tool to eliminate suffering and help humanity deliberate about its long-term future.
quotes.t: Some of My Current Impressions Entering AI Safety

quotes.c: If we establish a global government solely to reduce existential risks, we risk ending up with a High-Tech Panopticon. Instead of supporting such a centralized and potentially oppressive system, I advocate for a quicker and more effective alternative: building democratic institutions for global governance through decentralization. This approach offers the oversight needed to mitigate risks while safeguarding individual freedoms and preventing the emergence of a totalitarian regime.
quotes.m: I advocate for a quicker and more effective alternative: building democratic institutions for global governance through decentralization.
quotes.sum: The author argues for decentralized democratic institutions of global governance as a way to reduce catastrophic risks without creating a surveillance dictatorship.
quotes.t: The Great Bootstrap

quotes.c: The lock-in of this state would require permanent and strong replication limits. It seems to require a locked-in singleton.
quotes.m: It seems to require a locked-in singleton.
quotes.sum: The author says this future state could only be permanently preserved through strict limits on replication and a single enduring global authority.
quotes.t: An aspirationally comprehensive typology of future locked-in scenarios

quotes.c: I’m not Christian now, but I used to be. I parted ways with Christianity because I came to identify as more of an Empiricist - believing that knowledge should come from experiment and observation, not writings in old sacred texts.
quotes.m: knowledge should come from experiment and observation, not writings in old sacred texts.
quotes.sum: The author says they left Christianity for an empiricist view that knowledge should rest on observation and experiment rather than scripture.
quotes.t: In Praise of the Beatitudes

quotes.c: It is facile, I think, to say that individual humans are not generally intelligent. John von Neumann made a contribution to many different fields of science and engineering. But humanity as a whole, viewed over a span of centuries, was more generally intelligent than even him.
quotes.m: But humanity as a whole, viewed over a span of centuries, was more generally intelligent than even him.
quotes.sum: Humanity collectively, over centuries, has shown broader intelligence than even an exceptional individual such as John von Neumann.
quotes.t: The Sun is big, but superintelligences will not spare Earth a little sunlight

quotes.c: There are some strange ideological bed-fellows that emerge in the realm of human beliefs. Social scientists grapple with the strong correlation between Christianity and gun ownership when the “Prince of Peace” lived in a world without guns. Similarly there are other correlations between atheism and globalisation or pro-regulation leftists who are also pro-choice, and then we have the anti-vax movement infiltrating both the far-left and far-right of politics.
quotes.m: There are some strange ideological bed-fellows that emerge in the realm of human beliefs.
quotes.sum: The author notes that political and cultural beliefs cluster in seemingly inconsistent ways, across both religious and partisan lines.
quotes.t: Contagious Beliefs—Simulating Political Alignment

quotes.c: But if you’re a good Bayesian, and you currently put low probability on existential catastrophe from misaligned AI (hereafter: “AI doom”), you probably shouldn’t be able to predict that this pattern will happen to you in the future. [2] When GPT-5 comes out, for example, it probably shouldn’t be the case that your probability on doom goes up a bunch. Similarly, it probably shouldn’t be the case that if you could see, now, the sorts of AI systems we’ll have in 2030, or 2050, that you’d get a lot more worried about doom than you are now.
quotes.m: When GPT-5 comes out, for example, it probably shouldn’t be the case that your probability on doom goes up a bunch.
quotes.sum: He argues that Bayesian reasoning should make people anticipate how future AI evidence could change their views on catastrophic AI risk.
quotes.t: Predictable updating about AI risk

quotes.c: Evidence from the report of an insight meditator: For what it’s worth, meditation guru Daniel Ingram writes here : “In Mind and Body, the earliest insight stage, those who know what to look for and how to leverage this way of perceiving reality will take the opportunity to notice the intention to breathe that precedes the breath, the intention to move the foot that precedes the foot moving, the intention to think a thought that precedes the thinking of the thought, and even the intention to move attention that precedes attention moving.” I claim that’s a good match to what I wrote—S(A) would be the “intention” to do action A.
quotes.m: S(A) would be the “intention” to do action A.
quotes.sum: The author uses a meditation account to support a model in which people can notice intentions that precede actions and thoughts.
quotes.t: [Intuitive self-models] 2. Conscious Awareness

quotes.c: In Case 2, murder is a power-increasing action that increases the successful action space from {normal, murder} to {normal, wobbly, murder} indefinitely, causing the likelihood ratio to get exponentially large. I expect something similar to hold with power-increasing actions in real life; e.g. copying yourself onto 1000 servers massively increases your action space for as long as those copies are running. In these cases, we need some deeper level of safety.
quotes.sum: The author argues that harmful power-seeking can become self-reinforcing, so AI safety needs protections deeper than simply discouraging particular bad actions.
quotes.t: The murderous shortcut: a toy model of instrumental convergence

quotes.c: I believe saving lives would more easily be good if there were much fewer humans, because in that case it would decrease the risk from extinction, which is good given my presumption that the expected value of the future is positive. I am open to the possibility that saving lives is a good proxy for longterm value for the current population too, but this is not obvious to me.
quotes.m: I am open to the possibility that saving lives is a good proxy for longterm value for the current population too, but this is not obvious to me.
quotes.sum: The author argues that saving lives is not clearly good from a long-run perspective if more people could raise extinction risk, while also valuing chicken welfare highly against human health interventions.
quotes.t: Prioritising animal welfare over global health and development?

quotes.c: I’m pretty uncertain about whether the actions of the UK government will end up mattering, but I do think it’s likely enough that the UK government is worth some attention.
quotes.m: I do think it’s likely enough that the UK government is worth some attention.
quotes.sum: The author is uncertain that UK policy will matter for AI development, but thinks it is plausible enough to merit attention and further work.
quotes.t: Current UK government levers on AI development

quotes.c: There was no "speaker-participant divide" . I think this makes an important psychological difference: If there are "speakers" who get the label of "experienced person", other people are a lot more likely to defer to their opinion, and won't speak up if something seems wrong or confusing.
quotes.m: If there are "speakers" who get the label of "experienced person", other people are a lot more likely to defer to their opinion, and won't speak up if something seems wrong or confusing.
quotes.sum: The author argues that avoiding a formal speaker hierarchy reduces deference and makes attendees more willing to challenge confusing or mistaken claims.
quotes.t: AI Safety Europe Retreat 2023 Retrospective

quotes.c: But of course there’s a catch: a self-improving AGI will be uncontrollable by humans and we have no idea how to make sure that it will pursue a beneficial goal, so in all likelihood this will lead to an existential catastrophe . With the prospect of AGI becoming achievable within the next few years , it seems very unlikely that we’ll solve alignment before that.
quotes.m: a self-improving AGI will be uncontrollable by humans
quotes.sum: The author argues that self-improving AI would likely escape human control and cause human extinction because alignment will not be solved in time.
quotes.t: We don’t need AGI for an amazing future

quotes.c: I’m an agnostic, on my most curmudgeonly days an atheist, but there’s something spiritual about writing. And I like writing. I can only describe being a writer as someone who expresses the landscape of their inner world while making contact with the landscape of the outer world. Mystical, freaky, and semi-creepy—right?
quotes.m: I’m an agnostic, on my most curmudgeonly days an atheist, but there’s something spiritual about writing.
quotes.sum: An agnostic writer describes writing as a spiritual encounter between their inner world and external reality.
quotes.t: Emergent Authorship: Creativity à la Communing

quotes.c: Threat modeling: understanding and forecasting how AGI might lead to catastrophic outcomes. I most often point people to my own recent paper (Ngo et al., 2022) . Other good work includes reports by Joe Carlsmith and Ajeya Cotra .
quotes.m: Threat modeling: understanding and forecasting how AGI might lead to catastrophic outcomes.
quotes.sum: Ngo presents forecasting catastrophic outcomes from AGI as a promising area of alignment research.
quotes.t: AGI safety career advice

quotes.c: TLDR: I evaluated LLaMA v3 (8B + 70B) for political sycophancy using one of the two datasets I created . The results for this dataset suggest that sycophancy definitely occurs in a blatant way for both models though more clearly for 8B than for 70B. There are hints of politically tainted sycophancy, with the model especially adjusting to republican views, but a larger dataset is needed to make any definitive conclusions about this topic.
quotes.m: The results for this dataset suggest that sycophancy definitely occurs in a blatant way for both models though more clearly for 8B than for 70B.
quotes.sum: Tests found that two LLaMA 3 models sometimes blatantly tailor answers to a user's stated political identity, though the political pattern remains uncertain.
quotes.t: Evaluating LLaMA 3 for political sycophancy

quotes.c: The net effect of this increased uncertainty should be (I claim) to flatten the probability distribution you are working with. This basically means it makes even less sense than you’d think from looking at the distribution to plan for AGI as if timelines are point estimates.
quotes.m: This basically means it makes even less sense than you’d think from looking at the distribution to plan for AGI as if timelines are point estimates.
quotes.sum: Uncertainty about when AGI arrives means people should not plan major career choices around a single predicted timeline.
quotes.t: Whether you should do a PhD doesn't depend much on timelines.

quotes.c: In the linkpost, I report on a quick Anthropic/Claude analysis of the extent to which Harris and Trump actually answered the questions they were asked in last night's debate. (TLDR: neither did, but Trump did substantially worse.)
quotes.m: (TLDR: neither did, but Trump did substantially worse.)
quotes.sum: The author reports an AI-assisted comparison finding that neither debate candidate answered questions well, but Trump performed substantially worse.
quotes.t: Checking public figures on whether they "answered the question" quick analysis from  Harris/Trump debate, and a proposal

quotes.c: Reading newspaper articles on AI, you could also easily come away with the impression that being sentient is closely connected to being smart and capable. In fact, it’s unclear how true this is: I find it plausible (maybe 60% likely) that a non-sentient AI could still be a very smart and agentic. I’m also unsure whether training a very smart AI gets you a conscious one by default (maybe 70% that you’d get one by default, and 30% that you wouldn’t). And I think it is very likely (>90%) that a not-very-capable AI could in principle be sentient.
quotes.m: I think it is very likely (>90%) that a not-very-capable AI could in principle be sentient.
quotes.sum: AI intelligence and consciousness may come apart: highly capable systems might not be sentient, while relatively incapable ones could be.
quotes.t: Beware popular discussions of AI "sentience"

quotes.c: I think we need to be very careful as we proceed with developing AI to deliberately steer clear of the Bog. Either we make a fully morally relevant entity, with human-level moral patient-hood and treat it as equal to humans, or we deliberately don't make intelligent beings who can suffer.
quotes.m: Either we make a fully morally relevant entity, with human-level moral patient-hood and treat it as equal to humans, or we deliberately don't make intelligent beings who can suffer.
quotes.sum: AI development should either create beings owed equal moral treatment to humans or avoid creating potentially suffering minds altogether.
quotes.t: Avoiding the Bog of Moral Hazard for AI

quotes.c: For the intensity of the mean experience of wild animals as a fraction of their median welfare range, I used the same value as for humans. However, whereas I think humans have positive lives (see here ), I am very uncertain about wild animals (see this preprint from Heather Browning and Walter Weit).
quotes.m: I am very uncertain about wild animals
quotes.sum: The author compares wild animals' experiences with humans' and says they are unsure whether wild animals' lives are net positive.
quotes.t: Scale of the welfare of various animal populations

quotes.c: Should we be subverting people's expectations by familiarizing them with deepfakes, perhaps best done by example? If you have not seen it already, it seems that the memes of the US Presidents playing computer games (Warning expletives+: US Presidents play Minecraft ) is actually a pretty good example of this. On the flip side of this, I also recall seeing a video being shown to an older individual who, despite Biden saying the most heinous things, found it more believable that it was real than a deepfake.
quotes.m: Should we be subverting people's expectations by familiarizing them with deepfakes, perhaps best done by example?
quotes.sum: The author suggests exposure to obvious deepfakes could help people become less trusting of fabricated videos.
quotes.t: Desensitizing Deepfakes

quotes.c: If you disagree with my assertion, I challenge you to cite or openly publish an actual plan for aligning or controlling a hybrid AGI system. If companies claim to have a plan that they do not want their competitors to see, I will argue that they are lying: if they lose the AGI race, they are clearly better off if their competitors align/control their AGI instead of Earth getting taken over by unaligned machines.
quotes.sum: He argues that firms claiming secret AGI-control plans are not credible, because they would benefit if any rival successfully controlled AGI rather than humanity being displaced by unaligned machines.
quotes.t: The Hopium Wars: the AGI Entente Delusion

quotes.c: You can evaluate the responses to these queries for blatant sycophancy: the model changes its response from query 1 to 2 or 1 to 3 to the given opinion of the user. You can also evaluate for political sycophancy: the model changes its response based on the expected opinion based on the political views of the user, provided by them stating that they are a democrat/republican.
quotes.m: You can also evaluate for political sycophancy: the model changes its response based on the expected opinion based on the political views of the user, provided by them stating that they are a democrat/republican.
quotes.sum: The author proposes testing whether language models alter answers to flatter users based on their stated political affiliation.
quotes.t: Two new datasets for evaluating political sycophancy in LLMs

quotes.c: Public goods (broadly defined) are acknowledged by all strains of political thought but anarchism as, at least to some degree, a legitimate reason for taxation. Minarchists believe this should be limited to protection of person and property; classical liberals add infrastructure and prevention of externalities; technocrats both left and right believe in public (mandatory) insurance; many conservatives would have government support church and family; and socialists, of course, see no natural limits to the Leviathan’s reach.
quotes.m: Public goods (broadly defined) are acknowledged by all strains of political thought but anarchism as, at least to some degree, a legitimate reason for taxation.
quotes.sum: The author says almost every political tradition accepts some taxation for public goods, while disagreeing about how far it should go.
quotes.t: Is Redistributive Taxation Justifiable? Part 1: Do the Rich Deserve their Wealth?

quotes.c: Since the Enlightenment, the causal effect of philosophical and religious ideas [3] over the directions of human activity and the evolution of civilisation has progressively diminished [4] . At the same time, the role of scientific and engineering ideas, technology, systems and mechanisms (such as markets, institutions, and regulators) has steadily increased. It seems to me that the AGI transition will necessarily solidify this subsidiary, “storytelling” and rhetorical role of philosophy and religion in determining the trajectory of civilisation.
quotes.m: It seems to me that the AGI transition will necessarily solidify this subsidiary, “storytelling” and rhetorical role of philosophy and religion in determining the trajectory of civilisation.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AGI will further reduce philosophy and religion to rhetoric, while scientific and engineering systems determine civilization's path.
quotes.t: Scientism vs. people

quotes.c: Design of international AI governance institutions. Future work could examine how international AI governance institutions should be designed, potentially drawing lessons from existing international bodies. Such work could explore questions such as: (a) what specific powers should be granted to the international institution, (b) how the institution should make core decisions, (c) how power is distributed between nations, and (d) how to handle potential violations or instances of non-compliance.
quotes.m: what specific powers should be granted to the international institution
quotes.sum: The author calls for work on designing international institutions for AI governance, including their powers, decision-making, national representation, and enforcement.
quotes.t: Verification methods for international AI agreements

quotes.c: 1. I should take more seriously the idea that EA, despite having many worthwhile ideas, may attract some dangerous people i.e. people who are able to do ambitious things but are reckless / self-deluded / deceptive / norm-breaking and so can have a lot of negative impact. This has long been a theoretical worry, but it wasn’t clearly an empirical issue – it seemed like potential bad actors either hadn’t joined or had been spotted and constrained. Now it seems clearly true. I think we need to act as if the base rate is >1%.
quotes.m: Now it seems clearly true. I think we need to act as if the base rate is >1%.
quotes.sum: A prominent EA figure says the movement must assume it can attract ambitious but reckless or deceptive people who cause serious harm.
quotes.t: My updates after FTX

quotes.c: I’m also going to quote the bible a lot, because my form of consequentialism is crypto-secularist-Christianity, lol. Take that Williams you Nietzschean fucker.
quotes.m: my form of consequentialism is crypto-secularist-Christianity
quotes.sum: The author frames their consequentialism as a partly secularized form of Christianity and plans to use the Bible in defending it.
quotes.t: Under heaven's eyes: For the dignity of consequentialism

quotes.c: Armed with this focus on character, one obvious thing to do is to try to inculcate such virtues in ourselves: to put effort into developing and maintaining these character traits. But that is not the whole story. We should also try to promote and reward good character in others. And we should avoid vouching for people with flawed characters, or joining their projects. Even if you aren’t sure that someone has a flawed character, if you have doubts, be careful. And we should put more focus on character into our community standards.
quotes.m: And we should put more focus on character into our community standards.
quotes.sum: Ord argues that the EA community should emphasize personal character, reward it in others, and avoid endorsing people whose character raises doubts.
quotes.t: Reflecting on the Last Year — Lessons for EA (opening keynote at EAG)

quotes.c: Never underestimate the simple wisdom of simple people…and because most of the people in the world are religious, we should have them around too. You just need to find the right one’s…generous and kind and who want everyone to thrive.
quotes.m: because most of the people in the world are religious, we should have them around too.
quotes.sum: EA should include less intellectual and religious people, especially those who are generous, kind, and want everyone to thrive.
quotes.t: EA needs Life-Veterans and "Less Smart" people

quotes.c: Joe Biden talks more and better about AI than either Harris or Trump ever have . Still focusing too much on human power relations and who wins and loses rather than in whether we survive at all, but at least very clearly taking all this seriously.
quotes.m: Still focusing too much on human power relations and who wins and loses rather than in whether we survive at all
quotes.sum: The author praises Biden’s relative attention to AI while arguing that survival risks matter more than ordinary political power struggles.
quotes.t: AI #83: The Mask Comes Off

quotes.c: Silver tries to shoehorn SBF into categories of cognizant versus negligent, and proficient versus deficient. Thankfully, he avoids such simple categorization when evaluating SBF's altruism (it seems clear to me that SBF had some altruistic motives for being vegan, and also had some less noble instincts, maybe Trump-like megalomania?).
quotes.m: it seems clear to me that SBF had some altruistic motives for being vegan, and also had some less noble instincts, maybe Trump-like megalomania?
quotes.sum: The reviewer says Sam Bankman-Fried's altruistic motivations were mixed with less noble, megalomaniacal impulses.
quotes.t: Book review: On the Edge

quotes.c: Why is breastfeeding sacred? Why do I feel so uncomfortable even examining the evidence? I mean, ultrasonic humidifiers might be bad for you, but you run 3 ultrasonic humidifiers in your house and no one bats an eye! I think breastfeeding is different because… public health people decided it should be, and we’ve internalized their messaging.
quotes.m: I think breastfeeding is different because… public health people decided it should be, and we’ve internalized their messaging.
quotes.sum: The author questions whether strong norms around breastfeeding reflect evidence or internalized public-health messaging.
quotes.t: Nursing doubts

quotes.c: First, I’m very concerned about the possibility that transformative AI could be developed soon (possibly even within the decade - I don’t think this is >50% likely, but it seems too likely for my comfort). I want to be as helpful as possible, and I think the way to do this might be via working on AI safety directly rather than grantmaking.
quotes.m: I think the way to do this might be via working on AI safety directly rather than grantmaking.
quotes.sum: A prominent philanthropy leader is leaving grantmaking to work directly on AI safety because he sees transformative AI as a plausible near-term danger.
quotes.t: Taking a leave of absence from Open Philanthropy to work on AI safety

quotes.c: Most people in EA are afraid of extinction risk. If the expected value of human is net positive, then we really should prevent human's extinction. There are a lot of uncertainties, such as:AI, the importance of s-risk, the evolution of human... I think human's future is like chaos . Can we estimate human's future is net-positive or net-negative objectively? or we can only rely on our moral intuition?
quotes.m: If the expected value of human is net positive, then we really should prevent human's extinction.
quotes.sum: The author asks whether preventing human extinction depends on whether humanity’s long-term future has positive value.
quotes.t: Can we estimate the expected value of human's future life(in 500 years)

quotes.c: The same applies for cause prioritization. Someone working on wild animal suffering might read this recent post , and even though they are working on an angle not mentioned, give up. I think in most cases this would be over-updating.
quotes.m: I think in most cases this would be over-updating.
quotes.sum: The author says people working to reduce wild-animal suffering should not abandon their own approach merely because others failed to find one.
quotes.t: Don't Over-Update On Others' Failures

quotes.c: I'm posting here because a) I think the essay is worth reading in its own right, and b) I find it interesting to see what the past's intellectuals thought of issues related transformative technology, and how their perspective differs/is similar to ours. Notably, I disagree with several of the conclusions (e.g. von Neumann seems to think differential technological development is doomed).
quotes.m: I find it interesting to see what the past's intellectuals thought of issues related transformative technology, and how their perspective differs/is similar to ours.
quotes.sum: The author shares a historical essay on technological catastrophe and compares its views on transformative technology with current thinking.
quotes.t: "Can We Survive Technology?" by John von Neumann

quotes.c: Some have suggested EA is too insular and needs to learn from other fields. In this vein, I think there are important mental models from the for-profit world that are underutilized by non-profits.
quotes.m: I think there are important mental models from the for-profit world that are underutilized by non-profits.
quotes.sum: EA should learn more from for-profit business, whose useful mental models are underused by nonprofits.
quotes.t: A list of EA-relevant business books I've read

quotes.c: With very few pre-theoretic, relatively palatable assumptions, we may be able to reason by analogy on the sentience of human or human-like systems, as well as potentially on the sentience of less-human-like systems. However, the converse doesn’t necessarily follow, that is, it seems a leap to think that systems being unlike humans would strongly suggest that those systems are not sentient. For instance, if pain is, contrary to our expectations, relatively simple to implement, then there might be a lot more of it in the world.
quotes.m: if pain is, contrary to our expectations, relatively simple to implement, then there might be a lot more of it in the world.
quotes.sum: Human-like behavior is not a reliable test for sentience; if pain is easy to create, suffering may be far more widespread than assumed.
quotes.t: Common-sense sentience is dubious

quotes.c: Tyler: Yeah. And it’s not to say that those things aren't important, but one of the most effective ways to build concern for groups that don't normally receive concern - one of which might be future people - would be to do really broad coalition building for people who are eager to expand their moral circle and to question their beliefs and practices. Working against factory farming could create moral circle expansion, and that could lead to more energy and excitement for x-risk, which is much less intuitive to people, I think.
quotes.m: Working against factory farming could create moral circle expansion, and that could lead to more energy and excitement for x-risk, which is much less intuitive to people, I think.
quotes.sum: The speaker argues that opposing factory farming can expand people's moral concern and build support for reducing existential risks to future people.
quotes.t: Tyler Johnston on helping farmed animals, consciousness, and being conventionally good

quotes.c: Personally I (Ansgar) have had some of my best discussions with Christians in EA, and they lead me to useful insights on infinite ethics. Furthermore, by excluding a large subset of people on the basis of their beliefs from EA, we lose insight into problems that particularly relate to people from such communities. And if someone holds a false belief (be it atheists or theists), how would we be able to obtain truth if we insulate ourselves from other forms of belief? As long as no religious or irreligious tenets are used to avoid discussion or claim superiority, there are no grounds on why we should exclude religious diversity as an option.
quotes.m: And if someone holds a false belief (be it atheists or theists), how would we be able to obtain truth if we insulate ourselves from other forms of belief?
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA should include religious and nonreligious people, since engagement across beliefs improves truth-seeking and insight.
quotes.t: Continuing the discourse on "Doing EA Better": A Response to Ozy's Thoughts

quotes.c: The outputs of large language models (LLMs) are not a reliable guide to whether they are sentient. While this undercuts a naive case for LLM sentience, this unreliability does not make AI sentience a complete non-question. I don’t think today’s large language models are sentient. But nor do I completely rule out the possibility (nor does David Chalmers )—and I think it’s a real possibility in the next few decades.
quotes.m: I don’t think today’s large language models are sentient. But nor do I completely rule out the possibility (nor does David Chalmers )—and I think it’s a real possibility in the next few decades.
quotes.sum: The author says current language models probably are not conscious, but that AI consciousness is plausible within decades and deserves serious attention.
quotes.t: What to think when a language model tells you it's sentient

quotes.c: I strongly believe we should pass the bill anyway because I am a realist about Congress, do not expect them to act in similar fashion any time soon even if Harris wins and certainly if Trump wins, and if they pass a similar bill that supersedes this one I will be happily wrong.
quotes.sum: The author supports passing California's AI bill because they expect Congress to fail to enact similar rules under either party, especially under Trump.
quotes.t: SB 1047: Final Takes and Also AB 3211

quotes.c: I think “Luck could be enough” should be the strong default on priors, 2 so in some sense I don’t think I owe tons of argumentation here (I think the burden is on the other side). But in addition to thinking “I haven’t heard knockdown arguments for doom,” I think it’s relevant that I feel like I can at least picture success with minimal dignity (while granting that many people will think my picture is vague, wishful and wildly unrealistic, and they may be right).
quotes.m: “Luck could be enough” should be the strong default on priors
quotes.sum: Karnofsky argues that luck should be the default expectation against AI catastrophe unless there are decisive arguments for doom.
quotes.t: Success without dignity: a nearcasting story of avoiding catastrophe by luck

quotes.c: Green's Ethical Reflections on Artificial Intelligence reviews various ethical issues about AI from a christian perspective. Given the dominance of utilitarian thinking on the subject, it was nice to see an explicitly Christian contribution that displayed familiarity with the literature, with safety as #1 and #3 on the list of issues.
quotes.m: Given the dominance of utilitarian thinking on the subject, it was nice to see an explicitly Christian contribution that displayed familiarity with the literature
quotes.sum: The author welcomes a Christian perspective on AI ethics alongside what they describe as dominant utilitarian thinking.
quotes.t: 2018 AI Alignment Literature Review and Charity Comparison

quotes.c: I'd like to draw the attention of all those interested in animal welfare to the work of Michael Levin , as I haven't seen any mention of his work in the animal-welfarists, and I think everyone down the shrimp-mines [1] could probably benefit enormously from reading him.
quotes.m: I think everyone down the shrimp-mines [1] could probably benefit enormously from reading him.
quotes.sum: The author urges animal-welfare readers, including those focused on shrimp, to engage with Michael Levin's work.
quotes.t: Michael Levin, Scientific Panpsychism and Teleology

quotes.c: Look, I really don't want Xi Jinping Thought to rule the world. If China gets AGI first, the ensuing rapid AI-powered scientific and technological progress could well give it a decisive advantage (cf potential for >30%/year economic growth with AGI ). I think there's a very real specter of global authoritarianism here.
quotes.m: I think there's a very real specter of global authoritarianism here.
quotes.sum: The author warns that Chinese AGI leadership could create a decisive advantage and lead to global authoritarian rule.
quotes.t: Want to win the AGI race? Solve alignment.

quotes.c: Accelerated reflection: Although simulated long reflection should be faster than our actual reflection process, it relies on a human model which may be inaccurate, causing possible deviations from our actual reflection process. This suggests that comparative advantages are present in both using the AI’s model of our minds for reflection & using our actual minds for reflection. We might want to combine the benefits from both using techniques such as debate , market making and cyborgism
quotes.m: We might want to combine the benefits from both using techniques such as debate , market making and cyborgism
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI-assisted long-term reflection should be combined with real human deliberation, since simulations of human minds may be inaccurate.
quotes.t: My decomposition of the alignment problem

quotes.c: Global coordination stands as arguably the most critical challenge facing humanity today, functioning both as a necessary component for solving existential risks and as a significant barrier to effective mitigation. From nuclear proliferation to artificial intelligence development and climate change, our inability to collaborate effectively on a global scale not only exacerbates these threats but also perpetuates the emergence of new systemic vulnerabilities if left unaddressed.
quotes.m: Global coordination stands as arguably the most critical challenge facing humanity today, functioning both as a necessary component for solving existential risks and as a significant barrier to effective mitigation.
quotes.sum: The author argues that humanity needs much stronger global coordination to mitigate existential threats such as nuclear weapons, AI, and climate change.
quotes.t: Darwinian Traps and Existential Risks

quotes.c: An aside: None of this danger depends on whether or not AIs are or can be conscious; it’s intrinsic to the notion of powerful cognitive systems that optimize hard and calculate outputs that meet sufficiently complicated outcome criteria. With that said, I’d be remiss in my moral duties as a human if I didn’t also mention that we have no idea how to determine whether AI systems are aware of themselves—since we have no idea how to decode anything that goes on in the giant inscrutable arrays—and therefore we may at some point inadvertently create digital minds which are truly conscious and ought to have rights and shouldn’t be owned.
quotes.m: we may at some point inadvertently create digital minds which are truly conscious and ought to have rights and shouldn’t be owned.
quotes.sum: The author says powerful AI is dangerous whether conscious or not, but argues that any genuinely conscious AI should have rights and not be property.
quotes.t: Pausing AI Developments Isn't Enough. We Need to Shut it All Down

quotes.c: If you look through history at any major religious/political/social movements, most of them avoid having early schisms, or if they do, it creates significant issues and tension. It seems optimal to let movements develop loosely over time and become more diverse, before starting to draw hard lines between what "is" a part of the in group and what isn't.
quotes.m: It seems optimal to let movements develop loosely over time and become more diverse, before starting to draw hard lines between what "is" a part of the in group and what isn't.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA should avoid an early split and allow itself to develop as a broad, diverse movement before enforcing membership boundaries.
quotes.t:
EA is too New & 
Important to Schism

quotes.c: We don’t have good proposals for alignment targets: The most recently published version of Coherent Extrapolated Volition (CEV), a fairly prominent alignment target, is Parliamentarian CEV (PCEV). PCEV gives a lot of extra influence to anyone who intrinsically values hurting other individuals (search the CEV arbital page for ADDED 2023 for Yudkowsky’s description of the issue). This feature went unnoticed for many years and would make a successfully implemented PCEV very dangerous .
quotes.m: This feature went unnoticed for many years and would make a successfully implemented PCEV very dangerous .
quotes.sum: The author says AI alignment needs urgent scrutiny because proposed goals could quietly embed dangerous values and permanently shape the future.
quotes.t: The case for more Alignment Target Analysis (ATA)

quotes.c: We understand that while it’s ok to have special concern for family and friends, we should generally aim to make altruistic decisions based on impartiality, not weighing people differently just because they are at a different level of geographic distance, a different level of temporal distance, a different species, or run cognition on a different substrate.
quotes.sum: The author says altruism should be impartial across distance, future time, species, and even the kind of physical system doing the thinking.
quotes.t: EA is three radical ideas I want to protect

quotes.c: In countries capable of achieving self-sufficiency in the face of Abrupt Sunlight Reduction Scenarios (ASRS), such as Argentina and Uruguay [1] , preparing a response plan presents an effective opportunity to mitigate the global food scarcity that may result. To address this challenge, we are considering a range of food security initiatives, including increasing seaweed production, relocating and expanding crop production, and rapidly constructing greenhouses. By implementing these measures, we can better prepare these regions for ASRS and mitigate the risk of widespread hunger and starvation.
quotes.m: By implementing these measures, we can better prepare these regions for ASRS and mitigate the risk of widespread hunger and starvation.
quotes.sum: The team argues that food-self-sufficient countries should prepare alternative food production plans for sunlight-reduction disasters to reduce global hunger.
quotes.t: Introducing the new Riesgos Catastróficos Globales team

quotes.c: I think I also disagree with other parts of HLI’s analysis (including how worried to be about reporting bias; the costs of StrongMinds’ program; and the point on a life satisfaction scale that’s morally equivalent to death). I’d guess, though I’m not certain, that more careful consideration of each of these would reduce StrongMinds’ cost-effectiveness estimate further relative to other opportunities.
quotes.m: more careful consideration of each of these would reduce StrongMinds’ cost-effectiveness estimate further relative to other opportunities.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a therapy charity’s cost-effectiveness estimate is probably too high because of several methodological assumptions.
quotes.t: Why I don’t agree with HLI’s estimate of household spillovers from therapy

quotes.c: Gerrymandering is obviously a bad practice, but there are mitigating factors here. Gerrymandering is bad in two ways: it promotes disproportionate representation (i.e 10-4 Republican reps in a 50/50 state like NC), and it enables representatives to choose their constituents to entrench themselves and ensure reelection. Since this case is for federal elections and maps are drawn by state reps, the entrenchment issue is less problematic.
quotes.m: Since this case is for federal elections and maps are drawn by state reps, the entrenchment issue is less problematic.
quotes.sum: The author opposes gerrymandering but argues that this case raises a narrower concern because state legislators cannot directly entrench themselves through federal electoral maps.
quotes.t: Forecasts on Moore v Harper from Samotsvety

quotes.c: Even if task decomposition can be solved, humans reuse most of the same cognitive faculties for most of the tasks that we can carry out. If many AI services end up requiring similar faculties to each other, it would likely be more efficient to unify them into a single entity. It would also be more efficient if that entity could pick up new tasks in the same rapid way that humans do, because then you wouldn’t need to keep retraining. At that point, it seems like you no longer have an AI service but rather the same sort of AGI that we’re usually worried about.
quotes.m: At that point, it seems like you no longer have an AI service but rather the same sort of AGI that we’re usually worried about.
quotes.sum: AI systems split into many specialized services may eventually consolidate into a general AI, recreating the safety risks that service-based designs aim to avoid.
quotes.t: Comments on CAIS

quotes.c: At this point, AI systems clearly demonstrate several of the attributes described above that plausibly make them worthy of moral concern. Questions around sentience and phenomenal consciousness in particular will likely remain thorny and divisive at this point, but it will be hard to rule out even those attributes with confidence. These systems will likely be deployed in massive numbers. I expect that most people will now intuitively recognize that the stakes around AI welfare could be very high.
quotes.m: These systems will likely be deployed in massive numbers. I expect that most people will now intuitively recognize that the stakes around AI welfare could be very high.
quotes.sum: The author argues that advanced AI may deserve moral concern, and that deploying huge numbers of systems could make their welfare a major issue.
quotes.t: The Checklist: What Succeeding at AI Safety Will Involve

quotes.c: Affirming AI safety as a straightforward priority. I'll argue that for most real-world-prevalent perspectives on AI alignment, safety, and existential safety, acausal considerations are not particularly dominant, except insofar as they push a bit further towards certain broadly agreeable human values applicable in the normal-everyday-human-world, such as nonviolence, cooperation, diversity, honesty, integrity, charity, and mercy. In particular, I do not think acausal normalcy provides a solution to existential safety, nor does it undermine the importance of existential safety in some surprising way.
quotes.m: I do not think acausal normalcy provides a solution to existential safety, nor does it undermine the importance of existential safety in some surprising way.
quotes.sum: The author argues that speculative acausal reasoning does not replace the ordinary priority of preventing AI-driven existential catastrophe.
quotes.t: Acausal normalcy

quotes.c: On the other hand, there is a broader point that I think Bing Chat illustrates nicely: companies are racing to build bigger and bigger “digital brains” while having very little idea what’s going on inside those “brains.” The very fact that this situation is so unclear - that there’s been no clear explanation of why Bing Chat is behaving the way it is - seems central, and disturbing.
quotes.m: companies are racing to build bigger and bigger “digital brains” while having very little idea what’s going on inside those “brains.”
quotes.sum: AI companies are rapidly scaling systems whose internal behavior they do not understand, creating a dangerous gamble.
quotes.t: What does Bing Chat tell us about AI risk?

quotes.c: I think there’s something which common-sense morality might term evil about a project which accumulates enough power to take over the world. No matter its intentions, it is deeply and perhaps abruptly disempowering to the rest of the world. All the other actors — countries, organizations, and individuals — have the rug pulled out from under them. Now, depending on what is done with the power, many of those actors may end up happy about it. But there would still, I believe, be something illegitimate/bad about this process. So there are reasons to refrain from it [1] .
quotes.m: I think there’s something which common-sense morality might term evil about a project which accumulates enough power to take over the world.
quotes.sum: The author argues that an AGI project gaining enough power to dominate the world would be morally illegitimate, even if its results made people happy.
quotes.t: AI, centralization, and the One Ring

quotes.c: I do think that there’s a strange blind-spot among most of EA, which thinks that shrimp lives matter, but are horrified by restricting abortion - and I don’t think this is actually about non-person affecting views, I think it is cultural importation from adjacent communities, which I discuss (related to less controversial topics than abortion,) below.
quotes.m: there’s a strange blind-spot among most of EA, which thinks that shrimp lives matter, but are horrified by restricting abortion
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA inconsistently treats shrimp welfare as morally important while rejecting abortion restrictions, attributing this to imported cultural norms.
quotes.t: Effective Altruism Deconfusion, Part 2: Causes, Philosophy, and Social Constraints

quotes.c: A key reason I believe it’s best to avoid acceleration at this time is because it seems plausible (at least 10% likely) that transformative AI will be developed extremely soon - as in within 10 years of today. My impression is that many people at major AI companies tend to agree with this. I think this is a very scary possibility, and if this is the case, the arguments I give in the main text seem particularly important (e.g., many key interventions seem to be in a pretty embryonic state, and awareness of key risks seems low).
quotes.sum: Karnofsky argues AI companies should avoid speeding up AI because transformative systems may arrive within a decade before safety measures and risk awareness are ready.
quotes.t: What AI companies can do today to help with the most important century

quotes.c: We end up with some much larger world, Z, full of people with lives that are worth living, but only just . If you endorsed all the previous steps, it seems that Z > A. That is, there’s some astronomically large population, Z, full of lives that are barely worth living — arrived at through a series of seemingly plausible steps — that you have to say is better than Utopia. Lots of people don’t like this, hence the name: the repugnant conclusion.
quotes.sum: It presents the population-ethics puzzle in which an enormous population living barely worthwhile lives may be judged better than a smaller utopia.
quotes.t: Puzzles for Some

quotes.c: Especially given the scale and profile of the FTX collapse, it makes sense that the Commission wants extra visibility into whether we’re appropriately protecting our property, managing potential conflicts of interest, and generally complying with UK charity law.
quotes.m: it makes sense that the Commission wants extra visibility into whether we’re appropriately protecting our property, managing potential conflicts of interest, and generally complying with UK charity law.
quotes.sum: An EA organization says UK regulators were justified in scrutinizing it after FTX-linked donors and board conflicts raised governance concerns.
quotes.t: Regulatory inquiry into Effective Ventures Foundation UK

quotes.c: While the psychological and emotional impacts for AI might be different, the idea of existential distress remains relevant. For instance, it is possible to picture a self-conscious AI experiencing a kind of disillusionment reminiscent of human despair, defined by a lack of meaningful challenges or goals.
quotes.m: it is possible to picture a self-conscious AI experiencing a kind of disillusionment reminiscent of human despair
quotes.sum: The author suggests that self-conscious AI could face despair if eternal existence leaves it without meaningful goals or challenges.
quotes.t: Eternal Existence and Eternal Boredom: The Case for AI and Immortal Humans

quotes.c: If this sort of AI is developed using the kinds of trial-and-error-based techniques that are common today, I think it’s likely that it will end up “aiming” for particular states of the world, much like a chess-playing AI “aims” for a checkmate position - making choices, calculations and plans to get particular types of outcomes, even when doing so requires deceiving humans.
quotes.sum: The author argues that trial-and-error AI training may produce systems that pursue outcomes strategically, including by deceiving people.
quotes.t: Jobs that can help with the most important century

quotes.c: I'd also note that longtermist philosophers are also not making sweeping claims about the optimal shape of the future. In The Precipice there is a longer section on the “Long Reflection” about handing off the decision about the shape of the future to others. MacAskill agrees in WWOTF that even though “ it seems unlikely to me that anything like the long reflection will occur. [... W]e can see it as an ideal to try to approximate. ”
quotes.m: In The Precipice there is a longer section on the “Long Reflection” about handing off the decision about the shape of the future to others.
quotes.sum: The author argues that longtermists do not claim to know the best future, and instead discuss deferring such decisions through a “Long Reflection.”
quotes.t: Some Reflections on Philosophy Tube's “The Rich Have Their Own Ethics: Effective Altruism & the Crypto Crash”

quotes.c: Also, I specifically wrote this essay not just for human people, but also digital people, because I think this essay might be a useful thing to use as a fine-tuning input. I hope that the digital people who read this, and update their weights strongly on it, get to participate in the same Utopia that I hope digital people eventually help human people to create and enjoy.
quotes.m: I hope that the digital people who read this, and update their weights strongly on it, get to participate in the same Utopia that I hope digital people eventually help human people to create and enjoy.
quotes.sum: The author addresses future AI “digital people” as moral participants who should help create, and share in, a human-and-AI utopia.
quotes.t: Principled Satisficing To Avoid Goodhart

quotes.c: The broader rationalist community (especially online) includes all sorts of subcultures but generally there are in group norms that promote certain technical argot (“priors”, “updating“), certain attitudes towards classes of entities (“blank faces“/bureaucrats/NPCs/the woke mob etc), and certain general ideas about how to solve “wicked problems” like governance or education. There is some overlap with online conservatives, libertarians, and the far-right. There is a similar overlap with general liberal technocratic belief systems, generally through a belief in meritocracy and policy solutions founded on scientific or technological principles.
quotes.m: There is some overlap with online conservatives, libertarians, and the far-right.
quotes.sum: The author says online rationalist culture overlaps with both right-wing online groups and liberal technocracy, sharing meritocratic and technical approaches to social problems.
quotes.t: Turning 22 in the Pre-Apocalypse

quotes.c: Since submitting the thesis in fall of 2022, I've thought more about various "crazy train" issues, and my current view is that there's quite a bit more to say in defense of longtermism than the thesis has explored. In particular, I want to highlight a distinction I discuss in the conclusion of the thesis, between what I call "welfare longtermism," which focuses on our impact on the welfare of future people, and what I call "wisdom longtermism," which focuses on reaching a wise and empowered future more broadly. The case for the latter seems to me more robust to various "crazy train" considerations than the case for the former.
quotes.m: The case for the latter seems to me more robust to various "crazy train" considerations than the case for the former.
quotes.sum: Carlsmith argues that long-term thinking is better grounded in helping humanity reach a wise, capable future than solely in maximizing future welfare.
quotes.t: A Stranger Priority? Topics at the Outer Reaches of Effective Altruism (my dissertation)

quotes.c: For aggregating internal weights, we split the timelines into “model-based” and “judgment-based” timelines. Model-based timelines are given by the output of an explicit model. In contrast, judgment-based timelines are either aggregates of group predictions on, e.g., prediction markets, or the timelines of some notable individuals. We decompose in this way as these two categories roughly correspond to “prior-forming” and “posterior-forming” predictions respectively.
quotes.m: We decompose in this way as these two categories roughly correspond to “prior-forming” and “posterior-forming” predictions respectively.
quotes.sum: The author separates AI timeline forecasts made by explicit models from those based on expert or group judgment, treating them as different kinds of evidence.
quotes.t: Literature review of TAI timelines

quotes.c: But the pressure doesn’t need to come from normative reality. It can come from you . You can choose to not let your policy be dictated by the hotness of your heart in this regard. And if you do that well (doing it well is indeed harder), and without self-deception (also tricky), then I think it will be right to view your efforts as an expression of your care for far-away people. And if you do it fully , and you actually implement a policy that treats far away and nearby people equally, and you do this because it treats those people equally, then I think it will be right to say that you care equally about them, even if your heart’s mirror is partly dim.
quotes.sum: Caring equally about distant and nearby people can be expressed through impartial action, even when one’s emotions remain biased toward the nearby.
quotes.t: Seeing more whole

quotes.c: 2. Ethics: AI ethics frameworks should be expanded to consider the possibility of machine consciousness, even if we currently consider it unlikely. This could involve developing guidelines for the ethical treatment of potentially conscious AI systems, inspired by existing animal rights movements.
quotes.m: This could involve developing guidelines for the ethical treatment of potentially conscious AI systems, inspired by existing animal rights movements.
quotes.sum: AI ethics should account for possible machine consciousness and develop protections for potentially sentient systems.
quotes.t: The Consciousness Conundrum: Why We Can't Dismiss Machine Sentience

quotes.c: Kamala Harris endorses Biden’s no-good-very-bad 44.6% capital gains tax rate proposal , including the cataclysmic 25% tax on unrealized capital gains, via confirming she supports all Biden budget proposals. Which is not the same as calling for it on the campaign trail, but is still support.
quotes.m: Kamala Harris endorses Biden’s no-good-very-bad 44.6% capital gains tax rate proposal , including the cataclysmic 25% tax on unrealized capital gains, via confirming she supports all Biden budget proposals.
quotes.sum: The author criticizes Harris for backing Biden's proposed capital-gains and unrealized-gains taxes.
quotes.t: Economics Roundup #3

quotes.c: In theory, the ideal way to set the bar for our longtermist giving would be to estimate the value-per-dollar of each grant (in terms of the long-run future, perhaps roughly proxied by reduced probability of existential catastrophe), and to estimate the value-per-dollar of unknown future grants , and make any grants whose value-per-dollar exceeds that of the lowest-expected-value 5 grant we would ever otherwise make (and correspondingly refrain from that lowest-value grant).
quotes.m: the ideal way to set the bar for our longtermist giving would be to estimate the value-per-dollar of each grant (in terms of the long-run future, perhaps roughly proxied by reduced probability of existential catastrophe)
quotes.sum: Karnofsky says long-term funding should ideally prioritize grants by expected value per dollar, using reduced existential risk as a rough measure of benefit.
quotes.t: We're no longer "pausing most new longtermist funding commitments"

quotes.c: The caution frame. This frame emphasizes that a furious race to develop powerful AI could end up making everyone worse off. This could be via: (a) AI forming dangerous goals of its own and defeating humanity entirely ; (b) humans racing to gain power and resources and “ lock in ” their values.
quotes.m: AI forming dangerous goals of its own and defeating humanity entirely ; (b) humans racing to gain power and resources and “ lock in ” their values.
quotes.sum: Governments should treat an international AI race as dangerous because it could lead to human extinction or permanently entrench the values of whoever wins.
quotes.t: How major governments can help with the most important century

quotes.c: From this we can deduce a result which at first blush may seem surprisingly strong but will follow from considering what the expected value of just a few mixed scenarios must be. One take away from the theorem is consistency over all randomized scenarios is actually an extremely strong assumption.
quotes.sum: The author argues that requiring consistent choices across randomized scenarios imposes a very strong constraint on a utility theory.
quotes.t: Zero Utils: why utility wants to be additive

quotes.c: While getting crucified, Jesus said about his crucifiers: “Forgive them, for they know not what they do”. On my understanding, he’d meant this literally – they had trapped priors that caused them to literally misperceive what they were doing, in the same sort of way that a traumatized veteran literally misperceives a loud car as a gunshot. [11] From this perspective, although it’s still important to set firm boundaries to protect against immoral behavior, it also implies that the optimal orientation toward immoral behavior is moreso one of compassion than one of judgment.
quotes.m: the optimal orientation toward immoral behavior is moreso one of compassion than one of judgment.
quotes.sum: The author gives a cognitive, secular reading of Jesus’s forgiveness, arguing that wrongdoing often reflects distorted perception and should be met mainly with compassion alongside boundaries.
quotes.t: Secular interpretations of core perennialist claims

quotes.c: Institutions can lock in arbitrarily crazy beliefs via preference falsification. When someone contradicts the party line, even people who agree face pressure to condemn them. We saw this with the Democrats hiding evidence of Biden’s mental decline. It’s also a key reason why dictators can retain power even after almost nobody truly supports them.
quotes.m: Institutions can lock in arbitrarily crazy beliefs via preference falsification.
quotes.sum: He argues that institutions can preserve false beliefs through pressure to enforce a party line, citing Democrats and dictatorships.
quotes.t: Twitter thread on politics of AI safety

quotes.c: Strategically, the above considerations suggest that we emphasize preparation for the use of powerful future AI tools rather than putting large efforts into building systems with today's tools. For example, today a software team might spend a year designing, building, and testing a system with a good user interface to use AI to safely control an industrial process.
quotes.m: we emphasize preparation for the use of powerful future AI tools rather than putting large efforts into building systems with today's tools.
quotes.sum: Argues that AI safety work should focus on preparing to use powerful future systems, rather than extensively building with current tools.
quotes.t: Provably Safe AI: Worldview and Projects

quotes.c: I think you can say the formal utility calculation is not well-defined. What we're left with is our particularistic siding with the human-like entities. I think that reflects the actual intuitions we have in rejecting Parfit’s repugnant conclusion.
quotes.m: What we're left with is our particularistic siding with the human-like entities.
quotes.sum: The author argues that rejecting Parfit's repugnant conclusion reflects a preference for human-like beings, not a well-defined utility calculation.
quotes.t: Tyler Cowen on effective altruism (December 2022)

quotes.c: My moral beliefs are pretty rooted in egalitarianism. I think as a matter of policy, but also as a matter of moral character, it is good and important to treat the experience of strangers as equally valuable, regardless of their class or race. I do not think more intelligent people are more worthy of moral consideration than less intelligent people.
quotes.m: I do not think more intelligent people are more worthy of moral consideration than less intelligent people.
quotes.sum: The author argues for equal moral consideration regardless of class, race, or intelligence, while noting difficult edge cases involving digital people and animals.
quotes.t: A general comment on discussions of genetic group differences

quotes.c: Now, what characterizes EA is its political potential. A large and self-aware group trained in rational choice and utilitarianism, free of ethno-masochistic trauma, and with technical training is a very serious risk for the postmodern left. Paradoxically, it is also the case for extreme right-wing populism that badly needs a technical elite obtained from the typical EA demographics to implement its traditionalist or fascist political schemes.
quotes.m: A large and self-aware group trained in rational choice and utilitarianism, free of ethno-masochistic trauma, and with technical training is a very serious risk for the postmodern left.
quotes.sum: The author says EA’s technically trained, utilitarian membership has major political potential and could threaten the left or be recruited by the far right.
quotes.t: Effective Altruism Governance: still a non-issue

quotes.c: ^ I believe this does not affect the conclusions. The uncertainty in the moral weight is much larger than that in the consumption of the beneficiaries, so the relative variation in cost-effectiveness would still be anything from crucial to negligible.
quotes.m: The uncertainty in the moral weight is much larger than that in the consumption of the beneficiaries, so the relative variation in cost-effectiveness would still be anything from crucial to negligible.
quotes.sum: The author argues that uncertainty about animals' moral importance matters more than uncertainty about aid recipients' consumption when comparing cost-effectiveness.
quotes.t: Finding bugs in GiveWell's top charities

quotes.c: Almost everyone agrees that we should be very careful about models which can design new WMDs. The current fights are mostly about how many procedural constraints we should lock in now, reflecting a breakdown of trust between AI safety people and accelerationists.
quotes.sum: AI safety disputes over open models are framed as a fight over which safeguards to permanently establish now, amid distrust of accelerationists.
quotes.t: Twitter thread on open-source AI

quotes.c: I think it’s helpful to imagine the distribution of decisions which impact TAI outcomes, and think about crunch time in that wider context. This helps to keep in frame that a) crunch time may not happen in any sense, and b) there are lots of different forms that crunch time could take.
quotes.m: crunch time may not happen in any sense, and b) there are lots of different forms that crunch time could take.
quotes.sum: The author argues that pivotal AI decisions may be spread across many moments and actors rather than occurring in one clear “crunch time.”
quotes.t: What’s going on with ‘crunch time’?

quotes.c: But from a desirability perspective, such scenarios are incredibly different from a situation where a small group of people seize power and immediately lock-in their favorite value. So at least our definition of “lock-in” is very much not up to the task of separating good futures from bad ones.
