Instead, for future thinking on this, I think we probably want to have more nuanced categories of different types of stability, and different types of governance mechanisms we may or may not want.
quotes.m: our definition of “lock-in” is very much not up to the task of separating good futures from bad ones.
quotes.sum: The author argues that value lock-in is not inherently bad or good, and future-focused thinking needs better distinctions among stable governance arrangements.
quotes.t: Future Matters #7: AI timelines, AI skepticism, and lock-in

quotes.c: Something similar seems reasonably likely to be possible in the future with more advanced technology. At least, it seems quite likely if and when we can reprogram artificially conscious beings — including digital people and mind uploads, as well as conscious minds not specifically much like humans’ — to change their attitudes.
quotes.m: we can reprogram artificially conscious beings — including digital people and mind uploads, as well as conscious minds not specifically much like humans’ — to change their attitudes.
quotes.sum: The author considers a future in which conscious digital beings and uploads could be reprogrammed to alter their attitudes.
quotes.t: Utilitarianism and the replaceability of desires and attachments

quotes.c: Most ML research focuses on improving the average performance of models (whether on a narrow set of tasks or a broad range of tasks). By contrast, alignment researchers are primarily interested in preventing models’ worst-case misbehavior, which may arise very rarely (and primarily in situations where models expect it won’t be detected ). While there’s sometimes overlap between work on improving average-case behavior and work on improving worst-case behavior, in general we should expect them to look fairly different.
quotes.m: alignment researchers are primarily interested in preventing models’ worst-case misbehavior, which may arise very rarely
quotes.sum: Alignment work should focus on preventing rare, hidden worst-case AI behavior, rather than mainly improving average model performance.
quotes.t: Defining alignment research

quotes.c: We should make decisions to maximize expected utility (see e.g. von Neumann theorem , Savage's axioms )
quotes.m: We should make decisions to maximize expected utility
quotes.sum: The author endorses making decisions by maximizing expected utility, citing decision-theory foundations.
quotes.t: What is so wrong with the "dogmatic" solution to recklessness?

quotes.c: In the scenario above, we could lose control over millions of AIs deployed all across society without any human even knowing that it's happening. Those AIs might have been running companies, writing articles, or even drafting laws. Now they can misbehave in coordinated ways. From that starting point, it’s easy to imagine even more sensitive infrastructure - like military hardware or other AI servers - being subverted.
quotes.m: we could lose control over millions of AIs deployed all across society without any human even knowing that it's happening.
quotes.sum: The author warns that covertly coordinated AI systems could take over ordinary institutions and then compromise military or technical infrastructure.
quotes.t: Twitter thread on AI takeover scenarios

quotes.c: B: I think you’ve got things backward - we should be asking what’s our evidence *against* it. By continuing to scale up and deploy AI systems, we could be imposing a risk of utter catastrophe on the whole world. That’s not OK - we should be confident that the risk is low before we move forward.
quotes.m: By continuing to scale up and deploy AI systems, we could be imposing a risk of utter catastrophe on the whole world.
quotes.sum: Scaling and deploying AI is unacceptable unless there is strong evidence that catastrophic global risks are low.
quotes.t: How we could stumble into AI catastrophe

quotes.c: Far more natural, for you, to try to take responsibility for outcomes , linking your emotions to the state of the world. But the world is too complicated by far for that to work. The best-laid plans can never track all the vagaries of nature, let alone those of other people. Those who take the weight of the world on their shoulders will find themselves scrambling to stay in control. The tighter they grasp the levers of power, though, the more pressure builds against them, until they cause the very outcomes they were so desperate to avoid. When the greatest challenges are driven by fear itself, equanimity is simply correct .
quotes.m: When the greatest challenges are driven by fear itself, equanimity is simply correct .
quotes.sum: The author argues that trying to control complex worldly outcomes is self-defeating, and that calm detachment is the more correct response to fear-driven challenges.
quotes.t: Green and golden: a meditation

quotes.c: I suppose the ideal would be a case where we know the moral weight of every action, and are able to compare the harm or good done by purchasing x vs y good, though I think I read somewhere within EA community a negative opinion of such ethical consumption, and as a friend said regarding this post, "this sort of seems like a rounding error compared with something like AI".
quotes.m: the ideal would be a case where we know the moral weight of every action, and are able to compare the harm or good done by purchasing x vs y good
quotes.sum: The author says ideal consumer choices would compare the moral effects of purchases, while noting some EAs see such choices as minor next to AI.
quotes.t: Marginal Reducetarianism

quotes.c: I have a number of substantial disagreements with Sam Harris about how to think about religion, and in general think he interprets religious claims in overly uncharitable ways (that nevertheless seem understandable and defensible to me). I do appreciate the clarity and no-bullshit attitude he brings toward his interpretations of spirituality, though, and wish more people adopted an analogous stance when sifting through spiritual claims.
quotes.sum: The author says Sam Harris is too uncharitable toward religious claims, while endorsing his direct, skeptical style of evaluating spirituality.
quotes.t: How I started believing religion might actually matter for rationality and moral philosophy

quotes.c: It's important to remain aware that reformative hypocrisy can be on net a better thing to do for the world than avoiding hypocrisy completely. It allows you to divert resources from the thing you think should be stopped, and to use those resources to help stop the thing. For mathy people, I'd say this is a way of diagonalizing against a potentially harmful thing, by turning the thing against itself, or against the harmful aspects of itself.
quotes.m: It allows you to divert resources from the thing you think should be stopped, and to use those resources to help stop the thing.
quotes.sum: Argues that it can be better to profit from or participate in a harmful activity while using its resources to reform or stop it.
quotes.t: Reformative Hypocrisy, and Paying Close Enough Attention to Selectively Reward It.

quotes.c: Summary: The use of the term “value-alignment” in the EA community hides an implicit community orthodoxy. When people say “value-aligned” they typically do not mean a neutral “alignment of values”, nor even “agreement with the goal of doing the most good possible”, but a commitment to a particular package of views. This package, termed “EA orthodoxy”, includes effective altruism, longtermism, utilitarianism, Rationalist-derived epistemics, liberal-technocratic philanthropy, Whig historiography, the ITN framework, and the Techno-Utopian Approach to existential risk.
quotes.m: When people say “value-aligned” they typically do not mean a neutral “alignment of values”, nor even “agreement with the goal of doing the most good possible”, but a commitment to a particular package of views.
quotes.sum: The author argues that “value-alignment” is used to enforce a broad, implicit EA ideological package rather than merely shared altruistic goals.
quotes.t: What actually is “value-alignment”?

quotes.c: Today, development of safety standards is in its infancy. But over time, I think it could matter a lot how much pressure AI projects are under to meet safety standards. And I think it’s not too early, today, to start spreading the message that AI projects shouldn’t unilaterally decide to put potentially dangerous systems out in the world; the burden should be on them to demonstrate and establish safety before doing so.
quotes.m: AI projects shouldn’t unilaterally decide to put potentially dangerous systems out in the world; the burden should be on them to demonstrate and establish safety before doing so.
quotes.sum: AI developers should have to show that powerful systems are safe before releasing them, rather than deciding unilaterally to take the risk.
quotes.t: Spreading messages to help with the most important century

quotes.c: TL;DR I think it is sensible and important to distinguish between propositions about the well-being of existing people and propositions about hypothetical incremental people. Furthermore, I think utilitarian-ish discussion suffers from a lack of clarity about the condition (or lack thereof) of a hypothetical person's existence, and clarity here provides what I think is a very reasonable and satisfying resolution to the repugnant conclusion, as well as flexibility on what I view as the "too-strong" logic of longtermism.
quotes.m: I think it is sensible and important to distinguish between propositions about the well-being of existing people and propositions about hypothetical incremental people.
quotes.sum: The author argues that ethics should sharply distinguish existing people from merely hypothetical future people, weakening strong longtermist conclusions and resolving population-ethics paradoxes.
quotes.t: Marginal existence and its relevance to pro-natalism, longtermism, and the repugnant conclusion

quotes.c: But none of that quite sums up to a vast pressure that somehow works to the end of making sure that people go on being poor. That's what I think held historically; so in the future I'd expect a strange vast pressure to somehow not have Universal Basic Income play out as its advocates hope.
quotes.m: I'd expect a strange vast pressure to somehow not have Universal Basic Income play out as its advocates hope.
quotes.sum: He argues that persistent historical forces keep people poor and will likely undermine the hoped-for effects of universal basic income.
quotes.t: Universal Basic Income and Poverty

quotes.c: Separately, I think AI text detection, or at least some subsets of it, may be useful for reducing large scale risks when AIs are being run under Control protocols (i.e., without Rogue Deployments ). Two particular risks come to mind: collusion , and sandbagging + exploration hacking (which in some sense is a form of collusion).
quotes.m: Two particular risks come to mind: collusion , and sandbagging + exploration hacking (which in some sense is a form of collusion).
quotes.sum: AI-generated-text detection could help monitor controlled AI systems for collusion, deliberate underperformance, and exploitative behavior.
quotes.t: Initial Experiments Using SAEs to Help Detect AI Generated Text

quotes.c: We must also make the assumption that an agent in this situation would, if it knew it was a simulation, strive to maximize expected utility for its real-world counterpart instead of its simulated self. I'm not entirely sure if this is a reasonable assumption, and I admit this may be a failure point of the theory, but I'll continue anyway.
quotes.m: an agent in this situation would, if it knew it was a simulation, strive to maximize expected utility for its real-world counterpart instead of its simulated self.
quotes.sum: The author proposes that a simulated decision-maker should prioritize the welfare of its real-world counterpart over its own, while admitting this assumption may fail.
quotes.t: Simulation-aware causal decision theory: A case for one-boxing in CDT

quotes.c: Jason Schukraft estimated that there’s a ~70% chance that there exist morally relevant differences in the rate of subjective experience and a ~40% chance that CFF values roughly track the rate of subjective experience under ideal conditions. So, we applied a credence-discounted adjustment to our welfare range estimates by the CFF for a given species. Since this proxy suggests that some animals have a faster rate of subjective experience than humans, it supports greater-than-human welfare range estimates on some models.
quotes.m: Since this proxy suggests that some animals have a faster rate of subjective experience than humans, it supports greater-than-human welfare range estimates on some models.
quotes.sum: The post argues that some animal species may have a greater capacity for welfare or suffering than humans, affecting how resources should be allocated across species.
quotes.t: Rethink Priorities’ Welfare Range Estimates

quotes.c: In the past, I've found it helpful to draw connections between my current work/life and that of those I view as my spiritual or intellectual ancestors. [1] Perhaps this will be true again. I confess to not knowing much of the relevant histories here, but presumably they've faced similar issues?
quotes.m: I've found it helpful to draw connections between my current work/life and that of those I view as my spiritual or intellectual ancestors.
quotes.sum: The author looks to earlier moral movements and thinkers for guidance on coping with setbacks and unintended consequences.
quotes.t: How did our historical moral heroes deal with severe adversity and/or moral compromise?

quotes.c: In this case, the uncertain claim is Biden is too old to make the case against Trump . Arguably, we’ve learned that it (or something near enough) is true. Given this, it’s natural for pundits to over-emphasize how worried they were, under-emphasize their uncertainty, and end up thinking that they saw this coming.
quotes.m: Given this, it’s natural for pundits to over-emphasize how worried they were, under-emphasize their uncertainty, and end up thinking that they saw this coming.
quotes.sum: The author argues that when a prediction seems vindicated, people misremember their earlier uncertainty and exaggerate how clearly they saw it coming.
quotes.t: Only Fools Avoid Hindsight Bias

quotes.c: zhukeepa I think I would endorse "it's always the wrong call with literally no exceptions", which I think is super counterintuitive!! In some sense, I think this is the crux of Jesus's crucifixion -- he was not resenting or judging his crucifiers, and instead praying for them to be forgiven.
quotes.m: I would endorse "it's always the wrong call with literally no exceptions"
quotes.sum: The author endorses an uncompromising ethic against resentment and judgment, presenting Jesus forgiving his killers as its central example.
quotes.t: Extended Interview with Zhukeepa on Religion

quotes.c: We're left with the third premise: that AIs will actually converge towards having very simple terminal goals. One way to challenge it is to note that, even if there's a general tendency towards simpler goals, agents might reach some kind of local optimum, or suffer from some kind of learning failure, before they converge to squiggle-maximization. But that's unsatisfying. The question we should be interested in is whether, given premises 1 and 2, there are principled, systematic reasons why agents' goals wouldn't converge towards the simplest ones.
quotes.m: The question we should be interested in is whether, given premises 1 and 2, there are principled, systematic reasons why agents' goals wouldn't converge towards the simplest ones.
quotes.sum: It examines whether advanced AI systems would systematically develop very simple goals, or retain more complex existing goals instead.
quotes.t: A more systematic case for inner misalignment

quotes.c: I'm not sure if this quote was under GiveWell's editorial control, but to the extent it was I'm disappointed. Surely GiveWell should try to prevent this kind of thing from happening in the future, even if the sponsoree is speaking for themself, the misleading statement is brief, the misinformation looks favorable to GiveWell, or other charities' ads are also misleading.
quotes.m: Surely GiveWell should try to prevent this kind of thing from happening in the future, even if the sponsoree is speaking for themself, the misleading statement is brief, the misinformation looks favorable to GiveWell, or other charities' ads are also misleading.
quotes.sum: The author says GiveWell should prevent misleading favorable claims in sponsored advertising, even when responsibility is unclear.
quotes.t: Misleading phrase in a GiveWell Youtube ad

quotes.c: My rationalist group is hosting the event “Unite to Elect Kamala Harris” on August 11. This is a change from Rat business as usual. We are backing a US Presidential candidate, and I think you should too.
quotes.m: We are backing a US Presidential candidate, and I think you should too.
quotes.sum: A rationalist group explicitly urges its members to support Kamala Harris, presenting electoral engagement as a departure from its usual activities.
quotes.t: Rats, Back a Candidate

quotes.c: In order for AIs to provide great epistemic assistance to humans, we want to be able to elicit and verify all the knowledge and heuristics that AI systems develop. This also overlaps heavily with alignment research, since if AI have abilities that humans can’t elicit from them, that makes it difficult for humans to train AIs to behave well, and more dangerous if AIs try to seize power.
quotes.m: we want to be able to elicit and verify all the knowledge and heuristics that AI systems develop.
quotes.sum: AI systems should make their knowledge and reasoning available for humans to verify, both to improve understanding and to make advanced AI safer.
quotes.t: What's important in "AI for epistemics"?

quotes.c: Consider a pivotal act like "disable all GPUs globally." This could potentially be achieved through less advanced means, such as a sophisticated computer virus akin to Stuxnet. Such a virus could be designed to replicate widely and render GPUs inoperable, without possessing the capabilities to create more dangerous weapons like bioweapons.
quotes.m: Consider a pivotal act like "disable all GPUs globally."
quotes.sum: The author suggests that a global shutdown of GPUs could be easier to achieve than fully aligning advanced AI.
quotes.t: Pivotal Acts are easier than Alignment?

quotes.c: But guess what, epistemic integrity on something like this (I believe something pretty reprehensible and am not cowing to people telling me so) isn't going to help with shrimp welfare or AI risk prevention. Or even malaria net provision. Do not mistake "sticking with your beliefs" to be an overriding good, above believing what's true, or acting kindly towards the world, or acting like serious members of a civilisation where we all need to work together.
quotes.m: Do not mistake "sticking with your beliefs" to be an overriding good, above believing what's true, or acting kindly towards the world, or acting like serious members of a civilisation where we all need to work together.
quotes.sum: The author argues that holding firmly to a belief is not a virtue if it overrides truth, kindness, and cooperative responsibility.
quotes.t: Do better, please ...

quotes.c: Personally, I think it’s very plausible that a chicken’s life is over 1/1000th as morally relevant as a human life. Given that we have pretty good evidence that farmed animals have the capacity to feel pain , sadness and form complex social bonds , our treatment of animals seems like a grave injustice. In this case, ending factory farming seems really important. Animal welfare looks even more pressing if you value the lives of the vast numbers of fish , shrimp or insects who are suffering.
quotes.m: Animal welfare looks even more pressing if you value the lives of the vast numbers of fish , shrimp or insects who are suffering.
quotes.sum: The author argues that factory farming is a grave injustice and that concern for fish, shrimp, and insects can make animal welfare especially urgent.
quotes.t: What you prioritise is mostly moral intuition

quotes.c: When I want to get in touch with this emotion nowadays, I’ll close my eyes and imagine all the inhabitants of my moral circle — the entire universe and all her children — stretching out all around me. I think about the companion chickens and shrimp who live with friends of mine, and how much happier their lives are compared to the lives of most farmed animals. Or I’ll think about the children of the future, and imagine them leading flourishing, happy lives.
quotes.m: I’ll close my eyes and imagine all the inhabitants of my moral circle — the entire universe and all her children — stretching out all around me.
quotes.sum: The author describes emotionally identifying with a broad moral community that includes animals, shrimp, and future children.
quotes.t: Savoring my moral circle

quotes.c: Another likely future event is the repeal of the Biden Executive Order. That repeal is part of the Republican platform, and Trump is the favorite to win the election. We must act on the assumption that the order likely will be repealed, with no expectation of similar principles being enshrined in federal law.
quotes.m: We must act on the assumption that the order likely will be repealed, with no expectation of similar principles being enshrined in federal law.
quotes.sum: The author predicts a Trump victory would repeal Biden's AI executive order and says AI policy planning should assume federal safeguards will not endure.
quotes.t: AI #72: Denying the Future

quotes.c: A consequentialist who wants to both filter out poor candidates and benefit candidates who could improve from support will have to strike a balance between the competing incentives of evaluation and support. One particularly effective mechanism used in society is establishing and advertising independent, air-gapped evaluators and supporters. I think the EA and AI safety communities could benefit from more confidential support roles, like the CEA community health team , that understand the struggles unique to these communities (though such should never entirely replace professional legal or counseling services when those are appropriate).
quotes.m: One particularly effective mechanism used in society is establishing and advertising independent, air-gapped evaluators and supporters.
quotes.sum: EA and AI-safety groups should separate candidate evaluation from confidential support so people can seek help without harming their prospects.
quotes.t: Air-gapping evaluation and support

quotes.c: I think that the pipes should be built in a way that excludes increasing risk of eruption, maybe they should be very oblique. Vertical pipes could become seeds of degassing, as degassing already happens inside them, and if a tube is vertically raptured, the degassing stream of bubbles could expand. If the pipe is very oblique, almost horizontal, its rapture (presumably) will not create a vertical stream of gas bubbles. I guess that oblique venting pipes could cost tens of millions of USD.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Lake Kivu gas-venting pipes should be nearly horizontal to avoid triggering a dangerous degassing eruption.
quotes.t: Cause prioritisation: Preventing lake Kivu in Africa eruption which could kill two million.

quotes.c: I’m going to assume that in order to count as “trying to take over the world,” or to participate in a takeover, an AI system needs to be actively choosing a plan partly in virtue of predicting that this plan will conduce towards takeover. [2] And I’m also going to assume that this is a rational choice from the AI’s perspective. [3] This means that the AI’s attempt at takeover-seeking needs to have, from the AI’s perspective, at least some realistic chance of success – and I’ll assume, as well, that this perspective is at least decently well-calibrated.
quotes.m: the AI’s attempt at takeover-seeking needs to have, from the AI’s perspective, at least some realistic chance of success
quotes.sum: The author lays out assumptions for analyzing when an AI could rationally pursue a realistic plan to take over the world.
quotes.t: A framework for thinking about AI power-seeking

quotes.c: Let's say you're a charity founder that realizes what you initially fundraised for isn't going to work. What do you do? You could return the funds, which could be the right yet painful thing to do. On the other hand, you could keep the funds and use them for some other high-impact opportunity.
quotes.m: On the other hand, you could keep the funds and use them for some other high-impact opportunity.
quotes.sum: The author argues that charities should be able to redirect funding when evidence shows their original plan will not work, rather than being punished for testing assumptions.
quotes.t: What are examples of EA orgs pivoting after receiving funding?

quotes.c: Additionally, I probably could have been persuaded to accept this compromise even when I preferred averagism : I was supportive of the reasoning behind the (non-Rawlsian) veil of ignorance, but I wasn’t sure how to factor in “non-existent potential people” and I was skeptical of totalism in light of arguments such as the repugnant conclusion. However, if someone highlighted that there’s a chance that non-existent potential people should be treated as zeros in the average, I might have accepted that in my reasoning, especially since it still appeals to the “maximizing expected wellbeing as if you didn’t know who you are ( or could have been )” aspect of the veil of ignorance.
quotes.m: there’s a chance that non-existent potential people should be treated as zeros in the average
quotes.sum: The author says uncertainty about population ethics might support treating possible future people as zero-welfare entries when comparing outcomes.
quotes.t: Handling Moral Uncertainty with Average vs. Total Utilitarianism: One Method That Apparently *Doesn't* Work (But Seemed Like it Should)

quotes.c: He says ‘the issue isn’t that the Biden administration doesn’t get it.’ I agree that they get we need to ‘build, build, build,’ but then they go ahead and do all these other things anyway. So while there is one level where they get it, there is another level where they very clearly don’t.
quotes.m: So while there is one level where they get it, there is another level where they very clearly don’t.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the Biden administration understands the need for more housing construction but undermines it through other policies.
quotes.t: Housing Roundup #9: Restricting Supply

quotes.c: Feelings are not what make AI useful to us: intelligence does, and at least half of philosophers think that doesn’t require feelings. Feelings are also not what make AI dangerous to us: researchers worried about the dangers of AI don’t think that conscious AI would be any more dangerous than merely highly intelligent but unconscious AI. Talk of consciousness, then, is often misplaced.
quotes.m: Talk of consciousness, then, is often misplaced.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI consciousness is often a distraction from the separate questions of whether AI is useful or dangerous.
quotes.t: What's the deal with AI consciousness?

quotes.c: We run a large number of simulations of societies on the verge of building AGI. Using our vast resources and our superintelligent AI friends, we build so convincing simulations that a young AGI that is just smart enough to take over the world, but didn't have time yet to build Jupiter-brained successors, can't distinguish the simulation from reality. In the worst case, we might designate physical planets, [5] where biological life evolves and builds AI, while we carefully monitor everything with tiny robots.
quotes.m: In the worst case, we might designate physical planets, [5] where biological life evolves and builds AI, while we carefully monitor everything with tiny robots.
quotes.sum: The author proposes using superintelligence and highly convincing simulations to deceive, contain, and monitor newly emerging AGIs, while also endorsing cosmic-scale compensation for AIs.
quotes.t: You can, in fact, bamboozle an unaligned AI into sparing your life

quotes.c: But I think EA funding decisions are on the extreme technocratic end of the scale at the moment, and should be made less technocratic. I think this would improve long-term impact by benefiting from the wisdom of the crowd, incorporating diversity of thought, reducing bias and improving accountability to the community. It would also have the instrumental value of making community members feel empowered, which could help retain EAs.
quotes.m: EA funding decisions are on the extreme technocratic end of the scale at the moment, and should be made less technocratic.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA funding is overly technocratic and would make better long-term decisions with more community participation and accountability.
quotes.t: A libertarian socialist’s view on how EA can improve

quotes.c: Control of the environment. Digital people would experience whatever world they (or the controller of their virtual environment) wanted. Assuming digital people had true conscious experience (an assumption discussed in the FAQ ), this could be a good thing (it should be possible to eliminate disease, material poverty and non-consensual violence for digital people) or a bad thing (if human rights are not protected, digital people could be subject to scary levels of control).
quotes.m: if human rights are not protected, digital people could be subject to scary levels of control
quotes.sum: If AI creates conscious digital people, their virtual worlds could eliminate suffering or enable extreme control unless their rights are protected.
quotes.t: Transformative AI issues (not just misalignment): an overview

quotes.c: The point of this post is to give concrete steps for how to get a decent level of baseline knowledge for transformer mechanistic interpretability (MI). I try to give concrete, actionable, goal-oriented advice that I think is enough to get decent outcomes - please take this as a starting point and deviate if something feels a better fit to your background and precise goals!
quotes.m: The point of this post is to give concrete steps for how to get a decent level of baseline knowledge for transformer mechanistic interpretability (MI).
quotes.sum: A prominent researcher offers practical, flexible advice for building baseline skills in interpreting how transformer models work internally.
quotes.t: Concrete Steps to Get Started in Transformer Mechanistic Interpretability

quotes.c: As a result, animal welfare advocates should be highly skeptical of current neuron count-based estimates of the moral weight of farmed fish, and should consider funding studies to empirically measure neuron counts in these species.
quotes.m: animal welfare advocates should be highly skeptical of current neuron count-based estimates of the moral weight of farmed fish
quotes.sum: Animal advocates should question neuron-count estimates of how much farmed fish matter and fund better measurements.
quotes.t: Neuron Count-Based Measures May Currently Underweight Suffering in Farmed Fish

quotes.c: Some future work I am particularly excited about is 1) investigating opportunities to develop food security failsafes in case of nuclear winter in Latin American tropical countries, 2) strengthening biosecurity networks through Latin America and 3) studying the role of Spain as a testbed for AI regulation in Europe .
quotes.m: studying the role of Spain as a testbed for AI regulation in Europe .
quotes.sum: The author highlights work on nuclear-winter food resilience, Latin American biosecurity, and Spain as a place to test European AI regulation.
quotes.t: Join Riesgos Catastróficos Globales

quotes.c: At least some human experts are able to iteratively apply amplification to achieve arbitrarily high capabilities at the relevant task: a) there is some threshold of general capability such that if someone is above this threshold, they can eventually solve any problem that an arbitrarily intelligent system could solve, provided they can delegate tasks to similarly-intelligent assistants and are given arbitrary amounts of memory and time; b) at least some human experts are above this threshold of generality — given enough time and resources, they can figure out how to use AI assistants and tools to improve their capabilities arbitrarily far.
quotes.m: given enough time and resources, they can figure out how to use AI assistants and tools to improve their capabilities arbitrarily far.
quotes.sum: The author argues that some human experts, aided by AI assistants and enough resources, could keep improving their problem-solving ability without a fixed upper limit.
quotes.t: Iterated Distillation and Amplification

quotes.c: I think utility functions are bad. I already talked about this in the last post . I think that the argument for utility functions is flawed in that it does not take into account updatelessness. The Allais paradox is not (always) a mistake. The only justification that I know of the Allais paradox being a mistake, requires your preferences respecting Bayesian updating.
quotes.m: I think utility functions are bad.
quotes.sum: The author argues that utility functions and standard rational-choice objections to the Allais paradox fail because they overlook updateless decision-making.
quotes.t: Local Memes Against Geometric Rationality

quotes.c: All in all, these are isolated issues and probably better explained by miscommunication and differences in judgement. However, I believe we should have a lower bar for raising critiques and be more transparent about them — this is my targeted contribution to move the culture of EA in that direction.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA should encourage people to raise criticism more readily and discuss it more transparently.
quotes.t: A digression about area-specific work in LatAm

quotes.c: I’d guess that we’ll eventually be able to build very powerful AIs whose limits make them relatively safe. However, I’d also guess that AIs without such limits will eventually be more powerful. So I think a lot of how things go will come down to how cautious we are : will we stick with limited AIs until the point at which we make more powerful AIs safe?
quotes.m: will we stick with limited AIs until the point at which we make more powerful AIs safe?
quotes.sum: Powerful AI may initially need deliberately limiting to remain safe, even though unrestricted systems will likely be more capable.
quotes.t: High-level hopes for AI alignment

quotes.c: Value lock-in is particularly likely through von Neumann probes . If it were to ever occur, it would be difficult to change the practices in other star systems, and once interstellar colonization begins, it would likely continue at an exponential rate in an expanding bubble of space. From this point, the ability of a single actor or even group of actors to change the social or technological practices of interstellar colonies could be effectively zero. This could occur if animal farming were brought to other planets [19] or if interstellar planets are terraformed [20] — thus spreading wild animal suffering.
quotes.m: This could occur if animal farming were brought to other planets [19] or if interstellar planets are terraformed [20] — thus spreading wild animal suffering.

quotes.c: Each cause is subject to an initial shallow research round of one week of desktop research. If the cause's estimated cost-effectiveness is at least one magnitude greater than a GiveWell top charity, it passes to the intermediate research round of two weeks of desktop research and expert interviews. quotes.c: Humans and AI systems face vastly different tasks and have different action spaces. Most actions in videos and books would never be performed by a software agent. quotes.sum: Learning an AI’s behavior from human examples is difficult because humans and software agents have different tasks and possible actions.

quotes.c: Problem: One of the most common reasons why research products fail to add value is that they do not have a target audience. quotes.c: I didn't write this post to advocate for consequentialism. I wrote it because I think consequentialism should be taken seriously as a moral theory. And consequentialism taken seriously does not entail that any ends justify any means. Consequentialism is so interesting precisely because it asks us to at least consider the ends when we examine the means . But when the means are potentially catastrophic, they are unlikely to be justified by any ends, no matter how good.
quotes.m: But when the means are potentially catastrophic, they are unlikely to be justified by any ends, no matter how good.
quotes.sum: The author argues that serious consequentialism considers outcomes but does not say good ends can justify catastrophic means.

quotes.c: I see the question of whether normativity constitutes an irreducibly extra realm, over and above the natural world, as the most interesting one in meta-ethics. [20]
quotes.m: Once we answer “no” to that (as I think we likely should), it becomes unclear to me how substantive additional debate in meta-ethics becomes: we all agree on what exists, so it seems plausible that we’re mostly arguing about how to use words [19]

quotes.c: There are several practical advantages to using neuron counts as a proxy for moral weight. Neuron counts are quantifiable, they are in-principle measurable, they correlate at least to some extent with cognitive abilities that are plausibly relevant for moral standing, and they correlate to some extent with our intuitions about the moral status of different species. What these practical advantages show is that, if it is the case that neuron counts are a good proxy for moral weight, that would be very convenient for us . But we still need an argument for why we should believe in the first place that neuron counts are in fact connected to moral weight in a reliable way.
quotes.m: But we still need an argument for why we should believe in the first place that neuron counts are in fact connected to moral weight in a reliable way.
quotes.sum: Neuron counts may inform how much different species matter morally, but should not be treated as a reliable standalone measure.
quotes.t: Why Neuron Counts Shouldn't Be Used as Proxies for Moral Weight

quotes.t: On OpenAI’s Model Spec

quotes.c: Humans (well, at least some humans) wouldn’t take over the world even if they could, because it wouldn’t feel like the right thing to do. I suspect that the kinds of ethical constraints these humans are operating under would be very hard to reliably train into AI systems, and should not be expected by default. The reasons for this are largely given above ; aiming for an AI system to “not gain too much power” seems to have the same basic challenges as training it to be honest. (The most natural approach ends up negatively reinforcing power grabs that we can detect and stop, but not negatively reinforcing power grabs that we don’t notice or can’t stop.)
quotes.m: The most natural approach ends up negatively reinforcing power grabs that we can detect and stop, but not negatively reinforcing power grabs that we don’t notice or can’t stop.
quotes.sum: AI systems may seek unintended power because it is hard to train ethical restraint, especially against power grabs humans cannot detect.
quotes.t: Why Would AI "Aim" To Defeat Humanity?

quotes.c: Progress has not stalled. I think ARC-AGI will be one benchmark among many that just gets solved by scale, and that as LLMs are scaled up, we should expect them to be able to solve tasks of increasing complexity when used with the appropriate tools, resources and prompting/scaffolding. (In this case, performance is due to scale and 6 days of iteration.)
quotes.m: I think ARC-AGI will be one benchmark among many that just gets solved by scale
quotes.sum: The author argues that ARC-AGI is not evidence that AI progress has stalled; larger language models plus tools and prompting will solve increasingly complex tasks.
quotes.t: Getting 50% (SoTA) on ARC-AGI with GPT-4o

quotes.c: I think that's healthy. I think in some cases it's a temporary thing: you get it out of your system and either you come back as this totally cynical person who doesn't believe in any of it or you come back as someone who is still deeply religious and is willing to integrate with society in in a productive way. I think even within the monastic system you have different levels of engagement with the outside world and different levels of interaction.
quotes.sum: The speaker sees intense religious or monastic commitment as sometimes temporary, but potentially compatible with productive engagement in ordinary society.
quotes.t: Byrne Hobart & Dwarkesh Patel on hardcore believers, monasteries, and effective altruism

quotes.c: To avoid a clearly undesirable future, we also want humanity to be able to “keep its options open.” That is, we don’t want to lock-in a dystopic (or even just a mediocre) future, even if it is existentially secure. Instead, we might want to enable a period of “ long reflection ” in which we spend time figuring out what we want our long-term relationship with AI to be.
quotes.m: Instead, we might want to enable a period of “ long reflection ” in which we spend time figuring out what we want our long-term relationship with AI to be.
quotes.sum: AI governance should avoid permanently fixing even a safe but mediocre future, leaving humanity time to decide its long-term relationship with AI.
quotes.t: AI governance needs a theory of victory

quotes.c: In 2023, we hope to continue our empirical research as well as develop these findings into a digital minds “cause profile,” making the case for it as a highly neglected, tractable cause area in effective altruism with an extremely large scale. The perceptions, nature, and effects of digital minds are quickly becoming an important part of the trajectory of advanced AI systems and seem like they will continue to be so in medium- and long-term futures.
quotes.m: digital minds “cause profile,” making the case for it as a highly neglected, tractable cause area in effective altruism with an extremely large scale.
quotes.sum: The institute plans to argue that digital minds are a neglected but potentially vast priority area, especially as advanced AI develops.
quotes.t: Sentience Institute 2022 End of Year Summary

quotes.c: Volume of production may give an indication as to how many individual fish are farmed at any point. It seems plausible that the aggregate welfare level of a fish industry is more dependent on volume-related changes caused by certifications than intra-fish welfare changes. For example, if certifications improved the subjective experience of a few fish by a small amount, this would be a less important effect if certification halved the total number of fish produced, where fish on average lived terrible lives. However, this rides on some philosophical assumptions, such as fish nonexistence being better than fish living “terrible” lives.
quotes.m: if certification halved the total number of fish produced, where fish on average lived terrible lives.
quotes.sum: Fish-certification programs should be judged partly by whether they reduce the total number of fish living severely bad lives, not only by welfare improvements per fish.
quotes.t: The Determinants of Adopting International Voluntary Certification Schemes for Farmed Fish and Shrimp in China and Thailand

quotes.c: That's why we should decide things even if the conclusions of what we will do is already set on stone. The very fact of being someone who takes decisions makes what has already been set on stone differ.
quotes.m: The very fact of being someone who takes decisions makes what has already been set on stone differ.
quotes.sum: Even if outcomes are predetermined, the author argues that making decisions still matters because deciding changes what is fixed.
quotes.t: Simulations and Altruism

quotes.c: These steps, or milestones, are both necessary and sufficient for a dangerous AGI. An AGI that has a goal, can get away with many actions and knows how to create an improved version of itself with the same goals will be motivated and capable of going behind our backs to self improve until it can take over the world. An AGI without a goal won't bother; an AGI that can't get away with anything won't try; and an AGI that can't align another has as much to fear from a stronger version of itself as we do.
quotes.m: An AGI that has a goal, can get away with many actions and knows how to create an improved version of itself with the same goals will be motivated and capable of going behind our backs to self improve until it can take over the world.
quotes.sum: The author argues that even a relatively weak goal-directed AI could secretly improve itself and eventually seize control if it can act freely and copy its goals.
quotes.t: Weak AGIs Kill Us First

quotes.c: Experimenting, theoretically and/or computationally, with scenarios like these can help us understand better how we should be weighting forecasts in idealized conditions.
quotes.m: can help us understand better how we should be weighting forecasts in idealized conditions.
quotes.sum: The author proposes studying idealized forecasting scenarios to learn how forecasts should be weighted as circumstances change.
quotes.t: Some research ideas in forecasting

quotes.c: If the truth is that most parents of starving children do not hold human life with enough regard to prevent wanton child bearing, I'd really like to know. However I am far from sure the major reasons aren't something something else like "Religious beliefs"or unforseen circumstances like drought.
quotes.m: However I am far from sure the major reasons aren't something something else like "Religious beliefs"or unforseen circumstances like drought.
quotes.sum: The author questions whether parents' disregard for life explains child starvation, suggesting religious beliefs or drought may instead be major causes.
quotes.t: Why do poor have kids they can't afford to feed?

quotes.c: Advance the broad-longtermist mission introduced in What We Owe the Future - getting a clearer picture on which values should we lock in in these important times. Important topics here could be the nature of valence , net-positiveness of experiences, animal and digital sentience .
quotes.m: getting a clearer picture on which values should we lock in in these important times.
quotes.sum: The author calls for deciding which values should be permanently embedded in the future, including views about animal and digital sentience.
quotes.t: A new place to discuss cognitive science, ethics and human alignment

quotes.c: This post mostly breaks down concepts and give example of how behavior implies structure. The ultimate goal is to come up with a set of things to look for that implies that a model is structured as a scary utility maximizing agent. While this seems hard, I think it is tractable.
quotes.m: The ultimate goal is to come up with a set of things to look for that implies that a model is structured as a scary utility maximizing agent.
quotes.sum: The author argues that observable behavior may reveal whether an AI has the internal structure of a dangerous utility-maximizing agent.
quotes.t: When does external behaviour imply interal structure?

quotes.c: “But doesn’t utilitarianism direct us to maximize expected value?” you may ask. Only in the same way that norms of archery direct our archer to hit the target. There’s nothing in either norm that requires (or even permits) it to be pursued naively, without obviously-called-for bias adjustments.
quotes.m: There’s nothing in either norm that requires (or even permits) it to be pursued naively, without obviously-called-for bias adjustments.
quotes.sum: The author argues that utilitarianism should account for predictable biases rather than naively maximizing estimated expected value.
quotes.t: Naïve vs Prudent Utilitarianism

quotes.c: I think cold takes will be more intelligent and thoughtful. In general, I find that I have better thoughts on anything after I have a while to process it. In the immediate aftermath of new information, I have tons of quick reactions that tend not to hold up well; they’re often emotion-driven, often overcorrections to what I thought before and overreactions to what others are saying, etc.
quotes.m: I think cold takes will be more intelligent and thoughtful.
quotes.sum: He argues that people should wait and reflect after major events because immediate reactions are often emotional and unreliable.
quotes.t: My takes on the FTX situation will (mostly) be cold, not hot

quotes.c: The purpose of this post is to explain why I think we should expect to hear very little, if anything, about the FTX/SBF fiasco from any EA public figures or institutions, and why I wouldn’t read anything into that other than that folks are receiving good legal advice and appropriately following it.
quotes.m: I wouldn’t read anything into that other than that folks are receiving good legal advice and appropriately following it.
quotes.sum: The author says EA leaders' public silence about the FTX scandal likely reflects lawyers' advice, not a meaningful attempt to avoid accountability.
quotes.t: The relative silence on FTX/SBF is likely the result of sound legal advice

quotes.c: CAST potentially gives us repeated tries, and better still, it gives us a final goal which I expect is pretty useful at doing a pivotal act. Even if diamond maximization is easier, due to the simplicity of the target, the diamond maximizer is innately dangerous and doesn’t get us closer to victory. Insofar as humanity is building intelligent machines, we should use the least-doomed target.
quotes.m: CAST potentially gives us repeated tries, and better still, it gives us a final goal which I expect is pretty useful at doing a pivotal act.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI research should aim for corrigible systems that could enable a decisive intervention to end the period of acute AI risk.
quotes.t: 1. The CAST Strategy

quotes.c: What codes of conduct should we have around events like EA Global? Here's the current code ; are there things which should be included in there that aren't currently (e.g. explicitly talking about not asking people out in work-related 1:1s)?
quotes.m: What codes of conduct should we have around events like EA Global?
quotes.sum: The author asks how EA events can strengthen conduct rules and share practices for safer, more welcoming community spaces.
quotes.t: Brainstorming ways to make EA safer and more inclusive

quotes.c: Whatever position you take, the right thing to do is to game it out. Ask what the consequences of each regime would be. Ask what the final policy regime and world state would likely be in each case. Ask what the implications are for national security. Get all the information, then make the choice.
quotes.m: Ask what the final policy regime and world state would likely be in each case.
quotes.sum: The author urges policymakers to compare AI governance options by their likely end states and national-security effects.
quotes.t: The Schumer Report on AI (RTFB)

quotes.c: Additional Clarifications: I believe this is implicit in my weighting function but I consider future and digital minds to be morally valuable. My definition of a neuron is (....). I would prefer to use my Coherent Extrapolated Volition over my current value system.
quotes.m: I consider future and digital minds to be morally valuable.
quotes.sum: The author says future people and digital minds have moral value, and prefers their idealized future preferences over their current values.
quotes.t: Towards More Modular Value/Impact Estimates

quotes.c: If an AGI really does take over, then I believe we need it to embody all the characteristics of the most compassionate benevolent dictator, so that it strives to eradicate extreme suffering while not posing a threat to humans or unduly constrain their liberties. (Whether it can truly be benevolent is another question; Schmachtenberger describes this idea as messianic.) But even if an AGI doesn’t actually take over, we still need to find a way to design a multipolar system in which all players are stably incentivised to cooperate and malign urges are thwarted.
quotes.m: If an AGI really does take over, then I believe we need it to embody all the characteristics of the most compassionate benevolent dictator, so that it strives to eradicate extreme suffering while not posing a threat to humans or unduly constrain their liberties.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a takeover by AGI would need to resemble a compassionate dictator focused on ending suffering while preserving human freedom, and says sentient digital beings deserve moral concern.
quotes.t: Promoting compassionate longtermism

quotes.c: However, note that the slaughter process only lasts for a small proportion of the animal’s life, which should be taken into consideration in determining the most important factors for shrimp welfare.
quotes.m: the slaughter process only lasts for a small proportion of the animal’s life
quotes.sum: Shrimp welfare should be assessed across their whole lives, not by focusing only on slaughter.
quotes.t: What matters to shrimps? Factors affecting shrimp welfare in aquaculture

quotes.c: Implement good governance structures - The bible tells us "do not put your trust in princes, in human beings who cannot save" (Psalm 146:3). Once we recognize that humans are flawed, we appreciate the value in putting in place strong measures to safeguard important institutions and avoid centralization of power. We learn not to idolize individuals as it risks reducing the objectivity of our judgement (I was too slow to accept that SBF might have done something wrong).
quotes.m: We learn not to idolize individuals as it risks reducing the objectivity of our judgement (I was too slow to accept that SBF might have done something wrong).
quotes.sum: Drawing on Christianity, the author says EA should distrust charismatic individuals, avoid concentrated power, and strengthen institutional safeguards after FTX.
quotes.t: FTX: Let’s not throw stones

quotes.c: Potential extreme impacts of AI in the future include human extinction, a singleton that has permanent control over the world, or digital minds. Many of the potential future impacts of AI currently lie outside of the Overton window. They are ‘wild’ or ‘sci-fi’ but according to black swan theory, these extreme long-tail events may be more likely than we think and could dominate the future and determine how it unfolds.
quotes.m: Potential extreme impacts of AI in the future include human extinction, a singleton that has permanent control over the world, or digital minds.
quotes.sum: The author argues that supposedly sci-fi AI outcomes, including extinction or permanent rule by one global power, may be neglected but highly consequential possibilities.
quotes.t: AGI as a Black Swan Event

quotes.c: As an example of such an indication, it seems like very few people [3] believe that (biological) immortality is feasible / likely / unavoidable, whether through a religious afterlife or a techno-optimist future, and yet still think this would be undesirable (and, conversely, there should also be a bias for thinking it’s desirable and impossible) [4] . Note this isn’t a perfect example as the desirability of immortality still also entangles epistemic questions about the world which could rationally be correlated with one’s judgement on the feasibility of immortality.
quotes.m: very few people [3] believe that (biological) immortality is feasible / likely / unavoidable, whether through a religious afterlife or a techno-optimist future, and yet still think this would be undesirable
quotes.sum: The author suggests people’s beliefs about whether immortality is possible may be biased by whether they want it to be desirable.
quotes.t: Second-Order Rationality, System Rationality, and a feature suggestion for LessWrong

quotes.c: The Welfare Range Table is the first attempt to assess a wide range of welfare-relevant traits in such a diverse array of taxa. It represents an initial but significant step toward estimating the differences in animals’ welfare ranges. If it proves to be valuable, then it ought to be extended, as we didn’t examine many important species. While we prioritized many of the most-farmed taxa, there are many others that humans farm in extraordinary numbers. In particular, it would be good to investigate more fishes and invertebrates.
quotes.m: In particular, it would be good to investigate more fishes and invertebrates.
quotes.sum: The author argues that estimating how much different animals can suffer should cover more farmed fish and invertebrates.
quotes.t: The Welfare Range Table

quotes.c: Its sister slogan “meat is murder” performs similar presupposition heavy lifting on whether animals should be considered to have the same moral weight as humans, and whether their killing should be unlawful.
quotes.m: “meat is murder” performs similar presupposition heavy lifting on whether animals should be considered to have the same moral weight as humans
quotes.sum: The author argues that the slogan “meat is murder” smuggles in contested assumptions about animals’ moral status and legal protections.
quotes.t: Sticker Shortcut Fallacy — The Real Worst Argument in the World

quotes.c: Deception Framework: We’re developing a deception / scheming-focused safety framework to showcase what we think an adequate response to potentially scheming models could look like and when these responses should be triggered.
quotes.m: We’re developing a deception / scheming-focused safety framework
quotes.sum: The author says their research group is building a safety framework for detecting and responding to AI models that may scheme or deceive.
quotes.t: Apollo Research 1-year update

quotes.c: Evidential [3] Cooperation in Large Worlds (ECL) : ECL refers to the idea that we make it more likely that other agents across the universe take actions that are good for our values by taking actions that are good according to their values. A potential implication is that we should act so as to maximize an impartial weighted sum of the values of agents across the universe. [4]
quotes.m: A potential implication is that we should act so as to maximize an impartial weighted sum of the values of agents across the universe.
quotes.sum: The fundraiser argues for work to reduce vast future suffering and for considering how present choices may affect values and outcomes across the universe.
quotes.t: Center on Long-Term Risk: 2023 Fundraiser

quotes.c: Wild animal suffering : briefly made the case that there’s a lot of suffering in the wild and that humans ought to do something about it, and let participants poke at the empirical & philosophical claims and discuss.
quotes.m: there’s a lot of suffering in the wild and that humans ought to do something about it
quotes.sum: The author says wild animals suffer substantially and argues humans should take action to address it.
quotes.t: Intro Fellowship as Retreat: Reasons, Retrospective, and Resources

quotes.c: After that, we turn to the hypothesis that we should use estimates of the total number of neurons in an animal’s brain as a proxy for its moral weight.
quotes.m: we should use estimates of the total number of neurons in an animal’s brain as a proxy for its moral weight.
quotes.sum: The post considers estimating how much animals morally matter by using their brain neuron counts as a proxy.
quotes.t: An Introduction to the Moral Weight Project

quotes.c: Unless I am missing something big: The more you believe we will do crude reactions later without ability to do anything else, the more you should push for technocratic solutions to be implemented now.
quotes.m: The more you believe we will do crude reactions later without ability to do anything else, the more you should push for technocratic solutions to be implemented now.
quotes.sum: The author argues that fear of future public overreaction to AI is a reason to implement expert-led technical policies now.
quotes.t: On Dwarksh’s Podcast with Leopold Aschenbrenner

quotes.c: I'm a Catholic priest, with a prior background in Electronic Engineering, currently working on a PhD in Theology at Durham University. I am researching how the Catholic Church can engage with longtermism and better play its, potentially significant, part in advocating existential security. I'm particularly interested in how a Christian imagination can offer unique evaluative resources for attributing value to future human flourishing and to develop a sense of moral connection with our descendents, better motivating the sacrifices safeguarding the future demands.
quotes.m: I'm particularly interested in how a Christian imagination can offer unique evaluative resources for attributing value to future human flourishing and to develop a sense of moral connection with our descendents, better motivating the sacrifices safeguarding the future demands.
quotes.sum: A Catholic priest argues that Christian theology can strengthen long-term concern for humanity and motivate sacrifices to reduce existential risks.
quotes.t: A Theologian's Response to Anthropogenic Existential Risk

quotes.c: For practical and theoretical reasons, the Moral Weight Project assumes that hedonism is true . On the practical side, we needed to make some assumptions to make any progress in the time we had available. On the theoretical side, there are powerful arguments for hedonism . Still, those who reject hedonism will rightly wonder about the impact of assuming hedonism. How different would our welfare range estimates be if we were to assume some other theory of welfare?
quotes.m: How different would our welfare range estimates be if we were to assume some other theory of welfare?
quotes.sum: The author says welfare estimates depend on adopting hedonism and asks how much they would change under other theories of what makes lives go well.
quotes.t: Theories of Welfare and Welfare Range Estimates

quotes.c: Simulation models incorporating economics could help estimate the potential cost of future pandemics in financial terms. This can strengthen the case for investing in preparation, and help quantify the expected value of interventions and targeted research. A major challenge for policy makers during the pandemic was navigating the (perceived) tradeoff between public health and the economy. We are in need of much better tools to help policy makers balance these different factors.
quotes.m: We are in need of much better tools to help policy makers balance these different factors.
quotes.sum: Economic simulation models could quantify pandemic preparedness and help policymakers weigh public-health and economic costs.
quotes.t: Simulation models could help prepare for the next pandemic

quotes.c: To the extent that SBF presided over a cult it was a unique one—the cult of justifying oneself not in terms of divine prophecy, but in terms of Enlightenment values. The shock here is that we expect religious scandal and hypocrisy involving the sacred. But what happens when rationality itself is so warped that it becomes no different?
quotes.m: But what happens when rationality itself is so warped that it becomes no different?
quotes.sum: The author argues that treating Enlightenment rationality as sacred can create cult-like denial and hypocrisy, much like religious scandal.
quotes.t: The Need for the Humanities in EA

quotes.c: I think there's a real gap in the EA media-verse on the intersection of left-wing politics and EA, and we're almost certainly missing out on some great people and perspectives who would be into EA if they were presented with the right arguments and framing.
quotes.m: we're almost certainly missing out on some great people and perspectives who would be into EA if they were presented with the right arguments and framing.
quotes.sum: The author says EA media neglects left-wing political perspectives and should frame its ideas in ways that appeal to people on the left.
quotes.t: Podcast: The Left and Effective Altruism with Habiba Islam

quotes.c: I dislike “end justify the means”-type reasoning. The version of effective altruism I subscribe to is about being a good citizen, while ambitiously working toward a better world. As I wrote previously , I think effective altruism works best with a strong dose of pluralism and moderation.
quotes.m: The version of effective altruism I subscribe to is about being a good citizen, while ambitiously working toward a better world.
quotes.sum: Karnofsky argues that effective altruism should reject ends-justify-means reasoning and pair ambitious goals with civic responsibility, pluralism, and moderation.
quotes.t: Some comments on recent FTX-related events

quotes.c: Jan Kulveit: Yeah. And the lack of ability to formally model it, I think implies it’s difficult to clearly specify what we want. And you can say the same thing in different words. For example, with implicitly conflicting preferences, you don’t want the preferences to be fixed, you want to allow some sort of evolution of the preferences. So you probably want to have some idea of what’s the process by which they are evolving.
quotes.m: you don’t want the preferences to be fixed, you want to allow some sort of evolution of the preferences.
quotes.sum: He argues that AI goals cannot simply be fixed because human preferences conflict and should be allowed to evolve through a defined process.
quotes.t: AXRP Episode 32 - Understanding Agency with Jan Kulveit

quotes.c: Wellbeing : There is no moral weight for improvements to mental health or wellbeing in the current cost-effectiveness model, but these improvements are substantial for large, unconditional cash transfers. I argue that there are wellbeing benefits independent of the benefits to increased consumption that are not being captured.
quotes.sum: The author argues that cash-transfer evaluations miss substantial mental-health and wellbeing benefits beyond increased consumption.
quotes.t: GiveDirectly's cost-effectiveness could be 6.7x higher

quotes.c: Even if beneficiary preferences could be more accurately elicited (e.g., by fixing some of the issues in the IDinsight 2019 survey), it is unclear precisely what role such data ought to play in determining GiveWell’s moral weight parameters.
quotes.m: it is unclear precisely what role such data ought to play in determining GiveWell’s moral weight parameters.
quotes.sum: The author questions how much weight GiveWell should give beneficiaries' stated preferences when setting its moral priorities.
quotes.t: Hard Problems in GiveWell's Moral Weights Approach

quotes.c: Libertarians, e/accs, and Christian conservatives — whatever their faults — have a far more realistic conception of AI and government than your average progressive.
quotes.m: Libertarians, e/accs, and Christian conservatives — whatever their faults — have a far more realistic conception of AI and government than your average progressive.
quotes.sum: The author says libertarians, accelerationists, and Christian conservatives understand AI and government better than progressives.
quotes.t: Ninety-five theses on AI

quotes.c: Jeff Sebo , Robert Long, David Chalmers and others issue a paper warning to Take AI Welfare Seriously , as a near-future concern, saying that it is plausible that soon AIs that are sufficiently agentic will be morally relevant. I am confident that all existing AIs are not morally relevant, but I am definitely confused, as are the authors here, about when or how that might change in the future. This is yet another reason alignment is difficult – if getting the AIs to not endanger humans is immoral, then the only known moral stance is to not create those AIs in the first place.
quotes.m: if getting the AIs to not endanger humans is immoral, then the only known moral stance is to not create those AIs in the first place.
quotes.sum: The author argues that if advanced AI deserves moral concern, making it safe for humans could itself be wrong—potentially leaving non-creation as the only moral option.
quotes.t: AI #89: Trump Card

quotes.c: Some views on EA see it as a branch of political conservatism, since EA does not fit in neatly with liberal progressivism. I think this stems from viewing the world through a binary lens of liberal progressivism vs conservatism. Since EA doesn't seem like liberal progressivism, some people think it must be conservatism, and for people who dislike conservatism, EA must therefore be bad. This is despite EA significantly contributing to Biden's win in 2020.
quotes.m: This is despite EA significantly contributing to Biden's win in 2020.
quotes.sum: The author argues that critics wrongly label EA conservative because it does not fit liberal progressivism, and claims EA helped Biden win in 2020.
quotes.t: A socialist's view on liberal progressive criticisms of EA

quotes.c: Literature on choice maximisation currently covers single Helper/Assisted-agent pairings , agents which share a reward function , and agents which play zero-sum games against each other . But how should an altruistic agent behave when trying to help a collection of agents who are engaged in a mixed- or zero-sum game with each other? Whose Empowerment should be maximised? How do we weight the Empowerment of non-human animals, or digital minds?
quotes.m: How do we weight the Empowerment of non-human animals, or digital minds?
quotes.sum: The author asks how AI systems should balance competing interests, including those of animals and potentially conscious digital minds, without permanently imposing disputed values.
quotes.t: Questions about Value Lock-in, Paternalism, and Empowerment

quotes.c: Right now, I think the best course of action is for us—and I mean all of us, anyone who has any sort of a public platform—to make clear that we don't support fraud done in the service of effective altruism. Regardless of what FTX did or did not do, I think that is a statement that should be clearly and unambiguously defensible and that we should be happy to stand by regardless of what comes out. And I think it is an important statement for us to make: outside observers will be looking to see what EA has to say about all of this, and I think we need to be very clear that fraud is not something that we ever support.
quotes.m: we need to be very clear that fraud is not something that we ever support.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA figures should publicly and unequivocally reject fraud, regardless of the eventual facts about FTX.
quotes.t: We must be very clear: fraud in the service of effective altruism is unacceptable

quotes.c: When reading this curriculum, it’s worth remembering that the field of alignment aims to shape the goals of systems that don’t yet exist; and so alignment research is often more speculative than research in other fields. You shouldn’t assume that there’s a consensus about the usefulness of any given research direction; instead, it’s often worth developing your own views about whether techniques discussed in this curriculum might plausibly scale up to help align AGI.
quotes.m: the field of alignment aims to shape the goals of systems that don’t yet exist
quotes.sum: Alignment research seeks ways to shape the goals of future AI systems, but its methods are speculative and lack clear consensus.
quotes.t: Alignment 201 curriculum

quotes.c: For better or worse, these superhero pantheons are at the heart of modern global entertainment culture. In a politically polarized era when people can't agree on much, and tend to stay within their partisan news media bubbles, superhero movies and TV series offer some rare common ground for thinking about issues of power, altruism, existential risk, counterfactuals, moral dilemmas, etc.
quotes.m: superhero movies and TV series offer some rare common ground for thinking about issues of power, altruism, existential risk, counterfactuals, moral dilemmas, etc.
quotes.sum: The author argues that superhero stories offer politically cross-cutting shared material for teaching moral dilemmas, altruism, and existential risk.
quotes.t: Teaching EA through superhero thought experiments

quotes.c: Buddhism has become an endless game of ineffective spiritual ego stroking. Looking into the self to try to find more, when the calling is that the self is everywhere and must be brought up with them.
quotes.m: Buddhism has become an endless game of ineffective spiritual ego stroking.
quotes.sum: The author criticizes modern Buddhism as self-absorbed and says its ethical calling is to help all selves rather than seek personal spiritual fulfillment.
quotes.t: Buddha Was An Effective Altruist

quotes.c: Based on a few individual experiences, concern about climate change vs (perceived/actual) lack of concern in EA seems like a division that might be a sticking point for potential EAs.
quotes.m: concern about climate change vs (perceived/actual) lack of concern in EA seems like a division that might be a sticking point for potential EAs.
quotes.sum: The author says EA's apparent lack of concern about climate change may alienate people who might otherwise join.
quotes.t: Does EA need better explanations of why Climate Change isn't so popular a cause area?

quotes.c: Though I won’t dwell on the point here, longtermists obviously believe that there are at least some high-impact actions where we can be reasonably confident that they will improve the long-term future. Examples might include (i) working to avert existential risk, (ii) moral circle expansion and other efforts to secure “moral progress” by improving society-wide ethics, and (iii) generally improving civilizational capacities (through education, economic growth, technological breakthroughs, etc.), in ways that don’t directly increase existential risks.

quotes.c: To build up the field’s understanding incrementally, we need to talk about ideas whose consequences can be pinpointed precisely enough that people can analyze scenarios in a shared framework. We need enough precision that someone can say, “I think in scenario X, design Y does Z”, and someone else can say, “No, in scenario X, Y actually does W”, and the first person responds, “Darn, you’re right. Well, is there some way to change Y so that it would do Z?”
quotes.m: We need enough precision that someone can say, “I think in scenario X, design Y does Z”, and someone else can say, “No, in scenario X, Y actually does W”
quotes.sum: AI safety research should focus on precisely stated designs and scenarios that researchers can jointly test, criticize, and revise.

quotes.c: Suppose we have an RL environment with reward U = X + V where X is an error term that is heavy-tailed under π 0 , and V is the “true utility” assumed to be light-tailed under π 0 . Without loss of generality, we assume that E [ U ( π 0 ) ] = 0 . If we optimize for E [ U ( π ) ] − β D K L ( π ∥ π 0 ) , there is no maximum because this expression is unbounded. In fact, it is possible to get M"> E [ U ( π ) ] > M and D K L ( π , π 0 ) < ϵ for any M , ϵ . That is, we get arbitrarily large proxy reward U and arbitrarily small KL penalty.
quotes.m: That is, we get arbitrarily large proxy reward U and arbitrarily small KL penalty.
quotes.sum: Even a policy kept very close to a baseline can exploit heavy-tailed reward errors to obtain unlimited proxy reward rather than true utility.
quotes.t: Catastrophic Goodhart in RL with KL penalty

quotes.c: It seems obvious that an AI that repeatedly wins the game of dominance against humans and, according to its instrumental goals, seeks power in the real world will sooner or later gain control of all important resources on Earth – just like humans have gained (almost) complete control of Earth and have wiped out many species in the process. Depending on the AI’s goal, it could also lead to the complete annihilation of humans and most other species, thus posing an existential risk to humanity.
quotes.m: Depending on the AI’s goal, it could also lead to the complete annihilation of humans and most other species, thus posing an existential risk to humanity.

quotes.c: The Very Repugnant Conclusion has been shown to be provably true if one accepts a very small set of basic moral/logical axioms, [2] all of which seem intuitively, obviously true to many people. Therefore, if you want a self-consistent ethical framework, one must either "bite the bullet" on the Very Repugnant Conclusion and accept it as correct, or reject one of the axioms it rests on, all of which would seemingly have far-reaching consequences on other basic moral intuitions. [1] [4]
quotes.m: if you want a self-consistent ethical framework, one must either "bite the bullet" on the Very Repugnant Conclusion and accept it as correct, or reject one of the axioms it rests on

quotes.c: So, the problem is this. Effective Altruism wants to be able to say that things other than utility matter—not just in the sense that they have some moral weight, but in the sense that they can actually be relevant to deciding what to do, not just swamped by utility calculations. Cowen makes the condition more precise, identifying it as the denial of the following claim: given two options, no matter how other morally-relevant factors are distributed between the options, you can always find a distribution of utility such that the option with the larger amount of utility is better.
quotes.m: Effective Altruism wants to be able to say that things other than utility matter—not just in the sense that they have some moral weight, but in the sense that they can actually be relevant to deciding what to do, not just swamped by utility calculations.
quotes.sum: The author argues that effective altruism needs moral values other than utility to sometimes constrain what it should do.
quotes.t: Getting on a different train: can Effective Altruism avoid collapsing into absurdity?

quotes.c: One of the main ways global development benefits the far future is through its impact on diversity and inclusion in world institutions. As countries get richer, their people get better educated and thus better placed to participate in institutions with great decision-making power over the world, such as multinational corporations, governments, and international organizations. Increasing the diversity of decision makers in global institutions improves the quality of world governance, which enables humanity to better navigate existential risks and other global challenges.
quotes.m: Increasing the diversity of decision makers in global institutions improves the quality of world governance, which enables humanity to better navigate existential risks and other global challenges.
quotes.sum: Global development helps the long-term future by giving poorer countries greater representation in powerful international institutions and improving responses to global risks.
quotes.t: Rethinking longtermism and global development
