quotes.c: Another way of pointing at rationality realism: suppose we model humans as internally-consistent agents with beliefs and goals. This model is obviously flawed, but also predictively powerful on the level of our everyday lives. When we use this model to extrapolate much further (e.g. imagining a much smarter agent with the same beliefs and goals), or base morality on this model (e.g. preference utilitarianism, CEV), is that more like using Newtonian physics to approximate relativity (works well, breaks down in edge cases) or more like cavemen using their physics intuitions to reason about space (a fundamentally flawed approach)?

quotes.c: Patching with activations from “Il Colosseo è dentro” locates where the model stores the language of the prompt but may use the same factual recall machinery. quotes.c: I mean, I think that you could go faster towards those solutions than I did, and probably now I have definitely the instinct where I see people doing a task, and I'm like, try to do this with the language model, please. But I think that once you realize, oh, this direction, the broad direction of do the same thing you're doing, but automate it with the language model. That high level frame could be applied to, lots of different areas of alignment.
quotes.m: the broad direction of do the same thing you're doing, but automate it with the language model.
quotes.sum: He argues that many alignment tasks can be accelerated by reframing them as work to automate with language models.
quotes.t: How I select alignment research projects

quotes.c: In my view it is likely that large vertebrates can feel direct physical pain with intensity commensurate to that of humans, because we have both large and complex brains, and pain and pleasure are very simple functions. I can accept some “saturation” of the super-additivity of sentience regarding pain for large vertebrates. In any case, the deep extension of the moral circle (beyond the large vertebrates) implies a relatively clear measure of brain complexity and some hypotheses about the relation between that measure and sentience intensity.
quotes.m: the deep extension of the moral circle (beyond the large vertebrates) implies a relatively clear measure of brain complexity and some hypotheses about the relation between that measure and sentience intensity.
quotes.sum: The author argues that many vertebrates may feel pain as intensely as humans and that moral concern should extend farther based on brain complexity and sentience.
quotes.t: Super additivity of consciousness

quotes.c: The purple dots are the values that the agent sets the 5 known variables, and the un-stiff unknown variables to. Because V is defined as a minimum, and because at least one of the un-stiff unknown variables must be one the humans care about, the agent will set them all to the same value. The brown dots track the value of the stiff variables, while the blue points are the expected value of V.
quotes.m: Because V is defined as a minimum, and because at least one of the un-stiff unknown variables must be one the humans care about, the agent will set them all to the same value.
quotes.sum: It describes how an optimizing agent can exploit uncertainty in human values when a goal is defined as the minimum across variables.
quotes.t: Using expected utility for Good(hart)

quotes.c: The first post, Shut Up and Divide? , was written in response to Eliezer Yudkowsky's slogan of "shut up and multiply" but I think also works as a counter against Peter Singer's Drowning Child argument , which many may see as foundational to EA.
quotes.m: I think also works as a counter against Peter Singer's Drowning Child argument
quotes.sum: The author points to an argument challenging the utilitarian reasoning behind EA's drowning-child example.
quotes.t: Questioning the Foundations of EA

quotes.c: As explained above, ACE is not prioritizing heavily between existing interventions to help farmed animals. I think this is a major error not just from a formal point of view, but from a substantive point of view as well. One set of interventions is significantly more tractable than the rest of the interventions: interventions which aim to improve animal welfare standards by corporate outreach and campaigns.
quotes.m: One set of interventions is significantly more tractable than the rest of the interventions: interventions which aim to improve animal welfare standards by corporate outreach and campaigns.
quotes.sum: The author argues that animal-charity evaluators should rank interventions more rigorously, favoring tractable corporate animal-welfare campaigns.
quotes.t: An Evaluation of Animal Charity Evaluators

quotes.c: Here I want to flag one limitation and one potential risk of emphasizing longtermism. The limitation is the one I mentioned regarding climate change: it seems doubtful that emphasizing gains to people in the distant future will overcome the political forces of distrust, self-interest, partisan obstruction that stop us from taking catastrophic risks more seriously. If we are unlikely to devote sufficient resources and effort to preventing an accidental nuclear war for the sake of ourselves and our children, it seems unlikely that moral appeals to longtermism will help.
quotes.m: If we are unlikely to devote sufficient resources and effort to preventing an accidental nuclear war for the sake of ourselves and our children, it seems unlikely that moral appeals to longtermism will help.
quotes.sum: The author argues that appeals to help the far future may not overcome political self-interest and distrust, even for preventing nuclear catastrophe.
quotes.t: Effective altruism in a non-ideal world

quotes.c: People will think that renaming EA would be too much of a headache, or that it is not the sort of thing we could reach agreement on. But then “EA” will get locked in as a name. Later generations may think that it is a headache to undo the choices of the past or that they will not be able to reach agreement. But then path dependency wins. We don’t want that. We want a Long Reflection.
quotes.m: We don’t want that. We want a Long Reflection.
quotes.sum: The author argues EA should consider renaming itself now rather than let an inconvenient name become entrenched through path dependence.
quotes.t: EA Should Rename Itself

quotes.c: While as described above I think the current biggest problem we have to solve is figuring out how to reliably align a powerful AI at all, I did appreciate the discussion of value lock-in possibilities even when it’s aligned. I liked the section “Building a Morally Exploratory World” (beginning p.97) and would be concerned about AI safety researchers who think of alignment more as getting the AGI to have our current values rather than something like making the AI help us figure out what our ideal values are before implementing them.
quotes.sum: The author argues that aligned AI should help humanity discover its ideal values, rather than permanently enforce today's values.
quotes.t: My take on What We Owe the Future

quotes.c: Example #2 - Accuracy/Predictions : I'm from the US midwest. We all knew Trump was going to win in 2016, or at least that he had a good shot of winning. ( Personally, I think this was because more people in the midwest regularly talks to farmer/rural relatives or people who have them, but that's not super relevant to this post ). Not only were people on the coasts generally shocked, but the media reported that everyone was shocked.
quotes.m: We all knew Trump was going to win in 2016, or at least that he had a good shot of winning.
quotes.sum: The author argues that coastal and media circles missed Trump's electoral chances because they lacked contact with rural and Midwestern communities.
quotes.t: A slightly (I think?) different slant on why EA elitism bias/top-university focus/lack of diversity is a problem

quotes.c: Politics Conservatives are more likely to be rural, which means they live in low-population states. Low-population states have an outsize influence on the Senate and the Electoral College. Therefore, we can expect the Republican party to have considerable power going forward.
quotes.m: Therefore, we can expect the Republican party to have considerable power going forward.
quotes.sum: The author proposes outreach to US conservatives and religious people, partly because they expect Republicans to retain substantial political power.
quotes.t: [Cause Exploration Prizes] Outreach to Conservatives and Religious People

quotes.c: Compared to other communities, I think EA organizations and grantees are more likely to get funding from one of a small group of funders. Historical EA funding data is dominated by Open Philanthropy, Givewell, and (starting in 2022) FTX. Effective Altruism Data suggests that Founders Pledge might also be in this small dominant group.
quotes.m: Historical EA funding data is dominated by Open Philanthropy, Givewell, and (starting in 2022) FTX.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA funding is unusually concentrated among a small group of major funders.
quotes.t: EA is too reliant on personal connections

quotes.c: We intuitively understand the need for global cooperation, but as we continue to tire of dealing with one another's dogma and unbeknownst exploitation, can't we develop the gall to match the audacity of corporations and religion to shape the global order? Don't we need a binding agent for both left and right-centric thinkers, young and old and of any life circumstances that ought to have a shared cause?
quotes.m: can't we develop the gall to match the audacity of corporations and religion to shape the global order?
quotes.sum: The author calls for a unifying cause that can shape global order and bring together people across ideological and social divisions.
quotes.t: [Cause Exploration Prizes] Provisions For The Future Beyond Our Lifespans

quotes.c: DSA is a powerful tool in its own right, but I’d suggest the real value of DSA is giving us a framework to consider the ‘expected value of perfect information’ (EVPI). This is, formally, the price you’d pay to have perfect knowledge of the value of a parameter. Practically, it is another decision-tool; if the EVPI is more than the cost of generating the information then generating that information is more important than directly using the funds for philanthropic ends.
quotes.m: if the EVPI is more than the cost of generating the information then generating that information is more important than directly using the funds for philanthropic ends.
quotes.sum: The author argues that charities should fund research to reduce uncertainty when the expected benefit of better information exceeds its cost.
quotes.t: Methods for improving uncertainty analysis in EA cost-effectiveness models

quotes.c: Strong longtermists typically respond that if we’re worried about the risk of astronomical suffering, we should still be longtermists, but should focus our efforts on preventing astronomical risks rather than preventing human extinction. While this is sensible, longtermists don’t seem to be about to stop funding efforts to reduce extinction risk. And, if the expected value of the future is bad, trying to prevent human extinction has negative value.
quotes.m: And, if the expected value of the future is bad, trying to prevent human extinction has negative value.
quotes.sum: The author argues that preventing human extinction is not automatically good if the future could contain more suffering than wellbeing.
quotes.t: A Case Against Strong Longtermism

quotes.c: We talk about the recent LaMDA controversy about the sentience of large language models (see Robert's summary ), the metaphysics and philosophy of consciousness, artificial sentience, and how a future filled with digital minds could get really weird.
quotes.m: how a future filled with digital minds could get really weird.
quotes.sum: The author introduces a discussion of whether language models could be sentient and the strange ethical implications of a future populated by digital minds.
quotes.t: Robert Long on Why You Might Want To Care About Artificial Sentience

quotes.c: Although mental health conditions are better recognized nowadays and therefore treatment methods are improving, I argue that the underlying way we define mental health disorders does not promote the development of effective treatment interventions. The mental health diagnostic system has been categorical since its beginning days.
quotes.m: I argue that the underlying way we define mental health disorders does not promote the development of effective treatment interventions.
quotes.sum: The author argues that categorical mental-health diagnoses hinder the development of effective treatments.
quotes.t: [Cause Exploration Prizes]  Mental health diagnostic system

quotes.c: 16.) I think EA ignores digital sentience too much. I don't think any current AI systems are conscious but I think it could happen, and happen a lot sooner than we think. Transformative AI is potentially less than 20 years away and I think conscious AI could be even sooner, especially given that e.g., bees are likely conscious and we already have enough compute to achieve bee-compute parity on some tasks . Also there's so much we don't know about how consciousness works, I think it is important to tred with caution here. But if computers could easily make billions of digital minds, I don't think we're at all prepared for how that could unfold into a very near-term moral catastrophe.
quotes.m: But if computers could easily make billions of digital minds, I don't think we're at all prepared for how that could unfold into a very near-term moral catastrophe.
quotes.sum: EA should take possible AI consciousness seriously, because rapidly creating billions of digital minds could cause a near-term moral disaster.
quotes.t: 21 criticisms of EA I'm thinking about

quotes.c: People want to give to religious causes, to education, to cancer/AIDS/other disease research, to things that matter to them. Why isn't there an Education Charity Evaluators for people who care about education? Or a Christian/Jewish/Islamic Charity Evaluators for people who are going to make those donations anyways? A Cancer Charity Evaluators for people who lost a loved one to cancer? People are going to donate in these areas. Why aren't we trying to improve those donations?
quotes.m: People are going to donate in these areas. Why aren't we trying to improve those donations?
quotes.sum: The author argues that the movement should improve mainstream donations to causes people already care about, rather than focusing only on niche priorities and elite donors.
quotes.t: The Hundred Billion Dollar Opportunity that EAs mostly ignore

quotes.c: That said, I do think the view contains some under-appreciated insights that are worth taking on board, at least under the remit of “moral uncertainty”. For those concerned about the Repugnant Conclusion, I think perfectionism at least offers a better alternative than bleak “negative” views that deny any positive value to our existence.
quotes.m: For those concerned about the Repugnant Conclusion, I think perfectionism at least offers a better alternative than bleak “negative” views that deny any positive value to our existence.
quotes.sum: The author says perfectionism may be a useful response to population-ethics worries about the Repugnant Conclusion, especially under moral uncertainty.
quotes.t: The Nietzschean Challenge to Effective Altruism

quotes.c: Maximize Expected Choiceworthiness (MEC) is a theory about how we ought to make decisions under ethical uncertainty. [1] It says that we ought to handle ethical uncertainty in the way that Expected Utility Theory (EUT) handles descriptive uncertainty. I argue that MEC faces a dilemma: it either issues zero practical guidance or else is wildly fanatical in the decision-theoretic sense.
quotes.m: MEC faces a dilemma: it either issues zero practical guidance or else is wildly fanatical in the decision-theoretic sense.
quotes.sum: The author argues that applying expected-value reasoning to moral uncertainty either gives no decision guidance or produces extreme fanaticism.
quotes.t: A dilemma for Maximize Expected Choiceworthiness (MEC)

quotes.c: Besides its significant contribution to climate change, animal agriculture is also responsible for 80% of rainforest destruction [9] and uses 80% of agricultural land. [10] It contributes to world hunger and water scarcity through inefficient use of valuable resources, with 75% of the global soy harvest [11] and 30% of fresh water [12] consumed by animal agriculture. Given the broad negative effects of animal agriculture, it seems likely that it also causes significant amounts of wild animal suffering (e.g. due to the use of insecticides, habit loss, droughts, climate change, etc.)
quotes.m: Given the broad negative effects of animal agriculture, it seems likely that it also causes significant amounts of wild animal suffering (e.g. due to the use of insecticides, habit loss, droughts, climate change, etc.)
quotes.sum: The author argues that animal farming likely harms wild animals as well as contributing to environmental damage and resource scarcity.
quotes.t: The Importance of Intercausal Impacts

quotes.c: In terms of belief in an Omni-God, I have become a de-facto atheist, lost my faith recently, but since I think claiming I am 100% sure ''ethical monotheism'' and classical theism goes against the Middle Way, I will call myself a Teapot Agnostic, in the sense that while I think the existence of the abrahamic god is as unlikely as an invisible tiny teapot floating through space, I am still open to the existence of an Omni-God, if someone gives me a convicing reason to believe in one and answers my many questions.
quotes.m: I think the existence of the abrahamic god is as unlikely as an invisible tiny teapot floating through space
quotes.sum: The author describes losing belief in the Abrahamic God while retaining an agnostic openness to convincing evidence for a deity.
quotes.t: Advice for a 16-year-old girl

quotes.c: Long story short, I think reaching justification for that is not easy and perhaps not currently possible. However it’s not my intention to convert anyone to agnosticism, because I’m confident that most if not all religion may be fatally flawed and here’s why:
quotes.m: I’m confident that most if not all religion may be fatally flawed and here’s why:
quotes.sum: The author argues that certainty about religious belief or disbelief is difficult to justify, while maintaining that most religions are probably fundamentally flawed.
quotes.t: Why bother doing the most good?

quotes.c: If a hardware overhang is undesirable, it may be better if large, well-funded AI teams invested large amounts of money into hardware to be on the frontier of hardware advancement so that if hardware advances to the point where an ASI can be created, the first entity to create an ASI is likely to be a large, well-funded team. Since the first ASI could become a singleton [5] or perform a pivotal act , once the first aligned ASI is created, the risk of a subsequent unaligned ASI harming the world is probably low.
quotes.m: Since the first ASI could become a singleton [5] or perform a pivotal act , once the first aligned ASI is created, the risk of a subsequent unaligned ASI harming the world is probably low.
quotes.sum: It suggests concentrating AI hardware in well-funded teams so that the first aligned superintelligence can take decisive control and prevent later unsafe AI.
quotes.t: How Do AI Timelines Affect Existential Risk?

quotes.c: It’s very fashionable these days to say democracy is dying off. I don’t believe that, as I think a lot of this argument is rooted in golden ageism. That being said, Brexit/Trump/Bolsanaro and the broader global rise of (mostly right-wing) populism aren’t necessarily good news for EA causes or global security.
quotes.m: Brexit/Trump/Bolsanaro and the broader global rise of (mostly right-wing) populism aren’t necessarily good news for EA causes or global security.
quotes.sum: The author rejects claims that democracy is collapsing, but worries that right-wing populism may harm EA priorities and global security.
quotes.t: How should we invest in democracy as an EA-adjacent issue? Some early thoughts

quotes.c: Second, we don’t think that extreme stability (of the sort that could make the future contingent on early events) would necessarily require a lot of dedicated effort. The options for increasing stability we sketch in sections 0.2.2 and 6 and the assumption of a singleton -like entity in sections 0.3 and 8 are brought up to make the point that stability is feasible at least in those circumstances.
quotes.m: extreme stability (of the sort that could make the future contingent on early events)
quotes.sum: The author argues that AGI could make social values unusually stable, leaving the far future dependent on decisions made early on.
quotes.t: AGI and Lock-In

quotes.c: I think a central element of Magma’s approach should be employing a variety of AI systems with different capabilities and incentives, so that they can provide checks and balances on each other.
quotes.m: I think a central element of Magma’s approach should be employing a variety of AI systems with different capabilities and incentives, so that they can provide checks and balances on each other.
quotes.sum: He argues that advanced AI should be overseen by multiple AI systems with differing goals and abilities that can check one another.
quotes.t: How might we align transformative AI if it’s developed very soon?

quotes.c: I previously created a formal literature review of research on " The Moral Consideration of Artificial Entities " and a brief, informal primer on " The Importance of Artificial Sentience ." Tldr; seeking to expand the moral circle to include artificial sentient beings seems an important, neglected, and potentially tractable method for improving the long-term future and avoiding risks of astronomical suffering.
quotes.m: seeking to expand the moral circle to include artificial sentient beings seems an important, neglected, and potentially tractable method for improving the long-term future and avoiding risks of astronomical suffering.
quotes.sum: The author argues that extending moral concern to sentient AI could be a neglected way to improve the far future and prevent immense suffering.
quotes.t: The History of AI Rights Research

quotes.c: Obviously a very young religion so close to its vital source will see this more often than one established for centuries. In historic terms, we’re doing better than any spiritual movement in any previous century. But via the powers of explicit reasoning perhaps we can do even better. Every case like QCs is tragic and should cause some measure of regret and introspection.
quotes.m: In historic terms, we’re doing better than any spiritual movement in any previous century.
quotes.sum: The author frames their community as a young religion or spiritual movement and argues that explicit reasoning can reduce its tendency toward harmful zealotry.
quotes.t: Religion = Cult + Culture

quotes.c: Conclusion: Even if we survive the existential risks of the next few hundred years, it may not be possible to avoid the collapse of a highly technological civilization. This could greatly reduce the expected value of longterm interventions.
quotes.m: This could greatly reduce the expected value of longterm interventions.
quotes.sum: The author argues that technological civilization may eventually collapse even if near-term extinction risks are avoided, weakening the case for long-term interventions.
quotes.t: A critique of strong longtermism

quotes.c: 86% of Americans think Biden is too old for another term . And even though many Republican senators dislike Trump, they seem unlikely to endorse Biden, given the risk of backlash from their constituents .
quotes.m: many Republican senators dislike Trump, they seem unlikely to endorse Biden, given the risk of backlash from their constituents .
quotes.sum: The author argues that Biden's perceived age problem and Republican fear of voter backlash make cross-party support unlikely.
quotes.t: Using game theory to elect a centrist in the 2024 US Presidential Election

quotes.c: AI regulation can plausibly both affect the speed and the direction of the AI industry. Our prior should be that regulation slows down the speed of AI development, though some mechanisms discussed in the report could push the other way (e.g. increasing regulatory certainty). Further, we should expect regulation to incentivize the development of AI systems that can more cheaply and effectively comply with EU requirements, which seems useful if the requirements are well designed.
quotes.sum: EU AI rules will likely slow AI development while steering firms toward systems designed to meet European requirements.
quotes.t: Supplement to "The Brussels Effect and AI: How EU AI regulation will impact the global AI market"

quotes.c: Discussing extinction risks and stagnation risks together as “existential risks” also leads to a focus on the “astronomical waste” argument, since extinction risks and stagnation risks both prevent technological maturity from being achieved. Since technological maturity is an instrumental goal to maximising the number of consciousnesses, which is a terminal goal only desirable under non-person affecting total utilitarianism and prioritarianism, and most people don’t subscribe to these moral theories, use of the term “existential risk” makes the case for mitigating extinction risks less convincing.
quotes.m: Since technological maturity is an instrumental goal to maximising the number of consciousnesses, which is a terminal goal only desirable under non-person affecting total utilitarianism and prioritarianism, and most people don’t subscribe to these moral theories, use of the term “existential risk” makes the case for mitigating extinction risks less convincing.
quotes.sum: The author argues that calling extinction and stagnation “existential risks” smuggles in a controversial goal: maximizing future conscious lives.
quotes.t: “Existential Risk” is badly named and leads to narrow focus on astronomical waste

quotes.c: In August 2020, I correctly predicted there would be an unprecedented violent skirmish in D.C. sometime between the election and the inauguration (my premise was that Biden would win). However, I greatly overestimated the size of pro-Trump belligerents anticipating tens of thousands even eclipsing six figures. I also overestimated the scope of the violence.
quotes.sum: The author says they predicted post-election violence in Washington but expected it to be much larger and more violent than it was.
quotes.t: The top X-factor EA neglects: destabilization of the United States

quotes.c: People earlier in their careers, researchers, and people with expertise in many domains should consider learning to speed-read. Learning to speed-read (via a self-paced course) has made large, important bodies of literature significantly more accessible. It allows me to decide how much time I think it’s worth spending on a book, article or report, and to get as much information as I can within that self-imposed time constraint.
quotes.sum: The author recommends speed-reading as a way to make large bodies of research accessible and deliberately control time spent reading.
quotes.t: An Exercise in Speed-Reading: The National Security Commission on AI (NSCAI) Final Report

quotes.c: Haidt says right wingers and religious folks make better parents, citing that they are increasingly happier and more rooted in communities, liberal kids are more depressed and more vulnerable to phones. But while we should and do care a lot about it, being a good parent is not primarily about whether your kids are happy now. There are realistic margins where it is highly correct to make kids less happy now to give them better futures, and instill in them better skills, values and habits.
quotes.m: There are realistic margins where it is highly correct to make kids less happy now to give them better futures, and instill in them better skills, values and habits.
quotes.sum: The author argues that good parenting can rightly trade children’s present happiness for skills, values, habits, and better future prospects.
quotes.t: On the 2nd CWT with Jonathan Haidt

quotes.c: Yet, our ideas about what's sacred change. Five hundred years ago minor theological disagreements were enough to start wars, and now in much of the world people tolerate each other despite radically different beliefs. So although today the idea of moral trades and moral uncertainty may not appeal to everyone, in five hundred years these ideas may well come to be seen as the cornerstone of all functional societies. Perhaps at the end of our own Culture War, exhausted from the fighting, we'll be willing to adopt moral uncertainty and moral trade as necessary means for restoring peace.
quotes.m: Perhaps at the end of our own Culture War, exhausted from the fighting, we'll be willing to adopt moral uncertainty and moral trade as necessary means for restoring peace.
quotes.sum: The author argues that accepting moral uncertainty and bargaining across values could eventually become necessary for social peace.
quotes.t: Fundamental Uncertainty: Chapter 8 - When does fundamental uncertainty matter?

quotes.c: One might object that the Very Repugnant Conclusion has limited practical significance because it represents an unlikely scenario. But the same could be said about the Repugnant Conclusion (especially in its suffering-free variant). I do not claim that the Very Repugnant Conclusion is the most realistic case to consider. When I claim that it is more practically relevant than the Repugnant Conclusion, it is simply because it does explicitly involve tradeoffs between happiness and (extreme) suffering, which we know will also be true of our decisions pertaining to the future.
quotes.m: it does explicitly involve tradeoffs between happiness and (extreme) suffering, which we know will also be true of our decisions pertaining to the future.
quotes.sum: The author argues that population-ethics thought experiments matter because future choices will involve real tradeoffs between happiness and extreme suffering.
quotes.t: Critique of MacAskill’s “Is It Good to Make Happy People?”

quotes.c: I don’t have a considered view on which organisms are sentient or how much, or on how much different organisms matter morally compared to other organisms.
quotes.m: I don’t have a considered view on which organisms are sentient or how much, or on how much different organisms matter morally compared to other organisms.
quotes.sum: The author says they have not formed a settled view about which organisms are conscious or how much moral weight different organisms deserve.
quotes.t: What’s alive right now?

quotes.c: The obvious reason to form inside views is to form truer beliefs - AI X-risk is a weird, controversial and confusing thing, and it's important to have good beliefs on it. I think this is true to an extent, but that in practice inside views tend to feel true a lot more than they are true. When I have an inside view, that just feels like how the world is, it feels deeply true and compelling. But empirically, a lot of people have inside views, that are mutually contradictory, and all find their own views compelling. They can't all be right!
quotes.m: inside views tend to feel true a lot more than they are true.
quotes.sum: The author warns that personal intuitions about AI risk can feel compelling even when different people hold contradictory intuitions.
quotes.t: Concrete Advice for Forming Inside Views on AI Safety

quotes.c: This is the case for longtermism in a nutshell. The premises are simple, and I don’t think they’re particularly controversial. Yet taking them seriously amounts to a moral revolution—one with far-reaching implications for how activists, researchers, policy makers, and indeed all of us should think and act.
quotes.m: Yet taking them seriously amounts to a moral revolution—one with far-reaching implications for how activists, researchers, policy makers, and indeed all of us should think and act.
quotes.sum: MacAskill argues that longtermism should fundamentally reshape how everyone, including policymakers and activists, thinks and acts.
quotes.t: What We Owe the Future, Chapter 1

quotes.c: TLDR: Predictions about apocalyptic AI parallel both historical and contemporary Christain Apocalyptic claims(which I take to be untrustworthy). This is distinct from apocalyptic climate change which is non-analogous to such religious apocalyptic claims. Therefore we should treat the apocalyptic claims of climate scientists as more credible than those of AI researchers, and as a result, EA should place climate change as a higher priority than AI alignment. This is not to say that AI isn’t a risk, nor that alignment shouldn’t be a priority.
quotes.m: Therefore we should treat the apocalyptic claims of climate scientists as more credible than those of AI researchers, and as a result, EA should place climate change as a higher priority than AI alignment.
quotes.sum: The author argues that apocalyptic AI forecasts resemble unreliable religious prophecy, so EA should prioritize climate change above AI alignment.
quotes.t: The Credibility of Apocalyptic Claims: A Critique of Techno-Futurism within Existential Risk

quotes.c: Some AI researchers focus more on the ‘carrot’ of aligned benevolent AI, others on the ‘stick’ of existential risk. But the point is, AI will likely either be extremely good or extremely bad - it’s difficult to be AI-neutral.
quotes.m: AI will likely either be extremely good or extremely bad - it’s difficult to be AI-neutral.
quotes.sum: The author argues that advanced AI is unlikely to have neutral effects: it will be either extraordinarily beneficial or catastrophically harmful.
quotes.t: Longtermists Should Work on AI - There is No "AI Neutral" Scenario

quotes.c: Together with the rest of my research group we have launched our own research organisation: Epoch . We are working on anticipating the future of Artificial Intelligence. Back when I was interning at the Future of Humanity Institute, I resolved that one of my career goals would be to coordinate a research group.
quotes.m: We are working on anticipating the future of Artificial Intelligence.
quotes.sum: The author describes founding Epoch, a research group aimed at forecasting and preparing for AI's future development.
quotes.t: Bahamian Adventures: An Epic Tale of Entrepreneurship, AI Strategy Research and Potatoes

quotes.c: First, let's imagine that power in our hypothetical global government is never transferred, and some individual (or some group of like-minded individuals) has complete power over humanity in perpetuity. Technologies like digital people or biotech that allows for life extension may allow the same autocrat to rule over humanity for a very long time. This longevity may be even more extreme in the case of digital people, which may be able to be run at different relative speeds. If the digital autocrat and their subjects were run slower and faster respectively, a single autocrat could preside over virtually endless generations of subjects.
quotes.m: If the digital autocrat and their subjects were run slower and faster respectively, a single autocrat could preside over virtually endless generations of subjects.
quotes.sum: The author argues that life extension and digital people could let a single ruler retain total power over humanity across virtually endless generations.
quotes.t: Present-day good intentions aren't sufficient to make the longterm future good in expectation

quotes.c: The research above positions lobbying for unilateral divorce as a potentially effective lever in reducing suicide rates. Before funding such lobbying, we should first conduct further research to either strengthen or reject the hypothesis that divorce law does reduce suicides, and to investigate the role of country context.
quotes.sum: The author argues that unilateral-divorce laws may reduce suicide and should be researched further before advocacy is funded.
quotes.t: [Cause Exploration Prizes] Why we should work on preventing suicide

quotes.c: Facial expressions (alongside posture) can be used to measure track affective states, at least in non-human animals. That is, it is possible to train up an AI to recognise and measure different emotional expressions, allowing the measurement of wellbeing. To the best of my knowledge, this has been most extensively examined in animals—there is a rich literature looking at the emotional expressions of mammals in particular, and research looking at the emotional expression of pain in taxa beyond mammals. quotes.m: AI developers may want to possess remote shutdown ability for each other in order to disincentivize dangerous racing and allow a project with sufficient lead time to solve safety problems unencumbered.
quotes.sum: The author suggests industry-wide AI fallback rules, including possible mutual remote shutdown powers among labs, to curb dangerous races and buy time for safety work.
quotes.t: Idea: Safe Fallback Regulations for Widely Deployed AI Systems

quotes.c: Longtermism says to calculate expected value while treating lives as morally equal no matter when they occur. Longtermists do not discount the lives of future generations. In general, calculating the expected value of an action over the entire potential future is quite difficult, because we run into the cluelessness problem, where we just don't know what effects an action will have far into the future.
quotes.m: Longtermists do not discount the lives of future generations.
quotes.sum: Longtermism treats future people as morally equal to present people, while acknowledging that predicting far-future consequences is difficult.
quotes.t: Longtermism as Effective Altruism

quotes.c: Community Notes is a fact-checking tool available to US-based users of X/Twitter which allows readers to attach notes to posts to give them clarifying context. It uses an open-source bridging-based ranking algorithm intended to promote notes which receive cross-partisan support , and demote notes with a strong partisan lean.
quotes.m: It uses an open-source bridging-based ranking algorithm intended to promote notes which receive cross-partisan support , and demote notes with a strong partisan lean.
quotes.sum: The author describes Community Notes as a decentralized fact-checking system designed to reward cross-partisan agreement and penalize partisan ratings.
quotes.t: Community Notes by X

quotes.c: Suppose that we develop superintelligence safely, govern it well, and make good use of the cornucopian wealth and near magical technological powers that this technology can unlock. If this transition to the machine intelligence era goes well, human labor becomes obsolete. We would thus enter a condition of "post-instrumentality", in which our efforts are not needed for any practical purpose. Furthermore, at technological maturity, human nature becomes entirely malleable.
quotes.m: We would thus enter a condition of "post-instrumentality", in which our efforts are not needed for any practical purpose.
quotes.sum: A successful transition to superintelligent AI could make human work unnecessary and eventually make human nature fully changeable.
quotes.t: Nick Bostrom’s new book, “Deep Utopia”, is out today

quotes.c: I see the case for forcing divestiture of TikTok as overdetermined. It is functionally Chinese spyware, with a history of lying about it and doing things like tracking journalists. China does the same to similar American companies. China seems to very clearly be using its influence to move public opinion, and has now put out 150 million push notifications to call Congress on its behalf, and one has to wonder what deal was made with known dealmaker Donald Trump.
quotes.sum: The author argues that TikTok should be forced to divest because it functions as Chinese surveillance and political influence infrastructure.
quotes.t: On the Latest TikTok Bill

quotes.c: Engaging with the book also reconnected me to my own spiritual longing and the existential questions that brought me to effective altruism myself. Engaging with these foundations again added to my own sense of meaning in the world, so I'm sharing it for others to read, too.
quotes.m: Engaging with the book also reconnected me to my own spiritual longing and the existential questions that brought me to effective altruism myself.

quotes.c: Before I get into that, I want to explicitly say that the intention of these reading groups is open exploration of what the people in the group actually care about in their lives - rather than to rehearse standard EA arguments, or to practice some particular view of morality. I’m posting this on Forum because I expect there to be people in the EA space who would benefit from this sort of open exploration, not because I think that the good version of these groups is ‘how to live a good EA life’. I’m not interested in ‘a good EA life’: I am interested in people’s lives though, and what living a good life means to them.
quotes.m: I’m not interested in ‘a good EA life’: I am interested in people’s lives though, and what living a good life means to them.
quotes.sum: The author rejects prescribing a single “good EA life” and favors open exploration of what a good life means to each person.
quotes.t: Virtual how to live a good life reading groups

quotes.c: There were around 4 entries arguing that we were living through an ongoing collapse that is intrinsically associated with capitalism. This is a frame I have not engaged with a lot, which made it hard to assess the entries. quotes.c: That’s a $50 million increase over last year, significantly driven by GiveWell’s impressive progress on finding more cost-effective opportunities. quotes.sum: The author says GiveWell found far more highly cost-effective global-poverty funding opportunities than expected, prompting a $50 million increase in planned support.

quotes.c: Trying to line these up with historical societies or ideologies is ... difficult. Many societies do not have a concept of 'neighbor,' [2] and some do not understand ethics in terms of circles of moral concern. [3] A few moral systems are universalistic (i.e. they teach that people should have moral concern for all of humanity): Christianity, [4] liberal democracy, [5] and maybe Buddhism. [6] Actually practicing universalism is really hard: Most societies which preach universalism do not live up to its ideals.
quotes.m: Actually practicing universalism is really hard: Most societies which preach universalism do not live up to its ideals.
quotes.sum: The author argues that moral concern for all humanity is rare in practice, even among religions and political systems that preach it.

quotes.c: Always be thinking about what the best next experiment you run should be : When you show experimental results (in meetings or in slack), you should also include discussion of your proposed next possible steps immediately after (and proposed prioritization). The best researchers are able to iterate between running experiments and deciding on the best next step independently.
quotes.m: The best researchers are able to iterate between running experiments and deciding on the best next step independently.
quotes.sum: The author argues that alignment researchers should independently prioritize and propose their next experiments, rather than only reporting results.

quotes.c: (Tangentially: it is interesting to ponder what truth there is in past UN Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjöld's statement that: "It is more noble to give yourself completely to one individual than to labor diligently for the salvation of the masses." quotes.c: Third, values differ, and a broad-based movement benefits from encouraging diversity and disagreement [3] . For example, there are people who strongly discount the future. People who do not assign moral weight to animals. People who view mental suffering as more important than physical suffering. People who embrace person-affecting views. Average utilitarians. Negative utilitarians. And so on. And these different views lead to different conclusions about what maximizes ”the good” - meaning that different causes should be prioritized, even after accepting all of the fundamental goals of effective altruism.
quotes.m: these different views lead to different conclusions about what maximizes ”the good” - meaning that different causes should be prioritized, even after accepting all of the fundamental goals of effective altruism.
quotes.sum: The author argues that effective altruism should remain broad enough to include competing moral theories, because they imply different priorities.

quotes.c: What if Alex miscalculates, and attempts to seize power or undermine human control before it is able to fully succeed? quotes.c: However, I don’t think that the actions listed above should be a longtermist priority, partly because I think that digital minds are much more important. quotes.c: Community pressure : It is difficult to say no to community members, which can cause a long list of projects, causing self-investment to be deprioritised Possible mitigation: Part of my motivation to write this post is to make it common knowledge that community builders should self-invest, and community members should be understanding of this. quotes.c: One of the reasons for the debate around so-called “gain of function research”, the enhancement of potential pandemic pathogens, having stalled is the fact that researchers disagree over the benefits and risks of research. However, this does not mean that we should not try to calculate the expected value of a given experiment; rather we should try to pool the opinions of different experts to come up with a consolidated estimate.
quotes.m: However, this does not mean that we should not try to calculate the expected value of a given experiment; rather we should try to pool the opinions of different experts to come up with a consolidated estimate.
quotes.sum: The author argues that disputed high-risk pathogen research should still be assessed through pooled expert estimates of expected value.

quotes.c: If Bostrom is right that minimizing existential risk requires a stable and powerful global government, then politicide, propaganda, genocide, scapegoating, and stagnation are all instrumental in pursuing the strategy of minimizing anthropogenic risk. A global state with this goal is therefore itself a catastrophic risk.
quotes.m: A global state with this goal is therefore itself a catastrophic risk.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a powerful global state built to reduce existential risks could itself become a catastrophic danger.

quotes.c: For instance, what’s happened recently is that lots more resources entered the community (as tech stocks and crypto went up), so the bar was dropped, and then the market crash decreased the amount of resources available, so the bar was raised a bit. I think there’s a decent possibility that living as uploads may be more efficient, but I wanted to start by imagining a world where we’ve solved the biological system problems, because I think a good future for many will resemble that even if it’s implemented on different hardware.
quotes.sum: The author treats a future in which people live as digital uploads as a plausible, potentially more efficient alternative to biological life.

quotes.m: I think there are good reasons to think that the expected value of the future won’t be positive conditional on avoiding existential risks from bioweapons, climate change and nuclear war.

quotes.c: My estimate has many important limitations. For example, it omits potential downsides to R&D (e.g. increasing global catastrophic risks), and it focuses on a specific scenario in which historical rates of return to R&D continue to apply even as population growth stagnates. Alternative scenarios might change the bottom line. For instance, R&D today might speed up the development of some future technology that drastically accelerates R&D progress. This would significantly increase the returns to R&D, but in my view would also strengthen the case for Open Phil to focus on reducing risks from that technology rather than accelerating its development.
quotes.m: This would significantly increase the returns to R&D, but in my view would also strengthen the case for Open Phil to focus on reducing risks from that technology rather than accelerating its development.
quotes.sum: The author argues that even highly productive research may be less valuable than reducing the catastrophic risks created by the technologies it speeds up.

quotes.c: In practice, it seems very easy to overdo deference-morality - compared to our ancestral environment, it seems much less useful today. Also, whether or not deference-morality makes sense depends on how much you trust the agents you’re deferring to - but it’s often difficult to gain trust in agents more capable than you, because they’re likely better at deception than you. Cult leaders exploit this.
quotes.m: Cult leaders exploit this.
quotes.sum: Moral deference is often less useful today, and deferring to more capable people is risky because they may be better able to deceive or manipulate you.
quotes.t: Moral strategies at different capability levels

quotes.sum: The author argues that advanced AI could remain dangerous even if it is not conscious.

It seems hard to reasonably reject this possibility.
quotes.m: The flipside of using expected value reasoning with heavy-tails is that we have to use it with negative tails too [16]
quotes.sum: The author argues that longtermist calculations must count enormous possible future suffering as well as enormous benefits, which can make space expansion look harmful in expectation.
quotes.t: Red teaming a model for estimating the value of longtermist interventions - A critique of Tarsney's "The Epistemic Challenge to Longtermism"

quotes.c: Sometimes, people have a way higher opinion of me than is deserved, and put way too much stock in what I say. I think this is both empirically incorrect, and makes things feel way higher stakes for me! In general, giving advice is hard and noisy. If you ask someone else, they’ll likely disagree on a bunch of points!
quotes.m: In general, giving advice is hard and noisy. If you ask someone else, they’ll likely disagree on a bunch of points!

quotes.c: One of my pet peeves is people calling AI Safety a longtermist cause area. It is entirely reasonable to consider AI Safety a high priority cause area without putting significant value on future generations, let alone buying things like total utilitarianism or the astronomical waste arguments. Given fairly mainstream (among EAs) models of AI timelines and AI X-Risk, it seems highly likely that we get AGI within my lifetime, and that this will be a catastrophic/existential risk.
quotes.m: Given fairly mainstream (among EAs) models of AI timelines and AI X-Risk, it seems highly likely that we get AGI within my lifetime, and that this will be a catastrophic/existential risk.
quotes.sum: AI safety need not depend on valuing distant future generations: the author expects AGI within their lifetime and sees it as likely catastrophic or existential.
quotes.t: My Most Likely Reason to Die Young is AI X-Risk

quotes.c: As AIs become more powerful, we will need to carefully manage access to tools that could assist in causing harm, as well as information regarding dangerous viral genomes. [14] Restrictions can be designed to minimize impact on legitimate research, but in some cases there will be tradeoffs to be made.
quotes.m: Restrictions can be designed to minimize impact on legitimate research, but in some cases there will be tradeoffs to be made.
quotes.sum: As AI capabilities grow, access to harmful tools and dangerous virus information should be restricted, even if that sometimes burdens legitimate research.

quotes.c: First, this analysis assumes that most beings in the future will be descendants of current people. If there are digital beings that are worthy of moral consideration in the future, and the number of them dwarves physical people, then it’s possible that the Charlemagne Effect won’t be nearly as strong compared to the expected value of TLIs, even if existential risk is reduced by a minuscule amount. quotes.m: If there are digital beings that are worthy of moral consideration in the future, and the number of them dwarves physical people, then it’s possible that the Charlemagne Effect won’t be nearly as strong compared to the expected value of TLIs, even if existential risk is reduced by a minuscule amount.

quotes.t: The Charlemagne Effect: The Longtermist Case For Neartermism

quotes.c: I think the answer is no, because multiple billiard balls is a textbook example of a chaotic system that maximizes entropy quickly, and there's no reason information should be preserved for 20 seconds. quotes.m: there's no reason information should be preserved for 20 seconds.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a gas rapidly becomes unpredictable because chaotic collisions erase usable information.
quotes.t: Is a random box of gas predictable after 20 seconds?

quotes.sum: High confidence should imply confidence that one will not sharply revise that belief after further reflection.
quotes.t: Terminate deliberation based on resilience, not certainty

quotes.m: When considering a new addition to the board, I think the board should be asking something much closer to "Is this one of the 10 best people in the world to sit on this board?" than to "Is this person fine?"

quotes.c: Tractability - In general, we should not take existing costs and constraints as binding, because they can be changed by our actions. quotes.c: I thought Maxwell Tabarrok’s The Offense-Defense Balance Rarely Changes was a good contribution to the discourse, and appreciated his attempt to use various lines of data to “kick the tires” on the case that an AI could in principle defeat all humans by inventing technologies that would allow them to dominate humans. quotes.c: The return to working on existential risk (x-risk) is a function of three variables from a total utilitarian perspective. These are the productivity of the marginal dollar put into x-risk, the current level of existential risk and the expected value of the future.

quotes.c: Slightly technical why this happens: this phenomenon happens because the actors do not all have perfect knowledge of the true value of the action; instead, they all have some error in their estimation of the value. Because the actors are not coordinating, we should assume that their errors are not identical, meaning they disagree about their estimates of the value of the action. You could think about a random normal distribution of estimated-value clustered around the true value of the action. The more actors (estimated-values you draw from the normal distribution) the more likely you are to get an outlier who thinks the value is positive when it is actually negative.
quotes.m: The more actors (estimated-values you draw from the normal distribution) the more likely you are to get an outlier who thinks the value is positive when it is actually negative.
quotes.sum: Uncoordinated people can collectively cause harm because at least one may mistakenly judge a bad action to be beneficial and carry it out.
quotes.t: The Unilateralist's Curse, An Explanation

quotes.c: My argument (Cosmic's Mugger, or CM) is that there are cases where these two sentences are completely different. I'll describe a theoretical case where we would accept a 49.99% chance of doom just in order to speed up expansion by one second. This is a case where the quantity of good achievable increases exponentially over the length of the cosmic endowment (In this precise case, the quantity of good achievable with t seconds of cosmic endowment would be 2^t).
quotes.m: we would accept a 49.99% chance of doom just in order to speed up expansion by one second.
quotes.sum: The author argues that if future value grows exponentially with cosmic time, expected-value reasoning can imply risking near-certain doom to begin expansion one second sooner.
quotes.t: Cosmic's Mugger : Should we really delay cosmic expansion ?

quotes.c: If strong AIs are given objectives that are poorly specified, they could pursue undesirable actions and behave unethically. quotes.m: If these strong AIs are sufficiently powerful, these misspecifications could create an existential catastrophe.
quotes.sum: Poorly specified goals in very powerful AI systems could cause catastrophe, so researchers should develop better ethical objectives and avoid locking in bad values.

quotes.c: This won’t be true of everyone, but my impression is that people under about 25 often weigh others’ opinions more heavily and have a harder time expressing clearly when they’re uncomfortable with something.

quotes.c: “I believe in you” → “I predict the world will be a better place for your presence in it. quotes.c: A recent example of the effects of a large moral circle without utilitarianism is the overturning of Roe v. Wade. Anti-abortion activists and the Supreme Court justices who overturned it have a large moral circle as defined above, since they want to impose their values on an entire country. But they are not utilitarians with suffering-focused values, and are instead motivated by religious principles and the belief that life is sacred.

But I think if you refuse a bet, you should be able to reject this bet without taking into account what bets you have taken in the past or are still taking in the future.

quotes.c: Hiring people through a "Tour of Service" which is time-bound and has specific outcomes can address these concerns. An example summary of a Tour is: join CEA for two years with the goal of doubling the percentage of respondents to the EA survey who say they made an important connection on the EA Forum.
quotes.m: join CEA for two years with the goal of doubling the percentage of respondents to the EA survey who say they made an important connection on the EA Forum.
quotes.sum: EA organizations should offer fixed-term, outcome-based jobs so candidates need not commit to a role indefinitely.
quotes.t: EA Tours of Service

quotes.c: … to shame tech companies for building useless/flashy systems (e.g., autonomous agents trained in evolution-like environments to exhibit survival-oriented intelligence), so they remain focussed on building usable/useful systems (e.g., DALL-E, PaLM) preceding and during a tech company singularity. In other words, we should try to steer tech company singularities toward developing comprehensive AI services (CAIS) rather than AAGI.
quotes.m: we should try to steer tech company singularities toward developing comprehensive AI services (CAIS) rather than AAGI.
quotes.sum: The author argues that public pressure should steer rapidly advancing tech companies toward useful AI services rather than autonomous general AI systems.
quotes.t: "Tech company singularities", and steering them to reduce x-risk

quotes.c: There’s a tricky question about how fast we should be spending this down. Compared to others in EA, I think I’m unusually sympathetic to patient philanthropy : I don’t think the chance of a hinge moment in the next decade is dramatically higher than the chance of a hinge moment in 2072-82 (say); and I think our understanding of how to do good is improving every year, which gives a reason for delay.
quotes.m: I think our understanding of how to do good is improving every year, which gives a reason for delay.
quotes.sum: MacAskill argues that charitable funds may be worth saving for later, because future opportunities may be just as pivotal and people may learn better ways to help.
quotes.t: EA and the current funding situation

quotes.c: However, even then, there were plenty of people who found Brent to be toxic and dangerous — it was not a secret or even a controversial statement that Brent had a lot of darkness in him; I'd say that pro-Brent and anti-Brent people mostly just differed in how they assessed the expected value of interactions with him.
quotes.m: pro-Brent and anti-Brent people mostly just differed in how they assessed the expected value of interactions with him.
quotes.sum: The author says disagreement about a toxic community member was largely about whether interacting with him was worthwhile.
quotes.t: The impossible problem of due process

quotes.c: In the long run, in the absence of decisive theories of consciousness, it is not clear what mechanisms could cause a shift in approach to building apparent digital minds that would make them more likely to be conscious. It could require dismissing or down-weighting the value of many beings in our expanded moral circle. This might be politically or emotionally difficult.
quotes.m: It could require dismissing or down-weighting the value of many beings in our expanded moral circle.
quotes.sum: Uncertainty about AI consciousness could lead society to give moral weight to apparent digital beings, making later reversal emotionally and politically difficult.
quotes.t: The importance of getting digital consciousness right

quotes.c: (a) The AGI required to learn this imitation is extremely powerful, and this could imply a dangerous delay between when we can build any dangerous AGI at all, and when we can build AGIs that would work for alignment using perfect-imitation capability amplification.
quotes.sum: Capability amplification may require an extremely powerful AI before it can be used for alignment, leaving a dangerous period when unsafe AI arrives first.
quotes.t: Challenges to Christiano’s capability amplification proposal

quotes.c: There are two closely connected ways to prevent dangers of the future nuclear war: global government and an effective monitoring system. “Global government” is any type of organization which lower the number of independent actors in the world, which in our case are actors capable to develop or-and owning nuclear weapons. It could be a UN, a set of international treaties or one superpower which takes over the world, or even superintelligent AI turning into Singleton.
quotes.m: It could be a UN, a set of international treaties or one superpower which takes over the world, or even superintelligent AI turning into Singleton.
quotes.sum: The author argues that preventing future nuclear war requires global government and monitoring, potentially extending to a single superpower or an AI “Singleton.”
quotes.t: The future of nuclear war

quotes.c: Sentience is not limited to humans/biological beings It is perhaps a semantic issue where you draw the line about moral claims about sentience and sentient beings and empirical claims about sentience. But I think in particular the view that a “biological” body is not required for sentience and that e.g. digital minds could be sentient is an important consideration and relevant in a lot of longtermist EA prioritisation.
quotes.m: a “biological” body is not required for sentience and that e.g. digital minds could be sentient
quotes.sum: The author says sentience need not require a biological body, so digital minds may deserve moral consideration in long-term priorities.
quotes.t: What are the key claims of EA?

quotes.c: Some people have suggested that it’s important that early WAW interventions challenge these beliefs, because any analysis that ignores natural wild animal suffering is very incomplete. Tackling aquatic noise would not challenge these assumptions, while something like vaccinating wild animals for their own sake could challenge it (at least if it was done in a way where many people would hear about it). However, in Šimčikas (2021) , I argue that perhaps challenging these assumptions is less important in the long term because most of the expected wild animal suffering in the far future might be caused by humans (by spreading wildlife beyond Earth).
quotes.m: most of the expected wild animal suffering in the far future might be caused by humans (by spreading wildlife beyond Earth).
quotes.sum: The author argues that future human expansion beyond Earth could create most wild-animal suffering, making it a major long-term welfare concern.
quotes.t: Reducing aquatic noise as a wild animal welfare intervention

quotes.c: I broadly believe that the assumptions behind MSR make sense. But I think the standard presentations of it don’t give very good intuitions for how it might actually work in practice. In this post I present an alternative framing of MSR centered around the concept of “psychohistory”.
quotes.m: In this post I present an alternative framing of MSR centered around the concept of “psychohistory”.
quotes.sum: The author endorses the assumptions behind MSR and proposes explaining its practical operation through “psychohistory.”
quotes.t: A sketch of acausal trade in practice

quotes.c: For a problem to be 10x less tractable than the baseline, it would have to take 10 more doublings (1000x the resources) to solve an expected 10% of the problem. Most problems that can be solved in theory are at least as tractable as this; I think with 1000x the resources, humanity could have way better than 10% chance of starting a Mars colony [3] , solving the Riemann hypothesis, and doing other really difficult things.
quotes.sum: The author argues that problems worth analyzing usually differ by only about 100–1,000 times in how hard they are to solve, not by vastly larger amounts.
quotes.t: Most problems fall within a 100x tractability range (under certain assumptions)

quotes.c: There's been some discussion of what one's chances are if one takes more career risks to maximize expected value, using Sam Bankman-Fried as an example. So I want to tackle this from a different angle, looking at my own failure to make good on the most impactful career opportunity I've had thus far, in politics rather than earning to give.
quotes.m: what one's chances are if one takes more career risks to maximize expected value
quotes.sum: The author reflects on taking high-risk career paths to maximize expected impact, contrasting politics with earning money to donate.
quotes.t: How I torched my biggest career opportunity so far

quotes.c: Coal mining and climate is a factor that determines elections in Australia. The current Prime Minister once used a lump of coal as a prop in parliament. It is widely thought that he won the last election because the Labour party was insufficiently pro-coal. I think this is the kind of thing that it would be difficult to fully compensate for with money. It would be too hard to target the money effectively at those affected, and I think many people would view it as something ‘sacred and not to be traded off’.
quotes.m: I think many people would view it as something ‘sacred and not to be traded off’.
quotes.sum: The author argues that harms tied to coal and climate politics cannot always be adequately compensated with money, because people may treat them as non-negotiable values.
quotes.t: Should we buy coal mines?

quotes.c: I think there are a lot of important and reasonable concerns about spending money too quickly and without adequate oversight. We're making decisions that directly affect how many people spend a majority of their working hours, those decisions are hard to make, and there can be community-wide consequences to making them badly. It's also possible that some of our grantees are spending more than is optimal, and our funding is contributing to that.
quotes.m: We're making decisions that directly affect how many people spend a majority of their working hours, those decisions are hard to make, and there can be community-wide consequences to making them badly.
quotes.sum: A prominent funder acknowledges that rapid grantmaking can shape recipients' careers, create community-wide harms, and encourage wasteful spending without oversight.
quotes.t: Some clarifications on the Future Fund's approach to grantmaking

quotes.c: I think the arguments also apply to other invertebrates such as shrimp and gastropods (slugs and snails) but for simplicity, I’ve kept this post focused on insects.
quotes.m: I think the arguments also apply to other invertebrates such as shrimp and gastropods (slugs and snails)
quotes.sum: The author says their case for caring about insects likely extends to shrimp, slugs, snails, and other invertebrates.
quotes.t: Why should I care about insects?

quotes.c: What subculture you belong to doesn’t mean much about how right you are about something. Subcultures / echo chambers develop different ideas from the mainstream, some which will be valuable and many which will be pointless or harmful. (LessWrong was also very into cryonics at the time, and I think it’s right for that idea to get a lot less attention than AI safety.)
quotes.m: What subculture you belong to doesn’t mean much about how right you are about something.
quotes.sum: The author reflects that her initial resistance to AI safety was partly driven by group identity, and argues that subculture membership is not evidence of being right.
quotes.t: Messy personal stuff that affected my cause prioritization (or: how I started to care about AI safety)

quotes.c: Cleaning up public spaces seems like a winner to me. The work is never-ending, and it's hard to argue that public spaces should have more garbage or decay. Even if those public spaces are maintained by public employees it seems unlikely a small group of volunteers would in some way displace them or cause bad incentives.
quotes.m: Cleaning up public spaces seems like a winner to me.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA groups doing public-space cleanup is broadly useful and unlikely to undermine public workers.
quotes.t: EA group community service projects, good or bad idea?

quotes.c: I believe some people will bite the bullet and see no problem in this scenario (“as long as the AI is *really* aligned,” they’ll say). They may have a point. But for the others... I suspect that it’s very likely that any scenario where one lets something like an unbounded optimizer scan one's brain, simulate it, while still assigning to the copies the same “special” moral weight given to oneself tends to lead to similarly unattractive outcomes.
quotes.m: any scenario where one lets something like an unbounded optimizer scan one's brain, simulate it, while still assigning to the copies the same “special” moral weight given to oneself tends to lead to similarly unattractive outcomes.
quotes.sum: The author warns that allowing an aligned superintelligence to scan and copy minds may have disturbing consequences if copies are treated as morally equivalent to the original person.
quotes.t: A tentative dialogue with a Friendly-boxed-super-AGI on brain uploads

quotes.c: Lastly, I believe that we are missing an opportunity of taking advantage of cultural differences. EA's current understanding of altruism is based on western values of freedom, individualism, and reason. I sympathize with these values, but I know that the culture works differently in many places worldwide. Altruism is sometimes related to religious or family ties and helping the community, meaning that altruism in some areas is more of a communitarian than an individualistic effort.
quotes.m: EA's current understanding of altruism is based on western values of freedom, individualism, and reason.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA reflects Western individualist values and should engage cultures where altruism is rooted in family, religion, and community.
quotes.t: If EA Wants to Gain Relevance, We Need to Expand Ourselves to other Languages

quotes.c: Sentientism about moral patienthood : if a system (human, non-human animal, AI) has the capacity to have conscious valenced experiences—if it is sentient [3] —then it is a moral patient. That is, it deserves moral concern for its own sake, and its pain/suffering and pleasure matter. This assumption is why the Big Question is morally important. [4]
quotes.m: if a system (human, non-human animal, AI) has the capacity to have conscious valenced experiences—if it is sentient [3] —then it is a moral patient.
quotes.sum: The author argues that any sentient AI deserves moral concern because its suffering and pleasure matter for their own sake.
quotes.t: Key questions about artificial sentience: an opinionated guide

quotes.c: If such a warning shot occurs, is it appropriate to infer the responses of governments from their responses to other potential x-risk warning shots, such as COVID-19 for weaponized pandemics and Hiroshima for nuclear winter?
quotes.m: If such a warning shot occurs, is it appropriate to infer the responses of governments from their responses to other potential x-risk warning shots
quotes.sum: The author asks whether governments' reactions to COVID-19 and Hiroshima can predict how they would respond to an AI catastrophe warning.
quotes.t: How will the world respond to "AI x-risk warning shots" according to reference class forecasting?

quotes.c: At the core of Effective Altruism is the idea that we should “ shut up and multiply ,” which means ignoring our intuitions in favor of cold, dispassionate calculations of what is good. Since aesthetics are a key source of intuition on moral goodness, a utilitarian may be tempted to do away with them entirely — and thereby make themselves miserable.
quotes.m: Since aesthetics are a key source of intuition on moral goodness, a utilitarian may be tempted to do away with them entirely — and thereby make themselves miserable.
quotes.sum: The author argues that utilitarian calculation can suppress moral intuitions and aesthetic values, leaving people miserable.
quotes.t: Guided by the Beauty of One’s Philosophies: Why Aesthetics Matter

quotes.c: It might be possible to formalize what it means for an agent/moral patient to be safe via membranes/boundaries . This post tells one ( just one ) story for how the membranes idea could be useful for thinking about existential risk and AI safety.
quotes.m: It might be possible to formalize what it means for an agent/moral patient to be safe via membranes/boundaries .
quotes.sum: The author suggests using formal boundaries or “membranes” to define safety for agents and moral patients in AI-risk work.
quotes.t: Agent membranes/boundaries and formalizing “safety”

quotes.c: I think there definitely is a correlation between IQ and correct beliefs about topics such as climate change and creationism, due to a better ability to assess complicated claims. But that correlation is far from 100%. According to a pew poll , 2% of American scientists are creationists, and a further 8% think evolution was “guided by a superior being”.
quotes.m: I think there definitely is a correlation between IQ and correct beliefs about topics such as climate change and creationism, due to a better ability to assess complicated claims.
quotes.sum: The author argues that intelligence correlates with more accurate beliefs, including on climate change and creationism, but does not guarantee them.
quotes.t: The Leeroy Jenkins principle: How faulty AI could guarantee "warning shots"

quotes.c: Addressing Global Poverty as a Strategy to Improve the Long-Term Future has been discussed, and improving animal welfare could also impact the long-term future via e.g. expanding the moral circle. However, I am not aware of estimates of the total impact of GiveWell and ACE top charities. I think these would be valuable:
quotes.m: improving animal welfare could also impact the long-term future via e.g. expanding the moral circle.
quotes.sum: The author says animal welfare may improve the far future by broadening who people morally care about, and calls for estimates of charity impacts.
quotes.t: Are there any uber-analyses of GiveWell/ACE top charities?

quotes.c: This ancient (and wholly Christian) tool of thought is thinking that goes like this "the most likely explanation for a thing is the one with the fewest assumptions, so to find the true reasons for things we ought to shave away as many as possible." And so the creator was cut away as unnecessary to explain the creation, and His two realms of existence were shown to be an obvious one too many. But because the ones wielding the blade were authorities of the physical realm, they sliced away the spiritual.
quotes.m: But because the ones wielding the blade were authorities of the physical realm, they sliced away the spiritual.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Occam's razor helped secular thinkers dismiss spiritual reality because they were biased toward the physical world.
quotes.t: Musings on Cargo Cult Consciousness

quotes.c: However, as a sanity check, I will do the standard economist thing: use revealed preference, and assume that people are optimizing in a well-functioning market. Yes, this assumes many inaccurate things that could introduce distortions. It will also assume that the average value of leisure is exactly the same as the last hour. But I'm fairly sure that the distortions cause people to work more than they prefer, and to prefer to work more than their coherent extrapolated volition says they should prefer to. So this should be seen as an upper bound on the experience-value of working, and a lower bound on the value of leisure.
quotes.m: I'm fairly sure that the distortions cause people to work more than they prefer, and to prefer to work more than their coherent extrapolated volition says they should prefer to.
quotes.sum: The author argues that market choices likely make people work more than they truly would prefer, so observed wages understate leisure's value.
quotes.t: Valuing Leisure Time

quotes.c: Existential risk increases as more groups become tribal and more willing to try drastic things, because they may feel the game is unfair, systematically broken, or controlled by a small few. The more people who feel like the game is rigged or unfair, the more likely some may try to flip the playing board to end the game (e.g. Russia, populism, Trump elections).
quotes.sum: The author argues that perceived economic unfairness fuels tribalism and drastic political actions, increasing existential risk.
quotes.t: Economic Pie Research as a Cause Area

quotes.c: If you’re anti-speciesist but not vegan, I hope this thought experiment gives you pause for thought. Of course you can bite the bullet and say you wouldn’t abstain from eating humans in the thought experiment, but I suspect most of you wouldn’t admit to this. If you are adamantly against eating the humans in the thought experiment, you should be similarly against eating the animals we currently farm.
quotes.m: If you are adamantly against eating the humans in the thought experiment, you should be similarly against eating the animals we currently farm.
quotes.sum: The author argues that anti-speciesists who reject eating humans should also reject eating farmed animals.
quotes.t: An uncomfortable thought experiment for anti-speciesist non-vegans

quotes.c: The reasoning "I am bad at evaluating outcomes and most decisions are not so important anyway, so I should use these reliable rules-of-thumb" is consequentialist reasoning. I often think about "utilitarian virtues," like "the ability to shut up and multiply in difficult situations" or "actually implementing the plan you designed."
quotes.m: I often think about "utilitarian virtues," like "the ability to shut up and multiply in difficult situations" or "actually implementing the plan you designed."
