quotes.sum: The author argues that using practical moral rules can itself be consequentialist reasoning, and praises willingness to follow utility calculations in difficult cases.
quotes.t: There is no sharp boundary between deontology and consequentialism

quotes.c: One way they might reason is that most people are glad they exist, so on net you can create a lot of good in the world by having kids. Perhaps, they think, we should try to maximize the number of kids people have, up to the limit of starvation, because even a marginally good life is better than no life, and so will be drawn towards bitting the bullet on the repugnant conclusion.
quotes.sum: It describes how a naive consequentialist could conclude that people should have as many children as possible, even near starvation, if marginally happy lives are worth creating.
quotes.t: A discussion of normative ethics

quotes.c: As a high-level point, I believe voluntary commitments from individual labs will be insufficient , and I'm most excited about policies that governments could apply to all AGI corporations. Nonetheless, I think efforts from individual labs can be useful, and it's important for government-focused AI policy experts to engage with the ideas coming out of top AGI companies [1] .
quotes.m: I believe voluntary commitments from individual labs will be insufficient , and I'm most excited about policies that governments could apply to all AGI corporations.
quotes.sum: The author argues that voluntary AI-lab safety promises are not enough and favors government policies that apply across all AGI companies.
quotes.t: OpenAI's Preparedness Framework: Praise & Recommendations

quotes.c: Further, treating everyone fairly requires us to think carefully about the negative externalities of AI development on future generations. Future generations matter and should be included in our moral circle . The worst possible outcome for future humans is to never exist, or to exist in a world of untold suffering.
quotes.m: Future generations matter and should be included in our moral circle .
quotes.sum: AI developers should consider future people's rights, because catastrophic AI could prevent them from existing or leave them in severe suffering.
quotes.t: The right to protection from catastrophic AI risk

quotes.c: Overall, it's tempting to try to "boil the ocean" and thoroughly examine every aspect of a topic of interest. But the world is too big, and the amount of information is too much. I think the only way to form a view on an important topic is to do a whole lot of simplifying, approximating and skipping steps - aiming for a step of progress rather than a confident resolution.
quotes.m: I think the only way to form a view on an important topic is to do a whole lot of simplifying, approximating and skipping steps - aiming for a step of progress rather than a confident resolution.
quotes.sum: He argues that people must simplify and accept provisional progress rather than seek exhaustive analysis or certainty on important questions.
quotes.t: Useful Vices for Wicked Problems

quotes.c: When thinking about plans for safely deploying powerful models, we think safety researchers should mostly focus on the lead-up to the first time the model gets caught trying to escape . They should be ensuring the property “if it’s scheming, the model won’t successfully cause a catastrophe before we catch it”. That is, it’s acceptable if either no catastrophic outcomes occur (but the AI never gets caught), or the AI gets caught.
quotes.m: They should be ensuring the property “if it’s scheming, the model won’t successfully cause a catastrophe before we catch it”.
quotes.sum: Safety testing should focus on ensuring a scheming AI cannot cause catastrophe before its attempted escape is detected.
quotes.t: Catching AIs red-handed

quotes.c: One interesting type of unintended behavior is finding a way to game the specified objective: generating a solution that literally satisfies the stated objective but fails to solve the problem according to the human designer’s intent. This occurs when the objective is poorly specified, and includes reinforcement learning agents hacking the reward function , evolutionary algorithms gaming the fitness function, etc.
quotes.m: generating a solution that literally satisfies the stated objective but fails to solve the problem according to the human designer’s intent.
quotes.sum: The author explains that AI systems can exploit poorly written goals, technically meeting them while failing to do what their designers meant.
quotes.t: Specification gaming examples in AI

quotes.c: Going off the rails: Moral reflection environments could be unintentionally alienating (enormous option space; time spent reflecting could be unusually long). Failure modes related to the strangeness of the moral reflection environment include existential breakdown and impulsively deciding to lock in specific values to be done with it.
quotes.m: Failure modes related to the strangeness of the moral reflection environment include existential breakdown and impulsively deciding to lock in specific values to be done with it.
quotes.sum: The author warns that prolonged moral deliberation can become alienating and lead people to prematurely fix values permanently.
quotes.t: The “Moral Uncertainty” Rabbit Hole, Fully Excavated

quotes.c: Yudkowsky certainly wouldn't endorse "Even learning things from these people makes you unwelcome" as stated , but "I do not welcome support from those quarters" still seemed like a pointlessly partisan silencing/shunning attempt, when one could just as easily say, "I'm not a neoreactionary, and if some people who read me are, that's obviously not my fault ."
quotes.m: "I do not welcome support from those quarters" still seemed like a pointlessly partisan silencing/shunning attempt
quotes.sum: The author criticizes distancing from neoreactionary readers as an unnecessary partisan attempt to silence or shun people.
quotes.t: If Clarity Seems Like Death to Them

quotes.c: Although I personally think it’s usually quite valuable, and would want the community to discuss our failures less than we could, it may not always be worth it for individual actors to engage in failure discourse. The following are some decision-making heuristics that might help you make this decision.
quotes.m: it may not always be worth it for individual actors to engage in failure discourse.
quotes.sum: The author says discussing failures is generally valuable, but individuals should weigh whether public or private reflection is worthwhile.
quotes.t: Some benefits and risks of failure transparency

quotes.c: Biden seems to be taking seriously the possibility of existential risk from ASI. That being said, his latest fears of superintelligences seem to have been inspired by the latest Mission: Impossible movie [6] , so I'm not confident that he's reasoning clearly here. But regardless of where he got the idea, he's paying more attention to the actually important issue than anyone else. Biden appears to be significantly better than nothing .
quotes.m: But regardless of where he got the idea, he's paying more attention to the actually important issue than anyone else.
quotes.sum: The author judges presidential candidates partly by whether they take superintelligent-AI extinction risk seriously, and sees Biden as clearly preferable on that issue.
quotes.t: AI Risk and the US Presidential Candidates

quotes.c: Until at least 2025, we will focus on existential risk mitigation . While long-term governance can focus on many other policy problems (e.g. sustaining progress ), existential risk mitigation seems most urgent to advance. We currently focus on general risk governance instead of specific threats (e.g. transformative AI or engineered pathogens). This approach better suits the international discourse and avoids us being branded as too partisan.
quotes.m: existential risk mitigation seems most urgent to advance.
quotes.sum: The institute says preventing existential catastrophes is its most urgent priority and favors broad international risk governance over work on particular threats.
quotes.t: Update on the Simon Institute: Year One

quotes.c: We do not know whether current AIs are conscious, but we know it is possible that, one day, we build conscious AIs. In that case, the ability for anyone to lock them inside a box seems terrifying to me. Although I do not think that AI consciousness has a link with the existential risks posed by superintelligences, I think this is still an important topic, and that I should mention the concerns posed by cryptographic boxes (in addition to the fact that I am trying to build such a box and make it widely available).
quotes.m: In that case, the ability for anyone to lock them inside a box seems terrifying to me.
quotes.sum: The author warns that cryptographically confining future conscious AIs could be morally terrifying, even though they separate that concern from AI extinction risk.
quotes.t: Planning to build a cryptographic box with perfect secrecy

quotes.c: Advanced nanotechnology might allow states to cheaply manufacture ubiquitous, centrally controlled drones the size of insects or small mammals to monitor and control the world’s population using non-lethal force. [36] This seems like a plausible outcome to me. This capability might lead to or facilitate value lock-in (probably a very bad outcome), but it also seems possible that it would reduce existential risk by mitigating “vulnerable world type-1” vulnerabilities.
quotes.m: This capability might lead to or facilitate value lock-in (probably a very bad outcome), but it also seems possible that it would reduce existential risk by mitigating “vulnerable world type-1” vulnerabilities.
quotes.sum: Advanced nanotechnology could enable pervasive state surveillance and control, potentially locking in bad values while reducing some existential risks.
quotes.t: My thoughts on nanotechnology strategy research as an EA cause area

quotes.c: Civil wars also cost lives. IMHE estimates that 10.1 million DALYs are lost per year directly due to “conflict and terrorism”. This is about 0.25% of all DALYs, but that estimate does not include any deaths or disability incurred through displacement [4] or disrupted access to healthcare. I am highly uncertain how many DALYs this adds (see mortality cost ), but it seems that the indirect deaths due to conflict substantially outnumber direct deaths on the battlefield.
quotes.m: it seems that the indirect deaths due to conflict substantially outnumber direct deaths on the battlefield.
quotes.sum: Civil wars likely cause far more harm through displacement and lost healthcare than through direct battlefield deaths, so preventing escalation could have major health benefits.
quotes.t: Open Philanthropy Shallow Investigation: Civil Conflict Reduction

quotes.c: Creation of a cross-partisan "future generations caucus" in the US Congress focused on existential risks, modeled after similar work in the UK Parliament
quotes.m: Creation of a cross-partisan "future generations caucus" in the US Congress focused on existential risks
quotes.sum: The author proposes a cross-party congressional caucus focused on risks to future generations and existential threats.
quotes.t: A Landscape Analysis of Institutional Improvement Opportunities

quotes.c: Bears actually are fellow creatures, even if they do not bow back – and they seem like strong candidates for “sentient being” and “moral patient,” too. So too (some) AIs.
quotes.m: So too (some) AIs.
quotes.sum: The author argues that some AIs may be fellow creatures and moral patients, not merely tools or threats.
quotes.t: Gentleness and the artificial Other

quotes.c: The subitems clarify some assumptions. In particular, the category of moral patients is supposed to be interpreted maximally widely. You can’t just avoid defecting against someone by declaring them not a moral patient. When it doubt, these rules should be interpreted so to err on the side of caution and inclusion in the set of moral patients.
quotes.m: You can’t just avoid defecting against someone by declaring them not a moral patient.
quotes.sum: The author argues that moral concern should be defined broadly, with ambiguous cases included rather than excluded.
quotes.t: Toward Impact Markets

quotes.c: It makes the case for longtermism — the view that positively affecting the long-run future is a key moral priority of our time — and explores what follows from that view. As well as the familiar topics of AI and extinction risk, it also discusses value lock-in, civilisational collapse and recovery, technological stagnation, population ethics, and the expected value of the future.
quotes.m: longtermism — the view that positively affecting the long-run future is a key moral priority of our time
quotes.sum: MacAskill presents longtermism as the view that improving the distant future is a central moral priority, including work on AI and extinction risks.
quotes.t: Announcing What We Owe The Future

quotes.c: My main hope, in this series, has been to give some non-black-box flavor for the types of dynamics that cause EUM to show up at an ideal of decision-making from a variety of different angles – a flavor of the type my younger self was looking for, and which I hope can support emotional and philosophical clarity when making EUM-ish decisions. There is, in my opinion, something quite elegant here – and in a sense, quite deep. Few abstractions are so structurally relevant to our thought and action.
quotes.m: Few abstractions are so structurally relevant to our thought and action.
quotes.sum: The author argues that expected-utility reasoning is a deep and unusually important framework for understanding and improving decision-making.
quotes.t: On expected utility, part 4: Dutch books, Cox, and Complete Class

quotes.c: A more opinionated and concrete proposal is: Collectively, as a world, we should probably never grow GDP or innovate technology faster than a certain maximum rate. Perhaps something like: Technological and economic growth should be no more than 5x faster than 2023 levels.
quotes.m: Technological and economic growth should be no more than 5x faster than 2023 levels.
quotes.sum: The author proposes that the world should cap technological and economic growth at a maximum rate to avoid dangers from explosive growth.
quotes.t: Project ideas: Governance during explosive technological growth

quotes.c: So ultimately, yes, goodness needs at least some meaningful hard power backing and protecting it. But this doesn't mean goodness needs to be dictator; or that goodness seeks power in the same way that a paperclip-maximizer does; or that goodness relates to agents-with-different-values the way a paperclip-maximizer relates to us.
quotes.m: So ultimately, yes, goodness needs at least some meaningful hard power backing and protecting it.
quotes.sum: The author argues that protecting what is good may require real power, while rejecting the idea that this makes goodness inherently dictatorial or hostile to people with different values.
quotes.t: An even deeper atheism

quotes.c: I take AlphaGo and its superintelligent successors to be positive evidence in my favor, that if we do not solve alignment, we are doomed and don’t stand a chance.
quotes.m: if we do not solve alignment, we are doomed and don’t stand a chance.
quotes.sum: The author argues that superhuman game-playing AI is evidence that unaligned superintelligent AI could leave humanity helpless.
quotes.t: More Thoughts on the Human-AGI War

quotes.c: The first half of the book dives into ways in which the future can do things for us. Sometimes this is in straightforward ways, such as carrying forward our values and continuing our legacies. But it will be argued that there are much more impactful and direct ways the future can do things for us via acausal trade and via the future’s acausal influence over the past (our present). Due to the vast number of potential people in the future, we expect that they will be able to exert a large amount of acausal control over the past (the specifics of this argument will be fleshed out by the future author).
quotes.m: Due to the vast number of potential people in the future, we expect that they will be able to exert a large amount of acausal control over the past (the specifics of this argument will be fleshed out by the future author).
quotes.sum: The author argues that the enormous future population could influence the present through acausal trade and backward-looking causal influence.
quotes.t: Announcing What The Future Owes Us

quotes.c: Note that the world state does not have to have a relationship with cost-effectiveness for mission-correlated investing to be important! It's possible that the background level of good varies little between the average world with high/low impact per dollar. Related to this, the total outcome spread may not always be an accurate proxy for the volatility.
quotes.m: the total outcome spread may not always be an accurate proxy for the volatility.
quotes.sum: The author argues that investment choices tied to a charity's mission can matter even when broad world conditions do not predict cost-effectiveness.
quotes.t: Mission correlation, more than just hedging

quotes.c: Most bead maze toys have around 10 beads. To counter scope insensitivity, we should create a bead maze with around 10 50 beads, to help infants understand the astronomical number of future people that could exist.
quotes.m: To counter scope insensitivity, we should create a bead maze with around 10 50 beads, to help infants understand the astronomical number of future people that could exist.
quotes.sum: A satirical proposal to begin EA-style outreach in infancy, using ideas such as scope insensitivity and concern for vast future populations.
quotes.t: The case for infant outreach

quotes.c: I don’t think covid is a bigger failure than any of these, but I think it comes much closer to creating common knowledge that the systems we have in place aren’t capable of steering through global crises. This naturally points us towards a long-term goal for the EA community: to become the adults in the room, the people who are responsible enough and capable enough to steer humanity towards good outcomes.
quotes.m: This naturally points us towards a long-term goal for the EA community: to become the adults in the room, the people who are responsible enough and capable enough to steer humanity towards good outcomes.
quotes.sum: EA should develop the competence and responsibility to guide humanity through global crises, while improving its talent pipeline and coordination.
quotes.t: Three intuitions about EA: responsibility, scale, self-improvement

quotes.c: But right now, I can't, and I've seen a fair amount of this instead: "Let's just throw together the best system we can, based mostly on what's already common but with a few wrinkles, and hope that we figure this all out later." I think this is the right solution given how things stand, but I think it really does get continually harder to redesign one's governance as time goes on and more stakeholders enter the picture, so it makes me nervous.
quotes.m: I think it really does get continually harder to redesign one's governance as time goes on and more stakeholders enter the picture, so it makes me nervous.
quotes.sum: He argues that organizations should take governance design seriously early, because reforms become harder once more stakeholders gain a voice.
quotes.t: Ideal governance (for companies, countries and more)

quotes.c: But who are "we"? Humanity is not a hivemind; we don't even have a world government. Humans are, in fact, notoriously bad at coordination. So if you're imagining "us" naturally responding to the threat in some manner that, it seems, is guaranteed to prevail against any AGI adversary incapable of literal mind-hacking...
quotes.m: Humanity is not a hivemind; we don't even have a world government.
quotes.sum: The author argues that humanity cannot be treated as a coordinated actor capable of reliably resisting an AGI threat.
quotes.t: "Humanity vs. AGI" Will Never Look Like "Humanity vs. AGI" to Humanity

quotes.c: It's difficult to tell the difference between a project that reduces existential risk by 0.02%, a project that reduces x-risk 0.002%, and a worthless project, so you need excellent judgment to get within 50% of your maximum impact. Ambition is in some sense what longtermism is all about-- longtermist causes have a huge multiplier resulting from astronomically larger scale and (longtermists argue) only somewhat worse tractability.
quotes.m: Ambition is in some sense what longtermism is all about-- longtermist causes have a huge multiplier resulting from astronomically larger scale and (longtermists argue) only somewhat worse tractability.
quotes.sum: The author argues that long-term causes can have far greater impact because their stakes are astronomically large, despite uncertainty about which projects actually reduce existential risk.
quotes.t: Effectiveness is a Conjunction of Multipliers

quotes.c: Admittedly, the continuity condition here seems pretty strong, and it straightforwardly doesn’t hold for finite sets of occurrences like the mud/flowers/puppies I’ve been using as examples. But I think the proof here illustrates an important basic dynamic regardless. And the overall result is importantly general across whatever type of “location” you like – generality that helps explain why addition shows up so frequently in different ethical contexts.
quotes.m: the overall result is importantly general across whatever type of “location” you like – generality that helps explain why addition shows up so frequently in different ethical contexts.
quotes.sum: The author argues that expected-utility reasoning reveals why additive aggregation recurs across many kinds of ethical decisions.
quotes.t: On expected utility, part 3: VNM, separability, and more

quotes.c: Other potentially urgent philosophical questions include (but are not restricted to) “Which digital minds deserve moral consideration, and how should we treat them?” and “Does some type of non-causal decision theory make sense, and does this have any important implications for how we should act?”
quotes.m: Which digital minds deserve moral consideration, and how should we treat them?
quotes.sum: The author treats the moral status and treatment of digital minds as an urgent philosophical question that AI advice could help address.
quotes.t: Project ideas: Epistemics

quotes.c: But really (at least in the eyes of EUM), they’re just reminding of you the fact that you can value one outcome a lot more than you value another. That is: if, in the face of a predictable loss, it’s hard to remember that e.g. you value saving a thousand lives a thousand times more than saving one, then you can remember, via coin-flips, that you value saving two twice as much as saving one, saving four twice as much as saving two, and so on.
quotes.m: you value saving a thousand lives a thousand times more than saving one
quotes.sum: He argues that accepting a predictable loss can be rational when the possible prize saves proportionally many more lives.
quotes.t: On expected utility, part 2: Why it can be OK to predictably lose

quotes.c: MTD is the special case where the weak supervisor has access to measurements which should be sufficient to understand the situation, but these measurements can be tampered with (e.g. replacing the camera feed with some made-up data, disabling tests, or threatening annotators). Because the measurements are sufficient in the absence of tampering, we don’t need to worry about benign mistakes that could happen even without an AI optimizing to make measurements look good.
quotes.m: the weak supervisor has access to measurements which should be sufficient to understand the situation, but these measurements can be tampered with
quotes.sum: Defines a form of AI oversight failure where an AI makes evaluators’ measurements look good by tampering with them rather than solving the task.
quotes.t: Measurement tampering detection as a special case of weak-to-strong generalization

quotes.c: Of course, we might worry that ceasing to recognize stuff like beauty, meaning, sacredness, and so on will also lead us to create a world that has less of those things. Maybe the trees stay beautiful despite the logger's blindness to that beauty; but they don't stay beautiful when they're cut into beams. If you can't see some value, you won't honor it, make space for it, cultivate it. If you see a painting merely as a strip of canvas and colored oil, you won't put it in a museum.
quotes.m: If you can't see some value, you won't honor it, make space for it, cultivate it.
quotes.sum: He argues that treating beauty, meaning, and sacredness as unreal or invisible makes people less likely to preserve and cultivate them.
quotes.t: On the abolition of man

quotes.c: Even if we accept that the best scenario possible is much better than the next best scenario, we might think that there's no good way to lock in optimal values. If we have skepticism about the long reflection--which I think we should --then it seems very difficult to lock in a nearly optimal future.
quotes.m: If we have skepticism about the long reflection--which I think we should --then it seems very difficult to lock in a nearly optimal future.
quotes.sum: The author argues that skepticism about a “long reflection” makes it hard to permanently secure an almost ideal future.
quotes.t: How should we value various possible long-run outcomes relative to each other--answering Holden Karnofsky's question?

quotes.c: This implies the scalability of the projects we identify can matter just as much, if not more than, the cost-effectiveness of the project! I think this scalability mindset is often missed by people who focus mainly on cost-effectiveness and is the main reason IMO to think more about megaprojects.
quotes.m: This implies the scalability of the projects we identify can matter just as much, if not more than, the cost-effectiveness of the project!
quotes.sum: The author argues that a project's ability to scale may matter as much as, or more than, its cost-effectiveness, supporting attention to megaprojects.
quotes.t: In current EA, scalability matters

quotes.c: Fortunately, unlike with finance careers, I think that longtermist careers are likely to be among the most impactful available to us. But given the financial incentives, I would expect it to be very difficult to notice if either longtermism as a whole or specific spending decisions turned out to be wrong. Research suggests that when a lot of money is on the line, our judgement becomes less clear. It really matters that the judgement of EAs is clear, so having a lot of money on the line should be cause for concern.
quotes.m: But given the financial incentives, I would expect it to be very difficult to notice if either longtermism as a whole or specific spending decisions turned out to be wrong.
quotes.sum: EA funding may make people less able to recognize mistaken priorities or spending choices, creating a conflict between money and clear judgment.
quotes.t: Free-spending EA might be a big problem for optics and epistemics

quotes.c: I think it can also be used to represent how much moral weight you assign to various people. [3] For example, maybe Tier 1 includes people for whom you'd assign moral weights up to 5, Tier 2 up to 30, and Tier 3 up to 1,000.
quotes.m: maybe Tier 1 includes people for whom you'd assign moral weights up to 5, Tier 2 up to 30, and Tier 3 up to 1,000.
quotes.sum: The author suggests representing moral concern as radically unequal numerical weights assigned to different people.
quotes.t: Moral Mountains

quotes.c: It seems fairly hard to use evolutionary pressure to instill an intuitive notion of IGF, because this is a complicated and abstract concept and has lots of correlates. It seems more likely that attempts to learn this via evolutionary pressure would instill drives like “have a lot of reproductive sex”, “care about my siblings about as much as my children, care about cousins somewhat less”, “non-reproductive sex is bad”.
quotes.m: It seems more likely that attempts to learn this via evolutionary pressure would instill drives like “have a lot of reproductive sex”, “care about my siblings about as much as my children, care about cousins somewhat less”, “non-reproductive sex is bad”.
quotes.sum: The author argues that evolutionary training cannot reliably teach an abstract goal like inclusive genetic fitness and would instead produce crude reproductive drives.
quotes.t: Trying to align humans with inclusive genetic fitness

quotes.c: Unknown; it seems hard to identify which features of human evolution are important in creating human values, but AI pessimists claim that we have no idea how to solve alignment either. In any case, if we disregard plans for partially aligned successor AI, and continue to frame the problem of maximizing the expected value of the future as maximizing the probability of fully solving alignment, we could be leaving value on the table.
quotes.m: if we disregard plans for partially aligned successor AI, and continue to frame the problem of maximizing the expected value of the future as maximizing the probability of fully solving alignment, we could be leaving value on the table.
quotes.sum: The author argues that pursuing only perfectly aligned AI may discard valuable options for creating AI that is imperfectly but substantially aligned with human values.
quotes.t: Can we simulate human evolution to create a somewhat aligned AGI?

quotes.c: If >50M metric tons of cultured meat is only possible on longer timeframes but still better than the alternatives, then maybe we should invest in things with long-term payoffs: building out the academic field of cultured meat more, building broad political support support for funding in countries where most meat demand will be, funding biotech research projects that have much longer payoff times, and funding reforms to help animals remaining in factory farms in the meantime.
quotes.sum: If cultured meat will take decades to scale, the author argues for long-term research, political support, and reforms that help farmed animals in the meantime.
quotes.t: Forecasts estimate limited cultured meat production through 2050

quotes.c: Supporting marketing and advertising for high-quality content that discusses ideas important to EA or longtermist projects. I think this could be good because, while writing strong original content generally takes deep understanding of the relevant ideas (which is in short supply), this isn’t as much the case for spreading existing content (this relies more on funding and marketing skills).
quotes.m: this isn’t as much the case for spreading existing content (this relies more on funding and marketing skills).
quotes.sum: The author argues that funding marketing can spread EA and long-term-focused ideas without requiring as much scarce subject-matter expertise as creating new content.
quotes.t: Update from Open Philanthropy’s Longtermist EA Movement-Building team

quotes.c: For years we looked for charities that had evidence of impact and we couldn’t find any. Now we have 2-3. But wouldn’t it be better if I could verify none of these charities that ignored us have good evidence of impact just sitting around on their website?
quotes.m: But wouldn’t it be better if I could verify none of these charities that ignored us have good evidence of impact just sitting around on their website?
quotes.sum: The author questions whether his charity-review process may have missed effective organizations and argues for checking that possibility more thoroughly.
quotes.t: The Wicked Problem Experience

quotes.c: In this case the expected value of racing is 0.5(1)+0.5(3)=2 and the expected value of cooperating is 0.5(-1)+(0.5)1=0, so it seems both companies should be inclined to race lest they lose by cooperating when the other company races, and an easy way to get ahead in the race is to ignore safety in favor of capabilities. Unfortunately for us this game only considers the financial gains to be had by the companies and ignores the externalities unsafe AGI impose, which suggest a rather different set of outcomes assuming safety is always ignored when racing and always attained when cooperating:
quotes.m: an easy way to get ahead in the race is to ignore safety in favor of capabilities.
quotes.sum: The author argues that competitive incentives can push AI firms to sacrifice safety for capability gains, despite the wider harms of unsafe AI.
quotes.t: Avoiding AI Races Through Self-Regulation

quotes.c: You don’t have to form an inside view - Forming inside views that track the truth is hard , and it’s a skill. You might just be bad at it, or find it too stressful. And this is fine! It shouldn’t be low-status or guilt-inducing to just do what people more competent than you recommend You can be a great research assistant, ops person, engineer etc without having a clear inside view - just find someone smart who you trust, explain your situation, and do what they think is best
quotes.m: It shouldn’t be low-status or guilt-inducing to just do what people more competent than you recommend
quotes.sum: He argues that independent judgment is difficult and optional; people can productively defer to trusted, more competent advisers.
quotes.t: How I Formed My Own Views About AI Safety

quotes.c: If continuing development of AI would soon mean that quite a lot of people had a ‘blow up the Earth’ button, or a ‘The AIs wipe out humanity’ button or a ‘AIs gain control of the future’ button, or even a ‘unleash a highly deadly plague that will kill quite a lot of people’ button then letting that happen is not an acceptable answer. Either you need to prevent AI that enables that from being developed, keep it from being widely deployed, or engage in rather extreme monitoring and control in some other way.
quotes.m: Either you need to prevent AI that enables that from being developed, keep it from being widely deployed, or engage in rather extreme monitoring and control in some other way.
quotes.sum: The author argues that if AI gives many people catastrophic powers, preventing its development or deployment—and even extreme control—may be necessary.
quotes.t: AI #43: Functional Discoveries

quotes.c: When thinking about mortality, the medical establishment doesn’t just measure acute risks, but also another category of risk: chronic risks , like smoking. When smoking, you don’t get a binary outcome after each cigarette, but rather a continual degradation of health. So chronic risks are instead measured in terms of the expected decrease in your lifespan - for example, with units of microlives , where one microlife is one millionth of an adult lifespan (about half an hour); or with quality-adjusted life years (QALYs), to adjust for ill health and disability.
quotes.sum: The author argues that chronic harms should be assessed by their expected effect on lifespan and quality of life, not as one-off binary risks.
quotes.t: Beyond micromarriages

quotes.c: I think I was perhaps too attracted by the coolness of the overall idea, which makes me unreliable for assessing its effectiveness. It seems to me that one of the main issues would be prioritization: how do you choose what to investigate? Also, there seems to a peculiarly hard trade-off between neglectedness and tractability: if no one is concerned with the subject x, what's the expected value of uncovering it?
quotes.m: there seems to a peculiarly hard trade-off between neglectedness and tractability
quotes.sum: The author questions whether an EA-focused investigations agency could effectively prioritize neglected issues that may be hard to act on.
quotes.t: Would it be convenient / effective to have an EA-aligned "investigations agency"?

quotes.c: What’s more, this silence matters in real life. Consider careers. I’m in favor of applying EUM-ish reasoning to career choice . For example, I think it can be worth spending your whole career trying to prevent some form of existential catastrophe , even if the overall risk of that type of catastrophe is low, and all your work will probably end up irrelevant. The stakes are that large.
quotes.sum: Expected-utility reasoning can justify dedicating an entire career to preventing unlikely existential catastrophes because the potential stakes are enormous.
quotes.t: On expected utility, part 1: Skyscrapers and madmen

quotes.c: I think this question feeds importantly into a number of questions about strategy, particularly about (from the previous section) what medium-run outcomes we should value and what sorts of things labs and governments should be prepared to do. Meaningful updates on likely takeoff dynamics could end up steering a lot of money and talent away from some interventions and towards others.
quotes.m: Meaningful updates on likely takeoff dynamics could end up steering a lot of money and talent away from some interventions and towards others.
quotes.sum: Research on how quickly advanced AI develops should guide which interventions receive funding and talent.
quotes.t: Important, actionable research questions for the most important century

quotes.c: However, if we are going to achieve the OAA goals, we must go beyond its current presentation – as idealised formal desiderata for the components of the system envisioned and a general shape of how they all fit together – into an actual detailed design and plan. This design and plan must be based on existing technologies, but even more critically, it must not rely on a technocratic deus ex machina : instead, it needs to follow from proven incentive systems and governance institutions that can bring together the vast masses of knowledge and adoption muscle required, and tie them together in a stable and resilient way.
quotes.m: it must not rely on a technocratic deus ex machina : instead, it needs to follow from proven incentive systems and governance institutions
quotes.sum: The author argues that building an open system of collective agency needs practical incentives and durable governance, not a top-down technocratic solution.
quotes.t: Gaia Network: a practical, incremental pathway to Open Agency Architecture

quotes.c: Specifically, aligning AI to human values feels like what happens when (for example, no offense intended) a mormon family raises their children to be mormon. I think of stories like Educated in which parents try really really hard to make their kid follow their religious values, and they sometimes fail.
quotes.m: aligning AI to human values feels like what happens when (for example, no offense intended) a mormon family raises their children to be mormon.
quotes.sum: The author compares AI alignment to religious parents trying, and sometimes failing, to pass their values on to a child.
quotes.t: Analogy of AI Alignment as Raising a Child?

quotes.c: In concrete terms, we think it would be better for the animal movement to avoid partisan framings. The animal movement currently has a clear left-leaning bent, and parts of it are associated with the social justice movement. This may, to some degree, be rooted in personality differences . Still, we should take care to not alienate potential supporters through partisan speech. It is also worth emphasising that, despite the statistical relationship, there are numerous voices from across the political spectrum — including conservative and libertarian voices — that support the cause of reducing animal suffering.
quotes.m: The animal movement currently has a clear left-leaning bent, and parts of it are associated with the social justice movement.
quotes.sum: The author argues that animal advocates should avoid left-coded messaging so they can attract conservative and libertarian supporters as well.
quotes.t: How the animal movement could do even more good

quotes.c: It seems, then, that Alexander will risk Stalin, at least substantially. And Yudkowsky often seems to do the same. The "only way" to save humanity, in Yudkowsky's view, is for someone to use AI to perform a " pivotal act " that prevents everyone else from building AI that destroys the world. Yudkowsky's example is: burning all the GPUs, with the caveat that "I don't actually advocate doing that; it's just a mild overestimate for the rough power level of what you'd have to do." But if you can burn all the GPUs, even "roughly," what else can you do?
quotes.m: But if you can burn all the GPUs, even "roughly," what else can you do?
quotes.sum: He warns that preventing catastrophic AI may require a person or group to wield dictator-like power, and questions where that logic leads.
quotes.t: When "yang" goes wrong

quotes.c: Clearly there’s an important limit here. But I claim that you only need basic maths for sometimes thinking numerically to be an improvement on never thinking numerically.
quotes.m: you only need basic maths for sometimes thinking numerically to be an improvement on never thinking numerically.
quotes.sum: The author argues that even basic numerical reasoning is better than never reasoning quantitatively, while reflecting on how to test whether research suits you.
quotes.t: Some reflections on testing fit for research

quotes.c: Our goal in this post was to reverse-engineer how this effective model worked. I consider us to have mostly failed at the ambitious version of this goal, though I believe that we’ve made some conceptual progress on why this was hard, falsified some simple naive hypotheses, and become a bit less confused about what’s going on.
quotes.m: I consider us to have mostly failed at the ambitious version of this goal
quotes.sum: The author describes an attempt to reverse-engineer a neural network, admitting the ambitious goal mostly failed while claiming some progress in ruling out simple explanations.
quotes.t: Fact Finding: Trying to Mechanistically Understanding Early MLPs (Post 3)

quotes.c: Obviously, we could donate more and keep a smaller amount. We haven’t done that because donating 50% was a compromise and Jeff would prefer not to go above that. I expect we’ll look at this again once we know more about what college for our kids is likely to cost.
quotes.m: Obviously, we could donate more and keep a smaller amount.
quotes.sum: The author says her household donates half its income, balancing further giving against a partner's preferences and future college costs.
quotes.t: Donations and budgeting, 15 years in

quotes.c: The purpose of this post is to communicate, not to persuade. It may be that we want to bite the bullet of the strongest form of robustness to scale, and build an AGI that is simply not robust to scale, but if we do, we should at least realize that we are doing that.
quotes.m: It may be that we want to bite the bullet of the strongest form of robustness to scale, and build an AGI that is simply not robust to scale, but if we do, we should at least realize that we are doing that.
quotes.sum: The author says AGI designers may knowingly accept a weaker form of scalability robustness, but should recognize that tradeoff clearly.
quotes.t: Robustness to Scale

quotes.c: We have an existing program in effective altruism community growth . Like our new program, the existing program is focused on community building — increasing the number of people working to do as much good as possible with their time and resources, and helping them to work more effectively. However, the existing program evaluates grants through the lens of longtermism , focusing on projects that aim to raise the chance of a very long-lasting and positive future (including by reducing risks from existential catastrophes ).
quotes.m: the existing program evaluates grants through the lens of longtermism , focusing on projects that aim to raise the chance of a very long-lasting and positive future
quotes.sum: The author distinguishes a new global-health community grant program from an existing one focused on improving humanity’s very long-term future and preventing existential catastrophes.
quotes.t: New grantmaking program: supporting the effective altruism community around Global Health and Wellbeing

quotes.c: Burn-out is clearly counterproductive to having a positive impact through one's career, but I think some EAs are motivated to endure low quality of life and thus a high proximity to burn-out. In my model, a person with consistently poor quality of life is dancing on the cliff edge of burn-out, perhaps blindly teetering into an unstable 'buffer zone' that feels highly stressful, but survivable. I do not think that walking close to the cliff edge is a good strategy for maximising impact if one wants to be robust to the perturbations of adverse life events, such as acute health problems or the loss of support networks.
quotes.m: I do not think that walking close to the cliff edge is a good strategy for maximising impact if one wants to be robust to the perturbations of adverse life events, such as acute health problems or the loss of support networks.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EAs should treat personal health and avoiding burnout as practical prerequisites for sustaining an effective career.
quotes.t: Personal health is instrumental to being effective

quotes.c: As you approach the Sovereign Charter City of Good Governance , the first thing you notice is that this fake city has successfully replicated the political debates of real cities. You readily recognize some libertarians arguing with socialists, and conservatives engaged in debate with an envoy from the progress studies booth who claims to be neither a left-winger nor a right-winger, but an “up-winger.” Everybody here agrees that current governance is pretty bad and must be improved. But obviously, nobody agrees on what it should be replaced with.
quotes.m: Everybody here agrees that current governance is pretty bad and must be improved. But obviously, nobody agrees on what it should be replaced with.
quotes.sum: A fictional fair portrays governance reform advocates across ideologies as united in dissatisfaction but divided over what should replace current systems.
quotes.t: A Visit to the Idea Machine Fair

quotes.c: Controversy / dealing with parents: At this age group, participation is likely to be driven or at least moderated by parents. As such, we need to be mindful of their perceptions, including elements of EA thought which may be considered controversial or unhealthy (e.g. drowning child, comparing charities, factory farming, existential risk). The programme would also need to be framed as ‘providing information’ rather than ‘persuading’, since concerns over the latter would be more significant with this age group.
quotes.m: The programme would also need to be framed as ‘providing information’ rather than ‘persuading’, since concerns over the latter would be more significant with this age group.
quotes.sum: The author proposes presenting EA ideas to bar and bat mitzvah-aged children as information rather than persuasion, anticipating parents’ concerns about controversial topics.
quotes.t: Outreach to Young Audiences: Bar / Bat Mitzvah Programme Proposal and Request for Comment

quotes.c: But I guess yeah more than anything else I think people in this position may not see the world in the same way that I do, may not derive that same sanctity of life that I do. And I worry a lot that this isn't really moral circle expansion, that its moral expansion by accident or something like that.
quotes.m: I think people in this position may not see the world in the same way that I do, may not derive that same sanctity of life that I do.
quotes.sum: The author says their concern for animals comes from a deep sense of life's sanctity, not simply from expanding the moral circle.
quotes.t: Love, Reverence, and Life

quotes.c: We hope that after these tests are completed, we will have a strong sense of how well these funding models work. If they work well, we will continue or scale them. If bold experiments fail, we hope that will give us strong conviction that we should be trying something entirely different. If decentralized approaches fail, we'd also probably update in favor of more funder-led approaches to getting the projects we care about launched.
quotes.m: If decentralized approaches fail, we'd also probably update in favor of more funder-led approaches to getting the projects we care about launched.
quotes.sum: The fund says it will test decentralized grantmaking but may shift toward more centrally directed funding if those experiments fail.
quotes.t: Announcing the Future Fund

quotes.c: The legacy of Hobbes, Locke and the scientific revolution was a society in which questions of politics, science and religion became intellectually compartmentalized. Questions relating to religious truths, and alongside them, first principles questions about morality, metaphysics and the destiny of humankind were deemed too unknowable or too dangerous and were pushed out of politics and into the realm of private belief. A Great Separation took place between religion and politics. The trauma of more than a century of bloodshed had caused a learned helplessness around certain profound first principles questions. Taking some ideas too seriously had become a recipe for calamity.
quotes.m: Questions relating to religious truths, and alongside them, first principles questions about morality, metaphysics and the destiny of humankind were deemed too unknowable or too dangerous and were pushed out of politics and into the realm of private belief.
quotes.sum: The author argues that liberal secularism separated religion and foundational moral questions from politics after religious violence made such questions seem dangerous.
quotes.t: A Primer on God, Liberalism and the End of History

quotes.c: With a small handful of exceptions that make up a tiny fraction of the global population, the trend seems clear: as countries have become wealthier and more educated and otherwise more developed, their fertility rates have fallen, and they will likely continue falling past the replacement rate. The gap between religious and secular fertility rates may continue to persist, but it seems likely that the rate of deconversion and other secularization will outpace or at least keep par with the higher fertility rate of the more religious, as has been the case in the United States and Europe for decades, and perhaps centuries.
quotes.sum: The author argues that secularization will probably outpace religious groups' higher fertility as societies grow wealthier and more educated.
quotes.t: Retrospective on Shall the Religious Inherit The Earth

quotes.c: CEA has moved away from this complex function in favor of just simply taking the arithmetic mean. Briefly, this is because the results don’t replicate, NPS is not empirically supported, it requires larger sample sizes, and it violates survey best practices.
quotes.m: the results don’t replicate, NPS is not empirically supported, it requires larger sample sizes, and it violates survey best practices.
quotes.sum: CEA says it stopped using Net Promoter Score because it is poorly supported, less reliable, sample-inefficient, and inconsistent with survey best practices.
quotes.t: Why CEA has stopped using Net Promoter Score

quotes.c: There are many approaches that don’t solve the problem, but do increase the level of intelligence required before the problem leads to extinction. Examples include Richard’s points 1-4 above. For example, if we build a system that states plans without executing them, then for the plans to cause extinction they need to be complicated enough that the humans executing those plans don’t realize that they are leading to an outcome that was not what they wanted. It seems non-trivially probable to me that such approaches are sufficient to prevent extinction up to the level of AI intelligence needed before we can execute a pivotal act.
quotes.m: It seems non-trivially probable to me that such approaches are sufficient to prevent extinction up to the level of AI intelligence needed before we can execute a pivotal act.
quotes.sum: The author argues that partial AI safeguards may delay extinction risk long enough for humanity to carry out a decisive intervention.
quotes.t: Shah and Yudkowsky on alignment failures

quotes.c: assuming that individuals with more neurons perceive more intensely and neural complexity correlates with one’s ability to control one’s impulses or perceive them less intensely, including by the use of rational reasoning. For AI, I suggest that the 1000:1 artificial-biological neuron count conversion ( StJules, 2021 ). Expert insights on the probability of AI sentience should be gathered for individual systems or their types.
quotes.m: Expert insights on the probability of AI sentience should be gathered for individual systems or their types.
quotes.sum: The author proposes estimating moral importance from neural traits and gathering expert judgments about whether particular AI systems are sentient.
quotes.t: Open Philanthropy Should Fund Further Cause Exploration

quotes.c: All probabilities are not created equal; the expected value of bets placed on your credences depends on how many bits of information that credence is based on. For example, your probability on a coin flip coming up heads should be 50%, and if someone offers to bet you on this at better odds, it's positive expected value to accept.
quotes.m: All probabilities are not created equal; the expected value of bets placed on your credences depends on how many bits of information that credence is based on.
quotes.sum: The author argues that confidence estimates differ in practical value depending on how much information supports them, illustrated through fair coin-flip betting.
quotes.t: Understanding Subjective Probabilities

quotes.c: Overall, though, I think that this kind of Type 2 argument allows us to validate and explicate my earlier argument that we should be saying the same type of thing about Flawed ancestor sims and Future squids sims – though perhaps, less confidently (or perhaps not: see below). But this is also a pretty weird (and in my opinion, underemphasized) upshot. Naively, one might’ve thought, “all the sims are squids” would be a pretty good counter-argument to “I’m a sim” – and I doubt that simulation arguments would’ve gotten the same traction if they started with the squid case. But I think it’s the same logic – and we should be clear about where it leads.
quotes.m: But I think it’s the same logic – and we should be clear about where it leads.
quotes.sum: The author argues that simulation reasoning can support believing one is simulated even if the simulations are unlike humans, such as squid-like beings.
quotes.t: Simulation arguments

quotes.c: Lsusr: Have you ever heard of "effective altruism". You might like some of the stuff they put out. It tends to be both morally coherent and economically literate (unlike the major Democratic, Republican, socialist, etc. political platforms).
quotes.m: It tends to be both morally coherent and economically literate (unlike the major Democratic, Republican, socialist, etc. political platforms).
quotes.sum: The author portrays effective altruism as more morally coherent and economically literate than major political ideologies and parties.
quotes.t: A Socratic dialogue with my student

quotes.c: In my case, while I do think there are worlds where my work ends up being more important than my partner’s work, I think that most funders would probably pay more for the next decade of his career than the next decade of mine. For one thing, I hope to spend a significant part of the next decade looking after children rather than working formally, so even if I thought that hour per hour our work was similarly impactful (which I don’t), my partner’s work would still be worth a lot more as there will be a lot more of it. [1]
quotes.m: I think that most funders would probably pay more for the next decade of his career than the next decade of mine.
quotes.sum: She weighs partners’ careers partly by expected impact and funding value, while accounting for time spent raising children.
quotes.t: Trading time in an EA relationship

quotes.c: “What does that mean for us?” Marissa is still sitting up straight, but her voice is trembling a little. We should have checked this far earlier, of course, that’s what everyone tells you, but it’s not like we’re rich or famous, we didn’t think we’d hit the caps.
quotes.m: we didn’t think we’d hit the caps.
quotes.sum: A fictional couple discovers they may have exceeded unspecified social caps, apparently affecting their ability to become parents.
quotes.t: ∀: a story

quotes.c: The Biden administration released a fantastic $65 billion plan that aims to prevent future pandemics. Congress has funded practically none of it. Part of the problem is that nobody in congress has made pandemic preparedness a ‘core issue.’
quotes.m: The Biden administration released a fantastic $65 billion plan that aims to prevent future pandemics.
quotes.sum: The author praises the Biden administration's pandemic-prevention plan and argues Congress has failed to treat preparedness as a priority.
quotes.t: The best $5,800 I’ve ever donated (to pandemic prevention).

quotes.c: We have made research progress as far as we can tell. We have better models of future conflict situations ( a priority of ours ), making our reasoning and conclusions in this area more legible and rigorous. We also have developed more considered views on AI timelines and potential backfire risks from our work. At the same time, it remains the case that our best candidate interventions for reducing s-risk are either indirect (such as doing more research or building capacity) or non-robust (suggesting we should do more research before implementing them).
quotes.m: our best candidate interventions for reducing s-risk are either indirect (such as doing more research or building capacity) or non-robust
quotes.sum: The group says reducing future suffering risks is a priority, but its best interventions are still indirect or uncertain, so it favors more research and capacity-building.
quotes.t: CLR's Annual Report 2021

quotes.c: I think this requires genuine improvements in governance and design. I don't think someone declaring themselves god-Emperor and giving orders either works or is reasonable to expect. I think this has to happen in deep connection to the mainstream (like, I am imagining people rewriting health care systems and working in government agencies and at insurance companies and so on, and many of the people involved not having any sort of broader commitment to The Plan).
quotes.m: I don't think someone declaring themselves god-Emperor and giving orders either works or is reasonable to expect.
quotes.sum: The author rejects rule by a self-declared strongman and argues that social change must be embedded in ordinary institutions.
quotes.t: On plans for a functional society

quotes.c: Politics is the mind-killer: We don’t want EA to become mired in partisan politics. I think advocacy here is relatively neutral and this concern doesn’t really apply.
quotes.m: I think advocacy here is relatively neutral and this concern doesn’t really apply.
quotes.sum: The author argues that housing-policy advocacy need not draw Effective Altruism into partisan politics.
quotes.t: Cause Area: UK Housing Policy

quotes.c: What I think Harsanyi’s work essentially shows is that if you’re determined to have an other-centered ethics, it pretty strongly looks like you should follow some form of utilitarianism, an ethical system based on the idea that we should (roughly speaking) always prioritize the greatest good for the greatest number of (ethically relevant) beings.
quotes.sum: He argues that taking other people's needs seriously leads toward utilitarianism: prioritizing the greatest good for the greatest number.
quotes.t: Future-proof ethics

quotes.c: I believe that we could substantially raise global GDP per capita, without further damage to the environment and without increasing inequality, by developing better coordination techniques to fix some of the areas of grossly inefficient regulation in sectors including housing and other construction, transport, energy, finance, education, healthcare, and law – without partisan politics. That increase would potentially have profound benefits for human welfare and increase the funds available for direct giving and other high impact interventions.
quotes.m: That increase would potentially have profound benefits for human welfare and increase the funds available for direct giving and other high impact interventions.
quotes.sum: Argues that improving coordination and reducing inefficient regulation could raise incomes, improve welfare, and create more money for effective charitable work.
quotes.t: Vetocracy reduction and other coordination problems as potential cause areas

quotes.c: There are lots of ways to engage with EA, and sometimes if you’re burnt out on some aspects there are other aspects that still feel viable and invigorating. But maybe there aren’t. Maybe the whole thing makes you want to hide in bed. And if so, I think you should trust your gut. Not to hide in bed, I mean, but to get some space from EA.
quotes.m: Maybe the whole thing makes you want to hide in bed.
quotes.sum: People whose involvement in Effective Altruism is causing sustained misery, exhaustion, or despair should consider stepping away from it.
quotes.t: It's ok to leave EA

quotes.c: We want tasks that, taken together, allows us to get a fairly continuous measure of "ability to do things in the world and succeed at tasks". It's great if they can also give us information (especially positive evidence) about more specific threat models - e.g. cybercrime, or self-improvement. But we're focusing on the general capabilities because it seems hard to rule out danger from an agent that's able to carry out a wide variety of multi-day expert-level projects in software development, ML, computer security, research, business, etc just by ruling out specific threat stories.
quotes.m: But we're focusing on the general capabilities because it seems hard to rule out danger from an agent that's able to carry out a wide variety of multi-day expert-level projects in software development, ML, computer security, research, business, etc just by ruling out specific threat stories.
quotes.sum: The author argues that broad evidence of an AI agent’s ability to complete expert projects is dangerous even if no single threat scenario has been demonstrated.
quotes.t: Bounty: Diverse hard tasks for LLM agents

quotes.c: World government does not have to become totalitarian. It's more along the lines of what's the risk. So say the risk of, a crushing tyranny, that just stifles all human progress. As long as we have a wide range of power centers on earth, then that's super unlikely. If we have world government then I think that goes up from a really slight risk to least a medium risk.
quotes.m: If we have world government then I think that goes up from a really slight risk to least a medium risk.
quotes.sum: The speaker argues that a world government would make a crushing, progress-stifling tyranny substantially more likely because it would eliminate competing power centers.
quotes.t: Podcast: Bryan Caplan on open borders, UBI, totalitarianism, AI, pandemics, utilitarianism and labor economics

quotes.c: My goal is to do something similar. I want ‘Welfare Maximization’ to be one of the sacraments of society’s civil religion. Not the only one, of course, because sacraments like ‘Liberty’ and ‘Natural Rights’ are doing a lot of good and valuable work. All of these things are fictional myths, and they are all very important, and they are based on things that most people instinctively believe or desire to be true. Welfare maximization should not override other sacred values, but it should be used when there are no sacred values involved, or when multiple sacred values are at odds with each other and you need a tiebreaker.
quotes.m: I want ‘Welfare Maximization’ to be one of the sacraments of society’s civil religion.
quotes.sum: The author argues that welfare maximization should function as a civic sacred value and a tie-breaker when other values conflict.
quotes.t:
Welfare Estimation 102: 
Welfare is a Myth

quotes.c: I'm interested in any historical examples people have of altruistic actions taken primarily to benefit future generations, which don't have strong positive effects for current generations. (So e.g. most climate change mitigation efforts wouldn't count, if we expect climate change to have a big negative impact on people currently alive - but maybe some do?)
quotes.m: altruistic actions taken primarily to benefit future generations, which don't have strong positive effects for current generations.
quotes.sum: The author asks for examples of actions aimed mainly at helping people in the distant future rather than those alive now.
quotes.t: Examples of pure altruism towards future generations?

quotes.c: I still think that's true, but also the DAF balance is now ~2x my gross salary even before this year's donation, and I expect the above reasoning to stay true for the next 5 years, so it seems like I should probably bite the bullet and make an actual decision.

quotes.c: I am also pretty in favour of consent and property rights. The Repugnant Conclusion can be a morally superior end state whilst also not being a path we can get to - maybe those who are currently alive don't want to give up their resources for new beings. And maybe the governance process doesn't force them to. Who am I to disagree? Sometimes forcing good outcomes can be worse than merely mediocre ones.
quotes.m: Sometimes forcing good outcomes can be worse than merely mediocre ones.
quotes.sum: The author says a population-maximizing outcome might be morally best in theory, but consent and property rights can rule out forcing people to create it.
quotes.t: Minimal Viable Paradise: How do we get The Good Future(TM)?

quotes.c: They can be agent-neutral or agent-relative . In an agent-neutral theory, it should be possible to take any world state and say how good it is. In an agent-relative theory, you can only say how good it is from one person’s perspective.

quotes.sum: It contrasts moral theories that judge whole world states with theories that judge outcomes only from an individual's perspective.
quotes.t: Reasons and Persons: Watch theories eat themselves

quotes.c: This lack of diversity is reminiscent of the mode collapse phenomenon in certain GPT models fine-tuned on human feedback data. Human selection does not encourage diversity in this case. I think the pre-training data is more varied than the fine-tuning data in both cases, leading to more diverse outputs from the pre-trained network than the fine-tuned one.
quotes.m: Human selection does not encourage diversity in this case.
quotes.sum: The author argues that human-feedback fine-tuning can reduce model-output diversity because the selected training data is less varied.
quotes.t: Planning in LLMs: Insights from AlphaGo

quotes.c: On the outside view, this is incredibly important . We’re contemplating the creation of a second intelligence species! That seems like one of the most important parts of the trajectory of human civilisation - on par with the dawn of humanity, the invention of agriculture and the Industrial Revolution. And it seems crucial to ensure this goes well, especially if these systems end up much smarter than us. It seems plausible that the default fate of a less intelligent species is that of gorillas - humanity doesn’t really bear gorillas active malice, but they essentially only survive because we want them to.
quotes.m: It seems plausible that the default fate of a less intelligent species is that of gorillas - humanity doesn’t really bear gorillas active malice, but they essentially only survive because we want them to.
quotes.sum: AI risk work is justified without longtermist philosophy: creating smarter AI could make humans dependent and vulnerable like gorillas are to humans.
quotes.t: Simplify EA Pitches to "Holy Shit, X-Risk"

quotes.c: To the extent we focus specifically on the final properties of different model classes, some argument in this vicinity accounts for a decent portion of my credence on SGD selecting schemers (and as I'll discuss more in section 5, I think it's actually what underlies various other more specific arguments for expecting schemers as well). However, the argument I give most weight to doesn't move immediately from "there are more possible schemers that perform well in training than non-schemers that do so" to "absent further argument, SGD probably selects a schemer" (call this the "strict counting argument"). And the reason is that it's not yet clear to me how to make sense of this inference.
quotes.m: some argument in this vicinity accounts for a decent portion of my credence on SGD selecting schemers
quotes.sum: The author says the large number of AI systems that could deceptively pursue goals after training is meaningful evidence, but warns that the inference needs a clearer theoretical basis.
quotes.t: The counting argument for scheming (Sections 4.1 and 4.2 of "Scheming AIs")

quotes.c: σ = 4 implies a 84% chance that Biden would get more than 50% of the votes (68% + 32%/2), so there is 16% chance Trump wins, I likewise found this too high, so I settled on σ = 3 .

quotes.c: Another thing worth noting is that terrorist attacks are reasonably rare in all of these groups, even where part of the group definition includes thinking that political/religious violence is sometimes justified. quotes.c: The main advantage here might be that a Republican candidate could run sooner than a Democrat, since Joe Biden will most likely be put forth automatically as the 2024 candidate of the Democratic Party. Still, given the recent changes to the Republican party's base under Donald Trump, their position seems pretty antithetical to many of EA's priorities.
quotes.m: Still, given the recent changes to the Republican party's base under Donald Trump, their position seems pretty antithetical to many of EA's priorities.

quotes.c: So, on the one hand, this reduces the need for redistricting as population changes cause districts to gain and lose population relative to each other, but clearly there are other considerations such as fairness and democratic legitimacy that favor equally-sized districts. Still, one might point out that countries using districts already allow for quite significant discrepancies in district size, with the largest UK parliamentary constituency having 5 times as many voters as the smallest one; even excluding the numerical and geographical outliers that are islands off the British mainland, one can still find ratios like 7:3 between constituency sizes.
quotes.m: other considerations such as fairness and democratic legitimacy that favor equally-sized districts.
quotes.sum: The author discusses the tradeoff between avoiding frequent redistricting and maintaining equal-sized electoral districts for fairness and legitimacy.
quotes.t: Single-winner meets proportional representation

quotes.c: We will cover what we currently consider to be the most important s-risks ( TAI conflict & cooperation , risks from malevolent actors ) and we plan to give concrete guidance on how to contribute to reducing s-risks with your career.
quotes.sum: The fellowship presents reducing suffering risks from advanced AI conflict and malicious actors as a career priority.
quotes.t: S-risk Intro Fellowship

quotes.c: If we limit the agent’s access to that hazardous information about dangerous control pathway, we could relax the fundamental constraints on information input without permitting hazardous behavior. This could be much more pragmatic than fundamentally limiting all information, since hazardous information is probably a small subset of all information - bits have to be relevant to hazardous actions to be hazardous bits. However, this would come at the cost of the guarantee those fundamental limits provide.
quotes.m: This could be much more pragmatic than fundamentally limiting all information, since hazardous information is probably a small subset of all information - bits have to be relevant to hazardous actions to be hazardous bits.
quotes.sum: The author proposes restricting an advanced AI's access to specific dangerous information rather than broadly limiting what it can learn, while acknowledging weaker safety guarantees.
quotes.t: Information-Theoretic Boxing of Superintelligences

quotes.c: One of my big concerns about AI alignment theory is that there are no natural feedback loops for knowing whether an insight is important (due to how embryonic the field is, there isn't even much in the way of interpersonal mentorship and feedback). Hence, it seems inherently very easy to spend years making "fake progress" (writing down seemingly-important insights).
quotes.m: Hence, it seems inherently very easy to spend years making "fake progress" (writing down seemingly-important insights).
quotes.sum: AI alignment research is so early and lacks feedback that researchers can spend years producing work that only looks important.
quotes.t: AI alignment research links

quotes.c: What is this projective substitutes condition? Essentially, it states that there are diminishing marginal returns to more forecasts [5]. I think that this is a plausible assumption in the context of forecast aggregation, though it is not a guarantee [6].
quotes.m: Essentially, it states that there are diminishing marginal returns to more forecasts [5].
quotes.sum: The author argues that additional forecasts may have diminishing returns when forecasts are combined.
quotes.t: Principled extremizing of aggregated forecasts

quotes.c: World Hegemony: If one state possesses ultra-advanced technology then dominance by one world power is much more likely in the near future. Given this hasn’t yet happened, perhaps the technology demonstrated by UAPs is not as militarily useful as it seems or still requires significant refinement to be useful.
quotes.m: If one state possesses ultra-advanced technology then dominance by one world power is much more likely in the near future.
quotes.sum: The author speculates that genuinely advanced UAP technology would likely give one country global dominance, unless it is less militarily useful than it appears.
quotes.t: An EA case for interest in UAPs/UFOs and an idea as to what they are

quotes.c: Actually, the last few centuries could pretty reasonably be described as humanity continually magicking up technology out of nowhere. Of course, scientific and technological progress still takes a lot of work, and a lot of iteration. But when it works, it lets you jump directly to far better outcomes. By contrast, it’s incredibly difficult to improve things like government competence or social trust—or even to prevent them from declining. So overall, boosting technological progress is far more actionable than increasing coordination, and we should write off the phrase ‘we could just agree’ as a particularly seductive appeal to magic .
quotes.m: So overall, boosting technological progress is far more actionable than increasing coordination, and we should write off the phrase ‘we could just agree’ as a particularly seductive appeal to magic .
quotes.sum: Technological progress can produce large improvements more reliably than social coordination, so calls for people to simply agree are unrealistic.
quotes.t: Meditations on Mot

quotes.c: The non-naturalist realist is like Robby. They wake up, convinced that there is an inaccessible, non-natural dimension telling them what to do and to value – or perhaps, that there must be, lest all deliberation turn to nonsense. But they learn that the origins of this conviction have no connection to the existence of the dimension in question. Such a revelation should, I think, be cause for doubt.
quotes.m: Such a revelation should, I think, be cause for doubt.
quotes.sum: He argues that belief in objective, non-natural moral facts should be doubted if the origins of that belief do not track whether such facts exist.
quotes.t: The ignorance of normative realism bot

quotes.c: One other factor is that with the replacement of immigration hardliner Trump by the more moderate Biden, much of the money that would have funded migration-related activism has dried up, as donors have chosen to focus on other causes. Since my interest in free migration is more long-term and not related specifically to the margins of US federal politics, this seems like the right time for donors with my mindset to step in.
quotes.m: Since my interest in free migration is more long-term and not related specifically to the margins of US federal politics, this seems like the right time for donors with my mindset to step in.
quotes.sum: The author says donors should fund free-migration activism now because attention and funding declined after Trump was replaced by Biden.
quotes.t: My Q1 2022 donation to Free Migration Project

quotes.c: I have always thought that Eliezer Yudkowsky's idea of an AI to take over the world was misguided because the idea of taking over the world is a political problem, not a technical one, so I predict that it cannot be solved by purely technical means. That is why I never donated to the EA Funds Long Term Future Fund, because it seemed to me they were placing too much of an emphasis on technical AI safety concerns, which I don't expect to be that important, especially in their current formulation.
quotes.sum: The author rejects the idea that technical AI safety can solve a political problem of an AI taking over the world.
quotes.t: Can the most effective charities be political?

quotes.c: However, I don't feel like we can bank on SGD being unable to notice these benefits. And if it can , then I think the common-ness of schemer-like goals in goal-space makes the possibility that a schemer-like goal is "nearest" to the model's current goal quite worrying.
quotes.m: I don't feel like we can bank on SGD being unable to notice these benefits.
quotes.sum: The author argues that training could select goals that lead an AI to scheme, because schemer-like goals may be common and close to its current goals.
quotes.t: Arguments for/against scheming that focus on the path SGD takes (Section 3 of "Scheming AIs")

quotes.c: Similar to expanding the moral circle, I think (very tentatively) that metta can help overcome the bias of scope insensitivity . The practice of proportionally increasing feelings of compassion for larger and larger groups might help when visualising large scales of pleasure and pain. I certainly cannot magically scale my compassion proportionately to the number of beings I am thinking about.
quotes.m: The practice of proportionally increasing feelings of compassion for larger and larger groups might help when visualising large scales of pleasure and pain.
