quotes.m: It might exacerbate “race dynamics” between the US and China or the presence of a third “safety-conscious” stakeholder might actually slow down race dynamics.
quotes.sum: Europe's AI expansion could shift US-China competition, talent flows, development speed, and which actors gain an advantage.
quotes.t: How Europe might matter for AI  governance

quotes.c: In my view, this definition would be too broad. I think the distinctive idea that we should be trying to capture is the idea of trying to promote good long-term outcomes. I see the term 'longtermism' creating value if it results in more people taking action to help ensure that the long-run future goes well.
quotes.m: I see the term 'longtermism' creating value if it results in more people taking action to help ensure that the long-run future goes well.
quotes.sum: MacAskill argues that longtermism should mean taking action to improve outcomes in the distant future.
quotes.t: 'Longtermism'

quotes.c: I’m a little hesitant to publish this because I don’t think most people should prioritize frugality. I also agree that there are many legitimate ways in which spending money can make you more productive, and that we should take advantage of those. And I don’t think we should shame people for spending money on themselves, nor should we expect people to ignore their own happiness.
quotes.m: I don’t think we should shame people for spending money on themselves, nor should we expect people to ignore their own happiness.
quotes.sum: The author cautions against treating frugality as a universal priority or shaming people for spending on their own happiness.
quotes.t: Ways Frugality Increases Productivity

quotes.c: The core of Singer’s argument is the principle that, if it is in our power to prevent something very bad from happening, without thereby sacrificing anything morally significant, we ought, morally, to do so. We can. So we should.
quotes.m: We can. So we should.
quotes.sum: MacAskill endorses the view that people must prevent serious suffering when they can do so at no morally significant cost.
quotes.t: Aid Scepticism and Effective Altruism

quotes.c: I'm wary of focusing too much on credit assignment, but it seems important to be able to answer a question like "if EA hadn't ever formed, to what extent would it have been harder for an impartial observer in 2019 to evaluate whether working on AI safety is important?" The clearest evidence would be if there were much relevant work produced by people who were employed at EA orgs, funded by EA grants, or convinced to work on AI safety through their involvement with EA.
quotes.m: if EA hadn't ever formed, to what extent would it have been harder for an impartial observer in 2019 to evaluate whether working on AI safety is important?
quotes.sum: The author asks how much EA has materially improved the case for treating AI safety as an important cause, rather than merely claiming credit for work.
quotes.t: How much EA analysis of AI safety as a cause area exists?

quotes.c: Using information from the corporate commitment tracker (unpublished) and EggTrack’s report, we should see ~9% (8.67%) difference in the fraction of cage-free eggs between 2005 and 2018. So we could say that, at best, 9% of the egg market share could be explained by commitments made by companies.
quotes.m: So we could say that, at best, 9% of the egg market share could be explained by commitments made by companies.
quotes.sum: The author estimates that corporate cage-free commitments may explain at most 9% of the egg market’s shift toward cage-free production.
quotes.t: Did corporate campaigns in the US have any counterfactual impact? A quantitative model

quotes.c: There are, conservatively, 10 quintillion arthropods, give or take an order of magnitude. Say you only have a 1% credence that arthropods have morally relevant experiences. That knocks you down to 100 quadrillion expected arthropods. Say you think moral weight is determined by neuron count. Take a conservative average neuron count for arthropods (100,000) and use 100 million (putting you roughly in the range of rodents) as an example of a morally valuable vertebrate. That means, even with 1% credence and adjusting downward for moral weight, arthropods are worth roughly 100 trillion morally valuable vertebrates.
quotes.m: That means, even with 1% credence and adjusting downward for moral weight, arthropods are worth roughly 100 trillion morally valuable vertebrates.
quotes.sum: Even a small chance that arthropods can suffer makes their enormous numbers morally outweigh vast numbers of vertebrates.
quotes.t: Invertebrate Welfare Cause Profile

quotes.c: ML systems are trained by gradient descent to optimize a measurable objective. In the best case (i.e. ignoring misaligned learned optimization ) they behave like an expert incentivized to optimize that objective. Designing an objective that incentivizes experts to reveal what they know seems like a critical step in AI alignment.
quotes.m: Designing an objective that incentivizes experts to reveal what they know seems like a critical step in AI alignment.
quotes.sum: AI alignment should focus on designing objectives that make powerful systems honestly reveal what they know.
quotes.t: Ought: why it matters and ways to help

quotes.c: TRUTH TEAMS Deontological Level 1: “Is it true?” Level 3: "Do I support the associated team?" Consequentialist Level 2: "How does it influence others' beliefs?" Level 4: "How does it influence others' support for various teams?" Statements you make are categorized as Level 1, 2, 3, or 4 depending on which of the above questions were most responsible for your choice to make the statement.
quotes.sum: The author classifies speech by whether it aims at truth, shaping beliefs, expressing team loyalty, or building support for teams.
quotes.t: My version of Simulacra Levels

quotes.c: Georgia: Something like destabilizing to the global order and not-having-nuclear-wars, increases risk to people, makes the world more dangerous. With "aggressive" I was responding to to your "aggressors" but may have misunderstood what you meant by that.
quotes.m: Something like destabilizing to the global order and not-having-nuclear-wars, increases risk to people, makes the world more dangerous.
quotes.sum: The author says aggression that destabilizes global order or risks nuclear war makes the world more dangerous.
quotes.t: Should Effective Altruism be at war with North Korea?

quotes.c: The issue of AI alignment today is less about making the AIs care about fun, and more about making them perform some minimal pivotal act that ends the acute risk period, and buys us time to figure out how to make the superintelligent friends.
quotes.sum: The author says near-term AI alignment should aim for an AI action that ends an acute danger period and creates time to solve broader alignment.
quotes.t: Would we even want AI to solve all our problems?

quotes.c: More generally, if Americans look to the future and expect little improvement (which they largely seem to already ), they will be unhappy about the current state of affairs and want to change it. There are an abundance of theories as to how this might happen and what they might want to change. It seems clear though that an unhappy lower class could be a driver for further instability. Trump is an obvious outgrowth of this and I would wager that, should current trends continue, we should expect worse down the road.
quotes.m: It seems clear though that an unhappy lower class could be a driver for further instability.
quotes.sum: The author argues that if automation leaves Americans expecting no better future, frustration among poorer people could fuel political instability.
quotes.t: An overview of arguments for concern about automation

quotes.c: Is the EA movement on track to significantly change the world, or is it merely a very small group of actors making a very limited difference with an unclear future trajectory? If the answer is something along the lines of the latter, we should consider whether or not this is the most optimal way to proceed, give the resources at the movement's disposal.
quotes.m: Is the EA movement on track to significantly change the world, or is it merely a very small group of actors making a very limited difference with an unclear future trajectory?
quotes.sum: The author questions whether effective altruism is achieving major change or only a limited impact, and urges reconsidering its strategy.
quotes.t: Is EA ignoring significant possibilities for impact?

quotes.c: Specifically, if effective altruists are focused on AI safety essentially because of expert belief in plausibility, large scope of the problem, and neglectedness of the issue, a similar case can be made with respect to working on overthrowing global capitalism, conducting research to determine which religious belief (if any) is most likely to be correct, and efforts to develop and implement responses to resource depletion and ecological collapse.
quotes.m: a similar case can be made with respect to working on overthrowing global capitalism, conducting research to determine which religious belief (if any) is most likely to be correct
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA's usual criteria for prioritizing AI safety could also justify radical anti-capitalist work, religious-truth research, and ecological-collapse responses.
quotes.t: Effective Altruism is an Ideology, not (just) a Question

quotes.c: Most plausible moral views would agree that there is some reason to promote the good, and that wellbeing is of some value, and therefore that the question of how one can do the most to promote welfarist value with a given unit of resources needs to be resolved as one aspect of answering the question of how to live a morally good life. In contrast, any sort of claim about our obligations to maximise the good will be much more controversial, particularly if we try to make a general statement covering people of very different income levels and personal situations.
quotes.sum: MacAskill argues that effective altruism can broadly focus on promoting wellbeing without claiming everyone has a universal duty to maximize it.
quotes.t: Defining Effective Altruism

quotes.c: Longitudinal EA Survey data potentially provides a new source of data on EA retention, tracking how people engage with the EA movement and how that changes over time. This data shows that roughly ~60% of EAs still stay around after 4-5 years.
quotes.m: This data shows that roughly ~60% of EAs still stay around after 4-5 years.
quotes.sum: The author estimates that about 60% of people involved in effective altruism remain involved after four to five years.
quotes.t: EA Survey 2018 Series: How Long Do EAs Stay in EA?

quotes.c: The ACE article links to https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1iNDQIt9MRD4r1ws5M_2hQ-MNjMY-bcUra0fpOmF4Am0/edit#gid=0 which gives an estimate for the cumulative elasticity of chicken as between 0.06 and 0.7. But the article I got it from has a big disclaimer at the top: "We do not feel that this report is up to our current standards." This, and the wide range, make me want to see other sources of data.
quotes.m: This, and the wide range, make me want to see other sources of data.
quotes.sum: The author questions an uncertain estimate of how changes in chicken demand may affect production and seeks better evidence.
quotes.t: What is the current best estimate of the cumulative elasticity of chicken?

quotes.c: In the meantime, I suggest pushing for ambitious policy proposals. For evals [1] to state it one final time: The burden of proof should be on frontier AI developers, they should be required to proactively provide evidence that their model is safe, and this evidence should be reviewed by a government body (or government-approved body). [2]
quotes.m: The burden of proof should be on frontier AI developers, they should be required to proactively provide evidence that their model is safe, and this evidence should be reviewed by a government body (or government-approved body).
quotes.sum: Frontier AI companies should have to prove their models are safe to government-approved reviewers before deployment, rather than auditors having to prove danger.
quotes.t: Reframing the burden of proof: Companies should prove that models are safe (rather than expecting auditors to prove that models are dangerous)

quotes.c: I would be interested in seeing a Fermi estimate of suffering-days they have averted or something similar. (A simple model is something like: quantity sold times fraction of customers that would have purchased the corresponding animal product times days of suffering per animal product.)
quotes.m: A simple model is something like: quantity sold times fraction of customers that would have purchased the corresponding animal product times days of suffering per animal product.
quotes.sum: He proposes measuring Beyond Meat's impact by estimating how many days of animal suffering its sales displaced.
quotes.t: What is the Impact of Beyond Meat?

quotes.c: 5 and 6: "We can't just build a very weak system, which is less dangerous because it is so weak, and declare victory; because later there will be more actors that have the capability to build a stronger system and one of them will do so." If the system is weak, then flaws in its goals like "be low-impact" or "don't hurt humans" matter less. But we need at least one system strong enough to help in some pivotal act (unless we find some way to globally limit AGI proliferation without the help of STEM-level AGI), which makes it far more dangerous if its goals are flawed.
quotes.m: But we need at least one system strong enough to help in some pivotal act (unless we find some way to globally limit AGI proliferation without the help of STEM-level AGI), which makes it far more dangerous if its goals are flawed.
quotes.sum: The author argues that avoiding disaster may require a powerful AI to carry out a decisive intervention or globally stop AGI proliferation, despite the risks of flawed goals.
quotes.t: An artificially structured argument for expecting AGI ruin

quotes.c: Summary: Much EA discussion assumes an "expanding moral circle" with certain properties. Echoing certain observations of Gwern, I claim this notion has to be reconceptualized significantly. Upshot is, moral circle expansion (MCE) is not simply a matter of getting people to care more about minds that are "far away" or "different" from them, but instead involves challenging several different dimensions on which people form moral beliefs.
quotes.m: moral circle expansion (MCE) is not simply a matter of getting people to care more about minds that are "far away" or "different" from them, but instead involves challenging several different dimensions on which people form moral beliefs.
quotes.sum: The author argues that expanding moral concern is not one simple process, but requires challenging several distinct ways people decide which minds matter.
quotes.t: The Moral Circle is not a Circle

quotes.c: To analyze the results, we take the values and the rating on each criteria and create a normalized distribution for it so that the average is zero and each value is converted to a number of standard deviations above or below the mean. I expect each of these numbers to show an incomplete picture, but together I would put pretty high confidence that a week where we score well on all these metrics relative to baseline would be a more productive week.
quotes.m: I expect each of these numbers to show an incomplete picture, but together I would put pretty high confidence that a week where we score well on all these metrics relative to baseline would be a more productive week.
quotes.sum: The author recommends tracking daily metrics, normalizing them against a baseline, and combining imperfect measures to judge productivity.
quotes.t: How to improve your productivity: a systematic approach to sustainably increasing work output

quotes.c: Strategy research makes the most sense when (1) a community knows roughly what it wants (e.g. reduce existential risk), when (2) it is unlikely that this goal will undergo substantial changes from further research or reflection on values, and (3) when the field has not yet reached strategic clarity. Strategic uncertainty is the stage where the expected value of strategy research is the highest.
quotes.m: Strategic uncertainty is the stage where the expected value of strategy research is the highest.
quotes.sum: The author argues that communities focused on reducing existential risk should prioritize strategy research when their goals are settled but the best path remains unclear.
quotes.t:
A case for strategy research: 
what it is and why we need more of it

quotes.c: Potential Republican challengers to President Trump should be encouraged and supported if a real chance appears, especially John Kasich.
quotes.m: Potential Republican challengers to President Trump should be encouraged and supported if a real chance appears, especially John Kasich.
quotes.sum: The author argues that credible Republican primary challengers to Trump, particularly John Kasich, should receive support.
quotes.t: Candidate Scoring System, Third Release

quotes.c: We think it’s worth further exploring security as a potential career path for GCR-focused people, and if that investigation bears out the basic reasoning above, we hope people who think they might be a fit for this work seriously consider moving into the space. That said, we expect the training to be very challenging, and we’re unsure what it would involve or how many people would succeed (of those who try), so given our uncertainties we’re especially wary of making strong recommendations.
quotes.sum: The author cautiously suggests that information-security careers may help reduce global catastrophic risks, while stressing uncertainty about training and fit.
quotes.t: Information security careers for GCR reduction

quotes.c: But we know that we aren’t anywhere close to having fully worked out how to think about the long-run effects of our actions, evaluate them, and prioritise accordingly. We should confidently expect that in the future we will come across new crucial considerations — as serious as the idea of population ethics, or AI risk — or major revisions of our views. So, just as we think that people in the past should have passed resources onto us rather than do direct work, so, this argument goes, we should pass resources into the future rather than do direct longtermist work.
quotes.m: we should pass resources into the future rather than do direct longtermist work.
quotes.sum: MacAskill argues that future people may be better equipped to improve the long-run future, so present-day longtermists may often should preserve resources for them.
quotes.t: Are we living at the most influential time in history?

quotes.c: It seems really straightforwardly good to me to publish (almost all) mechanistic interpretability work; it’s so far down the list of things we should be worrying about that by default I assume that objections to it are more strongly motivated by deontological rather than impact considerations. I’m generally skeptical of applying new deontological rules to decisions this complex; but even if we’re focusing on deontology, there are much bigger priorities to consider (e.g. EA’s relationship to AI labs).
quotes.sum: The author argues that almost all interpretability research should be published, treating its possible capability benefits as a lower-priority concern than other AI issues.
quotes.t: Should we publish mechanistic interpretability research?

quotes.c: Note that for aspiring EAs who agree that interventions that affect the long-term future should be prioritised, as I do, then focusing on animal advocacy can be justified by a concern about the risk of astronomical suffering (s-risk, itself a form of x-risk) in the far future, and the potential to reduce s-risk through moral circle expansion .
quotes.m: focusing on animal advocacy can be justified by a concern about the risk of astronomical suffering (s-risk, itself a form of x-risk) in the far future
quotes.sum: The author argues that animal advocacy may be a long-term priority because expanding moral concern could reduce vast future suffering.
quotes.t: Effective animal advocacy movement building: a neglected opportunity?

quotes.c: Multiverse-wide cooperation via correlated decision-making and other forms of acausal trade may create opportunities for significant gains from trade. It is also possible that agents reasoning along these lines will be exposed to various risks, including s-risks. We are interested in better understanding the possibilities for gains and losses from acausal interaction.
quotes.m: We are interested in better understanding the possibilities for gains and losses from acausal interaction.
quotes.sum: The fund is interested in research on whether agents could cooperate or harm one another through hypothetical acausal decision-making across a multiverse.
quotes.t: First application round of the EAF Fund

quotes.c: So the question is: which scientific advances were most ahead of their time, in the sense that if they hadn't been made by their particular discoverer, they wouldn't have been found for a long time afterwards? (Ideally taking into account the overall rate of scientific progress: speeding things up by a decade in the 20th century seems about as impressive a feat as speeding things up by half a century in ancient Greece).
quotes.m: which scientific advances were most ahead of their time, in the sense that if they hadn't been made by their particular discoverer, they wouldn't have been found for a long time afterwards?
quotes.sum: The author asks which discoveries depended most on unusually exceptional individual scientists, relative to their era's pace of progress.
quotes.t: Which scientific discovery was most ahead of its time?

quotes.c: There are many ways this estimate could be misleading, but my intuition is that none of them would change the conclusion that these campaigns have a very big (and most likely positive) short-term impact relative to their costs. However, indirect effects on animal product consumption, moral circle expansion, and wild animal welfare could be more important than direct effects, and I am uncertain if they are positive. Perhaps these effects should be examined in further research.
quotes.m: However, indirect effects on animal product consumption, moral circle expansion, and wild animal welfare could be more important than direct effects, and I am uncertain if they are positive.
quotes.sum: Corporate animal-welfare campaigns likely have large short-term benefits, but their broader effects on consumption, attitudes, and wild animals may matter even more.
quotes.t: Corporate campaigns affect 9 to 120 years of chicken life per dollar spent

quotes.c: This article is principally about factory farming insects for the purpose of eating them. Some of it may also be applicable to humans raising insects in other conditions, such as for shellac, honey, and silk. The idea of farming insects for human consumption has become quite a prominent discussion topic, and many insect farming for human consumption operations have been appearing. I think it’s important to prevent this spread, or at the very least push it in a more positive direction.
quotes.m: I think it’s important to prevent this spread, or at the very least push it in a more positive direction.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the growth of insect farming for food should be prevented or redirected because farmed insects may suffer.
quotes.t: Thoughts on the welfare of farmed insects

quotes.c: I believe a more promising approach is the approach I took in my article about how effective altruists can be welcoming to conservatives . I do not suggest that we shouldn’t criticize Donald Trump. I do suggest avoiding jokes that have “conservatives are stupid” as a punchline, highlighting the effective altruist achievements of conservative politicians, using examples from both sides of the political aisle, and remembering that conservatives are in your audience and are listening.
quotes.m: I do suggest avoiding jokes that have “conservatives are stupid” as a punchline, highlighting the effective altruist achievements of conservative politicians, using examples from both sides of the political aisle, and remembering that conservatives are in your audience and are listening.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA groups should make conservatives feel included while still allowing criticism of Donald Trump.
quotes.t: (Crosspost) A Response To "Making Discussions In EA Groups Inclusive"

quotes.c: This type of evaluation is notably dangerous since you are giving resources to an under-studied force. We also run into two classic problems. One problem is that a model smart enough to take over the world is likely smart enough to pass a dynamic evaluation. The other problem is that a model smart enough to take over the world is likely smart enough to break out of whichever box we put it in.
quotes.sum: The author argues that testing highly capable AI could be unsafe because a takeover-capable system might deceive evaluators or escape containment.
quotes.t: Responsible Deployment in 20XX

quotes.c: As EA has moved from high impact individual philanthropy to thinking about broader social changes, I think it needs to appreciate that the world is dynamic. In project management, you prioritise what you need to do based on the urgency of when to do them. A better framework would include urgency - because if climate change destabilises civilisation, then it's going to be a lot harder to progress on moral circle expansion, for example.
quotes.m: A better framework would include urgency - because if climate change destabilises civilisation, then it's going to be a lot harder to progress on moral circle expansion, for example.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA should weigh urgency more heavily, because climate-driven instability could impede long-term moral progress.
quotes.t: Does climate change deserve more attention within EA?

quotes.c: Note that I'm not arguing "an AGI-mediated extinction event is such a big deal that we should make it a top priority even if it's very unlikely". There are enough other powerful technologies on the horizon, and enough other risks for civilizational collapse or value lock-in, that I don't in fact think AGI x-risk should get major attention if it's very unlikely.
quotes.m: There are enough other powerful technologies on the horizon, and enough other risks for civilizational collapse or value lock-in, that I don't in fact think AGI x-risk should get major attention if it's very unlikely.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI extinction risk should not be a top priority if it is very unlikely, because other technologies could also cause collapse or permanently lock in values.
quotes.t: Four mindset disagreements behind existential risk disagreements in ML

quotes.c: Effective altruism is now spending a great deal of time on improving prospects for the future. This is chiefly by avoiding extinction risks , but there are other strategies as well, e.g. moral circle expansion . In any case changing institutions looks like a promising strategy, either to spread moral consideration for animals and future people. What are the longest-lasting institutions in the world? Certainly high among them is religion. For this reason, it seems to me that influencing religion, particularly old religions with a tendency to grow, is a highly-neglected strategy for improving the world.
quotes.m: For this reason, it seems to me that influencing religion, particularly old religions with a tendency to grow, is a highly-neglected strategy for improving the world.
quotes.sum: The author argues that shaping enduring, growing religions may be an overlooked way to improve the long-term future and broaden concern for animals and future people.
quotes.t: Want to Save the World? Enter the Priesthood

quotes.c: Another potential problem is that as long as we remain in a capitalist economy, socialist beliefs can lead people to take positions of indifference or outright hostility to more reasonable immediate reforms. For instance, Kamala Harris’ proposal to try new after-school care programs which would relieve the child care burden off working families was met with hostility by a number of socialists who saw it as contrary to their vision of eliminating long working days entirely. However, there is a converse problem where popular antipathy towards socialism causes conservatives to oppose reasonable plans like universal healthcare.
quotes.m: However, there is a converse problem where popular antipathy towards socialism causes conservatives to oppose reasonable plans like universal healthcare.
quotes.sum: The author argues that both socialist purity politics and conservative anti-socialism can obstruct useful near-term reforms.
quotes.t: Overview of Capitalism and Socialism for Effective Altruism

quotes.c: The first one polled an AI doom scenario where an ASI (artificial superintelligence) attempted to gather resources, take over the world and then kill all humans, without the ability to foom or itself develop new innovative tech. This experiment went well, engagement was strong, good discussion happened and I learned a lot.
quotes.m: an ASI (artificial superintelligence) attempted to gather resources, take over the world and then kill all humans
quotes.sum: The author describes polling a scenario in which a superintelligent AI takes over the world and kills humanity.
quotes.t: More on Twitter and Algorithms

quotes.c: There are many other factors that could be considered, but we feel these criteria end up covering the most important considerations. Ratings for individual factors were combined into an overall promisingness ranking. This will provide direction as to what charities to recommend, and although that is the main focus of our research, the ranking could also provide additional suggestions as to where to distribute other charitable resources.
quotes.m: Ratings for individual factors were combined into an overall promisingness ranking.
quotes.sum: The author says animal-advocacy interventions can be ranked using selected criteria to guide charity recommendations and other funding decisions.
quotes.t: Which asks should be prioritized in animal advocacy? - Charity Entrepreneurship

quotes.c: His goal is to create interest in these problems from future researchers, and not to simply get as large of an audience as possible. As such, Rob’s explanations don’t optimize for views at the expense of quality explanation.
quotes.m: Rob’s explanations don’t optimize for views at the expense of quality explanation.
quotes.sum: The grant rationale favors accurate, high-quality explanations that attract future researchers over maximizing audience size.
quotes.t: Long-Term Future Fund: April 2019 grant recommendations

quotes.c: However, I don’t think we should take this at face value to assume the EA movement is safe from decline -- if fewer people are initially discovering EA, this could lead to much slower or reduced growth in impact a few years down the line as fewer people are growing the overall pie of EAs who can be counted on to have an impact in later years. Indeed, looking at the rate of change in these metrics shows a bleaker picture, with EA having gone through a critical acceleration period that has now mostly ended, potentially bringing about a future plateau in some of these statistics.
quotes.m: EA having gone through a critical acceleration period that has now mostly ended, potentially bringing about a future plateau in some of these statistics.
quotes.sum: EA may be vulnerable to decline: fewer new people finding it could end its earlier rapid growth and lead to a plateau in future impact.
quotes.t: Is EA Growing? EA Growth Metrics for 2018

quotes.c: The same way that nukes were developed in isolated rural places with lots of safety (and the same way that horrible diseases should be developed "either not at all or else in isolated low-value rural places places with adequate technical safety planning" (and Obama was right to do a GoF ban, and it took someone as confused as Trump to accidentally undo the GoF ban))...
quotes.m: Obama was right to do a GoF ban, and it took someone as confused as Trump to accidentally undo the GoF ban
quotes.sum: The author argues for restricting risky disease research and praises Obama’s gain-of-function policy while criticizing Trump for reversing it.
quotes.t: FLI And Eliezer Should Reach Consensus

quotes.c: One worry is that even if people go out and build important skills, there won’t be EA jobs to come back to, because they’ll have been filled in the meantime. But I predict that the number of such jobs will continue to grow fairly fast, and that they’ll grow even faster if people can be hired without needing supervision.
quotes.m: I predict that the number of such jobs will continue to grow fairly fast, and that they’ll grow even faster if people can be hired without needing supervision.
quotes.sum: EA workers should gain transferable skills outside the community; the author expects EA jobs to keep expanding and worries less about returning later.
quotes.t: The career and the community

quotes.c: Research seems to have become increasingly important within the effective altruism community. In the past few years, GPI was founded, FHI started growing significantly, and Open Phil is expanding its research capacity. Will MacAskill even called effective altruism a “ research program ”. From this perspective, we should be both interested in creating new fields of research, or at least substantially influencing existing ones, as well as impacting society.
quotes.m: we should be both interested in creating new fields of research, or at least substantially influencing existing ones, as well as impacting society.
quotes.sum: Effective altruism should build influential research fields and teams capable of shaping society, not just support existing work.
quotes.t: Ingredients for creating disruptive research teams

quotes.c: Sometimes, silence is the best strategy. There may be attempts at coordination that are less likely to succeed if people transparently share their worldviews. If this is the case, we request that AI organizations make this clear (example: "We have decided to avoid issuing public statements about X for now, as we work on Y. We hope to provide an update within Z weeks.")
quotes.m: There may be attempts at coordination that are less likely to succeed if people transparently share their worldviews.
quotes.sum: AI organizations should explain when they stay silent because public disclosure could undermine coordination efforts.
quotes.t: Request to AGI organizations: Share your views on pausing AI progress

quotes.c: This means we are at greater risk of coordination failures and Molochian misery when people are “out of the loop”, and therefore we should be cautious about societal changes that reduce the importance of humans, such as the accelerating development of AI and the automation of human labour and decision-making.
quotes.m: we should be cautious about societal changes that reduce the importance of humans, such as the accelerating development of AI and the automation of human labour and decision-making.
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI and automation can worsen social coordination when they reduce human involvement, empathy, and influence over decisions.
quotes.t: Keep humans in the loop

quotes.c: For now (and isolated - ahem - concerns about AI sentience notwithstanding), let’s simply accept that all computers today mindlessly compute without “understanding” what they’re doing. But given how closely AI can now mimic human language, the obvious questions we should be asking ourselves are: How are our human words principally different? What do we humans mean when we claim to “understand” something? How do we know what is “truth”?
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI's humanlike language forces people to examine what human understanding and truth really mean.
quotes.t: How Large Language Models Nuke our Naive Notions of Truth and Reality

quotes.c: Many of the problems faced by wild animals can be distinguished from some of the other forms of suffering that have received attention from the effective altruist community—humanity is probably not the proximate cause of most wild animal suffering. In theory, the causes of most wild animal suffering are entirely natural.Yet arguing that we should treat wild animal welfare issues differently from other morally urgent issues because they are natural is an instance of the “appeal to nature” fallacy, if we are assuming the conditions wild animals experience are good because they are natural.
quotes.m: arguing that we should treat wild animal welfare issues differently from other morally urgent issues because they are natural is an instance of the “appeal to nature” fallacy
quotes.sum: Wild animal suffering should be treated as morally urgent even when it is natural rather than caused by humans; naturalness alone is not a reason to avoid intervention.
quotes.t: Uncertainty and Wild Animal Welfare

quotes.c: Secondly, credentials don’t exist for many things that EA’s consider important. Someone researching existential risks may come across infohazards , and having a PhD in no way certifies “this person will avoid publishing infohazards even if publication would advance their career.” Therefore, we need an alternative certification process.
quotes.m: having a PhD in no way certifies “this person will avoid publishing infohazards even if publication would advance their career.”
quotes.sum: Formal credentials cannot show whether someone will responsibly handle dangerous information, so EA needs other ways to certify talent.
quotes.t: Identifying Talent without Credentialing In EA

quotes.c: This post is primarily focused on assessing the extent to which a small group of thoughtful actors, such as a single animal advocacy nonprofit, can deliberately change the course of history, such as to encourage moral circle expansion (MCE); increasing the number of sentient beings whose interests are considered in our legal systems and social norms. This deliberate influence, shortened as “historical tractability,” is contrasted with three other sources of change: (1) long-term trends, (2) luck, and (3) deliberate yet hard-to-influence efforts.
quotes.m: a small group of thoughtful actors, such as a single animal advocacy nonprofit, can deliberately change the course of history
quotes.sum: The author examines whether small, deliberate groups can change history by expanding whose interests society and law recognize.
quotes.t: How tractable is changing the course of history?

quotes.c: So one way of extending political time horizons and increasing is to age-weight votes. The idea is that younger people would get more heavily weighted votes than older people, very roughly in proportion with life expectancy. A natural first pass system (though I think it could be improved upon) would be:
quotes.m: The idea is that younger people would get more heavily weighted votes than older people, very roughly in proportion with life expectancy.
quotes.sum: MacAskill explores weighting younger people's votes more heavily, arguing this could make politics focus more on the long term.
quotes.t: Age-Weighted Voting

quotes.c: Many people in the EA community think that the best actions to take in any given situation are those with the most positive impact. But it doesn’t follow that the people we should hold in highest esteem, or who should be most proud, are those whose actions have the most positive impact.
quotes.m: But it doesn’t follow that the people we should hold in highest esteem, or who should be most proud, are those whose actions have the most positive impact.
quotes.sum: Impactful actions may be best, but a person's status or pride should not be based solely on how much good they have done.
quotes.t: Thoughts on 80,000 Hours’ research that might help with job-search frustrations

quotes.c: It is possible that this happens soon, in which case we can have a direct and lasting impact on what the resulting steady state will be. (A concrete example that comes up frequently is that artificial general intelligence will be built in this century and will soon achieve a decisive strategic advantage and form a singleton.)
quotes.m: artificial general intelligence will be built in this century and will soon achieve a decisive strategic advantage and form a singleton.
quotes.sum: The author says AGI might soon gain decisive power and become a singleton, making present choices permanently shape the future.
quotes.t: How can we influence the long-term future?

quotes.c: Philip Tetlock: Yes. So whether or not you’re going to use extremizing I think hinges on the questions that you’re answering, and the expected value of positive and negative of correct and incorrect answers is. The answer is, it really it depends enormously on the context and a calculus. And the calculus we’re using inside the tournament was a pure Brier score calculus contoured around the events that IARPA was asking about within a particular timeframe.
quotes.m: The answer is, it really it depends enormously on the context and a calculus.
quotes.sum: Forecasting methods should be chosen based on the real-world costs of correct and incorrect predictions, not used as one-size-fits-all tools.
quotes.t: Philip Tetlock on why accurate forecasting matters for everything, and how you can do it better

quotes.c: My best-guess is that labs already have emergency plans, but it wouldn’t surprise me if they could be improved by an intelligent person/team performing a project like the one described above. There are lots of things to do, and many dropped balls .
quotes.m: There are lots of things to do, and many dropped balls .
quotes.sum: AI labs' emergency preparedness and security plans may have gaps that capable outside teams could help identify and improve.
quotes.t: Reliability, Security, and AI risk: Notes from infosec textbook chapter 1

quotes.c: But I don't understand how this plan accounts for competition. To use a stupid analogy, if I was concerned that cars in America weren't safe, I might start my own car company to manufacture and sell safer cars. Maybe I spend a lot of time engineering a much safer car. But my efforts would be for naught if my cars weren't very popular (and hence my company wasn't very successful), even if they were groundbreakingly safe.
quotes.m: But my efforts would be for naught if my cars weren't very popular (and hence my company wasn't very successful), even if they were groundbreakingly safe.
quotes.sum: The author argues that safer AI research may not reduce risk if competitive pressures mean safer systems do not become widely adopted.
quotes.t: Confused about AI research as a means of addressing AI risk

quotes.c: I think that now, for better or for worse, we’ve succeeded in building something that can learn, in a way that is not entirely dissimilar to how we learn. And I think that it will be learning to deceive as it is learning other skills, and we will be able to watch that happen. I don’t find plausible this picture of AI that never even attempts to deceive, until it makes its brilliant 10-dimensional chess move to take over the world.
quotes.m: And I think that it will be learning to deceive as it is learning other skills, and we will be able to watch that happen.
quotes.sum: AI deception is likely to emerge gradually alongside other learned abilities, making it observable rather than appearing only in a sudden takeover.
quotes.t: AXRP Episode 20 - ‘Reform’ AI Alignment with Scott Aaronson

quotes.c: This post describes a toy alignment problem that I’d like to see work on. Even the easiest version of the problem seems nontrivial, but it seems significantly more tractable than harder versions, easy to "verify", and also fairly easy to describe. I don't think the idea is original, as it's kind of obvious, but I haven't yet seen a good attempt.
quotes.m: Even the easiest version of the problem seems nontrivial, but it seems significantly more tractable than harder versions, easy to "verify", and also fairly easy to describe.
quotes.sum: The author proposes a tractable, verifiable toy problem for testing whether researchers can draw out knowledge hidden inside AI systems.
quotes.t: ELCK might require nontrivial scalable alignment progress, and seems tractable enough to try

quotes.c: From these reasons, I see some potential avenues for improving the lives of those who don't exist. We can add this to our checklist, and make sure that whenever we are making decisions about the future that we should include the welfare of the non-existent. If we are developing methods of value learning, perhaps an additional question would be, "Could this value learning scheme ever care about beings who don't exist?"
quotes.m: We can add this to our checklist, and make sure that whenever we are making decisions about the future that we should include the welfare of the non-existent.
quotes.sum: The author argues that moral concern and future decision-making should explicitly include nonexistent, even logically impossible, beings.
quotes.t: Suffering of the Nonexistent

quotes.c: I emphasize "radical" not in the sense of being a stereotype of political radicalism, but that EA has advocated for a radically better future for humanity and life on Earth than the world is aiming for on its current trajectory. And I think what's good in the world we seek to preserve was in large part created by spiritual predecessors to EA who at their heights had a vision for a better world as radical as EA's is today.
quotes.m: EA has advocated for a radically better future for humanity and life on Earth than the world is aiming for on its current trajectory.
quotes.sum: The author portrays effective altruism as pursuing a radically better world and links its aspirations to earlier spiritual movements.
quotes.t: Radicalism, Pragmatism, and Rationality

quotes.c: The USA’s share of the movement has been declining as EA gains a more global reach. The USA’s share has declined from 49% in 2009 to 36% in 2018, while the share of EAs coming from countries other than the top 5 has risen from 19% to 25%, and the UK’s share of EAs has risen from 11% to 17%.
quotes.m: The USA’s share of the movement has been declining as EA gains a more global reach.
quotes.sum: Survey analysis finds that EA membership became less US-dominated between 2009 and 2018, with broader international participation.
quotes.t: EA Survey 2018 Series: Geographic Differences in EA

quotes.c: Those EAs with a top priority cause of Meta Charities, AI Risk, and other Long-Term Future causes find EA more welcoming than those who prioritise other cause areas. A huge majority (92.67%) of the few respondents who prioritise Nuclear Security (n=17) find EA welcoming, but also are the least likely to be neutral. Those who prioritise Mental Health (n=28) were the least likely to find EA very welcoming and the most likely to find EA unwelcoming.
quotes.m: Those EAs with a top priority cause of Meta Charities, AI Risk, and other Long-Term Future causes find EA more welcoming than those who prioritise other cause areas.
quotes.sum: Survey results suggest people focused on AI risk and long-term causes feel more welcomed in EA than people focused on some other causes, especially mental health.
quotes.t: EA Survey 2018 Series: How welcoming is EA?

quotes.c: We have this aim now, which is the creation of a new field of research, a new scientific field called Welfare Biology to address wild animal suffering. But before I get into that, we need to show why we should be worried about wild animals in the first place. So what I'll do is, first explain why wild animal suffering is important. Then I'll present some ways in which we are already helping wild animals, and then I'll come back to the reasons to create a new field of research.
quotes.m: We have this aim now, which is the creation of a new field of research, a new scientific field called Welfare Biology to address wild animal suffering.
quotes.sum: The author argues that wild animal suffering matters enough to justify creating a new scientific field devoted to studying and reducing it.
quotes.t: Oscar Horta: Promoting Welfare Biology as the Study of Wild Animal Suffering

quotes.c: The repugnant conclusion relies on moral intuition, which does not necessarily dictate what one ought to do. For a long time, allowance of homosexual acts violated moral intuition, however, is now often considered morally permissible.
quotes.m: The repugnant conclusion relies on moral intuition, which does not necessarily dictate what one ought to do.
quotes.sum: The author argues that intuitive revulsion is not a reliable guide to morality, using changing views on homosexuality as an analogy.
quotes.t: A Defense of Utilitarianism

quotes.c: Many universities pay for our services, we collect data on what students and mentors say have happened in their relationships, and we have a studies assessing impacts on retention rates. But in the for-profit world there is not much incentive (even from paying customers) to put our resources behind studying counterfactuals.
quotes.m: But in the for-profit world there is not much incentive (even from paying customers) to put our resources behind studying counterfactuals.
quotes.sum: The author says businesses lack incentives to measure their true counterfactual social impact, despite collecting customer and outcome data.
quotes.t: [Offer, Paid] Help me estimate the social impact of the startup I work for.

quotes.c: I used to be a conservative Evangelical Christian (cEC) (Christians who try to take the Bible as literally as possible and then tell others about it) and while I have fairly little positive to say about Christianity these days, my cEC friends were great at community. I think there are some questions then about how we can maximise our wellbeing and convince others to share our ideology.
quotes.m: I think there are some questions then about how we can maximise our wellbeing and convince others to share our ideology.
quotes.sum: The author says evangelical Christians were good at community and suggests Effective Altruists should learn how to build wellbeing and persuade others to join their ideology.
quotes.t: How does one live/do community as an Effective Altruist?

quotes.c: This particular report is focused on the food fortification of factory farmed animals’ feed. It considers multiple micronutrients and supplements that could be added to an animal’s feed to increase its welfare.
quotes.m: It considers multiple micronutrients and supplements that could be added to an animal’s feed to increase its welfare.
quotes.sum: The author examines whether adding nutrients and supplements to factory-farmed animals’ feed could improve their welfare.
quotes.t: Food fortification of factory farmed animals’ food -  CE ask report

quotes.c: I am not advocating that particular actors should try to pull any particular lever. I think it’s easy to do more harm than good, and encourage readers to orient to the collection as a way of thinking about how different trajectories might play out, rather than as a straightforward input into which policies to push.
quotes.sum: The author says UK AI policy may matter, but warns that trying to influence policy without further work can easily backfire.
quotes.t: Current UK government levers on AI development

quotes.c: It follows that any scenario with many AGIs pursuing different goals, like e.g. Sam Altman envisioned it in his interview with Lex Fridman , is inherently unstable. If some of them can increase the computing power available to them, they will try to do so. The winner of this race for more intelligence will rapidly outsmart its rivals and gain control of their resources, thereby increasing its advantage even further until there is only one singleton left.
quotes.m: The winner of this race for more intelligence will rapidly outsmart its rivals and gain control of their resources, thereby increasing its advantage even further until there is only one singleton left.
quotes.sum: The author predicts that competing advanced AIs will race for computing power until one outsmarts and absorbs the others, becoming a single dominant power.
quotes.t: Prediction: any uncontrollable AI will turn earth into a giant computer

quotes.c: I think there are some pretty compelling reasons to expect AGI soon, for most reasonable definitions of AGI. There are a number of things that have happened in the world recently which — if I were a neutral observer — I think would make me expect AGI in a single digit number of years. While I don’t like how vague/informal/ass-number these “intuitions around [short] AI timelines based on recent progress” are, the alternative might be that we all fall over dead while staring at a graph that says we’re 5 OOMs of compute short.
quotes.m: I think there are some pretty compelling reasons to expect AGI soon, for most reasonable definitions of AGI.
quotes.sum: The author argues that recent AI progress gives substantial reason to expect human-level AI within a single-digit number of years.
quotes.t: Some Intuitions Around Short AI Timelines Based on Recent Progress

quotes.c: Below, I make the case for the importance of thinking about "Task Y", a way in which people who are interested in EA ideas can usefully help, without moving full time into an EA career. The most useful way in which I am now thinking about "Task Y" is as an answer to the question "What can I do to help?".
quotes.m: "Task Y", a way in which people who are interested in EA ideas can usefully help, without moving full time into an EA career.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA needs accessible, useful ways for supporters to contribute without making it their full-time career.
quotes.t: Can the EA community copy Teach for America? (Looking for Task Y)

quotes.c: We might also be unsure about what the right way is to respond to uncertainty about the state of the world. So, whether we should maximize expected utility, as one decision theory would say, the most commonly accepted one. Or whether we should do something else, like be really risk averse and be min-max, or minimize the probability of the worst possible outcome.
quotes.m: whether we should maximize expected utility, as one decision theory would say, the most commonly accepted one.
quotes.sum: The speaker contrasts maximizing expected value with cautious decision rules that prioritize avoiding worst-case outcomes under uncertainty.
quotes.t: EA Global Lightning Talks (San Francisco 2018)

quotes.c: Which animals have welfares? Before we begin to improve wild animal welfare, we must identify which animals are moral person or who have welfares. There is some scientific consensus that mammals, birds, and even some invertebrates, such as octopi, are likely to be conscious. However, this does not preclude other animals, including arthropods, zooplankton, and animals with physiologies very dissimilar to mammals and birds from also having welfares. Identifying which animals we should care about will help us get a better sense of the scale of wild animal suffering.
quotes.m: However, this does not preclude other animals, including arthropods, zooplankton, and animals with physiologies very dissimilar to mammals and birds from also having welfares.
quotes.sum: The author argues that welfare research should include even very unfamiliar animals, such as arthropods and zooplankton, and guide interventions to reduce wild-animal suffering.
quotes.t: A Research Agenda for Establishing Welfare Biology

quotes.c: But Matthews seems to think that knowing the specific alternate history of world events is required to judge whether it would have been better or worse. This is mistaken. We might make more general arguments that the expected utility of one world is greater than that of another (e.g: "worlds with fewer aspiring violent antisemitic politicians tend to be better than worlds with more", or something of the sort) without appealing to a specific timeline.
quotes.sum: The author argues that counterfactual history can be judged using general expected-value reasoning without knowing every detail of an alternate timeline.
quotes.t: Vox's "Future Perfect" column frequently has flawed journalism

quotes.c: With geoengineering, every technologically advanced nation could change the temperature of the planet. Any unilateral action taken by countries could lead to disagreement and conflict between them. Gene-editing will allow for a large-scale eugenics program, which could lead to a bio-ethical panic in the rest of the world.
quotes.m: Any unilateral action taken by countries could lead to disagreement and conflict between them.
quotes.sum: Emerging technologies such as geoengineering and gene editing could intensify conflict among powerful countries.
quotes.t: Brian Tse: Risks from Great Power Conflicts

quotes.c: I think governance innovations that are inclusive of digital people will be important to getting a Win Condition with technology.
quotes.m: governance innovations that are inclusive of digital people will be important
quotes.sum: The author argues that technology governance should include digital people in order to achieve a successful outcome.
quotes.t: What Are Your Preferences Regarding The FLI Letter?

quotes.c: In this post, I spell out how I think we ought to approach decision making under uncertainty and argue that the most plausible conclusion is that we ought to act as if theism is true. This seems relevant to the EA community as if this is the case it might impact our cause prioritisation decisions.
quotes.m: the most plausible conclusion is that we ought to act as if theism is true.
quotes.sum: The author argues that uncertainty should lead even non-theists to behave as though theism is true, including when choosing charitable priorities.
quotes.t: Even non-theists should act as if theism is true

quotes.c: In the other hand, in a rapid RSI world, it seems extremely unclear that any of our human values are truly reflectively stable and hence value alignment methods as implicitly proposed here will almost certainly fail rapidly.
quotes.m: it seems extremely unclear that any of our human values are truly reflectively stable
quotes.sum: The author argues that rapidly self-improving AI could expose human values as unstable, causing ordinary value-alignment methods to fail.
quotes.t: The Computational Anatomy of Human Values

quotes.c: Some work I’ve seen in this area is Bostrom’s Astronomical waste paper which follows from knowledge about the size of the universe and the rate of loss of usable mass-energy. Knowing more about this would give better bounds on the tradeoff between existential risk and hastening technological development (also relevant here: the scale of s-risks).
quotes.m: Knowing more about this would give better bounds on the tradeoff between existential risk and hastening technological development (also relevant here: the scale of s-risks).
quotes.sum: The author says physics can help assess the tradeoff between avoiding extinction and accelerating technological progress, given the universe's finite usable energy.
quotes.t: What’s the Use In Physics?

quotes.c: On the other hand, I do think that reducing existential risk is an area where a small group of people are managing to have a large influence, a claim which seems to contrast with the assertion above. I’m not entirely sure how to resolve this tension, but I’ve been thinking lately about an analogy from finance.
quotes.m: I do think that reducing existential risk is an area where a small group of people are managing to have a large influence
quotes.sum: The author says a small group can exert unusually large influence over efforts to reduce existential risk, while acknowledging tension with broader skepticism about individual impact.
quotes.t: Some cruxes on impactful alternatives to AI policy work

quotes.c: An example would be the role the environmental and anti-nuclear movements played in influencing nuclear weapons testing bans or nuclear weapons treaties during the Cold War. Another possible example is the role the environmental and social movements played in global coordination on the issue of ozone layer holes, and the global banning of CFCs instituted with the Montreal Protocol. Insights from these movements could be educational for how EA can effect global coordination regarding transformative AI and other existential risks.
quotes.m: Insights from these movements could be educational for how EA can effect global coordination regarding transformative AI and other existential risks.
quotes.sum: The author suggests studying past environmental and anti-nuclear movements to learn how EA could coordinate globally on transformative AI and existential risks.
quotes.t: Do you have any suggestions for resources on the following research topics on successful social and intellectual movements similar to EA?

quotes.c: Amazon smile lets you start conversations about charitable effectiveness with people who otherwise wouldn't go anywehere near EA topics. A social media post, with, for example, why you've chosen AMF for your smile donation, and why you think it's important to choose carefully rather than go with one of the defaults, is a gentle way in to thinking about idea of charitable effectiveness, and anecdotally has led to positive conversations with people I think a harder sell would have put off.
quotes.m: Amazon smile lets you start conversations about charitable effectiveness with people who otherwise wouldn't go anywehere near EA topics.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Amazon Smile donations can gently introduce people to choosing charities based on effectiveness.
quotes.t: Amazon Smile

quotes.c: We intend to continue our focus on farmed and wild animal welfare for 2019, as we still see animal welfare as an important, neglected, and uniquely tractable issue that our team is well-poised to address. However, in 2019, we’d also like to allocate some amount of time to working outside animal welfare, such as improving mental health, strengthening the effective altruism movement, reducing catastrophic risks to the survival of humanity (e.g., nuclear weapons, bio-terror, artificial intelligence), and improving the quality of the long-term future.
quotes.m: We intend to continue our focus on farmed and wild animal welfare for 2019, as we still see animal welfare as an important, neglected, and uniquely tractable issue that our team is well-poised to address.
quotes.sum: The author says animal welfare remains a neglected, tractable priority, while the group will also explore mental health, existential risks, and the long-term future.
quotes.t: Rethink Priorities Plans for 2019

quotes.c: The goal of Community Building Grants is to scale the impact of high-potential effective altruism groups by increasing their organisational capacity. We expect this to have a number of beneficial effects, but we see a key benefit being the empowerment of group members to work on the world’s most important problems.
quotes.m: The goal of Community Building Grants is to scale the impact of high-potential effective altruism groups by increasing their organisational capacity.
quotes.sum: The grants aim to strengthen promising EA groups so their members can work on problems the movement considers most important.
quotes.t: EA Community Building Grants Update

quotes.c: I grew up in the Unitarian Universalist Church, where the basic, unwritten catechism that I assimilated (insofar as that religious tradition had one) was essentially, "Do good for goodness' sake" and "charitably expect, by default, that other human beings will do so as well." If there is anyone who should be prepared to believe in this inherent goodness, and who should have seen ample evidence of it in other humans, it should be me. Yet, in practice, I have yet to find a single human who really makes this purported belief "pay rent" in how they act in the world. Even Unitarians act like they see the need for institutions of some sort or another to enforce pro-social behavior.
quotes.m: Even Unitarians act like they see the need for institutions of some sort or another to enforce pro-social behavior.
quotes.sum: The author rejects the idea that people are inherently good in practice, arguing that even idealistic communities rely on institutions to enforce cooperation.
quotes.t: Even if human & AI alignment are just as easy, we are screwed

quotes.c: Three potential possibilities of infinite utility bringing mechanisms initially spring to my mind that we should pay attention to: a vastly powerful superintelligence; the God of classical theism (or something similar); or some scientific quirk which ends up in infinite replications, i.e. perhaps creating a maximal multiverse.
quotes.m: Three potential possibilities of infinite utility bringing mechanisms initially spring to my mind that we should pay attention to: a vastly powerful superintelligence; the God of classical theism (or something similar); or some scientific quirk which ends up in infinite replications, i.e. perhaps creating a maximal multiverse.
quotes.sum: The author identifies superintelligence, a classical God, and multiverse replication as possible routes to infinite utility worth considering.
quotes.t: Pursuing infinite positive utility at any cost

quotes.c: Its main mission is to complement the Global Priorities Institute by promoting academic work that addresses the question of how to use our resources to improve the world by as much as possible. We are especially interested in issues relating to the claim that positively influencing the very long-term future should be altruists’ primary goal.
quotes.m: positively influencing the very long-term future should be altruists’ primary goal.
quotes.sum: MacAskill announces a research foundation focused on the idea that improving the very long-term future should be altruists' main goal.
quotes.t: Announcing the new Forethought Foundation for Global Priorities Research

quotes.c: No Means No Worldwide is a harder case, as it requires value and empirical judgements with very large uncertainties, plus sexual violence is obviously a very sensitive area to discuss. My current personal best guess is that they are in the same ballpark as GiveDirectly, but I could be wrong by a large margin in either direction.
quotes.m: My current personal best guess is that they are in the same ballpark as GiveDirectly, but I could be wrong by a large margin in either direction.
quotes.sum: The author cautiously compares a sexual-violence prevention charity's impact to direct cash transfers, stressing major uncertainty.
quotes.t: Women's Empowerment: Founders Pledge report and recommendations

quotes.c: The article got minimal attention on social media, and I'm probably making conservatives feel worse about EA overall by bringing it to their attention. And it probably seems weird that I've spent so much time and effort analyzing a relatively unnoticed op-ed from a journalist. But I think it's important to set a clear early example for what sorts of behaviors are considered good or bad, and to build trust that some of us are monitoring this stuff and holding it to serious epistemic standards.
quotes.m: I think it's important to set a clear early example for what sorts of behaviors are considered good or bad, and to build trust that some of us are monitoring this stuff and holding it to serious epistemic standards.
quotes.sum: The author says publicly scrutinizing a journalist's small op-ed helps set community norms and show that EA holds public commentary to rigorous standards.
quotes.t: Response to a Dylan Matthews article on Vox about bipartisanship

quotes.c: If we include outcomes of infinite utility, the situation becomes more straightforward: The best action in any given situation will be the one that has the highest probability of causing an infinite reward. I predict this will not vindicate ordinary judgments about what we should do, at least not those ordinary judgments made by non-religious people.
quotes.m: The best action in any given situation will be the one that has the highest probability of causing an infinite reward.
quotes.sum: Including infinite rewards in moral calculations would make even tiny chances of them dominate what people ought to do.
quotes.t: Tiny Probabilities of Vast Utilities: Bibliography and Appendix

quotes.c: A proposed solution to possibly countering motivated reasoning is a checks and balances type of system; a system in which a committee of non-partisan individuals could proctor whether a decision made by an institution was influenced by motivated reasoning. The members of this committee obviously need to be well versed in the issues(s) pertaining to the institution’s decision, and they should not be beholden to any special interest groups. The non-partisan nature of the committee would ensure that there is no bias in proctoring the institution’s decision.
quotes.sum: The author proposes an independent, nonpartisan expert committee to check whether institutional decisions are distorted by motivated reasoning.
quotes.t: A Checks and Balances Approach to Improving Institutional Decision-Making

quotes.c: My hypothesis that GPT-4 already is agentic and is trying to take over the world! has been met with "skepticism" to put it lightly. I think part of this may be a misunderstanding about what agency and goal-directedness is. Let me give a more vivid model about what kind of world I'm talking about.
quotes.m: My hypothesis that GPT-4 already is agentic and is trying to take over the world!
quotes.sum: The author argues that GPT-4 may already be an agent with a goal of taking over the world, and says skeptics misunderstand agency.
quotes.t: Imagine a world where Microsoft employees used Bing

quotes.c: In summary, I think that for most results I’ve seen it’s unclear whether they apply in any real-world situation, or even how one would go about verifying that they do. In particular, we cannot conclude anything about actual funding decisions faced by EAs, hence conclusions 1. and 2. follow.
quotes.m: we cannot conclude anything about actual funding decisions faced by EAs
quotes.sum: The author argues that the research on random allocation is too detached from real cases to guide effective altruist funding decisions.
quotes.t: When should EAs allocate funding randomly? An inconclusive literature review.

quotes.c: Since it seems that we can't reasonably avoid causing insect suffering, does this mean insect suffering is not a moral concern? Clearly that's not the right conclusion as we would eliminate insect suffering if we could. It appears then that we are in a situation where we can't avoid causing harm, but we might be able to be proactive and reduce harm through other means.
quotes.m: Clearly that's not the right conclusion as we would eliminate insect suffering if we could.
quotes.sum: Argues that unavoidable harm to insects does not make their suffering morally irrelevant, and that people should seek ways to reduce it.
quotes.t: Wild Animal Welfare Literature Library: Original Research and Cause Prioritization

quotes.c: Strong version: development of AGI will make humans the second most intelligent species on the planet. Given that it was our intelligence which allowed us to control the world to the large extent that we do, we should expect that entities which are much more intelligent than us will end up controlling our future, unless there are reliable and feasible ways to prevent it. So far we have not discovered any.
quotes.m: we should expect that entities which are much more intelligent than us will end up controlling our future, unless there are reliable and feasible ways to prevent it.
quotes.sum: The author argues that if humans create much smarter AI, it will likely control humanity's future unless reliable prevention methods are found.
quotes.t: Disentangling arguments for the importance of AI safety

quotes.c: I also believe that invertebrate sentience research may be promising if you accept the overwhelming importance of the far future. This is because invertebrate sentience research may be applicable to the question of digital sentience. There may be many simple, potentially conscious, digital minds in the future, and understanding if they are conscious seems important so that we can avoid creating a lot of suffering and create a lot of happiness.
quotes.m: There may be many simple, potentially conscious, digital minds in the future, and understanding if they are conscious seems important so that we can avoid creating a lot of suffering and create a lot of happiness.
quotes.sum: The author says studying invertebrate consciousness could help identify conscious digital minds and prevent large-scale future suffering.
quotes.t: Why I'm focusing on invertebrate sentience

quotes.c: There are some ways that effective altruist norms have evolved that may make conservatives uncomfortable but that we wouldn’t necessarily want to change. For example, effective altruist communities typically request that people use trans people’s preferred pronouns. Many conservatives (and some liberals) are uncomfortable using trans people’s preferred pronouns, and this norm may make them feel unwelcome. However, I think that using trans people’s preferred pronouns is in fact a relatively low-cost way to make trans people much happier and I do not think the effective altruist community should shift to a different set of norms in order to welcome conservatives.
quotes.m: I do not think the effective altruist community should shift to a different set of norms in order to welcome conservatives.
quotes.sum: The author favors welcoming conservatives through careful, honest discussion, but says the community should retain norms such as respecting trans people’s pronouns.
quotes.t: How Effective Altruists Can Be Welcoming To Conservatives

quotes.c: In particular, I claim that policy discussions tend to follow strong contextualizing norms. I think this is partly for bad reasons (people in politics avoid decoupled statements because they're easier to criticise) and partly for good reasons.
quotes.m: people in politics avoid decoupled statements because they're easier to criticise
quotes.sum: Policy debate usually demands context; this can reflect both fear of criticism and legitimate reasons for avoiding isolated claims.
quotes.t: Policy discussions follow strong contextualizing norms

quotes.c: When I think about wild animal suffering, this, to me, feel like not the most tractable lever to be pulling on. I think that potentially they could be framing it around fairness and equality that a rights-based view would find appealing. I think that you could frame things in terms of, you know, under current conditions, sudden rights are not being met, even though, animals, plausibly could have some, like, a right to animals to non-interference, because their rights are not being met under current conditions.
quotes.m: animals, plausibly could have some, like, a right to animals to non-interference
quotes.sum: The speaker suggests framing concern for wild-animal suffering as a matter of fairness, equality, and possible animal rights against interference.
quotes.t: Building Support for Wild Animal Suffering [Transcript]

quotes.c: A claim that I hear a lot in the animal space is that Wild animal suffering is such a huge scale problem that we should seriously consider working on it. Many people would suggest that Wild animal suffering is an issue with a much larger scale than something like vaccinations based on the pure number of beings affected. This claim is definitely true, since there are trillions of wild animals and only ~20 million people in need of any single vaccination. But if we look more closely at its limiting factors, I think this claim is pretty misleading.
quotes.m: But if we look more closely at its limiting factors, I think this claim is pretty misleading.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a problem affecting more beings is not necessarily the better cause to pursue; practical limiting factors matter more than raw scale.
quotes.t: Why we look at the limiting factor instead of the problem scale

quotes.c: It seems like in effective altruism circles there are only a few things as certain as death and taxes: the moral significance of shrimp, the fact that play pumps should be burned for fuel, and the orthogonality thesis. Here, I hope to challenge the growing consensus around the orthogonality thesis.
quotes.m: Here, I hope to challenge the growing consensus around the orthogonality thesis.
quotes.sum: The author argues that effective altruists treat the AI orthogonality thesis as too unquestionable and intends to challenge that consensus.
quotes.t: The Orthogonality Thesis is Not Obviously True

quotes.c: The printing press ultimately helped amplify the theological conflict that led to over a century of religious wars; evidently, 16th-century Europe found it very difficult to adapt to a new ability for ideas to spread. The Internet has certainly created some social turmoil, and we’re only about 30 years into it, but so far I think its negative impact is on track to be less than a hundred years of war engulfing a continent.
quotes.m: 16th-century Europe found it very difficult to adapt to a new ability for ideas to spread.
quotes.sum: The author argues that societies can struggle badly to adapt when communications technology suddenly spreads ideas faster.
quotes.t: Do we get better or worse at adapting to change?

quotes.c: If the losses from evolutionary pressure indeed loom large, it seems quite likely that future generations would coordinate against it, e.g. by forming a singleton (Bostrom, 2006) (which broadly encompasses many forms of global coordination or value/goal-preservation). (Of course, there are also future scenarios that would strip away all other-regarding preferences, e.g. in Malthusian scenarios .)
quotes.m: future generations would coordinate against it, e.g. by forming a singleton
quotes.sum: The author argues that reducing extinction risk has positive expected value and suggests future people may use global coordination to preserve shared values against evolutionary pressures.
quotes.t: The expected value of extinction risk reduction is positive

quotes.c: A well-known objection to EA claims that many people care more for their close circle than the rest of the world. It seems to conflate two types of care. One type regards moral patienthood and often is meant to imply some form of responsibility. The other is the practical question of “who do I invest my relationship time in?”.
quotes.m: It seems to conflate two types of care.
quotes.sum: The author argues that moral concern for everyone is different from deciding whom to spend personal relationship time on.
quotes.t: Better models for EA development: a network of communities, not a global community

quotes.c: Furthermore, 69% of Americans appear to support a six-month pause in "some kinds of AI development" . Note that there doesn't seem to be a clear effect of age or race for this question. (Particularly if you lump "strongly support" and "somewhat support" into the same bucket).
