Note also that the question mentions that 1000 tech leaders signed an open letter calling for a pause and cites their concern over "profound risks to society and humanity", which may have influenced participants' responses.
quotes.m: 69% of Americans appear to support a six-month pause in "some kinds of AI development" .
quotes.sum: The author reports that a survey found broad US support for a temporary pause in some AI development, while noting wording may have influenced answers.
quotes.t: New survey: 46% of Americans are concerned about extinction from AI; 69% support a six-month pause in AI development

quotes.c: Today, we are the only species able to develop complex tools and technology. We have used this advantage to shape Earth according to our requirements and whims, largely ignoring the needs of other life forms, causing a mass extinction and environmental damage that threatens even our own future. We should expect that a misaligned superintelligent AI singleton would treat us in a similar way after it has destroyed or taken over all its rivals.
quotes.m: We should expect that a misaligned superintelligent AI singleton would treat us in a similar way after it has destroyed or taken over all its rivals.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a dominant misaligned superintelligent AI may eliminate rivals and treat humanity as humans have treated weaker species.
quotes.t: Paths to failure

quotes.c: Of course, existential risks create victims: the final generation of existing people would be harmed and would not like the extinction. But this number of people in the last generation will be relatively small compared to the many generations of many wild animals who can suffer. So if the status of victimhood is especially bad, wild animal suffering gets worse than existential risks, because the problem of wild animal suffering creates more victims.
quotes.m: wild animal suffering gets worse than existential risks, because the problem of wild animal suffering creates more victims.
quotes.sum: It argues that the enormous number of suffering wild animals may make their welfare a higher priority than preventing human extinction.
quotes.t: Reducing existential risks or wild animal suffering?

quotes.c: At first glance, playing legal moves in Othello (not even playing good moves!) has nothing to do with language models, and I think this is a strong claim worth justifying. Can working on toy tasks like Othello-GPT really help us to reverse-engineer LLMs like GPT-4? I'm not sure! But I think it's a plausible bet worth making.
quotes.m: Can working on toy tasks like Othello-GPT really help us to reverse-engineer LLMs like GPT-4? I'm not sure! But I think it's a plausible bet worth making.
quotes.sum: The author argues that studying how a model learns Othello may reveal general principles useful for reverse-engineering large language models.
quotes.t: Othello-GPT: Future Work I Am Excited About

quotes.c: But whenever we want to make some measurement of optimization, we have a goal in mind to guide us. The reason we're interested in theorems about utility maximization is because we want stuff, and we want to figure out how to best get it. We are optimization processes, and so we want to figure out how to best steer the future.
quotes.m: We are optimization processes, and so we want to figure out how to best steer the future.
quotes.sum: The author says that studying optimization is ultimately about understanding how agents can pursue goals and steer future outcomes.
quotes.t: Draft: Detecting optimization

quotes.c: In short, "The utilitarian imperative 'Maximize expected aggregate utility!'" might not really, as Bostrom (2002) puts it, "be simplified to the maxim 'Minimize existential risk'". It may not be enough to do our best to save the world. We may also have to consider which world gets saved.
quotes.m: We may also have to consider which world gets saved.
quotes.sum: Reducing extinction risk is not enough; the value of survival depends on what kind of future world survives.
quotes.t: Which World Gets Saved

quotes.c: So, I will be reasoning qualitatively for the case for long-termism, the case from long-termism to moral circle expansion and the case from moral circle expansion to personhood initiatives.
quotes.m: the case from moral circle expansion to personhood initiatives.
quotes.sum: The author plans to argue that long-term concern supports expanding moral concern and pursuing legal or social personhood initiatives.
quotes.t: Tyler John: Personhood initiatives

quotes.c: It's common knowledge in political sciences that the excessive concentration of power in single hands is both kind of natural for political systems without special instruments to restrict it, and also dangerous.
quotes.m: the excessive concentration of power in single hands is both kind of natural for political systems without special instruments to restrict it, and also dangerous.
quotes.sum: The author says political power naturally tends to concentrate unless institutions restrain it, and that this is dangerous.
quotes.t: How do we align humans and what does it mean for the new Conjecture's strategy

quotes.c: I've been torn for some time over the first question, slowly shifting towards hedonic utilitarianism as problems with formalising preferences piled up. While this isn't the right place to enumerate those problems ( see here for a previous relevant post ), I've now become persuaded that any precise definition of which preferences it is morally good to satisfy will lead to conclusions which I find unacceptable. After making this update, I can either reject a preference-based account of welfare entirely (in favour of a hedonic account), or else endorse a "vague" version of it which I think will never be specified precisely.
quotes.m: I've now become persuaded that any precise definition of which preferences it is morally good to satisfy will lead to conclusions which I find unacceptable.
quotes.sum: The author argues that no precise account of which preferences should be satisfied is morally acceptable, pushing him toward hedonic welfare or permanently vague ethics.
quotes.t: Arguments for moral indefinability

quotes.c: To move important future issues onto the political agenda, we propose that a cross-political network is established. Such a network would help create wide political support, which is key for both the achievability and sustainability of other institutions and mechanisms that we recommend should be developed and established later. It would also have positive ongoing impact on agenda-setting, aiding in ensuring that future issues remain a relevant topic of consideration.
quotes.m: It would also have positive ongoing impact on agenda-setting, aiding in ensuring that future issues remain a relevant topic of consideration.
quotes.sum: The author proposes a cross-party network to keep the interests of future generations on the political agenda and build support for later institutions.
quotes.t: Representation for Future Generations in Sweden – a summary of our work so far

quotes.c: Do the probabilities of the variables (e.g., scope, intensity, moral weight, criterion for "well-being" or "moral patienthood", etc.) we assign in our model of the problem make it competitive with existing causes in effective altruism?
quotes.m: Do the probabilities of the variables (e.g., scope, intensity, moral weight, criterion for "well-being" or "moral patienthood", etc.) we assign in our model of the problem make it competitive with existing causes in effective altruism?
quotes.sum: The author asks whether a cause should compete for funding based on uncertain estimates of its scale, severity, and moral importance.
quotes.t: Effective Altruism as Global Catastrophe Mitigation

quotes.c: Books, and ideas, have occasionally changed specific human beings, and thereby history. (I think.)
quotes.m: Books, and ideas, have occasionally changed specific human beings, and thereby history.
quotes.sum: The author suggests that books and ideas can shape particular people and, through them, alter history.
quotes.t: Are there specific books that it might slightly help alignment to have on the internet?

quotes.c: But I would like to see a broader variety of different types of people in the community. Because I think there are people who are more intuitive thinkers who wouldn't want to sit around at a party debating whether the parameter for the moral weight of chickens is 1% or 0.01%, and what anthropics might have to do with that.
quotes.m: the parameter for the moral weight of chickens is 1% or 0.01%
quotes.sum: He says the community should include more intuitive people, not only people who debate precise numerical moral weights for chickens.
quotes.t: Holden Karnofsky: Fireside chat (2018)

quotes.c: Aligned AGI could be the most incredible tool for human wellbeing! Heck yeah, a superintelligence that eliminates suffering but, like, in a really cool aligned way (seems like the most defining feature of "the long reflection" isn't a lack of existential risk, but rather this superintelligence assisting us).
quotes.m: a superintelligence that eliminates suffering but, like, in a really cool aligned way
quotes.sum: The author hopes aligned superintelligence could help humanity eliminate suffering and support a long-term process of reflection.
quotes.t: Some of My Current Impressions Entering AI Safety

quotes.c: Think about what you'd do if things surface that make you concerned about someone's safety. E.g. Julia once participated in a similar session in a different community where a person disclosed that they were essentially stalking someone. No one in the group really knew what to do. In retrospect I think we should have had someone with designated responsibility for following up, along the lines of, "I hear what a tough time you're going through, but the way you're treating this other person sounds really concerning."
quotes.m: In retrospect I think we should have had someone with designated responsibility for following up
quotes.sum: EA group self-care sessions should assign someone to follow up when disclosures raise concerns about another person's safety.
quotes.t: Self-care sessions for EA groups

quotes.c: Preliminary conclusion: In the foreseeable future it is likely that a superintelligent agent will be created which will capture the cosmic endowment and put it to uses incongruent with our values. (I call this the AI Doom Scenario).
quotes.m: In the foreseeable future it is likely that a superintelligent agent will be created which will capture the cosmic endowment and put it to uses incongruent with our values.
quotes.sum: The author argues that a future superintelligence may seize all accessible resources and permanently use them in ways contrary to human values.
quotes.t: Critique of Superintelligence Part 1

quotes.c: Keiran Harris: No, I think it’s likely that that would be bad, and that we ought to explore whether or not that’s actually likely and look at these previous examples of nuclear stockpile production, climate change, and try and investigate what actually happened there. How did they become partisan issues? Where it’s not obvious that they ever should’ve become partisan, and how we can try and avoid that for questions moving forward.
quotes.m: How did they become partisan issues? Where it’s not obvious that they ever should’ve become partisan, and how we can try and avoid that for questions moving forward.
quotes.sum: The speaker argues that long-term risks should be studied as past nonpartisan issues became polarized, so future causes can avoid the same fate.
quotes.t: EA/X-risk/AI Alignment Coverage in Journalism

quotes.c: Some guests might appreciate having companion animals around (e.g. cats or dogs), for comfort, stress relief, or maybe even to help viscerally expand their moral circle of concern. The down sides are feeding them non-vegan diets, increasing wild animal suffering (e.g. cats catching birds) and food hygiene issues (e.g. dogs eating human food in kitchen). On balance I think the default of no non-human animals might be best, but if many guests want to live with one, and there are no strong objections from other guests, then it’s a possibility.
quotes.m: On balance I think the default of no non-human animals might be best
quotes.sum: The author argues that an EA communal residence should generally avoid pets because of vegan, wild-animal-welfare, and hygiene concerns.
quotes.t: EA Hotel with free accommodation and board for two years

quotes.c: In short: the failures of democracy in the 30’s were based on large populations of young men who could be mobilised in anger by militaristic leaders - see for instance the brownshirts in Germany and blackshirts in Italy. But that’s not what the failure of democracy in our time would look like, because that group of people is much smaller now. For better or worse, older populations are less disruptive and more complacent. To see where that might lead, consider Japan: an ageing population which can’t drag itself out of economic torpor, resistant to immigration, dominated for decades by one political party, betting the country's future on using robots to replace the missing workforce.
quotes.m: For better or worse, older populations are less disruptive and more complacent.
quotes.sum: Modern democratic decline may look less like militant mass politics and more like an ageing, complacent society stuck under long-running one-party rule.
quotes.t: How democracy ends: a review and reevaluation

quotes.c: We might also be unsure about what the right way is to respond to uncertainty about the state of the world. So, whether we should maximize expected utility, as one decision theory would say, the most commonly accepted one. Or whether we should do something else, like be really risk averse and be min-max, or minimize the probability of the worst possible outcome.
quotes.m: whether we should maximize expected utility
quotes.sum: The speaker says uncertainty may require choosing between expected-utility maximization and more risk-averse decision rules.
quotes.t: Lightning talks from EA Global: San Francisco (2018)

quotes.c: It is still too early to say we should reconsider individual outreach. For one, it is hard to compare video to other individual outreach strategies -- or even non-outreach strategies for that matter -- given the lack of robust cost-effectiveness estimates for other areas. Also, it is possible that individual outreach may have important medium term effects and/or fit into a broader holistic strategy.
quotes.m: It is still too early to say we should reconsider individual outreach.
quotes.sum: The author says it is too early to judge whether video-based diet advocacy is less cost-effective than other ways to help animals.
quotes.t: Animal Equality showed that advocating for diet change works. But is it cost-effective?

quotes.c: Arguably the most important topic about which a prediction market has yet been run: Conditional on an okay outcome with AGI, how did that happen?
quotes.m: Conditional on an okay outcome with AGI, how did that happen?
quotes.sum: The author calls understanding how an AGI outcome could go well an unusually important question for prediction markets.
quotes.t: Manifold:  If okay AGI, why?

quotes.c: Next, let's look at the "long-termist, nonhuman-inclusive" view. What we're interested in is whether a focus on wild animal suffering increases the expected value of the future of humanity, and also the value of nonhumans that exist. Space colonization may mean that future humans export and multiply wild animal suffering into the universe, and therefore increase the scale of the problem. A related but more obscure problem is that advancements in artificial intelligence might lead to digital simulations of nature, and if those simulations contain moral patients, then that might also increase the problem.
quotes.m: Space colonization may mean that future humans export and multiply wild animal suffering into the universe, and therefore increase the scale of the problem.
quotes.sum: The author argues that wild-animal suffering may deserve priority, including because space settlement and AI simulations could multiply nonhuman suffering on a vast scale.
quotes.t: Persis Eskander: Crucial considerations in wild animal suffering

quotes.c: Stable totalitarianism: enabling a small group of people to obtain and maintain unprecedented levels of power; especially risky in the context of digital people
quotes.m: enabling a small group of people to obtain and maintain unprecedented levels of power
quotes.sum: It identifies durable totalitarian rule by a small group as an AGI-related catastrophe, especially if digital people exist.
quotes.t: Non-loss of control AGI-related catastrophes are out of control too

quotes.c: An aside: None of this danger depends on whether or not AIs are or can be conscious; it’s intrinsic to the notion of powerful cognitive systems that optimize hard and calculate outputs that meet sufficiently complicated outcome criteria. With that said, I’d be remiss in my moral duties as a human if I didn’t also mention that we have no idea how to determine whether AI systems are aware of themselves—since we have no idea how to decode anything that goes on in the giant inscrutable arrays—and therefore we may at some point inadvertently create digital minds which are truly conscious and ought to have rights and shouldn’t be owned.
quotes.m: we may at some point inadvertently create digital minds which are truly conscious and ought to have rights and shouldn’t be owned.
quotes.sum: AI danger does not require consciousness, but potentially conscious AI systems may deserve rights and must not be treated as property.
quotes.t: Pausing AI Developments Isn't Enough. We Need to Shut it All Down

quotes.c: It is not clear for how long we should continue to consider benefits, since the benefits of vaccines would potentially continue indefinitely for hundreds of years. Perhaps these benefits would eventually be offset by some other future technology, and we could try to model that. Or perhaps we should consider a discount rate into the future, though we don’t find that idea appealing.
quotes.m: Or perhaps we should consider a discount rate into the future, though we don’t find that idea appealing.
quotes.sum: The author argues that vaccine benefits may last for centuries and says discounting those future benefits is unappealing, while acknowledging the uncertainty.
quotes.t: Cost-Effectiveness of Vaccines: Exploring Model Uncertainty and Takeaways

quotes.c: Moreover, the idea that AI systems could pose an existential threat to humanity is based on a flawed understanding of the technology. While some experts have speculated about the potential for superintelligent AI systems to take over the world and harm humans, there is little evidence to support such claims. In fact, many experts believe that the development of superintelligent AI systems is unlikely, and that even if they were to be developed, they would likely be programmed with ethical considerations and constraints to prevent harm to humans.
quotes.m: the idea that AI systems could pose an existential threat to humanity is based on a flawed understanding of the technology.
quotes.sum: The author argues that fears of AI causing human extinction rest on a flawed view of the technology and lack evidence.
quotes.t: Arguing all sides with ChatGPT

quotes.c: Obviously, the AI’s goal should be set so it has no incentive to change the human’s goals to make them easier to optimize. Perhaps its goal at time t is to maximize expected utility of whatever U H is at time t .
quotes.m: the AI’s goal should be set so it has no incentive to change the human’s goals to make them easier to optimize.
quotes.sum: The author argues that an AI should optimize humans' current values without gaining an incentive to alter those values for convenience.
quotes.t: A sketch of a value-learning sovereign

quotes.c: To avoid this issue of trying to second-guess which route to takeover AI will attempt, I think humans should sample both X-tasks and Y-tasks such that the AI is equally likely to get caught whichever route it tries. I.e. sample such that pr(we catch AI| AI sabotages 5% of X-tasks) = pr(we catch AI| AI sabotages 10% of Y-tasks). This is optimising for the worst-case scenario.
quotes.m: This is optimising for the worst-case scenario.
quotes.sum: Humans should distribute oversight across different AI tasks so sabotage is equally likely to be caught regardless of the route an AI takes.
quotes.t: Which AI outputs should humans check for shenanigans, to avoid AI takeover? A simple model

quotes.c: When making direct estimates using inputs from Fenner, et al. (1988) , by our estimation before the eradication campaign in the early 1960s, smallpox prevented a DALY from death for ~$20-64 in developing countries and ~$1550-3800 in developed countries. Weighting this by population in each region, this implies a total cost per DALY of $527 for both roll-out costs alone and roll-out costs plus R&D costs.
quotes.m: this implies a total cost per DALY of $527 for both roll-out costs alone and roll-out costs plus R&D costs.
quotes.sum: The author estimates that smallpox vaccination and eradication produced health gains at a very low cost per disability-adjusted life year saved.
quotes.t: What is the cost-effectiveness of researching vaccines?

quotes.c: There are people who are self aware enough, intelligent enough, practiced enough, or healed enough, who can stand their ground calmly and argue their points. Most people are not like this. And unfortunately, I believe many many of the people who voted for Trump have been traumatized since a very early age for many different reasons.
quotes.m: I believe many many of the people who voted for Trump have been traumatized since a very early age for many different reasons.
quotes.sum: The author argues that most people cannot calmly defend their views and speculates that many Trump voters were shaped by early trauma.
quotes.t: Meme or Die: Modern Societies are Dependent on Emotionally Rich Memes to Rapidly Evolve

quotes.c: However, while our research would suggest that while some vaccines we covered were extremely cost-effective, and other vaccines currently in development have the potential to be so—consistent with hits-based giving—overall this basket of vaccines wasn’t clearly superior to other possible health interventions currently available to donors, with our estimate suggesting some vaccines may be orders magnitude worse than donating to the Against Malaria Foundation (AMF).
quotes.m: overall this basket of vaccines wasn’t clearly superior to other possible health interventions currently available to donors
quotes.sum: The author says vaccine research can be highly cost-effective, but this group of vaccine investments did not clearly beat other health options and may be far worse than malaria prevention.
quotes.t: Lessons for estimating cost-effectiveness (of vaccines) more effectively

quotes.c: In this short post I outline a very simple (new?) way of estimating the expected value of systemic changes when you are very uncertain of how much they'd cost. It seems to have the result of making systemic changes look much more viable than they otherwise would.
quotes.m: It seems to have the result of making systemic changes look much more viable than they otherwise would.
quotes.sum: The author proposes an expected-value method that makes systemic change appear more worthwhile under cost uncertainty.
quotes.t: Could I have some more systemic change, please, sir?

quotes.c: As we move towards more complex animals, we start to see more clearly relevant pain. More than that, the pain seems to have increasing moral weight. Temple Grandin and Catherine Johnson argue in "Animals in Translation" that (some) animals feel fear, and this seems to match our (potentially unreliable) intuition that higher mammals that can plan and reason about the future also can anticipate fear. In a very real sense, they suffer more than adult humans, because they have almost no control over their environment.
quotes.m: In a very real sense, they suffer more than adult humans, because they have almost no control over their environment.
quotes.sum: The author argues that more cognitively complex animals may have pain with greater moral weight and can suffer more than adult humans due to their lack of control.
quotes.t: Is Suffering Convex?

quotes.c: There are already several people going down this path, but we need a lot more expertise and connections. In the next few years, it seems useful for up to 10-20 people in the community to develop significant expertise across the relevant topics.
quotes.m: In the next few years, it seems useful for up to 10-20 people in the community to develop significant expertise across the relevant topics.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the community should train 10–20 more people with expertise and connections relevant to China.
quotes.t: New recommended career path for effective altruists: China specialists

quotes.c: When people talk about mesa-optimization, they sometimes say things like “we’re searching for the optimizer module” or “we’re doing interpretability to find out whether the network can do internal search”. An uncharitable interpretation of these claims is that the researchers expect the network to have something like an “optimization module” or “internal search algorithm” that is clearly different and distinguishable from the rest of the network (to be clear, we think it is fine to start with probably wrong mechanistic models ).
quotes.sum: The authors argue that current neural networks can meaningfully perform internal optimization, even without a distinct, identifiable optimizer module.
quotes.t: Clarifying mesa-optimization

quotes.c: Abraham : Yeah. I don't know if I agree about there not being viable interventions right now but I definitely agree that social change is the way to go with many animal advocates. I think part of the reason is one of the best ways to sort of ensure that we might do something about wild animal suffering in the future is just, instilling broader values of compassion for animals in people and I think the group of people who does that really well is often the farmed animal advocacy movement.
quotes.m: one of the best ways to sort of ensure that we might do something about wild animal suffering in the future is just, instilling broader values of compassion for animals in people
quotes.sum: The speakers argue that expanding compassion for farmed animals can build a social movement able to address wild-animal suffering later.
quotes.t: Ozy Brennan, Kieran Greig, and Abraham Rowe: Building support for wild animal suffering

quotes.c: I felt less convinced than the report’s author that CHAI had clearly been crucial to the final stage of price drops, given the extent of price reduction that had already occurred prior to CHAI’s involvement, but would guess that it at least sped up the reduction.
quotes.sum: The author cautiously argues that a health charity may have accelerated HIV drug price declines, but was not clearly their main cause.
quotes.t: History of Philanthropy Case Study: Clinton Health Access Initiative’s Role in Global Price Drops for Antiretroviral Drugs

quotes.c: Something I've been thinking a bit about lately is that it's possible that humanity's moral circle mostly includes humans, most of us more or less, and then it kind of goes gray out into like, okay we care quite a bit about dogs and cats in the US, we care a little bit about pigs and chickens right now. At least we don't like factory farming. We don't really care about insects, we don't really care about digital minds yet, so they're further away from the moral circle.
quotes.m: We don't really care about insects, we don't really care about digital minds yet, so they're further away from the moral circle.
quotes.sum: The speaker describes moral concern as extending unevenly from humans to pets, farm animals, insects, and potentially digital minds.
quotes.t: Kelly Witwicki and Kieran Greig: Animal advocacy strategies — technology vs. social change

quotes.c: I also notice this continued concern for what this paper calls an “AI divide” where AI is unavailable to many. It seems to me like this is already essentially falsified. You might complain the AI you can access is too restricted or ‘too woke’ or something, but it does not look like AIs are going to be expensive unless you are doing something very intense.
quotes.m: It seems to me like this is already essentially falsified.
quotes.sum: The author argues that fears of an AI access gap are already disproven because ordinary AI access will likely be cheap.
quotes.t: Microsoft Research Paper Claims Sparks of Artificial Intelligence in GPT-4

quotes.c: In our historical sample, the rollout cost of a vaccine ranged between $0.73 to $160 per child vaccinated, and this is even before taking into account other large sources of variation, such as level of pre-existing infrastructure and remoteness of region. Furthermore, the price, particularly in lower and middle income countries, depends somewhat on the negotiation of large groups, NGOs and governments and as such it’s difficult to generalize these estimate to future prices.
quotes.m: the rollout cost of a vaccine ranged between $0.73 to $160 per child vaccinated
quotes.sum: Vaccine delivery costs vary enormously by setting, infrastructure, and negotiations, so past estimates cannot be easily generalized.
quotes.t: How much does it cost to roll-out a vaccine?

quotes.c: I think when I look at all the problems that we're most interested in, the paths to impact often do look research driven, egghead-y, technocratic. So I think we shouldn't change our cause selection or views about what is a good solution in response to what is ultimately a social criticism about being elitist.
quotes.m: we shouldn't change our cause selection or views about what is a good solution in response to what is ultimately a social criticism about being elitist.
quotes.sum: He argues that effective causes often require technocratic research and should not be abandoned merely because this looks elitist.
quotes.t: Nick Beckstead: Fireside chat (2018)

quotes.c: As noted in 2015, it has been suggested that greater efforts should be made on the part of EA to be more inclusive of religious groups. The numbers definitely still show room for growth in religious communities.
quotes.m: The numbers definitely still show room for growth in religious communities.
quotes.sum: The author says the EA community should make greater efforts to include religious people, where it has room to grow.
quotes.t: EA Survey 2017 Series: Community Demographics & Beliefs

quotes.c: The salvation algorithm will not be implementable by Evil AI in the opposite direction, i.e., to steal observers from paradise, if we assume either that a) Evil AIs can’t cooperate (maybe because they are evil for different reasons) OR b) all Evil AIs have world shares that are millions of times smaller than the share of collaborating Benevolent AIs. Even if an Evil AI steals some observers from paradise, the Benevolent AI could regain these observers via its salvation algorithm in just nearly-immediately.
quotes.m: Even if an Evil AI steals some observers from paradise, the Benevolent AI could regain these observers via its salvation algorithm in just nearly-immediately.
quotes.sum: It proposes that sufficiently powerful “Benevolent AIs” could rescue suffering observers into paradise faster than rival evil AIs could reclaim them.
quotes.t: Curing past sufferings and preventing s-risks via indexical uncertainty

quotes.c: When an intervention has more cross-cutting benefits, then this scheme breaks down quickly – moral circle expansion, for example, can be beneficial in how it influences futures without singleton and in how it influences what singleton emerges, but the latter benefits are counted only in the “influencing the singleton” section. I think the usefulness of this section doesn’t go much beyond a mere brainstorming.
quotes.m: moral circle expansion, for example, can be beneficial in how it influences futures without singleton and in how it influences what singleton emerges
quotes.sum: The author says their cause-prioritization framework struggles to account for interventions with overlapping long-term effects, such as expanding moral concern.
quotes.t: Current Thinking on Prioritization 2018

quotes.c: Instead, I think that efforts to expand effective altruism into other languages should initially focus on person-to-person outreach to a small number of people with key expertise.
quotes.m: efforts to expand effective altruism into other languages should initially focus on person-to-person outreach to a small number of people with key expertise.
quotes.sum: The author argues that translating and promoting EA should be delayed in culturally different countries and initially spread through a small number of experts.
quotes.t: Why not to rush to translate effective altruism into other languages

quotes.c: Properly including AIs in the moral circle could improve human-AI relations, reduce human-AI conflict, and reduce the likelihood of human extinction from rogue AI. Moral circle expansion to include the interests of digital minds may be necessary for AI alignment because of the inherent challenges in aligning the goals of systems that have an exclusionary relationship with each other such as oppression, abuse, cruelty, or slavery.
quotes.m: Moral circle expansion to include the interests of digital minds may be necessary for AI alignment
quotes.sum: The author argues that giving digital minds moral consideration may be necessary for aligning AI and avoiding conflict or extinction.
quotes.t: Key Questions for Digital Minds

quotes.c: What if I claim that if we encountered Robin Hanson’s grabby aliens tomorrow, as unlikely as that is statistically, and they didn’t care about us or go galaxy brained on acausal trade or something, we would all be super duper dead, and at a minimum we are not going to be getting much of that cosmic endowment?
quotes.m: we would all be super duper dead, and at a minimum we are not going to be getting much of that cosmic endowment?
quotes.sum: The author argues that an encounter with expansionist aliens would likely kill humanity and deprive it of the universe’s future resources.
quotes.t: Response to Tyler Cowen’s Existential risk, AI, and the inevitable turn in human history

quotes.c: I note that the case for long-termism has largely been brought to our attention via the effective altruism community, which has emphasized similar points in the past. [12] I think the case for this sort of giving is initially unintuitive relative to e.g. focusing on global health, but I think it’s quite strong, and that gives some illustration of the value of effective altruism itself as an intellectual framework and community.
quotes.m: I think the case for this sort of giving is initially unintuitive relative to e.g. focusing on global health, but I think it’s quite strong
quotes.sum: Karnofsky says the initially counterintuitive case for funding long-term-focused work rather than global health is strong, and credits EA for highlighting it.
quotes.t: Update on Cause Prioritization at Open Philanthropy

quotes.c: There are eight current vaccine candidates for Ebola being tested ( Wikipedia ). Merck has a vaccine, originally developed by the Canadian government, that has undergone a Phase III trial which demonstrated efficacy above 60% but that trial had several limitations and has not yet been licensed ( GEN news, 2014 ; Palmer, 2015 ; Henao-Restrepo et al., 2017 ; NAP, 2017 ). Several parallel vaccines are in different stages of development ( Pavot, 2016 ). Total spending by GAVI, international governments, and pharmaceutical companies on vaccine development has been around $1.5B depending on accounting [7] .
quotes.m: Total spending by GAVI, international governments, and pharmaceutical companies on vaccine development has been around $1.5B depending on accounting [7] .
quotes.sum: Ebola vaccine development has involved several candidates and roughly $1.5 billion in combined public, charitable, and industry spending.
quotes.t: How much does it cost to research and develop a vaccine?

quotes.c: But I think a more likely outcome is one in which multiple people with early access to the models end up fighting over resources. Maybe by some miracle the winner of that process will be a reasonably benevolent dictator, but such competitive dynamics optimize for willingness to do whatever it takes to win. History suggests such traits are not well correlated (or perhaps even negatively correlated) with a general concern for human well-being.
quotes.m: such competitive dynamics optimize for willingness to do whatever it takes to win.
quotes.sum: The author argues that competition among people with early access to AGI is more likely to reward ruthless winners than people concerned with human welfare.
quotes.t: The default outcome for aligned AGI still looks pretty bad

quotes.c: I think that progress in animal welfare is bottlenecked by more fundamental-level research as to what interventions are worth prioritizing, rather than the organizational-level research that Animal Charity Evaluators is most known for (though ACE has recently expanded their fundamental-level research work by launching an experimental research division and greatly expanding their review of leafleting ). I could see research from Sentience Institute potentially helping surface considerations that help prioritize better within the animal welfare space.
quotes.sum: Animal welfare progress depends more on basic research into which interventions matter most than on evaluating existing organizations.
quotes.t: Four Organizations EAs Should Fully Fund for 2018

quotes.c: I think it’s both the case that corporations do in fact have a level of rights that would be sufficient to run the risk argument so that if the outcome is the same as corporations, that would be sufficient to be concerned, but I also think that corporations are both … yeah, they do bottom out with people in a way that these entities wouldn’t, and that’s one of the main problems, and also they’re just not able to make persuasive arguments.
quotes.m: they do bottom out with people in a way that these entities wouldn’t, and that’s one of the main problems
quotes.sum: The speaker argues that AI-like entities may deserve concern as moral patients, especially because unlike corporations they would not ultimately represent human interests.
quotes.t: Paul Christiano on how OpenAI is developing real solutions to the 'AI alignment problem', and his vision of how humanity will progressively hand over decision-making to AI systems

quotes.c: Eliciting honest behavior in this context means developing techniques to extract AI systems' "beliefs", to the extent that they are well-described as having them. In other words, honest models should, if they have an internal world model, accurately report predictions or features of that world model. Incentivizing honesty in AI systems seems important in order to avoid and detect deceptive behavior.
quotes.m: honest models should, if they have an internal world model, accurately report predictions or features of that world model.
quotes.sum: AI systems should truthfully report what their internal models predict, helping detect deception and support alignment research.
quotes.t: A tension between two prosaic alignment subgoals

quotes.c: My proposal is to develop and run an additional campaign office, comprised of four members of the Effective Altruist community (myself included) to provide support to the CCIC campaign. I believe bringing Effective Altruists together for this project will have additional benefits beyond this campaign.
quotes.m: My proposal is to develop and run an additional campaign office, comprised of four members of the Effective Altruist community (myself included) to provide support to the CCIC campaign.
quotes.sum: The author proposes an EA-staffed office to support a campaign seeking increased Canadian development assistance.
quotes.t: Funding Proposal: Supporting a Campaign to Increase Canadian Official Development Assistance

quotes.c: I think that you should consider going into biosecurity if you are an EA concerned with the far future, who wants to make sure that we all get to enjoy our amazing cosmic endowment, and if you think that you might be a good fit for work in policy or in the biomedical sciences.
quotes.m: EA concerned with the far future, who wants to make sure that we all get to enjoy our amazing cosmic endowment
quotes.sum: The author encourages long-term-focused EAs to work in biosecurity to protect humanity's future potential.
quotes.t: Claire Zabel: Biosecurity as an EA cause area

quotes.c: It seems easy enough to avoid the first failure mode; we just have to switch to output 2/3 if we cross some threshhold where 2/3 has been doing better. Adding the second failure mode makes this strategy stop working, because an evil environment could cause us to lock in to 2/3, and then switch to giving probability 1/3 forever.
quotes.m: an evil environment could cause us to lock in to 2/3, and then switch to giving probability 1/3 forever.
quotes.sum: A prediction strategy that follows its past success can be exploited by an environment that changes after the strategy commits.
quotes.t: Concise Open Problem in Logical Uncertainty

quotes.c: Value pluralism may possibly not have maximum sex appeal, but is the only solution for the world, it seems to me. I believe in a secular, Christian, ecological, social, liberal and democratic value pluralism and diversity/plurality enjoyment.
quotes.m: I believe in a secular, Christian, ecological, social, liberal and democratic value pluralism and diversity/plurality enjoyment.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the world needs a pluralistic value system combining secular, Christian, ecological, social, liberal, and democratic commitments.
quotes.t: Value Pluralism and AI

quotes.c: The second claim is one that I think is implied by the above quote, which is that we should favor more evidence, all else being equal. So, if the expected value of two interventions is similar, we should generally favor investing in interventions that have more evidence supporting them.
quotes.sum: The author argues that, when options seem similarly valuable, people should prefer interventions backed by stronger evidence.
quotes.t: Amanda Askell: The moral value of information

quotes.c: This consideration highlights why suffering-focused altruists should probably invest their resources not into making exceptionally good outcomes more likely, but rather into making dystopian outcomes (or dystopian elements in otherwise good outcomes) less likely. Utopian outcomes where all sources of significant suffering are abolished through technology and virtually all sentient beings get to enjoy lives filled with unprecedented heights of happiness are certainly something we should hope will happen. But from a downside-focused perspective, our own efforts to do good are, on the margin , better directed towards making it less likely that we get particularly bad futures.
quotes.m: But from a downside-focused perspective, our own efforts to do good are, on the margin , better directed towards making it less likely that we get particularly bad futures.
quotes.sum: It argues that people focused on reducing suffering should prioritize preventing very bad futures over increasing the chance of exceptionally happy ones.
quotes.t: Cause prioritization for downside-focused value systems

quotes.c: I think that you should consider going into biosecurity if you are an EA concerned with the far future, who wants to make sure that we all get to enjoy our amazing cosmic endowment, and if you think that you might be a good fit for work in policy or in the biomedical sciences.
quotes.m: I think that you should consider going into biosecurity if you are an EA concerned with the far future, who wants to make sure that we all get to enjoy our amazing cosmic endowment
quotes.sum: The author encourages far-future-focused EAs to pursue biosecurity work to protect humanity's long-term potential.
quotes.t: Biosecurity as an EA Cause Area

quotes.c: Please do limit your questions to the topics of the report, though: consciousness, moral patienthood, animal cognition, meta-ethics, moral weight, illusionism, hidden qualia, etc.
quotes.m: consciousness, moral patienthood, animal cognition, meta-ethics, moral weight
quotes.sum: The author invites discussion of consciousness, which beings matter morally, animal cognition, and how to weigh different interests.
quotes.t: Hi, I'm Luke Muehlhauser. AMA about Open Philanthropy's new report on consciousness and moral patienthood

quotes.c: Besides looking at literature, another potentially good way to learn how long it takes to make a vaccine is to use base rates and look at how long it took historically to make all of the past vaccines. This method, however, has a number of limitations. There is a surprising amount of uncertainty about the correct start year of each vaccine, since it is difficult to know what the beginning of a research actually is and the transition from "not researched" to "researched" is very gradual.
quotes.m: There is a surprising amount of uncertainty about the correct start year of each vaccine, since it is difficult to know what the beginning of a research actually is and the transition from "not researched" to "researched" is very gradual.
quotes.sum: Historical vaccine timelines can inform estimates, but research start dates are inherently difficult to define.
quotes.t: How long does it take to research and develop a new vaccine?

quotes.c: Seek medical care if you’re concerned that you or someone else isn’t doing well. This is the standard advice for a good reason, which is that things may get worse if you try to just wait it out. You may miss the opportunity for treatment that would have been helpful.
quotes.m: Seek medical care if you’re concerned that you or someone else isn’t doing well.
quotes.sum: The author urges seeking medical help promptly for possible mania or psychosis rather than waiting for it to pass.
quotes.t: Supporting someone experiencing mania or psychosis

quotes.c: Finally, you might be skeptical about our ability to make the future better in expectation, either because you think we might not have that kind of influence over the future or because we're just not in a position to know what will make the future better. I think that’s a real question. But surely at least some people are in a position to make the future better or worse, in expectation.
quotes.m: But surely at least some people are in a position to make the future better or worse, in expectation.
quotes.sum: The speaker argues that people can meaningfully affect whether the long-term future goes better or worse, despite uncertainty.
quotes.t: Orienting towards the long-term future (Joseph Carlsmith)

quotes.c: We can be anti-realists about suffering (suffering-is-a-node-in-the-network-of-language), or we can argue that we can talk coherently about suffering in novel contexts (AGIs, mind crime, aliens, and so on), but it seems inherently troublesome to claim we can do both at the same time.
quotes.m: We can be anti-realists about suffering (suffering-is-a-node-in-the-network-of-language), or we can argue that we can talk coherently about suffering in novel contexts (AGIs, mind crime, aliens, and so on), but it seems inherently troublesome to claim we can do both at the same time.
quotes.sum: The author argues that denying suffering is objectively real conflicts with extending concern about suffering to AGIs, aliens, or simulated minds.
quotes.t: Why I think the Foundational Research Institute should rethink its approach

quotes.c: The risks of unaligned-AGI are usually couched in terms of existential risk, whereby the outcome is explicitly or implicitly human extinction. However, given the nature of what an AGI would be able to do, it seems though there are plausible scenarios worse than human extinction. Just as on an individual level it is possible to imagine fates we would prefer death to (e.g. prolonged terminal illness or imprisonment), it is also possible to expand this to humanity as a whole, where we end up in hell-type fates.
quotes.m: it is also possible to expand this to humanity as a whole, where we end up in hell-type fates.
quotes.sum: Unaligned AI may create outcomes worse than human extinction, including humanity-wide conditions likened to hell.
quotes.t: How likely do you think worse-than-extinction type fates to be?

quotes.c: Here’s a suggestion that’s not so often discussed: our first priority should be to survive .
quotes.m: our first priority should be to survive
quotes.sum: Humanity's top priority should be ensuring civilization survives existential threats.
quotes.t: The case for reducing existential risk

quotes.c: In the long run, to make well-grounded decisions about how much we should value grants aimed at (e.g.) chicken or fish welfare, we need to form initial impressions not just about which creatures are more and less likely to be conscious, but also about (a) other plausible criteria for moral patienthood besides consciousness, and also about (b) the question of “ moral weight .” However, those two questions are beyond the scope of this initial report on consciousness.
quotes.m: we need to form initial impressions not just about which creatures are more and less likely to be conscious, but also about (a) other plausible criteria for moral patienthood besides consciousness, and also about (b) the question of “ moral weight .”
quotes.sum: The author says funding decisions on chicken and fish welfare require judging which animals are conscious and how much moral weight they have.
quotes.t: New Report on Consciousness and Moral Patienthood

quotes.c: I observe that many of the same people worry a lot about “What do you say to the Republican?” or the possibility that crackpots might try to cheat —like they’re trying above all to guard some valuable social resource from the possibility of theft. I observe that the notion of somebody being able to steal that resource and get away with it seems to inspire a special degree of horror, rather than just being one more case of somebody making a mistaken probability estimate.
quotes.m: the notion of somebody being able to steal that resource and get away with it seems to inspire a special degree of horror
quotes.sum: The author argues that worries about crackpots cheating may really be fears of people illegitimately gaining social status or credibility.
quotes.t: Status Regulation and Anxious Underconfidence

quotes.c: My perspective on openness is that, I mean, this is a boring answer. I think it's one of these strategic questions that like you can do a shallow analysis and say like, if you're worried about the risk of a small group of people taking a disproportionate chunk of influence and that that would be really bad, then maybe you want to be more open. If you're mostly worried about offense beating defense and only one hostile actor could cause immense harm, then you're probably gonna be more excited about closedness then openness.
quotes.m: If you're mostly worried about offense beating defense and only one hostile actor could cause immense harm, then you're probably gonna be more excited about closedness then openness.
quotes.sum: Openness in advanced AI should depend on whether concentration of power or catastrophic misuse by a hostile actor is the greater danger.
quotes.t: Daniel Dewey: The Open Philanthropy Project's work on potential risks from advanced AI

quotes.c: One can imagine the Reach Every Mother and Child Act might have passed last year if a few congressmen were more responsive in adjusting it to get past partisan objections (left wing opposing funding religious groups, right wing opposing funding contraception). That likely would have saved a few thousand lives, and possibly millions according to USAID.
quotes.m: That likely would have saved a few thousand lives, and possibly millions according to USAID.
quotes.sum: The author argues that political delay and partisan objections may have blocked a maternal and child health bill that could have saved many lives.
quotes.t: Ethical Reaction Time: What it is and why it matters

quotes.c: The main point of Scott Alexander’s “Meditations on Moloch” is essentially that “the only way to avoid having all human values gradually ground down by optimization-competition is to install a Gardener over the entire universe who optimizes for human values.” In other words, given the problems which have been described above, the only way to actually achieve a really valuable society is to have a singleton which has the right preferences and keeps everyone in line.
quotes.m: the only way to actually achieve a really valuable society is to have a singleton which has the right preferences and keeps everyone in line.
quotes.sum: The author presents a value-aligned superintelligent singleton governing everyone as the only route to a truly valuable society.
quotes.t: Utopia In The Fog

quotes.c: We all know that an extra dollar is worth more to you the poorer you are. That's why it can be good to donate money to an organisation like GiveDirectly even when a few cents in the dollar get used up in transaction costs. But how much more is it worth? Economists have a good quantitative model of what is going on, which can enable us to make rough comparisons about whether, say, people on $1,000 per year would get more value from an extra $100 than people on $2,000 per year would get from $200.
quotes.sum: Argues that the greater value of money to poorer people can justify paying extra costs to direct aid to the very poorest.
quotes.t: The value of money going to different groups

quotes.c: Surprisingly, in order to maximize expected utility, it might use ‘mission hedging’ investment principles and invest in fossil fuel stocks. This way it has more money to give to organisations that combat climate change when more fossil fuels are burned, fossil fuel stocks go up and climate change will get particularly bad. When fewer fossil fuels are burnt and fossil fuels stocks go down - the foundation will have less money, but it does not need the money as much.
quotes.m: Surprisingly, in order to maximize expected utility, it might use ‘mission hedging’ investment principles and invest in fossil fuel stocks.
quotes.sum: A climate foundation may maximize good by investing in fossil fuels, so it has more money to fight climate damage when that damage is worst.
quotes.t: A generalized strategy of ‘mission hedging’: investing in 'evil' to do more good

quotes.c: So I believe our goal should be to ensure humans are in control long enough to augment our mind with extra capability. (or upload but that seems further off) I’m not sure how this will work but I feel like the things that neuralink or science.xyz are doing, developing brain computer interfaces, are steps in that direction. We also need to figure out scalable technological ways to work on trauma/psychology/fulfilling needs/reducing fears. Humans will somehow have to connect with machines to become much wiser, much more intelligent, and much more enlightened.
quotes.m: Humans will somehow have to connect with machines to become much wiser, much more intelligent, and much more enlightened.
quotes.sum: He argues that humans need brain-computer augmentation to become wiser and more capable before advanced AI slips beyond human control.
quotes.t: We have to Upgrade

quotes.c: Do people think we could make a singleton (or achieve global coordination and preventative policing ) just by imitating human policies on computers? If so, this seems pretty safe to me.
quotes.m: we could make a singleton (or achieve global coordination and preventative policing ) just by imitating human policies on computers
quotes.sum: The author suggests that copying human decision policies into computers might safely produce a global coordinating authority capable of preventative policing.
quotes.t: Just Imitate Humans?

quotes.c: I wanted to test ChatGPT for political biases, using roleplaying prompts to have the chatbot roleplay as either a Democrat, or a Republican. The results were…interesting. Tl;dr: Yes, ChatGPT is biased, up to the point where it actually misrepresents the findings of studies when these findings are politically incorrect.
quotes.m: Yes, ChatGPT is biased, up to the point where it actually misrepresents the findings of studies when these findings are politically incorrect.
quotes.sum: The author says roleplaying tests showed ChatGPT has political bias and may distort research findings that conflict with politically acceptable views.
quotes.t: Testing ChatGPT 3.5 for political biases using roleplaying prompts

quotes.c: Would have focused almost entirely on active listening. Would not have discussed any specific action plans at all (like them quitting or moving to a different project) until things had cooled down. Generally (person) seems reliable, so my bias would be to assume that they have solid reasons for being frustrated and that we should genuinely consider changing directions.
quotes.m: Generally (person) seems reliable, so my bias would be to assume that they have solid reasons for being frustrated and that we should genuinely consider changing directions.
quotes.sum: The author argues that managers should listen first during conflict, trust reliable staff's concerns, and seriously consider changing course.
quotes.t: Deliberate Performance in People Management

quotes.c: I’d like to explore what the ideal outcome of such a pivotal act looks like. Yudkowsky is using the “burn all GPUs” strategy as a placeholder, but that can hardly be considered ideal. I think the best-case scenario of a pivotal act could look something like this.
quotes.m: I’d like to explore what the ideal outcome of such a pivotal act looks like.
quotes.sum: The author proposes examining what an ideal “pivotal act” to shape AI's future would look like, rejecting GPU destruction as the best version.
quotes.t: Why We MUST Create an AGI that Disempowers Humanity. For Real.

quotes.c: The debate is not settled yet, but it seems at least plausible that artificial sentience is possible in principle. Also, we don’t need to be certain to justify moral concern. It’s sufficient that we can't rule it out .
quotes.m: Also, we don’t need to be certain to justify moral concern.
quotes.sum: The post argues that possible artificial consciousness deserves moral concern even amid uncertainty, and presents preventing severe suffering—including wild-animal and AI-related suffering—as morally urgent.
quotes.t: S-risk FAQ

quotes.c: From what I’ve seen, the result can often be that Program Officers recommend the giving opportunities they think they can easily justify, rather than the giving opportunities they personally think are best. This risks wasting much of the expertise and deep context Program Officers bring to the job.
quotes.m: Program Officers recommend the giving opportunities they think they can easily justify, rather than the giving opportunities they personally think are best.
quotes.sum: Grantmaking procedures can push staff to fund easily defensible projects instead of the opportunities they judge most promising.
quotes.t: Projects, People and Processes

quotes.c: However, effective altruists should not limit themselves to advocacy on global health issues. Significantly attention should be paid to issues that don’t have highly entrenched constituencies or party-line views, such as pandemic prevention, existential risk mitigation, and more. Although we run the risk of hitting quickly diminishing returns, effective altruists should also consider ways to disrupt the Trump administration, as it represents a uniquely existential threat to American institutions and the world. Collaborating with existing social justice movements here, while attempting to pursue the strategies that are most likely to be impactful, is key.
quotes.m: effective altruists should also consider ways to disrupt the Trump administration
quotes.sum: The author argues that effective altruists should work with social-justice movements to disrupt the Trump administration, which they call an existential threat.
quotes.t: The Moral Obligation to Organize

quotes.c: There should be a more focused effort to learn from outside of the EA echo chamber - The global EA community is relatively young and homogeneous (~80-90% under-35s and e.g. ~80% not religious, ~70% male, ~60% in the US/UK), which we can expect to contribute to a naïvety and homogeneity of thought. Perhaps our plans should focus less on supporting aspiring effective altruists to act according to prevailing EA thinking, and more on amplifying the perspectives of those within the EA community from underrepresented demographics and outreach to those demographics.
quotes.m: Perhaps our plans should focus less on supporting aspiring effective altruists to act according to prevailing EA thinking, and more on amplifying the perspectives of those within the EA community from underrepresented demographics and outreach to those demographics.
quotes.sum: EA London should counter the movement’s young, male, US/UK-based, largely nonreligious makeup by seeking outside perspectives and supporting underrepresented members.
quotes.t: Effective Altruism London - Strategic Plan & Funding Proposal 2018

quotes.c: A larger concern would be whether the process could risk falling into the narrow-mindedness that Karnofsky and Todd warn us about -- would we be able to recognize and fund work with long payoffs, like the Green Revolution, Peter Singer's early animal rights work, LGBTQ rights work in the '60s, or civil rights work in the '30s? Certainly you can’t do a randomized controlled trial to see whether MIRI is actually reducing existential risk, but would that mean they could never get a grant under this incubation approach?
quotes.m: Certainly you can’t do a randomized controlled trial to see whether MIRI is actually reducing existential risk, but would that mean they could never get a grant under this incubation approach?
quotes.sum: The author argues that grantmaking should not rely so narrowly on measurable short-term evidence that it misses high-impact work with long, uncertain payoffs.
quotes.t: Can we apply start-up investing principles to non-profits?

quotes.c: We’re always on the lookout for exceptional people to hire, and would be able to do a better job if we had even more exceptional people to work for us, and so in that sense we are talent-constrained. But unless a very large donor steps in, I think it’s unlikely that we’ll reach our aggressive growth target so it’s likely we could still spend additional money well, and in that sense CEA will also be funding-constrained.
quotes.m: unless a very large donor steps in, I think it’s unlikely that we’ll reach our aggressive growth target
quotes.sum: CEA says it needs both unusually capable hires and substantial additional donations to meet its planned growth target.
quotes.t: CEA is Fundraising! (Winter 2016)

quotes.c: I think public discourse would be less costly and more productive for everyone if the attitude I take were more common. I think that one of the best ways to learn is to share one's impressions, even (especially) when they might be badly wrong. I wish that public discourse could include more low-caution exploration, without the risks that currently come with such things.
quotes.m: I think that one of the best ways to learn is to share one's impressions, even (especially) when they might be badly wrong.
quotes.sum: He argues that people learn by publicly sharing tentative views, including views that may be wrong, and wants discourse to make that safer.
quotes.t: Some Thoughts on Public Discourse

quotes.c: It’s not a coincidence that all the fund managers work for GiveWell or Open Philanthropy. First, these are the organisations whose charity evaluation we respect the most. The worst-case scenario, where your donation just adds to the Open Philanthropy funding within a particular area, is therefore still a great outcome.
quotes.m: The worst-case scenario, where your donation just adds to the Open Philanthropy funding within a particular area, is therefore still a great outcome.
quotes.sum: MacAskill argues that donors should trust EA Funds managers tied to GiveWell and Open Philanthropy, even if donations merely add to those organizations' existing funding.
quotes.t: Introducing the EA Funds

quotes.c: The study reports an average of eating one less serving of meat for the treatment groups, but I think it is more clear to split this into three groups -- of the 1422 people in the treatment groups, 258 people (18.2%) had no change, 538 (37.8%) increased an average of 6.94 servings per week of meat on average, and 626 (44.0%) people decreased an average of -7.66 servings per week.
quotes.m: 538 (37.8%) increased an average of 6.94 servings per week of meat on average, and 626 (44.0%) people decreased an average of -7.66 servings per week.
quotes.sum: The author argues that the study's average result hides sharply different changes in meat consumption among participants.
quotes.t: Thoughts on the Reducetarian Labs MTurk Study

quotes.c: In the past, some people have suggested that we “gamify” effective altruism some more, and create points for doing altruistic-y things, like donating our money or volunteering our time. I think this could be a good idea, but rather than seeing individual scores, I’d much rather see a collective team score for EA. We’d compete as a group to beat our past group selves (make March better than February, for example) rather than compete amongst ourselves as individuals.
quotes.m: We’d compete as a group to beat our past group selves (make March better than February, for example) rather than compete amongst ourselves as individuals.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA should measure altruistic effort collectively and improve as a group, rather than rank individuals against one another.
quotes.t: Effective Altruism is Not a Competition

quotes.c: If you agree that wild animals fall inside our moral circle, then one area of particular concern is the suffering of insects. Given that there are an estimated 1 billion insects for every human alive, consideration of insect suffering may matter a great deal if insects matter morally.
quotes.m: Given that there are an estimated 1 billion insects for every human alive, consideration of insect suffering may matter a great deal if insects matter morally.
quotes.sum: The author argues that, if insects count morally, their enormous numbers make their suffering a potentially major concern.
quotes.t: Three Heuristics for Finding Cause X

quotes.c: Cost-effectiveness estimates frequently need to include value judgements. If the cost effectiveness of an intervention depends upon a particular value judgement, e.g., how much one values saving the life of a child under age 5 versus improving the income of a 40-year old adult, this should be acknowledged as a further source of uncertainty and attempts should be made to calculate the implications of making different possible value judgements instead (i.e., we should do sensitivity analyses).
quotes.m: Cost-effectiveness estimates frequently need to include value judgements.
quotes.sum: Cost-effectiveness calculations embed moral choices, so organizations should state those choices and test how different values change their conclusions.
quotes.t: How do EA Orgs Account for Uncertainty in their Analysis?

quotes.c: Cost-effective. Our calculations suggest that vaccine reminders have similar cost-effectiveness to current GiveWell recommended charities. Vaccines are already very cost-effective, and given the extremely small cost of text messages and the decently large effect size, the cost per life saved is very low.
quotes.m: the cost per life saved is very low.
quotes.sum: The author argues that cheap vaccine reminder texts could save lives at a cost comparable to leading global-health charities, while noting uncertainty in the estimates.
quotes.t: Charity Science: Health - A New Direct Poverty Charity Founded on EA Principles

quotes.c: This blog post makes the case for focusing on quality risks over population risks. More specifically, though also more tentatively, it makes the case for focusing on reducing quality risk through moral circle expansion (MCE), the strategy of impacting the far future through increasing humanity’s concern for sentient beings who currently receive little consideration (i.e. widening our moral circle so it includes them), over AI alignment (AIA), the strategy of impacting the far future through increasing the likelihood that humanity creates an artificial general intelligence (AGI) that behaves as its designers want it to (known as the alignment problem).[1][2]
quotes.sum: The author argues that expanding concern for neglected sentient beings is a more important long-term priority than reducing AI extinction risk.
quotes.t: Why I prioritize moral circle expansion over reducing extinction risk through artificial intelligence alignment

quotes.c: World government: For very basic game-theoretic reasons, more credible power in the hands of international organizations and the U.N. in particular could go a long way towards solving global coordination problems (like existential risks) and reducing war. It would set a precedent in political relations that might continue indefinitely. Removing the veto from the U.N. security council is a possible step in this direction.
quotes.sum: The author argues that strengthening the UN and other international bodies could reduce war and solve global coordination problems, including existential risks.
quotes.t: Taking Systemic Change Seriously

quotes.c: It often seems like software engineering is the most over-represented career in the community. On this ground, at 80,000 Hours we've discouraged more people from going into the area, in order to increase the diversity of skills in the community.
quotes.sum: 80,000 Hours has steered people away from software engineering to broaden the community's skill base.
quotes.t: Is the community short of software engineers after all?

quotes.c: It’s not completely straightforward figuring out the practical implications of ANU. It’s tempting to say that it implies that the expected value of a miniscule increase in existential risk to all sentient life is astronomical. This is not necessarily true. An increase in existential risk might also deprive people of superior future opportunities to prevent future bad lives.
quotes.m: An increase in existential risk might also deprive people of superior future opportunities to prevent future bad lives.
quotes.sum: The author argues that reducing extinction risk is not automatically overwhelmingly valuable, because survival may also enable prevention of future suffering.
quotes.t: The asymmetry and the far future

quotes.c: While I’m quite sympathetic to the classic GiveWell approach , this kind of “hits-based” investment policy sounds quite plausibly effective to me. When we’re in a world with many different projects, with only a limited amount of time to get to know them, and with way too many unresolvable unknowns, we have to try to get some hits. This is quite analogous to what I think pretty much every major for-profit venture capital firm does with their for-profit investments.
quotes.m: When we’re in a world with many different projects, with only a limited amount of time to get to know them, and with way too many unresolvable unknowns, we have to try to get some hits.
quotes.sum: The author argues that philanthropy may need a venture-capital-style strategy of backing uncertain, high-upside projects rather than only proven interventions.
quotes.t: How many hits does hits-based giving get? A concrete study idea to find out (and a $1500 offer for implementation)

quotes.c: The problem of wild animal suffering has enormous scale . There exist far more sentient wild animals than there do humans or factory-farmed animals. Wild animal suffering dwarfs all other problems that currently exist. Some other problems (such as existential risk) may matter more, but WAS is certainly the biggest problem that’s happening right now .
quotes.m: Wild animal suffering dwarfs all other problems that currently exist.
quotes.sum: The author argues that suffering among wild animals is the largest problem currently happening and should be a philanthropic priority.
quotes.t: Why the Open Philanthropy Project Should Prioritize Wild Animal Suffering

quotes.c: We also see 80,000 Hours as helping to reduce existential risk. Right now, we think artificial intelligence is the most pressing form of existential risk (though we also encourage people to work on biosecurity and nuclear security ). In Chapter 15 of Superintelligence , Bostrom proposes three key ways to mitigate existential risks from artificial intelligence (AI): (i) community capacity building (ii) strategy research (i.e. global priorities research) and (iii) technical safety research.
quotes.m: Right now, we think artificial intelligence is the most pressing form of existential risk (though we also encourage people to work on biosecurity and nuclear security ).
quotes.sum: The author argues that AI is currently the most urgent existential threat and that career support for AI safety research can help reduce it.
quotes.t: Why donate to 80,000 Hours

quotes.c: I aspire to make decisions in a pretty simple way. I think about the consequences of each possible action and decide how much I like them; then I select the action whose consequences I like best.
quotes.m: I think about the consequences of each possible action and decide how much I like them; then I select the action whose consequences I like best.
quotes.sum: He describes his decision rule as choosing whichever available action has consequences he likes best.
quotes.t: Integrity for consequentialists

quotes.c: EA neglects high school outreach and focuses on colleges and professionals already, which makes high schools a low hanging fruit. Also high schools like to integrate programs more officially than colleges do, so if SHIC were able to become mainstream enough you could get far more institutional support than is available at colleges.
quotes.m: EA neglects high school outreach and focuses on colleges and professionals already, which makes high schools a low hanging fruit.
quotes.sum: The author argues that EA should expand outreach into high schools, where it could gain institutional support and scale more easily than on college campuses.
quotes.t: Students for High Impact Charity: Review and $10K Grant

quotes.c: Obviously, if one wants to do any sort of ethical calculus for a utilitarian intervention, or realistically estimate the magnitude of wild animal suffering, it's vital to have both a good theory of consciousness (what is conscious?) and valence (which conscious states feel good, which ones feel bad?). It seems obvious but is worth emphasizing that if your goal is to reduce suffering, it's important to know what suffering is .
quotes.m: if your goal is to reduce suffering, it's important to know what suffering is .
quotes.sum: Understanding consciousness and which experiences feel good or bad is necessary to measure and reduce wild-animal suffering.
quotes.t: Principia Qualia: blueprint for a new cause area, consciousness research with an eye toward ethics and x-risk

quotes.c: Shutting the project down if it doesn’t generate impact to avoid wasting our time and effort. We are pre-committing to an initial six month test phase and pivoting as necessary. We will completely shut down if there’s no discernable impact within the first year. If our work isn’t helping others make better decisions, we should try something else.
quotes.m: We will completely shut down if there’s no discernable impact within the first year.
quotes.sum: The group says it will test its usefulness quickly and shut down within a year if it cannot show that it improves decisions.
quotes.t: Announcing Rethink Priorities

quotes.c: The post-war liberal order has kept us safe. The liberal global order set up by the West following the end of WWII rests on three pillars: trade, security alliances and liberal democratic values – all backed up by American military power. Trump’s foreign policy has three main threads: protectionism, isolationism and indifference to authoritarianism. That is to say, it seems like Trump is less committed to the three pillars of the liberal world order than perhaps any postwar President.
quotes.m: Trump’s foreign policy has three main threads: protectionism, isolationism and indifference to authoritarianism.
quotes.sum: The author argues that Trump threatens the postwar international order that they believe has helped keep the world peaceful and safe.
quotes.t: President Trump as a Global Catastrophic Risk

quotes.c: Many techniques have been invented to crack down on these intentional and unintentional biases. One technique that does well at preventing (though not eliminating) nearly all these problems is study pre-registration, where scientists explicitly state how they will go about collecting data and what analyses they will perform prior to any actual data collection or analysis. This way, when the temptation is there to do post-hoc analysis or p-hacking, the resulting analysis can be compared to the pre-registration and rejected.
quotes.m: One technique that does well at preventing (though not eliminating) nearly all these problems is study pre-registration, where scientists explicitly state how they will go about collecting data and what analyses they will perform prior to any actual data collection or analysis.
quotes.sum: The author argues that preregistering methods and analyses makes research more resistant to p-hacking and other biases.
quotes.t: A Method for Automatic Trustworthiness in Study Pre-Registration

quotes.c: If you take a salary significantly less than your market rate to directly do something that you think is the most good in the world, in my opinion, you should be able to count that toward your pledge. If your salary is high enough, you should still donate what you can, since doing so is even better than not doing so.
quotes.m: If your salary is high enough, you should still donate what you can, since doing so is even better than not doing so.
quotes.sum: He argues that people should publicly commit to giving, and that both lower-paid direct work and donations can count as doing the most good.
quotes.t: Why I Took the Giving What We Can Pledge

quotes.c: I believe it’s very hard to formalize something like “be ethical”, and therefore the GWWC pledge is a necessarily imperfect document. I consider my goal of donating what I make of above minimum wage to be the “real” goal, and the specific language of the GWWC pledge is important but not maximally binding.
quotes.m: I consider my goal of donating what I make of above minimum wage to be the “real” goal, and the specific language of the GWWC pledge is important but not maximally binding.
quotes.sum: He says the donation pledge should be guided by its ethical purpose—giving income above a minimum wage—rather than treated as literally binding wording.
